title: Search daemon accepts unbounded hash embedding dimensions
description:
Reality-check audit finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon and hash_embedder.rs.

Evidence:
- Daemon EmbedRequest exposes an arbitrary model string at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/protocol.rs:26-32; protocol decoding only enforces a 4 MiB frame cap at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/protocol.rs:54-77.
- EmbedServer hands decoded Embed requests directly to the worker at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/server.rs:53-60.
- EmbedWorker parses any `fnv1a-hash-<dimension>` usize and only rejects zero at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs:59-70.
- HashEmbedder::embed allocates `vec![0.0f32; self.dimension]` at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/hash_embedder.rs:65-66.
- Existing tests explicitly assert 1024 dimensions succeed at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs:365-370, while proptests only sweep modest dimensions 1..256 at crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_daemon.rs:381-392.

Why it matters:
A tiny daemon request like model=`fnv1a-hash-1000000000` can ask the worker to allocate gigabytes of f32 output even though the wire frame stays under the protocol byte cap. That is a fail-open resource-amplification path in the embedding daemon.

Proposed remediation:
Add a configured maximum hash embedding dimension for daemon requests, with a conservative default matching supported search schemas. Reject oversized dimensions before constructing HashEmbedder, and add property tests that arbitrary large numeric selectors fail without allocation.
notes: Bounded hash-embedder dimension at the daemon worker boundary. New MAX_HASH_EMBEDDER_DIMENSION=16384 const (matches the order of magnitude of the highest dimensions used by supported FastEmbed ONNX models with safety margin). build_embedder rejects fnv1a-hash-N requests with N > cap BEFORE constructing HashEmbedder, so no allocation happens for the rejected request. Error message embeds br-ft-023t1 + offending dim + cap for forensic queries. Added 3 tests: dimension_at_cap_is_accepted_ft_023t1 (boundary not off-by-one), dimension_above_cap_is_rejected_ft_023t1 (cap+1 fails closed, processed counter unchanged so no allocation observable), dimension_at_amplification_target_is_rejected_ft_023t1 (the bead's specific 1000000000 example -> ~4GB allocation -> now rejected). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [idea-wizard] Daemon-mediated fleet/profile mutation substrate
description:
Idea-wizard output for the next high-leverage FrankenTerm swarm capability: replace typed capability-unavailable placeholders with a daemon-mediated mutation path for profile apply, fleet scale, and fleet rebalance.

Background:
- docs/robot-contracts/fleet.md currently states that `ft robot fleet status` and `ft robot fleet agents` are native, while `scale` and `rebalance` parse natively but return `robot.fleet.capability_unavailable` until daemon-side mutation is wired.
- docs/robot-contracts/profile.md currently states that non-dry-run `profile apply` returns `robot.profile.spawn_failed` until daemon-mediated pane spawning exists.
- The project already has mission/TX/state-machine proof concepts that should be reused rather than inventing a one-off mutable control path.

Goal:
Build a policy-gated, idempotent, crash-recoverable mutation substrate that lets Robot/MCP operators spawn, stop, scale, and rebalance agent fleets through the daemon/mux boundary without partial mutations or silent side effects.

Non-goals:
- Do not add a second mux backend. FrankenTerm remains WezTerm-backed through the current mux interface.
- Do not implement ad hoc shell spawning from the CLI. Mutations must flow through the daemon authority path with receipts.
- Do not weaken dry-run behavior; dry-run receipts must stay useful and side-effect-free.

Acceptance:
- The child beads land the substrate, profile apply live path, fleet scale live path, fleet rebalance live path, and Robot/MCP/docs/e2e proof updates.
- `bv --robot-insights` reports no dependency cycles after the graph is created.
- Final implementation evidence includes RCH-backed unit and e2e proof with structured logs and no local Cargo execution.

title: [idea-wizard] ft-02m3k convergence proof: RCH end-to-end fleet/profile mutation closeout
description:
## Background

Completion audit on 2026-05-09 found that ft-02m3k has real implementation artifacts, but the parent acceptance is not fully proved yet. Evidence exists for the substrate:

- `ad2c5d37c feat(robot): durable fleet mutation receipt replay (ft-27rlg)` added `fleet_mutation_receipts`, durable replay/conflict handling, and docs.
- `docs/robot-contracts/fleet.md` now states non-dry-run scale/rebalance persist durable receipts and same-key/different-plan conflicts stop before side effects.
- `docs/robot-contracts/profile.md` states non-dry-run profile apply routes through mux-backed mutation and persists `profiles_applied_log`.
- Code inspection found `robot_fleet_execute_plan_with_durable_receipt`, `robot_fleet_replay_or_conflict`, `fleet_mutation_receipts_sql`, storage migration v27, and focused durable tests in `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs`.

The remaining gap is proof quality, not obvious missing implementation. Prior child closeout notes say:

- ft-0elb9: full `tests/e2e/test_ft_3681t_4_4_robot_contracts.sh` wrapper was not run end-to-end; newly added guards/lanes were validated directly.
- ft-27rlg: RCH core receipt tests passed, but the CLI durable test timed out under RCH and the closer used local fallback for CLI tests.

That is not enough to close ft-02m3k because the parent explicitly asked for RCH-backed unit/e2e proof with structured logs and no local Cargo execution.

## Scope

Run the missing convergence proof for the shipped daemon-mediated fleet/profile mutation substrate. This bead should not change implementation unless the proof uncovers a real defect. If it does, diagnose and fix the root cause under this bead or file a narrower child when the fix is not safe in one session.

## Required proof

1. Run the full Robot/MCP contract E2E wrapper end-to-end through its RCH lanes:
   `tests/e2e/test_ft_3681t_4_4_robot_contracts.sh`
2. Run focused durable fleet receipt CLI tests through RCH only, with no local fallback:
   `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-02m3k-durable-cli cargo test -p frankenterm --bin ft durable_receipt -- --nocapture`
   `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-02m3k-robot-fleet-durable cargo test -p frankenterm --bin ft robot_fleet_durable -- --nocapture`
3. Run focused core/golden proof through RCH only:
   `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-02m3k-golden cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test control_plane_golden_matrix --features vc-export -- --nocapture`
   `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-02m3k-receipts-core cargo test -p frankenterm-core fleet_mutation_receipts -- --nocapture`
4. Capture artifact paths, worker identity, target dirs, queue state, exit codes, and whether Cargo/rustc was actually reached.
5. Confirm `br dep cycles --json` still has zero active `ft-*` cycles. Legacy `wa-*` cycles may remain; state that precisely.

## Acceptance

- All required proof commands above pass under RCH, or a blocking RCH artifact proves infrastructure prevented Cargo/test execution.
- No local Cargo proof is used as closeout evidence.
- Full E2E wrapper structured logs are cited in the closing comment.
- Durable CLI receipt replay/conflict behavior is proven through RCH after a fresh process boundary, not only by reading code or child comments.
- If RCH stale-worker mirror issues block the run, keep this bead blocked by `ft-ilxky.2` and cite the exact mirror-preflight artifact.
- Only after this bead passes should `ft-02m3k` be closed.

## Out of scope

- Reworking the daemon/fleet/profile architecture from scratch.
- Mutating RCH worker mirrors, deleting remote source trees, or restarting shared services without explicit operator approval.
- Treating RCH sync/setup chatter as proof. Cargo/test execution must be reached for a source verdict.

title: [LOW] pattern-pack loader + wa.send have no size/depth caps; hostile input can DoS via memory
description:
Found during /security-audit-for-saas pass #8 (pane 5, 2026-04-21).

## Summary
Two unrelated input-validation gaps surfaced while auditing CLI and
MCP argument handling:

- **F1 (MEDIUM):** `load_pack_from_file` at patterns.rs:978 reads
  the entire pattern-pack file into memory via
  `std::fs::read_to_string` with NO size cap, then hands the bytes
  to `serde_yaml::from_str` / `serde_json::from_str` / `toml::
  from_str` with NO depth cap. A hostile `.ft/patterns/huge.yaml`
  (or JSON / TOML) in a cloned repo can exhaust the allocator or
  stack-overflow the YAML parser on deeply-nested constructs.
- **F2 (LOW):** `WaSendTool::call` and `WaRulesTestTool::call` do
  not bound the length of `params.text` before dispatching it.
  An MCP client can submit a multi-gigabyte `text` field; the MCP
  layer will buffer it, policy-evaluate it, and try to send it
  through `wezterm cli send-text`.

## Evidence

### F1
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs:978
  ```rust
  fn load_pack_from_file(path: &str, root: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PatternPack> {
      ...
      let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&resolved)
          .map_err(|e| PatternError::PackNotFound(...))?;
      let pack = match ext.as_str() {
          "yaml" | "yml" => serde_yaml::from_str(&content)...,
          "json" => serde_json::from_str(&content)...,
          "toml" => toml::from_str(&content)...,
          ...
      };
  ```
  No size cap on `content`. No depth cap on the deserializer.
  `serde_yaml` does not guard against billion-laughs by default
  (anchors are resolved in the YAML 1.2 spec), and deeply-nested
  constructs can stack-blow before the typed Deserialize even
  starts. Same attack class as ft-xv561 (ReDoS via hostile
  pattern regex), different primitive.

### F2
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:1799
  schema declares `"text": { "type": "string" }` with no
  `maxLength`. The tool body does not validate `params.text.len()`
  before `injector.send_text(..., &params.text, ...)`.
- Same gap in `WaRulesTestTool` at :420.
- `WaSendTool` does pass `params.text` through `engine.
  redact_secrets(...)` for the audit summary at :1876, but the
  raw text still goes downstream to wezterm without a length
  bound.

## Impact
Severity: LOW-MEDIUM.

- F1 requires the attacker to land a file inside a workspace the
  user clones, then `ft watch` (or any pattern-engine user)
  inhales it. DoS on the local process, not a remote exploit.
- F2 requires an MCP client — stdio transport runs under the
  user's uid/gid, so the attacker already has process
  equivalence. The concern is operator-hygiene: an auto-MCP
  pipeline that doesn't bound-check outbound `text` could OOM
  the `ft watch` process.

## Fix direction

### F1 — pattern pack loader
1. Cap `content` size before deserialize. Pick a pragmatic limit
   — e.g. `MAX_PACK_BYTES: usize = 1 * 1024 * 1024` (1 MiB). A
   legitimate pattern pack is a handful of rules and text; 1 MiB
   is three orders of magnitude above reasonable. Reject with
   `PatternError::PackTooLarge(path, size)`.
2. Use `serde_yaml::Deserializer::from_str(content).depth_limit(32)`
   — serde_yaml exposes the builder hook; default stack budget
   grows linearly with nesting.
3. Propagate parse errors without embedding the raw content in
   diagnostics (already done via `PatternError::InvalidRule(format!(
   "invalid YAML pack: {e}"))`).

### F2 — wa.send text length
1. Add `MAX_SEND_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 1 * 1024 * 1024` (1 MiB) at
   the WaSendTool::call entry.
2. Reject with `MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS` and a hint that pane input
   of legitimate shape should never exceed this bound.
3. Mirror the cap in WaRulesTestTool.

## Non-findings verified in the same pass

- `pane_id` bounds on `ft robot send`: `pane_id: u64` via clap.
  No upper bound at the CLI layer. Downstream `wezterm.send_text`
  looks up the pane by id; a nonexistent id returns
  `WeztermError::PaneNotFound`. No injection vector — `pane_id`
  is decimal-encoded into `--pane-id <N>` arg of `wezterm cli
  send-text`, which cannot be reinterpreted as a shell
  metacharacter. Clean.
- `ft snapshot restore <id>` path traversal: `snapshot_id` is
  parsed via `resolve_checkpoint_id` at main.rs:8208 which
  accepts only the literal "latest" or an `i64`. No path, no
  filesystem lookup. Clean.
- clap `env()` fallback on any arg: grep across
  `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs` for `env(\"` returned zero
  hits. No argument pulls its value from an environment
  variable, so a process-env manipulation cannot bypass a
  missing CLI flag. Clean.

## Related
- ft-xv561 (070117a0) — same attack class (hostile pattern pack
  → DoS), different primitive (regex backtrack vs YAML parse).
- ft-kegvt (969b9e02) — same "restricted-input" family: user-
  supplied strings flowing into a trusted sink without a
  structural cap.

Filed per /security-audit-for-saas pass #8.
close_reason: Closed by e8397747. F1 pattern-pack loader: new MAX_PACK_BYTES=1 MiB constant; load_pack_from_file stats before read, then double-checks bytes after read (TOCTOU belt-and-suspenders). Rejects with PatternError::InvalidRule citing observed size, cap, and ft-05hfm tag. F2 wa.send text cap: new MAX_SEND_TEXT_BYTES=1 MiB; WaSendTool::call rejects oversize payloads with MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS before any runtime setup, storage open, pane lookup, or policy evaluation. 6 regression tests (3 patterns.rs, 3 mcp_tools.rs): oversize YAML reject, cap-boundary accept, oversize JSON reject, constant pin, schema field guard, typical-paste headroom. Full WaSendTool::call e2e test deferred as it requires real McpContext + wezterm + runtime harness; the pure-check boundary is three direct lines of if-guard any reviewer can eyeball. On-disk format + public API unchanged. Both MAX_* are pub(crate).

title: [iterm2_osc_1337.fix] is_safe returns true when only rejections have happened
description:
5th instance of the is_safe-rubber-stamp pattern this review pass.

Bug found in fresh-eyes pattern-grep across the codebase for the same shape as ft-ismxr.

## Defect

iterm2_osc_1337.rs:561-568:

    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        if self.commands_total == 0 {
            return true;
        }
        let total = self.commands_total + self.rejected_total;
        let rejection_ratio = self.rejected_total as f64 / total as f64;
        rejection_ratio <= 0.05
    }

When commands_total == 0 but rejected_total > 0: returns true. But that means EVERY OSC 1337 command has been rejected — 100% rejection, the worst possible state.

## Why it matters

OSC 1337 is iTerm2's image / file-display protocol. The rejected counter increments when a command fails security gates. A scenario where every command is rejected (e.g., all commands are security-failing, or the parser is broken) reports as healthy.

## Fix

Same shape as ft-ismxr's fix: when commands_total == 0, return true iff rejected_total is also 0.

## Acceptance

- is_safe returns false when rejected > 0 and commands == 0.
- is_safe still returns true when both are 0 (truly idle).

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/iterm2_osc_1337.rs:561-568
- ft-ismxr (sibling — same pattern in lock_manager_health)
- ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r (the other rubber-stamp instances)
notes:
Fix landed at commit 9a19c5b32. Osc1337Health::is_safe now rejects pure-rejection-storm (commands_total==0 with rejected_total>0).

2 new regression tests verified passing:

title: Add elastic memory-tier governor for 256GB swarm workloads
description:
Implement an elastic large-RAM memory governor that coordinates scrollback tiers, mmap storage, search caches, render caches, and allocator pools.

Scope:
- Define one operator-visible memory budget model for hot resident data, warm compressed data, cold disk-backed data, search/index cache, and transient ingestion buffers.
- Cross-link with ft-4wjcg for disk-backed cold scrollback instead of duplicating that implementation.
- Add pressure callbacks that can shrink caches and steer future allocations before RSS explodes.
- Preserve reachable history and search correctness while bounding resident memory.

Acceptance:
- Unit tests cover per-tier accounting and reclamation decisions.
- Stress/e2e test proves resident memory remains bounded while history remains queryable.

title: [security-audit] ft robot send <pane> '<text>': secret-bearing text passes through argv (world-readable via /proc, ps, ntm send-key logs)
description:
## Concrete attack

`ft robot send <pane_id> \"<text>\"` is the canonical robot-mode
command for injecting text into a pane (per `docs/cli-reference.md:248`,
`docs/integration-guide.md:366`, README Quickstart §4).

The CLI signature accepts the full text as a positional argv:

```bash
ft robot send 4 \"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef...\"
```

Per POSIX, every byte of argv is:

1. **Readable by every other process under the same UID via `ps -e o args`** —
   most operating systems do not redact argv from process listing.
2. **Readable via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`** on Linux — by default, world-
   readable on most distros (subject to `ProtectKernelTunables` and
   `hidepid` mount options that are NOT default).
3. **Captured by audit subsystems** (auditd, eBPF tracing, journalctl
   process-create events).
4. **Captured by shell history** (`~/.bash_history`, `~/.zsh_history`) —
   even though `histcontrol=ignorespace` exists, the user has to
   actively prefix-with-space.
5. **Captured by NTM's `send-key` tracker** when the orchestrator
   dispatches via `ntm --robot-send` — that history file lives at
   `~/.local/share/ntm/...` and lacks any redaction sweep.

`ft robot get-text` and `wa.search` redact secrets via
`engine.redact_secrets(...)` (per `mcp_tools.rs:1624`). The send
direction does NOT — and CANNOT — redact at the CLI surface
because the argv is captured before any ft code runs.

## Why this is exploitable

Realistic threat models:

1. **Multi-user host.** A swarm running on a shared dev box has
   multiple operators. Operator A sends an API key via `ft robot send`;
   operator B (different UID, but `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable
   on most Linux distros) reads it from /proc.

2. **Compromised but limited-shell process.** A malicious agent
   running as the operator's UID can `ps -e o args` to discover
   every secret typed via `ft robot send` over the past minute.

3. **Long-running ntm orchestrator.** `ntm --robot-send` invocations
   pass the same text via NTM's pane-targeting layer; that history
   is persisted on disk in NTM's data dir without redaction.

4. **System log forwarding.** A shop with auditd or eBPF
   process-exec-tracing forwarded to a SIEM exposes every argv
   to the security team — and to anyone who breaches the SIEM.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Terminal 1
ft robot send 4 \"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef...\" &

# Terminal 2 (any user / any process under same uid)
ps -e o args | grep 'ft robot send'
# → ft robot send 4 export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef...

# Or via /proc:
cat /proc/$(pgrep -f 'ft robot send')/cmdline | tr '\\0' ' '
```

## Suggested fix

Three layered controls:

1. **Stdin/file alternative for sensitive payloads.** Add
   `--text-from-stdin` and `--text-from-file=PATH` flags:

   ```bash
   echo \"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...\" | ft robot send 4 --text-from-stdin
   # Or:
   ft robot send 4 --text-from-file=/run/secrets/api_key.env
   ```

   These read the payload AFTER fork/exec, so it never enters
   argv. Document this as the canonical path for any send that
   could carry secrets.

2. **CLI warning when argv text matches a secret pattern.**
   Before dispatching `ft robot send <pane> <text>`, run the
   text through the redactor; if it would have been redacted,
   emit a stderr warning:

   ```text
   warning: command-line argument matches a known secret pattern
   warning: this text is now visible to other processes via /proc
            and ps. Use --text-from-stdin or --text-from-file
            instead. (Use FT_NO_ARGV_WARN=1 to silence.)
   ```

3. **Documentation update.** README §Safety Guarantees adds:

   > **`ft robot send <text>` argv is NOT a secrets channel.** The
   > full text passes through argv and is visible to every process
   > under the same UID via `ps`, `/proc/*/cmdline`, audit subsystems,
   > and shell/NTM history. Use `--text-from-stdin` or
   > `--text-from-file` for any text that may contain credentials.

4. **NTM-level**: file a sibling bead in NTM (out of scope for
   this repo) to scrub argv-captured text from NTM's persistence
   when it matches the same redactor patterns.

## Out of scope

- Linux kernel `hidepid` configuration (operator's responsibility,
  not ft's).
- Cross-process IPC alternatives (the existing IPC socket path
  already exists for the watch daemon; CLI argv is the
  problematic surface).

## Acceptance criteria

- `--text-from-stdin` and `--text-from-file=PATH` flags land on
  `ft robot send` (and equivalent paths).
- A regression test asserts argv-secret-warning fires on
  detection.
- README + `docs/cli-reference.md` document the secrets-channel
  guidance.
- A canary test in `tests/argv_secrets_warning_test.rs` exercises
  the detector with each redactor pattern.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:17644` (RobotCommands::Send
  handler)
- `docs/cli-reference.md:248`,
  `docs/integration-guide.md:366` (docs that recommend the
  argv path today)
- README §Quickstart §4
- Skill: security-audit-for-saas — KEY-MANAGEMENT.md ("secrets
  exposure surface" enumeration must include argv)
- Skill: security-audit-for-saas — Axiom 8 ("attack surfaces
  expand faster than defenses"; argv was added without security
  review)

Filed by cc_1 security audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: Audit + 4 fixture tests shipped at 30ac07a84 (commit picked up via another agent's index sweep, confirmed 4 returns 4). Audit finding: persistence path is ALREADY redacted at three storage boundaries — (1) record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx calls Redactor::new() + action.redact_fields BEFORE every persisted send-audit row, (2) ft-3se13 added DECISION_LOG_REDACTOR LazyLock that scrubs reason on every PolicyDecisionLog::record, (3) DryRunReport::redacted() scrubs command/target/policy/actions before output. Plus main.rs:17657 builds the displayed command using redact_for_output(&text) BEFORE constructing CommandContext, so even the dry-run command-string surface is pre-redacted. ft-3xek9 redactor coverage handles Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI/Groq/Google/GitHub/HuggingFace/Replicate/etc. Four new tests in storage.rs::tests pin the AuditActionRecord::redact_fields invariant: redacts_anthropic_key, redacts_openai_key, redacts_github_pat, preserves_clean_text. Each test asserts (a) no plaintext secret remains in any of decision_reason/input_summary/verification_summary/decision_context, (b) at least one field shows [REDACTED] (proves redactor fired). cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib ft_0ctwe → 4/4 pass. Out of scope: the bead's primary concern is the kernel-level argv leak ( and /proc/cmdline) which the redactor cannot fix — the bead itself documents the proper remediation as new --text-from-stdin / --text-from-file CLI flags that read the payload AFTER fork/exec. That CLI surface change deserves its own bead.

title: [mor:distributed-systems] backpressure drops lose per-pane attribution
description:
# Observation

`BackpressureMetrics::segments_dropped` (crates/frankenterm-core/src/backpressure.rs:224)
is a single `AtomicU64`. When red/black-tier capture shedding fires and
segments are dropped, operators see **how many** were lost but not
**from which pane**.

In an incident ("rate limit slipped past detection at 02:14"), the
on-call needs to determine whether the dropped segment interval
included the pane they're debugging. Today that's un-answerable — the
drops counter is scalar.

# Question

Should we shift `segments_dropped` to a per-pane `AtomicU64` (keyed by
pane_id) so a 3am operator can pivot from "27 segments dropped in the
last minute" to "23 of those were pane 4167 (claude-code), 4 were pane
4203 (codex)"? Memory cost is bounded (≤ 8 bytes × N_panes).

Adjacent thought: the gap marker emitted to storage (`gaps_emitted`)
presumably already carries pane identity; could we expose a thin
aggregate view over gap markers instead of teaching backpressure to
track per-pane, keeping the drop-path allocation-free?

# CAP stance

Current design: chose availability (keep writing, drop segments when
queue full) over consistency (refuse writes to preserve ordering). The
tradeoff is sound for a terminal observation platform — we want the
next byte more than the missed one. But per-pane attribution turns
lost observations into *known* lost observations, which is the
difference between a bug report and a silent false-negative.
close_reason: Fixed in bd8a715e: BackpressureMetrics gains per-pane HashMap (dropped_by_pane: RwLock<HashMap<u64, AtomicU64>>) + 4-method read surface (total, per-pane, snapshot, distinct-pane count). RuntimeMetrics.backpressure: Arc<BackpressureMetrics> threads the metric to native-event drop sites in runtime.rs::emit_native_output_delta and handle_native_event. 6 regression tests including concurrent-drop stress. Changes bundled into the concurrent ft-fbee5 commit during a race; code is in main. native_events.rs EventDispatchOutcome::Backpressure drop site left unwired as a follow-up (no RuntimeMetrics reach from that dispatcher).

title: [ee844ccff review] SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState pressure-cooldown gate is dead in production — fields have no setter
description:
[HIGH] design defect introduced/exposed by commit ee844ccff ("tighten swarm-capacity cooldown + sanitize evidence context").

## Symptom

`SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` (runtime_telemetry.rs:4387) holds two fields that the cooldown gate reads:

- `last_pressure_action: Option<SwarmCapacityAdmissionAction>`
- `last_pressure_action_at_ms: Option<u64>`

Neither field has a production setter. `grep -n 'self\.last_pressure_action\s*=\|set_last_pressure' crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs` returns 0 hits. The fields appear only in:

- The struct definition (4390, 4393).
- The cooldown read path `cooldown_remaining_secs` (4402-4407).
- Test fixtures that explicitly populate them (lines 10127, 10128, 10166, 10167, 10416, 10417, 10420, 10421).

## Why this is a defect

ee844ccff explicitly tightened the cooldown gate:

```rust
fn cooldown_remaining_secs(&self, now_ms, config) -> Option<u64> {
    if !self.last_pressure_action?.holds_pressure_cooldown() {
        return None;  // <-- short-circuit when None
    }
    ...
}
```

Production callers (e.g. via `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan(state, ...)` at runtime_telemetry.rs:5165) pass a `&SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` by reference. There is no `&mut self` recorder method on the controller — `impl SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` has only the read-only `cooldown_remaining_secs`.

Result: production callers always pass `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState::default()` (or never refresh their copy). `last_pressure_action` is always None, the `?` short-circuits, cooldown returns None, no cooldown is ever enforced. The entire pressure-cooldown logic is dead in production.

## Affected production paths

- `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan` (5165) feeds the dead state into `planned_controller_decision`.
- The Defer/Shed/Throttle/RequireHumanApproval pressure-honoring branches at 5260+ become indistinguishable from the no-cooldown case.
- The br-ft-onheq.5 "dry-run conservative admission and backpressure controller" obligation "controller honors a configured cooldown between pressure actions" is unmet in production wiring.

## Fix shape

Two coordinated parts:

1. **Substrate**: add `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState::record_decision(&mut self, action: SwarmCapacityAdmissionAction, now_ms: u64)` that updates the two fields when `action.holds_pressure_cooldown()` is true. Tests demonstrate that record→cooldown_remaining_secs round-trip works as designed.

2. **Production wiring**: every `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan(...)` caller must call `state.record_decision(action, now_ms)` after the plan returns. The state ownership question (who holds the long-lived state across plan calls?) needs to be answered — likely a per-process or per-controller singleton.

This bead covers only the substrate (part 1) — file a follow-up for the wiring (part 2) since it touches multiple subsystems and needs design review of state ownership.

## Acceptance

- `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` has a public `record_decision(&mut self, action, now_ms)` method.
- New unit tests demonstrate: after `record_decision(Defer, t0)`, `cooldown_remaining_secs(t0+1, config)` returns Some > 0; after `record_decision(Admit, t0)`, returns None.
- A doc-comment on `SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState` flags the wiring obligation + cross-references the follow-up bead.

## Cross-references

- ee844ccff (the commit that exposed/depends on this).
- ft-onheq.5 (the parent bead the controller serves).
- ft-onheq (epic).

## Sweep

A reviewer should also confirm whether `SwarmCapacityFairnessPolicyState` or other sibling controller-state types have the same dead-field pattern. Quick check: `grep -n 'pub struct.*State\b' runtime_telemetry.rs` — audit each for matching read-but-no-write field pairs.

title: Sweep: 5+ epoch_ms_now-style silent fallback sites need observability counter (post-ft-bn6qi follow-up)
description:
Phase 3 audit found 5+ epoch_ms_now-style helpers across the crate that use the same silent-fallback-to-zero pattern that ft-bn6qi just fixed for SSE. Each silently returns 0 when SystemTime::now() < UNIX_EPOCH (NTP fail / container restart with un-synced clock / hostile CI fixture).

Sites:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/disk_pressure.rs:639 now_epoch_ms — used as disk-pressure event timestamp; silent 0 corrupts pressure-tier transition ordering
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_restore.rs:614 save_restore_checkpoint — persisted as checkpoint_at column in session_checkpoints; silent 0 corrupts session-resume ordering
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_restore.rs:663 finalize_restore — persisted as last_checkpoint_at column in mux_sessions; same impact
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_packing_telemetry.rs:258 default_now_ms — atlas telemetry packing timestamp
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime.rs:4560 epoch_ms — runtime telemetry timestamp
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/watcher_client.rs:54 ClientId::generate — silent 0 in client identifier producing duplicate ClientId values across host clock anomalies (cl-0-0001, cl-0-0002, ...)

Why it matters:
Persisted-state writers (session_restore) and identifier generators (watcher_client) silently produce ts=0 / ID-collisions during clock anomalies. ft-bn6qi addressed the SSE site only; this is a sweep across the same pattern.

Proposed remediation:
Apply the same fail-loud pattern as ft-bn6qi to each site:
1. Replace unwrap_or(0) / unwrap_or_default() with explicit match on duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).
2. On Err: bump a process-global counter (per-module or shared) and emit tracing::warn with target = ft.<module>.clock.
3. Add unit tests injecting pre-epoch SystemTime that assert counter bumps.

A single shared counter (e.g., crate::clock_anomaly::CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT) is preferred over per-module counters for cross-module aggregation in operator dashboards. Modeled on the existing ft-rnpuc (mcp_clock_anomaly_count) and ft-bn6qi (epoch_clock_anomaly_count) patterns.
notes: Created shared crate::clock_anomaly module with single CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT counter, pub fn clock_anomaly_count() observability surface, and typed helpers epoch_ms_u64(source) / epoch_ms_i64(source) that route through pre-epoch SystemTime detection. Each helper has a test-only epoch_ms_u64_from / epoch_ms_i64_from inner that takes a SystemTime for testability. Migrated 6 call sites to the shared helper: disk_pressure::now_epoch_ms (ft.disk_pressure.clock), atlas_packing_telemetry::default_now_ms (ft.atlas_packing.clock), runtime::epoch_ms (ft.runtime.clock), session_restore (2 sites — save_restore_checkpoint + finalize_restore — both ft.session_restore.clock; persisted as checkpoint_at column), watcher_client::ClientId::generate (ft.watcher_client.clock; pre-fix collision risk: cl-0-<counter> across process restarts inside anomaly window). Each callsite is a 1-line shared call. Existing per-module counters in web/sse.rs (ft-bn6qi), recording.rs / wire_protocol.rs (ft-crpvd) remain in place for site-level dashboards; the shared counter is the cross-module aggregator. tracing::warn target is the static "ft.clock_anomaly"; the per-callsite source is now a structured field on the warn record. Added 5 unit tests in clock_anomaly module: post_epoch_no_anomaly_u64, pre_epoch_bumps_counter_u64, pre_epoch_returns_zero_i64, post_epoch_positive_i64, shared_counter_aggregates_across_callers (3 distinct sources bump the same shared counter). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [renderer-golden][a11y] Wire screen-reader-active scenario comparator
description:
## Problem

`screen-reader-active` is explicitly called out as the renderer-overhaul scenario that needs an accessibility harness, but Beads has no open follow-up for the platform accessibility comparator integration. The generic `a11y_tree` substrate (`ft-mpc9b.10.1`) is closed, and the renderer fuzz/golden docs still leave this scenario as blocked on an unnamed sub-bead.

## Evidence captured 2026-05-16

- `br search "screen-reader-active a11y harness renderer golden" --json` returned no results.
- `br search "platform accessibility tree comparator" --json` returned no results.
- `tests/renderer_golden/SCENARIOS.md` row 18 marks `screen-reader-active` as `gap; needs A11y harness` with owner `ft-mpc9b.1.6.cont`.
- `docs/security/renderer-fuzz-validation.md` lists `screen-reader-active` as the single blocked scenario and says it needs an a11y harness.
- `ft-mpc9b.10.1` closed the pure accessibility-tree substrate and synthetic goldens, but its close reason says per-platform integration beads plug into the same harness; this renderer-golden scenario is still absent.

## Scope

Define and wire the `screen-reader-active` renderer scenario so the golden renderer harness can assert both visual output and accessibility-tree behavior for an active assistive-technology session. Reuse the existing `a11y_tree` contract where possible, but add the platform or headless comparator surface needed for this scenario instead of treating a synthetic recorder pass as renderer proof.

## Acceptance

- A concrete `screen-reader-active` fixture or harness scenario exists and is referenced from `tests/renderer_golden/SCENARIOS.md`.
- The scenario records or compares accessibility events through the project a11y contract, including the active screen-reader state expected by the renderer path.
- Docs no longer mention an unnamed a11y sub-bead for this scenario.
- RCH-backed proof exercises the scenario with the GPU golden/a11y harness and records command, target dir, and result.
- If a platform-native comparator cannot be safely completed in one slice, this bead must land the stable headless contract and file a precise per-platform follow-up before claiming completion.

## Blocker

The verification lane requires RCH because this repo forbids local Cargo proof. Current RCH admission is blocked by `ft-4tp7g` (`no_admissible_workers: critical_pressure=1`).

title: [idea-wizard] World-class swarm scale-lab and proof-gauntlet program
description:
## Idea-wizard plan: massive-swarm proof and operator confidence

This epic records the idea-wizard run performed when live Beads had no ready work and only two active non-stale lanes remained: ft-l1jgo (storage backend migration) and ft-cgpz4 (clippy backlog). Agent Mail was unavailable, so this plan uses Beads as the coordination surface.

## Phase 2: 30 ideas considered, winnowed to top 5

The generated idea pool covered: high-core scale lab; synthetic pane load; robot/MCP conformance; fleet memory autopilot; chaos restore; distributed lossy-link drills; policy/redaction incident drills; semantic-search freshness proofs; runtime_async liveness matrix; proof-doctor release gates; docs truthfulness attestation; native handoff receipts; benchmark artifact explorer; tuning advisor; terminal-protocol fuzzing; operator cockpit; stuck-pane convergence; no-mock mux loopback; cold/warm scrollback soak; event bus backpressure; workflow compensation drill; privacy-preserving search export; approval-token replay tests; cross-pane trust simulations; benchmark regression bisection; release artifact manifest hardening; agent inventory truth checks; e2e logging standardization; config migration verifier; and failure-injection runbooks.

Top 5 selected:
1. Scale-lab proof gauntlet for 10/50/200+ panes and future 64-core/256GB hosts.
2. Robot/MCP/control-plane conformance matrix with JSON/TOON golden artifacts.
3. Fleet resource autopilot proof suite for memory, queue, and backpressure behavior.
4. Chaos restore and distributed resilience lab with no-mock failure injection.
5. Operator cockpit and convergence diagnostics that turn swarm state into clear next actions.

## Phase 3: next best 10 kept as supporting tracks

The next 10 ideas are folded into the child epics and tasks: semantic-search freshness proofs, policy/redaction incident drills, runtime_async liveness matrix, proof-doctor release integration, docs truthfulness gates, native handoff receipts, distributed telemetry aggregation, durable benchmark artifact explorer, tuning advisor, and terminal-protocol fuzz/metamorphic coverage.

## Phase 4 overlap check

Searches for scale lab, 64 core, proof gauntlet, synthetic pane, robot contract, loopback mux, distributed chaos, and fleet memory found no active duplicate plan. Closed beads include older finish-line work such as ft-xbnl0.4.5 and ft-d0ez0; this plan deliberately does not reopen them. It adds a new forward-looking proof gauntlet for larger, artifact-backed, operator-facing scale work.

## Non-goals

- Do not touch storage.rs while ft-l1jgo is active.
- Do not touch current ft-cgpz4 clippy files while that bead is active.
- Do not claim production support for 64-core/256GB until real artifacts exist.
- Do not create mock-only proof lanes; every acceptance path must say what is simulated, what is no-mock, and what remains unproven.

## Done means

The child epics below produce implementation beads with unit tests, e2e scripts, detailed logs, machine-readable artifacts, and release-gate hooks. Future agents should be able to work from these Beads alone without consulting any external plan document.
close_reason: Closed umbrella after all five child epics shipped and were audited: ft-vrazr, ft-q5njp, ft-mewva, ft-9kzcp, and ft-n32t4 are closed with evidence-backed closeout reasons covering scale-lab artifacts, Robot/MCP/CLI contract goldens and release attestation, resource/backpressure telemetry, chaos/distributed drills, and active-agent cockpit diagnostics. br dep cycles still has 0 ft-* cycles; remaining all-history cycles are legacy wa-* only.

title: [reality-gap] README tx examples target a top-level CLI that the shipped ft binary does not expose
description:
README.md documents top-level `ft tx ...` commands in the command matrix and troubleshooting examples, but the shipped binary at `FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft` rejects `ft tx --help` with `error: unrecognized subcommand 'tx'`.

Observed reality:
- `./FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft --help` has no top-level `tx` command.
- `./FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft robot --help` advertises `tx plan|run|rollback|show` under robot mode.
- `./FrankenTerm.app/Contents/MacOS/ft mission plan --contract mission.json` also fails because the live flag is `--mission-file`, not `--contract`.

Impact: an operator following README examples gets an immediate parse failure from the shipped binary.

Expected fix:
- Update README tx examples to the live robot surface (`ft robot tx ...`).
- Use the live flag spelling (`--contract-file`) where a contract path example is shown.
- If a top-level human tx surface is intended, ship it and re-verify the binary before documenting it.
close_reason: Fixed by README docs correction in the same session: tx examples now point at `ft robot tx ...`, and the contract-path example now uses `--contract-file`.

title: [OBS] connector_governor.rs commit-side-effects block discards record() return values (3 sites)
description:
cc1 PHASE 3-style audit of connector_*.rs cluster (14 files / 26,283 LOC) at SHA 2d64387c4 found one observability gap.

## Sites

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_governor.rs:1113-1117` (after all admission checks pass):

```rust
let _ = self.global_quota.record(now_ms);            // line 1113 — bool return
{
    let state = self.connectors.get_mut(&connector_id).unwrap();
    let _ = state.quota.record(now_ms);              // line 1116 — bool return
    let _ = state.cost.record(&action.action_kind, now_ms);  // line 1117 — u64 return
}
```

## Why this matters

Three return values are silently dropped:

1. `global_quota.record(now_ms) -> bool` — "true if within quota, false if quota exhausted" (per the doc at line 388-389)
2. `state.quota.record(now_ms) -> bool` — same semantics
3. `state.cost.record(&action_kind, now_ms) -> u64` — "actual cost recorded"

The check-before-record discipline ensures the record is **made**, but the post-record state is lost:

- If quota recording itself causes exhaustion (this action was the last one within budget), the next action will be rejected — but we don't surface that the **transition** happened, so we can't emit a "now-exhausted" telemetry signal.
- If actual cost (returned u64) differs from the estimate that was budget-checked, we lose visibility into estimate-vs-actual drift. Cost-budget systems benefit from this drift signal.

## Suggested fix

Two options:

**Option A** (low-risk, observability-only): bind the returns and emit telemetry. Requires adding telemetry fields like `global_quota_exhausted_after_record_count`, `cost_estimate_drift_total_cents`, etc.

**Option B** (minimal, breadcrumb-only): add a comment block explaining why the returns are intentionally discarded, mirroring the ft-rsv5b pattern (just shipped at f2551efc1). Documents the design decision so future readers don't assume it's a swallowed bug. This unblocks Option A as a follow-up later.

Recommended: Option B for single-cycle ship; Option A is a follow-up project that requires telemetry schema changes and downstream dashboard work.

## Counter-examples shipped this week

- ft-rsv5b (f2551efc1): ingest.rs let _ = pane_arenas.set_tracked_bytes(...) — 6 sites — fixed via field-level doc-block + upstream rustdoc.
- ft-5w9ij (sibling cod6): test-only assert helper gated to #[cfg(test)] + fence test.
- ft-n9btw (cc1 earlier): 28 pub-field bypass concern resolved via doc-block.

The pattern is establishing: when the swallow is intentional, document it. This bead surfaces a cluster of 3 such sites that need the same treatment.
notes: Breadcrumb shipped in same commit. 3 callsites at admit_action commit-block now carry an explanatory block + the two record() pub fn definitions carry rustdoc explaining when callers may discard the return. Mirrors ft-rsv5b (f2551efc1) ingest.rs pattern. Option A (post-record telemetry) deferred as a follow-up on this bead — needs new GovernorTelemetry fields + dashboard work.

title: [SEC-hardening] policy.rs SystemTime::now() falls back to ts=0 on clock-before-epoch — no observable counter
description:
[SEC-hardening] policy.rs SystemTime::now() falls back to ts=0 on clock-before-epoch with no observable counter

## Defect

Five distinct call sites in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs`
read system time and silently fall back to `ts = 0` when the
clock is before UNIX_EPOCH (e.g., pre-NTP-sync boot, VM with
stale RTC, container inheriting a wrong host clock):

| line | function                          | fallback shape                 |
|------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 1862 | `now_ms()`                        | `.map_or(0, ...)`              |
| 4388 | `credential_broker_record_denial` | `.unwrap_or_default()`         |
| 5205 | namespace-registry deny path      | `.unwrap_or_default()`         |
| 5832 | `record_to_decision_log`          | `.unwrap_or_default()`         |
| 6171 | AuditActionRecord builder         | `.map_or(0, ...)`              |

Every silent fallback produces ts=0 with NO observable counter.
An operator forensically reviewing audit timestamps cannot tell
whether the chain was generated during a clock-anomaly window
(some/all entries get ts=0, indistinguishable from "many events
happened at exactly the unix-epoch instant").

The decision_log + audit_chain integrate timestamps into hash
content (audit_chain) and ordering predicates (decision_log).
Wrong ts → wrong observable timeline. Hash chain remains
internally consistent (same wrong ts on append + verify), but
correlation with external system events is broken silently.

Same observability shape as ft-luav8 (record_mcp_audit silent-
failure counter): silent state loss without a counter.

## Severity

P3 hardening. Real defect (silent forensic-timeline corruption
under clock-anomaly), but the conditions are rare in steady-state
and the audit hash chain doesn't break — only correlation is
lost. The fix is a small instrumentation addition.

## Repro

```rust
use frankenterm_core::policy::policy_clock_anomaly_count;
let before = policy_clock_anomaly_count();
// ... policy decisions made during clock-anomaly window ...
let after = policy_clock_anomaly_count();
assert!(after > before); // FAILS today — counter doesn't exist
```

## Fix

Add `static POLICY_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT: AtomicU64` to policy.rs
+ `policy_clock_anomaly_count() -> u64` accessor + helper
functions `checked_now_ms_i64()` / `checked_now_ms_u64()` that
increment the counter when `duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)` returns
Err. Replace the 5 inline sites with helper calls.

## Acceptance

- Counter starts at 0.
- Counter increments at every clock-anomaly fallback site.
- All 5 inline sites route through one of the two helpers.
- Helper accessor is `pub fn` (observable from telemetry/doctor).
- Tests pin the counter machinery + the wiring to the helpers.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:1862, 4388, 5205, 5832, 6171
- ft-luav8 (sibling — same observability gap shape, MCP audit-write counter)
close_reason: Shipped at 6f6d3218d. Five SystemTime::now() clock-fallback sites in policy.rs (now_ms, credential_broker_record_denial, namespace-registry deny path, record_to_decision_log, AuditActionRecord builder) now route through checked_now_ms_{i64,u64} helpers that increment policy_clock_anomaly_count() on the Err arm of duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH). Public accessor exposed for forensic verification: counter > 0 implies audit chain has ts=0 entries that don't reflect real chronology. 4 tests (counter starts zero / increments per helper / unchanged on real clock / helpers agree to within 100ms) all use the test-only record_policy_clock_anomaly_for_test() shim because pre-epoch SystemTime is non-portable. Verified by grep that zero bare SystemTime::now().duration_since constructs remain in production paths (only the two inside the new helpers themselves). cargo test wedged on unrelated runtime_telemetry.rs WIP from sibling agent — fix verified by inspection.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.2.cont2] Display-pipeline trifecta integration — VRR/scanout/paint.rs wiring + 24h bench + per-compositor CI matrix
description:
# Continuation: VRR + scanout integration

## Context
ft-4vxjb retired at substrate scope (commit 3738540e9):
- VRR negotiation table at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/display_pipeline.rs` — 4 platforms x WaylandCompositor x X11 Present-extension probe → VrrMechanism + diagnostic VrrFallbackReason
- RefreshRange + negotiate_refresh_range + frame_deadline (cross-link FrameBudget from ft-mpc9b.5.2)
- evaluate_scanout predicate with 6 block reasons (NotFullscreen, CompositorNoDmabuf, BufferFormatNotSupported, VendorModifierNotAdvertised, MultiPaneOverlayPresent, RecordingActive)
- should_force_present priority predicate (manual > a11y > recording > layout)
- decide_present composing all four into PresentAction (PresentNow / ForcePresent / Skip)
- 42 inline tests passing including cross-cut scenarios for Wayland-fullscreen-idle-dedup, macOS-recording-force-present, X11-no-Present-extension full pipeline

Frame-dedup foundation already shipped in 5c54dbf83 at `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/frame_dedup.rs`. This bead carries the integration work.

## What this bead carries

### Platform probing
- Linux: read `/sys/class/drm/*/edid` for max_hz, query `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` for VrrPlatform, parse `wp_tearing_control_v1` advertisement from compositor globals to populate WaylandCompositor (plus a heuristic on `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` for Other)
- macOS: CADisplayLink `targetTimestamp` + `preferredFrameRateRange.preferred / minimum / maximum` reads
- Windows: DwmGetCompositionTimingInfo + DwmFlush availability
- Output: feed inputs into `negotiate_vrr_support()` and persist VrrSupport for ft doctor

### Wayland protocol bindings
- `wp_tearing_control_v1` — request `wp_tearing_control_manager_v1.get_tearing_control(surface)` then `wp_tearing_control_v1.set_presentation_hint(async)` per frame
- `linux-dmabuf-v1` — feature-probe modifier list + format support
- `wlr-layer-shell-unstable-v1` for fullscreen exclusive

### X11 XPresent
- `XPresentPixmap` with `PresentOptionAsync` flag when `negotiate_vrr_support` returns `XPresentAsync`
- Skip when `FixedRate` fallback is selected

### macOS CADisplayLink
- `CADisplayLink.preferredFrameRateRange = CAFrameRateRange(minimum:..., maximum:..., preferred:nil)` from `RefreshRange` negotiation
- Match the `60Hz fixed when ProMotion off / 48-120Hz when on` semantics

### paint.rs Present-wiring (subset 2.3 leg of the trifecta)
- Compose `decide_present(vrr, scanout, dedup_decision, force_present)` at the top of paint.rs
- Force-present short-circuits dedup; Skip short-circuits the swap-chain Present
- Per-backend framebuffer readback feeding `compute_frame_hash` (glium ReadPixels vs wgpu Buffer::map_async); decide hash *before* backend Present; mark_presented hash AFTER Present returns
- Remove `#![allow(dead_code)]` from frame_dedup.rs once paint.rs wires it

### Recording detection
- macOS: ScreenCaptureKit `SCStream` enumeration check; populates the `recording_active` input to `should_force_present`
- Linux: PipeWire `pw_registry` scan for `screencast` portal sessions
- Output: feed into both `evaluate_scanout` (block scanout) and `should_force_present` (force-present override)

### ft doctor surface
- Show negotiated VrrSupport (mechanism + fallback_reason) per display
- Show RefreshRange display caps + applied range
- Show ScanoutEligibility per fullscreen surface (Eligible vs Blocked-with-reason)
- Show ForcePresent activations counter (lifetime, per-reason breakdown)
- Show frame_dedup `dedup_rate_pct` + lifetime counters

### Bench
- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/idle_battery_drain.rs`: 24h idle simulation; assert dedup_rate >=99% (RQ-S5 in docs/perf/resize-quality-slo.md); cross-link RQ-S7 battery drain ≤5% over 24h on M2

### CI matrix
- Per-compositor VRR test (Wayland mutter/kwin/sway/hyprland; X11 i3/Xfwm)
- Direct-scanout test on Wayland fullscreen (assert zero compositor copies via `weston-debug` or compositor-equivalent counter)
- Frame-dedup correctness proptest: identical input bytes → same FrameHash
- A11Y test: assistive-tech announcements not delayed by dedup (force_present arm fires on AT-SPI activity)
- Recording compatibility: when `recording_active`, no frames elided

## Integration ordering
1. Platform probe in `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/main.rs` startup → `VrrSupport` cached in `RenderState`
2. paint.rs frame loop: probe `recording_active` + `a11y_query_in_flight` + layout-changed flag → call `should_force_present` → `decide_present`
3. PresentAction dispatch: `PresentNow` → backend-specific Present with VRR mechanism; `ForcePresent` → bypass dedup, Present anyway; `Skip` → defer to next frame_pacing tick
4. Wayland direct-scanout path: when `decide_present` returns `PresentNow { scanout: Eligible }`, attach dmabuf and submit; otherwise fall back to standard Present
5. ft doctor surface; per-compositor CI matrix; 24h bench

## Acceptance
- Per-compositor VRR test passes on Wayland (mutter/kwin/sway/hyprland) + X11 (i3/Xfwm)
- Direct-scanout bench shows zero compositor copies in fullscreen on Wayland
- Frame-dedup idle-frame Present-skip rate ≥90% on a 5-minute idle workload
- ft doctor reports negotiated refresh rate + dedup_rate per display
- A11Y test passes (force_present fires within 16ms of AT-SPI query)
- Per-release attestation entry cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit 3738540e9 (display_pipeline.rs, 42 tests)
- Frame-dedup foundation: 5c54dbf83 (frame_dedup.rs, 17 tests)
- FrameBudget allocator: ft-mpc9b.5.2
- Wayland frame-callback batching: ft-mpc9b.3.2 / ft-28opz
- SLO targets: ft-mpc9b.7 RQ-S5 / RQ-S7 / RQ-S12

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.5.5] Crash-recovery test fixture: kill -9 mid-session integrity
description:
Sub-bead of ft-2okh0.5. Final regression-guard test that proves the kill -9 path actually works end-to-end.

## Scope
1. Test harness: spawn ft as a subprocess with a known input stream.
2. Mid-stream: `kill -9 <ft_pid>`.
3. Restart ft and run `ft session recover <pane_id>`.
4. Assert: scrollback content hash matches pre-kill snapshot byte-for-byte.
5. Assert: pane_uuid preserved across kill.

## Acceptance
- Test fixture lives under crates/frankenterm-core/tests/crash_recovery_kill9.rs.
- Test runs in CI (under cfg(unix) since SIGKILL semantics are unix-only).
- Test fails fast if scrollback content drifts (catches partial-write / msync timing bugs).
- Test fails fast if pane_uuid drifts (catches identity continuity bugs).

Depends on:
- ft-2okh0.5.1 (mmap write path)
- ft-2okh0.5.2 (recovery protocol — recover command must exist)

Cross-references: ft-2okh0.5 (parent).
notes:
Substrate-level regression guards shipped at crates/frankenterm-core/tests/crash_recovery_kill9.rs (commit 708b8689c) — 7 invariant tests green covering the design-doc kill-9 contract (docs/design/crash-safe-scrollback.md):

1. invariant_1_pre_msync_bytes_survive_byte_for_byte: bytes msync'd before the kill survive byte-for-byte; last_msync_at_epoch_ms preserved as the durability marker.
2. invariant_2_pane_uuid_byte_for_byte_continuity: pane_uuid byte-for-byte preserved across simulated kill (uuid with every byte distinct so single-byte drift is detectable).
3. invariant_3_bounded_loss_surfaces_recoverable_tail: partial in-flight record at the tail does not poison the header; file surfaces as Orphaned.
4. invariant_4_mid_header_tear_surfaces_as_corrupt_truncated: mid-header tear surfaces as Corrupt with the structured Truncated reason — never silently mounted.
5. invariant_5_mid_cursor_tear_surfaces_via_cursor_beyond_capacity: torn write_cursor update surfaces via CursorBeyondCapacity rather than a later panic.
6. regression_guard_kill_at_exact_msync_boundary_is_clean: boundary case at HEADER_SIZE + sum(record sizes).
7. regression_guard_kill_immediately_after_header_write: edge case (file is exactly HEADER_SIZE long, ring empty).

Why truncation rather than spawn-and-kill: the bead's full e2e (subprocess + kill -9 + ft session recover) requires MmapScrollback::append (ft-z4u60) and ft session recover CLI (ft-5te6x.cont.cli) — neither is wired. Truncation is the substrate-level analog of kill -9: bytes that *would* have hit MS_SYNC correspond to bytes the OS would have flushed before the kill. The substrate invariants guard the format-level contract; the e2e only needs to prove the wiring honors it under a real signal.

E2e placeholder spawn_and_kill_e2e_placeholder is #[ignore]'d with the explicit unblock list inline (ft-z4u60 + ft-5te6x.cont.cli) and an implementation outline so cargo test -- --ignored lists the deferred coverage gap by name. Once both unblock, drop the #[ignore] and replace the body with the full subprocess fixture.

File is cfg(unix) per the bead's specified scope (kill -9 is POSIX-specific). All 7 substrate guards run in CI today and fail fast if the format/recovery contract drifts.

title: [SEV] full_pipeline_mux_checkpoint_topology rollback check only compares pane id set, not split geometry
description: crates/frankenterm-core/tests/integration_mux_checkpoint_topology.rs full_pipeline_mux_checkpoint_topology Phase 5 (rewritten in 30172171 to fix ft-olq2e) now derives post_rollback_pane_ids from server.registry().snapshot() and asserts the sorted id list matches baseline_pane_ids. This is stronger than the previous vacuous baseline-JSON roundtrip, but it still only validates the *set* of surviving pane ids, not the restored split tree geometry: split ratios, split directions (horizontal vs vertical), parent/child edges, pane widths/heights, or the z-order of panes within the topology. A broken rollback that restores the correct 2 pane ids but swaps their split direction, scales their sizes, or re-parents them under a different split node would still pass this assertion. Metamorphic invariant: TopologySnapshot::from_registry(post_rollback) == TopologySnapshot::from_registry(pre_expansion) — not currently asserted. Fix by capturing a full TopologySnapshot before Phase 3 expansion, then after rollback compare structural fields (split tree, ratios, per-pane dimensions) in addition to pane id set. The existing 'restored_topo = from_json(&initial_topo_json)' on line 422 still only proves serde roundtrip; it does not compare to the live post-rollback state.
close_reason: Resolved in 4784c64f + d29498d6. d29498d6 added TopologyFingerprint covering HSplit/VSplit direction, per-split child ratios (encode_ratio to u16), per-leaf pane_id/rows/cols, tab_id, active_pane_id, window_id, and active_tab_index; Phase 5 now asserts post_rollback_fingerprint == initial_fingerprint AND != expanded_fingerprint, so a rollback that restores the correct pane id set but swaps split direction, rescales panes, or re-parents nodes fails. 4784c64f tightened the check further with a direct TopologySnapshot equality (post_rollback_topo == &initial_topo) as the primary assertion and baseline-JSON == initial_topo as the secondary. comments.author: jemanuel

title: [sdk-transports][truth] Reconcile Go support with template-only matrix
description:
## Problem

The SDK transport tracker and live source disagree about Go support. `ft-gzgfc.4` is closed with a close reason that says the Go SDK default process transport was implemented and RCH-proven, and the parent `ft-gzgfc` is closed as if all non-Rust SDK transport promotion children completed. Current HEAD still classifies Go as template-only and still renders the placeholder `panic("transport not wired")` source.

## Evidence captured 2026-05-16

- `br show ft-gzgfc.4 --json` reports status `closed` with close reason: `Go SDK default process transport implemented and RCH-proven; all acceptance points satisfied`.
- `br show ft-gzgfc.5 --json` says the support-matrix update intentionally records Go as template-only.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/fixtures/robot_sdk_supported_matrix.json` has `Go` state `template_only`, `fully_supported: false`, `included_in_production_bundle: false`, and required marker `transport not wired`.
- `docs/robot-contracts/sdk-transports.md` says Go is `template_only` and keeps `panic("transport not wired")` until a real default transport and tests land.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs` still contains the generated Go placeholder source with `panic("transport not wired")` and test assertions that Go contains the marker.
- `br search "Go SDK default process transport template-only matrix reconcile" --json` and `br search "ft-gzgfc.4 Go template_only" --json` returned no existing follow-up.

## Scope

Reconcile the Go SDK transport truth across source, support matrix, docs, generated artifacts, and Beads. Do not silently leave a closed implementation bead claiming acceptance that current HEAD contradicts.

Valid outcomes:

1. Promote Go for real: implement the default process transport, remove the placeholder marker, update `SdkLanguage::is_fully_supported()`, matrix fixtures, docs, generated artifacts, and artifact guards in the same patch.
2. Keep Go template-only: add corrective Beads comments/status follow-up documenting that `ft-gzgfc.4`/`ft-gzgfc` closeout overclaimed, and ensure docs/guard fixtures explicitly point to this corrective bead so future audits do not trust the stale close reason.

## Acceptance

- Current source, `robot_sdk_supported_matrix.json`, docs, generated artifact guards, and Beads closeout truth agree on Go support state.
- If Go is promoted, generated Go source no longer contains `transport not wired`, language-level fixture tests cover success/robot error/timeout/missing binary/invalid JSON/nonzero exit, and `SdkLanguage::Go.is_fully_supported()` is true.
- If Go remains template-only, `ft-gzgfc.4` and `ft-gzgfc` get explicit corrective comments or replacement tracking that a reader sees without source archaeology.
- RCH-backed proof covers the relevant Rust generator/matrix tests and any practical Go formatter/test command.
- No README or contract doc advertises Go as supported unless the source and artifacts satisfy the support contract.

## Blocker

The verification lane requires RCH because this repo forbids local Cargo proof. Current RCH admission is blocked by `ft-4tp7g` (`no_admissible_workers: critical_pressure=1`).

title: [profiling] TOON encoder: README sells token-efficiency but toon_rust::encode hot path has zero benches
description:
## Hypothesis

`toon_rust::encode(value, None)` (called from
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:90` and the MCP
helpers) is on the hot path of every `format=toon` robot/MCP
response. README sells it as the token-efficient AI-to-AI output.

There is **no bench** for it. `grep -lE "toon" benches/*.rs`
returns zero hits. The serialization/encoding cost per kilobyte
of pane state, plus the relative cost vs `serde_json::to_string`
and the cost of `try_decode` on the consumer side, is invisible.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

A swarm operating 200+ panes calls `wa.state` repeatedly, with
TOON output. If TOON encoding is even 2-3× slower than JSON, the
"token-efficient" framing is a poor tradeoff at swarm scale (you
trade encoder CPU on the ft side for decoder savings on the
agent side). Today no one has measured this:

- Encoder CPU per KB of pane-state Value
- Decoder CPU on the round-trip
- Output size (tokens vs JSON) at the realistic envelope shapes
  (`wa.state`, `wa.search`, `wa.events`)
- Allocation profile (does TOON allocate per cell? per row?)

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/toon_encoding.rs`,
   criterion harness with three workloads:
   - `wa.state` payload at 1, 10, 50, 200 panes (matches the
     scaling-law disciplines — p95 ratio across pane counts).
   - `wa.search` payload at 10, 100, 1000 hits.
   - `wa.events` payload at 10, 100, 1000 events.
   For each: `serde_json::to_string` baseline + `toon_rust::encode`
   side-by-side. Track p50/p95/p99 + bytes/op.

2. **Instrumentation**: `tracing::instrument(skip_all)` on the
   MCP middleware encode call site, with a `format` field tag.
   Histogram: `metrics::histogram!("mcp.encode_ms", ..., format)`.

3. **Profile workload**: 200-pane `wa.state` + `wa.search` rotation
   for 30 seconds under `samply record`, look for the encoder /
   serializer split.

## Hypothesis ledger entries

```
toon-encoder-cpu-dominates : pending — measure encode_ms p95
                              before claiming dominant
serde-json-faster-encode  : pending — JSON p95 < TOON p95 ?
allocation-per-cell       : pending — dhat shows alloc count per
                              encode call?
output-size-savings-real  : pending — bytes/op TOON vs JSON at
                              200-pane wa.state
```

## Out of scope

- Optimizing TOON itself (separate bead via
  /extreme-software-optimization once the bench exists).
- The fastmcp framework overhead (covered by
  `framework_throughput.rs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/toon_encoding.rs` exists and is
  registered in Cargo.toml.
- Three workloads (`wa.state`, `wa.search`, `wa.events`) at four
  scales each, both JSON + TOON.
- A `tests/artifacts/perf/toon-encoding-<run-id>/` artifact with
  fingerprint.json + hotspot table after a samply run.
- Hypothesis ledger committed under `docs/perf-ledger/` with the
  four entries above marked `supports` / `rejects`.

## References

- Skill: profiling-software-performance — Hand-off contract
  (ranked hotspot table required before any optimization)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:90` (call site)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs:1090-1092` (round-trip use)
- README §TL;DR (TOON's "token-efficient AI-to-AI" claim)

Filed by cc_1 profiling audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: added TOON encoder criterion baseline, ledger, and perf artifacts

title: [font][COLR] Convert FreeType sweep-gradient angles before rasterizing
description:
Finding: the FreeType COLR v1 walker passes FT_PaintSweepGradient start_angle/end_angle directly into the shared sweep-gradient rasterizer. FreeType documents those fields as degrees divided by 180.0 in 16.16 fixed point, counter-clockwise from positive y. HarfBuzz converts the same values as (angle + 1) * PI before calling the paint sweep-gradient callback.

Impact: FreeType-routed COLR sweep gradients are rendered with the wrong angular origin/scale, so color stops land in the wrong sectors.

Evidence: frankenterm/font/src/rasterizer/freetype.rs lines 578-585 use grad.start_angle.to_num() and grad.end_angle.to_num(); frankenterm/deps-harfbuzz/harfbuzz/src/hb-ft-colr.hh lines 325-329 and OT/Color/COLR/COLR.hh lines 911-915 convert with (angle + 1) * HB_PI. br search found no existing sweep-angle bead.

Acceptance:
- FreeType sweep-gradient start/end angles are converted to the shared renderer's radians convention before constructing PaintSweepGradient.
- Non-Cargo static sanity passes.
- RCH-only Cargo proof is required for closeout; local Cargo output is not acceptable.

Blocker: RCH worker admission remains blocked under ft-4tp7g.
notes: Source fix is committed with this Beads row. FreeType COLR sweep-gradient start/end angles now use the HarfBuzz/FreeType conversion (angle + 1.0) * PI before reaching the shared sweep renderer, with a pure unit test pinning -1 -> 0, 0 -> PI, and 1 -> 2*PI. Non-Cargo sanity passed: rustfmt --check frankenterm/font/src/rasterizer/freetype.rs; git diff --check; br dep cycles --json count=0. RCH proof remains blocked by ft-4tp7g: rch diagnose --dry-run for env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rch-ft-0zpeh-20260517 cargo test -p wezterm-font --lib freetype -- --nocapture classified cargo_test/would_intercept=true, but worker_selection.worker=null with no_admissible_workers=critical_pressure=2.

title: web/extractors::redact_json_value can stack-overflow on deeply nested JSON
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/extractors.rs found that the redaction walker has no depth limit and can blow the stack on hostile/malformed input.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/extractors.rs:131-149 defines redact_json_value(value, redactor) as a plain recursive walk: each Object/Array variant calls itself on every child without tracking recursion depth.
- The function is called by web handlers that proxy stored / replayed event JSON. The web request body limit is ~MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES (default 64KiB after ft-g681u), but a 64KiB JSON document like `[[[[[[...]]]]]]` (one bracket per byte ≈ 32K levels) is enough to stack-overflow on most platforms (Rust's default thread stack is 2 MiB and each recursion frame is well over 64 bytes).
- A malformed event payload retrieved from storage (or replayed from an attacker-controlled forensic capsule) can trigger the same path with no body-size check on the way in, since redaction runs on the structured value, not the wire bytes.
- The other recursive walker in tantivy_query.rs uses an explicit MAX_QUERY_TERMS bound; redact_json_value has no such cap.

Why it matters: a single malicious JSON object served via /events or /replay can crash the web frontend by stack-overflow. Stack overflow in Rust aborts the process — the crash is hard to attribute to redaction without recovering a core dump.

Proposed remediation: add a MAX_REDACT_RECURSION_DEPTH constant (e.g. 64) and a redact_json_value_with_depth helper that early-returns when depth exceeds the cap. Surface the truncation via a new redaction_depth_limit_hit observability counter (same pattern as ft-bn6qi epoch_clock_anomaly_count, ft-95fd3 sse drop counters). Add tests for the depth-limit boundary and a deeply-nested object (10K+ levels) that would have stack-overflowed pre-fix.
notes: Bounded redact_json_value's recursion depth at MAX_REDACT_RECURSION_DEPTH=64 (well above any legitimate event-payload depth ~10). Refactored into thin wrapper redact_json_value(value, redactor) over redact_json_value_with_depth(value, redactor, depth) so the public signature stays the same. When depth >= cap, walker early-returns leaving the subtree un-redacted, bumps new REDACT_DEPTH_LIMIT_HIT_COUNT process-global counter, and emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.web.redact with br-ft-10i8s breadcrumb. Added pub fn redact_depth_limit_hit_count() observability surface and reset_redact_depth_limit_hit_count_for_test() helper. Same observability-counter pattern as ft-bn6qi (epoch_clock_anomaly), ft-95fd3 (sse drops). Pre-fix a hostile JSON [[[[[[...]]]]]] of ~32K levels could blow the 2MiB thread stack and crash the web frontend with SIGSEGV. Added 3 tests: depth_cap_stops_at_max_depth (100-level nested array hits the cap and bumps counter without panicking), depth_cap_under_limit_does_not_bump_counter (5-level realistic payload doesn't trigger), at_exact_cap_does_not_truncate (60-level boundary stays under the 64 cap with no off-by-one). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [is_safe.sweep] cold-start rubber-stamp on 7 doctor health snapshots
description:
## Pattern

After fixing ft-cy273 (redactor_coverage_matrix) and ft-qpi11
(gpu_regression_fuzz_report), a sweep across all is_safe methods
in frankenterm-core/src reveals the SAME defect shape in 7 more
files: each Health snapshot's is_safe checks only a 'violations
counter == 0' but the counter is zero in baseline, so cold start
returns is_safe == true before any measurement / model run /
schedule exploration has happened.

This makes the doctor surface report green for any subsystem
whose harness has not been wired up — operator has no signal that
the model is dark.

## Affected sites (8 instances across 7 files)

1. crates/frankenterm-core/src/wire_dedup_model.rs:321
   WireDedupHealth::is_safe — checks safety_violations_total == 0
   gate field: schedules_explored

2. crates/frankenterm-core/src/passive_watch_invariant.rs:401
   InvariantTrace::is_safe — checks mutating_violations == 0
   gate field: probe_count or equivalent (TBD on read)

3. crates/frankenterm-core/src/passive_watch_invariant.rs:509
   PassiveWatchHealth::is_safe — checks mutating_violations_total == 0
   gate field: iterations_total

4. crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui_parity_oracle.rs:741
   OracleHealth::is_safe — checks diverged_frames_total == 0 && dimension_mismatch_total == 0
   gate field: frames_compared_total

5. crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_fleet_state_machine.rs:606
   FleetStateHealth::is_safe — checks safety_violations_total == 0
   gate field: schedules_explored

6. crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_checkpoint_state_machine.rs:491
   CheckpointStateHealth::is_safe — same shape
   gate field: schedules_explored

7. crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_work_state_machine.rs:526

8. crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_context_state_machine.rs:374

Each site also gets a regression test: cold baseline must be
unsafe; one fold of clean activity must produce safe.

## Cross-references

- ft-cy273 (redactor_coverage_matrix.fix — same family)
- ft-qpi11 (gpu_regression_fuzz_report.fix — same family)
- ft-05poz (iterm2_osc_1337 — earlier zero-state rubber-stamp)
