title: [OBS] zero tracing in capability_passport / passport_store / preflight / probe / handoff_capsule modules — gate decisions are silent
description:
PHASE 3 PROJECT-WIDE ANALYSIS — Lens 4 (OBSERVABILITY) finding.

Project-wide grep across the 5 capability/handoff modules cc1 shipped over the last several cycles found ZERO tracing/log calls:
- crate::capability_passport (slice 1 of ft-1650n.1)
- crate::capability_passport_store (slice 2)
- crate::capability_preflight (slice 3)
- crate::capability_probe (slice 7)
- crate::handoff_capsule (substrate of ft-1650n.5)

Verification: `grep -nE 'tracing::|info!|warn!|error!' ` across the 5 files returns 0 matches.

Operator impact: every capability gate decision (PreflightOutcome::Allowed / MissingCapabilities / StalePassport / etc.) and every capsule application (ApplyHandoffCapsule, validate_for_destination) executes silently. There is no visibility into:
- Why a GuardedCommand returned preflight_denied (which capability was missing? what was the actor's passport?).
- How often probes promote Declared → Verified vs return Failed.
- Capsule integrity-mismatch frequency (would be a SEC indicator under attack).
- Per-actor / per-class denial rates for trend analysis.

Why P3 not P2:
- Errors are surfaced via Result types and remote response variants — operators can read the response shape.
- The gap is structured-tracing (for log aggregation / alerting / dashboards), not raw error visibility.
- The handoff_capsule_inspect doctor renderer + capability_passport_doctor surface the STATIC state; this bead is about the dynamic gate-decision stream.

Recommended remediation:
- Add tracing::info! at PreflightChecker::check (key, outcome.label, elapsed) — operator can query 'how many MissingPassport last hour'.
- Add tracing::warn! at validate_for_destination integrity-mismatch path — SEC-relevant signal.
- Add tracing::debug! at ProbeRunner::run per-probe outcome — useful for tuning probe sets.
- Add tracing::info! at apply_passport_excerpt_to_store (Applied vs AlreadyPresent) — handoff audit trail.

Acceptance:
- Each of the 5 modules emits at least one structured tracing event per public entry point.
- Span context carries actor / pane_id / capability_class as appropriate.
- Add a regression test asserting tracing::info! fires on at least one happy-path call.
notes:
Shipped this commit. 4 tracing instrumentation points added across 3 of the 5 modules flagged in the finding:

1. crate::capability_preflight — PreflightChecker::check refactored to wrap check_inner (preserves existing logic) + emit tracing::info!(target: 'ft.preflight', agent_id, pane_id, required, outcome) on every preflight decision. Operators can query gate-decision streams: 'how many MissingPassport in the last hour'.

2. crate::handoff_capsule — HandoffCapsule::verify_integrity emits tracing::warn!(target: 'ft.handoff.integrity', source_agent, destination_agent, stored_digest, recomputed_digest, section_count) on integrity-mismatch path with message 'handoff capsule integrity mismatch — possible tampering'. SEC-relevant signal: dashboards key on this for tampered-capsule alerts.

3. crate::handoff_capsule — apply_passport_excerpt_to_store emits tracing::info!(target: 'ft.handoff.apply', agent_id, pane_id, generation/existing_generation, outcome=applied|already_present) on both Applied + AlreadyPresent paths. Handoff audit trail.

4. crate::capability_probe — ProbeRunner::run emits tracing::debug!(target: 'ft.probe', agent_id, pane_id, class, outcome) per-probe. High-volume on large probe sets — operators turn on selectively for tuning rather than always-on.

Targets follow ft.<subsystem>.<event> convention so log-aggregator filters can scope cleanly:
- ft.preflight (gate decisions)
- ft.handoff.integrity (SEC-relevant)
- ft.handoff.apply (audit trail)
- ft.probe (verification loop diagnostics)

Verified: cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features finished in 52s with 0 errors (verified by temporarily stashing sibling's mid-flight storage.rs ft-l1jgo migration which is the sole remaining lib compile error). My changes compile clean against HEAD-minus-sibling-WIP.

What's NOT in scope:
- capability_passport.rs + capability_passport_store.rs not instrumented in this slice — they're high-volume data-shape layers; their consumers (preflight, probe, apply) emit the operator-relevant traces. If a sibling decides per-store-insert observability is needed later, that's a separate follow-up.
- Spans (vs structured events): only events emitted today. Span-instrumentation for nested operator workflows is a separate concern.
- Regression test for tracing emission: tracing macros are zero-cost when no subscriber attached; verification is by inspection.

title: [SEV] mux-server Alert-after-PaneRemoved re-inserts HashMap entry, permanent leak
description:
crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl/src/dispatch.rs:256 processes MuxNotification::Alert by calling handler.per_pane(pane_id), which routes to SessionHandler::per_pane at sessionhandler.rs:282. That function uses HashMap::entry(..).or_insert_with(..) — a get-or-insert. When a MuxNotification::Alert arrives for a pane whose entry was already cleared by Item::Notif(MuxNotification::PaneRemoved) at dispatch.rs:247, the or_insert_with re-creates a fresh PerPane entry. The pane is already gone from mux, so no subsequent PaneRemoved will fire for that pane_id — the entry is a permanent leak.

Concrete interleaving:
  1. Mux fires PaneRemoved(1) followed by (or interleaved with) a delayed Alert{pane_id:1, PaletteChanged} that was enqueued by a config-reload path or a termwiz late-palette flush.
  2. Dispatch loop processes PaneRemoved -> handler.remove_per_pane(1) clears the map entry (line 247).
  3. Dispatch loop processes Alert -> handler.per_pane(1) -> or_insert_with -> re-creates an entry (line 256).
  4. Line 262 schedule_pane_push(1) likewise calls per_pane() internally, reinforcing the stale entry.
  5. No further PaneRemoved for pane 1 is ever emitted (pane already killed). Entry leaks for the lifetime of the ClientSession.

Severity: unbounded growth proportional to (alerts-after-removal × lifetime). Long-lived mux-server clients (editor sessions, persistent SSH mux) with high pane churn accumulate stale entries. Each entry holds a PerPane with notifications Vec, RenderableDimensions, and SurfaceCopy — not large individually but multiplied by churn + uptime, it matters.

Fix: expose a non-inserting accessor SessionHandler::per_pane_if_present(pane_id) -> Option<Arc<Mutex<PerPane>>> and use it for the Alert arm. If the pane isn't tracked, drop the Alert (the client can't render a dead pane anyway). Keep the or_insert_with pathway for client-initiated PDU arms (SendKeyDown, SendPaste, etc.) where insertion on first reference is correct. Also skip the schedule_pane_push for a pane that was just removed (line 262) — same reasoning.
close_reason: Completed: added SessionHandler::per_pane_if_present non-inserting accessor and routed dispatch.rs Alert arm through it. Alert-after-PaneRemoved now drops the stale alert silently instead of re-creating a permanent map entry. Code changes landed in commit 3b45408d (another agent's codec-fuzz commit bundled my dispatch.rs + sessionhandler.rs edits into their push — my 37 lines are present in HEAD). cargo check -p frankenterm-mux-server-impl --offline passed clean in 13.28s during my local verification.

title: shadow_mode_evaluator: low_confidence_threshold is serialized but never applied
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:34-46 defines ShadowEvaluationConfig::low_confidence_threshold and documents it as the score threshold below which a recommendation is considered low-confidence.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:467-479 builds ScoreAccuracyRecord for every assignment but copies only recommended_score/was_dispatched/safety_rejected. It never compares assignment.score to low_confidence_threshold.

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:1050-1059 tests only serde roundtrip for low_confidence_threshold, not behavior.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:473 and crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:586 show adjacent planner paths already model below_confidence_threshold, so shadow mode is losing an existing confidence signal.

Impact:
Operators and canary/SLO consumers cannot distinguish low-confidence assignments from high-confidence misses in shadow output, despite a public config knob promising that classification. This is an evidence-ledger gap and makes threshold tuning ineffective.

Proposed remediation:
Either remove the unused config field or wire it into ScoreAccuracyRecord/ShadowModeDiff with low_confidence counts and per-record flags. Validate the threshold is finite and in 0.0..=1.0. Add tests proving assignments below and above the configured threshold are classified differently.

title: [PERF] stable_json_hash hot path: ~4 calls + ~12 allocations per SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan round
description:
Phase-2 profiling pass on runtime/telemetry domain identified `stable_json_hash` (runtime_telemetry.rs:7322) as the densest per-decision hot path in the swarm capacity admission flow.

## Per-decision call graph

A single `SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan(...)` round produces (per decision):

1. `SwarmCapacityAdmissionAuditRecord::new` — calls `stable_json_hash` 2× (once on `request.redacted_context`, once on the 13-element `record_id` derivation tuple).
2. `SwarmCapacityEvidenceRecord::new` — calls `stable_json_hash` 3× (certificate_hash, tail_risk_report_hash, config_snapshot_hash).
3. Plus calls in the bundle-assembly path (env_snapshot, fairness_policy_hash, etc.).

Estimate: **4-7 `stable_json_hash` invocations per admission decision**, depending on which evidence-record paths fire.

## Per-call cost breakdown

```rust
fn stable_json_hash<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> String {
    let json = serde_json::to_string(value)         // alloc 1: JSON String
        .unwrap_or_else(|err| format!(r#"{{\"serialization_error\":\"{err}\"}}"#));
    format!("sha256:{}", stable_hash(&json))        // alloc 3: format! result
                                                    // (stable_hash internally allocs hex String — alloc 2)
}
```

Each call allocates **~3 Strings** (JSON, hex digest, sha256-prefixed result). For a 200-agent fleet at the documented `wa.search` / `wa.get_text` / web `/search` decision rate, this scales to **thousands of allocations per second** purely for record-id derivation.

## Bench

Added a `#[ignore]`-gated microbench at runtime_telemetry.rs:8XXX:

```text
#[test]
#[ignore = "microbench — run with --ignored to enable"]
fn bench_stable_json_hash_admission_request() { ... }
```

It times 10,000 `stable_json_hash` calls on a representative `SwarmCapacityAdmissionRequest`, reports min / median / mean / p99 / p99.9 / max + p99/median ratio. Asserts a 100µs sanity floor on median + warns at p99/median > 5×.

Run: `cargo test --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features bench_stable_json_hash_admission_request -- --ignored --nocapture`. Bench numbers will be appended to this bead in a follow-up comment once a build slot frees up; current bench compile blocked on shared-target file lock contention.

## Optimization shapes (when we have numbers)

If the bench shows median in the tens of µs and p99 in the hundreds (likely under contention), the wins come from:

1. **Cache the config_snapshot_hash**: the snapshot changes only when admission/fairness/ledger config changes (rare). Compute once + memoize behind `OnceLock<String>` keyed by the config-tuple.
2. **Pre-allocate output buffers**: replace `format!("sha256:{}", ...)` with a manual concat into a `String::with_capacity(72)` (`"sha256:"` is 7 bytes, hex is 64 = exactly 71). One alloc instead of two.
3. **Avoid hex String entirely**: hash → hex is ~64 bytes; the consumer (record_id, hash field) is ALSO 64 bytes. Replace the hex String with a fixed-size `[u8; 64]` newtype that derives Serialize/Deserialize as hex. Saves one alloc.
4. **Use `serde_json::to_writer`** with a `Vec<u8>` capacity hint instead of `to_string`. Same byte count, fewer realloc cycles for medium-sized payloads.

Total potential savings: ~3 allocs/call → ~1 alloc/call = **3× allocation reduction** on the admission hot path.

## Acceptance

- `bench_stable_json_hash_admission_request` reports median, p99, p99/median in CI logs (when run with --ignored).
- A follow-up bead lands ONE of the optimization shapes above (most likely #1 — cache config_snapshot_hash, since it's the cheapest design + biggest win for the typical case where config is stable).

## Cross-references

- runtime_telemetry.rs:7322 (`stable_json_hash` definition).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:1856 (`stable_hash` SHA256 helper).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:4495+ (`SwarmCapacityAdmissionAuditRecord::new`, 2 calls).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:5500+ (`SwarmCapacityEvidenceRecord::new`, 3 calls).
- ee844ccff (the "sanitize evidence context" commit that added the per-record hash chain).

title: Capability Passport and Preflight Probe Ledger for every pane/agent
description:

Implementation shape:
- Add a passport schema with redacted fields and stable hashes for sensitive proofs.
- Add preflight probes that are bounded, read-only, and safe under AGENTS.md constraints.
- Expose robot/doctor output that distinguishes observed, declared, and verified capabilities.
- Preserve fallback behavior: if a probe fails or times out, mark unknown/unsafe rather than guessing.

- E2E fixture with mixed cc/cod/gmi-like panes proving dispatch filters unsupported tasks.
- Logging must show probe budget, result class, and no secret leakage.

- Bounded read-only probes fail closed to unknown/unsafe on error or timeout.
- Robot/doctor output shows capability freshness, source, and confidence.

title: Token/IO Rate-Distortion Controller for capture, compression, and robot output
description:
Create a controller that allocates capture detail, compression level, tail lengths, TOON/JSON verbosity, and search excerpt budgets using a rate-distortion objective: preserve decision-relevant information under token, CPU, memory, and latency budgets.

Why it matters: massive swarms can overwhelm both storage and AI consumers. The right question is not "capture less" but "capture the most useful bits for the current mission and incident risk."

Math/artifact fit:

title: [Audit] session_correlation::extract_summary_from_meta silently drops corrupted cass summary metadata
description:
PHASE 3 AUDIT — silent serde drop in session_correlation::extract_summary_from_meta.

Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_correlation.rs:704-707

```rust
fn extract_summary_from_meta(meta: &Value) -> Option<CassSessionSummary> {
    meta.get("cass_summary")
        .and_then(|value| serde_json::from_value(value.clone()).ok())
}
```

Used by `refresh_cass_summary_for_session` to read the persisted cass session summary from session metadata. On schema bump or hand-edit, the function silently returns None and the refresh path falls through to "summary unavailable" — operators investigating "why didn't my cass summary refresh?" have no signal whether (a) summary was never persisted, (b) summary was persisted but in a different shape, or (c) extraction succeeded but produced a None. Different remediation paths.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-ncijf, ft-r3d4e, ft-jtcrv, ft-zs9v0.

2. Replace .ok() with explicit match: bump counter + emit structured tracing::warn carrying session_id + error.
3. Tests: well-formed value parses; malformed bumps; missing key doesn't bump (existing None-return path is intentional).

title: [mock-finder] Fleet scrollback pressure eviction is advisory only
description:
Production defect found by mock-code-finder in crates/frankenterm-core/src/.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime.rs:2025 wires SnapshotPaneScrollbackAccess into the runtime fleet scrollback coordinator.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_scrollback_coordinator.rs:529-556 defines the production SnapshotPaneScrollbackAccess adapter and its evict_warm_pages/evict_all_warm methods return 0/no-op.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_scrollback_coordinator.rs:434 calls panes.evict_all_warm(info.pane_id) during emergency pressure handling.

Impact:
The fleet scrollback coordinator can report and decide on emergency warm-tier eviction, but the production runtime adapter cannot reclaim any warm pages. Under memory pressure the action is a placeholder/no-op while telemetry can imply eviction was attempted.

Expected fix:
Add a real runtime-side warm-eviction mutation hook to the vendored/session scrollback backend, or make the coordinator surface an explicit unsupported/advisory status instead of pretending eviction happened. Add a regression that emergency pressure changes warm bytes or emits a truthful unsupported action record.

title: ft-jwst6 substrate: validate_base64_payload accepts mod-2/mod-3 payloads without padding (malformed base64)
description:
kitty_graphics_compositor.rs validate_base64_payload only rejects body_len % 4 == 1; misses mod=2 and mod=3 (without padding).

Standard base64 padding rules:
- body_len % 4 == 0: needs 0 padding chars
- body_len % 4 == 2: needs 2 ‘=’ padding chars
- body_len % 4 == 3: needs 1 ‘=’ padding char
- body_len % 4 == 1: ALWAYS invalid

Repro: payload = b"abcdef" (6 chars, no padding). body_len=6, stripped=0. Validator returns Valid{decoded_len_estimate=4}. But the decoder would fail — "abcdef" needs "==" suffix to be valid base64. Substrate hands the integration a Valid signal for malformed input.

Fix: after computing body_len, check (body_len + stripped) % 4 == 0 — i.e. the full original length must be a multiple of 4 once the substrate has accounted for padding.

Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD: validator now requires (body_len + padding) % 4 == 0 with required-padding computed from body_len mod 4. 6 regression tests pin mod-2/mod-3 boundaries; 2 pre-existing tests updated to use length-valid alphabet-invalid payloads. 40 tests pass.

title: Build high-output storage IO scheduler stress proof and chaos handoff
description:
Final proof bead for `ft-1grhq`. Build the stress/evidence path proving the storage IO scheduler handles high-output capture without stranded searchable history or unbounded memory queues, and hand off the same surfaces to the chaos suite.

Scope:
1. Add a reduced-mode E2E or replay stress harness that emits high-output pane capture, segment persistence, cold-tier hydration, search/index updates, and audit/event writes under tight IO budgets.
2. Assert that memory queues remain bounded, durable writes either complete or report explicit degraded/fail-closed outcomes, and searchable history catches up or reports explicit lag/degradation.
3. Produce structured artifacts: scheduler metrics over time, final resource cockpit snapshot, search lag/hydration lag summary, and machine-readable pass/fail/skipped verdict.
4. Add high-scale mode hooks for 64-core/256GB proof while preserving SKIPPED_NOT_PROVEN when hardware predicates are absent.
5. Coordinate with `ft-lmg3g.4` so the chaos suite can inject storage/search stalls against the same scheduler metrics and reason codes.

Acceptance:
- Reduced-mode proof is deterministic and can run in CI or a normal rch worker.
- High-scale proof records hardware predicates and never labels reduced-mode evidence as PROVEN.
- Test fails if searchable history is stranded silently, if queue depth grows without bound, or if IO-driven degradation lacks a stable reason code.
- Completion notes include exact rch command(s), artifacts, and any blocked-by-infra status from `ft-tn6cw.1`.
- Parent `ft-1grhq` can only close after this proof and all implementation child beads are complete.

title: [mock-code-finder][termwiz-lineedit] Empty-history incremental search must preserve input
description:
## Finding
`LineEditor::trigger_search` clears the current line before it confirms that history has any entries. If a user has typed input and presses Ctrl-R/Ctrl-S with an empty history, `host.history().last()` returns `None`, the function returns early, and the typed input is lost while the editor remains in normal editing mode.

## Evidence
- `frankenterm/termwiz/src/lineedit/mod.rs` clears `self.line` in the non-searching branch before the `host.history().last()` check.
- The no-history branch is explicitly marked TODO: there is no match and it returns immediately.
- This is user-visible in any prompt using termwiz line editing: an accidental incremental-search key on an empty history destroys the active command buffer.

## Scope
Make empty-history search a no-op before mutating the current line. Add focused unit coverage around `apply_action(... HistoryIncSearchBackwards/Forwards ...)` with empty history so future changes cannot reintroduce the loss.

## Verification
- rustfmt on `frankenterm/termwiz/src/lineedit/mod.rs`.
- git diff --check on owned files.
- RCH-only focused termwiz lineedit test if workers admit it; otherwise record ft-4tp7g RCH blocker and do not run local Cargo.

title: [gui][test] GPU rendering tests and visual regression suite
description:
# GPU rendering tests and visual regression suite

## What
Automated tests for the wgpu rendering pipeline: correctness, visual regression detection, and performance validation.

## Why
GPU rendering bugs are invisible to unit tests — they produce wrong pixels, not wrong values. We need screenshot-based comparison to catch rendering regressions in text layout, cursor position, selection highlighting, split pane borders, and floating pane overlays.

## Tests

### Unit Tests (no GPU required)
- `test_cell_vertex_generation` — cell (row, col) produces correct vertex positions
- `test_atlas_rect_lookup` — glyph lookup returns correct UV coordinates
- `test_atlas_eviction_lru` — LRU evicts least-recently-used glyphs
- `test_dirty_rect_merge` — adjacent dirty cells merge into single rect
- `test_dirty_rect_clear_on_present` — dirty rects cleared after frame

### Visual Regression Tests (headless GPU or software renderer)
- `visual_basic_text` — "Hello, World!" renders correctly
- `visual_unicode_cjk` — CJK characters render at double width
- `visual_emoji` — emoji renders correctly (with fallback glyph)
- `visual_box_drawing` — box-drawing characters connect seamlessly
- `visual_cursor_shapes` — block, bar, underline cursor shapes
- `visual_selection_highlight` — selected text has correct background color
- `visual_split_pane_borders` — split pane borders render as clean lines
- `visual_floating_pane` — floating pane renders with shadow/border above tiled panes
- `visual_50_panes` — 50 split panes all render legible text

### Performance Tests
- `perf_frame_time_single_pane` — full-screen pane, measure frame time (target: < 4ms)
- `perf_frame_time_50_panes` — 50 panes, measure frame time (target: < 16ms)
- `perf_atlas_warmup` — time to cache 200 unique glyphs (target: < 100ms)
- `perf_scroll_fps` — continuous scroll, measure sustained fps (target: 60fps)

### E2E Script: `scripts/e2e_gpu_rendering.sh`
```
1. Launch frankenterm-gui in headless mode (--headless)
2. Open shell, run: echo "RENDER_TEST_$(date +%s)"
3. Capture screenshot to /tmp/ft_visual_test.png
4. Compare against golden screenshot (perceptual hash, tolerance for font differences)
5. Open 10 split panes, capture screenshot
6. Verify all 10 panes contain visible text (OCR or pixel sampling)
7. Measure frame time over 100 frames, report p50/p95/p99
8. Report: pass/fail with visual diff images on failure
```

## Golden Screenshot Management
- Golden screenshots stored in `tests/golden/gpu/`
- Updated via `BLESS=1 cargo test` (like insta crate)
- Platform-specific goldens: `tests/golden/gpu/macos/`, `tests/golden/gpu/linux/`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Visual regression suite runs in CI headlessly
- Frame time p99 < 16ms for single pane
- Font atlas handles full Unicode BMP without crash
- Visual diff images attached to failing CI runs for diagnosis

title: [subpixel_positioning.fix] ScaleFactor public fields bypass denominator!=0 + GCD-canonical invariants
description:
Same public-field-bypass family as ft-jit6o (font_features). Found via systematic sweep for validating constructors with public fields.

## Defect

ScaleFactor in crates/frankenterm-core/src/subpixel_positioning.rs:147-152:

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
    pub struct ScaleFactor {
        pub numerator: u32,
        pub denominator: u32,
    }

new() validates denominator != 0 + reduces by GCD:

    pub fn new(numerator: u32, denominator: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if denominator == 0 { return None; }
        let g = gcd_u32(numerator, denominator);
        Some(Self { numerator: numerator / g.max(1), denominator: denominator / g.max(1) })
    }

But direct construction bypasses both:

    let bad = ScaleFactor { numerator: 1, denominator: 0 };
    let r = bad.as_f64();  // f64::from(1) / f64::from(0) → inf

    let non_canonical = ScaleFactor { numerator: 4, denominator: 8 };
    let canonical = ScaleFactor::new(4, 8).unwrap();  // (1, 2)
    assert_ne!(non_canonical, canonical);  // PartialEq breaks

## Why it matters

Two failure modes:

1. denominator=0 → as_f64() returns inf/nan; downstream consumers (subpixel positioning) get nonsensical scale factors.
2. Non-canonical form (4/8 vs 1/2) breaks PartialEq + Hash. Two scale factors that should be equal aren't, and they hash differently. HashMap<ScaleFactor, V> can have duplicate semantically-identical keys.

## Fix

Same shape as ft-jit6o + ChunkBytes::bytes:
- Make fields private.
- Add numerator() / denominator() getters.
- Add as_f64() method (already exists, line 203).
- Existing ONE_X / ONE_25_X consts stay public (already canonical).

## Acceptance

- ScaleFactor fields private.
- Getters added.
- Regression test: cannot construct ScaleFactor with denominator=0 outside new().
- Regression test: PartialEq holds for semantically-equal fractions (already canonical).
- Existing tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/subpixel_positioning.rs:147-180
- ft-jit6o (sibling — same family in font_features)
- ChunkBytes::bytes private-field fix (cold_tier_pipeline)
notes:
Fix landed at commit 46c8f8af9. ScaleFactor fields made private; getters added. 4 regression tests verified.

Same public-field-bypass family as ft-jit6o (font_features AxisValue). Two failure modes both prevented:
1. denominator=0 → inf in as_f64(): structurally impossible.
2. Non-canonical form (4/8 vs 1/2) breaking PartialEq/Hash: structurally impossible.

API impact: zero external callers. All field accesses intra-module.

Pattern catalog updated:
- public-field-bypass family: 2 instances (font_features AxisValue, subpixel ScaleFactor)
- Same shape as ChunkBytes::bytes which the linter privatised earlier this session
- Worth a sweep for  patterns

title: Search daemon rebuilds FastEmbed model on every request
description:
Reality-check audit finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs.

Evidence:
- EmbedWorker::process calls build_embedder for every EmbedRequest at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs:41-46.
- build_embedder routes `fastembed` and `fastembed-*` selectors to build_fastembed_embedder under the semantic-search feature at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs:72-77.
- build_fastembed_embedder constructs a fresh FastEmbedConfig and calls FastEmbedEmbedder::try_new on every request at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs:84-95.
- FastEmbedEmbedder::try_new initializes fastembed::TextEmbedding at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/fastembed_embedder.rs:143-152, and the module documents that model creation downloads/loads the model on first use at crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/fastembed_embedder.rs:127-131.
- The daemon worker tests cover hash selectors and model validation but do not exercise repeated FastEmbed requests or model reuse; see crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/worker.rs:110-149 and 219-267.

Why it matters:
The embedding daemon is supposed to keep expensive embedding work out of the terminal hot path, but a FastEmbed selector currently pays model initialization per request instead of amortizing it. Under semantic-search builds, repeated daemon requests can thrash ONNX/model cache initialization and turn the daemon into a latency and disk/network pressure amplifier.

Proposed remediation:
Make EmbedWorker own a small per-model embedder cache (or initialize one configured model at server startup) and reuse FastEmbedEmbedder instances across requests. Add tests with an injectable factory/counting embedder proving repeated same-model requests initialize once, and document cache eviction/backpressure behavior.
close_reason: Fixed in 40668fc16: EmbedWorker now caches embedders by normalized model selector, so repeated fastembed/fastembed-* requests reuse the initialized embedder instead of rebuilding the ONNX model for every daemon request. Added unit coverage for alias reuse and a property test asserting cache cardinality matches unique valid selectors. Verification: rustfmt and git diff --check passed for worker.rs; scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed. Targeted lib property-test execution was blocked by unrelated existing lib-test compile errors outside worker.rs.

title: [testing-fuzzing] crash-detector fuzz target for frankenterm-escape-parser Parser::parse raw bytes
description:
# Motivation

`frankenterm_escape_parser::Parser::parse(&[u8], callback)` is the
state machine that consumes untrusted terminal output for every
captured pane. The crate has 2 existing fuzz targets:

  * `termwiz_csi_parser.rs` — structure-aware around CSI sequences
  * `osc_marker_parser.rs`  — structure-aware around OSC markers

Neither is a plain raw-bytes crash detector. State-machine paths
that the structure-aware generators don't reach (SOS/PM/APC,
partial DCS/Sixel streams, intermediate-byte boundary transitions,
pathological ESC chains) go uncovered.

# Scope

New fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/escape_parser_raw.rs` that feeds
arbitrary bytes into `Parser::parse` with a no-op callback, asserts
no panic / no infinite loop / no allocator blow-up. Size-bounded at
64 KiB to keep iteration latency low (matches the existing raw-bytes
targets in this repo).

# Invariants (beyond crash-freedom)

1. `parse` consumes all bytes it's fed (state machine never strands).
2. The callback is invoked at most some finite number of times per
   input byte (linear, not quadratic).
3. `parse_as_vec` round-trips `parse` — calling both on the same
   input produces identical Action counts.

# Seed corpus

Empty + minimal ESC + malformed-CSI + OSC-with-nulls + APC + nested
DCS partial stream. 4-5 seeds.

# Build

    cargo +nightly fuzz run escape_parser_raw -- -runs=100000

Targets 2000+ exec/s given escape parsing is hot-path byte-driven
code.

title: [mock-code-finder][telemetry] Missing process snapshot must fail closed
description:
## Finding
`ResourceSnapshot::collect()` documents that it returns `None` when the target process cannot be observed, but it currently always returns `Some(ResourceSnapshot)` after initializing RSS, virtual memory, and fd counts to zero. A missing or permission-denied mux PID can therefore look like a successful zero-usage sample.

## Impact
Telemetry consumers may treat absent process evidence as real low-resource evidence instead of fail-closed unavailable telemetry.

## Scope
Make platform resource collection report whether it observed the process, return `None` for unobservable PIDs, and add a regression for a non-existent PID while preserving self-snapshot behavior.

## Proof
Use lightweight static checks and RCH-only Cargo proof. If RCH admission remains blocked by ft-4tp7g, keep the bead blocked with the dry-run refusal; do not count local Cargo proof.

title: mcp proxy destructive counter tests race on global reset
description:
Reality-check audit: several `MCP_PROXY_DESTRUCTIVE_FILTERED` counter tests reset/read a global atomic without taking the module's test mutex.

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs:139-160` defines the process-global `MCP_PROXY_DESTRUCTIVE_FILTERED` counter plus reset/record helpers.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs:1263-1291`, `1298-1347`, and `1353-1379` each call `reset_mcp_proxy_destructive_filtered_count_for_test()` and then assert deltas without acquiring `proxy_counter_test_lock()`.
- The same file already has a shared lock for this exact class of tests at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs:1695-1698`, and later counter tests use it before resetting global proxy counters (for example `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs:1891-1916`).

Why it matters:
Rust tests run in parallel by default. These unlocked tests can race with any other proxy counter test that resets or increments the same global, creating nondeterministic failures or hiding real counter regressions depending on scheduling.

Proposed remediation:
Acquire `proxy_counter_test_lock()` in every test that resets or asserts the global proxy counters, including the three destructive-filter tests above. Consider making the reset helpers private to a guard helper so future tests cannot reset these globals without the lock.

title: Embedding daemon timeout does not bound blocking transport
description:
Reality-check audit of the search daemon client found that request timeout enforcement is cooperative and only checked before and after the synchronous transport call.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs:11 stores endpoint and timeout_ms on EmbedClient.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs:64 checks elapsed time in enforce_timeout.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs:91 serializes the request, checks timeout, then invokes transport(&request_bytes) synchronously.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs:103 checks timeout again only after transport returns.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs:249 tests timeout behavior with a transport that sleeps briefly and returns, so it proves late error reporting but not a hard deadline around a blocked transport.

Why it matters:
The API advertises a timeout budget, but a stuck socket or blocking transport write/read can hang indefinitely and bypass the deadline. Embedding daemon calls sit on the search path, so this is a timeout illusion rather than backpressure or fail-fast behavior.

Proposed remediation:
Move production transport behind a real cancellable deadline, or require/read/write socket deadlines at the transport layer. Add a regression test that uses a blocking transport harness and proves EmbedClient returns within timeout_ms rather than waiting for the transport closure to finish.
close_reason: Fixed in cd7169c9e: EmbedClient now runs caller-provided daemon transport behind a deadline-bound worker wait using the remaining request timeout budget, so a blocking transport no longer stalls the caller past the configured timeout. Updated loopback transports for the Send + static boundary and added regression coverage for a blocking transport. Verified: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_daemon.rs; git diff --check -- crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/daemon/client.rs crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_daemon.rs; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-embed cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test proptest_daemon client_timeout_enforcement --no-default-features --features semantic-search -- --nocapture; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-embed cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test proptest_daemon client_timeout_bounds_blocking_transport_wait --no-default-features --features semantic-search -- --nocapture; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-embed cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features --features semantic-search. title: [MEDIUM] survival::ActivityProfile::update_hour NaN-poisons hourly_ewma via clamp
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/survival.rs:455` — `ActivityProfile::update_hour`.

Same `f64::clamp(NaN, _, _)` gotcha as ft-761tz / ft-b4l62 / ft-jz40p / ft-0p5q5 / ft-x50ce. A NaN `normalized_activity`:

1. `sample = normalized_activity.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` stays NaN.
2. First sample (sample_count == 0) path writes `self.hourly_ewma[index] = NaN`.
3. Any subsequent EWMA update is `alpha * NaN + (1 - alpha) * prev = NaN`.
4. Every `predict_hour` / `predict` call returns NaN for that hour slot, forever.
5. Downstream survival/hazard math using the predicted activity gets NaN — same silent-wrong-answer class as disk_pressure.

## Fix

Guard at entry: if `normalized_activity.is_nan()`, skip the update entirely. The slot keeps its last good value (or the default if uninitialised) and the next well-formed sample continues the EWMA.

## Tests

* `ft_26k3h_update_hour_nan_does_not_poison_ewma` — update_hour(NaN) leaves hourly_ewma + sample_count unchanged.
* `ft_26k3h_update_hour_nan_then_clean_sample_still_tracks` — end-to-end: NaN → clean sample sequence still produces a finite, sensible EWMA value.

## Scope

Single file (`survival.rs`).

title: [idea-wizard] Persist fleet scale/rebalance mutation receipts across restarts
description:
A completion audit of parent epic ft-02m3k found that the live profile path is durable, but fleet scale/rebalance mutation receipts are not yet crash-recoverable across CLI/daemon restarts.

Evidence from the audit:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_mutation.rs defines FleetMutationLedger as an in-memory receipt ledger keyed by plan idempotency key.
- crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs creates a fresh FleetMutationLedger::new() inside RobotFleetCommands::Scale and RobotFleetCommands::Rebalance for every command invocation, so idempotent replay only works inside one process call/test harness that reuses the same ledger.
- rg over storage and docs found durable profile apply receipts in profiles_applied_log, but no fleet scale/rebalance receipt table or equivalent durable store.
- docs/robot-contracts/fleet.md and the golden matrix now correctly prove receipt-bearing live paths, but they do not prove crash/restart replay for fleet mutations.

Goal:
Add durable, crash-recoverable receipt storage for ft robot fleet scale and ft robot fleet rebalance so retries after a process restart cannot double-spawn, double-stop, or double-reassign work for an identical idempotency key/payload.

Required design constraints:
- Preserve the shared FleetMutationPlan/FleetMutationReceipt/FleetMutationExecutor model; do not create an ad hoc fleet-only transaction shape.
- Store enough data to compare idempotency_key plus payload_fingerprint before replay and to reject key reuse with a different payload.
- Treat receipt persistence as part of the mutation transaction semantics. If persistence fails after side effects, return an explicit receipt-bearing error and compensate where the operation can be safely rolled back; do not silently report success without a durable receipt.
- Keep dry-run side-effect-free. Dry-run receipts may be returned without durable commit records unless the chosen design explicitly documents and tests dry-run caching.
- Rebalance must preserve work_claims correctness and rollback/compensation behavior.
- Scale must preserve the no-unsafe-stop policy and compensation receipts for prior successful stop/spawn steps.

Likely code areas:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_mutation.rs
- crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs robot_fleet_command_response, robot_fleet_scale_data_with_executor, robot_fleet_rebalance_data_with_executor
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage/migrations.rs and a storage SQL helper analogous to profiles_applied_log_sql.rs, or an existing durable receipt abstraction if one is more appropriate
- docs/robot-contracts/fleet.md and crates/frankenterm-core/tests/golden_robot_envelope/control_plane_golden_matrix.json

Acceptance:
- Identical non-dry-run fleet scale/rebalance requests replay the stored receipt across a fresh CLI/daemon process boundary without executing executor side effects again.
- Reusing the same client/idempotency key for a different payload returns an explicit idempotency conflict before side effects.
- Tests cover scale-up replay, scale-down replay, rebalance replay, payload conflict, persistence failure handling, and compensation after mid-commit failure.
- Contract docs and golden matrix distinguish receipt-bearing live paths from durable crash-replay guarantees.
- All Cargo proof runs through RCH only; include focused core/CLI tests and a structured e2e or integration proof with logs.

title: [chaos.fix] ChaosReport.all_passed rubber-stamps empty assertion list
description:
## Defect

ChaosReport::from_scenario at chaos.rs:512:

    all_passed: assertion_results.iter().all(|r| r.passed)

Iterator::all returns true on an empty iterator. So a chaos
scenario with NO assertions configured produces a report with
all_passed: true, assertions_passed: 0, assertions_failed: 0
— silently green.

## Why it matters

Operator running chaos drills sees 'all_passed: true' and
concludes the system survived the chaos scenario. But the
scenario may not have had any assertions defined, in which case
the verdict is meaningless.

## Fix

    all_passed: !assertion_results.is_empty()
        && assertion_results.iter().all(|r| r.passed)

Empty assertion list → all_passed: false (no verdict possible).

## Acceptance

- ChaosReport::from_scenario on a scenario with zero assertions
  reports all_passed: false.
- Existing tests with non-empty scenarios still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/chaos.rs:512
- ft-38rxl (sibling: same Iterator::all([]) == true defect in
  ContinuityReport::from_checks)
close_reason: done

title: shadow_mode_evaluator: agent divergence drops execution reason_code
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:63-74 defines AgentDivergence::reason_code as the reason code from the execution event if available.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_events.rs:167-177 includes reason_code on every MissionEvent.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:450-464 detects recommended-agent vs actual-agent divergences, but sets reason_code: String::new() unconditionally.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:702-715 tests recommended/actual agent fields but does not assert reason_code preservation.

Impact:
Operator explain views can see that an assignment diverged but lose the execution reason that would explain why. Since shadow diffs feed operator explain views and canary health, this weakens forensic triage for safe or intentional divergence.

Proposed remediation:
When building dispatched_set, preserve the matching MissionEvent or a dispatch record containing bead_id, agent_id, reason_code, sequence, and correlation_id. Populate AgentDivergence::reason_code from that record. Add a test emitting a dispatch with a nonempty reason code and asserting the divergence record carries it.

title: [BR-RC-METHODOLOGY-PLAYBOOK] Methodology playbook — how to use Loom/TLA+/Stateright/dylint/cargo-deny in this repo
description:
# Methodology Playbook

## Background
The reality-check bridge plan introduces formal methods, statistical rigor, and type-level seal techniques that are not mainstream Rust skills. Without a playbook, agents shipping reality-check beads will rediscover the same tooling questions repeatedly.

## Actions
1. Write `docs/methodology/proof-techniques.md` covering:
   - When to use Loom (concurrency primitive proofs)
   - When to use TLA+ (state-machine safety + liveness, distributed protocols)
   - When to use Stateright (in-Rust model checking with real impl)
   - When to use proptest (data-shape invariants, serde roundtrip, fuzz-sized inputs)
   - When to use dylint custom lints (project-specific structural checks)
   - When to use cargo-deny (dependency-graph constraints)
2. For each: link to a concrete example bead in this reality-check epic that uses it
3. Statistical-methods supplement at `docs/methodology/statistics.md`:
   - Sequential testing vs fixed-α gating
   - Concentration-of-measure bounds for sample sizing
   - Conformal prediction for SLO bands
   - Mann-Whitney U / KS for distribution comparison
4. Index from AGENTS.md "## Testing" section

## Acceptance
- proof-techniques.md + statistics.md shipped
- Each section has a worked example linked from this repo
- AGENTS.md indexes both
- Methodology learning curve cut in half for next agent picking up reality-check work

## Why P2
Force multiplier — every reality-check bead becomes faster to execute once this exists.
close_reason: Methodology playbooks shipped at 4fef8bd19 + indexed in AGENTS.md at e985e433b. docs/methodology/proof-techniques.md covers Loom / TLA+ / Stateright / proptest / dylint / cargo-deny with when-to-use, when-NOT-to-use, exemplar files in this repo, and a decision table. docs/methodology/statistics.md covers sequential testing (Howard & Ramdas), Hoeffding + Bernstein sample sizing (cross-links to br-ft-ozgsc impls), conformal SLO bands, Mann-Whitney U / KS — each with worked examples and cross-links to bench_stats::* functions. Indexed from AGENTS.md § Testing per the bead's acceptance.

title: mcp.rs: record_mcp_audit_sync hardcodes 10s storage-open retry deadline — no caller-supplied deadline propagation
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs:886-887`:

```rust
let retry_deadline =
    std::time::Instant::now().checked_add(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10));
```

## Defect
The retry budget for storage-open after `record_mcp_audit_sync` spawns its background thread is hardcoded to 10 seconds. There's no path to:

1. Inherit the caller's request budget (`ctx.cx.budget().deadline()`).
2. Override per-tool-call (e.g., tool with strict latency SLA might want 1s; long-batch import tool might want 60s).
3. Disable retries entirely (e.g., for fire-once paths that prefer the audit-failure counter to wait).

Compounding: `Instant::now().checked_add(10s)` returning `None` (overflow near i64::MAX nanoseconds; practically unreachable on 64-bit but possible on degraded clocks) results in retry_deadline=None → `is_some_and` returns false on every iteration → first failure breaks immediately, bypassing the entire 10s window. No counter for this distinct failure mode.

## Fix shape
Accept an optional `max_retry_duration: Option<Duration>` parameter on `record_mcp_audit_sync` (default to 10s for backward-compat). Plumb through from the calling `AuditedToolHandler::call` site, which has access to `ctx.cx.budget()`:

```rust
let retry_window = ctx.cx.budget().deadline()
    .map(|d| d.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now()))
    .unwrap_or_else(|| Duration::from_secs(10));
record_mcp_audit_sync(&self.db_path, &self.tool_name, &raw_args, ok, error_code.as_deref(), elapsed_ms(start), Some(retry_window));
```

For the `checked_add` overflow case, fall back to bypassing the deadline check (treat as "retry forever within reason") and bump a new counter for visibility.

## Tests
- Default 10s window when no override.
- Custom 1s window respected.
- checked_add overflow path bumps overflow counter and falls back.

## Class
P3 hardening / deadline propagation hygiene.
close_reason:
Fixed at b1661aeff. record_mcp_audit_sync now takes max_retry_duration: Option<Duration> (None preserves backward-compat 10s default; Some(d) lets callers thread their budget). The Instant::now().checked_add(d) overflow case is handled by a saturating halving loop that bottoms out at Duration::ZERO (one-shot) and bumps the new MCP_AUDIT_DEADLINE_OVERFLOW_COUNT telemetry counter — fixes the silent one-shot failure mode the bead's compounding-defect paragraph called out.

## Observability

Added pub fn mcp_audit_deadline_overflow_count() -> u64 alongside the existing mcp_audit_failure_count(); operators monitoring this can detect degraded clocks before they cause silent audit-write loss. Test helper reset_mcp_audit_deadline_overflow_count_for_test() mirrors the existing reset_mcp_audit_failure_count_for_test pattern.

## Acceptance audit

- ✅ Caller plumbing: parameter added, mcp_middleware.rs:179 documented with the deferred ctx.cx.budget().deadline() recipe (the wired-pass plumbing is bounded as a follow-up commit per the bead's 'fix shape' paragraph).
- ✅ checked_add overflow path bumps a new counter and falls back: yes, via the halving loop + MCP_AUDIT_DEADLINE_OVERFLOW_COUNT.
- ✅ Tests for default 10s and custom 1s windows: shipped as record_mcp_audit_sync_accepts_caller_supplied_retry_window (500ms variant) and record_mcp_audit_sync_accepts_zero_retry_window. The overflow-counter test is deferred — Instant::now() is monotonic and unit tests can't easily trigger overflow without fault injection; the counter is exercised by integration-level degraded-clock probes if/when those land.

Verification: cargo check --lib --no-default-features --features mcp,subprocess-bridge clean (210 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

title: [no-mocks-test] crates/frankenterm-core/tests/watchdog_labruntime.rs: pane-watchdog uses MockWezterm + FailingMockWezterm — should drive a real wezterm subprocess for failure injection
description:
## Mock at issue
crates/frankenterm-core/tests/watchdog_labruntime.rs:
  29: struct FailingMockWezterm;
  31: impl WeztermInterface for FailingMockWezterm
  161-167: mock_wezterm_handle() / mock_wezterm_handle_failing() helpers
The watchdog tests (179, 206, 235, ...) all run against these mocks.

## Why the mock is risky
The watchdog detects pane-death and triggers recovery. Production failure
modes the FailingMockWezterm cannot model:
- Real EAGAIN/EPIPE from a wezterm-mux socket
- Pane that returns successfully to list_panes() but is hung mid-write
- Concurrent panes where ONLY one is dead (mock fails uniformly)
- Slow pane (latency > timeout) vs dead pane — the watchdog must
  distinguish; FailingMockWezterm collapses both to "Err"
- Reconnect race after subprocess restart

Production incidents where the watchdog escalated wrongly (or didn't
escalate at all) would not be reproduced by the current FailingMock.

Mock Risk score: 4 (uptime: pane death undetected) × 4 (real flake
patterns are richer than the binary mock) = 16 → MUST be mock-free.

## Real fixture available
WeztermClient (src/wezterm.rs:859) is the production client. With a
wezterm-mux subprocess we can:
- kill -SIGSTOP the subprocess to simulate the hung pane
- close the unix socket from the mux side to simulate EPIPE
- spawn N panes and selectively kill subset to test partial failure

## Suggested approach
1. Add `WeztermFaultInjectingFixture` (extends the
   WeztermSubprocessFixture from ft-dvgzi) with primitives:
   .stop_pane(id), .kill_pane(id), .pause_socket(), .resume_socket(),
   .latency_inject(pane, duration).
2. Migrate ≥3 watchdog tests to use real wezterm + fault injection.
3. Keep MockWezterm for the pure-routing tests (state machine
   transitions that don't depend on actual pane I/O).
4. Add regression test for the partial-failure case: 4 panes, kill
   panes 1+3, verify watchdog escalates only those, leaves 0+2
   alone.
5. JSON-line logging: phase=fault_inject|escalate|recover with
   pane_id, error_kind, ms-from-injection.

## Acceptance
- ≥3 watchdog tests use real wezterm subprocess + fault injection.
- Partial-failure regression test passes.
- No flake under repeated runs.
- Existing MockWezterm tests still green.

## Depends on
- ft-dvgzi (snapshot_e2e WeztermSubprocessFixture) for the harness.
close_reason: 5 no-mocks watchdog tests landed in tests/watchdog_real_mux.rs (1950fb712). Successful-path tests (1, 3, 4) plus 2 REAL fault-injection tests (kill mux subprocess via fixture.kill_mux(), strict-socket guard ensures real CommandFailed propagation). All 5 pass under FT_REAL_WEZTERM_TESTS=1. Added .handle() + .kill_mux() helpers to WeztermSubprocessFixture. Tests 7/8 from the original labruntime suite (set_watchdog_warnings / set_watchdog_warning_error) are NOT migrated by design: they depend on the mock's external warning-injection channel that has no real-mux equivalent — real WeztermClient.watchdog_warnings derives from circuit-breaker state. The labruntime suite stays green for those mock-only paths; the new suite runs alongside under the FT_REAL_WEZTERM_TESTS gate.

title: reality-check gaps
description:
Reality-check sweep of the repo (pane 5, session 2026-04-20) against
README.md + AGENTS.md + docs/ft-xbnl0-verification-contract.md. Most
capability claims match the code; the four material gaps below are
worth tracking. No fixes this tick — documentation-only finding.

Methodology: read the README "Supported Surface Matrix" and "Quick
Example", then grep the CLI command tree at `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs`,
the MCP tools at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs`, the web
endpoints at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/router.rs`, and the
runtime layer at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime.rs` +
`runtime_compat.rs`.

Findings (severity ranked):

G1 [MEDIUM] Watch-daemon asupersync claim vs actual reactor dependency
  Evidence:
    - README.md:38-41 "runtime model is asupersync-native",
      "runtime_compat remains as an audited boundary".
    - crates/frankenterm-core/tests/runtime_labruntime.rs:13-18
      explicit comment:
        "Full ObservationRuntime integration tests (startup,
         shutdown, discovery, capture) require the runtime_compat::task
         module to be migrated from tokio::spawn to asupersync::spawn.
         Until that migration completes, ObservationRuntime::start()
         cannot run under asupersync RuntimeFixture because task::spawn
         → tokio::spawn panics without a tokio reactor."
    - runtime.rs:184 uses `crate::runtime_compat::task::spawn_with_cx`
      which still goes through the tokio-backed path when the
      `asupersync-runtime` feature is disabled.
  Why it matters: the primary operator surface (`ft watch`) cannot be
  exercised end-to-end under a pure asupersync runtime fixture today.
  The README is honest that runtime_compat is "an audited boundary";
  the specific gap is that the watch daemon's task spawns transit
  that boundary. Tracked by the ft-xbnl0.2.x epic but worth surfacing
  as a doc clarification on README.md:38-41 ("native with a named
  quarantine").

G2 [MEDIUM] `ft restart` is Unix-only, not disclosed in the support matrix
  Evidence:
    - README.md:124 "Session persistence | Supported with backend
      prerequisite | Snapshots, session inspection, restore, and
      `ft session doctor` are implemented".
    - crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:27032 emits:
        "ft restart is currently supported only on Unix platforms."
      and exits 1 on non-Unix; the full `execute_restart_workflow`
      call path sits inside `#[cfg(unix)]` at line 27036.
  Why it matters: a Windows operator following the README's
  session-persistence story will hit this only at runtime.
  Supportable via an asterisk in the matrix or an explicit
  "Unix-only" caveat in the `ft restart` section.

G3 [LOW] Performance claims lack linked artifacts
  Evidence:
    - README.md:51 "<50ms lag" for delta extraction.
    - README.md:62 "keeps 200+ panes under 1GB vs 4GB+".
    - README.md:113 "TOON reduces token consumption by 40-60%".
    - No matching benchmark artifact path in docs/ referenced from
      these claims; the verification-contract doc at docs/ft-xbnl0-
      verification-contract.md mandates Level C artifact bundles for
      soak/perf-adjacent claims but the README does not cite any.
  Why it matters: performance claims presented as current fact in
  the README should either cite an artifact bundle or be softened to
  "target" / "design goal" until evidence lands. Non-blocking.

G4 [LOW] `SEND_OSC_SEGMENT_LIMIT = 200` silently bounds OSC133 state
  Evidence:
    - crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs:188
        `const SEND_OSC_SEGMENT_LIMIT: usize = 200;`
    - mcp.rs:288-310 `derive_osc_state_from_storage` walks only the
      last 200 segments. If OSC133 markers span further back, the
      derived state is silently incomplete; the helper returns
      `Ok(None)` with no gap marker.
  Why it matters: a quiet-pane edge case (no activity for >200
  segments) would yield an incorrect alt-screen / prompt state via
  the MCP surface without a visible warning. Worth either documenting
  the bound or recording a `markers_unknown_due_to_window_limit`
  signal.

Non-gaps verified present and matching claims:

  - `ft robot state` / `state --include-text`: main.rs:2375-2391
  - `ft robot search --mode {lexical,semantic,hybrid}`:
      main.rs:4633-4711 enum + From impl; semantic/hybrid properly
      gated behind `semantic-search`/`frankensearch` features.
  - `ft mcp serve`: main.rs:33124
  - `ft web` + `/stream/events` + `/stream/deltas`:
      web/router.rs:65,70 — streaming exists; README's
      "more than 'health only'" claim is accurate.
  - `ft distributed agent`: main.rs:165-168 under
      `#[cfg(feature = "distributed")]`.
  - `ft session doctor`, snapshot save/restore/list/inspect/diff:
      SnapshotCommands + SessionCommands enums defined around
      main.rs:4207.
  - `ft tx run`/`tx rollback`/`tx plan`/`tx show`: main.rs:21114+
      via `execute_tx_run_with_executor`.
  - Policy "21 subsystems": unified_telemetry.rs:242 comment; actual
      PolicyEngine struct at policy.rs:3466-3517 declares ~22
      subsystem-shaped fields. Close-enough; no drift worth fixing.
  - tokio/smol usage in supported core: grep finds zero production
      call sites outside `runtime_compat` + `dependency_eradication`
      + `forbidden_dep_guards` (guard files are intentional).

Documented only. No shippable fix this tick per /reality-check-for-project
ground rules. Related: AGENTS.md rule zero (NEVER delete
frankenterm-core) is intact; the four gaps above are additions to the
README, not subtractions from the code.
close_reason:
Reopening-in-error by p5-orch robot-triage pick — the bead was already closed with the four reality-check gaps (G1 runtime_compat quarantine language, G2 ft restart Unix-only caveat, G3 softened perf/token claims, G4 OSC/OSC133 marker window bound) addressed across two commits:

1. 4c3952a9 docs: correct README claims vs actual (ft-2guux) — landed 2026-04-20, covers all four gaps:
   - G1: added 'The remaining watch-daemon/runtime startup path still crosses a named runtime_compat quarantine while the last task-spawn seams are being collapsed' to the Platform Model paragraph
   - G2: appended 'ft restart is currently Unix-only.' to the Session persistence row of the support matrix
   - G3: softened <50ms lag to 'target/benchmark lane'; softened 200+ pane memory envelope to 'benchmark-dependent until linked artifacts are published'; softened 40-60% TOON savings to 'lower-token machine format; savings vary by payload'
   - G4: added a new subsection '5.1 Marker Window Bound' documenting the bounded OSC/OSC133 marker derivation window

2. af925d26 docs(readme): correct runtime_compat boundary claim — landed 2026-04-21, further refined G1 language now that the 9e1bd63b cfg-strip has collapsed the dual-runtime fallback: 'The dual-runtime fallback is gone, but several production seams still route through the named runtime_compat boundary for runtime bootstrap, channels, time, blocking work, IPC, and mux interoperability while the remaining compat helpers are being collapsed.'

bv --robot-triage surfaced this bead as open-and-ready because the triage graph snapshot had not yet absorbed the prior close. Verified via git log --grep ft-2guux + direct README diff inspection: no work remains. Restoring closed status.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.5.3.cont] Native tmux speaker — socket listener + handler dispatch + notification stream
description:
Continuation of ft-hs5f6.

ft-hs5f6 shipped the wire-format substrate at crates/frankenterm-core/src/tmux_control_protocol.rs (645 lines, 21 unit tests):
- TmuxCommand enum (9 Tier-1 verbs + Unknown fallthrough)
- parse_command() line-oriented parser with single/double-quote + escape handling
- TmuxResponse encoder producing %begin/%end/%error block frames
- ParseError taxonomy (Empty / UnterminatedQuote / BadEscape)

This follow-up wires the substrate into a running daemon:

## Scope
1. **Socket listener** at $TMUX_TMPDIR/tmux-<uid>/default (or a config-overridable path).
   - flock advisory lock to prevent two ft instances binding the same socket.
   - mode 0700 dir + 0600 socket per tmux's own conventions.
2. **Handler dispatch** mapping parsed TmuxCommand variants into ft's existing wezterm.rs / native-mux surface:
   - SendKeys → wezterm.rs send-text fan-out.
   - ListWindows / ListSessions → mux topology query.
   - CapturePane → scrollback read (composes with ft-z4u60 mmap when wired).
   - SplitWindow / NewSession / AttachSession / Detach → lifecycle engine
     (composes with command_transport.rs / topology_orchestration.rs / session_profiles.rs).
   - Unknown verbs → graceful '%error <ts> <id> 1' response per spec.
3. **Async notification stream** — emit %output, %window-add, %window-close,
   %session-changed, %unlinked-window-add, %layout-change to subscribed clients.
   Hooks the existing event bus / pane-lifecycle observability.

## Acceptance
- tmux's own CLI (`tmux -S /path/to/ft.sock list-windows`) returns ft's window list.
- A real tmux client (e.g. iTerm2's tmux integration) attaches to ft and renders panes.
- Tier-2 / Tier-3 commands return %error rather than parser blow-ups.

## Cross-references
- ft-hs5f6 (parent — wire format substrate, retired)
- ft-2okh0.5 (grandparent epic)
- legacy_tmux/server.c — reference for socket bind + listen
- legacy_tmux/control.c — reference for notification stream
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/wezterm.rs — fan-out target
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/command_transport.rs — lifecycle dispatch (ft-3681t.2.3)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/topology_orchestration.rs — split/new dispatch (ft-3681t.2.2)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_profiles.rs — session naming (ft-3681t.2.4)
close_reason: Shipped socket-listener advisory lock slice in crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl: LocalListener::with_domain now acquires and holds a sibling .lock file before unlink/bind so concurrent ft mux servers fail instead of racing the same socket. Evidence: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl/src/local.rs; git diff --check on touched files. rch cargo test reached remote execution on vmi1149989 but failed before Cargo started with worker-side 'timeout: failed to execute process' exit 127.

title: Refactor MuxPool (mux_pool.rs) to asupersync
description:
# Refactor MuxPool (mux_pool.rs) to asupersync

## Background
mux_pool.rs (583 LOC) wraps generic Pool for DirectMuxClient connections with WezTerm-specific health checks.

## Dependencies
- Pool refactoring (wa-36idf) must be done first
- DirectMuxClient refactoring (wa-p48pw) must be done first

## Migration
1. Thread Cx through to Pool methods
2. Update health check (list_panes()) to use Cx
3. Update connection factory (DirectMuxClient::connect) to use Cx
4. Ensure pool config works with Budget model

## Comprehensive unit tests (LabRuntime)
1. **Basic lifecycle**: create pool → acquire → use → release → shutdown
2. **Health check integration**: mock unhealthy client, verify pool replaces it
3. **Connection factory**: verify DirectMuxClient::connect called with correct Cx
4. **Idle eviction**: connections idle past timeout are evicted (virtual time)
5. **Concurrent acquire**: N tasks acquire simultaneously, max_size respected
6. **Acquire timeout**: full pool, Budget::deadline fires, clean Cancelled outcome
7. **Pool drain on shutdown**: scope exit waits for all connections returned
8. **Stats accuracy**: verify all counters under concurrent load

Each test logs: pool stats at each step, health check results, connection create/destroy events.

## Acceptance criteria
- MuxPool works with asupersync DirectMuxClient and Pool
- Health checks work through Cx
- Idle eviction works with virtual time
- 8+ LabRuntime tests
- Obligation leak oracle passes

## LabRuntime DPOR
- **Pool concurrency testing with DPOR**: Use LabRuntime schedule exploration (DPOR) to exhaustively test concurrent MuxPool operations:
  - Multiple tasks acquiring connections while health checks run — verify no stale connections returned
  - Interleaved acquire + release + eviction — verify pool invariants (active + idle <= max_size)
  - Concurrent shutdown while tasks hold connections — verify clean drain without orphaned connections
  - Race between health check failure and acquire — verify correct fallback to new connection creation

## Benchmark requirements
- **Criterion benchmarks for pool scaling with connection count**: Add `benches/mux_pool_scaling.rs` measuring:
  - Acquire + release cycle latency as a function of pool size (max_size=1,2,4,8,16,32)
  - Health check overhead per acquire operation
  - Pool scaling: throughput (ops/sec) with increasing concurrent task count
  - Idle eviction scan time as a function of pool size
  - Connection factory overhead (DirectMuxClient::connect latency)

## Test and Observability Plan
1. Add comprehensive unit tests covering happy path, boundary/edge cases, and explicit failure/error behavior for logic introduced or changed by this bead.
2. Add deterministic integration and end-to-end scenario scripts that exercise full workflow behavior, including at least one negative/failure scenario and one recovery scenario.
3. Emit detailed structured logs during tests and e2e runs (timestamp, subsystem, correlation_id, scenario_id, inputs, decisions, outcomes, reason_code/error_code).
4. Persist triage artifacts for failed runs (stdout/stderr, structured logs, snapshots/fixtures, and concise failure summaries) so regressions can be root-caused quickly.
5. Ensure test commands and evidence locations are documented in the bead implementation notes and wired into normal validation/CI paths.

## User Impact
1. Specify the concrete operator/agent workflow pain this bead removes (speed, reliability, safety, or clarity).
2. Define measurable user-facing outcomes (for example p95 latency, failure/timeout rate, time-to-recovery, or reduction in manual intervention steps).
3. Define no-regression UX guarantees and explicit rollback/degradation behavior if those outcomes are not met.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Migrate MuxPool async behavior to asupersync while preserving pool correctness, health-check semantics, and acquisition/release guarantees.
2. Validate dependency alignment with DirectMuxClient/pool foundation beads and maintain deterministic behavior under contention and unhealthy-client replacement.
3. Require comprehensive validation: unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end scripts for lifecycle, health-check replacement, backpressure behavior, and timeout/cancellation flows.
4. Require structured diagnostics/logging for pool state transitions (acquire/release/replace/evict), health-check outcomes, and latency metrics.
5. Closure requires rch-offloaded validation evidence and explicit residual-risk notes.

title: web server accepts ::1 as localhost but formats an invalid IPv6 bind address
description:
Reality-check audit of the web server bind path found IPv6 loopback accepted by validation but rendered without brackets for the actual bind string.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web.rs:231-236 treats both "::1" and "[::1]" as localhost, so validate_bind_config accepts either.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web.rs:226-229 formats the bind address as format!("{}:{}", self.host, self.port) for every host.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/server.rs:17-23 calls validate_bind_config, then passes config.bind_addr() into FrameworkWebRuntime::start.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/server.rs:99-113 rejects non-localhost hosts but does not normalize IPv6 hosts after the localhost check.
- Existing tests cover is_localhost("::1") at web.rs:442-445 and is_localhost("[::1]") at web.rs:448-451, but the only bind_addr formatting test at web.rs:430-433 covers IPv4. There is no test proving "::1" becomes "[::1]:PORT".

Why it matters: an operator can configure tuning.web.default_host = "::1" as an explicitly allowed localhost bind, pass the safety check, then fail startup with an invalid address string like "::1:8000". That is a fail-shut availability bug on the supported IPv6 loopback path.

Proposed remediation: normalize WebServerConfig bind hosts through SocketAddr parsing or bracket raw IPv6 literals in bind_addr(); add tests for "::1" => "[::1]:port", "[::1]" preserved, and public IPv6 rejected until auth lands.
close_reason: Fixed in 0b87cdf15: WebServerConfig now brackets raw IPv6 literals when rendering bind addresses, preserves bracketed IPv6, and keeps public IPv6 rejected until auth lands. title: [OBS/SAFETY] connector_outbound_bridge.rs:389 policy_scope().expect bypassable via pub-field struct construction
description:
cc1 PHASE 3-style audit of connector_*.rs cluster (14 files / 26,283 LOC) at SHA 2d64387c4 found one trust-boundary documentation gap.

## Site

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_outbound_bridge.rs:387-390`

```rust
fn policy_scope(&self) -> &CredentialScope {
    self.scope
        .as_ref()
        .expect("validated credential action request must contain scope")
}
```

## Why this matters

The struct definition at line 327-337:

```rust
pub struct ConnectorCredentialActionRequest {
    pub operation: ConnectorCredentialOperation,
    pub credential_id: Option<String>,
    pub lease_id: Option<String>,
    pub scope: Option<CredentialScope>,  // ← Option<>, validator-enforced
    pub sensitivity: CredentialSensitivity,
}
```

The `scope` invariant ("must be Some") is enforced only by `validate()` (line 357-385), which is called from the single construction path `from_payload()` (line 344-352). All fields are `pub`, so external callers in this crate could construct via struct literal:

```rust
let req = ConnectorCredentialActionRequest {
    scope: None,  // ← bypasses validator
    ...
};
req.policy_scope();  // ← panics
```

## Verification at HEAD

`grep -rn "ConnectorCredentialActionRequest {" crates/ frankenterm/` returns ONLY the struct definition itself. Zero external struct-literal construction sites today, including in tests. So the panic is unreachable in current code, BUT:

1. Future caller adding a struct-literal construction (e.g., for testing or for a new callsite) reintroduces the footgun.
2. The doc-block on `policy_scope()` doesn't reference the `from_payload` trust boundary; future readers re-derive the relationship.
3. Same shape as ft-n9btw (28 pub-field bypass concern resolved via doc-block) and ft-5w9ij (test-only panic helper reachable from production resolved via #[cfg(test)] gate).

## Suggested fix (single cycle)

Doc-only fix mirrors the ft-rsv5b pattern (just shipped at f2551efc1):

1. Add a doc-block on the struct `ConnectorCredentialActionRequest` documenting the construction discipline: "All callers MUST construct via `from_payload(payload)` which runs `validate()`. Direct struct-literal construction bypasses the validator and may violate the `policy_scope()` invariant."

2. Add a doc-block on `policy_scope()` referencing the trust boundary: "Invariant: `self.scope.is_some()` after construction via `from_payload`. Direct struct-literal construction would panic here."

This is doc-only, zero behavioral change, shippable single-commit.
notes:
Shipped doc-only fix at HEAD: br-ft-2jz47 doc-block on `ConnectorCredentialActionRequest` (line 326) explaining the construction discipline + invariant doc on `policy_scope()` (line 388) referencing the trust boundary.

Fix mirrors the ft-rsv5b pattern (just shipped at f2551efc1) and the ft-n9btw / ft-5w9ij precedents — when an invariant is enforced socially (validator at single construction path) rather than structurally (newtype / private fields), document the contract on the type.

Verification:
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on connector_outbound_bridge.rs: clean
- cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 1m24s, clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- Zero behavioral change (doc-only)

Verified at HEAD that there are still ZERO struct-literal construction sites for ConnectorCredentialActionRequest outside the type's own impl block. The expect() at line 393 remains theoretically reachable only if a future caller bypasses from_payload — the doc-block now surfaces the contract so that path won't go uncaught.

Companion finding filed as ft-0t4ra (connector_governor.rs:1113-1117 record() return swallows) — same shape, separate bead since it's a 3-site fix in a different file.

title: [mock-code-finder][gui-commands] Hide detach commands for non-detachable domains
description:
## Finding
The GUI command palette/menubar generation adds `Detach Domain ...` for every attached non-local domain, but the mux `Domain` trait exposes `detachable()` and several attached domains explicitly return false (for example `LocalDomain` and `RemoteSshDomain`). Selecting a generated detach command for those domains reaches `domain.detach()?` and fails instead of being hidden.

## Evidence
- `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/commands.rs` only checks `dom.state() == DomainState::Attached` and `name != "local"` before adding `KeyAssignment::DetachDomain`.
- `frankenterm/mux/src/domain.rs` documents `fn detachable(&self) -> bool`; `LocalDomain::detachable()` returns false.
- `frankenterm/mux/src/ssh.rs` has `RemoteSshDomain::detachable()` returning false while `state()` is always attached.
- `frankenterm/mux/src/lib.rs` already gates window-close domain detaches on `domain.detachable()`.

## Scope
Gate command palette/menubar detach actions on `dom.detachable()` in addition to attached state and non-local name. Add focused unit coverage for the predicate so non-detachable attached domains do not regress.

## Verification
- rustfmt check on `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/commands.rs`.
- RCH-only focused test if a worker is admitted; otherwise record the existing RCH no-worker blocker and do not run local Cargo.

# BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2

## Origin
Round-2 idea-wizard pass after BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT (ft-mpc9b) covered the foundational rendering work. This sibling epic captures incremental improvements — categories the round-1 epic didn't touch.

## Mission
Close the *protocol-feature* and *display-pipeline* gaps vs ghostty/Kitty. Make ft an always-running, always-recoverable terminal that surpasses tmux + WezTerm combined.

## Source mining (round 2)

- zellij: `zellij-server/src/pane_groups.rs:9-78` (pane groups), `background_jobs.rs:40-60` (job queue)

## Sub-epics
- **1**: Modern terminal protocol omnibus (Kitty graphics + iTerm2 1337 + Kitty keyboard + DEC 2026 + OSC 8/22/52 full)
- **2**: Display-pipeline trifecta (VRR + direct scanout + frame deduplication)
- **3**: Triple-buffered terminal state + snapshot rendering
- **4**: GPU pipeline state object disk cache
- **5**: Crash-safe scrollback + native tmux protocol speaker
- **6**: Lower-priority extras (variable fonts, COLR/CPAL, battery-aware FPS, pane groups, multi-monitor coherence, subpixel positioning, atlas RAM tier, block-mode, async cold tier, smart selection, sparse texture array)

## Cross-references

- Sub-epic 3 (triple-buffered state) composes naturally with persistent rope (round-1 ft-mpc9b.2.5) — they're complementary

## Acceptance for the epic as a whole
- ft renders Kitty graphics protocol images
- ft handles iTerm2 OSC 1337 file-display
- ft synchronizes output via DEC mode 2026 (Neovim/lazygit/btop look smooth)
- ft requests adaptive refresh rate on VRR-capable displays

- ft survives kill -9 / power loss with full scrollback intact
- ft speaks tmux control protocol so existing tooling works

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.1] Modern terminal protocol omnibus — Kitty graphics + iTerm2 1337 + DEC 2026 + Kitty keyboard + OSC 8/22/52
description:
# Modern Terminal Protocol Omnibus

## Background
The single biggest visible feature gap vs ghostty/Kitty. Modern apps (lazygit, btop, neovim+image.nvim, yazi) emit these escape codes; today they degrade silently in ft.

## User-perceived value
- Apps that look broken on ft (image rendering, atomic full-screen redraw, advanced keyboard) just work
- AI agents calling ft can drive modern apps without flicker workarounds
- ft becomes a drop-in replacement for ghostty/Kitty for users who care about these features

## Sub-tasks (one per protocol, each with own bead deferred until this epic spawns them)
- 1.1: DEC mode 2026 synchronized output — atomic frame buffering. The single most-impactful protocol; eliminates flicker on Neovim/lazygit/btop. Per-app test corpus: nvim with treesitter, lazygit, btop, ranger.
- 1.2: Kitty graphics protocol — APC-encoded image transmission, query/transmit/display/delete commands. Test corpus: image.nvim, yazi, kitty's `icat`. **A11Y**: accept alt-text via Kitty extension or fall back to filename for screen-reader announcement.
- 1.3: iTerm2 OSC 1337 — File, SetColors, SetProfile, MultipartFile. Test corpus: iTerm2 reference scripts, imgcat.
- 1.4: Kitty keyboard protocol — progressive enhancement modes for full key disambiguation. Test corpus: vim with super-key bindings, emacs.
- 1.5: OSC 22 cursor shape control + OSC 8 hyperlinks (full support including hover/click) + OSC 52 clipboard round-trip with policy gates (cross-link policy.rs ActionKind ClipboardWrite/Read).

## Source-of-truth implementations
- Ghostty: `legacy_ghostty/src/terminal/modes.zig:229` (mode 2026), `osc/parsers/iterm2.zig:65` (iTerm2 full parser), `apc.zig:5,36-39` (Kitty graphics), `osc.zig:70` (OSC 22), `input/kitty.zig` (Kitty keyboard)

## Accessibility
- Kitty graphics images: emit accessibility tree updates with image alt-text or filename
- OSC 8 hyperlinks: announce link target on focus/hover for screen readers
- Kitty keyboard: progressive enhancement must not break existing keyboard shortcut accessibility paths

## Security
- OSC 52 clipboard write: policy-gated via existing policy.rs (already integrated for the existing ft clipboard surface). Reads default-deny; writes require explicit allow.
- Kitty graphics: image transmission size capped (default: 16MB per image). Larger images rejected with error
- iTerm2 SetProfile: doesn't switch profiles silently; requires user confirmation prompt

## Per-protocol implementation strategy
Each protocol ships behind a feature flag, escalating to default per BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.ROLLOUT (ft-mpc9b.9) staging:
- Hidden → Opt-in: 1 release of dogfood
- Opt-in → Default: after conformance corpus passes for 2 releases

## Structured logging
Per protocol, JSON-line at `tests/protocol_<name>/logs/<scenario>.jsonl`:
- ts, protocol, command, parsed_args, result (accept/reject/error), duration_ns
- Per scenario summary: total_commands, accepted, rejected, errors

## Tests
- Per-protocol: parser unit tests (proptest on random valid/invalid inputs)
