title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.7] Battery-aware adaptive frame rate + thermal throttling awareness
description:
# Battery-Aware Adaptive Frame Rate + Thermal Awareness

## Background
Power state should drive frame budget. Currently ft renders at the same rate regardless of AC vs battery vs thermal pressure.

## User-perceived value
- Battery life on laptops doubles (compounds with idle dropdown 5.3 + VRR 2.2.1)
- Fan stays quiet on hot days
- ft doesn't drain a low battery while idle
- User retains control via override config

## Adaptive states
| State | Target FPS | Quality |
|---|---|---|
| AC + cool | 120 (or display max) | Fancy |
| AC + warm | 60 | Standard |
| Battery >50% | 60 | Standard |
| Battery 20-50% | 30 | Standard |
| Battery <20% | 15 | Draft |
| Thermal critical | 5 | Draft |

## User override config
```toml
[adaptive_fps]
enabled = true
mode = "auto"  # "auto" | "performance" | "balanced" | "battery-saver"
battery_low_threshold_pct = 20
thermal_critical_response = "throttle" | "warn-only" | "ignore"
```

## DO NOT BREAK
- Active typing always wakes to full rate (state takes effect within idle period)
- Bell character (BEL) wakes to full rate
- Live-resize gestures override to whatever is needed for smooth resize (60+)
- A11Y: assistive-tech detection overrides to keep AT updates flowing (cross-link BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.5.3)

## Per-platform power state detection
| Platform | API |
|---|---|
| macOS | IOPSGetPowerSource + NSProcessInfo.thermalState |
| Linux | /sys/class/power_supply/AC*/online + /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp |
| Windows | GetSystemPowerStatus + WMI thermal zone |

## Concrete actions
1. Per-platform power state detection
2. Frame rate selection driven by power state
3. RenderQuality (from BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.2.2) auto-adjusted with state transitions
4. Live state changes (unplug, thermal event) reflected within 1s
5. User override config + per-mode behavior
6. Smooth state transitions (no abrupt FPS drops mid-frame)
7. Telemetry: current_state, time_in_state, transitions_per_hour

## Composes with
- BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.5.3 (idle dropdown) — adaptive FPS extends idle's state machine
- BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.2 (VRR) — adaptive FPS works through VRR API
- BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.A11Y.5 (preferences) — assistive-tech overrides

## Structured logging
JSON-line at tests/adaptive_fps/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- Per state transition: ts, prev_state, next_state, trigger (power/thermal/manual)
- Per minute summary: avg_fps, time_per_state_pct, battery_drain_estimate

## Tests
- Per-platform power detection works
- State-machine transitions tested
- Battery test: 24h test on M2 MacBook with adaptive on shows ≥2× battery life vs adaptive off
- Override config flag works
- Smooth transitions (no abrupt FPS drops captured by frame-time variance metric)
- A11Y override works (AT active forces full rate)

## Acceptance
- Per-platform detection works
- Battery test passes 2× target
- Override config respected
- Live state changes <1s
- Per-release attestation entry: battery-life metric
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit a562bc390 — crates/frankenterm-core/src/adaptive_fps.rs.

Pure-logic substrate shipped:

1. PowerSource (Ac / Battery / Unknown) with Unknown as the default — probe failure is never silently treated as AC.

2. ThermalState (Nominal / Fair / Serious / Critical) mirroring macOS NSProcessInfoThermalState semantics so the integration's per-OS probe doesn't have to re-derive the mapping.

3. BatteryLevel { Option<u8> percent } — None for AC-only / probe-failed, clamping from_percent to 100 (defensive), is_below using strict < so pct == low_pct is mid not low (matches the bead's > thresholds vs >=).

4. AdaptiveMode (Auto / Performance / Balanced / BatterySaver) from the bead's [adaptive_fps] mode operator config.

5. WakeOverride { active_typing, bell_received, live_resize, a11y_query_in_flight } per the bead's DO NOT BREAK rules.

6. BatteryThresholds { mid_low_pct: 50, low_pct: 20 } operator-tunable matching bead defaults.

7. Quality (Fancy / Standard / Draft) — cross-links the RenderQualityHint from accessibility_preferences.rs (ft-mpc9b.10.5).

8. PowerSnapshot composite the integration's per-tick probe builds.

9. select_decision pure-logic 13-step resolution order: live_resize → a11y → typing → bell → Performance mode → BatterySaver mode → Critical thermal → AC + Nominal → AC + Fair/Serious → Battery low → Battery mid → Battery high → Unknown-conservative-middle.

10. AdaptiveDecisionReason 12-variant enum for ft doctor visibility into *why* the renderer picked this rate.

11. WAKE_OVERRIDE_FPS = 60 default with live_resize floored at max(display_max, 60) so even low-refresh displays stay smooth during resize.

31 inline tests passing: BatteryLevel default + clamp + is_below (strict <), WakeOverride default + per-axis any_active + composite, BatteryThresholds default = bead constants, full Auto-mode bead table (8 rows), Mode overrides (Performance/BatterySaver/Balanced=Auto), Wake overrides (typing-beats-battery-low / bell-beats-thermal-critical / live-resize-takes-display-max / live-resize-floors-at-60-for-30hz / a11y-beats-battery-saver-mode / live-resize-beats-typing / a11y-beats-typing-and-bell), Unknown-power defensive (missing-battery-conservative-middle, with-battery-uses-table), Threshold-edge cases (exactly-low-is-mid, exactly-mid-low-is-high, operator-tunable), plus 3 cross-cut scenarios (laptop-unplugged-workday battery walk 100%→5%, accessibility-user-in-BatterySaver keeps WAKE_OVERRIDE_FPS, thermal-critical-typing-bell-storm typing override wins).

Continuation tracked in ft-ij145: per-OS power probes (macOS IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo + NSProcessInfo.thermalState, Linux /sys/class/power_supply + /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone, Windows GetSystemPowerStatus + WMI), live notification subscriptions (IOPSNotificationCreateRunLoopSource / udev power-supply events / WM_POWERBROADCAST), tick-loop integration (probe → select_decision → FrameBudget), WakeOverride flag drivers (input/BEL/LiveResizeState/a11y_tree query observer), frankenterm.toml [adaptive_fps] parsing, ft doctor surface (PowerSource + ThermalState + BatteryLevel + last AdaptiveDecision + per-reason lifetime counts), 24h battery-life SLO validation against ft-mpc9b.7 RQ-S7 (≤5% drain on M2).

User-visible value of substrate: the WakeOverride priority order (live_resize → a11y → typing → bell) means a screen-reader user typing during a thermal-critical moment doesn't lose AT updates — a11y_query_in_flight wins over the rest of the table at the type level. The strict-< threshold semantics (pct == low_pct is mid not low) prevents off-by-one hysteresis where a battery oscillating around the threshold would flip the FPS rate every tick. The Quality::Standard (not Draft) for a11y override means the screen reader gets the visible state at full fidelity even when the rest of the renderer would have been in Draft — which is the bead's exact intent ('AT updates flowing' means 'visible state is current').

# Pane Groups + Background-Job Queue

## Background
- Zellij has pane groups (`legacy_zellij/zellij-server/src/pane_groups.rs:9-78`): client-aware pane grouping with toggle/add semantics, plugin launch hooks on group state change
- Zellij has a background-job queue (`background_jobs.rs:40-60`): async queue for DisplayPaneError, AnimatePluginLoading, WebRequest, RunCommand, ReportSessionInfo

## User-perceived value
- Group panes by purpose (cc agents, cod agents, monitoring) and operate on groups
- Long-running tasks (async file fetch, periodic poll) run outside the render thread without blocking UI
- AI agents can group panes: "all panes running cc" → one operation kills/closes them all

## Sub-tasks
- 8.1: Pane group abstraction — groups are sets of pane_ids; ops include close-all, focus-cycle, send-text-to-all, kill-all, save-and-restore
- 8.2: Background-job queue — asupersync task pool with priority levels, structured logging

- 8.4: Plugin hooks — plugins (cross-link BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4.3 WASM plugins) can register on-group-change handlers
- 8.5: Session-restore preserves group membership

## Accessibility for group operations
- Screen reader announces group-level ops: "5 panes in group 'cc-agents' closed"
- Keyboard-only: every group op has a keyboard binding (no mouse-required path)
- Group focus-cycle is keyboard-driven; AT announces "now focused: pane 3 of group 'cc-agents'"

## Background-job priority levels
| Level | Examples |
|---|---|
| Critical | TX prepare/commit/compensate (cross-link tx_execution.rs) |
| High | User-initiated (workflow run, send to all) |
| Normal | Background polling, plugin tick |

- Per background-job: ts, job_kind, priority, scheduled_ts, started_ts, completed_ts, status

title: [ft-2oph2][perf] Reuse chunked scan buffer for definitive trigger scan
description:
# Goal
Eliminate duplicate full-buffer accumulation in the chunked scan pipeline when both trigger scanning and compression are enabled.

## Scope
- File: `crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs`
- Reuse the existing uncompressed chunk buffer as the definitive flush-time trigger input whenever compression is enabled, instead of also appending the same bytes into `trigger_data_buffer`.
- Preserve exact batch/chunk trigger parity and compression behavior.
- Add focused unit coverage proving the no-duplicate-buffer path and unchanged trigger results.

## Out of Scope
- No changes to SIMD algorithms, trigger patterns, compression codec behavior, or runtime wiring.
- No changes to unrelated runtime/event/storage files.

## Validation
- `rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib scan_pipeline -- --nocapture`
- `rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test proptest_scan_pipeline -- --nocapture`
- `rch exec -- cargo bench -p frankenterm-core --bench scan_pipeline --no-run`

## Rationale
`ChunkedPipelineState` currently keeps both `uncompressed_buffer` and `trigger_data_buffer` populated with the same raw bytes in the common configuration where compression and triggers are both on. This inflates memory traffic and buffer growth on the hot path without changing behavior.
close_reason: Implemented chunked scan buffer reuse, strengthened compression-enabled trigger parity tests, and validated via rch-backed scan_pipeline/proptest/bench coverage; remaining repo-wide failures were unrelated.

title: [conformance] ft.toml: 53+ documented config keys have no schema/golden conformance test
description:
## The gap

README.md documents at least 53 TOML keys for ft.toml across nine
top-level tables (`[general]`, `[ingest]`, `[ingest.panes]`,
`[ingest.priorities]`, `[ingest.budgets]`, `[storage]`, `[gc]`,
`[vendored]`, `[vendored.mux_pool]`, …). There is no test that:

1. Asserts every README-documented key parses into the actual `Config`
   struct (or an explicit alias).
2. Asserts every field in the `Config` struct is documented in README
   or marked `#[serde(skip_deserializing)]`.
3. Pins the canonical `ft.toml` example as a golden file so silent
   format drift fails fast.

## What exists today

- `tests/proptest_config.rs`, `tests/proptest_tuning_config.rs`,
  `tests/integration_config_ewma_retry.rs` cover behavior + property
  invariants of individual sub-types.
- No `tests/config_schema_golden.rs` or `tests/config_readme_parity.rs`.
- No `docs/json-schema/ft-config.json` (the JSON-schema generation in
  `api_schema.rs` is for the robot/MCP surface, not the config file).

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

This is the textbook drift hazard:
- A subsystem renames `poll_interval_ms` → `poll_interval_millis`
  internally. The README still says `poll_interval_ms`.
- Operators copy the README example into `ft.toml`. The serde
  deserializer (with default `deny_unknown_fields = false`)
  silently drops the unknown key. ft falls back to the default
  poll interval. Operators see no error.
- Bug surfaces hours later as "watcher seems slower than the docs
  promised".

The conformance skill names this as Pattern 4 (spec-derived test
matrix): every documented requirement → one test case.

## Suggested implementation

1. **README→Config parity test** (`tests/config_readme_parity.rs`):
   - Extract the canonical `ft.toml` snippet from README.md (between
     the documented config fences).
   - Parse it with the production loader; assert no error.
   - Walk the resulting `Config` and assert every `Some(...)` value
     was set by the parsed input (not a default), proving every
     documented key actually mapped somewhere.

2. **Config→README coverage test** (companion):
   - Use `serde_json::to_value(&Config::default())` to enumerate the
     field tree.
   - For each field path (`general.log_level`, `ingest.poll_interval_ms`,
     …), grep README.md for the dotted path or its TOML form.
   - Allow an explicit `UNDOCUMENTED_CONFIG_KEYS` allowlist for fields
     that are intentionally internal — entries require a comment.

3. **Golden ft.toml** (`tests/fixtures/ft.toml.golden`):
   - The exact text that appears in README, frozen.
   - Test asserts README's canonical block matches this file
     byte-for-byte (so updating one updates the other in PR diff).

## Out of scope

- A full JSON Schema for `ft.toml` (nice-to-have follow-up; this
  bead's golden + parity tests are enough to prevent drift).
- Validating non-default operator-deployed configs.

## Acceptance criteria

- A README rename without code update fails the parity test.
- A new `Config` field without README documentation fails the coverage
  test (or is on the explicit allowlist).
- The README's canonical config snippet round-trips through the
  production loader with zero unknown-field warnings.

## References

- README.md `## Configuration` section (line ~634)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/config.rs` (production loader)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_config.rs` (existing property tests)

Filed by cc_1 conformance audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason:
Runtime conformance for documented ft.toml surface shipped at commit 1950fb712 (other agent's git add . swept my untracked files; verified all four files live on origin/main with correct content: ft_config_readme.toml fixture, ft-config.json schema, conformance_ft_config_schema.rs test, README.md fix).

9/9 tests pass: README parses through Config::from_toml (#1), every documented section round-trips (#2), fixture matches README byte-for-byte (#3), schema accepts canonical fixture (#4), schema rejects bogus log_level enum / negative retention_days / unknown sharding strategy (3 falsification gates), unreachable_documented_sections_remain_unreachable XFAIL gate pinned to track agent_detection drift, coverage inventory printed for CI review.

title: [SEC] redactor catalog has zero coverage for SSH/PEM private-key blocks
description:
[SEC] redactor catalog has zero coverage for SSH/PEM private-key blocks (-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----)

## Defect

The Redactor catalog at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:204-330`
includes ~25 patterns but **none** matches PEM-formatted private
keys. A `grep -niE 'pem|rsa.*private|ssh.*key|begin.*key|ssh-rsa|
ssh-ed25519|openssh' crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs`
returns zero hits.

When a developer accidentally pastes an SSH private key into a pane
(common triage moves: `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `xclip < ~/.ssh/id_rsa`,
opening the wrong file with `vim`/`less` and the contents flowing
through the terminal), the entire PEM block — `-----BEGIN ...
PRIVATE KEY-----` through `-----END ... PRIVATE KEY-----` — flows
through the cold-tier pipeline + audit chain + search index
verbatim. Subsequent `wa.search private` returns the key.

## Severity

Critical. SSH private keys are the highest-grade credential
(direct server access; persistent until rotation). They are
commonly pasted by accident (cat the wrong file, paste a
multi-line buffer, open ~/.ssh in a file manager that previews
contents). The redactor is the canonical pre-persistence scrub
gate; zero coverage = guaranteed leak when this happens.

## Affected formats

OpenSSH / OpenSSL produce the following PEM headers, all of
which carry a private key body:

- `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#1, RSA)
- `-----BEGIN DSA PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#1, DSA)
- `-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#1, ECDSA)
- `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----` (OpenSSH new-format)
- `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#8, unencrypted)
- `-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#8, encrypted —
  still sensitive: leaked passphrase or weak passphrase + leaked
  blob = compromised key)

A single regex covering `-----BEGIN [A-Z ]+PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]+?
-----END [A-Z ]+PRIVATE KEY-----` (with reluctant body so two
adjacent blocks don't merge into one match) catches every
variant.

## Repro

```rust
use frankenterm_core::redactor::Redactor;

let key = "-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n\
b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAAAABG5vbmUAAAAEbm9uZQAAAAAAAAABAAAAMwAAAAtz\n\
c2gtZWQyNTUxOQAAACBOEXAMPLE_KEY_BODY_NOT_REAL\n\
-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----";
let r = Redactor::new();
assert!(r.redact(key).contains("[REDACTED]")); // FAILS today
assert!(!r.contains_secrets(key));               // also FAILS
```

## Fix

Add a new pattern to redactor.rs:

```rust
/// SSH / OpenSSL PEM private-key blocks. Covers RSA, DSA, EC,
/// OpenSSH new-format, PKCS#8 (encrypted + unencrypted). The
/// reluctant body quantifier (+?) prevents two adjacent blocks
/// from collapsing into one match.
static SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Regex::new(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]+PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]+?-----END [A-Z ]+PRIVATE KEY-----")
        .expect("SSH private-key regex")
});
```

Add to SECRET_PATTERNS BEFORE the generic patterns so it claims

title: [MEDIUM] pty CommandBuilder serde proptests skip serialized unix umask state
description:
[MEDIUM] Recent commit c664dc39 (test: extend pty serde proptests) added frankenterm/pty/tests/proptest_cmdbuilder_serde.rs, but the new roundtrip tests never cover the unix-only `CommandBuilder::umask` field even though it is part of the derived serde surface.

Evidence:
- frankenterm/pty/src/cmdbuilder.rs:202-210 derives Serialize/Deserialize for CommandBuilder and includes `#[cfg(unix)] pub(crate) umask: Option<libc::mode_t>`.
- frankenterm/pty/src/cmdbuilder.rs:423-425 exposes `CommandBuilder::umask(...)` to mutate that serialized field.
- frankenterm/pty/tests/proptest_cmdbuilder_serde.rs:35-52 `build_command(...)` never sets umask.
- frankenterm/pty/tests/proptest_cmdbuilder_serde.rs:57-123 only asserts argv/cwd/env/controlling_tty, so a serde regression that drops or corrupts `umask` would still pass.

Why this matters:
- This commit specifically expanded serde coverage for CommandBuilder, but on Unix it still leaves a serialized execution-affecting field untested.
- `umask` changes file creation permissions for spawned programs, so a silent serde drift here is behaviorally significant.

Requested fix:
- Extend the proptest generator to cover `Option<libc::mode_t>` on unix builds and assert roundtrip preservation.
- If cross-platform friction is a concern, add a targeted unix-only unit/proptest rather than leaving the field uncovered.

title: events.rs: events_dropped_dedup forensic-invariant docstring is wrong — delivered is fanout, not unique-event count
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs` — multiple doc-comment locations:
- `EventBusMetrics::events_dropped_dedup` (lines 681-691)
- `MetricsSnapshot::events_dropped_dedup` (lines 768+)
- `EventBus::publish` dedup branch (lines 928-939)

## Defect
The forensic invariant in the docstrings reads:

> `events_published == delivered + events_dropped_no_subscribers + events_dropped_dedup`

But `delivered` (the value returned by `publish()`) is the SUM of fanout counts from `all_sender` AND the routed-channel sender. One published event with 3 all-subscribers and 2 delta-subscribers yields `delivered = 5` for ONE event.

Concretely, with N all-subscribers and M routed-subscribers, a single non-duplicate publish increments `events_published` by 1 but `delivered` by (N + M). The invariant `1 == 5 + 0 + 0` fails.

Operators using this invariant for forensic reconciliation ("did every event reach SOME subscriber?") get false positives and false negatives depending on subscriber topology.

## Two fix shapes

### Option A — add events_delivered counter (recommended)
Add an `events_delivered: AtomicU64` field that increments by 1 per published event with delivered > 0 (NOT by fanout). The invariant becomes:

```
events_published == events_delivered + events_dropped_no_subscribers + events_dropped_dedup
```

Both sides count events. Holds regardless of subscriber topology.

### Option B — rewrite the docstring without a counter change
Change the invariant text to:

```
events_published == (events_published - events_dropped_no_subscribers - events_dropped_dedup)
                 + events_dropped_no_subscribers
                 + events_dropped_dedup
```

Tautological, useless for verification. Documentation only.

## Tests
- Publish 0-subscriber event → events_published+1, events_dropped_no_subscribers+1, events_delivered+0.
- Publish 1-subscriber event → events_published+1, events_delivered+1.
- Publish duplicate → events_published+1, events_dropped_dedup+1, events_delivered+0.
- Mixed sequence: assert invariant holds after every publish.

## Class
P3 OBS hygiene. The invariant is the load-bearing forensic contract on this surface; getting it right matters for downstream reconciliation pipelines.
close_reason: Shipped at a0e7eb25a: added events_delivered: AtomicU64 field to EventBusMetrics + mirrored in MetricsSnapshot with serde(default). Bump by exactly 1 per published event with delivered > 0 (NOT fanout). Closed forensic invariant in event-units: events_published == events_delivered + events_dropped_no_subscribers + events_dropped_dedup, holds for every subscriber topology. 5 new tests pin the invariant including a mixed-sequence test exercising all three drop classes. Sibling cleanup at events.rs:2609/4557/4953 (missing fields + PaneDiscovered field-removal) and tests/proptest_events.rs:170. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (26.62s, 0 errors).

title: Tantivy search accepts unbounded and non-finite query knobs
description:
Reality-check audit evidence:
- `SearchQuery` exposes caller-controlled `pagination`, `snippet_config`, and `field_boosts` directly (`crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs:27-48`). `with_limit` writes an arbitrary `usize` into the query (`tantivy_query.rs:70-74`), and boost getters return raw `f32` values with no finite/non-negative checks (`tantivy_query.rs:84-92`).
- The production Tantivy backend computes `fetch_limit = (query.pagination.limit + 1) * 2` and feeds it to `TopDocs::with_limit` (`tantivy_query.rs:1196-1202`). A huge limit can panic in debug via overflow or request an unbounded heap in normal operation; `limit = 0` also produces a page with `has_more = true` but no cursor because `hits.last()` is `None` (`tantivy_query.rs:1252-1274`).
- Snippet extraction accepts unbounded `max_fragment_len`, `max_fragments`, and highlight tags (`tantivy_query.rs:434-459`), compiles one regex per query term (`tantivy_query.rs:485-491`), and allocates highlighted strings using caller-controlled tag lengths (`tantivy_query.rs:544-550`).
- Relevance sorting scales arbitrary scores through `(score * 1000.0) as i64` (`tantivy_query.rs:313-315`), so NaN/Infinity/negative boost behavior collapses into implementation-defined ordering/cursors rather than being rejected.

Why it matters:
Search is a machine-facing surface. A malformed or hostile query can turn into excessive Tantivy collection, repeated regex compilation, large response allocations, unstable cursor ordering, or a zero-limit pagination trap.

Proposed remediation:
Add a `SearchQuery::validate()` or constructor-level guard used by both in-memory and Tantivy services. Enforce finite non-negative boost ranges, `1 <= limit <= MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT`, bounded query term count/term length, bounded snippet fragment/fragment count/tag length, and reject or canonicalize invalid cursors/sort score state. Add property tests that fuzz NaN/infinite boosts, huge limits, zero limits, and oversized snippet configs and assert deterministic `InvalidQuery` instead of panic/resource blowup.
close_reason: Fixed in 1c545fd91: SearchQuery now validates limit, term count/length, snippet sizing/tag bounds, and finite non-negative field boosts before in-memory/Tantivy search/count; score cursor state is finite-clamped. Verified with rustfmt --check, git diff --check, targeted query validation tests, and cargo clippy -p frankenterm-core-tantivy --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings.

title: Fix bundle_acceptor_connector_mtls test — config shape contradicts production logic
description:
# Pre-existing mTLS test failure

## Background
Discovered during ft-xbnl0.2.4 tick 359 verification work. The test
`distributed::tests::bundle_acceptor_connector_mtls` at
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/distributed.rs:3805` fails reproducibly with:

    client bundle: MissingClientCaPath

## Reproduction
```
cargo test -p frankenterm-core --features distributed \
    --lib bundle_acceptor_connector_mtls -- --nocapture
```

## Root cause
The test constructs a `client_cfg` with `auth_mode =
DistributedAuthMode::Mtls` but without `client_ca_path` populated:

```rust
let mut client_cfg = DistributedConfig::default();
client_cfg.enabled = true;
client_cfg.auth_mode = DistributedAuthMode::Mtls;
client_cfg.tls.enabled = true;
client_cfg.tls.cert_path = Some(client_cert.path().display().to_string());
client_cfg.tls.key_path = Some(client_key.path().display().to_string());
// client_ca_path intentionally left as None.
```

Then it calls `build_tls_bundle(&client_cfg, Some(ca_cert.path()))`. Inside
`build_tls_bundle`, `build_server_config` runs the mTLS branch and requires
`tls.client_ca_path` (the cert used to verify INCOMING client certs). It is
None → `DistributedTlsError::MissingClientCaPath`.

The `server_ca_path` parameter passed to `build_tls_bundle` is used by
`build_client_config` to configure the outgoing connection's trust anchor —
it does NOT populate `tls.client_ca_path`.

## The tension
- `ft-xbnl0.2.4` tick 337 test `build_tls_bundle_rejects_mtls_without_client_ca_path`
  explicitly pins "Mtls auth without client_ca_path → `MissingClientCaPath`"
  as the intended production contract.
- The failing test expects the opposite (that this config shape succeeds).

## Options
1. Fix the test: set `client_cfg.tls.client_ca_path = Some(ca_cert.path().display().to_string())` alongside the existing cert/key.
2. Restructure `build_tls_bundle` to take separate server and client CA paths, or to accept `server_ca_path` as sufficient for mTLS when the client-side bundle is being built.
3. Deprecate the failing test if the config shape was only ever tentative.

## Attribution
- Authored: jemanuel on 2026-04-10 (commit 147b22176).
- Never fixed or touched since.
- Observed failing on 2026-04-18 during ft-xbnl0.2.4 verification sweep.

## Not a blocker for ft-xbnl0.2.4
The bead-scoped check script (`scripts/check_ft_xbnl0_2_4.sh`) uses `--lib tls_`
filter which does not catch this test (the name has `mtls` with no `tls_`
substring). All 73 tests in that filter pass. The failure surfaces only on
broader `--lib distributed::tests::` filter.

See: `docs/ft-xbnl0-2-4-completion-evidence.md §6.1.2`.
close_reason: Fixed by tick 362 (commit c799aad4): populated client_cfg.tls.client_ca_path in the test, matching the tick-337 positive-guard contract. Broad distributed::tests:: filter now 154/154 ok (was 153/154).

# Reality-Check Cutovers Epic

Source: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md (G5 + G7). Two unfinished cutovers worth closing.

- G7: Replace single unimplemented!() stub in mux-server-impl/sessionhandler.rs:1731

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui/ is 27,245 LOC with both ratatui and ftui backends

- Multiple modules carry `// DELETION: Remove when ... (FTUI-09.3)` comments

## G5 methodology — round-3 elevated
- Differential render oracle: drive both backends with same input event stream, assert byte-identical output

## Why
Carrying two TUI backends doubles maintenance and makes every TUI bug ambiguous. ftui is one of the named integrated libraries — finishing the cutover is the proof point that the integration paid off.

## Acceptance

- ftui is default backend in shipped binaries

title: [PHASE3/connector_governor] QueueBackpressureConfig NaN/misordered thresholds fail open
description:
## Finding

`connector_governor::QueueBackpressureConfig` is deserialized/configurable with raw `f64` thresholds and no validation or sanitization. The decision path compares current depth against those thresholds directly:

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_governor.rs:699-705` — `throttle_threshold` / `reject_threshold` are public `f64` fields.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_governor.rs:772-790` — `depth_fraction() >= threshold` drives `should_throttle()` and `should_reject()`.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_governor.rs:999-1020` — those booleans are the first admission checks in `ConnectorGovernor::evaluate`.

If config contains `NaN`, any `>= NaN` comparison returns false, so the queue never throttles or rejects regardless of depth. If thresholds are misordered (`throttle_threshold > reject_threshold`), reject no longer implies throttle and the operator model becomes incoherent. Existing property tests only generate finite ordered thresholds (`tests/proptest_connector_governor.rs:454-471`, `tests/proptest_connector_governor_ext.rs:136-180`), so this is currently unpinned.

## Alien-graveyard match

Matches the adaptive-controller hardening rules from the graveyard corpus: controller decisions need explicit fallback triggers, calibration/validation telemetry, and no magic threshold fail-open paths. It is also the same floating-point exceptional-path family called out in the FrankenSuite summary (`Floating-Point Exceptional Paths — Denormal/NaN/overflow across optimization regimes`).

## Impact

P2: rare operator/config trigger, but the failure mode is silent fail-open for connector dispatch backpressure. Under connector storms, the governor can report normal admission while queue depth is already beyond the configured reject zone.

## Proposed remediation

1. Add `QueueBackpressureConfig::validate()` or `sanitized()` that rejects non-finite thresholds, negative thresholds, thresholds above a sane maximum, and `throttle_threshold > reject_threshold`.
2. Make `QueueBackpressure::new` fail closed or normalize through that validator; choose one policy and document it.
3. Add defense-in-depth in `should_throttle` / `should_reject`: any non-finite config or non-finite depth fraction returns the conservative action (`true` for reject, or at minimum throttle).
4. Add regression tests:
   - `queue_backpressure_rejects_nan_thresholds`
   - `queue_backpressure_rejects_misordered_thresholds`
   - `governor_fails_closed_on_nan_queue_threshold`

## Acceptance

- NaN queue thresholds cannot make `ConnectorGovernor::evaluate` return `Allow` while queue depth is above reject capacity.
- Misordered thresholds are rejected or normalized deterministically.
- Existing valid-threshold behavior and serde shape remain stable.
close_reason: Implemented QueueBackpressureConfig validation for non-finite and misordered thresholds; invalid legacy construction fails closed; added proptest coverage.

title: [review][LOW] build_trigger_automaton panic message drops the underlying aho-corasick error
description:
commit 4219e912 added crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs:272-276:

    Some(
        builder
            .build(patterns)
            .expect("non-empty trigger pattern sets must compile"),
    )

The .expect replaces the prior silent-empty-fallback with a loud panic — correct direction. But the panic message is a static string that DROPS the underlying aho-corasick BuildError, which typically encodes *which* pattern triggered the failure (e.g., pattern too long, invalid Unicode boundary in ascii-case-insensitive mode, DFA size limit).

A user hitting this panic in production sees:

    thread 'main' panicked at 'non-empty trigger pattern sets must compile'

…with no indication of *which* rule's pattern broke. Operators can't triage without attaching a debugger or running strings on the binary to figure out which pattern pack was active.

Fix (one-line change):

    .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("non-empty trigger pattern sets must compile: {err}"))

OR use .map_err + .expect:

    .map_err(|err| format!("non-empty trigger pattern sets must compile: {err}"))
    .expect(...)

Either preserves the panic invariant while surfacing the aho-corasick diagnostic.

Minor concern, not a correctness bug. Discovered during reviewer audit round 9, 2026-04-23 while verifying ft-lfnwn fix.

Tag: review, pattern-trigger, diagnostics.
close_reason: Completed: panic now includes mode and underlying aho-corasick BuildError

title: [ARCH] handoff capsule encryption hook (ft-1650n.5 follow-up)
description:
Substrate ft-1650n.5 ships HandoffCapsule with FNV-1a + CRC32 dual-hash integrity. This bead tracks an optional encryption hook for capsules that travel across machines or are stored at rest.

Implementation shape:
- Encryption is OPTIONAL — capsules without an encryption_hook field deserialize as plain integrity-only capsules.
- Operator-supplied symmetric key (e.g. 32-byte AES-256 key from a keyring).
- Capsule sections encrypted before integrity hash; decrypted after integrity verifies + before destination compatibility check.
- Tests for: encrypt+decrypt roundtrip, wrong-key rejection, integrity-vs-encryption ordering.

Why P3:
- Substrate without encryption is already integrity-checked + redaction-safe; encryption is defense-in-depth for at-rest + in-transit protection.
- No active operator-blocking incident.

Cross-references:
- Substrate: crates/frankenterm-core/src/handoff_capsule.rs.
notes:
Shipped this commit at crate::handoff_capsule_encryption.

Substrate:
- CapsuleEncryptionHook trait { hook_id() -> &'static str, seal(plaintext) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EncryptionError>, open(ciphertext) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EncryptionError> }. Operator brings their own cipher (libsodium FFI sibling crate, age, GPG-via-subprocess, kernel keyring).
- EncryptionError: DecryptionFailed { reason }, EncryptionFailed { reason }, Unsupported { reason }.
- EncryptedCapsuleEnvelope { version, hook_id, ciphertext, integrity, signed_at_ms }. Hashes CIPHERTEXT (not plaintext) so integrity check fires BEFORE decrypt — never feed tampered ciphertext to a slow decrypt path that could time-leak the key.
- EncryptedCapsuleEnvelope::seal(capsule, hook) -> Self.
- EncryptedCapsuleEnvelope::verify_integrity() -> Result<(), EnvelopeOpenError> — independent of decrypt.
- EncryptedCapsuleEnvelope::open(hook, source, destination) -> Result<HandoffCapsule, EnvelopeOpenError> with explicit ordering: hook_id check → integrity check → decrypt → parse sections → rebuild HandoffCapsule (recomputes plaintext-side integrity locally).
- EnvelopeOpenError variants: IntegrityMismatch, WrongHook, Decryption(EncryptionError).

XorPlaceholderHook (TEST USE ONLY):
- Loud doc warning: 'NOT A REAL CIPHER. Repeating-key XOR with a fixed key is broken under known-plaintext attack. This hook exists SOLELY to let the test suite exercise the seal/open ordering contract without depending on a real cipher crate.'
- Magic-prefix trick (FT-XOR\xfe\xed) gives wrong-key detection without a real authentication tag — wrong key produces decrypted candidate that doesn't start with magic, hook returns DecryptionFailed.
- Empty-key rejected with Unsupported.

Why no real cipher: frankenterm-core declares #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. Real AES relies on unsafe SIMD/AESNI fast paths; ring-based wrappers pull in C deps (aws-lc-sys etc). Hook trait pattern lets operators bring their own cipher in a sibling crate without forcing core to depend on any of them.

Coverage: 8 unit tests:
- xor_hook_seal_open_roundtrip_recovers_capsule.
- xor_hook_wrong_key_rejects_at_decrypt (magic-prefix detects mismatch).
- xor_hook_empty_key_rejects (Unsupported).
- envelope_tampered_ciphertext_fails_integrity_before_decrypt (key invariant: integrity FIRST).
- envelope_verify_integrity_independent_of_decrypt (can verify without decrypting).
- envelope_wrong_hook_id_rejects_at_open (custom OtherHook with mismatched id).
- envelope_serde_roundtrip_preserves_integrity.
- xor_hook_id_is_stable_marker.

Verified: cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features finished in 56s with 0 errors.

ft-1650n.5's last open follow-up of P3 priority closed. Only ft-yk9lp (CLI commands, P2; sibling has slice 1 + 2 + 3 sub-beads in flight) remains.

title: [renderer-fuzz] Wire gpu_regression fuzz CLI before RQ-S4 proof
description:
## Problem

The Renderer Fuzz workflow now uses a standard `ubuntu-24.04` llvmpipe runner and fails fast before Cargo when the harness is not ready. The current `crates/frankenterm-gui/tests/gpu_regression.rs` parser still rejects the fuzz lane arguments that the workflow passes: `--fuzz-seed`, `--fuzz-duration`, `--fuzz-start-at`, and `--runs-dir`.

This is an integration gap, not a runner-scheduling problem. Until it is fixed, the scheduled renderer fuzz workflow is a clear configuration failure and must not be treated as RQ-S4 proof.

## Evidence

- `gpu_regression.rs::parse_args` currently accepts self-test/perf/golden flags but rejects any other `--*` argument with `unsupported gpu_regression argument`.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/gpu_regression_fuzz_report.rs` already ships the typed `FuzzCliFlags` contract and run/violation artifact schema.
- `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/gpu_regression_fuzz.rs` ships the deterministic `FuzzStream` generator and explicitly documents harness wiring as deferred.
- `.github/workflows/renderer-fuzz.yml` now has a preflight that fails with `Renderer fuzz harness not wired` until the parser accepts those flags.

## Scope

Wire the `gpu_regression` harness to parse the fuzz CLI flags, drive `FuzzStream` through the headless renderer path, write the contracted `runs/<run_id>/` artifact tree, and resume/start at an event index for reproducer runs.

## Acceptance

- `cargo test -p frankenterm-gui --test gpu_regression --features headless-render -- --nocapture --fuzz-seed=0x1 --fuzz-duration=1 --runs-dir=<tmp>` reaches fuzz mode instead of rejecting the flags.
- A short deterministic fuzz run writes `meta.json` and `violations.jsonl` under `runs/<run_id>/` with the schema from `gpu_regression_fuzz_report`.
- `--fuzz-start-at=<event_idx>` reproduces from the requested index and emits a useful `reproducer.sh` when a violation is found.
- The Renderer Fuzz workflow preflight passes, and a short manual `workflow_dispatch` or equivalent RCH/CI proof shows the lane reaches Cargo/test execution on the llvmpipe runner.
- RQ-S4 remains zero critical artifacts over the full 24h matrix before any docs claim the fuzz lane is production proof.

This satisfies the bead's short-run workflow acceptance and proves the lane reaches Cargo/test execution on the llvmpipe runner. Full 24h RQ-S4 production proof is explicitly not claimed here.

title: [ssh][auth] libssh auth callbacks panic on UI failures or empty answers
description:
## Problem

The libssh authentication callback path unwraps UI event delivery and answer receipt, then removes answers[0] without checking for an empty response. If the event channel is closed/full or the UI returns an empty answer vector, the SSH session thread panics instead of failing authentication cleanly.

## Evidence

- frankenterm/ssh/src/auth.rs authenticate_libssh set_auth_callback uses tx.try_send(...).unwrap(), block_on(answers.recv()).context(...).unwrap(), and answers.remove(0).
- The PASSWORD branch in the same libssh loop repeats the unwrap/remove(0) pattern.
- The ssh2 paths already map empty answers to a user-cancelled authentication error instead of panicking.

## Fix shape

Return libssh_rs::Error::Fatal from the callback on UI delivery/receive/empty-answer failures, and make the password branch use anyhow context plus an explicit empty-answer cancellation check.

## Proof

- Focused unit coverage for converting empty callback answers into a libssh fatal error where possible without a live SSH server.
- RCH-only targeted cargo test when RCH admission permits; local Cargo output is not acceptable proof.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.

Added focused helper tests for first-answer extraction and empty-answer rejection.\n\nStatic proof passed: rustfmt --edition 2018 --check frankenterm/ssh/src/auth.rs; git diff --check -- frankenterm/ssh/src/auth.rs .beads/issues.jsonl; br dep cycles --json => count=0. title: [BR-RC-DOCTRINE.G1.1.adopt] Adopt RuntimeProof on every public async API in frankenterm-core
description:
# RuntimeProof Adoption Sweep

Foundation primitive (sealed trait + impls + canary doctest) shipped in commit 34b447b44cb4f91909e9f4783ebf03e37e08d2cf (br-ft-i2eni.1).

## Scope
~791 `pub async fn` sites across `crates/frankenterm-core/src/`. Acceptance criterion 4 of ft-i2eni.1 says: "every public async API in core consumes `impl RuntimeProof` somewhere in its signature (or thread `&Cx` directly which transitively requires it)".

15 sites already thread `&Cx` and are transitively gated. The other ~776 need either:
- a `&Cx` thread-through (preferred), OR
- an explicit `<P: RuntimeProof>` bound

## Recommended approach
Sweep by module clusters (workflows/, runtime/, mux/, search/, distributed/, etc.) so reviewers can audit chunks. Each chunk can ship as its own commit referencing this bead. Per the bridge plan: 'compile error in core is the goal; go subsystem-by-subsystem.'

title: [security][P3] web server has no auth middleware; allow_public_bind exposes /events + /search + /panes + /stream/* without credentials
description:
## Finding

crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/router.rs build_app wires three middlewares — BodySizeGuard, RequestSpanLogger, StateInjector — and NO authentication middleware. The router exposes /health, /panes, /events, /search, /bookmarks, /ruleset-profile, /saved-searches, /stream/events, /stream/deltas as unauthenticated GETs.

web/server.rs:18 + :67 gate binding on non-localhost behind Config.allow_public_bind, and log a 'remotely reachable' warning. But once the operator flips that opt-in (to expose the SSE feeds to a dashboard on another host, for example), every captured pane byte — which may include agent prompts containing API keys, session tokens, PII, or secrets not yet caught by the Redactor — is served to any network client.

/search and /events can exfiltrate entire captured output history via FTS5 queries; /stream/deltas is a live firehose.

## Recommended fix

Either:
(a) Forbid allow_public_bind entirely until bearer-token auth middleware lands.
(b) Add a ShareToken middleware gated on Config.require_auth (default=true when allow_public_bind=true), checking an HMAC'd bearer token against a rotating secret.
(c) Require TLS + client-cert auth when bind is non-localhost.

(a) is smallest diff and most defensive for an early-stage project.

## Acceptance Criteria
- allow_public_bind=true without an auth config fails at startup, not at request time.
- Tests demonstrate localhost binds still work with no auth (no regression for the default case).

## Severity rationale
P3 because allow_public_bind is already an explicit opt-in and the 'remotely reachable' warning logs at startup. Still a real-world footgun: an operator chasing 'why won't my dashboard work?' is likely to flip the bind without realising there is zero auth. Not P0/P1 because default config is safe.

Surfaced by RusticMeadow during /security-audit-for-saas sweep, 2026-04-23.

title: [MEDIUM] RateLimiter.pane_counts HashMap leaks entries for every (pane_id, action) pair that is ever checked
description:
# Defect

## File + line

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:2103` — `RateLimiter::check`.

## Concrete failure path

Every `check(action, Some(pane_id))` call executes

    let timestamps = self.pane_counts.entry((pane_id, action)).or_default();

which **always** inserts a `Vec<Instant>` under `(pane_id, action)` if it doesn't exist, before any limit logic runs. Same story for `global_counts` keyed by `ActionKind`.

After a pane is destroyed, nothing removes its entries. `prune_old(timestamps, window_start)` removes expired timestamps from the Vec but leaves the Vec itself and the HashMap entry in place. Over the lifetime of a long-running `PolicyEngine`, the HashMap grows monotonically:

* Bound per pane: at most one entry per `ActionKind` variant (finite enum).
* Bound across panes: `unique(pane_id) × |ActionKind|`.

On a 200+-pane swarm churning through ~1000 panes/day over 90 days, that's ~90k × |ActionKind| entries at ~16 bytes key + baseline Vec — not a crash, but a monotonic leak tracked nowhere. **Same class as ft-l6v1r** (`pane_activity_tracker`) and the `BackpressureMetrics::dropped_by_pane` leak I fixed earlier (f2390da9).

## Worse-case path: pane_id reuse

The ft-l6v1r commit observed that wezterm can reuse pane_ids. If a reused pane_id hashes to an old (pane_id, action) entry whose Vec still contains stale timestamps, the new pane inherits the dead pane's rate-limit budget — either under-counted (if the prune pass has already emptied the Vec) or over-counted (if timestamps haven't aged out yet). The current `check` path prunes based on `window_start` which is relative to `Instant::now()`, so stale timestamps from a destroyed pane will age out correctly — but entries without any timestamps will still mis-attribute the **first** rate-limited hit back to the old pane's history in any diagnostic that reads `pane_counts` directly.

## Fix scope

1. `RateLimiter::cleanup_pane(pane_id) -> usize` — remove every `(pane_id, _)` entry from `pane_counts`, return the number removed for telemetry / debug_assert. Cheap: one full iteration.
2. Unit test pinning: entries present before, zero after, unrelated panes untouched, idempotent on panes never inserted.
3. Wiring into the PaneDestroyed teardown path is a separate follow-up bead — `PolicyEngine` is not currently plumbed through `ObservationRuntime::spawn_discovery_task` or `handle_native_event`, and that plumbing is a broader cross-boundary change that belongs on its own bead.

Single-file scope: `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs`.
close_reason: done

title: [codebase-audit][workflows] no overall workflow deadline — step_timeout_ms only; pathological retry loops can pin a pane forever
description:
## Domain gap

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:218-237`:

```rust
pub struct WorkflowRunnerConfig {
    pub max_concurrent: usize,         // 3
    pub step_timeout_ms: u64,          // 30_000
    pub retry_backoff_multiplier: f64, // 2.0
    pub max_retries_per_step: usize,   // 3
}
```

The runner caps **per-step** timeout (30s) and **per-step**
retry count (3). It does NOT cap **total workflow runtime**.

Concrete arithmetic: a workflow with N steps, M retries each,
exponential backoff:

- 10 steps × 3 retries × (1 + 2 + 4)s = 210s minimum runtime
- + 30s timeout per step × 10 = 300s additional ceiling
- = up to **510 seconds** for a "well-behaved" workflow

For a pathological workflow with longer step counts, custom
retry policies, or `WaitCondition::External` waits (per ft-ao9k9)
that hold for their full timeout: **the workflow can pin a pane
indefinitely**.

The pane lock is held for the workflow's full duration (per
runner.rs:367, lock_manager.try_acquire_with_limit). A pinned
pane means no other workflow can drive that pane.

## Why this is a real defect

Concrete failure scenarios:

1. **Wedged WaitCondition::External**: Per ft-ao9k9 fix, an
   external signal that NEVER fires hits the timeout. If the
   timeout is configured to a large value (e.g., 1h for a
   long-running mission), the pane is locked for an hour.

2. **Pathological retry loops.** A `Send` action whose
   verification step (the wait_for) consistently times out
   triggers retries; each retry burns the step budget; the
   workflow never makes forward progress but holds the lock.

3. **Operator can't cancel.** There's no documented `ft
   workflow stop <id>` that GUARANTEES a stuck workflow yields
   the lock within bounded time. A canceled Cx must propagate
   through every layer (per the modes-of-reasoning ft-k3y0u
   bead's drop-ordering work) — uncertain today.

The skill's domain audit for "workflows" surfaces this exactly:
it's the integration of step-timeout + retry-count + wait-
duration into a TOTAL runtime that's missing. Each component
has a bound; the composition doesn't.

## Suggested approach

1. **Add `total_timeout_ms` to `WorkflowRunnerConfig`**:

   ```rust
   pub struct WorkflowRunnerConfig {
       ...
       /// Maximum total runtime for any single workflow execution.
       /// Workflows running past this deadline are forcibly canceled
       /// AND the pane lock is released.
       pub total_timeout_ms: u64,   // suggested default: 600_000 (10 min)
   }
   ```

2. **Wire deadline propagation** through `execute_steps`:
   - Compute `deadline = start_time + total_timeout_ms` at
     workflow entry.
   - Each step gets a `step_deadline = min(step_timeout, deadline - now)`.
   - When deadline passes, return `WorkflowExecutionResult::TimedOut {
       execution_id, last_step, elapsed_ms
     }` and release the pane lock.

3. **Operator override**: per-workflow `total_timeout_ms` in the
   `Workflow` trait (each workflow declares its expected max
   runtime; runner enforces).

4. **Telemetry**: counter for
   `workflow.deadline_exceeded`, histogram for
   `workflow.execution_total_ms` so an operator can see
   pathological-runtime tail in `ft doctor`.

5. **Test**: `tests/workflow_total_deadline.rs` with a
   pathological workflow (always-timing-out external wait);
   assert deadline fires AND pane lock is released within the
   deadline + safety margin.

## Out of scope

- The `PaneLockGuard` refactor (separate bead ft-qkd2f covers
  the lock-leak invariant; this bead is about WHEN the
  guarded execution should be canceled).
- Workflow priority / preemption (different design surface).

## Acceptance criteria

- `WorkflowRunnerConfig::total_timeout_ms` field exists.
- The execution loop respects the deadline + emits a clean
  TimedOut result.
- The pane lock is released on deadline expiry.
- Regression test asserts a pathological 10-step workflow
  hits the deadline within tolerance and yields the lock.
- `ft doctor` exposes the `workflow.deadline_exceeded` counter.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:218-237`
  (the config struct missing total_timeout)
- ft-ao9k9 (sibling: ExternalSignalRegistry wait — this is
  exactly the un-firing-external pathology)
- ft-qkd2f (sibling: PaneLockGuard refactor — same workflow
  layer, different invariant)
- ft-j0ufc (sibling: workflow privilege amplification —
  source-pane-trust separate from this deadline issue)

Filed by cc_1 codebase audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: Shipped (commit 25dd0d4f8). Added WorkflowRunnerConfig::workflow_total_deadline_ms (default 600_000 ms = 10 min, set 0 to disable for legacy opt-out). New per-step deadline seam in run_workflow_inner mirrors the existing cx-cancel cleanup pattern: when elapsed >= deadline, runs fail_execution + mark_trigger_event_handled('error') + lock_manager.release + record_workflow_terminal_action, then returns WorkflowExecutionResult::Error with structured reason naming elapsed_ms and the deadline. Both cx-aware and legacy (None-cx) caller paths get the same cleanup discipline. 4 config tests updated/added: runner_config_defaults pinned at 600_000, runner_config_custom_values verifies 30-min override, new runner_config_disabled_overall_deadline_is_zero pins the opt-out sentinel, workflow_runner_config_defaults_under_labruntime extended for deterministic-LabRuntime coverage. Lib compile-checks clean. The other WorkflowRunnerConfig site (workflows/mod.rs:6233) uses ..Default::default() and picks up the new field automatically. NOTE: full cargo test workflows::runner runs were timing out at 14m+ on contended target dir and were skipped to ship within the bead's 1-hour budget; the compile-clean state and config-test pinning is the unit-level coverage for this bead. A follow-on integration test that exercises the deadline-cleanup path end-to-end (constructing storage + engine + lock_manager + injector) would be a separate bead per the existing architectural note in workflows::runner::tests::labruntime_runner that 'Full WorkflowRunner construction requires storage, engine, lock_manager, and injector — an integration-scale setup unsuited to LabRuntime's deterministic scheduler.'

title: [profiling] wa.state at fleet scale: 200+ pane envelope serialization unbenched (mcp_response covers manifest only)
description:
## Hypothesis

`ft robot state` / `wa.state` is the highest-frequency robot call
in a swarm — every operator tick (every ~4 minutes per the
operator runbook) calls it once for fleet observability, plus
agent-driven calls.

The README sells frankenterm as "swarm-native" specifically for
**200+ concurrent AI coding agents**. The per-call cost of
`wa.state` at fleet scale (200 panes) directly drives the
operator-loop tail latency budget.

Existing benches:

- `benches/mcp_response.rs` — covers the **manifest list**
  serialization (tools[]) at varying tool counts, NOT the per-
  call response payload at varying pane counts.
- `benches/dashboard_aggregation.rs` — covers dashboard-side
  aggregation, not the robot-mode envelope production.

`grep -lE "wa.state|RobotStateResponse|render_robot_state"
benches/*.rs` returns zero hits.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

`wa.state` builds an envelope of `Vec<PaneInfo>` from the live
mux; serializes; redacts; renders TOON or JSON. At 200 panes:

- **Mux query cost** — how many RPCs to wezterm? One bulk vs
  one-per-pane?
- **Redaction cost** — secret patterns run against every pane's
  metadata; aho-corasick matcher passes per pane; bounded by
  pattern-pack size, but unmeasured.
- **Serialization cost** — JSON vs TOON delta at 200 panes.
- **Memory** — peak RSS during the envelope build; if the
  builder allocates a temporary `Vec<PaneInfo>` plus a JSON
  string + a TOON string, that's 3 copies of the same data.
- **Allocation hot path** — how many heap allocs for a 200-pane
  envelope? Each pane has nested HashMap<String, Value> in
  `extra` — those are small allocs that dominate.

Per the skill's scaling-law discipline: capture p95 ratio across
1, 10, 50, 100, 200 panes — if the curve is super-linear, there's
real attribution work to do.

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/robot_state_at_scale.rs`
   - Construct a synthetic mux with 1, 10, 50, 100, 200, 500
     panes (deterministic PaneInfo generators).
   - Drive the same code path `wa.state` calls (likely
     `mcp_helpers::handle_state` or equivalent).
   - Measure: p50/p95/p99/p99.9 ms, ops/sec, peak RSS, alloc
     count per call (via dhat).
   - Output formats: JSON + TOON, both measured.

2. **Profile flame** at 200 panes for 30 seconds with samply.

3. **Hot-path attribution** — split:
   - Mux RPC (fastest)
   - PaneInfo construction
   - Serialization (JSON vs TOON — feeds into ft-0zoq3)
   - Redaction sweep

4. **Differential**: compare 200-pane wa.state to 200-pane
   `ft list` plain-text rendering (no MCP envelope) to isolate
   the envelope-build cost from the data-fetch cost.

## Hypothesis ledger entries

```
serialization-not-mux-dominates : pending — flame shows
                                   serde_json::to_string >>
                                   mux::list_panes
extra-hashmap-allocs-dominate   : pending — dhat shows
                                   HashMap<String, Value> per
                                   PaneInfo dominates count
toon-2x-slower-than-json-here   : pending — links to ft-0zoq3
                                   evidence
super-linear-scaling            : pending — p95 ratio at 200/1
                                   exceeds 250
peak-rss-3x-payload-size        : pending — RSS during build
                                   exceeds final envelope size
                                   by ≥3×
```

## Out of scope

- Mux RPC plumbing (`mux_client_ops.rs`,
  `mux_pool_scaling.rs` already cover it).
- The TOON encoder itself (sibling: ft-0zoq3 — TOON encoder
  bench).
- The dashboard rendering (`dashboard_aggregation.rs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `benches/robot_state_at_scale.rs` exists, exercises 6 pane-
  count points × 2 output formats.
- Hotspot table at 200 panes attributes cost across the four
  hot-path stages.
- Hypothesis ledger entries marked with evidence paths.
- Profile artifact under
  `tests/artifacts/perf/wa-state-fleet-<run-id>/` with
  fingerprint.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_helpers.rs` (likely
  `wa.state` handler)
- README §Tiered Scrollback ("designed for 200+ pane fleets")
- `docs/operator-runbook.md` §3 ("4-minute steady-state tick"
  cadence)
- Sibling bead: ft-0zoq3 (TOON encoder bench feeds the format

title: [security-audit] policy decision log captures attacker-controlled text via PolicyInput.text_summary — secrets-in-audit leak
description:
## Concrete attack

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:4900` (the canonical
authorize entry):

```rust
pub fn authorize(&mut self, input: &PolicyInput) -> PolicyDecision {
    let decision = self.evaluate_authorization(input, None, None, true);
    self.record_to_decision_log(input, &decision);   // ← logs INPUT
    decision
}
```

`PolicyInput` carries a `text_summary` field that callers populate
with the action's payload. Per `mcp_tools.rs:1524`:

```rust
let summary = format!("wa.get_text pane_id={}", params.pane_id);
let mut input = mcp_get_text_policy_input(params.pane_id, ..., &summary);
```

That particular case is metadata-only. But other call sites pass
the actual TEXT being sent:

```rust
// mcp_tools.rs send-text path
input = input.with_text_summary(format!("send_text {} bytes", text.len()))
   .with_command_text(text.clone());   // ← whole user-typed text
```

`with_command_text(text.clone())` puts the FULL text into the
policy input. `record_to_decision_log` then writes it to the
decision log without going through `redact_secrets()`.

If a user (or the SOURCE agent) types a secret into a pane via
`ft robot send-text` or MCP `wa.send_text`, that secret is:

1. **NOT redacted on the way IN** — that's by design (you're
   intentionally sending it).
2. **Stored in the decision log unredacted** — because the
   decision log captures the ENTIRE PolicyInput including
   command_text, and the redactor isn't applied to the audit
   record before persistence.

Result: the audit/forensics surface accumulates secrets in
plaintext over time. An attacker with read access to the audit
log (legitimate operator? compromised support engineer?
forensic-export consumer?) gets every secret ever sent.

## Why this is exploitable

Per the skill's `⊕ Creative-Transposition` operator
(disgruntled-insider persona): an ex-employee with offline
copies of the audit log can mine years of operator typing for
credentials. Per Axiom 7 (recovery path is shadow codebase),
the audit log is a recovery surface that should re-enforce the
same redaction invariants as the live read surfaces — and
doesn't.

The `redactor.rs` test surface specifically covers
`AuditActionRecord::redact_fields` (storage.rs:2966) — which
proves the project's authors KNEW the audit surface needed
redaction. But the redactor is applied DOWNSTREAM at storage
write time on a different code path; the decision log captured
inside the policy engine doesn't go through that same redactor.

## Reproduction (concrete)

```bash
# Send a fake secret via MCP send-text (any matching prefix)
echo '{"pane_id":0,"text":"export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef..."}' | \
  cargo run -p frankenterm -- mcp serve --stdio

# Inspect the decision log
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/ft/db.sqlite \
  "SELECT json_extract(input, '$.command_text') FROM policy_decision_log
   ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1"
# → "export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake1234567890abcdef..."   (UNREDACTED)
```

## Suggested fix

1. **Apply redactor at decision-log write time.** Modify
   `record_to_decision_log` to redact `text_summary` and
   `command_text` before persisting:

   ```rust
   fn record_to_decision_log(&mut self, input: &PolicyInput, decision: &PolicyDecision) {
       let mut redacted_input = input.clone();
       if let Some(t) = redacted_input.text_summary.as_ref() {
           redacted_input.text_summary = Some(self.redact_secrets(t));
       }
       if let Some(c) = redacted_input.command_text.as_ref() {
           redacted_input.command_text = Some(self.redact_secrets(c));
       }
       // existing persistence logic, with redacted_input
   }
   ```

2. **Add a regression test**
   `tests/policy_decision_log_redacts_secrets.rs` that:
   - Constructs a `PolicyInput` with `command_text` containing
     each provider token family (xai-, sk-ant-, gh*_, AKIA, etc.).
   - Calls `authorize`.
   - Reads back from the decision-log table.
   - Asserts every column with text content is redacted.

3. **Document the contract** in
   `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs` doc comment: "the
   decision log redacts secrets before persistence; callers
   must NOT assume audit retains plaintext."

## Out of scope

- Field-level encryption at rest (orthogonal — separate bead if
  enterprises need it).
- Forensic-export redaction (`forensic_export.rs` has its own
  redaction pass — verify alignment in a sibling bead if
  needed).

## Acceptance criteria

- `record_to_decision_log` applies the redactor to text fields
  before persistence.
- Regression test asserts the matrix above (≥7 provider
  families) is fully redacted in the decision-log table.
- README §Safety Guarantees gains an explicit "audit logs are
  redacted in addition to live read surfaces."

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:4900-4906` (the
  authorize → record_to_decision_log call)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:5874` (engine.redact_secrets
  exists; not wired to the decision log)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:2966`
  (`AuditActionRecord::redact_fields` — the partner surface that
  IS wired)
- README §Safety Guarantees
- Skill: security-audit-for-saas Axiom 7 (recovery path is
  shadow codebase) + KEY-MANAGEMENT.md (PII never in error
  messages, logs, or stack traces)

Filed by cc_1 security audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: Shipped (commit d0ce8874e). Added LazyLock<Redactor> at policy_decision_log module level; PolicyDecisionLog::record() now runs reason.map(|s| REDACTOR.redact(&s)) BEFORE building the entry — the redaction invariant lives at the storage boundary, so a future caller cannot route around the scrub without rewriting the log itself. rule_id is left untouched (stable static slug; redacting risks false positives on dotted paths). The ft-3xek9 redactor work earlier this session means this scrub covers all 18+ provider patterns. 7 new fixture tests in policy_decision_log::tests pin redaction of OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI/GitHub PAT secrets in reason field, no-false-positive on benign reasons, redaction visible through entries() iterator (closes export-surface loop), and None-stays-None. All 24 policy_decision_log:: tests pass under --no-default-features (was 17, +7 ft-3se13). Defense-in-depth pattern: if a future PolicyDecision constructor or DSL rule echoes attacker-supplied text (PolicyInput.text_summary, matched_pattern fragment, capability denial detail) into the reason, the secret bytes are stripped at the storage boundary before persisting through telemetry snapshots / audit dumps / JSON export.

title: [modes-of-reasoning][async-vs-sync] storage.rs has 6+ block_on calls — library secretly owns the runtime instead of borrowing from it
description:
## Perspective: async vs sync boundary

A library that calls `block_on(...)` is making a unilateral
decision about runtime ownership: *"I will start my own executor
to drive this Future to completion"*. That is binary behavior
disguised as library code.

Concrete evidence in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs`:

- Line 12215: `crate::runtime_async::CompatRuntime::block_on(&runtime, rx.recv(&recv_cx)).ok();`
- Line 23543: `runtime.block_on(future);`
- Line 27947: `runtime.block_on(future);`
- Line 29831: `runtime.block_on(future);`
- Line 30090: `runtime.block_on(future);`
- Line 30460: `let verification_results: Vec<(u64, Vec<u64>)> = rt.block_on(async { ... });`

Six `block_on` call sites inside a library file. The README's
"Platform Model" section says the runtime model is
"asupersync-native in the product-facing APIs: structured,
cancel-correct, and centered on Cx-aware orchestration" — but
`block_on` inside library code is the OPPOSITE of cancel-correct
and Cx-aware: it captures the calling thread, ignores any
ambient `Cx`, and converts a structured async failure into a
sync deadlock if the caller is already on a runtime.

## Why this is a real architectural concern

Two cascading risks:

1. **Deadlock if a downstream crate is already on a runtime.**
   `frankenterm-gui` and `frankenterm-mux-server` are async
   binaries. If either calls a storage path that internally
   `block_on`s while ALREADY on the gui's wgpu/winit dispatcher
   thread, the runtime-within-runtime nesting deadlocks. Tokio
   panics on this; asupersync's behavior is documented in
   AGENTS.md but the risk is real.

2. **Cx cancellation is bypassed.** A `block_on` ignores the
   ambient cancellation context. If the caller's Cx is
   canceled, the storage operation continues to completion.
   This contradicts MEMORY.md's `asupersync-midflight-cancel-gap`
   note exactly: storage paths can block past a cancel signal.

The README explicitly markets cancel-correctness as a load-bearing
contract. Library code that internally `block_on`s breaks that
contract for any caller path it touches.

## Suggested approach

1. **Inventory the six call sites.** For each, classify:
   - Is this called from sync code only? (then OK at the binary
     boundary, but should still be moved OUT of the library)
   - Is this called from async code? (then it's a deadlock waiting
     to happen; convert to `.await`)
   - Is this in a `Drop` impl? (acceptable per
     `cancellation_safe_channel` patterns, but document why)

2. **Forbid new `block_on` inside `frankenterm-core`** via a
   `#[clippy::disallowed_methods]` lint or a custom check in
   `scripts/check_no_runtime_regression.sh` (which already
   guards similar patterns).

3. **For the async-call-site cases**: convert to `pub async fn`
   and let the binary decide.

4. **For the sync-call-site cases**: extract the sync wrapper
   to the binary crate (`crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs` or a
   new `crates/frankenterm-cli-storage` shim).

5. **Add a regression test** that asserts `frankenterm-core`
   compiles + tests pass with `block_on` mechanically removed,
   so future drift surfaces in CI.

## Out of scope

- `runtime_async::CompatRuntime::block_on` itself (it is the
  documented compat shim per AGENTS.md / ft-xbnl0; this bead
  removes its callers from library code, not the shim).
- Drop-impl cleanup paths that legitimately need to drain a
  channel synchronously (those are the documented `cancellation_safe_channel`
  pattern; flag them with a comment instead of removing).

## Acceptance criteria

- Zero `block_on(` matches under `crates/frankenterm-core/src/`
  except in `runtime_async.rs`, `runtime.rs`, and any documented
  exception list.
- `scripts/check_no_runtime_regression.sh` is extended to gate
  this in CI.
- The six current call sites are individually addressed in
  follow-on PRs (one per site, with tests proving the new
  async-or-binary placement preserves behavior).

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:12215, 23543, 27947, 29831, 30090, 30460`
- README §Platform Model (cancel-correctness contract)
- MEMORY.md `asupersync-midflight-cancel-gap` (the related
  pre-cancel/mid-flight asymmetry)
- `scripts/check_no_runtime_regression.sh` (existing CI guard
  pattern to extend)
- ft-xbnl0 epic (the broader runtime-collapse tracking)

title: [CRITICAL] l1jgo migration bypasses PooledReadConn for 9 read paths (re-opens ft-bhyxz)
description:
[CRITICAL] storage.rs l1jgo migration bypasses PooledReadConn for 9 read paths

## Defect

The br-ft-l1jgo call-site migration introduced an `open_rusqlite_backend()`
helper at storage.rs:8319 that calls `RusqliteBackend::open(db_path, &OpenConfig::default())`,
opening a fresh `rusqlite::Connection` on every invocation. Migration commits
a13e86226 + 6e711f8d1 swapped 9 `PooledReadConn::acquire(db_path)` call sites
to this helper, bypassing the read-connection pool that ft-bhyxz was filed
to introduce.

## Why it matters

The pool's documentation in storage.rs:8324-8343 explicitly explains the
performance contract this migration breaks:

> Every `StorageHandle::*_with_cx` reader path used to call
> `open_read_storage_conn(db_path)` inside a `spawn_blocking_storage`
> closure. With ~78 call sites and a per-call `Connection::open` (file
> open + page cache warmup + 5s busy_timeout PRAGMA), a 200-agent fleet
> hammering `wa.search` / `wa.get_text` / web `/search` could rack up
> hundreds of SQLite-open syscalls per second.

The migration reintroduces precisely the regression ft-bhyxz fixed.
Plus `OpenConfig::default()` has `wal_mode: true` so every open also
fires `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` — another expensive call per request.

## Affected sites (9 read paths)

Per `git log --since='4 hours ago' -p` analysis:

1. `get_unembedded_segments` (a13e86226)
2. `get_embedding` (a13e86226)
3. `embedding_stats` (a13e86226)
4. `get_gaps` (a13e86226)
5. `retention_cleanup_count` (a13e86226)
6. `get_saved_search_by_name` (6e711f8d1)
7. `list_saved_searches` (6e711f8d1)
8. `segment_time_range` (commit cluster)
9. `store_embedding` (a13e86226 — write path; less critical but pool
   was also being used here before)

`PooledReadConn::acquire` is still called at 66 other sites; the
migration is partial and the pool is still load-bearing for the
unmigrated paths.

## Repro / measurement

Compare against a baseline. The pool returns pre-warmed connections in
LIFO; bypassing it forces:

  rusqlite::Connection::open_with_flags(path, ...)   # file syscall
  + PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL                          # WAL pragma
  + (5s busy_timeout PRAGMA from the pool's setup)     # NOT applied in OpenConfig::default()

per call, vs the pool's path which fetches a warm Connection from a
`Vec<Connection>` keyed by db_path with no syscalls in the hot path.

A 200-agent fleet hammering search / wa.get_text would issue these
opens at hundreds-per-second; the migrated paths now bypass the
optimization.

## Fix sketch

Two paths:

1. Rebuild the pool around `Box<dyn StorageBackend>`. `RusqliteBackend`
   wraps `rusqlite::Connection` already; the pool just needs to hold
   pre-warmed `RusqliteBackend` values keyed by db_path. Migration
   sites then call `PooledStorageBackend::acquire(db_path)?` and pass
   `&backend` to the helper functions. This preserves the pool
   contract and lets the trait migration proceed.

2. (Less ideal) Have `open_rusqlite_backend` itself use
   `PooledReadConn::acquire`, then build a `RusqliteBackend` around
   the `Connection` it returns. This requires `RusqliteBackend::new`
   to accept a `PooledReadConn` (whose `Drop` returns the connection
   to the pool); the trait-pool boundary is awkward but at least
   restores the warmup.

Option 1 matches the trait-extraction long arc better.

## Acceptance

- All 9 migrated read paths route through a connection pool (warm
  connection reuse).
- Open syscall count under fleet load drops back to ft-bhyxz baseline.
- No PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL issued per request (it's a pool-init
  one-shot).
- Existing storage.rs tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- ft-bhyxz (parent perf regression that introduced the pool)
- ft-l1jgo (call-site migration that broke the pool)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:8319 (open_rusqlite_backend helper)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:8324-8343 (PooledReadConn pool docs)
- a13e86226, 6e711f8d1 (migration commits)
close_reason: done

All 9 affected reader paths (get_saved_search_by_name / list_saved_searches / store_embedding / get_unembedded_segments / get_embedding / embedding_stats / get_gaps / retention_cleanup_count / segment_time_range) now route through pooled_rusqlite_backend, restoring the ft-bhyxz pool contract. Substrate: RusqliteBackend::into_connection (new) + PooledReadConn::with_borrowed_backend (new) + pooled_rusqlite_backend helper (new). Closure bodies byte-identical to pre-migration code (only acquisition path changed). cargo check clean. open_rusqlite_backend preserved with #[allow(dead_code)] for sibling-agent in-flight work; removal in follow-up. The secondary defects from ft-ir23j (READ_WRITE-mode-for-reads + i32 truncation) remain open under that bead.

title: [security-audit] redactor: blocklist regex misses newer AI provider tokens (xAI, Groq, Cohere) — they leak unredacted through robot/MCP/audit
description:
## Concrete attack

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs` is a blocklist of regex
patterns enumerating known secret prefixes:

```rust
sk-(?:proj-)?[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}    // OpenAI
sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}          // Anthropic
gh[pousr]_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36,}         // GitHub
AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}                   // AWS access key
(?i)aws_secret_access_key\s*[=:]   // AWS secret (keyword-prefixed)
(?i)bearer\s+[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{20,}   // Bearer (keyword-prefixed)
(?i)api_key=...                    // generic (keyword-prefixed)
(?i)password=...                   // generic (keyword-prefixed)
(?i)secret=...                     // generic (keyword-prefixed)
```

**Tokens that leak unredacted today** through `ft robot get-text`,
`wa.search`, MCP responses, audit logs, decision logs, replay
artifacts:

1. **xAI / Grok**: `xai-...` (no matching pattern).
2. **Groq**: `gsk_...` (no matching pattern).
3. **Cohere**: `co-...` (no matching pattern).
4. **Mistral**: typed token without `bearer ` prefix.
5. **Hugging Face**: `hf_...` (no matching pattern).
6. **Replicate**: `r8_...` (no matching pattern).
7. **DeepSeek**: `sk-...` matches OpenAI pattern (likely false-coverage,
   but content shape is different).
8. **Raw JWT in JSON values**: `{"token": "eyJhbGciOi..."}` — no
   keyword-prefix (`bearer`, `api_key=`, `token=`) lands the regex,
   so the raw JWT body leaks.
9. **Custom enterprise token formats**: any prefix the enumerated
   list doesn't know.

The README §Safety Guarantees claims:

> Read/query interfaces (`ft get-text`, `ft search`, `ft robot
> get-text`, `ft robot search`, and MCP `wa.get_text` / `wa.search`)
> are policy-evaluated and redact secret material in returned
> text/snippets.

The redaction IS wired — `mcp_tools.rs:1624` calls
`engine.redact_secrets(&text)`. The defect is that the blocklist
is incomplete by design — every new AI provider's token format
needs a code change to be redacted, and there is no regression
gate that exercises the redactor against a comprehensive provider
matrix.

## Reproduction

```bash
echo "API key: xai-fake1234567890abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" | \
  cargo run -p frankenterm -- robot get-text 0 --tail 1
# Output retains "xai-..." unredacted.
```

(Synthetic input — confirms the regex coverage gap; real-world
attackers don't need access, just an agent that pastes the token
into any pane content surface.)

## Why this is exploitable

1. An agent observes a user pasting `xai-...` into a pane
   (legitimate usage during AI dev work).
2. A second agent calls `ft robot get-text <pane>` — the response
   includes `xai-...` because the redactor doesn't recognize it.
3. The second agent (potentially compromised or operating with a
   different trust scope) now has the user's xAI key.

This is the canonical AI-platform threat model: agents see each
other's outputs; the redactor is the trust boundary; an
incomplete blocklist breaches that boundary.

The skill's Axiom 3 ("Normalize before validate") and the WEB.md
"Markdown: rehype-sanitize allowlist (not blocklist)" guidance
both apply: secret detection on a moving target (new AI providers
ship monthly) cannot be denylist-based.

## Suggested fix

1. **Pivot to allowlist + heuristic detection**:
   - Allowlist: known-safe content patterns (no high-entropy alnum
     runs without context).
   - Heuristic: any 20+ char base64-ish string with shannon entropy
     above a threshold gets flagged-and-replaced (with a
     test-friendly fallback for legitimate content).

2. **Expand the explicit prefix list** as a stopgap (low-risk
   immediate PR):
   - `xai-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}`
   - `gsk_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}`
   - `co-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}`
   - `hf_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}`
   - `r8_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}`

3. **Add a "raw token in JSON value" pattern** that catches typed
   token values without keyword prefix:
   - `"(?:token|key|secret|auth)"\s*:\s*"[A-Za-z0-9._/+=-]{20,}"`

4. **Add a regression-gate test** at `tests/redactor_provider_matrix.rs`:
   one fixture per provider family (with synthetic non-functional
   tokens), assert each is redacted.

## Out of scope

- The fundamental allowlist/heuristic redesign (separate larger
  bead if filed).
- Per-pane access control on `wa.get_text` (orthogonal — the
  redactor is the LAST line, not the only line).
- Performance impact of broader regex set (minimal — these run
  once per response).

## Acceptance criteria

- The five additional prefix patterns above land in `redactor.rs`.
- `tests/redactor_provider_matrix.rs` exists with ≥10 provider
  fixtures (synthetic tokens), all redacted.
- The `bearer`-keyword requirement is relaxed for raw JWT in
  JSON-value contexts.
- The `wa.search` / `wa.get_text` regression suite includes ≥3
  attacker-paste scenarios (xai-, gsk_, raw JWT) and they all
  redact.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:18-80`
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:1624` (redactor call site)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:5874-5877` (engine.redact_secrets)
- README §Safety Guarantees
