title: ft-mpc9b.4.4 substrate: Center tile placement can overlap Left/Right when widths sum exactly to bar_width
description:
status_bar.rs layout engine places Center tiles at the geometric midpoint regardless of Left/Right placement. When total width fits but tightly:

Example: bar_width=22, Left=10, Right=8, Center=4, total=22.
- Left placed at x=0..10
- Right placed at x=14..22
- Center: centre_start = (22-4)/2 = 9; placed at x=9..13
- Overlap: cell 9 belongs to both Left and Center.

Fix options:
1. After computing centre_start, clamp so center doesn't intersect Left's x_end or Right's x_start; if would still overlap, drop the center tile (TruncatedByWidth) and retry layout.
2. Alternative: detect overlap post-layout and report the colliding tile in dropped[] list.

Option 1 is preferred — keeps the layout correct rather than reporting after the fact.

Also: status_bar.rs has 3  truncations (left_x, right_x, centre_x are u32). At bar widths >65535 cells these silently overflow. Practical risk near zero but defensive substrate should clamp.
close_reason: Fixed at 53329ec46: centre placement clamped to [left_x_end, right_x_start − centre_total) band; centre tile dropped TruncatedByWidth when band too narrow. as-u16 truncations clamped at u16::MAX. 2 regression tests added.

title: [HIGH] semantic_chunk_embeddings lacks FK to output_segments/panes; prune_chunks_through_ordinal has no production caller → orphan vector accumulation
description: semantic_chunk_embeddings is owned by crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs, not storage.rs, and it lives in a standalone sqlite DB opened by ChunkVectorStore::open(). SQLite foreign keys cannot reference parent tables absent from the same DB. Direct repro: sqlite3 ':memory:' "PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; CREATE TABLE child(x INTEGER REFERENCES parent(id)); INSERT INTO child(x) VALUES (1);" fails with 'no such table: main.parent'. So adding FK to panes/output_segments here is not a valid ≤30-line safe fix. A real fix needs a migration-plan bead: either rehome the vector store into the main storage DB, mirror parent tables into the vector DB, or solve retention/orphan cleanup without impossible cross-DB FKs. Leaving for owner with more context.
notes: Blocked on schema reality: semantic_chunk_embeddings lives in crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs as a standalone sqlite store with only semantic_generations in the same DB. SQLite foreign keys cannot reference tables absent from that DB; sqlite3 ':memory:' 'PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; CREATE TABLE child(x INTEGER REFERENCES parent(id)); INSERT INTO child(x) VALUES (1);' fails with 'no such table: main.parent'. So adding FK to panes/output_segments in this store is not a valid migration unless the vector store is rehomed into the main storage DB or those parent tables are mirrored into the vector DB. No code shipped for this bead to avoid landing a broken schema premise.
close_reason: Closed in df1c2ca01: proposal at docs/proposals/ft-3zr5f-semantic-chunk-orphan-decision.md (3 architectural options: rehome / mirror / explicit cleanup; recommends Option A) + regression guard at tests/ft_3zr5f_chunk_vector_store_dormant.rs (fails CI if a production caller appears without resolving the orphan-vector question). Live-code audit confirms ChunkVectorStore has zero production callers today — bug is dormant. Implementation tracked as ft-g2jko (triggers when a production caller is intended). Closed as 'dormant + guard active' rather than left BLOCKED indefinitely; the HIGH priority was a credibility hazard with no actionable path.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
# Gap

`semantic_chunk_embeddings` (crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs:593-618)
stores raw `pane_id`, `start_segment_id`, `end_segment_id` INTEGERs but has
ONLY a composite FK to `semantic_generations(profile_id, generation_id)`.
There is no FK to `panes(pane_id)` or `output_segments(id)`.

The main schema (crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:104) sets
`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, and the segment-level FK chain cascades on
pane deletion:
  panes → output_segments ON DELETE CASCADE (storage.rs:148)
  output_segments → segment_embeddings ON DELETE CASCADE (storage.rs:162)

But semantic_chunk_embeddings is NOT in the cascade chain. Two explicit
failure modes:

1. `prune_segments_sync` (storage.rs:14157) runs
   `DELETE FROM output_segments WHERE captured_at < ?1`. Cascade cleans
   segment_embeddings via FK. semantic_chunk_embeddings rows still carry
   the now-deleted start_segment_id / end_segment_id values — orphans.
2. Direct pane deletion (pane tombstone) cascades through panes →
   output_segments, but semantic_chunk_embeddings rows keyed on the old
   pane_id stay in the table indefinitely.

The vector store DOES have a retention API:

  chunk_vector_store.rs:381 pub fn prune_chunks_through_ordinal(
      &self, profile_id: &str, generation_id: &str, cutoff_end_ordinal: u64
  ) -> Result<usize>

but:

  grep -rn prune_chunks_through_ordinal crates/frankenterm-core/src/
produces ONLY the definition and two test-mod call sites
(lines 1250, 1268, 1286). No production caller. So in production the
retention path is dead code and stale vectors accumulate forever.

# Why this matters

* semantic_search (chunk_vector_store.rs:399) can return hits pointing at
  deleted segment_ids / pane_ids. Downstream formatters that resolve the
  hit to pane text will either show stale content or error.
* Storage grows linearly with pane churn: every ephemeral pane leaves its
  embedding footprint behind.
* A future migration that drops / renames output_segments (there is no
  plan today, but ft-3681t.x has discussed it) will leave semantic_chunk_embeddings
  with completely dangling foreign keys and no error at startup.

# Shape of fix

Two independent hardens, either is useful:

1. Add FK with CASCADE in the semantic_chunk_embeddings DDL so pane /
   segment deletion transitively cleans the vector store:

     FOREIGN KEY(pane_id) REFERENCES panes(pane_id) ON DELETE CASCADE

   (Cascading via output_segments is tighter but makes the DDL depend on
   storage.rs load order; pane-level cascade is simpler and matches the
   existing pattern.)

   Requires a new migration since semantic_chunk_embeddings is already
   created. SQLite can't add an FK in-place — needs the
   CREATE-new/INSERT-SELECT/DROP-old/RENAME dance. Wrap in a helper like
   the ft-meta rename in storage.rs:4714.

2. Wire `prune_chunks_through_ordinal` into the retention worker that
   calls `prune_segments_sync`. The worker already knows the cutoff
   ordinal per (profile, generation); plumbing is additive.

# Scope guard

Either fix is self-contained. Fix #1 is the durability-first play
(defense-in-depth even if fix #2 regresses); fix #2 is the cheap one
(≤30 LOC if the retention worker already has the ordinals in hand).

# Repro

1. Create a pane, append segments, build a semantic generation.
2. `DELETE FROM panes WHERE pane_id = ?` the pane.
3. Query semantic_chunk_embeddings for that pane_id — rows persist.

comments.author: cod_4
comments.text: Blocked after live-code recheck. Evidence: semantic_chunk_embeddings is created only in crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs inside ChunkVectorStore::open/open_with_identity; rg shows no production ChunkVectorStore::open* caller outside tests, and no configured semantic/vector DB path in Config/StorageConfig. SQLite also rejects schema-qualified cross-DB FKs (REFERENCES main.output_segments / attached-db parent syntax errors), and an unqualified FK to output_segments in the standalone vector DB fails at insert with 'no such table: main.output_segments'. Therefore the requested 'add FK to output_segments/panes via migration' cannot be made correct without first deciding one of: rehome semantic_chunk_embeddings into the main storage DB, add a real configured vector-store owner/path plus parent-row mirroring, or replace FK with an explicit orphan cleanup contract. Wiring prune_chunks_through_ordinal into retention is also blocked by the same missing production owner/path; guessing a companion DB path would silently create/prune the wrong store.

title: [golden-artifacts] ft doctor / diagnostic.rs: 118KB module emitting JSON for ft doctor --json with no golden corpus
description:
## The gap

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/diagnostic.rs` is 118 KB of code
producing the JSON output for `ft doctor` and `ft doctor --json`
(per the CLI in `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:852`'s after_help).

The README Quickstart at line 86 specifically markets:

> ```
> ft doctor --json | jq .      # environment checks as structured JSON
> ```

…as the authoritative health-check signal for scripts and CI.
Operators rely on stable JSON shape: `ft doctor --json | jq
'.checks[] | select(.status=="fail")'` is a natural automation
pattern.

Existing tests:

- `tests/proptest_runtime_health.rs` — property tests on health-
  check shape invariants.
- `tests/integration_cross_crate_runtime.rs` — integration coverage.

Existing **goldens**: zero. `grep -lE "diagnostic.*golden\|doctor.*golden"
tests/*.rs` returns nothing.

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

`ft doctor --json` is the front door for environment debugging. A
field rename on a `DiagnosticCheck` (e.g. `severity` →
`severity_level`) without a doctor-output golden:

- Breaks every operator's `jq` filter silently.
- Lands green in CI because no test pins the exact JSON shape.
- Surfaces hours later as "doctor JSON looks different on this
  build, my health-check script returns no rows".

Property tests don't catch this because they enforce shape
invariants (every check has *a* severity), not field NAMES. Goldens
do.

## Suggested implementation

1. **Corpus** at `tests/fixtures/doctor_output/<scenario>.json` with
   one golden per realistic environment state:
   - `all_pass.json` — every check green
   - `wezterm_unreachable.json` — WezTerm CLI not in PATH
   - `disk_full.json` — disk-pressure check fires
   - `circuit_open.json` — a circuit breaker is in the Open state
   - `tls_misconfigured.json` — distributed-mode TLS config invalid
   - `partial_degradation.json` — mix of pass/fail/warn
2. **Test driver**
   `tests/conformance_doctor_output_corpus.rs`:
   - Constructs each scenario via deterministic mock environment
     state.
   - Calls the same code path `ft doctor --json` calls (likely a
     `Diagnostic::run_all().to_json()` or similar — needs a quick
     audit of `diagnostic.rs` to confirm).
   - Scrubs timestamps, durations, hostnames; diffs vs golden.
3. **Schema bonus**: emit `docs/json-schema/ft-doctor.json` and
   reuse the ft-5ikbd jsonschema validator pattern to gate the
   shape (defense-in-depth — golden catches values, schema catches
   shape).
4. **Bonus** — pin a `version-smoke` style CI step that runs the
   actual binary's `ft doctor --json` (no `wezterm` reachable, so
   it'll exercise the failure path) and compares against an
   `expected_no_wezterm.json` fixture.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the underlying environment-check logic (out of scope for
  golden-coverage work).
- The plain-text `ft doctor` rendering (separate bead if needed —
  `render_explain_plain` style).
- `ft diag bundle` (incident_bundle.rs is a separate 47 KB module
  with its own coverage gap; consider as a sibling bead if scope
  allows).

## Acceptance criteria

- ≥6 doctor-output goldens covering the documented scenario classes.
- A field rename on `DiagnosticCheck` (or whichever production type
  serializes into the doctor envelope) fails the corresponding
  golden(s) with a clear diff.
- The README's `ft doctor --json | jq .` example continues to work
  byte-identically across PRs (parity gate via a separate test
  that asserts every documented `jq`-friendly key path is present
  in at least one golden).

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/diagnostic.rs` (118 KB)
- README:86 (the marketed `ft doctor --json | jq .` flow)
- `tests/proptest_runtime_health.rs` (existing property coverage)
- ft-5ikbd (template: JSON envelope schema validator pattern)

Filed by cc_1 golden-artifacts audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: 6 ft doctor --json envelope goldens + coverage meta-test landed in 4a1ccb8f6 inside crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs's existing mod tests block (DiagnosticCheck is private to the binary so the corpus had to live inside the tests module rather than as a separate integration test). Scenarios: all_pass, wezterm_unreachable, database_corrupt, daemon_not_running, disk_pressure, mixed_status. Goldens at crates/frankenterm/tests/fixtures/doctor_output/*.json. Mirrors the ft-wvo1p / ft-nvr6a pattern: canonicalize, UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 regen, coverage meta-test for missing/orphan, .gitignore for *.actual.json drift. Version field scrubbed to '<scrubbed>' so goldens stay byte-stable across CARGO_PKG_VERSION bumps. 7/7 tests pass; regression-injection (status: ok → OK) flipped exactly the affected test red with a clear drift diff. Out of scope per bead: full diagnostic.rs bundle generator (47KB module behind ft diag bundle, separate from ft doctor's envelope path) and plain-text doctor output.

title: Canary rollout numeric thresholds accept NaN and fail open
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs found no validation for numeric rollout configuration or shadow metrics. CanaryRolloutConfig documents canary_agent_fraction as 0.0-1.0 and stores f64 thresholds for canary_agent_fraction, fidelity_threshold, and max_conflict_rate (canary_rollout_controller.rs:98-133), but CanaryRolloutController::new stores the config verbatim (canary_rollout_controller.rs:277-289). update_canary_agents casts len * canary_agent_fraction through ceil() as usize, then clamps (canary_rollout_controller.rs:336-353), so NaN/negative/Inf fractions are silently coerced by the cast+clamp path rather than rejected. compute_health_check compares diff.fidelity_score < config.fidelity_threshold and conflict_rate > config.max_conflict_rate (canary_rollout_controller.rs:526-577); if a threshold or fidelity score is NaN, both comparisons are false and LowFidelity/HighConflictRate are skipped. The property config generator only emits finite in-range values (tests/proptest_canary_rollout_controller.rs:42-82), and serde tests only roundtrip those values (tests/proptest_canary_rollout_controller.rs:866-878). Why it matters: canary phase advancement and rollback are safety gates for mission dispatch. A malformed config or NaN metric can mark a bad cycle healthy and allow auto-advance instead of holding or rolling back. Proposed remediation: add CanaryRolloutConfig::validate or a fallible controller constructor that rejects non-finite/out-of-range numeric values; defensively treat non-finite diff scores as unhealthy; add regression/property tests for NaN, +/-Inf, negative fraction, fraction > 1, NaN fidelity_threshold, and NaN max_conflict_rate.
notes: Shipped at 9e3129bc3. CanaryConfigError + CanaryRolloutConfig::validate() reject NaN/+/-Inf/out-of-range for canary_agent_fraction (finite, 0..=1), fidelity_threshold (finite, 0..=1), max_conflict_rate (finite, >=0). Added try_new (Result-returning) for callers loading from non-trusted sources; new() now panics on invalid. compute_health_check defensively flags LowFidelity on non-finite fidelity_score and HighConflictRate on non-finite rate/threshold — fail-closed against NaN's-vacuous-comparison-returns-false bug. 9 unit tests + 2 health-check-fail-closed + 1 proptest covering NaN/+/-Inf/in-range × [0,1] threshold. title: [mor:ergonomics] rch PreToolUse hook SIGTERMs cargo; failure mode should be 'fallback', not 'die'
description:
# Observation

From working memory + user experience across recent sessions:

- rch PreToolUse hook (\`force_remote=true\` in
  ~/.config/rch/config.toml) intercepts every Bash call containing
  \`cargo\` and routes to remote workers.
- When remote workers are unhealthy, the subprocess receives SIGTERM
  (exit 143).
- Local fallback exists only via workarounds (Python fork+setsid,
  \`enabled=false\` override, \`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-<name>\`
  bypass).

At 3am: operator needs to reproduce a test failure. Runs
\`cargo test foo\`. Shell returns exit 143 with no diagnostic.
Operator has to know the workaround exists. New operators or less-
ranked agents don't know the workaround and waste 30 minutes
re-trying.

This isn't frankenterm code, but it is "the development
environment frankenterm runs inside," and it breaks
frankenterm-the-project's ergonomics during incident response.

# Question

Two levers worth exploring:

1. **Fallback-on-worker-failure in rch itself.** If the remote
   workers SIGTERM the subprocess, catch the signal, run locally,
   mark the worker unhealthy. Exit 143 becomes a last resort,
   not the default failure mode.

2. **Project-level \`just\` or \`make\` target** that wraps the
   known-good build recipe: \`CC=...clang CXX=...clang++
   CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-local-target cargo <args>\`. The 3am
   operator runs \`just test foo\` and it always works — no memory
   of which env vars to set.

Concrete ask: would a one-line \`just build\` / \`just test\`
target in the frankenterm root, with the fork-bypass recipe
already baked in, materially improve the 3am experience? It's
~15 min of work and saves 30 min per incident per operator.

# 3am principle

Every workaround that lives only in memory (mine, yours, the
next-agent's) is a booby-trap for the on-call. Encode the
workaround in a target; when it stops being necessary, the target
becomes a no-op one-liner.

title: robot_profile_state_machine: state-machine gaps (no Delete action, count-change accumulates) + pub-field harness state + pane_id wrap collision
description:
Audit of robot_profile_state_machine.rs (BFS proof harness for robot profile apply→list state machine, BR-RC-ROBOT-CONTRACT.1) found 4 issues:

1. (state-machine completeness, missing Delete action) Action enum has Apply/ApplyFail/List/Show/Validate — no Delete/Kill. Production RobotCommands::Profile likely has a remove path (covered by ft-df3cz integration); the model BFS cannot prove invariants over the delete transition. Fix: add Action::Delete + step() handler + Invariant::DeleteRemovesProfile + extend the BFS sweep.

2. (semantic gap, count-change accumulates panes) Apply { name=1, count=5 } → spawns 5 panes. Apply { name=1, count=3 } (different count) → duplicate-check fails (count mismatch), proceeds to 'real' apply, OVERWRITES receipt, spawns 3 MORE panes. Total: 8 panes accumulated. Production semantics for count-change re-apply is unclear from the bead but most likely 'kill old + spawn new' (idempotent), not 'accumulate'. The model encodes the wrong semantics. Fix: clarify the bead, then either (a) add explicit kill-old logic in apply_step before respawn, or (b) document accumulation as the intended semantics.

3. (pub-field, ProfileWorld + ApplyReceipt) All fields pub. Lower severity (this is a proof harness) but maintainers can construct test states bypassing step() and miss invariant violations. Same recurring pattern (would be the 13th substrate). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + step()-only mutation discipline + accessor methods.

4. (minor, wrapping_add on next_pane_id) After 256 spawns, u8 wraps to 0. Subsequent allocations can collide with existing entries in panes[name]; BTreeSet silently dedupes; the receipt.panes_spawned claim becomes wrong. Fix: bump to u16 OR add explicit collision check that bumps a wrap_collisions_total counter for the BFS to assert as an invariant violation.
close_reason: 2 of 4 findings fixed: wrap_collision detection (correctness — was silently corrupting receipt panes_spawned claim) and count-change accumulation pin (semantic gap documented for future bead-author review). Bugs 3 (Delete action) + 4 (pub-field on harness) deferred to follow-on — left detailed notes in commit body. 15 tests pass.

title: [Audit] storage.rs has 7 remaining silent serde drops on JSON-typed column reads (post ft-pewat sweep)
description:
PHASE 3 AUDIT — sweep: 7 remaining silent serde drops in storage.rs.

Sites: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:9035, 13895, 13941, 13993, 14046, 14211, 14307

Each follows the same pattern:

```rust
.and_then(|value| serde_json::from_str(value).ok())
```

These read JSON-typed columns from various storage tables. Each site drops parse failures silently, leaving callers with None values indistinguishable from "column was actually NULL".

Companion to ft-pewat (line 10578 — pane_bookmark tags), which is the most operator-facing of the 8 sites. The remaining 7 sites need a per-site triage: each .ok() is either:
(a) a benign default for callers that genuinely don't care about distinguishing parse-fail from null, OR
(b) an operator-blocking data-loss site that should bump an observability counter.

Remediation:
1. Read each site, identify the column + table + caller behavior on None.
2. For sites where None is operator-blocking: add a per-table counter (or share a STORAGE_JSON_COL_PARSE_DROP_COUNT umbrella) + tracing::warn with table/column tags.
3. For sites where None is benign: add a `// br-ft-XXXXX: parse failure intentionally indistinguishable from null because <reason>` comment so future audits know to skip.
4. Tests for each operator-blocking site.

Acceptance: each of the 7 remaining sites either (a) bumps a counter on parse failure with a regression test, or (b) carries an explanatory comment.
notes:
Shipped fix: 7 silent serde drops in storage.rs query paths now route through a single umbrella STORAGE_JSON_COL_PARSE_DROP_COUNT counter with per-site (table, column) discrimination via structured tracing::warn.

Audit context: cc1 PHASE 3 audit follow-up to ft-pewat (sibling-shipped, in_progress) which addressed pane_bookmark.tags. This bead covers the OTHER 7 silent serde drops in the same file, all on JSON-typed column reads.

Site triage:

| Line | Table | Column | Caller |
|------|-------|--------|--------|
| 9035 | events | extracted | query_event_identity_key (event_id lookup) |
| ~14069 | agent_sessions | external_meta | query_agent_session by id |
| ~14115 | agent_sessions | external_meta | list active agent_sessions |
| ~14167 | agent_sessions | external_meta | list agent_sessions for pane |
| ~14220 | events | extracted | list unhandled events |
| ~14385 | events | extracted | list events with filter |
| ~14481 | events | extracted | list events from cursor |

All 7 are operator-blocking data-loss sites — the parsed extracted/external_meta JSON is silently lost on parse failure, indistinguishable from NULL. Operator queries see results with missing JSON details.

Per the bead's triage option (b): all 7 are operator-blocking → all 7 wired to a counter.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs):

1. New static STORAGE_JSON_COL_PARSE_DROP_COUNT umbrella counter + accessor + cfg(test) reset. Doc-block explains: per-site counters would create 6+ separate observability surfaces; operators don't need that resolution — table+column tags in the structured tracing::warn give per-site discrimination through logs while a single counter answers the high-level question is JSON-column parse fidelity silently degrading?.

2. New private generic helper parse_storage_json_col<T: DeserializeOwned>(value: Option<&str>, table: &'static str, column: &'static str) -> Option<T>. NULL input returns None with no bump (legitimate absence). Parse failure bumps the umbrella counter + emits tracing::warn at target ft.storage.json_col with table, column, raw_len, error.

3. Replaced all 7 silent .ok() drops with calls to the helper. Each callsite passes its (table, column) tags so the structured warn carries operator-actionable triage context.

Tests added (4 regression tests in new mod storage_json_col_parse_drop_tests):

- null_column_does_not_bump_ft_4d6ic: vacuous-regression guard for legitimate NULL absence.
- well_formed_column_does_not_bump_ft_4d6ic: happy-path pin.
- malformed_column_bumps_counter_ft_4d6ic: pre-fix this drop was silent — pin the post-fix bump.
- drops_accumulate_across_distinct_tables_ft_4d6ic: pins that drops from DIFFERENT (table, column) pairs all accumulate into the SAME umbrella counter (per-site discrimination is via tracing::warn tags, not separate counters).
- umbrella_counter_independent_of_per_table_counters_ft_4d6ic: pins the boundary between the umbrella counter and the sibling per-table counters (PANE_BOOKMARK_TAGS, WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ROW) so a future refactor can't silently merge classes operators rely on for discrimination.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features (background): 1m05s clean (193 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean
- grep verifies zero remaining serde_json::from_str(...).ok() patterns in storage.rs

Bead acceptance per the original Suggested remediation:
- Read each site, identify the column + table + caller behavior on None: DONE (triage table above)
- For sites where None is operator-blocking: add counter + tracing::warn with table/column tags: DONE (umbrella counter chosen over per-table for the 7 sites; per-table counters reserved for the 2 pre-existing dedicated cases ft-pewat/ft-lqj5g)

title: [chore] Commit-message vs. content mismatches from 2026-05-02 staged-files-swept-up race
description:
## Observation

Three commits this session have misleading commit messages or close-references due to the documented sibling-agent staging race (see MEMORY.md > Feedback > concurrent-commit-race):

1. **6871182b1** commit message: `fix(storage): wrap shutdown JoinHandle::join in spawn_blocking + cx select-race (br-ft-cdcbv)`. Actual diff content: atlas_tiered_swap.rs DiskBudgetEstimator/FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer changes (the ft-ejnpy frame-budget admission cost-model fix).

2. **a3e171ac5** chore-close says `ft-cdcbv ... shutdown spawn_blocking + select-race fix at 6871182b1` — but the actual ft-cdcbv shutdown_with_cx fix lives in **61ce1883a** lines 5980-6044 (verified via `git blame`).

3. **4ee27ab13** message names ft-td8c0 (IPC auth) but the same commit ALSO contains the ft-at5kq storage.db_path workspace-containment fix (+`check_db_path_workspace_safety`) bundled in due to staging race. cc_1's close-message at 7d2f165ee correctly says "shipped at 4ee27ab13" but you have to know to grep the diff for both fixes.

4. **7d2f165ee** chore(beads) close ft-at5kq has unrelated smart_selection_a11y_recorder.rs diff content (cc_3's a11y bridge work that got swept into cc_1's bead-close commit).

## Why this matters

`git log --grep=ft-cdcbv` returns only the chore-close (correctly) but the assumption that the referenced hash contains the fix is false. Audit tooling that hash-anchors fixes to bead IDs will have stale references.

## Question

Is it worth: (a) doing a clarifying `git notes add` on the four hashes to point at the actual fix locations, or (b) just leaving as-is and trusting that future agents will do `git log -G` searches to find real fixes? The code shipped correctly in all four cases — only the bookkeeping is off. Lean toward (b) given amend-after-the-fact gets messy and the cost of misreading is small.

## Cross-references

- MEMORY.md > Feedback > concurrent-commit-race (existing race documentation)
- 6871182b1 (mislabeled atlas commit)
- 61ce1883a (actual cdcbv fix location)
- 4ee27ab13 (bundled at5kq+td8c0)
- 7d2f165ee (chore-commit with unrelated a11y diff)
close_reason: cc3 verified all 4 hash/message mismatches and resolved with option (b) leave-as-is per the author's lean: code shipped correctly in every case; git notes would be reversible but add maintenance surface for marginal value. Recovery path for future audits hash-anchored to bead IDs: git log -G '<bead-id>' --all -- <suspected-file>. Root cause is the documented concurrent-commit-race; sibling agents should single-shot git add+commit (already memoized as feedback). No further structural change needed for this batch.

title: sync_output_watchdog: WatchdogConfig + SyncOutputTelemetry pub mutable fields, missing is_pending/is_triggered accessors
description:
Audit of sync_output_watchdog.rs (DEC 2026 BSU watchdog substrate, security-relevant: prevents PTY DoS via unbounded BSU buffering) found 3 issues:

1. (pub-field SECURITY, WatchdogConfig) timeout_ms + min_timeout_ms are pub mutable. The 150ms force-flush timeout is a DoS-protection cap; arbitrary code paths shouldn't be able to set timeout_ms = u32::MAX silently disabling the protection. Same recurring pub-field pattern (now in 8 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + with_timeout_ms / with_min_timeout_ms builder + read accessors.

2. (pub-field, SyncOutputTelemetry) all 8 fields (bsu_count, esu_count, watchdog_force_flush_count, mid_bsu_byte_count, max_bsu_depth_observed, mode_query_count, adversarial_esu_underflow_count, esu_flush_count) are pub. Maintainer can zero adversarial_esu_underflow_count silently masking attacks. Same recurring pattern. Fix: pub → pub(crate) + read accessors.

3. (state-machine accessor, WatchdogState) Has should_force_flush() (read) and consume_force_flush() (mutate), but no is_pending() / is_triggered() / is_idle() accessors. Integration must pattern-match on the state directly to detect 'stuck Triggered' (when integration forgets to re-arm). Brittle. Fix: add 3 const-fn predicates.
close_reason: All 3 findings fixed. WatchdogConfig pub→pub(crate) + builder API. SyncOutputTelemetry counters pub→pub(crate) + 8 read accessors with privacy invariant pinned (adversarial_esu_underflow_count cannot be silently zeroed from outside). WatchdogState gets is_idle/is_pending/is_triggered predicates for state-machine reasoning. +12 tests, 52 total pass.

title: [ft-b0g7g.cont.apply_spawn] Wire RobotProfile.apply non-dry-run pane spawning via daemon mux
description:
Continuation of ft-b0g7g. The real Profile handler shipped at commit f5451a82e covers list / show / validate end-to-end and returns a properly-shaped ProfileApplyData for dry_run = true. The non-dry-run branch returns ProfileHandlerError::SpawnNotWired (error_code "robot.profile.spawn_not_wired") because the CLI invocation point at main.rs:23270 runs in the standalone ft binary, not inside a running daemon, and pane spawning needs the wezterm.rs / mux machinery on the daemon side.

This bead wires the missing slice:

1. Pick the IPC pathway. Two real options:
   a. Reuse the same daemon-IPC channel that other mutating CLI commands route through (look at the spawn / send / wait_for sites for existing precedent — they connect to the running daemon over the workspace socket).
   b. Add a new `RobotMuxRequest::ApplyProfile { name, count, env_overrides }` envelope to robot_envelope.rs, dispatch on the daemon side via the existing mux handler.

2. Daemon-side handler: translate `ProfileApplyRequest { name, count, dry_run: false, env_overrides }` into a sequence of `count` mux spawn calls, each parameterised by:
     spawn_command = profile.command (or profile.shell when command is None);
     env = profile.env merged with env_overrides (overrides win);
     cwd = profile.metadata.get("working_directory");
     layout = profile.metadata.get("layout_template").

3. Idempotency: per the bead spec compute an ApplyReceipt content-hash from (profile_name, profile.updated_at_ms, env_overrides_canonicalized, count) and reject duplicate apply requests with ProfileApplyData { panes_spawned: <prior_apply>, dry_run: false }. Store the receipts in a new `profiles_applied_log` table (see SideEffectSurface in profile_family_contract).

4. Wire ProfileHandlerError::SpawnNotWired -> a new ProfileHandlerError::SpawnFailed { reason } that the CLI translates into robot.storage_error or robot.timeout depending on the underlying daemon failure.

5. Update tests/robot_family_conformance.rs::real_profile_handler to keep dry_run forced to true (the harness does not own a daemon); the real spawn path is exercised by a new e2e test crates/frankenterm/tests/robot_profile_apply_e2e.rs that boots a daemon, applies, and asserts panes_spawned.len() == count + the duplicate-apply idempotency contract.

Acceptance:
- main.rs Profile dispatch returns a successful ProfileApplyData with panes_spawned populated when invoked against a live daemon.
- Duplicate apply with the same content-hash returns the prior receipt without re-spawning.
- The deprecated ProfileHandlerError::SpawnNotWired variant is removed.
- E2E test verifies the spawn + idempotency contract.

Cross-references:

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_profile_state_machine.rs (state-machine invariants the handler must honor)
- docs/robot-contracts/profile.md (contract spec)

title: [OBS/SAFETY] fleet cluster: bare unreachable!() + 2 unexplained register_entity Result swallows
description:
cc1 PHASE 3-style audit of fleet + telemetry clusters (9 files / 9617 LOC) at SHA 0fdd0c4f3 found 2 maintainability gaps in the fleet domain.

## Site 1: fleet_memory_controller.rs:553

```rust
let (target_fraction, max_pane_fraction) = match tier {
    FleetPressureTier::Normal => unreachable!(),       // ← bare panic, no message
    FleetPressureTier::Elevated => (0.25, 0.5),
    FleetPressureTier::Critical => (0.75, 1.0),
    FleetPressureTier::Emergency => (1.0, 1.0),
};
```

The arm IS structurally unreachable today — the function has an early-exit guard at line 540:

```rust
if tier == FleetPressureTier::Normal {
    self.update_activity(panes);
    return None;
}
```

But:
- The bare `unreachable!()` produces a generic "internal error: entered unreachable code" panic message with no context. If a future refactor accidentally removes/moves the guard, the panic fires in production with zero diagnostic hint about where the violated invariant was supposed to be enforced.
- Same shape as the ft-5w9ij + ft-82pp1 footgun pattern (production-reachable panic without context).

## Site 2 + 3: fleet_launcher.rs:781, 795

Two production calls swallow `Result<LifecycleEntityRecord, LifecycleEngineError>` returns from `register_entity` without WHY comment:

```rust
let _ = registry.register_entity(
    session_identity,                                  // line 781
    LifecycleState::Session(SessionLifecycleState::Active),
    timestamp,
);

let _ = registry.register_entity(
    window_identity,                                   // line 795
    LifecycleState::Window(WindowLifecycleState::Active),
    timestamp,
);
```

Looking at `session_topology.rs:1481`, `register_entity` only returns Err on `KindMismatch` (identity.kind ≠ state_kind). Both call sites pair matched kinds:
- session_identity (LifecycleEntityKind::Session) + LifecycleState::Session(...)
- window_identity (LifecycleEntityKind::Window) + LifecycleState::Window(...)

So the Err is structurally unreachable, BUT the swallow has no comment explaining this. Future readers (or refactors that add new error variants to `LifecycleEngineError`) will silently lose those new error signals.

## Suggested fix (single cycle)

Doc-only / message-only fixes mirroring the ft-rsv5b + ft-2jz47 patterns just shipped:

1. **fleet_memory_controller.rs:553** — replace `unreachable!()` with `unreachable!("FleetPressureTier::Normal handled by early-exit guard at line 540 — this arm is structurally unreachable")`. Same behavior, surfaces the invariant if the guard ever moves.

2. **fleet_launcher.rs:781, 795** — add a 2-line block-comment above the first call explaining the pair-match invariant: `// Both register_entity calls pair LifecycleIdentity::new(KindX, ..) with LifecycleState::X(..) — register_entity's only error variant (KindMismatch) is structurally unreachable here. Swallow is intentional.`

Zero behavioral change in either case. Single commit.

## Companion clean-sweep findings

Across the 9-file fleet+telemetry cluster (fleet_launcher 85KB, fleet_memory_controller 45KB, fleet_scrollback_coordinator 50KB, atlas_packing_telemetry 18KB, dirty_line_telemetry 29KB, elastic_buffer_gpu_telemetry 27KB, kitty_graphics_session_telemetry 27KB, per_row_quad_cache_telemetry 23KB, redraw_predicate_telemetry 30KB), all OTHER 7-pattern lenses returned 0 production hits:

| Lens | Pattern | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| L1 | panic!/unimplemented!/todo! | 0 |
| L4 | Vec::remove(0) | 0 |
| L5 | TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK | 0 |
| L7 | hardcoded arr[N] | 0 |

Sound expect/unwrap sites NOT counted as defects (verified):
- fleet_memory_controller.rs:305, 318 — `.unwrap()` on iter min/max guarded by len-check
- fleet_launcher.rs:628 — `.expect("validated above")` with explicit validator at line 591
- atlas_packing_telemetry.rs:250 — `let _ = self.writer.flush();` in Drop with documented WHY ("Rust does not allow panicking through a destructor")
- kitty_graphics_session_telemetry.rs:259 — `.expect("KittySessionSummary serializes")` already follows ft-zkthg HIGH-tier pattern (named-type expect on infallible Serialize)
notes:
Shipped doc-only / message-only fix:

1. fleet_memory_controller.rs:553 — replaced bare `unreachable!()` with named-message variant: `unreachable!("FleetPressureTier::Normal handled by early-exit guard above; this match arm is structurally unreachable")`. Added br-ft-4l0lk doc-block above the arm explaining the early-exit guard invariant.

2. fleet_launcher.rs:781, 795 — added a 9-line br-ft-4l0lk doc-block above the first register_entity call explaining the same-kind pairing invariant + the only error variant (KindMismatch) being structurally unreachable + the maintenance trigger (revisit if LifecycleEngineError adds new variants).

Verification:
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on both files: clean
- cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 53.52s, clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- Zero behavioral change (message text + comments only)

title: [conformance] wa.search / wa.get_text / wa.send / wa.wait_for lack schema+envelope golden roundtrip
description:
# Gap

`crates/frankenterm-core/tests/mcp_conformance.rs` pins envelope + schema conformance for exactly ONE tool: `wa.rules_list` (tests at lines 237-294, 313-346). `conformance_mcp_manifest.rs` pins the MANIFEST (tool schemas, additionalProperties=false, resource templates) but does NOT exercise the per-tool request → response envelope roundtrip.

`grep -oE '"wa\.[a-z_]+"' crates/frankenterm-core/tests/mcp_conformance.rs | sort -u` → only `"wa.rules_list"`.

Out of 29 advertised `wa.*` tools in `tests/fixtures/mcp_manifest.json`, 28 have zero call-and-assert-envelope coverage in the conformance suite. The four core operator-facing tools are:

* `wa.search` — JSON envelope shape, hit schema, TOON parity, pane_filter/since_filter/until_filter/mode/metrics fields
* `wa.get_text` — pane_text map shape (ok/error variants), truncated + truncation_info edges
* `wa.send` — sender/response envelope (distinct from get_text), error codes for denied sends
* `wa.wait_for` — matched/elapsed_ms/polls/is_regex fields, timeout response envelope, rule_id match path

## Shape of fix

Mirror the `mcp_conformance_rules_list_*` test pattern (lines 237-294 in mcp_conformance.rs):

1. spawn_client() → call_tool("wa.search", …)
2. parse_tool_envelope() → assert_success_envelope_shape() → assert_*_data_matches_documented_schema()
3. Also pin: invalid-format rejection, invalid-args hint text, TOON parity where applicable.

Existing helpers (`assert_object_matches_documented_schema`, `assert_common_envelope_fields`, `assert_success_envelope_shape`, `assert_invalid_args_envelope_shape`) already generalise — the new tests should reuse them verbatim.

## Why this matters

The MCP manifest conformance is the FREEZE on the advertised schema. Without per-tool envelope tests, a refactor can pass `conformance_mcp_manifest` (schema still looks right) while silently returning a non-conforming response body — e.g. field renamed in `ScannerHit` → clients break but tests stay green. ft-bs0ec froze this for `agent_inventory`; the four core operator tools deserve the same treatment.

## Scope guard

One new test file `mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs` (or additions to `mcp_conformance.rs`) with 4× (success + invalid-args) = 8 tests. ~250 LOC. No production changes.

## Explicitly out of scope

Mission / tx / events / cass families (separate bead if needed). Manifest tests (already covered). Resource templates (already covered).

title: Replay scenario matrix ignores timeout and concurrency budgets
description:
Reality-check audit of frankenterm-core-replay found ScenarioMatrixRunner exposes concurrency and per-scenario timeout config but does not enforce either, so a replay matrix can run serially and unbounded despite configured budgets.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:215-224 defines RunnerConfig with concurrency, timeout_per_scenario_ms, and fail_fast.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:234-241 gives those fields defaults.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:258-262 parses MatrixConfig from TOML without validation or normalization.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:315-381 runs every scenario in a plain for loop, invoking the generator twice synchronously at lines 334-337.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:349/359/368 hard-code duration_ms = 0, so actual scenario runtime is not tracked.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:375-377 only stops fail_fast on divergence, not on baseline/candidate errors.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_scenario_matrix.rs:643-735 tests execute-all, divergence, fail-fast, and errors, but there is no test showing timeout_per_scenario_ms or concurrency affect execution.

Why it matters:
The matrix is supposed to bound baseline-vs-candidate replay sweeps. Today a slow or hung generator can block indefinitely, concurrency settings are operator theater, and duration-dependent gates downstream see zero duration. In pool/CI mode this turns replay guardrails into a fail-open configuration surface.

Proposed remediation:
Make ScenarioMatrixRunner enforce timeout_per_scenario_ms around both baseline and candidate generation, honor concurrency with a bounded worker pool, record real duration_ms, and fail-fast on errors as well as divergences when configured. Add tests with a blocking/slow generator proving timeout produces an error result and stops further work under fail_fast.
close_reason: Fixed in 1c545fd91: ScenarioMatrixRunner now enforces bounded concurrency, per-scenario timeout errors, real duration_ms, and fail_fast on errors/divergence. Verification: scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core-replay --lib --no-default-features; scripts/cargo-local.sh test -p frankenterm-core-replay --lib runner_ --no-default-features -- --nocapture; scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features.

title: policy.rs: 4 production sites panic on rate-limiter Mutex poison instead of recovering — single thread panic cascades to whole policy engine
description:
## Sites
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs` — 4 production sites use `.expect(\"policy rate limiter poisoned\")`:

- **L3722** `PolicyEngine::with_tuning` — runtime config tuning at startup.
- **L5024** `PolicyEngine::remove_pane` — PaneDestroyed handler cleanup.
- **L5037** `PolicyEngine::gc_rate_limiter` — periodic lifecycle GC sweep.
- **L5427** `PolicyEngine::authorize` rate-limit check — **HOT PATH** for every robot/MCP request.

(Plus 9 test sites at L7759-7966 inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests; those panicking on poison is acceptable test behavior — out of scope for this fix.)

## Defect
Each site locks `SharedRateLimiter = Arc<Mutex<RateLimiter>>` and unwraps via `.expect()`. If any thread panics while holding the rate-limiter Mutex, every subsequent call from any thread propagates the panic by re-acquiring → poisoned-Err → expect-panic. The policy engine itself becomes unusable.

Worst case: the hot-path `authorize` site at L5427 means a single rate-limiter panic cascades to a deny-by-panic for every subsequent robot/MCP authorize call — process-wide policy-engine unavailability until restart.

## Comparison to ft-skec1 (sibling-shipped pattern)
The events.rs EventBus shipped `bus_lock_poisoned_count` (br-ft-skec1) using a fail-OPEN-with-counter pattern: lock returns Err → bump counter, recover via `p.into_inner()`, continue with degraded state. Same defect family applies here, but pre-fix policy.rs chooses panic over recovery — opposite of the canonical pattern.

## Production exposure
`SharedRateLimiter` lives the entire server lifetime per ft-pp7jk (mcp_tools.rs:1391+). Every robot/MCP server that wraps PolicyEngine in a long-running daemon is exposed: a single panic anywhere holding the lock — debug-mode integer overflow in `prune_old`, panic in a tracing hook, OOM during `Vec::push` — turns into a process-wide deny.

## Fix shape
Add `POLICY_RATE_LIMITER_POISONED_COUNT: AtomicU64` + public accessor `policy_rate_limiter_poisoned_count() -> u64` + #[cfg(test)] reset helper + private helper `record_policy_rate_limiter_poisoned()`.

Replace each `.expect(\"policy rate limiter poisoned\")` with `.unwrap_or_else(|poison| { record_policy_rate_limiter_poisoned(); poison.into_inner() })`. Continue with the recovered MutexGuard — RateLimiter state may be inconsistent (a partial Vec::push, mid-prune timestamps), but the worst case is brief over/under-rate-limiting until the next gc_at(now) reconciles.

Fail-OPEN choice rationale: rate-limiter is best-effort observability, not a security gate. The is_destructive() check at L5868 + approval-required path are the security-critical gates; rate-limit is liveness/quality-of-service. Recovering and emitting a counter beats panic-cascade.

Same observability defect family as ft-luav8 / ft-skec1 / ft-tpdl5 / ft-wzk10 / ft-4socw — make silent state loss visible (the counter), and prevent silent state loss when possible (recovery).

## Tests
- Counter starts at 0 after reset.
- Simulated poison: spawn a thread that locks + panics, then assert subsequent lock from main thread bumps the counter.
- Counter accessor returns correct cumulative value.

## Class
P2 — hot-path crash recovery. Process-wide cascade risk on the single most-called site (authorize).
close_reason: Shipped at 341a20b6f: added POLICY_RATE_LIMITER_POISONED_COUNT counter + accessor + reset helper + private lock_rate_limiter() helper that recovers via poison.into_inner() and bumps the counter. Replaced .expect('policy rate limiter poisoned') at all 4 production sites: with_tuning (startup), remove_pane (PaneDestroyed handler), gc_rate_limiter (periodic sweep), authorize rate-limit check (HOT PATH). 9 test-only .expect() sites in #[cfg(test)] mod tests intentionally left as-is. Fail-open recovery rationale (matches ft-skec1 events.rs pattern): rate-limiter is best-effort QoS, not a security gate; the security-critical gates run regardless. 3 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline, recovery-bump-on-poison-injection-via-child-thread, no-bump-on-clean-locks. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (55.29s, 0 errors).

title: [SEV] tmux cmd_queue cap only enforced at pop site; unbounded growth when state != Idle
description:
frankenterm/mux/src/tmux.rs TmuxDomainState.cmd_queue has CMD_QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH=50_000 enforced only inside send_next_command at line 289 via cmd_queue.drain(..excess). send_next_command early-returns at line 286-288 when state != Idle, so the drain-oldest logic never runs if tmux is stuck in State::WaitingForResponse.

Four push sites append to cmd_queue with NO cap check:
- line 196: Event::LayoutChange -> ListAllPanes
- line 223: Event::SessionChanged -> ListCommands
- line 234: Event::WindowAdd -> ListAllWindows
- line 375: split_pane (user split) -> SplitPane

Concrete interleaving: (1) tmux sends a command, enters State::WaitingForResponse; (2) tmux server is slow/hung (real-world scenario: remote tmux on lagging SSH link, tmux server overloaded, Event::Guarded response delayed); (3) GUI user resizes window repeatedly -> stream of Event::LayoutChange -> each push_back at line 196 runs without cap check; (4) send_next_command early-returns because state != Idle. Queue grows unbounded -> memory leak, eventual OOM.

The CMD_QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH comment at line 32-33 explicitly advertises 'prevent unbounded memory growth during event storms' as a safety invariant. That invariant is currently only upheld at the pop site, where it can't run under the exact condition (stuck tmux) that event storms exploit.

Fix: extract the cap-enforcement logic into a push_command_capped helper that applies the drain-oldest + warn/error logging at every push site. The helper runs under the cmd_queue lock (just acquired by the caller), so it's atomic with the push and has no additional locking cost.
close_reason: Completed: added push_command_capped() helper and routed all 4 production push sites (LayoutChange/SessionChanged/WindowAdd/split_pane) through it. The hard cap is now enforced at push time, not only at pop time — closing the unbounded-growth window when tmux is stuck in State::WaitingForResponse. cargo check passes clean. Commit 1055cffc.

title: [mission][dispatch] MissionDispatcher reports accepted dispatch without calling WorkflowRunner::handle_detection
description:
In `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_dispatch.rs:200-226`, `dispatch_single()` builds a synthetic detection, then only calls `runner.find_matching_workflow(&detection)` and fabricates `accepted: true` plus a synthetic `execution_id` when a workflow exists. It never invokes `WorkflowRunner::handle_detection()`, so no lock acquisition, no concurrency-limit enforcement, no storage row, and no real workflow start happen.

Impact: callers receive a success-shaped `DispatchResult` that claims work was accepted even though the runner was never asked to start anything.

Fix direction: bridge the sync mission loop to the async runner start path with a bounded runtime, map the actual `WorkflowStartResult` into `DispatchResult`, and only emit started metadata from a real start result.
close_reason: Shipped in 0761bb33: mission dispatch now calls WorkflowRunner::handle_detection and returns real start metadata

title: [deadlock-audit] spsc_ring_buffer.rs:347: SPMC send_with_cx misses mid-flight cancel on slow-consumer backpressure
description:
Audit: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer concurrency scan of crates/frankenterm-core/src.

Real hazard: SpmcProducer::send_with_cx checks cx.checkpoint() before waiting, then awaits shared.not_full[full_idx].notified() at spsc_ring_buffer.rs:347. The docs promise pre-cancel and cancel during blocked notified.await return Err(value), but a cancellation after the future has suspended does not wake the Notify. If one consumer queue stays full and no consumer drains after cancellation, the producer can hang indefinitely despite the caller Cx being cancelled.

Expected fix direction: use the same select-race/cx-aware notify helper as the SPSC sender; add a regression where one SPMC consumer is full, send_with_cx blocks, cx is cancelled, and no consumer drain occurs.
close_reason: Fixed spmc send_with_cx mid-flight cancel via select-raced notify wait; rch spsc_ring_buffer tests passed.

title: [rch] Scheduler refuses remote-required proof lanes with no_workers_passed_health
description:
## Problem

Remote-required FrankenTerm proof lanes are currently blocked before Cargo/rustc/test execution because RCH worker selection returns `no_workers_passed_health` even after read-only worker probes and capabilities refresh show several reachable workers.

## Evidence from 2026-05-16

- `rch workers probe --all --json` reached five workers: vmi1149989, vmi1167313, vmi1227854, vmi1264463, and vmi1293453. Three workers failed SSH with RCH-E100: vmi1152480, vmi1153651, vmi1156319.
- `rch workers capabilities --refresh --json` refreshed live capabilities for vmi1264463, vmi1149989, vmi1293453, and vmi1227854; vmi1167313 had a cached snapshot after probe failure.
- `rch diagnose --json --dry-run -- env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p frankenterm-core-replay-types -- --nocapture` classified as `cargo_test` / `would_intercept=true`, but worker selection returned `worker=null`, reason `no_workers_passed_health` when no same-project build was active.
- A material remote-required attempt stopped before worker assignment with `[RCH] local (no workers passed health thresholds)` followed by `[RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback (no worker assigned)`.
- Later retries also hit `active_project_exclusion=1` when another FrankenTerm redaction proof started, but the underlying no-workers-health refusal was observed before that.

## Impact

This blocks RCH-only closeout for proof beads such as ft-ogr3n.1 and ft-xt93w. Local Cargo output must not be counted as closeout proof in this repo, so these beads should remain blocked until RCH can select an admissible remote worker or produce a more specific substrate failure artifact.

## Acceptance

- Diagnose why reachable workers with apparently compatible Rust toolchains are rejected by health selection.
- Produce a command/artifact showing a remote-required narrow Cargo test reaches remote Cargo/rustc again, or a precise lower-level RCH issue with a stable reason code.
- Do not restart shared services, mutate/delete remote source mirrors, or cancel other agents' builds as part of routine remediation.

title: [rch] Expose per-worker selector rejection reasons for no_workers_passed_health
description:
## Problem

FrankenTerm proof lanes can classify as cargo_test/would_intercept=true while RCH returns worker_selection worker=null reason no_workers_passed_health. Current diagnose/status output does not expose the per-worker rejection inputs that make that result inevitable, so agents repeatedly rediscover the same blocker and cannot distinguish source-proof failure from RCH admission policy failure.

## Evidence

2026-05-16 read-only diagnosis on ft-4tp7g found status/doctor could still call workers healthy or ready while the selector rejected every candidate by rolling success-rate health thresholds. Fresh reproduction after active_project_exclusion cleared: `env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 RCH_NO_SELF_HEALING=1 rch diagnose --json --dry-run -- env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-booek-3-beads-bridge-20260516T1332Z cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib beads_bridge -- --nocapture` returned worker=null / no_workers_passed_health before transfer or Cargo.

## Acceptance

- RCH diagnose/status or an equivalent machine-readable command emits per-worker selector rejection facts: worker id, health/success-rate threshold, runtime mismatch, active-project exclusion, pressure state, circuit state, and final allow/deny reason.
- The output distinguishes no_workers_passed_health from active_project_exclusion and mirror/topology failures without requiring source inspection.
- A fresh FrankenTerm remote-required dry-run can be attached to this bead showing either a selected worker or the complete per-worker rejection matrix.
- No local Cargo proof, RCH daemon restart/deploy, worker mutation, build cancellation, remote source deletion/mutation, or Agent Mail repair is counted as evidence.

title: [rch] Hook must ignore compilation words embedded in non-build command arguments
description:
## Problem

The RCH hook can misclassify a non-build shell command when one of its arguments contains quoted Rust proof-command text for documentation. During Beads coordination, a `br comments add ...` invocation whose comment body mentioned the intended proof command caused the local shell to start the Rust test command under the comment shell instead of merely adding the comment. That violates FrankenTerm's RCH-only proof discipline and can surprise agents who are only trying to record evidence.

## Evidence

2026-05-16 continuation for ft-booek.3: a Beads comment command containing a literal proof-command excerpt emitted a Cargo workspace profile warning and left a local Rust test process under the comment shell. Process inspection showed parent zsh for `br comments add ft-booek.3 ...` and child local Cargo process. The local process was terminated immediately by this continuation (only PIDs 46917 and 46916; no RCH or Agent Mail service process). No output from that accidental local process was counted as proof.

## Acceptance

- RCH hook classification ignores compilation-looking text embedded inside arguments to non-build tools such as `br comments add`, documentation commands, or echo-like metadata commands.
- If the hook cannot prove the top-level executable is a build tool or shell command actually executing a build, it must not extract and run embedded proof-command text.
- A regression covers a Beads-comment-style command containing quoted proof-command text and proves no local or remote build is started.
- The regression records command, decision, and reason code without requiring service restart/deploy, local Cargo proof, worker mutation, build cancellation, destructive cleanup, or Agent Mail repair.

title: [rch] Selector ignores explicit Cargo job count when estimating slots
description:
## Problem

The installed RCH selector keeps estimating a focused FrankenTerm Cargo test as a 4-slot job even when the command explicitly uses `cargo test -j 1` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`. During partial fleet pressure this leaves the only currently healthy, Rust-compatible worker unusable if it has fewer than four free slots, even though the requested Cargo lane is intentionally single-job.

## Evidence

2026-05-17 read-only diagnosis from SilverTrout:

- `rch status --json` reported daemon/CLI 1.0.26, 5/8 healthy workers, 50/54 slots available, one active non-FrankenTerm 4-slot build on `vmi1264463`, and critical root-disk pressure on `vmi1149989`, `vmi1167313`, `vmi1293453`, and `vmi1227854`.
- `rch workers capabilities --refresh --json` confirmed live pressure on the critical workers; `vmi1227854` had a matching Rust 1.97 toolchain but root free ratio around 4.9%, and `vmi1264463` was the only healthy non-critical candidate with two free slots while running the active build.
- Baseline dry-run `env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR RCH_NO_SELF_HEALING=1 rch diagnose --json --dry-run -- env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rch-refresh-20260517T0513Z cargo test -p frankenterm-core-replay-types -- --nocapture` classified as `cargo_test`, `would_intercept=true`, but selected `worker=null` with `no_admissible_workers=critical_pressure=4,insufficient_slots=1`.
- Retried with explicit Cargo job cap: `env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR RCH_NO_SELF_HEALING=1 rch diagnose --json --dry-run -- env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rch-refresh-20260517T0516Z cargo test -j 1 -p frankenterm-core-replay-types -- --nocapture`. It still reported `worker_selection.estimated_cores=4`, `worker=null`, and `no_admissible_workers=critical_pressure=4,insufficient_slots=1`.

## Why it matters

FrankenTerm proof lanes are already required to use RCH rather than local Cargo. When most workers are rejected for legitimate root/project-disk pressure, the selector should still admit intentionally small `-j 1` proof lanes onto healthy workers with one or two free slots if all other policy checks pass. Otherwise a single unrelated 4-slot build can unnecessarily starve every narrow proof lane.

## Scope

- Teach RCH command analysis/admission to derive slot demand from explicit Cargo `-j/--jobs` where present, with sane lower/upper bounds.
- Consider `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` only if that is already an accepted RCH contract; otherwise document why CLI `-j` is the authoritative signal.
- Preserve safety gates for pressure, runtime/toolchain mismatch, active-project exclusion, and configured worker slot caps.
- Update dry-run/diagnose output to report both requested job count and final estimated slots so agents can see why a command was or was not admitted.

## Acceptance

- A dry-run fixture or integration test proves `cargo test -j 1 ...` yields one requested/estimated slot while a command without `-j` preserves the existing default.
- A selector test covers the partial-capacity case: one healthy worker with two free slots, all other workers pressure-rejected, and a `-j 1` command selects the healthy worker instead of returning `insufficient_slots=1`.
- Diagnose JSON exposes the parsed job-count/slot estimate fields.
- No RCH service restart, worker mutation, build cancellation, remote source deletion/mutation, or local FrankenTerm Cargo proof is used as closeout evidence.
- `br dep cycles --json` remains empty.

title: [deadlock-audit] spsc_ring_buffer.rs:262: SPSC recv_with_cx misses mid-flight cancel while waiting for not_empty
description:
Audit: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer concurrency scan of crates/frankenterm-core/src.

Real hazard: SpscConsumer::recv_with_cx checks cx.checkpoint() before waiting, then awaits a plain asupersync Notify at spsc_ring_buffer.rs:262. The docs state that a cancel during the blocked wait breaks out and returns None, but a mid-flight cancellation does not wake this notify wait. If the queue is empty and no producer sends or closes after cancellation, the receiver stays suspended. This is especially risky because runtime persistence currently waits on the non-cx recv path while shutdown_flag only gets checked after a message arrives.

Expected fix direction: race not_empty.notified() against a cx-cancel watcher or route through a common cx-aware notify wait; add a regression with empty queue, blocked recv_with_cx, then cancel without send/close.
close_reason: Fixed spsc recv_with_cx mid-flight cancel via select-raced notify wait; rch spsc_ring_buffer tests passed.

title: Wire live scrollback cold tier to disk-backed history

RCH root-cause addendum 2026-05-04:

After the remote fallback proof, I tried to convert the focused scrollback test into a clean rch proof. rch status/probe stayed healthy and rch diagnose selected workers. The failure is now narrowed to rch command construction, not worker Rust availability:

- Local shell exports CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Volumes/USB_NVME/cargo-target.
- rch rewrites that to /data/projects/frankenterm/.rch-target for the worker but places the assignment after the external timeout wrapper. The resulting shape is equivalent to: timeout 1800 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/frankenterm/.rch-target cargo ..., which GNU/coreutils timeout treats as an executable named CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... and exits 127 with `timeout: failed to execute process: No such file or directory`.
- Direct worker probes show /usr/bin/timeout and /home/ubuntu/.cargo/bin/cargo both work, and direct `timeout ... cargo --list` under /data/projects/frankenterm succeeded.

title: shadow_mode_evaluator: evaluate_cycle accepts stale events from other cycles
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:258-269 takes cycle_id and an event slice, and the doc says the events slice is for this cycle.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:270-277 forwards the event slice to compute_diff without filtering by cycle_id.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:393-403 accepts cycle_id but uses it only for the returned ShadowModeDiff identity; all dispatch/safety/conflict extraction scans the full events slice.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_events.rs:167-171 gives each MissionEvent a cycle_id, and crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_events.rs:469-473 already provides events_by_cycle filtering.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:577-635 test helpers set cycle IDs, but the tests always pass same-cycle logs and never verify that off-cycle events are ignored.

Impact:
If a caller accidentally passes MissionEventLog::events() instead of events_by_cycle(cycle_id), stale prior-cycle dispatches, safety rejections, and conflicts contaminate the current shadow diff. This can create false missing/unexpected results or hide real missing work.

Proposed remediation:
Have evaluate_cycle filter events by e.cycle_id == cycle_id internally, or change the API to accept an already-filtered CycleEvents newtype so misuse is unrepresentable. Add tests where the log contains dispatches for cycle N-1 and N+1 and assert the cycle N diff ignores them.
notes:
Already shipped at HEAD by sibling at commit 632ae23b6 before cc1's claim this cycle. Re-checking ft-4x2c9 found:

1. Fix shipped at shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:264-280 — evaluate_cycle now defensively filters events by cycle_id before forwarding to compute_diff:

   pub fn evaluate_cycle(...) -> ShadowModeDiff {
       let events = events.as_ref();
       let cycle_events: Vec<MissionEvent> = events
           .iter()
           .filter(|event| event.cycle_id == cycle_id)
           .cloned()
           .collect();
       let diff = compute_diff(cycle_id, timestamp_ms, recommendations, &cycle_events, ...);
       ...
   }

2. Doc comment updated at line 261-262: 'events may contain events from adjacent cycles; only matching cycle_id events are considered.'

3. Proptest shipped at shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:717-766 — `evaluate_cycle_filters_events_to_requested_cycle_ft_4x2c9`:
   - Generators: prior_noise ∈ 0..16, future_noise ∈ 0..16, target_dispatched: bool
   - Cycle layout: N-1=40 (prior noise: dispatches/safety/conflicts), N=41 (target), N+1=42 (future noise: dispatches/rejections/retry-storms/auto-resolved-conflicts)
   - Asserts: emissions_count = exactly target_dispatched (0/1), unexpected_executions empty, safety_gate_rejections=0, retry_storm_throttles=0, conflicts_detected=0, conflicts_auto_resolved=0 — i.e., NONE of the off-cycle events leak into the cycle-41 diff
   - Conditional asserts: when target_dispatched, missing_executions empty + dispatch_rate=1.0 + agent_match_rate=1.0 + is_healthy(); when not, missing_executions has the recommendation + dispatch_rate=0.0 + !is_healthy()

The test name explicitly contains 'ft_4x2c9' confirming the bead was the impetus. Sibling commit message ('chore(mission_events,shadow): borrow-extension fix + evaluate_cycle by-ref API') didn't mention the bead in the title — that's why the bead remained open at sibling's commit time.

Bead acceptance per original Proposed remediation:
✅ Filter events by e.cycle_id == cycle_id internally in evaluate_cycle
✅ Add tests where the log contains dispatches for cycle N-1 and N+1 and assert the cycle N diff ignores them (proptest covers exactly this with prior_noise/future_noise generators)

cc1 verified the fix presence by grep + read of file at HEAD. No additional code change needed; closing the bead administratively.

title: fleet_launcher::allocate_weighted u32 weight sum overflows on hostile AgentMix
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_launcher.rs found that allocate_weighted's total_weight sum can overflow.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_launcher.rs:82-103 defines AgentMixEntry with weight: u32 and no upper bound. Default = 1.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_launcher.rs:978: total_weight = mix.iter().map(|e| e.weight).sum::<u32>() — unchecked u32 addition.
- A FleetSpec with two AgentMixEntry entries each carrying weight: u32::MAX (or any combination summing past u32::MAX, e.g. 5 entries of weight=1_000_000_000 sums to 5e9 > 4.29e9) panics in debug builds and silently wraps in release builds.
- Wrap path: total_weight = small_number, quotas = (e.weight * total) / small_number = potentially huge, the  cast then saturates at u32::MAX, and the largest-remainder distribution sends u32::MAX-many slots to the first entry. The plan emerges with absurd allocations.

Why it matters: FleetSpec is operator-controlled (TOML config / CLI flags / persisted state). A malformed or hostile spec turns a config-validation surface into a denial-of-service / mis-allocation vector. The wrap path is especially insidious: no panic, no error, just nonsensical pane allocations under release mode.

Proposed remediation: use saturating_add when summing weights, OR validate at FleetSpec construction that the weight sum fits in u32. Add tests for total_weight near u32::MAX boundary and ensure the function returns a graceful fallback (all-zero allocation? error?) rather than overflowing.
notes: Replaced unchecked .sum::<u32>() in fleet_launcher::allocate_weighted with saturating_add fold. AgentMixEntry.weight is operator-controlled u32 with no upper bound, so a malformed FleetSpec with weights summing to >u32::MAX (e.g. two entries with weight=u32::MAX, or 5 entries with weight=1B) used to panic in debug and silently wrap to a small number in release — the wrap path then produced absurd quotas where one entry got u32::MAX-many slots. Saturating_add clamps to u32::MAX so the largest-remainder math stays finite and slot-conservation is preserved. Added 2 regression tests: allocate_weighted_does_not_panic_on_overflowing_weights_ft_4x6de (two u32::MAX entries, total=10, asserts sum==10), allocate_weighted_handles_many_large_weights_ft_4x6de (5 entries of 1B summing to 5e9, asserts conservation). br-ft-4x6de comment in helper. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [Audit] undo::parse_undo_payload silently drops corrupted undo records
description:
PHASE 3 AUDIT — silent serde drop in undo::parse_undo_payload.

Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/undo.rs:744-748

```rust
fn parse_undo_payload(undo: &ActionUndoRecord) -> Option<serde_json::Value> {
    undo.undo_payload
        .as_deref()
        .and_then(|payload| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(payload).ok())
}
```

Used by the undo machinery to extract execution_id (and other recovery identifiers) from a stored undo payload. On parse failure the function silently returns None, and callers fall through to "no execution_id available" — meaning the operator's undo command silently can't locate its target.

Why it matters: undo is a data-recovery primitive. A silent parse failure makes "I tried to undo and nothing happened" indistinguishable from "the action was never recorded for undo" — different remediation paths.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-ncijf, ft-r3d4e, ft-jtcrv.

Remediation:
1. Add UNDO_PAYLOAD_PARSE_DROP_COUNT AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset.
2. Replace .ok() with explicit match: bump counter + emit structured tracing::warn carrying action_id (from undo record) + error.
3. Tests: well-formed JSON parses without bump; malformed bumps.
notes: Replaced .ok() in undo::parse_undo_payload with explicit match. New UNDO_PAYLOAD_PARSE_DROP_COUNT counter + pub fn undo_payload_parse_drop_count() observability surface + cfg(test) reset helper. Parse failure bumps counter and emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.undo.parse with audit_action_id (from the ActionUndoRecord) + error %display + br-ft-4ymqn breadcrumb. NULL undo_payload (action not undoable) is intentionally NOT counted (legitimate absence). Returns None so scalar contract stays the same. Added 3 tests: null_does_not_bump (legitimate absence sanity), well_formed_does_not_bump (happy path), malformed_bumps_counter (2 distinct undo records each malformed -> count=2). Same observability defect family as ft-yygus, ft-k6uwb, ft-zhnaw, ft-94cdu, ft-lqj5g, ft-bn6qi, ft-crpvd, ft-0n4nx. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: RobotCommands::Workflow builds PolicyEngine without require_prompt_active/command_gate/rules — bypasses operator safety config
description:
AUTH BYPASS (robot mode mutations, Severity: Medium).

crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs has 10 PolicyEngine::new call sites. 8 of them wire require_prompt_active from config + .with_command_gate_config(config.safety.command_gate.clone()) + .with_policy_rules(config.safety.rules.clone()). Two do NOT, both under RobotCommands::Workflow:

Site 1 (main.rs:19831, RobotCommands::Workflow::Run):

  let policy_engine = PolicyEngine::new(
      config.safety.rate_limit_per_pane,
      config.safety.rate_limit_global,
      false, // Don't require prompt active for robot mode
  )
  .with_tuning(&config.tuning);

No command_gate, no policy_rules, and require_prompt_active hardcoded false. This engine is fed into CxPolicyInjector → WorkflowRunner; any workflow step that calls send_text (e.g., handle_compaction sending '/compact', handle_usage_limit sending '/refresh') bypasses:
  - the operator's safety.require_prompt_active=true policy,
  - every [[safety.rules]] custom gate,
  - the [safety.command_gate] allow/deny list.

Site 2 (main.rs:20511, RobotCommands::Workflow::Abort): identical construction. abort_execution_with_cx runs compensation steps through the same injector; any send_text in a compensation path bypasses the same three surfaces.

Compare the correctly-gated paths:
  - RobotCommands::Send at main.rs:17652 uses config.safety.require_prompt_active AND .with_command_gate_config + .with_policy_rules.
  - Non-robot workflow invocations at main.rs:21361, 21533, 25051, 27347 all wire the full policy surface.

NOT a duplicate of ft-48ah6 (read-only policy): this bead is specifically about the write/mutation surface (workflow's send_text / command-bearing steps). ft-48ah6 covered the read/search side.

Fix: replace the hardcoded 'false' with config.safety.require_prompt_active at both sites, and chain .with_command_gate_config(config.safety.command_gate.clone()) + .with_policy_rules(config.safety.rules.clone()) before passing the engine to PolicyGatedInjector. Rate-limit args are already correct.

Regression test: a send inside a robot-invoked workflow must be DENIED when config.safety.require_prompt_active=true AND no prompt is active, matching the direct-send gate behavior. Currently it is allowed.
close_reason: Fixed in 834b59f2. Both RobotCommands::Workflow::Run (main.rs:19831) and ::Abort (main.rs:20520) now build PolicyEngine with config.safety.require_prompt_active and chain .with_command_gate_config + .with_policy_rules — matching the construction at RobotCommands::Send (main.rs:17652) and non-robot workflow sites (21361/21533/25051/27347). Regression test robot_workflow_policy_engine_denies_send_when_prompt_required_ft_4z7vh asserts SendText is denied when require_prompt_active=true + command_running. Test binary compile is currently blocked by pre-existing concurrent-agent breakage (E0603 macro select private, E0063 missing defer_fts_triggers field) unrelated to this fix.

title: ft-mpc9b.8 substrate: RegressionState::should_file_p1 returns true on every observation in ConsecutiveRegression — duplicate P1 beads filed
description:
competitor_delta.rs RegressionState transitions:
- SingleRegression + Regressed → ConsecutiveRegression
- ConsecutiveRegression + Regressed → ConsecutiveRegression (sticky)

should_file_p1 returns true for ConsecutiveRegression. Integration calls observe() then queries should_file_p1; if integration files a bead each time, repeated regressions across releases produce duplicate P1 beads.

Tracked under self-review pass.

title: [golden-artifacts] TOON encoder: format=toon emits across robot+MCP, no exact-bytes corpus pinning the rendered output
description:
## The gap

ft's robot mode and MCP layer support `format=toon` for token-
efficient AI-to-AI output (per README's TL;DR: 'TOON-compact —
use this when piping to an AI'). Two existing tests:

- `tests/proptest_toon_roundtrip.rs` (21 KB) — proves
  `serialize → deserialize == identity` for arbitrary inputs.
- `tests/wa_mission_toon_mcp_conformance.rs` and
  `wa_tx_toon_mcp_conformance.rs` — assert TOON output for specific
  mission/tx envelopes parses back into the expected JSON shape.
- `tests/golden_pane_state_toon.rs` — pins ONE TOON output (pane
  state). 5.6 KB.

Property tests enforce shape invariants. The mission/tx tests
enforce parses-back-to-JSON. **Neither pins the exact rendered
TOON bytes for the broader robot envelope corpus.**

`grep -lE "toon.*golden\|TOON_GOLDEN\|to_toon.*golden"
tests/*.rs` returns zero hits beyond `golden_pane_state_toon.rs`.

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

The README's TL;DR sells TOON specifically as 'token-efficient AI-
to-AI output'. The encoded *bytes* are the value proposition — a
new field on a robot envelope that adds 50 tokens per response,
or a re-ordering that makes the output less compressible by an
AI's vocabulary, breaks the entire 'token-efficient' contract
silently. Property tests don't catch this because they preserve
roundtripability, not byte-economy.

Concrete drift hazards a corpus would catch:
- TOON encoder version change reorders fields, blowing up token
  counts.
- A robot tool gains an `Option<String>` field that serializes as
  `key=null,` even when None — invisible in JSON, present in TOON,
  uses tokens.
- Whitespace drift between major TOON versions silently hits the
  full robot/MCP surface.

## Suggested implementation

Mirror the structure of `tests/golden_robot_envelope/` (which I
shipped runtime-validation for in ft-5ikbd) but for TOON output:

1. **Corpus** at `tests/fixtures/toon_envelope_corpus/<tool>.toon`
   with one frozen TOON rendering per robot tool that pins
   meaningful output (state, get-text, search, send, mission_state,
   tx_run, tx_show, …).
2. **Generator** (or test-side fixture builder) that produces a
   deterministic input envelope per fixture and renders it via the
   production TOON encoder. The same input is checked into
   `tests/fixtures/toon_envelope_corpus/<tool>.input.json` so the
   regeneration command is auditable.
3. **Test driver**
   `tests/conformance_toon_envelope_corpus.rs`:
   - For each `<tool>.input.json`, render via the production TOON
     encoder, scrub timestamps/elapsed_ms/durations, diff against
     `<tool>.toon`.
   - Bonus: assert byte-count is within ±10% of a stored
     `<tool>.byte_budget.txt` so regressions in token-economy
     surface as test failures (not just silent bloat).
