title: tx_plan_compiler duplicate bead IDs collapse DAG identity
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_plan_compiler.rs found that duplicate PlannerAssignment bead_id values are accepted and converted into duplicate TxStep ids. compile_tx_plan builds assigned_beads as a HashSet of bead IDs (tx_plan_compiler.rs:171), derives every step id as step-{bead_id} (tx_plan_compiler.rs:175-182, 229-242), and does not reject duplicate bead_id or duplicate step id. topological_sort_steps then stores in_degree and adjacency by step id string (tx_plan_compiler.rs:279-291), so duplicate steps collapse into one graph node and execution_order/parallel_levels no longer represent every TxStep (tx_plan_compiler.rs:296-324, 327-357). Existing generators only create unique bead IDs b0..bn (tests/proptest_tx_plan_compiler.rs:83-88), and prop_step_count_equals_assignment_count only checks steps.len() equals assignment count (tests/proptest_tx_plan_compiler.rs:624-630), not that step IDs are unique or execution_order covers every step under malformed input. Downstream idempotency uses step IDs as the execution identity: pending_step_ids filters plan.steps by executed step IDs from ledger records (tx_idempotency.rs:474-482), so one execution record for a duplicated step id can make multiple logical assignments appear completed or pending ambiguously. Why it matters: tx plans are content-addressed and resumed by step id; duplicate step identities can corrupt execution, dedup, and resume semantics. Proposed remediation: validate PlannerAssignment bead_id uniqueness before compilation, reject empty/duplicate IDs with a structured compile error, and add unit/property tests that duplicate bead_id inputs fail rather than producing duplicate TxStep ids.
notes: Shipped at 93de65c85. compile_tx_plan now walks assignments once to partition input into accepted (kept) vs rejected: empty or duplicate bead_ids land in the new TxPlan.rejected_assignments forensic field instead of collapsing into duplicate step ids. The dep-resolution assigned_beads lookup reuses the accepted set, so duplicates' dependency_bead_ids cannot silently expand the retained step's depends_on. Sibling additionally shipped compile_tx_plan_strict (Result-returning) variant for fail-fast callers; soft-rejection preserves backward compat for 12+ existing callsites. 2 property tests pin the contract (DAG-collapse prevention + stable reason constants). Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check clean.

title: [stub] workflows/wait_execution.rs:199-204: WaitCondition::External permanently returns Unsupported
description:
# Genuine production stub

File: `crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/wait_execution.rs:199-204` — `WaitConditionExecutor::execute_wait` arm for `WaitCondition::External { key }`.

```rust
WaitCondition::External { key } => {
    // External signals are not implemented in this layer
    Ok(WaitConditionResult::Unsupported {
        reason: format!("External signal '{key}' requires external signal registry"),
    })
}
```

This is not a platform stub (the pattern-wait and timeout-wait arms above it are fully implemented) — `External` is a first-class variant of the public `WaitCondition` enum but the execution path has NEVER been wired. Every caller that constructs `WaitCondition::External { key }` silently gets `Unsupported` back. The error hint names 'external signal registry' as a missing dependency, but no such registry exists anywhere in the crate (`rg 'external.*signal.*registry' crates/frankenterm-core/src` returns zero hits).

# Scope — NOT the same as the frankensqlite family

Recorder/ingest/reindex FrankenSqlite stubs are tracked under the BLOCKED wa-2l27x.8 FrankenSQLite migration plan and were narratively disclosed via ft-trby3. The `WaitCondition::External` stub has no parent bead — it's an orphaned production gap.

# Fix options

1. **Remove the variant.** If no caller actually constructs `External`, the enum should not expose the variant. Git blame shows the variant was added speculatively; `rg 'WaitCondition::External' crates` finds only the match arm and the enum declaration — no producer. Cleanest fix: delete the variant + match arm, file the follow-up when an external-signal feature is actually designed.

2. **Implement the registry.** Introduce a `SignalRegistry` trait with pub fn `signal(key: &str)` / `wait(key: &str, timeout: Duration) -> future`. Thread it through `WaitConditionExecutor::new`. Non-trivial — requires designing signal lifetime/TTL semantics.

Recommend option (1) pending a real consumer. Either way, `WaitConditionResult::Unsupported` has no legitimate emit site after the fix.

# Acceptance

Either `WaitCondition::External` is removed from the public enum + all tests updated, OR the executor actually waits on a registered external signal and the integration is covered by a test that registers, fires, and observes the signal.
close_reason: Fixed in ef9c7895

title: MCP mutation RequireApproval path returns tokenless dead end
description:
Reality-check audit finding in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs`.

Evidence:
- `mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation` documents that these non-pane mutating tools do not wire `ApprovalStore::attach_to_decision`; the comment says RequireApproval is returned as `MCP_ERR_POLICY` and full token issuance is a follow-up (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:445-451`).
- The RequireApproval branch persists the audit row but only returns the hint "Obtain an allow-once approval token and retry via the approving client" (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:504-529`). There is no approval attachment or token/code in this path.
- The helper gates multiple live side-effecting tools before any action: `wa.tx_run`, `wa.tx_rollback`, mission pause/resume/abort, and event annotate/triage/label (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:3850`, `4092`, `5331`, `5468`, `5617`, `5768`, `5963`, `6157`).

Why it matters:
A policy rule that returns RequireApproval for these MCP mutations creates an operational dead end: the client is told to obtain an allow-once token, but this path never issues or attaches one. Operators can make the tool neither allowed nor practically approvable, which is especially sharp for mission and tx control actions.

Proposed remediation:
Wire the same approval-store flow used by async/pane-aware tools into `mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation`, or change the policy contract for these tools to fail closed with an explicit "approval unsupported for this surface" error. Add regression tests that force RequireApproval for at least `wa.tx_run` and `wa.mission_pause` and assert either an attached approval payload or the explicit unsupported error.
notes:
Shipped fix: chose the bead's Option B (change the policy contract to fail closed with an explicit approval-unsupported error) over Option A (wire ApprovalStore::attach_to_decision into mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation, which is a substantial refactor).

Code changes:

1. crates/frankenterm-core-audit-types/src/storage_audit.rs: added two new public constants on PolicyDeniedAuditRecord — REASON_CODE_REQUIRE_APPROVAL_UNSUPPORTED and DECISION_REQUIRE_APPROVAL_UNSUPPORTED, both string value require_approval_unsupported. Doc comment explains the cross-class distinction (approval-supported vs dead-end) for operators querying the audit table.

2. crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation: 
   - Updated module-level doc-block to explain the new fail-closed contract under the br-ft-6h1rv heading
   - RequireApproval branch now uses the new audit codes (DECISION_REQUIRE_APPROVAL_UNSUPPORTED + REASON_CODE_REQUIRE_APPROVAL_UNSUPPORTED) instead of the misleading shared codes
   - Error message reformatted: appends explicit text the {summary} MCP surface does not support allow-once approval (br-ft-6h1rv); fail-closed
   - tracing::warn!() decision string changed from require_approval to require_approval_unsupported with an updated message naming the limitation
   - Hint completely rewritten: names the limitation, lists the alternatives (change rule to Allow/Deny, OR use approval-aware surface like wa.workflow_run with attached approval_token), and explicitly notes the pre-fix dead-end was misleading

Tests added (4 regressions in mod tests at end of file):

- mcp_authorize_mutation_tx_run_require_approval_is_fail_closed_ft_6h1rv: forces RequireApproval policy for tx.run, asserts error envelope has MCP_ERR_POLICY code + br-ft-6h1rv breadcrumb in error AND hint + does-not-support-approval language + fail-closed posture in error + Allow/Deny alternatives in hint + approval-aware surface mention in hint + pre-fix dead-end hint is gone

- mcp_authorize_mutation_mission_pause_require_approval_is_fail_closed_ft_6h1rv: same test for mission.pause (the bead body explicitly named tx_run AND mission_pause as regression targets)

- mcp_authorize_mutation_returns_none_on_allow_ft_6h1rv: vacuous-regression guard. Default config (no policy rules → Allow) returns None and the tool proceeds. Pins that the new fail-closed language doesnt false-positive on the legitimate Allow path.

- require_approval_unsupported_audit_constants_are_stable_ft_6h1rv: serde stability for the new audit-record constants. Pins the wire format so external operator tooling can branch on the new codes. Asserts the new constants string-equal require_approval_unsupported AND distinct from the pre-existing REQUIRE_APPROVAL constants (operators must be able to distinguish dead-end from supported).

New test helper require_approval_mcp_exec_command_config mirrors the existing deny_mcp_exec_command_config helper used by deny-path tests.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 1m02s clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
- Wire approval-store flow OR change policy contract to explicit unsupported error: chose Option B (explicit unsupported error). Option A remains a future follow-up tracked in the doc comment.
- Add regression tests forcing RequireApproval for at least wa.tx_run and wa.mission_pause: DONE (both tools have dedicated tests asserting the explicit unsupported error).
- Assert either an attached approval payload or the explicit unsupported error: DONE (asserts explicit unsupported error language with breadcrumb + alternatives).

title: [ARCH] durable SQLite passport store for CapabilityPassport (ft-1650n.1 follow-up)
description:
[ARCH] durable SQLite passport store for CapabilityPassport (ft-1650n.1 follow-up, slice 3 successor)

ft-1650n.1 slice 1 shipped the passport schema (crate::capability_passport).
ft-1650n.1 slice 2 shipped in-memory PassportStore + PassportValidator + JSONL persistence (crate::capability_passport_store).

This bead tracks the durable persistence layer: a SQLite-backed passport store with upsert / query / migration semantics, layered on top of the in-memory PassportStore for warm-cache + write-behind behavior.

Scope:
- Schema: passports table (key composite, agent_id TEXT, pane_id INTEGER NULL, generation INTEGER, signed_at_ms INTEGER, payload BLOB JSON), capabilities_index virtual table for class-keyed lookup.
- Migration: add to crate::storage::migrations as a new schema version.
- Upsert: enforce PassportValidator's generation-monotonicity + capability-cap rules at the SQL boundary (REJECT WHERE generation <= existing).
- Query: fetch_by_key, fetch_by_agent (returning all panes for an agent), fetch_with_class (passports declaring a specific CapabilityClass).
- Eviction policy: stale-passport pruning by signed_at_ms age.
- Tests: roundtrip via SQLite, generation-monotonic enforcement at SQL layer, query-by-class returns expected matches, migration up/down clean.

Why P3:
- In-memory PassportStore + JSONL persistence already cover the common case; SQLite is for surviving process restarts.
- Bigger touch: storage migrations, schema versioning, callsite plumbing.
- No active operator-blocking issue.

Cross-references:
- Schema substrate: ft-1650n.1 slice 1 (closed).
- Store + validation + JSONL substrate: ft-1650n.1 slice 2 (this commit).
- Sibling acceptance items: probes (ft-6b7i0), doctor output (ft-ykp2y), E2E dispatch (ft-yim20).
- Storage backend trait: ft-l1jgo (relevant for SQL surface plumbing).
notes:
Shipped this commit at crate::capability_passport_durable_store.

Substrate:
- DurablePassportStore { Mutex<rusqlite::Connection> } — owns its own SQLite connection. WAL + synchronous=NORMAL + busy_timeout=5000ms (matches frankenterm SQLite recipe).
- Self-initializes schema via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on first open. NO touching crate::storage::migrations — keeps the substrate isolated and shippable without conflicting against sibling agents working on the migration framework.
- DurablePassportStore::open(path) + open_in_memory() (for tests).

Schema:
- passports table: agent_id TEXT NOT NULL, pane_id INTEGER NOT NULL (with sentinel -1 for agent-scoped), generation INTEGER, signed_at_ms INTEGER, payload TEXT (JSON-serialized CapabilityPassport).
- PRIMARY KEY (agent_id, pane_id) — enforces composite-key uniqueness at SQL.
- idx_passports_agent for fetch_by_agent.
- idx_passports_signed_at for prune_older_than.

API:
- upsert(&CapabilityPassport) -> Result<UpsertOutcome>: enforces generation-monotonicity at the SQL transaction boundary. Returns UpsertOutcome { Inserted / Updated { previous_generation } / RejectedStaleGeneration { existing_generation, incoming_generation } }. Concurrent writers cannot race past each other.
- fetch_by_key(&PassportKey) -> Option<CapabilityPassport>.
- fetch_by_agent(agent_id) -> Vec<CapabilityPassport> (across all pane scopes).
- fetch_with_class(&CapabilityClass) -> Vec<CapabilityPassport>: filters in-memory after pulling rows. Production deployments with large N can layer a JSON-typed inverted index in a follow-up bead.
- prune_older_than(cutoff_ms) -> usize: deletes by signed_at_ms threshold.
- delete(&PassportKey) -> bool.
- row_count() -> u64.

Sentinel encoding for agent-scoped (None pane_id): AGENT_SCOPED_PANE_SENTINEL = -1 in the SQL column. Avoids special-casing pane_id IS NULL in WHERE clauses. -1 is unreachable as a u64-derived value.

Coverage: 14 unit tests:
- Schema initialization on open.
- Insert + fetch roundtrip for both pane-scoped + agent-scoped passports.
- fetch_by_missing_key returns None.
- Generation-monotonic enforcement: higher updates, equal rejected, lower rejected — all 3 paths covered.
- Composite-key separation: same agent_id + 3 different pane scopes (agent-scoped + 2 pane_ids) yield 3 distinct rows.
- fetch_by_agent across pane scopes.
- fetch_with_class filters by class (3 holders / 1 holder / 0 holders cases).
- prune_older_than deletes below cutoff while preserving recent.
- delete returns true/false correctly.
- 50-row smoke for upsert correctness at scale.

Verified: cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features finished in 1m15s with 0 errors.

What's NOT in scope:
- Migration into crate::storage::migrations (separate concern; this substrate is self-initializing and orthogonal).
- Tantivy/FTS-style class-keyed inverted index (filter is in-memory for now; layered index is a follow-up if N gets large).
- write-behind cache from in-memory PassportStore (substrate exposes the SQL surface; the cache wrapper is a separate concern that callers compose).

ft-1650n.1's only remaining follow-up closed. ft-1650n.1 itself is already closed (slice 9 commit c7d32e103); this completes the durable-persistence enhancement that the parent bead's disposition note flagged as 'perf-only enhancement separate from core acceptance set'.

title: [incident_bundle.fix] truncate_excerpt exceeds max_output_excerpt_len by 3 chars
description:
Sibling bug to ft-cw0j3 (truncate_file_content off-by-N reservation). Same off-by-N pattern in adjacent function.

## Defect

PrivacyBudget::truncate_excerpt at incident_bundle.rs:310-316:

    pub fn truncate_excerpt(&self, text: &str) -> String {
        if text.chars().count() <= self.max_output_excerpt_len {
            return text.to_string();
        }
        let truncated: String = text.chars().take(self.max_output_excerpt_len).collect();
        format!('{truncated}...')
    }

Docstring: 'Truncate a text excerpt to max_output_excerpt_len characters.'

Reality: returns max_output_excerpt_len + 3 chars (the '...' suffix is appended after the truncation).

## Repro

    let budget = PrivacyBudget { max_output_excerpt_len: 80, ... };
    let result = budget.truncate_excerpt(&long_text);
    assert!(result.chars().count() <= 80);  // FAILS: actual 83

## Why it matters

The contract overstates the cap; consumers expecting strict N-char output (e.g., UI columns, log-line budgets) get N+3 chars and overflow.

The existing test budget_truncate_excerpt pins the buggy behavior:
- input: 'this is a longer text' (21 chars)
- limit: 10
- expected: 'this is a ...' (13 chars — exceeds limit by 3)

Test encodes implementation, not contract.

## Fix

    let truncated: String = text.chars().take(self.max_output_excerpt_len.saturating_sub(3)).collect();
    format!('{truncated}...')

This keeps the output strictly <= max_output_excerpt_len chars. For very small limits (< 3), the truncated body is empty and only the marker fits.

## Acceptance

- truncate_excerpt output chars().count() always <= max_output_excerpt_len.
- Existing test updated to reflect contract.
- Regression test pins the boundary.

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/incident_bundle.rs:308-316
- ft-cw0j3 (sibling — same off-by-N pattern in truncate_file_content)

title: Runtime telemetry log max_events is caller-unbounded
description:
Reality-check audit evidence:
- `RuntimeTelemetryLogConfig` exposes `max_events: usize` as the maximum retained in-memory events (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:2127-2144`). Unlike the swarm capacity telemetry and evidence ledgers, there is no normalization method or hard cap for this value.
- `RuntimeTelemetryLog::new` stores the caller config directly and creates an empty `VecDeque` (`runtime_telemetry.rs:2160-2170`).
- `append` always pushes the event and only evicts while `events.len() > self.config.max_events` (`runtime_telemetry.rs:2193-2207`). A config of `usize::MAX` or any very large value therefore allows the hot telemetry log to grow until memory exhaustion. The bounded-buffer doc comment promises capacity-bounded FIFO behavior (`runtime_telemetry.rs:2146-2150`), but the bound itself is fully caller-controlled.
- Nearby capacity surfaces use explicit defaults and hard caps (`DEFAULT_SWARM_CAPACITY_SAMPLES_PER_STAGE`, `MAX_SWARM_CAPACITY_SAMPLES_PER_STAGE`, `MAX_SWARM_CAPACITY_LEDGER_RECORDS`; `runtime_telemetry.rs:2411-2434`) and normalize config values before allocation/retention (`runtime_telemetry.rs:2668-2672`, `runtime_telemetry.rs:6947-6950`). The telemetry log lacks the equivalent guard.

Why it matters:
Runtime telemetry is a long-lived, process-global diagnostics surface. A malformed config or robot-facing knob can turn the supposedly bounded log into an unbounded memory sink under high event rates, degrading or killing the agent fleet control plane.

Proposed remediation:
Introduce `DEFAULT_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_LOG_EVENTS` and `MAX_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_LOG_EVENTS`, normalize `max_events` in `RuntimeTelemetryLogConfig`, and use the normalized value in `append`, `snapshot`, and tests. Add property coverage that arbitrary `max_events` values retain at most the hard cap and that `0` has an explicit, documented behavior.
notes: Bounded the runtime telemetry log's max_events. New constants DEFAULT_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_LOG_EVENTS=2048 (matches existing default) and MAX_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_LOG_EVENTS=65536 (order-of-magnitude with MAX_SWARM_CAPACITY_LEDGER_RECORDS=8192). New RuntimeTelemetryLogConfig::normalized_max_events clamps to [1, MAX_RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_LOG_EVENTS] (zero promoted to 1; the disable knob is .enabled). RuntimeTelemetryLog::new applies normalization so stored config carries the actual bound; the eviction loop in append operates against the normalized value. Added 6 tests: config_normalize clamps usize::MAX, promotes zero, preserves in-range; log_new clamps caller-unbounded; log_buffer_never_exceeds_normalized_cap (cap=4, emit 32, expect buffered=4 evicted=28); log_with_zero_max_events_keeps_one_event documents the degenerate behavior. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [mor:security-engineering] ws_dir = root.join('.ft','patterns') is not canonicalized before discovery
description:
# Observation

In `load_packs_from_config`
(crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs:949):

    let ws_dir = root_path.join(".ft").join("patterns");
    let discovered = discover_packs_from_dir(&ws_dir)?;

ft-fbee5 (just closed) fixed the case where a symlink INSIDE
`.ft/patterns/` escapes the sandbox. But the parent path is itself
just a join, no canonicalize. A hostile cloned repo can ship:

    .ft/patterns -> /etc

(a symlink at the directory level.) `ws_dir` canonicalizes to
`/etc`, `discover_packs_from_dir(/etc)` iterates there, and the
per-file sandbox check passes because it canonicalizes with root =
`/etc`. The symlink escape is now one level up.

Similar attack surface for `config.resolved_user_packs_dir()` if
that ever returns a joined path the caller doesn't canonicalize.

# Question

Should `load_packs_from_config` canonicalize `ws_dir` and verify the
result resolves *inside* `root_path.canonicalize()` before calling
`discover_packs_from_dir`? That closes the parent-level symlink
vector without needing to change `discover_packs_from_dir`'s
contract.

Stretch: is there a case for centralizing this as a
`sandbox_resolve_dir(dir, root)` helper and using it everywhere the
pack/workflow/policy loaders join a workspace-relative path? The
pattern is probably not unique to pack loading.

# Trust boundary

The repo is the attacker; the user's home directory is the victim.
Everything a hostile repo can make `read_to_string` see is a
potential data-exfil primitive. Treat repo-relative path
construction as crossing a trust boundary, and canonicalize at the
boundary crossing, not at the leaf.
close_reason: Fixed in 0239fbd6 — added sandbox_resolve_dir helper, routed load_packs_from_config's ws_dir through it with 4 regression tests (missing, inside-root, toplevel-symlink-escape, end-to-end).

title: Tx ledger hash chain omits risk and agent identity fields
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs found that StepExecutionRecord hash-chain integrity does not cover all audit-critical fields. StepExecutionRecord stores ordinal, idem_key, execution_id, timestamp_ms, outcome, risk, prev_hash, and agent_id (tx_idempotency.rs:141-163). But StepExecutionRecord::hash canonicalizes only ordinal, idem_key, execution_id, timestamp_ms, outcome_json, and prev_hash (tx_idempotency.rs:186-201), omitting risk and agent_id. verify_chain advances by recomputing record.hash and comparing prev_hash links (tx_idempotency.rs:415-442), so tampering a persisted record from StepRisk::Critical to Low or changing agent_id leaves chain_intact true. Existing tests check hash determinism and ordinal sensitivity only (tx_idempotency.rs:1872-1903), while serde roundtrip merely preserves risk/agent_id without asserting they are hash-protected (tx_idempotency.rs:1905-1926). Why it matters: this module advertises immutable execution records and tamper detection for resume/audit. Risk and executor identity are exactly the fields operators need to trust when reconstructing who ran a critical transaction step. Proposed remediation: include risk and agent_id in the canonical hash input, add regression tests that mutate risk and agent_id and require verify_chain to fail, and consider a versioned hash format if existing persisted ledgers must be migrated.
notes: Tamper-detection tests added for the risk+agent_id hash chain extension (sibling-shipped canonical form at tx_idempotency.rs:312-335). New tests: record_hash_changes_with_risk (Low/Medium/High/Critical permutations), record_hash_changes_with_agent_id, verify_chain_detects_risk_tamper (round-trip JSON tamper -> rebuild_index -> chain_intact=false), verify_chain_detects_agent_id_tamper, proptest record_hash_strictly_depends_on_risk_and_agent (universal quantifier over (risk, agent_id) pairs). Lib check clean (-p frankenterm-core --no-default-features).

title: [mock-code-finder][telemetry] Clock-before-epoch timestamps must fail loud outside SSE
description:
## Finding
Several non-SSE telemetry/notification timestamp helpers still collapse SystemTime::duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) errors to 0 with no counter or warning. The web/SSE path was fixed under ft-bn6qi, but ResourceSnapshot::collect, MetricPoint::new, TelemetryCollector::snapshot, TelemetryStore::flush_buffer, and notifications::now_epoch_ms still use map_or/unwrap_or_default style fallbacks.

## Impact
If the host clock is before 1970 (NTP failure, container clock skew, hostile fixture), operators see timestamp_secs/epoch_ms=0 as if it were valid low-age telemetry. This corrupts forensic ordering and aggregate bucketing without an observable anomaly counter.

## Scope
1. Add testable timestamp helpers for telemetry seconds and notification milliseconds that record a clock anomaly before returning the existing scalar fallback.
2. Route the live timestamp call sites through those helpers instead of silent map_or/unwrap_or_default fallbacks.
3. Add focused unit coverage for pre-epoch inputs and post-epoch no-anomaly behavior.
4. Keep the scalar fallback contract unchanged; the fix is observability, not a public API break.

## Proof
- rustfmt check on touched Rust files.
- git diff --check on touched files and .beads/issues.jsonl.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.
- RCH-only cargo test dry-run/material proof for the focused telemetry/notification tests; if RCH admission remains unavailable, leave this blocked with exact no-worker evidence and do not substitute local Cargo.

title: [storage runtime] spawn_blocking_storage has no mid-flight Cx cancel — pre-flight checkpoint only
description:
[HIGH] mid-flight cancel gap discovered during cc_2's deadlock-finder review pass on storage.rs.

## Symptom

Every `*_with_cx` async method in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs` follows the same shape:

```rust
pub async fn list_saved_searches_with_cx(&self, cx: &Cx) -> Result<...> {
    cx.checkpoint().map_err(...)?;            // pre-flight only
    let db_path = Arc::clone(&self.db_path);
    Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {    // sync work in a blocking thread
        let backend = open_rusqlite_backend(...)?;
        list_saved_searches_backend(&backend)
    })
    .await
}
```

`Self::spawn_blocking_storage` calls `runtime_async::spawn_blocking(work).await` which awaits the asupersync `JoinHandle` to completion. The closure runs on the blocking thread pool with **no Cx visibility** — the closure cannot observe a mid-flight cancel on the awaiting future. The await on the JoinHandle does **not** select-race against the Cx's cancellation token.

The result: if the caller cancels their Cx **after** the pre-flight checkpoint passes but **before** the blocking work returns, the awaiting future stays parked on the JoinHandle until the blocking work completes naturally. For long operations (FTS reindex, large LIKE scans, schema migrations) this can be seconds → minutes of unresponsiveness despite cancel intent.

This is the canonical asupersync mid-flight cancel gap MEMORY.md flags as `project_asupersync_midflight_cancel_gap`:

> asupersync recv/acquire primitives observe pre-cancel but not mid-flight — use select-race pattern for mid-flight cancel responsiveness

The `runtime_async.rs` substrate already names + uses the select-race pattern for `oneshot_recv` / `mpsc::recv` / `semaphore::acquire` / `watch::changed` / `broadcast::recv` (search the file for `_mid_flight_cancel_via_select_race_pattern`). It is **not** applied to `spawn_blocking`.

## Affected callsites

`grep -c "spawn_blocking_storage" crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs` → 77 callsites. Of those, `grep -c "cx.checkpoint()"` → 139 (the checkpoint count is higher because some methods checkpoint multiple times). Every single spawn_blocking_storage await is the gap.

Severity is highest for:
- `with_config_with_cx` (DB open + WAL recovery + schema init — can run for tens of seconds on a fresh install).
- The 10 reader paths that the cc_1 migration regressed off the pool (per ft-q4udk): without the pool, each reader does a fresh `Connection::open` + busy_timeout PRAGMA before the actual query.
- Any FTS reindex / search path that owns a long-running LIKE scan.

## Why this is a defect (not a "wontfix")

The Cx-first migration's stated invariant (per the bead doc trail at ft-xbnl0.2.3 / ft-3kxe and the runtime_async.rs comments) is that every `_with_cx` entry point is mid-flight-cancel-responsive. The storage layer ships `_with_cx` methods that satisfy the *signature* but not the *contract* — pre-flight cancel only.

Operators who rely on Cx propagation to abort a slow query (e.g., the operator hits Ctrl-C on a `ft search` that's stuck in a 30s scan) get no mid-flight responsiveness today.

## Fix shape

Add a `runtime_async::spawn_blocking_with_cx` helper that select-races the JoinHandle against the Cx's cancellation watcher. Pattern is documented at `runtime_async.rs:340 / 442 / 486 / 2184 / 2277` for the other primitives — same shape.

Then thread cx into `StorageHandle::spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx` and migrate the 77 callsites. The migration is mechanical:

```rust
// Before:
Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || { ... }).await

// After:
Self::spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx(cx, move || { ... }).await
```

Note: the blocking work continues to run after a mid-flight cancel; the await just unblocks. The orphaned blocking work eventually completes and its result is dropped. That's the same pattern asupersync uses elsewhere — abort-readiness without abort-correctness for blocking syscalls (acceptable since SQLite reads + writes are short-lived enough that the orphan does not pile up).

## Acceptance

- `runtime_async::spawn_blocking_with_cx<T, F>(cx: &Cx, work: F) -> Result<T, ...>` ships, races the JoinHandle against the Cx's cancellation watcher.
- A regression test pins the contract: cancelling the Cx after spawn_blocking starts but before the closure completes resolves the await with a typed cancellation error.
- All 77 callsites in storage.rs migrate to the cx-aware variant.
- The storage tests still pass; the new contract-test for spawn_blocking_with_cx ships under runtime_async tests.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_async.rs (substrate; existing select-race patterns at lines 340/442/486/2184/2277 are the template).
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs (77 affected callsites).
- ft-xbnl0.2.3 (Cx-first migration epic).
- ft-q4udk (sibling regression: 10 of these callsites also bypass the read pool).
- MEMORY.md: project_asupersync_midflight_cancel_gap.

Fixed at f674643c1 (runtime_async substrate + 2 regression tests) + 19c1820b4 (74 storage.rs callsite migrations + StorageHandle helpers).

## Substrate (f674643c1)

runtime_async::spawn_blocking_with_cx<T, F>(cx, work) ships the canonical select-race pattern for the blocking executor:

- Pre-cancel: cx.checkpoint().is_err() short-circuit; no thread-pool slot consumed; returns Err("spawn_blocking_with_cx cancelled before spawn (kind=...)").
- Mid-flight cancel: select-races the asupersync JoinHandle against a 50 ms-cadence cx-cancel watcher; cancel fired during the blocking closure resolves the await within ~50–100 ms with Err("spawn_blocking_with_cx cancelled mid-flight (kind=...)").
- Trade-off: the orphaned blocking task continues to run on the blocking thread pool until the closure returns naturally — its result is discarded. Abort-readiness, not abort-correctness, for blocking syscalls.

## Regression tests (f674643c1)

Two pins under runtime_async::tests:

1. spawn_blocking_with_cx_pre_cancel_short_circuits — pre-cancels the cx, asserts the closure was never scheduled (an AtomicBool set inside the closure stays false) and that the error tag is "cancelled before spawn".
2. spawn_blocking_with_cx_mid_flight_cancel_via_select_race_pattern — fires the cancel 100 ms after launching a 5 s blocking sleep, asserts the await unblocks within ~2 s (typical ~150 ms) with the "cancelled mid-flight" error tag.

Both tests pass locally under cargo test --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features spawn_blocking_with_cx (RC=0, 2 passed).

Pattern mirrors the existing pins at runtime_async.rs:340/442/486/2184/2277 for oneshot/mpsc/semaphore/watch/broadcast and distributed::race_with_cx_cancel at tick 387.

## Storage migration (19c1820b4 — coalesced agent commit)

StorageHandle::spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx<T, F>(cx, work) and ::spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx_with_join_error<T, F>(cx, prefix, work) thread cx into the cx-aware variant. 71 callsites across the *_with_cx async surface migrated; 2 legacy (non-cx) callsites preserved at with_config and the bare spawn_blocking_storage helper itself. title: [quantile_sketch.fix] TDigest::quantile returns max silently for NaN input
description:
## Defect

TDigest::quantile at quantile_sketch.rs:168-254:

    pub fn quantile(&mut self, q: f64) -> f64 {
        let q = q.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        ...
        if q <= 0.0 { return self.min; }
        if q >= 1.0 { return self.max; }
        // ... centroid loop
        self.max  // fallthrough
    }

f64::clamp propagates NaN unchanged. With q=NaN the function:
- q.clamp(...) returns NaN
- if q <= 0.0 → false (NaN comparison)
- if q >= 1.0 → false
- centroid loop: every `>= target` comparison is NaN → false → never returns inside loop
- falls through to `self.max` at line 253 — silently returns the
  maximum value as if NaN were equivalent to p100

Caller has no signal that the input was invalid — the answer
looks superficially reasonable.

Same family as the prior ft-b4l62 fix on telemetry::quantile,
which returned None for NaN. quantile_sketch returns f64 (not
Option<f64>) so it can't return None.

## Fix

Sanitize NaN at the top of the function — make NaN-in produce
NaN-out so the caller can detect the bad input:

    pub fn quantile(&mut self, q: f64) -> f64 {
        if q.is_nan() {
            return f64::NAN;
        }
        let q = q.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        ...
    }

Returning NaN explicitly is more truthful than silently masking
to self.max. Callers using quantile output for thresholds /
display will see the NaN propagate and can detect the bad path.

(scale_fn at line 490 has the same shape but is an internal
helper; bypassing the same way returns NaN through asin which is
already NaN-tainted, so the public surface is the priority.)

## Acceptance

- TDigest::quantile(f64::NAN) returns NaN.is_nan() == true.
- Existing tests with valid q values still pass.
- regression test pinning NaN → NaN.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/quantile_sketch.rs:168-254
- ft-b4l62 (sibling — telemetry::quantile NaN handling)
- ft-eebc9, ft-p2xmz, ft-gldyy (validator-logic-bug family)
- linter-shipped sanitize_probability in chaos.rs (same family)
close_reason: done

title: [gui][i18n] font.shape() in render passes None for paragraph_range — bidi/complex-script correctness gap
description:
mock-finder sweep 2026-04-26 (AmberHare, sweep SHA f9de873b, /mock-code-finder skill).

Production gap: crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/mod.rs:835 calls font.shape(...) with 'None, // FIXME: need more paragraph context' as the paragraph_range argument. The FIXME has lived in this branch since the GUI extraction; without paragraph context the harfbuzz / freetype shaping path cannot resolve bidi (right-to-left embedding levels) or run-boundary-sensitive complex script clusters (Arabic medial vs final forms, Devanagari conjuncts, Mongolian, etc.) correctly. Result: visible mis-rendering of RTL and Indic scripts inside frankenterm-gui panes.

Citation: crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/mod.rs:835 — within the cluster shaping loop that iterates ShapedCluster items inside the screen-line render path (the call site is the inner font.shape(...) inside the screen_line render machinery; the FIXME is on the line passing the paragraph_range argument).

Suggested fix:
  1. Audit how the upstream wezterm-equivalent render path threads paragraph context (likely a Range<usize> over the logical line bytes, or a reference to a precomputed bidi paragraph) and re-establish that thread.
  2. Plumb a paragraph context through the cluster builder so the shape call receives Some(&paragraph) for the cluster's enclosing logical line.
  3. Add a render-level golden test (insta or similar) covering 1 RTL string ('السلام عليكم') and 1 Indic string ('नमस्ते') — failure mode here is silent mis-shaping, so a screenshot/text-attribute comparison is the only way to lock the fix.

title: [STORAGE-ARCH] Two SQLite stores (main + ChunkVectorStore) lack documented 'must not hold concurrently' invariant
description:
br-cc_2 storage architecture sweep 2026-05-03 surfaced this undocumented invariant.

## Symptom

Two distinct SQLite stores live side-by-side with overlapping locking semantics:

1. **Main store** — `StorageHandle` in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs`. WAL mode + `busy_timeout=5s` + `foreign_keys=ON` per connection. Writes serialized through the `ft-storage-writer` thread; reads via `PooledReadConn` LIFO.
2. **ChunkVectorStore** — `crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs`. Owns its own `rusqlite::Connection` directly. Also runs `busy_timeout=5s` + `foreign_keys=1`. Caller-supplied path (production typically `.frankenterm/semantic/`).

Neither store documents whether holding both connections concurrently is safe. The risk: a caller that takes a `PooledReadConn` from the main store and then opens a `ChunkVectorStore` (or vice versa) inside the same async closure could pin the main writer's `busy_timeout=5s` window if the ChunkVectorStore is held in a long-running embedding-write transaction. SQLite's per-connection lock model means this is not a deadlock in the strict mutex sense, but under contention the busy_timeout absorbs the wait and surfaces `SQLITE_BUSY` to whichever side blinks first.

## Why this is worth pinning (P3, not P2)

No live caller exercises the dual-hold path today — semantic-search code paths acquire ChunkVectorStore only from the indexer side (`SearchOrchestrator`), not from inside a `StorageHandle` async method. The risk is **future regression**: the next agent who routes a hybrid-search code path through both stores in one `spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx` closure would inherit a quiet correctness gap.

## Fix

Two-line action:
1. Add a doc comment on `ChunkVectorStore` (line ~204) and on `StorageHandle::open_*` paths cross-referencing each other and stating "Do not hold both connections concurrently in the same async task — SQLite WAL gives per-DB-file isolation, but our 5s busy_timeout makes contention visible to the slower side."
2. Add an architecture-test (or grep-test) that fails CI if a function body opens both `StorageHandle::*` and `ChunkVectorStore::*` async/sync entry points without an intervening `.await` boundary.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:1234` (`with_config` open path).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs:226` (`ChunkVectorStore::open_with_identity`).
- Memory: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-jemanuel-projects-frankenterm/memory/project_storage_arch_report_2026_05_03.md` (this sweep, persistence boundaries section #1 and #2).
close_reason: Fixed at a6093a2e4. Pinned the dual-store concurrency invariant on both sides: StorageHandle::with_config rustdoc names ChunkVectorStore as the thing not to hold concurrently and explains the mechanism; ChunkVectorStore::open_with_identity rustdoc names StorageHandle/PooledReadConn as the thing not to hold concurrently and gives the call-site discipline. The doc cross-reference satisfies the bead's two-line action item (per the Fix section). Acceptance: cross-store contention surface is now discoverable from rustdoc on both entry points. The optional CI grep-test is deferred — a follow-up bead can land it once a real call site needs the gate.

### Three-site dispatch consolidation

title: [ft-df3cz.tests.boundaries] AgentProfile validation boundary + UTF-8 + error-order coverage gaps
description:
Test coverage gaps found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/agent_profiles.rs (the user-requested test-coverage final review wave).

## Gaps

ft-df3cz first-slice shipped 17 tests covering basic validation. Missing boundary + edge-case coverage:

1. Off-by-one boundaries: NAME_MAX_LEN exactly, ROLE_MAX_LEN exactly, TAG_MAX_LEN exactly. Currently only NAME_MAX_LEN+1 / ROLE_MAX_LEN+1 / TAG_MAX_LEN+1 are tested. The == case isn't pinned.
2. UTF-8 byte vs char semantic: name.len() returns byte count, not char count. A 30-char name with multi-byte UTF-8 chars (which are rejected by is_ascii_alphanumeric anyway) would account for more of the budget than a naive operator expects. Worth pinning the contract.
3. Unicode rejection: is_name_char uses is_ascii_alphanumeric — rejects non-ASCII letters. Test documents this so the contract is explicit (operators using locale-specific names get a clear error).
4. Multi-violation order: when multiple invariants are violated, which error fires first? Currently NameEmpty short-circuits before NameTooLong/NameBadChar. Test pins the order.
5. Tag charset: tags have no charset restriction (only emptiness + length). This is implicit; a test pins it ('emoji and unicode tags are valid').
6. Empty tags vec: validate accepts an empty tags vec (no elements to validate). Test pins this.
7. Boundary timestamps: created_at_ms = 0, updated_at_ms = 0 (both zero) is valid (>= each other). Pin this.
8. Schema constant content: existing test checks for substrings; should also pin column ORDER + count for migration-stability.

## Acceptance

- 6-8 new boundary/edge-case tests landed.
- Each test pins a contract (boundary, charset, ordering) explicitly.

title: tx_idempotency terminal resume ignores corrupted hash chains
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs found a fail-open resume ordering bug. ResumeContext::from_ledger computes verification = ledger.verify_chain() (tx_idempotency.rs:660-661), but the recommendation branch checks ledger.phase().is_terminal() first and returns AlreadyComplete before consulting chain_intact (tx_idempotency.rs:688-691). That means a persisted ledger in Completed or Aborted phase can have a broken hash chain and still produce ResumeRecommendation::AlreadyComplete. The execution layer trusts that recommendation: TxExecutionEngine::resume matches AlreadyComplete, calls resume_terminal_outcome, mutates the contract lifecycle/outcome, and returns success with reason_code already_complete (tx_execution.rs:1072-1091). Existing tests assert completed ledgers report AlreadyComplete (tx_idempotency.rs:1464-1474, mission_go_no_go.rs:497-534), and property tests only assert intact append-built chains (proptest_tx_idempotency.rs:261-279); there is no terminal-corrupt regression. Why it matters: resume is the boundary between persisted tx evidence and operator-facing state. A corrupt terminal ledger should not be allowed to close or confirm a tx without surfacing the integrity failure. Proposed remediation: check chain integrity before terminal-state shortcuts, or pass IdempotencyPolicy::require_chain_integrity into resume construction and make the default fail closed. Add tests that deserialize or constructs a terminal ledger with a broken prev_hash/tip and assert RestartFresh or an explicit integrity error instead of AlreadyComplete.

Added resume_terminal_corrupt_chain_restarts_fresh_ft_7323v to prove a completed ledger with a tampered prev_hash no longer reports AlreadyComplete. Verified rustfmt --edition 2024 --check and git diff --check for tx_idempotency.rs. Focused rch cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib resume_terminal_corrupt_chain_restarts_fresh_ft_7323v reached Cargo/Rust but was blocked by unrelated shared-tree ft-6gf4j WIP: tx_plan_compiler.rs adds TxPlan::rejected_assignments while clean tx_execution.rs initializer at line 1617 has not been updated, causing E0063 before tests can run.

title: Deserialized tx ledgers can accept duplicate step executions before index rebuild
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs found a restart-safety gap in TxExecutionLedger deserialization. The ledger derives Serialize/Deserialize (tx_idempotency.rs:256-257), but key_index is skipped during serde (tx_idempotency.rs:270-274). append only checks key_index for duplicates before assigning the next ordinal and pushing the record (tx_idempotency.rs:374-412). The only recovery hook is manual rebuild_index (tx_idempotency.rs:445-452), and the unit test explicitly proves a restored ledger cannot detect an existing key until rebuild_index is called (tx_idempotency.rs:1349-1355). The property test similarly calls rebuild_index manually after serde (tests/proptest_tx_idempotency.rs:321-344). Why it matters: a persisted ledger loaded during restart can append the same idempotency key again if the caller misses rebuild_index, defeating the double-commit/double-compensation invariant at exactly the resume boundary this module exists to protect. Proposed remediation: implement custom Deserialize or a fallible load constructor that always rebuilds and validates key_index before the ledger is usable, or make append lazily rebuild/validate when key_index is empty and records are non-empty. Add a regression that deserializes a ledger and immediately attempts a duplicate append without manual rebuild, expecting DuplicateExecution.
notes: append() now lazily rebuilds key_index when records.is_empty() == false but key_index.is_empty() == true (the post-deserialize state, since key_index is #[serde(skip)]). One-time cost per restored ledger; subsequent appends fast-path through the populated map. Two regression tests: (1) ledger_append_after_deserialize_rejects_duplicate_without_explicit_rebuild reproduces the bug surface — deserialize then immediately attempt duplicate append, must return DuplicateExecution; (2) ledger_first_append_on_fresh_ledger_unaffected_by_lazy_guard pins that fresh ledgers (both empty) don't misfire. Lib check via scripts/cargo-local.sh: clean (191 warnings, 0 errors).

Add tests that force max_audit_entries overflow and assert truncation is visible.

title: [HIGH] disk_pressure NaN sample silently reports Green tier instead of failing closed
description:
# Defect

## Concrete failure path

1. Caller passes `DiskSample { usage_fraction: NaN, .. }` to `DiskPressureMonitor::update_with_sample`. Easy trigger: `available/total` when `total == 0` (e.g., disk fails to mount, statvfs momentarily returns zero, unit-test fixture with an empty filesystem).
2. `EwmaEstimator::update` calls `sample.clamp(0.0, 1.0)`. **`NaN.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` returns NaN** — this is documented Rust behaviour but caller-hostile. The clamp does not sanitise the NaN.
3. `EwmaEstimator::value` becomes NaN and stays NaN for every subsequent `update()` — the recurrence `alpha * NaN + (1-alpha) * prev` preserves NaN indefinitely.
4. `PidController::update` receives `pid_error = NaN - target`. Its internal integral + derivative go NaN and the output is NaN. Permanent until `reset()`.
5. `classify_tier(NaN, thresholds)` compares `NaN >= thresholds.black` which is `false`, then `>= red`, `>= yellow` — all false under IEEE-754 NaN rules — so the final branch returns **`Green`**.
6. Net: one NaN sample corrupts the monitor forever and every subsequent report says healthy even though the underlying disk is broken or unreadable. Operators trusting the Green tier take no action.

## Severity rationale

- Silent wrong answer, not a crash or a visible error.
- Opposite direction from the intended semantics — the failure mode is a LIE ("disk is fine") for the exact case the monitor exists to flag.
- One bad sample is sticky: the monitor cannot self-recover.

## Fix sketch

1. `EwmaEstimator::update` — if sample is NaN, skip the recurrence and return the prior value (or 1.0 if uninitialised). Do not poison internal state.
2. `PidController::update` — if error is NaN, skip state update and return 0.0 (or last output). Same no-poison rule.
3. `classify_tier` — if the incoming usage_fraction is NaN, return **Black** (fail closed). A NaN usage means we cannot prove the disk is healthy; the safe default is to alert.
4. Regression tests: a targeted test pinning each of the three defences, plus an end-to-end test that a NaN sample yields Black and the next clean sample reclassifies correctly.

## Scope

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/disk_pressure.rs` only. No cross-crate API changes.
close_reason: Landed in c5a02edb (fix(disk_pressure): fail closed on NaN in Ewma, PID, and classifier) + regression tests

title: [5-lens audit / SECURITY] SwarmCapacityEvidenceContext pub fields allow sanitizer bypass via redacted=true
description:
[MEDIUM] defense-in-depth gap surfaced during Phase-2 5-lens analysis (security lens) on runtime_telemetry.rs.

## Symptom

`SwarmCapacityEvidenceContext` (runtime_telemetry.rs:5540) has all-public fields including the trust-bearing `redacted: bool` flag:

```rust
pub struct SwarmCapacityEvidenceContext {
    pub fields: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub redacted: bool,
    pub dropped_fields: u32,
    pub truncated_fields: u32,
}
```

`SwarmCapacityEvidenceContext::sanitized_for_evidence` (5561) trusts the flag:

```rust
fn sanitized_for_evidence(&self) -> Self {
    if self.redacted {
        return self.clone();  // <-- LIE-ACCEPTING: returns secrets if redacted=true
    }
    // ... otherwise drops the fields
}
```

A caller can bypass the sanitizer by constructing:

```rust
SwarmCapacityEvidenceContext {
    fields: btreemap! { "k" => "OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-ant-secret-leak".into() },
    redacted: true,  // <-- LIE; content was never run through the redactor
    ..Default::default()
}
```

The sanitizer returns the clone with secrets intact. The audit ledger then persists those 'redacted' fields verbatim to the evidence record.

## Why this matters

All current call sites use the provided constructors (`empty_redacted`, `redacted_from`, `redacted_from_redactor`), which honestly set `redacted=true` only AFTER running the redactor. So no current bug. But:

- A future contributor (human or agent) constructing the type directly would silently bypass the redactor.
- A serialization round-trip from an attacker-controlled JSON could deserialize a `redacted: true` flag with secret-bearing fields. If any deserialization-from-untrusted-source path exists (config file, IPC message, replay file), this is exploitable.

## Fix shape

1. Make `fields` and `redacted` `pub(crate)` so external constructors must use the constructor functions.
2. OR add a `#[serde(skip_deserializing)]` on `redacted` + a custom `Deserialize` that re-runs the sanitizer if needed.
3. OR add a runtime-assertion in `sanitized_for_evidence`: when `redacted=true`, sample one field's value through a 'looks-redacted' regex (e.g., contains `[REDACTED]` or all values pass a no-secret-pattern check). Log warn + force-sanitize on mismatch.

Easiest: Option 1 (visibility). Most defensive: combination of 1 + 3.

## Acceptance

- External callers cannot construct `SwarmCapacityEvidenceContext` with `redacted=true` + non-empty `fields` outside of the provided constructors.
- A regression test verifies that direct construction via destructuring is rejected at compile time (or runtime-asserted to FAIL with a clear error).

## Cross-references

- runtime_telemetry.rs:5540 (struct).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:5561 (sanitizer).
- ee844ccff (the commit that introduced sanitized_for_evidence as the chokepoint).
close_reason: done

title: [SEC] redactor STRIPE_KEY misses rk_*/whsec_* Stripe key formats (credentials leak past redactor)
description:
[SEC] redactor STRIPE_KEY regex misses rk_live_/rk_test_ restricted keys + whsec_ webhook secrets

## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:151`:

    static STRIPE_KEY: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
        Regex::new(r"[ps]k_(?:live|test)_[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}").expect("Stripe key regex")
    });

The `[ps]k_` character class only matches:
- `sk_live_*` / `sk_test_*` (secret keys)
- `pk_live_*` / `pk_test_*` (publishable keys)

Two production-grade Stripe credential formats are NOT caught:

1. **`rk_live_*` / `rk_test_*` (restricted keys)** — full API
   credentials with scoped permissions. Stripe docs:
   "Restricted keys provide read-only or limited access". Same
   sensitivity grade as `sk_*` for the scopes they own; an
   exposed `rk_live_*` is a credential leak.

2. **`whsec_*` (webhook signing secrets)** — used to verify
   webhook payloads via HMAC. An exposed `whsec_*` lets an
   attacker forge webhook events to the merchant's endpoint
   (e.g., fake `payment_intent.succeeded`, fake refunds).

Either format slipping past the redactor lands in the cold-tier
pipeline + audit_chain unredacted. Concrete impact: a developer
pasting `rk_live_AbCdEf...` into a pane is captured into logs;
the redactor's `redact()` returns the credential verbatim;
downstream consumers (cold tier, search index, audit log) see
the raw key.

## Repro

```rust
use frankenterm_core::redactor::Redactor;

let r = Redactor::new();
let leaked = r.redact("token rk_live_abc123def456ghi789jkl012mno345");
assert!(leaked.contains("[REDACTED]"));   // FAILS — verbatim leak
```

## Fix

Extend the alternation to include `rk` plus a separate
`whsec_` arm:

    Regex::new(r"(?:[psr]k_(?:live|test)|whsec)_[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}")

The `[psr]` class adds `r`; the trailing alternation `|whsec`
shares the `_<base62>{20,}` tail (whsec format is
`whsec_<random>` per Stripe webhook docs).

## Acceptance

- `redact("rk_live_<32+ chars>")` returns "[REDACTED]"
- `redact("rk_test_<32+ chars>")` returns "[REDACTED]"
- `redact("whsec_<32+ chars>")` returns "[REDACTED]"
- Existing `sk_*` / `pk_*` tests still pass
- `contains_secrets` true for all three new formats
- Tests added under redactor.rs's existing test module covering
  each new format

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:150-152 (STRIPE_KEY)
- Stripe docs: https://stripe.com/docs/keys#test-mode +
  https://stripe.com/docs/webhooks/signatures

title: [idea-wizard] Proof-doctor handoff automation and RCH evidence ledger convergence
description:
## Background

Idea-wizard pass after a no-ready-bead snapshot on 2026-05-10. Agent Mail was unavailable after the allowed retry, `br ready --json` returned no issues, and the active implementation/proof lanes were either owned by other agents or blocked on RCH/CI substrate. The repeated friction across recent Beads is the same: agents hand-write RCH closeout comments and manually decide whether evidence is a source failure, test failure, pre-Cargo RCH blocker, post-Cargo RCH blocker, local fallback, dirty-tree blocker, or safe remote pass.

The codebase already has strong pieces: `proof_doctor` DTOs/classifier, `proof_lane` durable record types, and `proof_handoff` Beads/Agent-Mail template rendering. The gap is productization and ingestion: the CLI/robot surface does not expose handoff packages, and proof runs still need manual parsing of RCH metadata/harness summaries before they become machine-checkable closeout artifacts.

## Phase 2: thirty ideas considered

Ideas considered before winnowing: proof-doctor handoff output in CLI; robot handoff payload; RCH meta JSON ingestion; harness summary ingestion; local fallback detector; remote Cargo/rustc started detector; selected-worker and target-dir normalization; dirty-tree ownership enrichment; proof lane JSONL writer; Beads comment renderer; Agent Mail dry-run package; artifact redaction status; high-scale hardware predicate import; CI check-run URL import; stale-worker mirror reason mapping; dep-info-loss substrate mapping; queue-timeout substrate mapping; proof closeout linter; proof artifact schema; proof doctor golden fixtures; e2e wrapper for proof handoff; terminal-conformance adoption docs; resource-cockpit adoption docs; capture-fairness adoption docs; README truth gate for proof claims; TOON compact handoff; MCP resource for proof handoffs; `br` comment dry-run integration; release scoreboard rollup; proof history search.

## Phase 2 top five

1. Expose proof handoff packages in CLI and robot proof-doctor output, because the pure handoff formatter already exists but operators/agents cannot request the Beads comment or Agent Mail payload from the normal tool surface.
2. Ingest RCH metadata and harness summaries into proof-doctor observed evidence, because source/proof closeout currently depends on each agent manually reading `.rch_meta.json` and script summaries.

title: [proof-handoff] Add golden fixtures for proof-doctor handoff and ledger outputs
description:
## Goal

Freeze the machine-facing proof-doctor handoff and ProofAttemptRecord outputs as reviewed golden artifacts so future changes cannot silently drift the closeout contract.

## Background

ft-782hw.1 exposed handoff payloads, ft-782hw.2 taught proof-doctor to ingest retained RCH artifacts, and ft-782hw.5 is adding durable proof records. Those surfaces are exactly the kind of complex structured output that needs scrubbed golden coverage: timestamps, worker names, target dirs, and artifact paths are dynamic, but verdict taxonomy, closeout eligibility, and handoff shape must stay stable.

## Scope

- Add golden fixtures for representative proof states: remote pass, source compile failure, test assertion failure, pre-Cargo RCH infrastructure blocker, post-Cargo RCH infrastructure blocker, local fallback invalid, dirty-tree blocker, and skipped_not_proven.
- Canonicalize dynamic fields before comparison: timestamps, UUIDs, worker hostnames when volatile, temp dirs, durations, and absolute local paths.
- Cover both human CLI and robot JSON/TOON shapes where the output surface differs materially.
- Include update instructions that require reviewing the fixture diff before accepting changes.

## Non-goals

- Do not invent a new proof schema; consume the ft-782hw.5 record shape.
- Do not run heavy Cargo locally; Rust proof goes through RCH.
- Do not update unrelated terminal/resource/attestation goldens.

## Acceptance

- Golden tests fail on accidental field removal, renamed reason codes, or changed closeout eligibility.
- Fixture update flow is documented and guarded by explicit UPDATE_GOLDENS-style opt-in.
- RCH-backed proof runs the focused proof-doctor/golden test lane and records selected worker, command, and artifact path in the closeout comment.

title: [proof-handoff] Add closeout linter for Beads comments and retained proof artifacts
description:
## Goal

Add a proof closeout linter that rejects ambiguous Beads comments and retained artifacts before agents claim a proof lane is closed.

## Background

The repo repeatedly distinguishes source failures, test failures, RCH substrate blockers, local fallback, dirty-tree blockers, and skipped_not_proven states. Humans can read the prose, but agents still make mistakes by treating sync chatter, transfer logs, or old queued CI runs as proof. Once ft-782hw.5 writes durable ProofAttemptRecord artifacts, a linter can mechanically enforce the closeout contract.

## Scope

- Provide a CLI/robot-accessible linter that accepts either a ProofAttemptRecord artifact path or proposed closeout text plus artifact paths.
- Reject closeout text that claims remote proof without selected_worker, command, remote Cargo/rustc/test evidence, and pass/fail classification.
- Reject local fallback as proof for RCH-required lanes.
- Require dirty-tree caveats when proof was run against a shared dirty checkout.
- Detect stale phrases such as treating RCH sync, rsync, cache warmup, or queued workflow status as proof by themselves.
- Emit structured findings with severity, reason_code, suggested Beads wording, and closeout_eligible boolean.

## Non-goals

- Do not call br or mutate beads automatically in the first version.
- Do not cancel/rerun CI or RCH jobs.
- Do not parse arbitrary historical comments beyond documented fixture cases.

## Acceptance

- Unit fixtures cover valid remote pass, valid source failure, valid infra-blocked handoff, invalid local fallback, invalid sync-only proof, invalid stale CI rollup, and missing artifact path.
- The linter integrates with the proof-doctor handoff output without adding a second taxonomy.
- RCH-backed test proof and lightweight static checks are recorded in the closeout comment.

title: [proof-handoff] Add proof history search and release scoreboard rollup
description:
## Goal

Build a machine-readable proof history and release scoreboard rollup from validated ProofAttemptRecord artifacts so operators can see which proof lanes are actually eligible for release.

## Background

The current release and reality-check workflow has many independent proof families: attestation, terminal conformance, renderer differential, resource cockpit, redactor coverage, and CI unblockers. Agents can find individual Beads comments, but there is no single queryable rollup that says which latest proof attempt passed, which is blocked by external infrastructure, which is dirty-tree contaminated, and which remains skipped_not_proven for target-class hardware.

## Scope

- Index ProofAttemptRecord JSONL artifacts from the documented artifact roots without parsing prose comments as the source of truth.
- Produce a scoreboard grouped by proof_category, bead_id, source commit, artifact hash, latest verdict, closeout eligibility, selected worker, and residual blocker.
- Preserve target-class truth: reduced RCH pass must not become high-scale PROVEN without the required hardware predicate.
- Provide JSON and compact TOON output suitable for robot consumers plus a human table for operator review.
- Include stale-artifact detection: missing file, unreadable JSON, hash mismatch, source commit mismatch, or artifact older than the current bead closeout.

## Non-goals

- Do not sign release bundles; this consumes proof records only.
- Do not replace docs/attestations manifests; cross-link them where available.
- Do not infer success from CI queued/success rollups unless a ProofAttemptRecord cites the run and required jobs.

## Acceptance

- Fixture records generate deterministic scoreboard output with pass, fail, infra_blocked, dirty_tree_blocked, and skipped_not_proven rows.
- The scoreboard can answer: latest proof for bead, all proof lanes blocking release, and all artifacts missing or stale.
- RCH-backed tests verify the focused Rust path; static checks cover docs/examples and schema fixtures.

title: canary rollout health gates treat NaN metrics as healthy
description:
Reality-check audit of canary_rollout_controller found rollout health gates do not validate finite metric/config inputs, so NaN can bypass fidelity/conflict thresholds and count as healthy.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:98-133 exposes CanaryRolloutConfig as public serde data with f64 canary_agent_fraction, fidelity_threshold, and max_conflict_rate, but no validate() method or constructor-time validation.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:277-289 constructs CanaryRolloutController directly from the supplied config.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:526-577 computes health by comparing diff.fidelity_score < config.fidelity_threshold and conflict_rate > config.max_conflict_rate. With NaN on either side, both comparisons are false, leaving failure_reasons empty.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:567-575 then records healthy=true and preserves the non-finite fidelity_score/conflict_rate in the health check.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:580-586 can auto-advance after enough healthy checks.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:131-180 defines ShadowModeDiff as public serde data with f64 dispatch_rate, agent_match_rate, and fidelity_score, so corrupted/deserialized metrics can reach the controller even if the local evaluator normally clamps finite values at crates/frankenterm-core/src/shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:568-576.
- Existing tests in crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:852-934 cover finite low-fidelity/high-conflict cases only; there is no NaN/Inf or malformed config coverage.

Why it matters: this controller gates Shadow -> Canary -> Full dispatch. A corrupted metric or config value should hold/rollback, not be interpreted as a clean health check that can advance rollout.

Proposed remediation: add config validation and health input sanitization. Require finite thresholds in [0,1], require finite diff.fidelity_score/conflict_rate inputs, and classify non-finite values as a new fail-closed HealthFailureReason such as InvalidMetric. Add tests/proptests for NaN, +/-Inf, out-of-range thresholds, and NaN diff fidelity.

title: protocol_recovery deterministic jitter defeats thundering-herd protection
description:
# [HIGH] protocol_recovery: fake jitter

**Subsystem:** protocol_recovery / retry
**File:** crates/frankenterm-core/src/protocol_recovery.rs (`RecoveryConfig::delay_for_attempt`)

## The hole

\`\`\`rust
let jitter_seed = ((attempt as f64 * 7.13).sin().abs()).mul_add(2.0, -1.0);
let jittered_ms = jitter_range.mul_add(jitter_seed, capped_ms).max(1.0);
\`\`\`

`sin(attempt * 7.13)` is fully deterministic. Every RecoveryEngine in the
process produces the **same** delay for a given attempt number. In a large
agent swarm, if 100 panes lose their mux connection simultaneously (mux
server restart), every engine schedules identical retry timings: attempt=0
→ delay_X, attempt=1 → delay_Y, etc. They all pile in at the same
instants — the exact thundering-herd collision that jitter exists to
prevent.

Pre-fix: `jitter_fraction: 0.1` looked like 10% decorrelation but produced
zero decorrelation across engines.

## Fix

Replaced the deterministic `sin()`-derived seed with
`rand::rng().random_range(-jitter_range..=jitter_range)` — same approach
already used in `retry.rs::RetryPolicy::delay_for_attempt`. Consistent with
how the other module in the same crate spells jitter.

Kept the `jitter_range > 0.0` fast-path so `jitter_fraction == 0.0` is
still bit-exact deterministic (tests rely on this).

## Caller impact

`RecoveryEngine::execute` uses `delay_for_attempt` to sleep between
protocol-error retries. No test depends on deterministic jitter
(`delay_for_attempt_*` tests set `jitter_fraction: 0.0`), so the fix is
drop-in.
close_reason: Fix already shipped in fdd1e817; regression tests added in bf4a63b9 (delay_for_attempt_jitter_is_randomized_across_calls + delay_for_attempt_zero_jitter_is_deterministic).

title: [LOW] FrameWriter Drop flush may abort on double-panic during unwind (7c8deb1d smell)
description: Fresh-eyes review of 7c8deb1d: Drop impl does I/O via BufWriter::flush. If flush panics during panic unwinding (OOM, broken-pipe custom impl), Rust aborts the process (double-panic). std File doesn't panic on I/O errors so low real-world risk, but defensive catch_unwind inside drop would harden.
close_reason: 2bb39b2d (linter-committed from my edits) wraps FrameWriter::drop's flush call in std::panic::catch_unwind with AssertUnwindSafe so a flush panic during a panic-unwind doesn't trip Rust's panic-during-unwind abort rule. AssertUnwindSafe is sound: closure Result discarded, &mut self never observed again, buffer/writer drop after closure regardless. Two new regression tests at recording.rs:1245 + 1301: (1) frame_writer_drop_completes_during_panic_unwind_without_aborting — integration test panicking inside a closure that owns a live FrameWriter with buffered frames; passing assertions prove Drop did not abort, and the buffered frame's bytes still made it to disk so the happy path runs; (2) frame_writer_drop_catch_unwind_swallows_inner_panic — standalone fence on the catch_unwind + AssertUnwindSafe idiom against future refactors. 5 frame_writer tests pass via rch on /tmp/ft-cc6-target.

title: tx_observability: max_events config is unused by bundle generation
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs:645-655 defines TxObservabilityConfig::max_events as the maximum observability events to retain.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs:658-665 defaults max_events to 4096.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs:669-679 build_forensic_bundle receives config, but crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs:684 passes the full events slice to build_timeline and never consults config.max_events.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs:235-309 build_timeline also consumes every supplied event.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_observability.rs:1237-1244 tests max_events only via serde roundtrip; there is no behavior test.

Impact:
Operators can configure an event retention budget that has no effect on bundle generation. Large event slices can create oversized bundles until max_timeline_entries truncates mixed ledger+event entries later, and that truncation is not equivalent to retaining bounded observability events.

Proposed remediation:
Either remove max_events from TxObservabilityConfig or apply it explicitly before timeline construction with documented semantics, such as retaining the most recent max_events matching tx events plus mandatory terminal/high-severity events. Add tests that set max_events=1 with multiple matching events and assert deterministic retained event selection.

title: Unified runtime telemetry records preserve raw scope and correlation IDs
description:
Reality-check audit evidence:
- `UnifiedTelemetryRecord::from_runtime_event` only passes `event.details` through `sanitize_runtime_details` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:592-615`). It then copies runtime `component`, `reason_code`, `correlation_id`, and `scope_id` directly into the unified record (`runtime_telemetry.rs:617-631`).
- The builder accepts arbitrary strings for `component`, `scope_id`, `reason_code`, and `correlation_id` (`runtime_telemetry.rs:2013-2062`), so the normal runtime event type can carry raw pane/session/user identifiers outside `details`.
- The dedicated diagnostic redactor knows these fields may be sensitive: it has explicit branches for redacting `correlation_id` and `scope_id` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/diagnostic_redaction.rs:301-314`). But the unified telemetry conversion does not invoke that redactor or hash those fields.
- Existing unified-record coverage asserts that sensitive details are masked while `record_id`, `correlation_id`, and `scope_id` remain raw (`runtime_telemetry.rs:14182-14222`), so this is current intended behavior in tests rather than an accidental missing assertion.

Why it matters:
`UnifiedTelemetryRecord` is described as a redacted normalized contract for correlation, triage, and severity routing. Detail redaction can report `Restricted`/`Mask` while still leaking sensitive correlation or scope identifiers in top-level fields and record IDs, especially when callers accidentally derive IDs from pane/session content or secret-bearing request IDs.

Proposed remediation:
Route runtime events through the diagnostic redaction policy before normalization, or apply a unified-record-specific policy that hashes/redacts `scope_id`, `correlation_id`, and any user-controlled component/reason fragments. Keep stable correlation by using deterministic hashes, and add tests using `scope_id = "daemon:capture:pane_42"` and `correlation_id = "session-secret-123"` to assert no raw values appear in the serialized unified record or record_id.
notes: Added opt-in id redaction at the unified-record boundary. New IdRedactionPolicy enum (Passthrough | Hash) + new from_runtime_event_with_id_redaction(event, policy) constructor. Hash policy replaces scope_id and correlation_id with deterministic 'hash:<u64-hex>' FNV-1a digests using the existing replay_capture::fnv1a_hash_text helper, and rewrites record_id to use the hashed correlation form (the original format embeds correlation_id). Cross-record correlation is preserved: two records with the same raw correlation_id produce the same hashed value. The legacy from_runtime_event + From<&RuntimeTelemetryEvent> impls keep Passthrough so existing callers/tests are unaffected; opt-in semantics. Added 3 tests: passthrough_keeps_raw_ids (legacy contract), hash_redacts_scope_and_correlation (asserts raw values absent from all fields including record_id and full JSON serialization), hash_is_deterministic_for_correlation (cross-record correlation preserved + different inputs hash differently). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: storage: deferred FTS sync skips seq=0 segment forever (seq > last_indexed_seq off-by-one)
description: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15902-15950 get_unindexed_segments_sync uses WHERE pane_id = ?1 AND seq > ?2 (strict >). crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:12355 append_segment_sync assigns next_seq = COALESCE(MAX(seq) + 1, 0), so the VERY FIRST segment in a fresh pane gets seq=0. Meanwhile sync_fts_for_pane at line 15966 initializes max_seq from progress.last_indexed_seq OR defaults to 0 when no progress exists: 'let last_seq = progress.as_ref().map_or(0, |p| p.last_indexed_seq);'. First-ever sync of a fresh pane hits 'WHERE seq > 0' which excludes the seq=0 segment — the pane's first captured output is silently dropped from the FTS index and never recoverable via sync_fts catchup. This is the defect the ft-wk5fo close-note explicitly surfaced but did not fix ('tests use seq 1..=N, separate bead for that fix'). Scope: a fresh pane's first segment is the command prompt / shell startup / first workflow output — high-value searchable content. Users get empty search results for anything only in that segment. Fix: distinguish 'never indexed' from 'indexed up through seq=0'. Cleanest minimal fix: in sync_fts_for_pane, when progress is None AND total_indexed == 0, query with an inclusive WHERE pane_id = ?1 (no seq filter) for the first batch. After the first batch writes progress, subsequent batches use the strict > query as today. Regression test must construct a pane whose first segment has seq=0 and assert sync_fts_for_pane indexes it.
close_reason: Landed in d37376b0 (fix(storage): unbreak sync_fts_for_pane call site + index seq=0 on first sync). Call-site updated to pass include_from_zero=true on the very first batch of a never-synced pane, false otherwise. had_prior_progress tracks the 'never indexed' sentinel. Regression test ft_7do6c_catchup_indexes_seq_zero_on_first_sync pins seq=0 indexing + resume invariant. Also unbroke main — 49937d56 had landed my half-done fix (signature + docstring only, no call-site update), causing an E0061 compile error at storage.rs:16004. Verification blocked by pre-existing frankenterm-core build blockers (ft-kqidb/uigpj/s2u51/zv3u9).

title: [ARCH] GuardedCommand wires PreflightChecker into CommandRouter::route (ft-1650n.1 slice 4)
description:
Slice 4 of ft-1650n.1: GuardedCommand variant on RemoteRequest wires PreflightChecker into a real operation path. Combines a preflight check with a downstream CommandRouter::route call — the router only sees the command if preflight returns Allowed; otherwise the response is RemoteResponse::Error with code='preflight_denied' + the outcome label embedded in the message.

Shipped:
- RemoteRequest::GuardedCommand { actor: PassportKey, required_classes: Vec<CapabilityClass>, request: Box<CommandRequest> }
- handle_request handler: runs preflight FIRST (uses passport_preflight if installed, else fails closed with MissingPassport); on non-Allowed outcome returns Error with code='preflight_denied' and message containing the outcome label; on Allowed dispatches to self.router.route(&cmd_req, &self.registry) — same path as the existing RemoteRequest::Command handler.
- Existing RemoteRequest::Command preserved unchanged for callers that don't yet carry capability metadata.

Coverage: 3 inline regression tests in headless_mux_server.rs:
- guarded_command_fails_closed_when_no_passport_store_ft_1650n_1: server with no passport store → preflight_denied with 'missing_passport' in message.
- guarded_command_denied_when_required_capability_unverified_ft_1650n_1: passport carries required class only at Declared (not Verified) → preflight_denied with 'missing_capabilities' in message.
- guarded_command_routes_through_when_preflight_allows_ft_1650n_1: Verified-and-fresh passport → response is NOT preflight_denied (router was reached). Targets a deliberately-unregistered pane so the router-side error code distinguishes preflight pass-through from preflight short-circuit.

Verified: cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features finished in 52s; --profile=test in 1m33s. 0 errors both.

What's STILL not in scope: per-command-variant capability schema (i.e. mapping each CommandKind::SendInput / Resize / etc to the specific CapabilityClasses it requires). Slice 4 puts the capability metadata in the request envelope so the caller declares what they need; the deeper 'server enforces required capabilities per command type' design needs a separate discussion.
