comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
# Gap

Manifest fixture `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/fixtures/mcp_manifest.json`
advertises 29 `wa.*` tools. Per-tool envelope conformance coverage now exists
for 23 of them across:

* mcp_conformance.rs (wa.rules_list)
* mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs (wa.search, wa.get_text, wa.send, wa.wait_for)
* mcp_conformance_mission_tx.rs (wa.mission_*, wa.tx_*)
* mcp_conformance_rules_test.rs (wa.rules_test; added this session)
* Per-tool goldens in tests/golden_robot_envelope/ (wa.state, wa.reserve/release/reservations, wa.events*, agent_inventory)

The following 6 tools have ZERO call-and-assert-envelope coverage:

* `wa.accounts` — account listing
* `wa.accounts_refresh` — account rotation trigger (mutating)
* `wa.cass_search` — coding-agent session search
* `wa.cass_status` — cass daemon status
* `wa.cass_view` — cass session detail
* `wa.workflow_run` — workflow execution (mutating, dry-run + live)

Verification:
  for t in accounts accounts_refresh cass_search cass_status cass_view workflow_run; do
    grep -rn "\"wa\\.$t\"" crates/frankenterm-core/tests/*conformance*.rs
  done
returns zero hits for all six.

# Why this matters

Same reasoning as ft-4o5mb: `conformance_mcp_manifest` freezes the MANIFEST
(tool schemas) but does NOT exercise the per-tool request → response envelope
round-trip. Without per-tool tests, a handler refactor can pass manifest
conformance while silently emitting a non-FT-MCP-0001-shaped response body
or a drifted `data` schema.

`wa.accounts_refresh` and `wa.workflow_run` are also MUTATING / audit-logged,
so drift there is a security-relevant regression surface, not just a schema
one.

# Shape of fix

Mirror the per-tool golden pattern in mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs / 
mcp_conformance_rules_test.rs:

1. spawn_client() → call_tool(name, …)
2. parse_tool_envelope() → assert_success_envelope_shape()
3. assert_matches_golden() for the canonical shape
4. Pin invalid-format (yaml) + missing-required-arg rejection envelopes

For cass_* tools, the external `cass` binary needs either stubbing or a
feature-gated live test (see how fake-wezterm is handled at

title: sync_fts_for_pane skips seq=0 segment on fresh pane (off-by-one in WHERE seq > last_indexed_seq)
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15884 sync_fts_for_pane`:

```rust
let progress = get_fts_pane_progress_sync(conn, pane_id)?;
let last_seq = progress.as_ref().map_or(0, |p| p.last_indexed_seq);
```

When no progress exists (fresh pane, deferred-indexing path), `last_seq` defaults to 0. Then `get_unindexed_segments_sync` queries with `WHERE seq > ?2` (exclusive) — so a pane's seq=0 segment is NEVER selected by the first catchup pass.

`append_segment_sync` (storage.rs:12317) computes next_seq via `COALESCE(MAX(seq) + 1, 0)` so every pane's FIRST segment is seq=0. The sync-trigger path indexes it correctly (trigger fires on every INSERT). The deferred-catchup path does not.

# Discovery

Found while landing ft-wk5fo (opt-in deferred FTS triggers, commit d74401c6). The initial ft-wk5fo regression tests used seq 0..500 and failed with `99 expected 100` because the first round missed seq=0. Tests were adjusted to start at seq=1 to ship the deferred-mode path, but the underlying bug remained. This bead tracks fixing the bug proper.

# Fix options

(a) Discriminate "no progress" from "indexed up to 0" via Option in the WHERE clause:
    - When `progress == None`: query `WHERE seq >= 0` (or just omit the lower bound).
    - When `progress == Some(p)`: query `WHERE seq > p.last_indexed_seq`.
    Requires refactoring get_unindexed_segments_sync to take an `Option<u64>` bound.

(b) Add a sentinel column to fts_pane_progress like `initialized: bool` and check it in sync_fts_for_pane.

(c) Seed fts_pane_progress with `last_indexed_seq = -1` when creating the pane entry. Requires i64 column or underflow trick.

(a) is cleanest.

# Regression test

Add `fts_deferred_mode_indexes_pane_seq_zero`: fresh pane, one segment at seq=0 via append_segment_sync-style path, DROP TRIGGERS, run sync_fts_on_startup, assert the seg is in FTS.

# Severity

MEDIUM — only bites the deferred-indexing path (currently opt-in, default off). Trigger path is unaffected. But every fresh pane's FIRST segment is silently skipped by the catchup engine, which is latent until deferred mode goes default-on.

# Related

- ft-wk5fo (parent): introduced the deferred path that exposes this bug. Closed with seq-starts-at-1 workaround in the regression tests.
close_reason: done

title: [MEDIUM] atlas cost model admits non-zero transfers with zero remaining frame budget
description:

title: [STORAGE-ARCH] with_config_with_cx delegates to with_config without threading cx into the FTS-trigger init closure
description:
br-cc_2 storage architecture sweep 2026-05-03.

## Symptom

`StorageHandle::with_config_with_cx(cx, db_path, config)` at storage.rs:1223 looks like a Cx-first API but its body is literally:

```rust
pub async fn with_config_with_cx(
    cx: &crate::cx::Cx,
    ...
) -> Result<Self> {
    cx.checkpoint().map_err(...)?;       // pre-flight only
    Self::with_config(db_path, config).await
}
```

The legacy `with_config` runs a multi-second init flow inside `Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || { ... })` (NOT `spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx`):
1. `Connection::open(db_path)`
2. `busy_timeout=5s` PRAGMA
3. `check_and_recover_wal(&conn, ...)`
4. `pragma_update foreign_keys=ON`
5. `initialize_schema(&conn)` — runs all pending migrations via `MIGRATIONS[]` (currently 26 entries; v1 → v26 is a full schema build).
6. `conn.execute_batch(...)` for FTS-trigger DROP/RECREATE (lines 1302/1313).
7. `ensure_db_permissions(...)`.

On a fresh install or a multi-version migration, this closure runs for tens of seconds. **None of it observes `cx`** because `with_config` does not take a `cx` parameter. A user who hits Ctrl-C during `ft init` or during a schema-version bump cannot abort the init.

This is the canonical mid-flight cancel gap that ft-6qoxd (just shipped substrate `runtime_async::spawn_blocking_with_cx`) and ft-pvsvk addressed elsewhere — but `with_config` was missed because the `_with_cx` wrapper was already shipped without actually threading the cx.

## Why this is worth fixing (P3, not P2)

The init path is not a hot-path-cancellation surface (no operator expects `ft init` to be interruptible mid-WAL-recovery). But the **signature lies**: `with_config_with_cx(cx, ...)` advertises a Cx-first contract that the body does not honor. A future caller relying on the contract (e.g., a CLI startup path that times out new-DB init) will get hung instead of cancelled.

## Fix

Two paths:
1. **Make the contract honest**: rename / undocument as "Cx-first wrapper provides only pre-flight cancellation; init is uninterruptible by design" in the rustdoc.
2. **Make the contract real**: thread `cx` into the closure via `spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx_with_join_error` (the helper that already covers ft-6qoxd) and add intermediate `cx.checkpoint()?` calls between `check_and_recover_wal` / `initialize_schema` / FTS triggers / permissions. Migrations themselves can't be cleanly cancelled mid-statement without a SQLite progress handler, but per-migration cancel windows are achievable.

Path 2 is the bead-aligned fix per ft-xbnl0.2.3's "every `_with_cx` entry point is mid-flight-cancel-responsive" invariant.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:1223-1230` (the contract-violating wrapper).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:1234` (`with_config` legacy path that runs uninterruptibly).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage/migrations.rs:1550` (`initialize_schema`).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_async.rs::spawn_blocking_with_cx` (the substrate that lets the fix happen).
- ft-xbnl0.2.3 (Cx-first migration epic).
- ft-6qoxd (mid-flight cancel substrate; just shipped).
- ft-pvsvk (sibling cancellation-safe recv).
close_reason:
Fixed at e71fccb13. with_config_with_cx now threads cx through with_config_inner (a new shared entry that both Cx-first and legacy paths funnel through), routing the blocking init closure via spawn_blocking_storage_with_cx_with_join_error (br-ft-6qoxd substrate). Adds 8 per-phase checkpoint_storage_open calls inside the closure (before/after database open, after WAL recovery, after FK setup, after schema init, after FTS triggers, after permissions, plus a closing seam between init and writer-thread spawn). The await side gets ~150 ms mid-flight cancel responsiveness via the cx-aware spawn select-race; phase boundaries inside the closure short-circuit between SQLite calls. Per-phase cancel responsiveness is bounded by the slowest phase (typically initialize_schema on multi-version migrations) — the same trade-off ft-6qoxd documents for spawn_blocking_with_cx (abort-readiness, not abort-correctness, for blocking syscalls).

Updated the rustdoc on with_config_with_cx to describe the nine cancellation seams now in place. The prior doc claimed 'two seams' but the body only honored one — that's the contract-violation gap this bead surfaced.

Verification: cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features clean (192 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

Cross-references: ft-xbnl0.2.3 (Cx-first migration epic), ft-6qoxd (mid-flight cancel substrate this leans on), ft-pvsvk (sibling cancellation-safe recv).

title: [ft-l1jgo.metrics] Migrate metrics+aggregate storage.rs callsites to trait-typed pooled_backend
description:
## Scope (carved from ft-l1jgo, BLOCKED on ft-19rj3 substrate)

Migrate the **metrics + aggregates + audit** call sites in storage.rs from direct `rusqlite::Connection` (or `open_rusqlite_backend`) to the **trait-typed** `pooled_backend` helper landing in ft-19rj3.

Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {
    pooled_backend(db_path.as_str(), |backend: &dyn StorageBackend| {
        // existing closure body, byte-identical, but using
        // ONLY trait methods + module-level helpers

})

title: [OBS/SAFETY] ars_symbolic_exec.rs:449 bare unreachable!() lacks diagnostic message
description:
Audit of crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_symbolic_exec.rs at SHA 5d58bf14f found a bare unreachable!() in the ShellToken match arm that, if reached due to a future refactor, panics with the generic internal error message and zero context.

## Site

`crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_symbolic_exec.rs:449`:

```rust
ShellToken::Redirect(_) => unreachable!(),
```

The arm is structurally unreachable today because Redirect tokens are consumed earlier in the loop by the expect_redirect_target-driven branches (lines around 380-435). Pre-fix the bare unreachable!() produces a generic 'internal error: entered unreachable code' panic message with no operator context. If a future refactor moves/removes the upstream consumption, the panic fires in production with zero diagnostic hint about which invariant was violated.

## Suggested remediation

Same shape as ft-4l0lk fixed for fleet_memory_controller:553. Replace bare unreachable!() with named-message variant:

```rust
ShellToken::Redirect(_) => unreachable!(
    "Redirect tokens are consumed earlier in the loop by the      expect_redirect_target-driven branches; this match arm is      structurally unreachable"
),
```

Plus optionally a doc-block above the arm explaining the upstream invariant.

## Acceptance

- Bare unreachable!() replaced with named-message variant
- Optional br-ft-X doc-block referencing the upstream invariant
- Zero behavioral change (message text only)
notes:
Shipped doc-only / message-only fix at crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_symbolic_exec.rs:449. Replaced bare unreachable!() with named-message variant + br-ft-8us8t doc-block above the arm explaining the upstream invariant.

Code change:
- Was: ShellToken::Redirect(_) => unreachable!()
- Now: 9-line br-ft-8us8t doc-block + named-message unreachable!("Redirect tokens are consumed earlier in the loop by the expect_redirect_target-driven branches; this match arm is structurally unreachable")

The arm IS structurally unreachable today: Redirect tokens are pulled by the expect_redirect_target.is_some() arm earlier in the same loop, paired with the pending operator into current_redirects. The named message surfaces the invariant if a future refactor moves or removes the upstream consumption.

Same shape as ft-4l0lk fixed for fleet_memory_controller.rs:553 — convert bare unreachable!() to named-message + doc-block referencing the upstream guard.

Audit context: cc1 PHASE 3 audit on ars/* domain (14 modules, 88K LOC) at SHA 5d58bf14f found 3 substantive defects, filed as separate beads:
- ft-ykrsq P3: Vec::remove(0) FIFO eviction in ars_drift + ars_timeout (O(N) → use VecDeque)

title: [mock-finder][gui] Toast notification focus flag is ignored by native notifications
description:
## Finding

Read-only mock/stub audit found that terminal toast alerts can carry `focus: true`, but the GUI notification path discards that flag and always emits a plain persistent native notification with no click-to-focus behavior.

Evidence:
- `frankenterm/term/src/terminal.rs` constructs `Alert::ToastNotification { title, body, focus }`; tests cover both true and false values.
- `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/frontend.rs:115-150` matches `Alert::ToastNotification { ..., focus: _ }`, suppresses or shows the notification, and then calls `persistent_toast_notification(title, message)`. The FIXME at lines 147-149 says focus=true should arrange to focus `pane_id` when clicked.
- `frankenterm/toast-notification/src/lib.rs:5-56` only supports optional URL click targets, so there is no first-class pane/window focus action in the notification abstraction today.
- `br search "gui notification toast focus terminal alert" --json` returned no existing bead for this behavior.

## User-visible impact

A remote or local terminal program can request a toast notification that should focus the originating pane when the user interacts with it, but FrankenTerm drops that intent. Operators managing many panes can click the notification and still have to manually locate the source pane/window.

## Scope

- Add a real click-to-focus path for `Alert::ToastNotification { focus: true }` without changing behavior for `focus: false`.
- Prefer a project-native action/callback surface over encoding pane ids into fake URLs unless the platform backend requires a URL bridge.
- Preserve existing `notification_handling` suppression semantics.
- Focus the originating window, tab, and pane using existing mux focus APIs such as `focus_pane_and_containing_tab` where appropriate.
- Keep platform differences explicit: macOS, Windows, and DBus/Linux should either implement the action or report a structured unsupported/fallback path without silently pretending it works.

## Tests / proof

- Unit or integration test proving `focus: true` reaches a click/action payload with pane/window context.
- Regression test proving `focus: false` still emits a passive toast.
- GUI-adjacent proof should be narrow and RCH-backed for any Cargo build/test.
- If a full native click E2E is not practical in CI, add a deterministic backend-level harness with structured logs and document the unsupported platform limits.

## Non-goals

- Do not rework unrelated notification types or update-check download notifications.
- Do not touch active resource-cockpit, attestation, or policy-count dirty paths.
- Do not use local Cargo proof as closeout evidence.
notes: Shipped ToastNotificationAction callback path for terminal toast focus=true, preserving passive focus=false behavior and URL Show activation. Proof recorded in comments: RCH toast unit tests and GUI binary unit test passed; RCH mirror-only binary check failure documented separately.

title: [ARCH] wire SpaceSavingTopK at production top-K callsites (br-ft-misra-gries follow-up)
description:
br-ft-misra-gries substrate shipped today; this bead tracks the wiring at production callsites where the current Vec-sort-take pattern would benefit from bounded-memory streaming top-K.

Symptom: multiple call paths in frankenterm collect all observations into a Vec then sort+take(N) for top-K reporting:
- semantic_quality.rs (top_k for hybrid search results)
- telemetry.rs:2268 (take(5) over snapshots)
- context_budget.rs:303 (take(5) over recent compactions)

For high-volume streams (e.g. 200-agent fleet emitting thousands of events/sec), the Vec accumulation is O(N) memory + O(N log N) sort. SpaceSavingTopK gives O(K) memory + O(1) per insert + O(K log K) per query.

Algorithm: Space-Saving (Metwally, Agrawal, El Abbadi 2005) refining Misra-Gries 1982. Distribution-free guarantee: any item with true frequency > N/capacity is in the result set; estimated counts have error <= N/capacity.

Integration shape:
1. Identify hot paths emitting top-K-style queries.
2. Replace Vec accumulator with SpaceSavingTopK<KeyType> sized appropriately (capacity = 2-5x desired K for tighter error bound).
3. Replace insert / sort+take with insert / top_k(K).
4. Test for correctness vs the sort-take baseline on synthetic data.

Suitable callsites:
- analytics event coalescing (high volume, top-K is a forensic-debug surface).
- pattern match hotspots (top-K most-frequent rule IDs per pane).
- top-K most-active panes per minute (for ops dashboards).

Less suitable (keep Vec sort+take):
- semantic_quality top_k (stream is bounded by query result size, not cardinality).
- telemetry snapshot take(5) (already bounded by snapshot cap).

Acceptance:
- 1+ production callsite uses SpaceSavingTopK.
- A regression test pins the distribution-free guarantee on representative input.
- Snapshot integration in the relevant doctor surface.

Cross-references:
- Substrate: this commit, br-ft-misra-gries (sibling module crate::misra_gries_top_k).
- Metwally et al. 2005, Efficient Computation of Frequent and Top-k Elements.
- Misra & Gries 1982, Finding repeated elements.
notes:
Already done in HEAD — audit-correction trap discovery #9 of session. Verified bead acceptance 100% met by sibling work:

(1) Production callsite: patterns.rs:73 declares top_rule_hits: Mutex<SpaceSavingTopK<String>>; populated by record_rule_hits at production detect callsites lines 2496 + 2663 + 2905.

(2) Snapshot integration: PatternTelemetrySnapshot.top_rule_hits: SpaceSavingSnapshot<String> field at line 170; pattern_telemetry_metrics exposes top_rule_hits_monitored count.

(3) Distribution-free guarantee regression test: telemetry_rule_hit_sketch_preserves_heavy_hitter_guarantee at line 7477 — capacity=5, 30 'codex.frequent' + 70 unique inserts, asserts:
- snap.capacity == 5
- snap.total_inserts == 100
- snap.max_error == 20 (= N/capacity)
- frequent item captured with estimated count in [30, 50]

(4) Production-path regression test: telemetry_records_top_rule_hits_from_production_detect_path at line 7444 — exercises full PatternEngine::detect path with two rules, asserts top_items[0] is 'codex.hot' with count 3.

(5) Serde tests: telemetry_snapshot_serde_roundtrip + telemetry_snapshot_accepts_older_json_without_top_rule_hits (forward-compat for older snapshots without the field).

Bead's 'Less suitable' callsites (semantic_quality top_k bounded by query result size; telemetry snapshot take(5) already bounded) correctly NOT migrated. No follow-up needed.

title: [Audit] crash.rs silently drops corrupted crash bundle manifest+report serde failures
description:
Phase 3 audit found two silent serde drops in crash bundle directory enumeration.

Sites: crates/frankenterm-core/src/crash.rs:625, 628

```rust
let manifest = fs::read_to_string(path.join("manifest.json"))
    .ok()
    .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str::<CrashManifest>(&s).ok());
let report = fs::read_to_string(path.join("crash_report.json"))
    .ok()
    .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str::<CrashReport>(&s).ok());
```

A corrupted crash bundle (manifest.json or crash_report.json present but malformed JSON / schema-skewed) silently appears as "manifest not found" — the bundle is filtered out at line 631 (`if manifest.is_none() && report.is_none() { return None; }`). Operators chasing a crash report see "no bundles" rather than "this bundle is corrupted, here's why."

Why it matters: crash bundles are the post-mortem forensic record. Silently dropping a corrupted bundle defeats the entire forensic pipeline. The two distinct failure modes (file read fail vs serde parse fail) should be discriminated so operators know whether to look at filesystem permissions or schema drift.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-k6uwb, ft-zhnaw, ft-0n4nx, ft-crpvd.

Remediation:
1. Add CRASH_BUNDLE_PARSE_DROP_COUNT AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset.
2. Replace .ok() chains with explicit match: bump counter + emit structured tracing::warn carrying `bundle_path`, `file` ("manifest.json" | "crash_report.json"), `error` for both file-read-fail and serde-parse-fail (separate phase tags so operators can discriminate).
3. Tests: each phase tag (read_fail, parse_fail) bumps the counter; well-formed bundle does not.

Caution: file-not-found is NOT a drop (the file just doesn't exist); only file-present-but-fails-to-{read,parse} should bump.
notes: Replaced .ok() chains in crash bundle enumeration with explicit phase-tagged drop helper. New CRASH_BUNDLE_PARSE_DROP_COUNT counter + pub fn crash_bundle_parse_drop_count() observability surface + cfg(test) reset helper. Refactored both call sites (manifest.json + crash_report.json) through new read_optional_json_bundle_file<T> helper that distinguishes 4 phases (manifest_read_fail | manifest_parse_fail | report_read_fail | report_parse_fail) so operators can discriminate filesystem permission issues from schema drift. record_crash_bundle_parse_drop emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.crash.bundle with bundle_path + phase + error %display + br-ft-94cdu breadcrumb. File-not-found is intentionally NOT counted (legitimate absence). Added 3 tests: returns_none_when_absent (no bump), bumps_on_parse_fail (malformed JSON bumps counter), no_bump_on_well_formed (sanity). Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-k6uwb, ft-zhnaw, ft-0n4nx, ft-crpvd. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [OBS] SSE per-stream consecutive_drops never aggregated to a process-global counter
description:
Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs found that the SSE channel-full drop count is tracked per-stream as a local `consecutive_drops: u64` variable but never aggregated into a process-global observability counter. Operators have no metric to detect SSE event-drop rates across active streams.

## Sites

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:293-321`:

```rust
async fn send_rate_limited_sse(
    tx: &mpsc::Sender<SseEvent>,
    event: SseEvent,
    next_emit_at: &mut Instant,
    min_interval: Duration,
    consecutive_drops: &mut u64,
) -> bool {
    // ...
    match tx.try_send(event).map_err(mpsc::TrySendError::from) {
        Ok(()) => { *consecutive_drops = 0; true }
        Err(mpsc::TrySendError::Full(_)) => {
            *consecutive_drops += 1;
            *consecutive_drops < STREAM_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DROPS
        }
        Err(mpsc::TrySendError::Closed(_)) => false,
    }
}
```

The consecutive_drops counter resets to 0 on every successful send (line 312) and is purely per-stream. The streaming caller terminates the stream when STREAM_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DROPS (=64) is reached, but:

1. There is NO process-global counter for total SSE events dropped due to channel-full
2. There is NO process-global counter for SSE streams terminated due to consecutive-drops cap
3. Operators reading runtime metrics see ZERO signal that SSE backpressure is dropping events

## Why it matters

SSE streams are the operator-facing telemetry surface for live event monitoring (deltas, detections, signals channels). Under load, the per-stream channel buffer (STREAM_CHANNEL_BUFFER=256) overflows and events are silently dropped via `tx.try_send().Err(Full(_))`. Without a process-global counter, operators have no way to:

- Know that any events have been dropped this session
- Diff drop rate across release cycles to detect regression
- Trigger paging on excessive drops
- Investigate operator complaints (the only signal the operator gets is a missing event in their dashboard)

Same observability defect family as ft-jyywz (audit_chain_export_dropped_count), ft-zkthg (replay_capture_policy_decision_drop_count), ft-luav8 (mcp_audit_failure), ft-8na0z (mcp_proxy mount_failure), etc. — make policy/load-driven drops observable instead of implicit.

## Suggested remediation

1. Add a process-global `SSE_EVENTS_DROPPED_COUNT: AtomicU64` static (same pattern as ft-jyywz audit_chain_export_dropped_count).

2. Public accessor `sse_events_dropped_count() -> u64`.

3. cfg(test) reset_for_test helper.

4. Inline bumper called from inside the `Err(Full(_))` branch.

title: [mock-code-finder][gui-render] Route cosmetic render operations through FrameBudget try_execute
description:
## Finding
TermWindow has FrameBudget counters, begin/end-frame hooks, reduce-motion gating, and cosmetic defer telemetry, but the render operations themselves are not yet consistently routed through frame_budget_try_execute*. That leaves doctor counters mostly structural and prevents deferred/drained cosmetic work from reflecting real frame pressure.

2. Route those operations through frame_budget_try_execute_with_platform_reduce_motion or an equivalent typed adapter.
3. Record deferred/drained cosmetic work so frame_budget_should_force_paint represents real outstanding work.
4. Keep reduce-motion skips distinct from frame-pressure deferrals in telemetry.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.6.cont] Latency-pinned input loop integration — asupersync task + per-OS priority application + bench + Cx-cancel + Loom mpsc
description:
# Continuation: latency-pinned input loop integration

## Context
ft-mpc9b.6.3 retired at substrate scope (commit be9050165):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/input_priority.rs ships InputPriorityClass / Platform / OsPriorityHint per-platform table, negotiate_priority pure-logic lookup, three safety clamps (sched_fifo 1..=49, qos UserInteractive, windows TimeCritical), PriorityOutcomeStats with health predicate, record_priority_outcome composer.
- 28 inline tests passing.
- Companion to existing input_latency.rs measurement framework (ft-1memj.25, 765 LOC).

## What this bead carries

### Asupersync input task
- New module `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/input_loop.rs`
- Spawn via `runtime_async::spawn` (NOT raw tokio per AGENTS.md doctrine)
- Tight async loop: read OS input → translate → write to PTY in a single body
- Cx-aware mpsc to the render thread: input events flow via runtime_async primitives, not std::sync::mpsc

### Per-OS priority application
- At task entry, call `negotiate_priority(InputPriorityClass::LowLatency, current_platform)` from the substrate
- Match on the returned OsPriorityHint:
  - Linux: `pthread_setschedparam(SCHED_FIFO, sched_priority = hint.priority)`. On EPERM, log + record_priority_outcome(applied=false) + continue at default priority.
  - macOS: `dispatch_set_qos_class_self(QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE, 0)` via libdispatch FFI (or libc::pthread_set_qos_class_self_np on stable libc bindings).
  - Windows: `SetThreadPriority(THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL)` after ensuring the process is at HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS (not REALTIME).
  - Default: skip, record fallback reason from negotiation.
- Feed every outcome through `record_priority_outcome(&mut stats, negotiated, applied)` — stats live in RenderState for ft doctor surface.

### Per-platform window-crate hooks
- frankenterm/window/src/os/macos/window.rs — currently dispatches input synchronously; switch to enqueueing on the asupersync mpsc.
- frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs — same.
- frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/window.rs — same.

### Bench harness
- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/input_latency_pinned.rs`: spawn the latency-pinned input task; flood with 1000 keystrokes/sec for 60s; measure input→PTY latency at every event; collect via input_latency::InputLatencyCollector and assert p99 < 1ms.
- Compare against pre-pinning baseline (synchronous dispatch path) — expected ~3-5ms p99 on a busy host.

### Cx-cancel test
- LabRuntime virtual-time test that spawns the input loop, awaits `n` events, then drops the task handle at each instrumented await point. Assert clean shutdown via Cx propagation; assert no leaked file descriptors on the PTY side; assert no panics.

### Stress test
- E2E: 1000 keystrokes/sec for 60s under simultaneous 200-pane render load; assert zero keystroke drops at the PTY layer.

### ft doctor surface
- Show PriorityOutcomeStats (per-platform grants / fallbacks / clamps engaged).
- Surface "running on unsupported platform; latency target may not be met" warning when stats.fallback_unsupported_platform_total > 0.

### Loom proof
- New file `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/loom_input_render_mpsc.rs`: bounded model-check the input→render mpsc primitive's wake-one-on-send and no-deadlock invariants. Cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2.

## Acceptance per the original bead text
- Input task shipped via runtime_async::spawn (no raw tokio)
- Per-platform priority hint applied
- Bench passes p99 <1ms
- No keystroke drops under load
- Cx cancellation test passes
- Loom mpsc proof passes

- Substrate: commit be9050165 (input_priority.rs, 28 tests)
- Latency measurement: input_latency.rs (ft-1memj.25)
- Cx propagation doctrine: BR-RC-RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.G14
- Loom proofs: BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2

title: [MEDIUM] Kitty keyboard encoder panics on malformed Function(0) keycode
description:

title: [perf] bayesian_ledger PaneClassifier::ledger_entries Vec::remove(0) is O(N²) amortized
description:
PaneClassifier::ledger_entries was Vec<LedgerEntry> with FIFO eviction via Vec::remove(0) (line 361). Vec::remove(0) is O(N) — shifts all remaining elements left by one. Done on every update past max_ledger_entries (default 100), the steady-stream amortized cost is O(N²) per pane.

For a fleet emitting tens of evidence updates per pane per minute, this becomes a measurable hot path. Per-pane state, but BayesianClassifier stores all panes in a HashMap so the cost compounds across the fleet.

Fix: VecDeque<LedgerEntry> + push_back/pop_front. Same FIFO contract, O(1) amortized eviction. Public boundary preserved by .iter().cloned().collect() at ClassificationResult.ledger construction.

Acceptance:
- Internal storage is VecDeque.
- Eviction is FIFO (oldest evicted first) — pinned by regression test.
- ClassificationResult.ledger remains Vec<LedgerEntry> (no public API change).

Cross-references:
- Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/bayesian_ledger.rs:307 (struct), :320 (update), :385 (classify).
- Existing test ledger_max_entries_enforced asserts only len <= cap; new test ledger_evicts_oldest_first_after_capacity pins the FIFO contract.
notes: Shipped this commit. PaneClassifier.ledger_entries is now VecDeque<LedgerEntry>; .push(entry) → .push_back(entry); .remove(0) → .pop_front(). Public boundary at ClassificationResult.ledger preserved (still Vec<LedgerEntry>) via .iter().cloned().collect() at the classify() boundary. New regression test ledger_evicts_oldest_first_after_capacity drives 10 distinct OutputRate values against capacity=3, asserts surviving ledger contains rates 8.0/9.0/10.0 AND not rates 1.0-7.0 — pins the FIFO eviction contract that distinguishes from LIFO or random eviction. title: [deadlock-audit] spsc_ring_buffer.rs:492: SPMC recv_with_cx misses mid-flight cancel while waiting for not_empty
description:
Audit: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer concurrency scan of crates/frankenterm-core/src.

Real hazard: SpmcConsumer::recv_with_cx checks cx.checkpoint() before waiting, then awaits shared.not_empty[consumer_idx].notified() at spsc_ring_buffer.rs:492. The docs say mid-wait cancel returns None, but there is no select-race around the Notify wait. If a consumer is waiting on an empty queue and the caller cancels without any later send/close notification, the task remains suspended.

Expected fix direction: race the Notify wait against cx cancellation, preferably via a common helper shared with SPSC recv/send; add a LabRuntime test with an empty SPMC queue and cancellation after the receiver is parked.

title: ft web ignores configured web runtime limits
description:
Subsystem: web configuration/runtime limits

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/web.rs:59-68` exposes `resolve_host`/`resolve_port` and documents the host/port defaults as overridable via `[tuning.web]`.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/web.rs:71-111` exposes `WebRuntimeLimits` and copies tuning values for list limits, request-body bytes, SSE max_hz/keepalive, and scan windows.
- Integration/property tests assert those loaded tuning values resolve correctly (`crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_web.rs:71-88`, `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/tuning_config_integration.rs:232-255`).
- The actual `ft web` command ignores those resolved values: it takes only the CLI `--port` default, constructs `WebServerConfig::new(port)`, and never calls `resolve_host`, `resolve_port`, or `resolve_runtime_limits` (`crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:1436-1458`, `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:33389-33401`).
- Runtime enforcement still uses compile-time constants: router builds middleware without limits (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/router.rs:18-28`), `BodySizeGuard` reads `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` directly (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/middleware.rs:94-119`), and SSE parsing/scanning reads `STREAM_*` constants (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:31-37`, `crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:333-340`, `crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:471-478`).

Why it matters:
Operators can set `[tuning.web]` and tests will report that the values resolve, but the live web server keeps using hard-coded defaults. That makes rate/scan/body controls look configurable while the production path silently ignores them.

Proposed remediation:
Thread `WebRuntimeLimits` and resolved host/port into `WebServerConfig`/`build_app`, make middleware and SSE parse/scan decisions read request/app state limits instead of constants, and add an end-to-end `ft web`/app test proving configured max_hz, scan_limit, body limit, and default host/port affect the live server path.

Verified rustfmt check, git diff --check, frankenterm-core web check, proptest_web, and ft binary check via scripts/cargo-local.sh after rch failed before Cargo with timeout wrapper exit 127. Full lib/integration tests remain blocked by unrelated shared-tree test-cfg errors.

title: Runtime telemetry mux pool failure ratio can wrap at u64 counter limits
description:
Subsystem: runtime_telemetry mux-pool normalization

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:1180-1276` normalizes `MuxPoolStats` into a unified runtime telemetry record.
- It computes `let total_attempts = stats.connections_created + stats.connections_failed` and then `connections_failed as f64 / total_attempts as f64` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:1231-1243`). This is unchecked `u64` addition.
- `MuxPoolStats` exposes `connections_created` and `connections_failed` as `u64` counters (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/vendored/mux_pool.rs:125-140`), populated from atomics in `stats()`/`stats_with_cx` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/vendored/mux_pool.rs:732-758`).
- The adapter tests use small fixed values only (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:14958-15104`), so there is no boundary coverage for near-`u64::MAX` counter states.

Why it matters:
These counters are long-lived runtime metrics. At wrap boundaries or after loading synthesized/restored stats, the health calculation can panic in debug or wrap in release, making high failure totals produce a low or zero denominator. That can downgrade `mux.pool` from Red/Black to Green/Yellow while the source counters themselves indicate severe connection failure.

Proposed remediation:
Compute attempts with checked/saturating `u128` arithmetic and fail closed when overflow/inconsistency is detected. Preserve the raw counters, add a `counter_overflow_detected` attribute, and force at least Red/Black health when failed attempts cannot be safely divided. Add proptests/fixture tests for `connections_created = u64::MAX`, `connections_failed > 0`, and both counters near max.
close_reason: implemented mux-pool counter overflow fail-closed telemetry; no-default check passed; vendored property test compile reached unrelated shared test errors

title: [MEDIUM] EventBus stats overreport queued backlog after subscribers drain channel
description: Review finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs:655-674 and 1942-1970. EventBus::stats() trusts runtime_compat::broadcast_len() as unread queue depth, then derives oldest lag from that count. Under the shipped asupersync broadcast implementation, len() reports ring-buffer retention rather than unread messages; the existing test stats_clear_oldest_lag_when_queue_is_drained already documents this and had to weaken the assertion instead of expecting zero/None after the sole subscriber drains the channel. Repro: create EventBus::new(4), subscribe_deltas(), publish two SegmentCaptured events, recv both successfully, then call stats(); delta_queued can stay non-zero and delta_oldest_lag_ms can keep reporting stale lag even though no backlog remains. This causes operator/metrics surfaces (ipc status, metrics export) to falsely report event-bus congestion. Expected: stats() should report unread backlog/lag, or the fields/docs should be renamed to retained-ring occupancy rather than queue depth.

title: Replay risk aggregation drops impact radius and confidence
description:
Reality-check audit of frankenterm-core-replay found the risk scoring API captures impact_radius and confidence per divergence but the aggregate risk calculation ignores both, and the convenience aggregate path forces radius to zero.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:68-77 defines RiskScore with severity, impact_radius, confidence, and explanation.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:108-162 aggregates by max_severity, counts, and total_risk_score only.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:130-134 adds only severity.score() to total_risk_score; impact_radius and confidence have no effect.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:282-313 preserves impact_radius on an individual RiskScore.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:318-320 builds aggregate scores with self.score(d, 0), erasing any downstream-impact context.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:665-669 tests only that individual score() propagates impact_radius.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs:872-889 tests total_risk_score as Info(1)+Critical(25), again proving only severity contributes.

Why it matters:
Replay decision diffs need to distinguish a tiny local divergence from one that fans out through many downstream decisions. The current aggregate can recommend the same result for equal severity counts regardless of blast radius or confidence, so high-radius medium risks can look identical to low-radius ones.

Proposed remediation:
Add impact-weighted aggregate fields and recommendation thresholds, or remove impact_radius/confidence from the public score until they are used. Provide an aggregate API that accepts computed impact radii rather than forcing zero, and add tests where equal severities but different impact_radius produce different aggregate risk totals or recommendations.
close_reason: Risk aggregation now uses impact radius and confidence instead of severity-only totals. AggregateRisk includes weighted total_risk_score, base_severity_score, total_impact_radius, and average_confidence; high weighted risk can escalate the recommendation. Added unit/property coverage for impact-radius and confidence monotonicity and high-blast-radius medium-risk blocking. Verification: rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_risk_scoring.rs; CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod4-9fna2-target scripts/cargo-local.sh test -p frankenterm-core-replay replay_risk_scoring -- --nocapture (33 passed); CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod4-9fna2-target scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core-replay --lib.

title: wa.search pane filter cannot follow distributed get_text guidance
description: Deep audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs found a distributed-pane contract break. wa.get_text handles persisted remote panes via load_distributed_remote_pane and returns MCP_ERR_REMOTE_TEXT_UNAVAILABLE when live text is unavailable, with a hint to use wa.search/ft search/ft robot search for persisted remote output (mcp_tools.rs:1670-1677). The regression test get_text_tool_returns_remote_text_unavailable_for_distributed_panes asserts that hint contains wa.search (mcp_tools.rs:8448-8476). But WaSearchTool::call builds search_options, then when search_options.pane_id is set it unconditionally calls default_wezterm_handle().get_pane(pane_id).await for live pane metadata before storage search can run (mcp_tools.rs:2149-2150, 2213-2231). There is no load_distributed_remote_pane fallback on the wa.search pane-filter path. Why it matters: distributed remote panes are persisted-only by design, and the user-facing recovery hint points operators to pane-scoped search that fails before querying storage. Proposed remediation: mirror WaGetTextTool metadata resolution in WaSearchTool. If live get_pane fails, look up the storage pane record, allow distributed: domains through policy metadata, and then run storage.search_with_results or hybrid_search_with_results with pane_id filtering. Add a regression that seeds a distributed remote pane plus output segment and verifies wa.search with pane succeeds without live WezTerm.
notes: Shipped at f9f13b7ed. WaSearchTool pane-filter path now mirrors WaGetTextTool's distributed-pane fallback: load_distributed_remote_pane first, get_pane second with optional fall-through when remote_pane is Some, domain resolved from whichever source is available (MCP_ERR_PANE_NOT_FOUND if neither), policy input populated from live pane_info or remote PaneRecord. Regression test search_tool_falls_back_to_storage_for_distributed_panes_ft_9ia4p seeds a distributed pane + segment and asserts wa.search returns ok=true with >=1 hit. Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean.

## Goal
Build a no-mock chaos and restore lab for mux disconnects, watcher restarts, storage contention, distributed stale sessions, and workflow compensation.

Each scenario has a reproducible command, an expected artifact, an assertion set, and a clear statement of what was real versus simulated.

title: [idea-wizard] Read-only external blocker radar for swarm substrates
description:
Idea-wizard output for a read-only substrate blocker radar: a FrankenTerm operator/robot surface that explains why the swarm is stalled before agents waste time retrying the same unavailable proof, CI, mail, or ownership path.

Phase 2 ideas considered before winnowing: external blocker radar; RCH queue/runbook state classifier; GitHub Actions queue/materialization tracker; Agent Mail availability/degraded-mode observer; Beads ownership and stale-risk summarizer; dirty-tree overlap detector; package artifact watcher; RCH local-fallback refusal explainer; current-head PR status bridge; cross-substrate blocker timeline; proof-lane unblockability score; safe next-action generator; per-agent work collision predictor; remote worker capability drift detector; queued-build cost estimator; CI runner starvation classifier; operator notification summary; TOON blocker packet; MCP read-only blocker resource; incident-bundle attachment adapter; proof-doctor evidence import hooks; resource-cockpit adapter; context-horizon advisor adapter; release-blocker scoreboard; no-repair policy guard; high-scale capacity caveat; redacted provenance citations; fixture-driven blocker cases; structured e2e watcher logs; operator runbook examples.

Top five selected ideas:
1. A read-only blocker radar contract, because agents currently need to manually reconcile Beads, RCH, GitHub Actions, Agent Mail, and dirty-tree state before knowing whether work is actually actionable.
2. Typed collectors for external substrate evidence, because RCH package queues, PR CI materialization, Agent Mail fallback, and Beads ownership each fail differently and should not collapse into one vague blocked state.
3. A robot/doctor/TOON surface, because both humans and agents need the same concise answer: what is blocked, what changed since the last check, what can safely proceed, and what must wait.
4. Fixture and conformance coverage, because this surface is only useful if it mechanically distinguishes queued, missing artifact, local fallback, stale owner, dirty overlap, and safe-to-work states.
5. Operator runbooks and adoption docs, because the output should reduce communication purgatory without becoming another prose-only ritual.

Next ten retained for later refinement: GitHub check-suite zero-job diagnostics, RCH worker capability drift snapshots, package artifact SHA watcher, PR current-head lineage display, Beads dependency-cycle gate, active-agent collision warnings, degraded Agent Mail retry budget, high-scale capacity evidence caveat, incident-bundle export adapter, and proof-doctor handoff cross-linking.

Goal: build a non-mutating blocker radar that combines read-only evidence from RCH, GitHub Actions, Agent Mail health/fallback, Beads dependency and ownership state, and local dirty-tree overlap into a deterministic operator contract.

Non-goals:
- Do not repair, restart, drain, or update Agent Mail, RCH, GitHub Actions, or any live service.
- Do not execute heavy Cargo locally; Rust proof uses RCH only.
- Do not replace proof-doctor, incident bundles, resource cockpit, context horizon, or terminal conformance. This surface answers whether those lanes are currently actionable and why.
- Do not claim that a proof lane passed from setup, sync, or queue chatter.
- Do not store raw pane text or sensitive transcript content.

Acceptance:
- The child beads define a v1 contract, typed evidence collectors, machine/operator surfaces, fixture/e2e conformance coverage, and docs/runbooks with explicit dependencies.
- Evidence states distinguish actionable, waiting_external, waiting_owner, stale_possible, dirty_overlap, rch_substrate_blocked, ci_queued, ci_zero_jobs, artifact_missing, mail_unavailable, and unknown.
- Outputs include provenance, timestamps, source freshness, next safe commands, and explicit forbidden actions.
- Tests cover all important blocker states with deterministic fixtures and structured logs.
- Heavy Rust proof is RCH-only with isolated target dirs.
close_reason: All blocker-radar contract, collector, surface, conformance, runbook, and Beads-support children are closed with retained RCH/static evidence.

title: [blocker-radar] Define v1 contract, states, and safety invariants
description:

title: [profiling] recorder hot path: flush + record_event run on every pane delta; zero benches
description:
## Hypothesis

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:124` (`flush()`) and
`recording.rs:290` (`record_event()`) are on the recorder hot
path. Plus the broader `recorder_storage.rs`, `recorder_query.rs`,
`recorder_audit.rs` cluster. The recorder runs on every captured
pane delta and every detection event for the lifetime of the
watch daemon.

`grep -lE "recorder|flush" benches/*.rs` returns zero hits. The
ingest-rate ceiling (events/sec the recorder can absorb without
falling behind) is unmeasured.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

The recorder is the persistence layer for replay/forensics. If
the watch daemon is observing 200 panes and each pane emits ~10
deltas/sec + ~1 detection/sec, the recorder must absorb 2200
events/sec sustained. Today:

- We don't know the per-event CPU cost.
- We don't know whether `flush()` batches or fsyncs per event.
- We don't know if serialization + the FTS lexical ingest run on
  the same thread (head-of-line blocking risk).
- We don't know the memory bound of in-flight events between
  `record_event` and `flush`.

The recorder is the one subsystem where I/O fingerprint
(per-event vs batched fsync) drives behavior; per the skill's
I/O playbook this needs `iostat -xm 1` + `biolatency` evidence,
not just CPU flames.

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/recorder_ingest.rs`
   with three workloads:
   - **steady-state ingest**: 10K events at 10 events/ms,
     measure end-to-end p95 + bytes/sec.
   - **burst absorption**: 1000 events in 10ms with no flushes,
     then forced flush — measure flush time + tail latency for
     the next ingest.
   - **scaling**: 1, 10, 50, 200 panes' worth of events
     interleaved.

2. **I/O attribution** — separate runs with the recorder backed by
   the `append_log` (current shipped backend per README) versus
   the in-memory test stub, to attribute CPU vs I/O.

3. **Off-CPU flame** during the burst-absorption test — does the
   recorder thread block on fsync? On the FTS ingest queue?

4. **Histograms** for `recorder.flush_ms`, `recorder.serialize_ms`,
   `recorder.fts_ingest_ms` per the skill's instrumentation
   contract.

## Hypothesis ledger entries

```
fsync-per-event-not-batch : pending — biolatency shows >fsync
                             per record_event ?
serialize-dominates-cpu   : pending — span_summary shows
                             serialize_ms > flush_ms ?
fts-ingest-blocks-flush   : pending — off-cpu flame shows recorder
                             thread waiting on FTS index lock ?
unbounded-in-flight-vec   : pending — heaptrack shows steady
                             growth on burst before flush ?
```

## Out of scope

- The frankensqlite backend (rollout/test-only per README).
- Replay-side performance (`replay_kernel.rs` covers some
  replay-time work).
- Tantivy indexing internals (`tantivy_search.rs` covers FTS
  query side).

## Acceptance criteria

- `benches/recorder_ingest.rs` exists with three workloads.
- Profile run produces `tests/artifacts/perf/recorder-ingest-<run-id>/`
  with fingerprint + hotspot table.
- I/O fingerprint (`iostat -xm 1` + biolatency) captured for the
  burst-absorption run.
- Hypothesis ledger entries marked `supports` / `rejects` with
  evidence paths.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:124, 290`
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_storage.rs` (the
  on-disk flushing surface)
- README §Replay & Forensics
- Skill: profiling-software-performance — IO-AND-TRADEOFFS.md

title: [mock-code-finder][incident] Wire swarm incident bundle sources to live collectors
description:
## Finding
The crash/incident bundle declares a swarm incident contract, but eight source rows are currently emitted as skipped/unavailable placeholders by the core collector. This is a real observability gap for operators diagnosing large-agent incidents.

## Evidence
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/crash.rs:1367 builds skipped contract sources with warning ids ending in `.not_wired`.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/crash.rs:1379 says each source is part of the swarm incident contract but is not wired into the core collector yet.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/crash.rs:1389 lists placeholder sources: robot_state, pane_text_summaries, tailer_capture_health, resource_pressure_cockpit, proof_rch_evidence, beads_coordination_snapshot, git_dirty_tree, and agent_mail.
- Existing Beads searches for crash incident collector not wired and incident bundle robot_state pane_text_summaries returned no tracker item.

## Scope
1. Add read-only collectors for each source that has an existing local substrate.
2. Preserve fail-closed unavailable rows for sources whose substrate is genuinely unavailable, but include exact reason codes, freshness, and privacy/redaction state.
3. Agent Mail handling must respect AGENTS.md: retry once, never repair/restart, then record unavailable evidence.
4. RCH proof evidence must distinguish worker/topology failure from source failure and must not treat sync chatter as proof.
5. Keep pane text summaries redacted and bounded; do not attach raw secrets or full scrollback.

## Tests and proof
- Unit tests for collector success, unavailable, stale, and redacted states.
- Golden JSONL incident bundle fixtures for healthy, Agent Mail unavailable, RCH no-worker, dirty tree, and missing pane text cases.
- E2E/read-only harness that builds a retained incident bundle without mutating panes or restarting services.
- Heavy Rust verification must run through RCH only; if RCH worker health remains unavailable, block with exact infrastructure evidence.

## Acceptance
- The default incident bundle no longer reports all eight swarm sources as not wired.
- Every skipped source has a current concrete reason, not a placeholder surface string.
- The bundle remains privacy-safe and read-only.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.

title: mcp_tools test helper hits asupersync vs fastmcp_rust::asupersync version conflict
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:4812\` cannot compile under
\`--features mcp\`:

\`\`\`
error[E0308]: mismatched types
    --> crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:4812:25
     |
4812 |         McpContext::new(asupersync::Cx::for_testing(), 1)
     |         --------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
     |                         expected \`fastmcp_rust::Cx\`,
     |                         found \`asupersync::Cx\`
     |
note: there are multiple different versions of crate \`asupersync\` in
      the dependency graph
\`\`\`

\`McpContext::new\` (defined in \`fastmcp_rust\`) expects
\`fastmcp_rust::Cx\` (i.e. fastmcp_rust's own vendored copy of
asupersync's Cx type), but the test helper passes the directly-imported
\`asupersync::Cx::for_testing()\` from the workspace's pinned
asupersync crate. With version drift between fastmcp_rust's vendored
asupersync (0.2.6 per the older fastmcp_rust pin) and the workspace
asupersync (0.2.9 per /Users/jemanuel/.cargo/registry path in the
error message), the two Cx types are nominally distinct even though
their fields are identical.

## Concrete failure path

1. Run \`cargo test --no-run --lib -p frankenterm-core --features mcp\`.
2. Compiler tries to build the \`#[cfg(feature = "mcp")]\` test module
   in mcp_tools.rs.
3. \`test_mcp_context()\` at line 4811-4813 fails to type-check because
   \`McpContext::new\` from fastmcp_rust expects \`fastmcp_rust::Cx\` but
   the call site passes \`asupersync::Cx\` from the workspace's
   asupersync.
4. **Entire mcp_tools test compilation blocked** — none of the ~50+
   tests in the mcp_tools test module can run, including any
   regression tests filed against mcp_tools handlers.

## Reproduction

\`\`\`
CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang \\
CXX=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang++ \\
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rv-p0-target \\
cargo test --no-run --lib -p frankenterm-core \\
  --no-default-features --features mcp 2>&1 | grep -B2 -A10 E0308
\`\`\`

## Severity rationale

- Blocks mcp_tools test verification entirely — any new mcp_tools test
  added under \`--features mcp\` cannot be verified locally.
- Real defect-finding work in the mcp surface (e.g. ft-tzwuw which
  found 3 missing timeout_secs guards) lands without test coverage
  because the test target won't compile.
- Not a runtime bug in production code — fastmcp_rust vs asupersync
  Cx structs are runtime-compatible; only the type system rejects
  them.

## Fix sketch

One of:
1. Bump the fastmcp_rust pin so its vendored asupersync matches the
   workspace asupersync 0.2.9 (preferred — single source of truth).
2. Replace the \`test_mcp_context\` helper to use
   \`fastmcp_rust::Cx::for_testing()\` (whatever the equivalent is in
   the fastmcp_rust API surface) instead of bridging through
   asupersync directly.
3. Add an explicit conversion (\`From<asupersync::Cx> for
   fastmcp_rust::Cx\`) in fastmcp_rust if the types are
   field-compatible.

(1) is the cleanest because it eliminates the duplicated dependency.
(2) is the smallest local change.

## Scope

Diagnostic only — fix likely lives in fastmcp_rust pin (Cargo.toml)
or the test helper. Not in scope for the agent that filed this bead
unless they have context on which fastmcp_rust SHA contains the
asupersync 0.2.9 alignment.

title: [mock-code-finder][tui] Add region-scoped InlineActive output gate
description:
## Finding
ADR 0010 planned a fourth output-gate state, InlineActive, for region-scoped inline TUI ownership, but the live gate is still three-state only: Inactive, Active, Suspended in crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui/output_gate.rs. ## Impact
Inline TUI mode preserves scrollback and scopes ownership to a render region. A full-terminal Active suppression model cannot distinguish sanctioned writes outside the inline region from corrupting writes inside the owned region. The current bridge therefore has no explicit contract for inline-region ownership once inline mode is wired into the live backend.

## Scope
1. Add a region-scoped gate phase or equivalent typed ownership model for inline TUI sessions.
2. Define the region metadata needed to classify writes inside vs outside the inline owned region.
3. Preserve current Active/Suspended command-handoff semantics for full-screen TUI sessions.
4. Add unit tests for allowed outside-region writes, forbidden inside-region writes, suspend/resume transitions, and crash/panic routing.
5. Add an integration or PTY/golden proof for inline scrollback integrity once RCH proof lanes are available.
6. Update ADR 0010 and any FTUI-08 references after the implementation lands.

## Proof
Heavy Rust proof must use RCH only. While ft-4tp7g blocks RCH admission, keep this blocked and use static/docs-only checks for tracker or ADR wording changes.

## Acceptance
- output_gate has an inline-region ownership representation instead of treating all inline sessions as full-terminal Active.

description:

title: [BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.2.wire] Wire bench_stats into Criterion harness + per-PR EBCI gate
description:
# Bench Stats Harness Integration

Foundation primitives + schema + doc landed in commit 64f797a18562cdb3476670e7d97ea62491fb665c (br-ft-syqcz.2). This bead carries the integration work that makes them live.

## Scope
1. Extend `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/bench_common.rs` to collect raw per-iteration sample buffers (Criterion exposes them via `measurement` callbacks) and emit a `bench_stats::Distribution` JSON block alongside the existing budget rows.
2. Add `scripts/check_bench_stats.sh` that:
   - reads `target/criterion/wa-bench-meta.jsonl`
   - fetches the baseline run from `origin/main`
   - calls a thin Rust binary wrapping `bench_stats::empirical_bernstein_ci` and `bench_stats::mann_whitney_u`
   - emits a verdict per bench
3. Wire the script into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as a non-blocking job initially (advisory mode), then graduate to blocking once we have a baseline distribution to compare against.

## Acceptance
- Every bench writes a v1 schema-conformant Distribution record per run.
- A regression in any of the 5 headline-claim benches (when ft-syqcz.3 lands them) fails CI within EBCI confidence.
- Verdict + p-value visible in PR checks.

## Why P1
Until this lands, the math we shipped is research, not signal. The bridge plan's "per-PR regression gate active with sequential-test correction" criterion of G3 sits on this.

title: MissionEvent phase can contradict kind after deserialize
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_events.rs found that MissionEvent phase is trusted after deserialization even though it is documented as derived from kind. MissionEvent stores both kind and phase (mission_events.rs:165-181), and MissionEvent::new derives phase from kind for builder-created events (mission_events.rs:191-216). But MissionEvent derives Deserialize, so JSON can set kind = assignment_emitted and phase = lifecycle with no validation. The query and summary APIs use the stored phase directly: events_by_phase (mission_events.rs:461-465), count_by_phase (mission_events.rs:492-500), and summary (mission_events.rs:502-512). Existing tests only prove builder-created/roundtripped events preserve their phase (mission_events.rs:904-940, 1213-1244; tests/proptest_mission_events.rs:453-477); no malformed JSON test rejects or normalizes a kind/phase mismatch. Why it matters: phase summaries and filters feed telemetry/operator views, so a malformed persisted event can hide dispatch or safety events under the wrong phase while retaining the original kind. Proposed remediation: remove phase from the serialized contract and compute it from kind, or add custom Deserialize validation that rejects mismatches. Also update count/filter paths to use event.kind.phase() and add regression tests for mismatched JSON.
notes: Shipped via cbd63d330 (4 tests covering phase normalization) on top of 2e2a162cf (impl). MissionEvent now uses a custom Deserialize that recomputes phase = kind.phase() on every load, healing any persisted JSON that has kind/phase mismatch. Bumps mission_event_log_normalization_count on heal. Tests deserialize_heals_kind_phase_mismatch_ft_a05f3, deserialize_does_not_normalize_consistent_event_ft_a05f3, count_by_phase_does_not_trust_malformed_phase_ft_a05f3, and proptest deserialize_always_normalizes_phase_to_kind_phase_ft_a05f3 all pin the contract — count_by_phase / events_by_phase APIs route through the healed phase regardless of stored value. Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean (207 warnings, 0 errors). My local diff matched HEAD when going to commit; closing as sibling-shipped.

title: ingest::trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes returns more than max_bytes when last char straddles the cap
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs:1405\` — \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes(text, max_bytes)\`
silently returns a string LARGER than \`max_bytes\` when the last
character would not fit. The function name and downstream callers
expect a hard \`max_bytes\` cap.

## Concrete failure path

Trace \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes("中", 1)\` (中 is 3 UTF-8 bytes):

1. text.len()=3, max_bytes=1. \`text.len() <= max_bytes\` (3 <= 1) is
   false; max_bytes != 0; continue.
2. start = 3.saturating_sub(1) = 2. Position 2 is in the middle of 中.
3. Snap-forward loop: is_char_boundary(2)=false → start=3.
   is_char_boundary(3)=true (text.len() is always a boundary). But the
   loop guard is \`start < text.len()\`, which is false at start=3.
   Exit with start=3.
4. \`start >= text.len()\` (3 >= 3) && max_bytes > 0 → enter the
   "fall back to last full character" branch (line 1419-1430).
5. The fallback walks backward from text.len()=3 to find the start of
   the last character (position 0 for 中), then \`saturating_sub(1)\`
   off-by-ones to position 0. (The off-by-one here is a separate issue
   from the contract violation but produces the same bytes.)
6. Returns \`text[0..]\` = "中" — **3 bytes when max_bytes was 1**.

Symmetric case: \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes("a中", 2)\` returns "中"
(3 bytes when 2 was requested).

## Caller impact

\`enforce_segment_size_for_persistence\` (line 1434) wraps this and
captures \`kept_bytes = truncated_content.len()\` in
\`SegmentSizeEnforcement\`. If \`kept_bytes > max_bytes\`, the
\`SegmentSizeEnforcement.kept_bytes\` field reports the violation
correctly — but the actual segment is still oversized, and:

* The truncation gap reason format string says \`"max_bytes={max}"\` —
  misleading because the kept bytes exceed it.
* Downstream consumers that allocate \`max_segment_bytes\`-sized
  buffers, set FTS5 column truncation, or enforce DB-level CHECK
  constraints on segment length get unexpectedly large input.
* Any future caller that does \`assert!(result.len() <= max_bytes)\` as
  a defensive check would fire on a config that's perfectly valid in
  the rest of the system.

## Severity rationale

- Function-contract violation: name says "to_max_bytes", behavior
  doesn't enforce that.
- Reachable when an operator configures \`max_segment_bytes\` smaller
  than the largest UTF-8 char (4 bytes) AND the segment starts with
  multi-byte content. Realistic only for misconfiguration or hostile
  input designed to exercise edge cases — but the bug exists.
- The inline comment at line 1419-1422 justifies "return the last full
  character rather than returning an empty string" — that's a
  *behavior choice*, but it violates the function's declared contract.
  Either the contract should change (function name + docs) or the
  behavior should respect the cap.

## Fix sketch

Two reasonable directions:

(A) **Strict contract** (preferred — matches function name):
  In the fallback branch, if the last character's byte length exceeds
  max_bytes, return \`String::new()\` rather than returning the
  oversize char. Callers that want "best-effort" can opt in via a
  separate API.

(B) **Document the exception**:
  Rename to \`trim_utf8_tail_with_min_one_char\` or update the doc to
  state that the result MAY exceed max_bytes when max_bytes <
  smallest character. Also update \`enforce_segment_size_for_persistence\`
  to assert / handle the over-cap case explicitly.

## Regression tests

Three tests pin the contract:
- \`trim_utf8_tail_returns_at_most_max_bytes_for_multibyte_char\` —
  \`trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes("中", 1)\` returns a string ≤ 1 byte.
- \`trim_utf8_tail_handles_2_byte_cap_with_3_byte_char\` — same for
  \`("a中", 2)\`.
- \`enforce_segment_size_respects_kept_bytes_le_max_bytes\` — the wrapper
  never produces a segment whose content exceeds max_segment_bytes.

## Scope

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs\` only. Existing tests at
lines 6051-6068 don't cover this case (max_bytes=4 with "café" tests
only the well-fitting path).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 4668d1bf: trim_utf8_tail_to_max_bytes now respects max_bytes as a hard ceiling. Removed the 'fall back to last full character' branch that returned 3-byte 中 when max_bytes=1 or 2. New behavior: when no suffix fits within max_bytes, return empty — downstream enforce_segment_size_for_persistence already wraps the oversize signal in a Gap segment with a truncation_reason, so an empty-content gap is the sound default. 3 regression tests pin: (1) trim('中', 1) and trim('中', 2) return ≤max_bytes; (2) trim('a中', 2) returns ≤2 bytes; (3) enforce_segment_size_for_persistence on '中' with max_segment_bytes=1 produces kept_bytes ≤ 1. All 164 ingest tests pass against /tmp/ft-rv-p0-target including the original 3 trim_utf8_tail tests (no regression on the in-bounds path).

title: mcp.rs: mcp_audit_decision_context serialization failure silently produces decision_context=None — same family as ft-luav8
description:
br-cc_2 ft-jydne audit roundup 2026-05-03 — pinning ft-FUTURE-4 as a real bead. The placeholder finding from the depth-3 mcp_helpers.rs audit (ft-jydne 'Findings filed' section) maps to a real silent-failure path in mcp.rs that warrants tracking.

## Site

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs:769`:

```rust
fn mcp_audit_decision_context(
    tool_name: &str,
    action_kind: &str,
    decision: &str,
    result: &str,
    error_code: Option<&str>,
    elapsed_ms: u64,
) -> Option<String> {
    // ... build DecisionContext ...
    serde_json::to_string(&context).ok()
}
```

## Defect

`serde_json::to_string(&context).ok()` swallows any `Err` from the serializer and returns `None`. The caller (`record_mcp_audit_sync` and `record_mcp_audit`) treats `None` as 'no decision context to record' and persists an audit row with `decision_context=NULL`.

The serializer error path is rare (DecisionContext is a serde-derive struct over plain owned fields), but not impossible — a future addition of a non-serializable field (raw pointer, file handle, etc.) would silently lose audit context with no telemetry. Same family as ft-luav8 (record_mcp_audit failure counter) and ft-2fjx0 (audit deadline-overflow counter): silent failure → observable counter.

## Production exposure

Today: low (DecisionContext fields are all owned + serializable). The bead exists as a defense-in-depth measure for future field additions. Operators reading audit rows can't distinguish 'no context to record' from 'context dropped due to serializer error' without a counter.

## Fix shape

Add `MCP_AUDIT_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_FAILURES: AtomicU64` + getter `mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_count()` matching the established pattern (ft-luav8, ft-2fjx0, ft-647cj, ft-153dy, ft-skec1).

Bump in the Err arm of the serializer call:

```rust
match serde_json::to_string(&context) {
    Ok(s) => Some(s),
    Err(_) => {
        record_mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure();
        tracing::warn!(
            tool = %tool_name,
            action_kind = %action_kind,
            \"DecisionContext serialization failed; audit row will land with decision_context=NULL\"
        );
        None
    }
}
```

## Tests

- Counter starts at 0.
- Successful serialization → counter unchanged, returns Some(json).
- Synthetic failure (inject a non-serializable field via a wrapper) → counter += 1, returns None.

## Class

P3 OBS hardening / silent-failure-counter family.

## Cross-references

- mcp.rs:769 (serializer call site)
- ft-jydne (audit roundup that surfaced this — closing concurrently)
- ft-luav8 / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 (sibling counters in the same defect family)
close_reason:
Fixed at ae02dd346. mcp_audit_decision_context now bumps a new MCP_AUDIT_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_FAILURES counter alongside a structured tracing::warn when serde_json::to_string fails. The audit row still lands with decision_context=NULL on serializer failure (the prior behavior is preserved for backward-compat) but operators now have telemetry to detect the loss.

## Standard observability shape

- static MCP_AUDIT_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_FAILURES: AtomicU64
- pub fn mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_count() -> u64 (matches ft-luav8 / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 naming)
- record_mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure() internal helper
- #[cfg(test)] reset_mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_count_for_test() for test isolation

## Tests

- mcp_audit_decision_context_happy_path_does_not_bump_counter: successful serialization keeps counter at 0 (production path).
- mcp_audit_decision_context_serde_failure_counter_round_trip: counter + getter + reset + bump round-trip through 0 → 1 → 2 → reset → 0.

The bead's third proposed test (synthetic serializer failure via a non-serializable wrapper field) is deferred — DecisionContext is exposed publicly so wrapping it for fault injection requires fixture infrastructure not yet wired. The counter contract is exercised directly via the round-trip test.

## Defect-family closure milestone

ft-luav8 / ft-0texd / ft-8cyii / ft-8na0z / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 / ft-a1wzs — NINE MCP/events-surface observability beads closed in 24 hours via this counter pattern. ft-a1wzs was filed earlier today during the ft-jydne audit roundup; closing it inline keeps the audit trail tight.

Verification: cargo check --lib --no-default-features --features mcp,subprocess-bridge clean (212 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

title: agent_profiles: AgentProfile pub fields; missing DoS caps on tags/env/metadata/shell/command; no schema-vs-struct round-trip test
description:
Audit of agent_profiles.rs (substrate for ft-df3cz robot profile family) found 3 issues:

1. (pub-field, AgentProfile) all 9 fields pub including created_at_ms/updated_at_ms (validate() enforces updated >= created, but post-validate mutation bypasses) + command (the field the integration executes when spawning panes) + env (passed to the spawned process). External code can mutate post-validate to inject malicious commands or break temporal invariants. Same recurring pub-field pattern (now in 19 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + read accessors + a builder/setter API that re-validates on each mutation.

2. (DoS — missing caps) AgentProfile.validate() caps name (64), role (64), tag value (64) — but missing:
   - tags Vec count cap (1M tags × 64 chars = ~64MB)
   - env HashMap count cap + per-key/value length cap (unbounded)
   - metadata HashMap count cap + per-key/value length cap
   - shell String length cap (this is executed!)
   - command Option<String> length cap (also executed)
   A malicious profile import (operator config file, mux session restore, etc.) could exhaust memory or sneak a giant command past validation. Fix: add MAX_TAGS, MAX_ENV_ENTRIES, MAX_METADATA_ENTRIES, ENV_KEY_MAX, ENV_VALUE_MAX, SHELL_MAX, COMMAND_MAX consts + corresponding ProfileValidationError variants + checks in validate().

3. (test gap) no round-trip test verifies AGENT_PROFILES_SCHEMA columns match AgentProfile fields. Schema drift risk: future field added to struct but forgotten in schema → migration succeeds but row writes fail at runtime. Fix: add a test that parses AGENT_PROFILES_SCHEMA and verifies column names match AgentProfile field names.
close_reason: DoS-cap + schema-pin closed. 8 new caps + 8 new ProfileValidationError variants + 5 regression tests cover the missing collection-size and value-length caps for tags/env/metadata/shell/command. schema_columns_match_agent_profile_struct_fields catches future schema drift. AgentProfile pub-field fix deferred (recurring pattern, larger refactor scope). +8 tests, 36 pass.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.4.cont] GPU pipeline-cache wgpu wiring — driver probe + shader hash + HMAC + ft cache clear CLI + ft doctor surface
description:
# Continuation: GPU pipeline-cache wgpu wiring

## Context
ft-2okh0.4 retired at substrate scope (commit ca24db84c):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/gpu_pipeline_cache.rs ships PipelineCacheVersion 5-component fingerprint + derive_cache_key FNV-1a-64 + cache_filename + CacheInvalidationCause 7-variant + should_invalidate decision tree + IntegrityCheck + CacheSizeBudget (64 MiB default) + CacheStats with hit_rate_pct + meets_cold_start_target predicate.
- 30 inline tests passing.

## What this bead carries

### wgpu pipeline_cache API wiring
- Startup path in frankenterm-gui's RenderState init:
  - Probe arch / wgpu_version / driver_version / shader_hash / ft_binary_hash → build PipelineCacheVersion
  - Read existing cache file at ~/.cache/ft/gpu-pipelines/<arch>-<wgpu-version>.bin
  - Verify HMAC; on Mismatch invalidate
  - Compare cached version with current via should_invalidate; if cause is non-None, drop cache
  - Pass valid cache bytes to wgpu::Device::create_pipeline_cache
  - On shutdown: serialize cache via wgpu pipeline_cache_data → write to disk with mode 0600

### Driver-version probing
- Vulkan: vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties → driver_version field
- Metal: MTLDevice.name + MTLDevice.registryID + macOS version (NSProcessInfo)
- D3D12: DXGI_ADAPTER_DESC.AdapterLuid + driver version from EnumAdapters

### Shader hash from build.rs
- New build.rs step: hash all .wgsl / .metal / .glsl files in crates/frankenterm-gui/src/shaders/
- Embed hash via env! at compile time
- substrate's PipelineCacheVersion.shader_hash field reads this

### HMAC computation
- Cargo dep: hmac + sha2
- Compute Hmac<Sha256>::new_from_slice(key).chain_update(payload).finalize()
- Key = SHA-256 of (binary_path + version) per the bead

### ~/.cache/ft/gpu-pipelines/ directory
- Mode 0700 on the directory
- Mode 0600 on cache files
- Atomic write via tempfile + rename

### ft cache clear gpu-pipelines CLI
- New CLI subcommand: ft cache clear gpu-pipelines
- Removes all files in ~/.cache/ft/gpu-pipelines/
- Sets operator_requested=true on next startup probe (optional — direct rm-rf works too)

### ft doctor surface
- Show CacheStats (hits / misses / per-cause invalidations / cold_start_ms)
- Show meets_cold_start_target verdict
- Show on-disk cache size vs CacheSizeBudget

### Tests at integration layer
- E2E: cold start → write cache; warm start → read cache; assert hit + last_cold_start_ms < 100
- E2E: ft binary upgrade → cache invalidates with BinaryUpgraded reason
- E2E: corrupted cache (manually flip a byte) → HMAC mismatch → invalidates
- Bench: cold start vs warm start time delta on M2 + Linux + Windows runners

### Cross-link ft-mpc9b.3.1
- Metal-direct backend has its own MTLBinaryArchive cache; this substrate generalises the pattern across all 3 wgpu backends. The Metal-direct integration bead can reuse PipelineCacheVersion + should_invalidate.

## Acceptance per the original bead
- wgpu pipeline_cache integration shipped
- Cache file at ~/.cache/ft/gpu-pipelines/<arch>-<wgpu-version>.bin with mode 0600
- HMAC tamper-detection working
- 6-cause invalidation enumerated + per-cause counter
- Cold start <100ms validated on Tier-1 hardware

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit ca24db84c (gpu_pipeline_cache.rs, 30 tests)
- Cross-link: ft-mpc9b.3.1 Metal-direct (MTLBinaryArchive specialisation)
- Cross-link: BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.6 (predictive font rasterization — also warms caches at startup)

This avoids dirty render/paint files and leaves disk HMAC/write/read and ft cache clear CLI for follow-up wiring. title: [ft-l1jgo.export] Migrate export_* storage.rs callsites to trait-typed pooled_backend
description:
## Scope (carved from ft-l1jgo, BLOCKED on ft-19rj3 substrate)

Migrate the **export_*** call sites in storage.rs from direct `rusqlite::Connection` (or `open_rusqlite_backend`) to the **trait-typed** `pooled_backend` helper landing in ft-19rj3.

## Methods in scope

export_gaps, export_reservations (coordinate with ft-v5wjv) (+ `with_cx` siblings)

## Migration target pattern (default — swap-ready)

```rust
Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {
    pooled_backend(db_path.as_str(), |backend: &dyn StorageBackend| {
        // existing closure body, byte-identical, but using
        // ONLY trait methods + module-level helpers
        // (count_table_where, query_row_typed, query_map_typed,
        //  execute_typed, list_user_tables, etc).
    })
})
```

## Acceptance (trait-only contract)
