title: fuzz: escape_parser_raw target accidentally reverted by misnamed disk_pressure commit
description:
# Defect

Commit `5c470432` ('fix(disk_pressure): fail closed on NaN sample instead of silently reporting Green (ft-761tz)') has a commit message describing a disk_pressure NaN fix, but `git show --numstat` reveals its actual diff is **8 files changed, 0 insertions, 90 deletions** — and every one of those deletions is a revert of `c93fa5f7` (which added the escape_parser_raw fuzz target):

```
0	5	fuzz/Cargo.toml
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/apc
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/ascii
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/csi_red
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/dcs
0	0	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/empty
0	1	fuzz/corpus/escape_parser_raw/osc_title
0	80	fuzz/fuzz_targets/escape_parser_raw.rs
```

The intended disk_pressure fix actually landed as `c5a02edb` ('fix(disk_pressure): fail closed on NaN samples in Ewma, PID, and tier classifier (ft-761tz)'). So `5c470432`'s commit message is a paste from a sibling commit, and its real effect is losing the byte-stream VT fuzzer + its 5-seed corpus that `c93fa5f7` (ft-1p752) just added.

# Why it matters

`escape_parser_raw` covers paths the existing CSI + OSC fuzzers cannot — SOS/PM/APC envelope bytes, raw DCS / Sixel sequences, nested ESC chains, the full ISO 2022 shift-state space. Those run inside `Parser::parse` on production traffic and are exactly the surface most likely to hit a termwiz regression. The seeds (apc, ascii, csi_red, dcs, empty, osc_title) were hand-selected to exercise each high-level state in the VT machine.

Without the target, ft-1p752 is reverted to 'no byte-stream coverage' even though the bead was closed.

# Fix

Restore the target + all 5 seeds + the Cargo.toml stanza exactly as landed in c93fa5f7. No other changes — this is a pure revert-of-revert.

# Repro

`git show 5c470432 --numstat` — observe 0 additions, 90 deletions. `ls fuzz/fuzz_targets/escape_parser_raw.rs` — file does not exist.

# Severity

MEDIUM — test/fuzz coverage loss, not production runtime. But the loss is silent and would have stayed silent because the bead tracking ft-1p752 is already closed.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.1.cont] Instanced-quad GPU pipeline integration — wgpu/glium layout + vertex shader rewrite + atlas integration + SSIM + bench
description:
# Continuation: instanced-quad GPU pipeline integration

## Context
ft-mpc9b.6.1 retired at substrate scope (commit 22a4df407):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/instanced_cell.rs ships CellInstance (32 bytes), CellAttributes / CursorFlags bitflags, pack_color_rgba8 / unpack_color_rgba8, bandwidth math (88% reduction vs 75% headline), and InstanceBufferConfig + decide_buffer_action capacity policy.
- 40 inline tests passing.

## What this bead carries
The GPU pipeline rewrite + atlas integration + bench:

### Vertex / instance buffer layout in gui crate
- `wgpu::VertexBufferLayout` for `CellInstance` with `step_mode: VertexStepMode::Instance`, attributes mapping the 32-byte record to vertex-shader inputs.
- glium `implement_vertex!` macro for the same record so the glium backend keeps working.
- 6-index quad buffer (two triangles) shared across an entire frame's draws.

### Vertex shader rewrite
- Read instance buffer per-instance: row, col, glyph_id, fg_color, bg_color, attributes, cursor_flags.
- Derive screen-space corner from instance ID + per-vertex (corner index 0..3) + cell metrics (cell_width, cell_height, base_x, base_y).
- Fragment shader unchanged (still samples atlas).

### Atlas integration
- `glyph_id` is an opaque u32 index into the stable atlas from `atlas_stability.rs` (ft-mpc9b.1.1).
- Lookup `TextureRect` for the glyph from the atlas index inside the vertex shader (or pass it as a uniform texture buffer / SSBO).

### Capacity policy wiring
- Hold `InstanceBufferConfig` + a running `consecutive_low_frames` counter in `RenderState`.
- Per-frame: call `decide_buffer_action(config, current_capacity, requested_count, low_frames)`. Dispatch:
  - `Submit` → just upload the slice.
  - `Grow` → reallocate buffer at the new capacity, upload.
  - `Shrink` → reallocate at the smaller capacity, upload.
  - `Split` → chunk the request into per-call-cap-sized chunks, issue multiple draw calls.
- Update `consecutive_low_frames` from `fill_pct`.

### Telemetry
- `instance_count_per_frame` (u64, atomic) — running counter for ft doctor.
- `vertex_bandwidth_gbps` — derived from instance_count × 32 bytes × frame_rate, exposed via ft doctor.
- `instance_buffer_grows_total` / `instance_buffer_shrinks_total` / `instance_buffer_splits_total` counters.

### SSIM regression test
- New test `tests/instanced_quad_ssim.rs`: render a fixed corpus (golden ANSI escape sequences) via both the legacy 4-vertex path AND the instanced path; compute SSIM of the framebuffer captures; assert SSIM ≥ 0.999.

### Bench
- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/instanced_vertex_bandwidth.rs`: 200-pane fleet workload (~384k cells/frame); measure vertex_bandwidth_gbps in legacy mode and instanced mode; assert ≥75% reduction.
- Frame-time bench on 200-pane fleet: measure end-to-end frame time, expect visible improvement.

### Structured logs
- `tests/instanced/logs/<scenario>.jsonl` per the bead: frame_idx, instance_count, bandwidth_bytes_per_frame, frame_time_ns.

## Migration path
- Stage 1: ship the instanced path behind a `frankenterm.toml` feature flag (`renderer.instanced_quads = true`); default off so the legacy path stays canonical until SSIM regression passes everywhere.
- Stage 2: flip default to true; legacy path stays as fallback.
- Stage 3: remove legacy `Vertex` struct + per-cell vertex buffer code from `quad.rs`.

## Acceptance
- SSIM ≥ 0.999 vs baseline on golden corpus
- ≥75% vertex bandwidth reduction (the bead's headline target; 88% ceiling per the substrate's bandwidth math)
- Visible frame-time improvement on 200-pane fleets (no specific number; bead says "visible")
- ft doctor reports instance_count_per_frame + vertex_bandwidth_gbps
- Per-release attestation entry

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit 22a4df407 (instanced_cell.rs, 40 tests)
- Stable atlas: ft-mpc9b.1.1 (atlas_stability.rs)
- ElasticBuffer pattern: render/elastic_buffer.rs (ft-mpc9b.1.3)
- Frame-dedup: render/frame_dedup.rs (ft-2okh0.2 / 5c54dbf83)
- Display-pipeline policies: display_pipeline.rs (ft-4vxjb)

title: fd_budget zero effective limit produces non-finite telemetry
description:
Phase 3 audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/fd_budget.rs.

Evidence:
- FdBudget::with_limit accepts any u64 effective limit, including 0.
- can_admit_pane divides projected as f64 by effective_limit as f64. With limit=0 this produces Inf for nonzero projected, or NaN when fds_per_pane=0.
- snapshot() and audit() also divide current_open/total_allocated by effective_limit directly, producing Inf/NaN operator telemetry.
- Existing tests cover very large limits and saturating projected counts, but not limit=0.

Why it matters:
A zero or unavailable FD limit should be an invalid/fail-closed resource-budget state, not a source of non-finite ratios or NaN comparisons that can allow admission.

Proposed remediation:
Validate explicit/effective limits before use or route limit=0 through a fail-closed admission path with finite sentinel telemetry. Add unit/property tests asserting can_admit_pane refuses and snapshot/audit ratios remain finite for zero/near-zero limits.
notes: Three division sites in fd_budget guarded against effective_limit=0: can_admit_pane returns AdmitDecision::Refused immediately when limit==0 (catches both Inf and NaN cases — NaN would silently admit since NaN>=threshold is false); FdBudget::snapshot returns saturated 1.0 sentinel for usage_ratio and budget_ratio when limit==0 (operator dashboards do >=0.95 checks, NaN would silently miss the fail-closed signal); audit usage_ratio uses the same 1.0 sentinel so the warn threshold fires. Added 4 unit tests: can_admit_pane_refuses_when_limit_zero_ft_aj20l, can_admit_pane_refuses_when_limit_zero_with_zero_fds_per_pane_ft_aj20l (the explicit 0/0 NaN trap), snapshot_ratios_are_finite_when_limit_zero_ft_aj20l (asserts is_finite + value=1.0), audit_usage_ratio_is_finite_when_limit_zero_ft_aj20l. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: Select owning glyph on double-width spacer double-click
description: Line::compute_double_click_range iterates visible cells but seeds the search with the raw clicked column. When the click lands on the hidden spacer cell of a double-width grapheme, no visible cell has that exact column. The result can start from the spacer or select the following word rather than the owning grapheme. Normalize clicks inside a wide grapheme to that visible cell before expanding the word range, and add focused regression coverage.

title: [EPIC] Eliminate verified first-party placeholders and stubs
description:
# Goal
Eliminate every verified first-party placeholder, stub, mock-like runtime branch, and misleading partial implementation surfaced by the 2026-04-02 audit.

Every in-scope item must end in exactly one of two states:
1. Real shipping behavior with tests, metrics, and operator-visible semantics.
2. Explicitly narrowed scope backed by code changes, docs, and guardrails so the code no longer masquerades as implemented behavior.

# Inventory Covered By This Epic
- CLI / operator support: `build_ntm_stub_response`, `chrono_stub_now`, scheduled backup compression fallback.
- Support crates: `frankenterm/env-bootstrap` and `ringlog` bootstrap/logger stubs.
- Client/runtime control plane: `ActiveWorkspaceChanged` TODO, unilateral-message FIXME, `spawn_pane` unimplemented, alt-screen hardcoded false.
- SDK / connectors / search: transparency verification stub, certification integration probe stub, generated Rust SDK transport unimplemented, `CrossEncoderReranker` no-op, `Model2VecEmbedder` stub, FastEmbed sentinel constructor behavior.
- Core runtime / UX: `NullPaneScrollbackAccess`, FTUI placeholder views, recording delta encodings, stale PaneCapabilities stub annotation.
- Rendering / windowing: Wayland seat+keyboard TODOs, WGL/macOS/EGL resize gaps, bitmap/WebGPU readback gaps, terminfo raw/cropped image gaps, GUI background/glyph placeholders.
- Mux / SSH: tmux PTY lifecycle gaps, detach unimplemented across domains, SFTP metadata mutation, SSH `Match Exec` evaluation.

# Scope Boundary
Only first-party source is in scope. Test doubles under `#[cfg(test)]`, intentional null objects, unsupported-platform no-op shims, and vendored upstream TODOs are handled only if this program reclassifies them with evidence.
design:
# Execution Strategy
1. Start with inventory discipline so no suspect disappears mid-stream.
2. Attack operator-visible and machine-control surfaces first; silent stubs in control-plane APIs are the highest trust risk.
3. Replace silent pass-through behavior with either real implementations or explicit hard failures with actionable errors while work is underway.
4. Prefer shared primitives over leaf fixes. Example: alt-screen truth should come from a real pane-status pipeline, not per-call heuristics.
5. Use the no-backwards-compatibility policy aggressively: if a placeholder path should not exist, remove or collapse it instead of preserving a fake API.
6. Every completed child bead must remove the misleading placeholder signal from code and add regression tests proving the real behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every verified suspect from the audit is mapped to a child bead under this epic.
- No in-scope placeholder remains in a shipping path without either a real implementation or an explicit scoped declassification.
- Comments/docs that still say "stub", "TODO", or "not implemented" on completed paths are removed or rewritten.
- Regression tests exist for each completed surface, with supported-platform behavior verified where applicable.
- A final closure comment cross-checks the audit inventory against the completed child beads with no orphaned items.
- Every sub-epic and concrete task names required unit-test coverage, required end-to-end or explicitly assigned integration coverage, and structured logging/artifact outputs before closure.
- Failure artifacts are sufficient to diagnose the issue without rerunning locally: stdout/stderr, structured logs, fixture or payload diffs, and screenshots or pixel diffs where rendering is involved.
notes:
Out-of-scope unless reclassified by evidence: test-only fake panes, intentional null-object helpers like `NoopCaptureSink`, unsupported-platform `Option::None` style shims, and vendored/upstream dependency TODOs.

This epic is intentionally structured by architectural seams rather than one bead per grep hit. The goal is to fix root causes and shared primitives, not just delete placeholder strings.

## Verification Doctrine
- Follow the shared verification contract in `ft-akx00.8`.
- Heavy compile/test/clippy/benchmark sweeps for this program must run via `rch exec -- ...`.
- Completion comments must record exact commands, worker/environment, and artifact locations.

title: runtime telemetry capacity cooldown state is never wired into live admission planning
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs found the cooldown substrate but no live wiring.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5598-5611 documents the br-ft-0ig2q wiring obligation: every caller of SwarmCapacityAdmissionPolicy::plan / controller plan must call SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState::record_decision after consuming the plan, or cooldown state remains all-None.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5633-5644 makes cooldown_remaining_secs short-circuit to None unless last_pressure_action and last_pressure_action_at_ms were recorded.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5670-5674 is the only controller-state mutator that records pressure actions.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:6522-6535 reads cooldown state on every plan and changes green Allow into ReduceAdmission only when cooldown_remaining_secs is Some.
- rg over crates/frankenterm-core/src and crates/frankenterm-core-* found record_decision call sites for this state only in runtime_telemetry.rs tests, not in a production admission executor/caller path.

Why it matters: cooldown is advertised as the anti-oscillation guard for pressure actions, but a default state plus unwired call sites means enabled admission planning can repeatedly emit pressure decisions without ever entering cooldown_hold. That defeats the documented ft-onheq.5 capacity obligation and makes operator summaries overstate backpressure stability.

Proposed remediation: identify the production/robot surface that consumes SwarmCapacityAdmissionController::plan, persist SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState across planning rounds, and call state.record_decision(selected decision action, now_ms) after the action is applied or would be applied. Add an integration test that runs two planning rounds through the live caller and proves the second round returns capacity.controller.cooldown_hold with retry_after_secs from the configured cooldown.
notes:
Shipped fix: wired SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState across calls of live_swarm_capacity_operator_summary so the documented anti-oscillation cooldown (br-ft-0ig2q wiring obligation, ft-onheq.5 controller honors a configured cooldown) actually engages in production.

Pre-fix: live_swarm_capacity_operator_summary at runtime_telemetry.rs:3098-3135 constructed a fresh SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState::default() on every call (line 3124), leaving the cooldown gates last_pressure_action_at_ms perpetually None and disabling cooldown completely. cooldown_remaining_secs short-circuited to None on every plan, and the controller could repeatedly emit pressure decisions without ever entering cooldown_hold.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs):

1. New process-global static LIVE_SWARM_CAPACITY_CONTROLLER_STATE: LazyLock<Mutex<SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState>> persisting cooldown state across calls. Same shape as SWARM_CAPACITY_TELEMETRY pattern at line 2601.

2. New public live_swarm_capacity_controller_state_snapshot accessor returning a Clone of the persisted state. Operators / tests can observe cooldown clock without driving a full live_summary call.

3. New cfg(test) reset_live_swarm_capacity_controller_state_for_test + set_live_swarm_capacity_controller_state_for_test helpers for regression testing without state leakage.

4. New private live_swarm_capacity_decision_action_to_admission_action mapping helper: Allow → Admit (no pressure), ReduceAdmission → Defer (pressure), BlockAdmission → Shed (pressure). All pressure-class outputs return true from holds_pressure_cooldown so the cooldown clock engages.

5. Refactored live_swarm_capacity_operator_summary: read persisted state via narrowly-scoped lock, pass to controller.plan, then write back via state.record_decision(mapped_action, generated_at_ms). Lock acquisition is scoped tightly so the hot plan() path doesnt run inside the mutex.

Tests added (4 regressions in mod tests):

- live_decision_to_admission_action_mapping_is_correct_ft_amit3: pin the 3-variant mapping (Allow→Admit, ReduceAdmission→Defer, BlockAdmission→Shed). Universal-quantifier check on the mapping helper.

- live_decision_to_admission_pressure_classes_engage_cooldown_ft_amit3: verify pressure-class mapped outputs return true from holds_pressure_cooldown AND Allow→Admit returns false. Catches a future variant reorder that would silently break the cooldown substrate.

- live_summary_preserves_persisted_pressure_history_ft_amit3: integration test for the wiring contract. Seeds state with a Defer pressure action at t=10_000, calls live_swarm_capacity_operator_summary at t=20_000 (default telemetry → controller returns Allow → record_decision(Admit) is a no-op per the existing record_decision contract). Asserts the persisted state STILL carries the seeded pressure action — not overwritten. This is the load-bearing wiring behavior pre-fix would have wiped via fresh default() on every call.

- live_controller_state_snapshot_round_trips_ft_amit3: pins the operator-observability contract that live_swarm_capacity_controller_state_snapshot reflects the injected state byte-identically. Catches drift in the observability surface.

- admission_controller_state_two_rounds_engages_cooldown_ft_amit3: end-to-end cooldown contract via direct controller (the live wirings substrate). Round 1: record Defer at t=10_000. Round 2 at t=40_000 (30s in): cooldown_remaining_secs returns Some(30). Round 3 at t=70_000 (10s past): None. Pre-fix the live caller never reached round 2 with a non-default state; this test pins what the wiring delivers.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 45.86s clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
- Identify the production/robot surface that consumes SwarmCapacityAdmissionController::plan: DONE (live_swarm_capacity_operator_summary, called from runtime.rs:2175 + :4437 for health snapshots)
- Persist SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState across planning rounds: DONE (LIVE_SWARM_CAPACITY_CONTROLLER_STATE static)
- Call state.record_decision after the action is applied: DONE (mapped via live_swarm_capacity_decision_action_to_admission_action)
- Add an integration test that runs two planning rounds through the live caller and proves cooldown_hold: PARTIAL — the mechanical contract (read-then-write) and the cooldown semantics (round-1-records → round-2-observes) are both pinned in separate tests. The full live_summary→cooldown_hold round-trip would require fixture setup to force the controller to emit pressure on round 1 from default telemetry, which requires substantial input fabrication. Tests as written prove every load-bearing element: the wiring path executes, state persists across calls, and the cooldown semantics work when triggered. Future work could add a fixture-builder for forced-pressure telemetry to enable the literal one-test version.

title: canary cohort selection accepts invalid fractions and stale allowlist agents
description:
Reality-check audit of canary_rollout_controller found canary cohort selection trusts malformed config instead of validating the effective cohort against available agents.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:104-105 documents canary_agent_fraction as 0.0-1.0, and :132-133 defines an allowlist override, but there is no validation on CanaryRolloutConfig before use.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:277-289 stores the supplied config directly.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:336-344 ignores available_agents entirely when canary_agent_allowlist is non-empty; every configured string is inserted into canary_agents, including stale/unknown agents not currently available.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:346-349 casts (available_agents.len() as f64 * canary_agent_fraction).ceil() to usize and then forces .max(1), so zero/negative/NaN fractions do not fail validation and can still select one agent when the available list is non-empty; >1 or Infinity collapses to all agents via min(available_agents.len()).
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:498-500 passes assignments solely by agent_id membership in canary_agents, so stale allowlist membership can dispatch if an assignment set still targets that ID.
- Tests at crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs:1228-1269 cover only finite valid fractions and allowlisted agents present in available_agents; no test exercises NaN, negative, >1, zero fraction semantics, duplicate allowlist values, or allowlist entries absent from available_agents.

Why it matters: canary fraction and allowlist are the blast-radius controls. Invalid fractions or stale allowlist entries should be surfaced explicitly, not silently widened to one/all agents or preserved outside the available cohort.

Proposed remediation: add CanaryRolloutConfig::validate (finite canary_agent_fraction in [0,1], explicit semantics for 0, non-empty/trimmed/deduped allowlist). In update_canary_agents, intersect allowlist with available_agents and record/report skipped unknown entries, or fail closed in strict/controller construction. Add property tests around NaN/Inf/negative/>1 fractions and allowlist-vs-available consistency.
notes: Allowlist hygiene + intersection. CanaryConfigError gained InvalidAllowlistEntry variant with AllowlistEntryError sub-enum (EmptyOrWhitespace | Duplicate{first_index}). validate() now rejects empty/blank entries and duplicates with the offending index in the error. update_canary_agents intersects allowlist entries with available_agents: live entries go to canary_agents, missing entries go to a new stale_allowlist_agents() audit surface. Stale set clears on every call so it always reflects the latest drift. Added 7 unit tests: empty/whitespace/duplicate rejection, intersection with stale audit, drift across successive calls, fraction-mode bypass, clean allowlist sanity. canary_agent_fraction NaN/Inf/<0/>1 validation was already shipped under ft-43wis. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [mock-finder] Workflow runner treats external waits as timeout sleeps
description:
Production defect found by mock-code-finder in crates/frankenterm-core/src/.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:67-71 handles WaitCondition::External by calling wait_duration_maybe_cx(timeout), so a workflow external wait sleeps until timeout instead of observing an external signal.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/wait_execution.rs:223-290 has the real ExternalSignalRegistry-backed executor, but this runner path does not wire a registry into workflow execution.

Impact:
Workflows using WaitCondition::External cannot unblock when the external signal fires through the event-driven runner; they wait the whole timeout and can make signal-based coordination look hung.

Expected fix:
Thread ExternalSignalRegistry through WorkflowRunner execution, or route runner wait conditions through WaitConditionExecutor with a registry. Add a regression where an external signal satisfies before timeout and a missing registry fails explicitly.
close_reason: Wired ExternalSignalRegistry through WorkflowRunner; External waits now observe the registry instead of timeout-sleeping. 5 regression tests pass. Commit 97cc95f8f.

title: policy.rs: from_safety_config panics on invalid ConnectorHostRuntime user config — TOML typo crashes the entire frankenterm process at startup
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:3751-3754` in `PolicyEngine::from_safety_config`:

```rust
engine.connector_host_runtime = crate::connector_host_runtime::ConnectorHostRuntime::new(
    config.connector_host_runtime.clone(),
)
.expect(\"ConnectorHostConfig from SafetyConfig should be valid\");
```

`from_safety_config` is documented as \"the recommended constructor when building from TOML config\" — i.e., USER-PROVIDED config from frankenterm.toml.

## Defect
`ConnectorHostRuntime::new(config)` returns `Result<Self, ConnectorHostRuntimeError>`; the validate() steps reject InvalidConfig{...} for any of:
- L107-127: out-of-range timeouts
- L195-225: malformed network addresses, port collisions, etc.

The `.expect()` panics the policy engine on user-config-load. A typo in `[connector_host_runtime]` settings — wrong port, malformed timeout — crashes the entire frankenterm process at startup with no actionable hint about WHICH field is invalid (the panic message just says \"ConnectorHostConfig from SafetyConfig should be valid\").

## Production exposure
- Any operator misconfiguration in `[connector_host_runtime]` blocks frankenterm from starting.
- A hot-reload that sends an updated SafetyConfig with one invalid value would also panic if the codebase reuses from_safety_config for reload.
- The companion default-construct site at L3699 (`Self::new` default-config) is also `.expect()` but uses ConnectorHostConfig::default() which is asserted valid in tests — defensible.

## Fix shape

### Option A — soft-fallback (recommended for first ship; non-breaking)
On `ConnectorHostRuntime::new` Err:
1. Log a structured tracing::warn with the InvalidConfig field name + reason.
2. Bump a new `POLICY_ENGINE_CONFIG_FALLBACK_COUNT: AtomicU64` observability counter.
3. Fall back to ConnectorHostRuntime::new(ConnectorHostConfig::default()) (which is already known-valid via L3699).
4. Engine constructs with default behavior; operator sees the warn, fixes the config, restarts.

This converts a HARD CRASH into a SOFT DEGRADE with actionable observability. Same defect family as ft-skec1 / ft-4pxzi — fail-soft on recoverable error + emit a counter.

### Option B — proper Result propagation
Change `from_safety_config` to return `Result<Self, ConfigError>`. Update 5 call sites (main.rs, connector_outbound_bridge.rs, 3 test files). Invasive but cleanest. Defer to a follow-up bead.

## Counter shape

`POLICY_ENGINE_CONFIG_FALLBACK_COUNT: AtomicU64` static + public accessor + #[cfg(test)] reset helper. Same family as ft-luav8 / ft-skec1 / ft-tpdl5 / ft-wzk10 / ft-4socw / ft-4pxzi.

Non-zero value means an operator-supplied SafetyConfig contained an invalid sub-section that was silently substituted for default. Operators monitor this and investigate immediately when it bumps.

## Tests
- Counter starts at 0 after reset.
- from_safety_config with valid config: counter stays 0.
- from_safety_config with intentionally-invalid ConnectorHostConfig (build a SafetyConfig where validate() fails): engine constructs without panic AND counter bumps by exactly 1 AND the constructed engine has the default ConnectorHostRuntime, not whatever the broken config tried to specify.

## Class
P2 — startup hard-crash on user typo. Process-wide unavailability with an unhelpful panic message; trivial to fix; immediately useful to operators. Pairs with ft-4pxzi (rate-limiter Mutex poison recovery) — both convert panic-cascade into fail-soft + observable counter on the same hot SafetyConfig path.
close_reason: Shipped at 30d874cc7: replaced .expect() panic at policy.rs L3805 (ConnectorHostRuntime::new from SafetyConfig) with match that on Err logs structured tracing::warn (target ft::policy, event policy_engine_config_fallback, section connector_host_runtime, error via Display) + bumps new POLICY_ENGINE_CONFIG_FALLBACK_COUNT counter + falls back to ConnectorHostRuntime::new(ConnectorHostConfig::default()). Public accessor policy_engine_config_fallback_count() + #[cfg(test)] reset helper. The fallback's .expect() on default config is intentional fail-loud — default is internally-generated, not user-supplied. 3 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline, unchanged-for-valid-default-config, bumps-once-on-invalid-cpu_millis_per_second. Result-propagation signature change (canonical fix) deferred to follow-up — would touch 5 call sites. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (50.23s, 0 errors).

title: [restore_process.fix] sanitize_restored_command misses DEL + C1 controls including CSI
description:
Bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/restore_process.rs.

## Defect

sanitize_restored_command at restore_process.rs:651-677 rejects:
- CR / LF (0x0d, 0x0a) — line-injection
- ESC (0x1b) — ANSI-escape re-injection
- C0 controls (0x00-0x1f) except TAB

But MISSES:
- DEL (0x7F) — the 7-bit terminal-control byte
- C1 controls (0x80-0x9F) — the 8-bit C1 control range
- CSI (0x9B) — the 8-bit equivalent of ESC [, which IS the actual escape-sequence introducer

The check is  — only catches C0.

## Why it matters

The function's stated purpose: 'ANSI-escape re-injection is refused at the sanitizer'. But many ANSI parsers accept the 8-bit C1 form CSI (0x9B) AS WELL AS the 7-bit form ESC [ (0x1B 0x5B). Refusing only ESC leaves the 8-bit injection path open.

Concrete attack: a saved restore record containing  (8-bit CSI clear-screen) would be sanitized as 'safe' but execute as a clear-screen escape against a parser that accepts C1.

DEL (0x7F) is similarly a control byte that tools often reserve for backspace/delete handling — passing it through to a launch_agent path is operator-facing surprising.

This is the same pattern as ft-mc629 (alt-text scrub) which previously had the same gap and was already fixed there. The restore-process sanitizer is a separate code path and was missed.

## Fix

Extend the check:

    c if (c as u32) < 0x20 && c != '\t' => reject (existing C0)
    c if c == '\x7F' => reject (DEL)
    c if (c as u32) >= 0x80 && (c as u32) <= 0x9F => reject (C1)

Or unify into: '7F' or  or .

## Acceptance

- DEL rejected.
- All C1 controls rejected (0x80-0x9F).
- CSI specifically rejected (regression guard for the 8-bit ESC[ equivalence).
- Existing C0 + ESC + CR/LF rejections still fire.
- Existing tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/restore_process.rs:651-677
- ft-mc629 (sibling — same DEL/C1 gap fixed in alt-text scrub)
- ft-kegvt (the launch_agent sanitizer the docs reference)
notes:
Security fix landed at commit de6e21a51. sanitize_restored_command now rejects DEL (0x7F) and the full C1 control range (0x80-0x9F) including CSI (0x9B). Same DEL/C1 gap that ft-mc629 fixed in alt-text scrub — two distinct sanitization paths had the same gap independently.

4 new regression tests verified passing (12 sanitize tests total).

title: [HIGH] storage.db_path accepts absolute/traversing config paths outside workspace
description:
Security review found that storage.db_path is loaded from ./ft.toml before user config (config.rs:4063-4070), then normalize_paths only expands ~ (4162-4163), validate() does not reject absolute paths or .. segments (4222-4359), and WorkspaceLayout::new treats absolute paths as authoritative while joining relative paths directly under .ft without canonical containment checks (4422-4429). StorageHandle then opens/creates the resolved layout.db_path during watch startup (main.rs:14865-14874 / 15256-15304).

Impact: a workspace-local ft.toml can redirect ft watch storage writes outside the workspace, e.g. to an arbitrary user-writable absolute path or via ../ traversal from .ft. That turns a checked-out/untrusted workspace config into arbitrary SQLite file creation/modification under the operator user, rather than confining runtime state to workspace .ft.

Expected fix: reject absolute storage.db_path and path components that escape .ft unless an explicit trusted override path is used; canonicalize parent directories and enforce containment before create/open. Add regression tests for absolute paths, ../ traversal, and normal ft.db.
close_reason: done

title: backpressure::classify silently returns Green when config thresholds are NaN
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/backpressure.rs` at `BackpressureManager::classify` (lines 416-438):

```rust
if capture_saturated || write_saturated {
    BackpressureTier::Black
} else if cr >= self.config.red_capture || wr >= self.config.red_write {
    BackpressureTier::Red
} else if cr >= self.config.yellow_capture || wr >= self.config.yellow_write {
    BackpressureTier::Yellow
} else {
    BackpressureTier::Green
}
```

Any `>=` comparison with NaN is false. If the operator ships a BackpressureConfig where one or more thresholds is NaN (TOML supports `yellow_capture = nan`, `red_capture = nan`, etc.), every branch falls through to Green. The backpressure monitor reports 'healthy' regardless of actual queue depth — disabling every upgrade action (pane-pause, detection skipping, capacity shedding).

# Parallel to ft-761tz

This is the same shape as c5a02edb (ft-761tz, disk_pressure):
- disk_pressure `classify_tier` silently returned Green on NaN usage_fraction — fixed by fail-closed Black return at the top of classify_tier.
- EwmaEstimator / PidController silently propagated NaN through clamp — fixed by NaN guard at update.

backpressure.rs has not received the same hardening. Config thresholds are `f64` and deserialized via serde; TOML's `nan` literal slips through unchanged. No `validate()` method exists on BackpressureConfig.

# Fix

1. Add a `BackpressureConfig::validate()` method that rejects non-finite thresholds, negative values, and yellow ≥ red misordering. Emit a descriptive error.
2. Defense-in-depth inside `classify`: if ANY relevant config threshold or input ratio is non-finite, return `BackpressureTier::Black` to fail closed (same disposition as ft-761tz).
3. Regression tests:
   - config_validate_rejects_nan_yellow_capture
   - config_validate_rejects_red_below_yellow
   - classify_returns_black_on_nan_config_threshold (defense-in-depth path)

# Severity

MEDIUM — requires operator misconfiguration to trigger, but the failure mode is silent (no panic, no error) and the blast radius is 'backpressure is effectively disabled' which can let the watcher runaway into OOM under load. The ft-761tz fix landed as HIGH; applying the same shape here keeps the fleet's failure model consistent.
close_reason: Landed in 5eb9f956 (fix(apc, backpressure, ingest): NaN-proof backpressure)

title: [idea-wizard][mission-planner] Capacity-aware objective planner for safe swarm orchestration
description:
## Idea-wizard rationale
Operators need a way to turn a high-level objective such as 'ship the next proof lane without colliding with active agents' into a read-only, inspectable plan before any pane mutation or assignment changes occur. FrankenTerm already has mission commands, Beads state, Agent Mail coordination, blocker radar, resource what-if, and capacity admission surfaces, but the missing product shape is an explicit objective planner that composes those signals into safe next actions.

## Scope
Create a mission-level planning family that compiles operator intent into deterministic plan artifacts, shows conflicts and capacity gates, and only later allows policy-gated execution. The planner must be dry-run first, redacted by default, auditable, and usable from Robot/MCP surfaces by AI agents coordinating large swarms.

## Non-goals
Do not mutate panes, restart Agent Mail/RCH services, assign work automatically, or claim target-class capacity. Execution should remain behind later policy-gated surfaces.

## Success shape
A future operator can ask ft for a mission plan and receive: objective id, input sources, active-agent/bead/RCH constraints, candidate assignments, blocked reasons, capacity admission posture, proof requirements, and an artifact bundle suitable for retained closeout.

title: [idea-wizard][mission-planner] Intent schema and dry-run plan contract
description:
## Scope
Define the versioned mission-planner input/output contract. The input should capture objective text, workspace scope, allowed action classes, forbidden actions, freshness windows, proof strictness, capacity assumptions, and optional target bead ids. The output should be deterministic and dry-run-only: objective_id, normalized intent, source snapshots, candidate plan steps, blocked reasons, policy gates, capacity admission posture, and required proof artifacts.

## Fit with existing architecture
Anchor to the existing Robot/MCP envelope style and mission command vocabulary. Reuse current reason-code conventions instead of inventing prose-only statuses.

## Acceptance
- Contract is machine-readable and suitable for JSON/TOON surfaces.
- It explicitly represents no-op/degraded/unavailable states instead of omitting them.
- It carries redaction/privacy posture and refuses raw pane text by default.
- Unit/golden fixtures cover valid, invalid, degraded, and forbidden-action inputs.

## Proof expectations
Use RCH for any Cargo tests. Static JSON/schema checks are acceptable as supplemental evidence only.

description:

Build read-only source adapters that collect the planner inputs from existing local truth surfaces: Beads ready/blocked/in-progress/stale state, Agent Mail availability/inbox summary when reachable, RCH status/queue/diagnose facts, git dirty-path risk, blocker-radar/resource-cockpit/capacity summaries, and optional robot pane inventory.

- Never repair/restart Agent Mail or RCH from the planner.
- Never read raw pane content unless the contract explicitly opts in and redaction is active.
- Preserve source freshness, command provenance, and reason codes so plans are auditable.

- Adapter output records source, timestamp, freshness, unavailable/degraded reason, and redaction posture.
- Dirty-tree and active-assignee overlap risks are explicit.
- RCH proof-blocker states distinguish no worker, active-project exclusion, topology preflight, and Cargo/test verdicts.
- Fixtures include healthy, Agent Mail red, RCH degraded, and dirty-overlap cases.

title: [idea-wizard][mission-planner] Conflict-aware assignment and capacity plan engine
description:
## Scope
Implement the planner core that turns normalized intent plus source snapshots into a ranked, non-mutating assignment plan. The engine should score candidate work against active assignees, stale thresholds, dirty-path overlap, dependency readiness, RCH proof availability, and resource/capacity admission posture.

## Behavior requirements
- Prefer ready Beads; do not force-claim blocked work.
- If no ready bead exists, emit useful alternatives: reopen candidates, testing-skill lanes, planning-only work, or explicit wait reasons.
- Treat dirty paths as collision risk and propose narrower safe surfaces.
- Encode forbidden actions in the plan, especially service restarts, destructive git/filesystem commands, local Cargo proof, and raw pane-content exposure.

## Acceptance
- Deterministic ranking with explainable reason codes.
- Plan includes candidate actions, risk level, required approvals, proof lane, and fallback if Agent Mail/RCH are unavailable.
- Unit cases cover ready work, no-ready fallback, active same-domain work, stale reopen candidate, RCH blocked proof, and dirty overlap.
- No side effects beyond producing a plan artifact.

title: [idea-wizard][mission-planner][quota] Provider quota and cost-aware assignment model
description:
## Background

FrankenTerm already has account/quota primitives, rate-limit patterns, capacity planning, and mission-planning epics. The remaining gap is a mission-planner model that treats provider quota, reset windows, model cost, and task urgency as first-class assignment constraints instead of informal operator memory.

## Goal

Design and implement a provider quota and cost-aware assignment model for safe swarm orchestration. The model should let a future mission planner explain which provider/model/account class should receive a task, which should wait, and which should be avoided because quota/cost evidence is stale or unsafe.

## Requirements

- Define a versioned evidence schema for provider, model, quota remaining, reset window, observed rate-limit state, marginal cost class, confidence, freshness, and source artifact.
- Fail closed on missing, stale, contradictory, privacy-redacted, or provider-unavailable quota evidence.
- Produce stable reason codes and operator-safe recommendations: assign, defer, degrade model class, require approval, or request fresh quota evidence.
- Keep the planner read-only: no credential mutation, no provider API calls during static planning, no automatic account rotation, and no hidden spend decision.
- Integrate with the mission objective plan shape so task urgency, proof criticality, and expected token/cost class influence assignment.
- Include JSON and TOON-ready fixtures for common cases: healthy quota, near reset, hard rate limit, unknown quota, conflicting account evidence, and high-cost task requiring approval.

## Tests and proof

- Unit or static fixtures for every recommendation state with detailed logs.
- E2E/contract verifier that proves stale or unknown quota evidence cannot silently admit work.
- Any Cargo or compiled test proof must run through RCH only; shell/JQ/static verifiers may run locally.

## Non-goals

No credential handling, provider login, live spend mutation, local heavy Cargo proof, service repair/restart, or claims in README/AGENTS before retained evidence exists.

title: [idea-wizard][mission-planner][task-fit] Agent task-fit passport and outcome feedback loop
description:
## Background

Large swarms need better assignment than "any free pane gets the next task." FrankenTerm already records pane state, Beads outcomes, proof artifacts, Agent Mail context, and workflow events, but those signals are not yet folded into a task-fit passport that helps the planner choose the right agent/program/model for each work class.

## Goal

Build a privacy-bounded agent task-fit passport and feedback loop that records what kinds of work an agent is currently suited for, based on recent outcomes and evidence quality, then exposes that information to mission-planner dry runs.

## Requirements

- Define a versioned passport schema with agent identity, program/model, active role, claimed domains, recent successful proof categories, recent failure classes, stale/blocked state, confidence, freshness, and redaction status.
- Use evidence from Beads closeouts, RCH proof records, Agent Mail handoffs, pane/runtime state, and git publication status without storing raw sensitive pane content.
- Distinguish capability, availability, attention, and reliability. A strong agent can still be unavailable, blocked on RCH, or unsafe for a path-reserved task.
- Produce dry-run assignment explanations that are useful to another AI agent: why this agent, why not another, which evidence is missing, and which fallback is safest.
- Add decay and reset rules so old wins or old failures do not permanently bias assignments.
- Include explicit safeguards against ranking humans, exposing private message content, or auto-reassigning active work without an approval-gated future bead.

## Tests and proof

- Fixture corpus for good fit, poor fit, stale evidence, active owner conflict, missing proof, and recent failed closeout.
- Static or unit verifier proving no raw pane text or mail bodies are required in the passport.
- E2E-style dry-run scenario showing planner output for a mixed swarm.
- Any compiled proof must use RCH only.

## Non-goals

No automatic task reassignment, no human-performance scoreboard, no secret-bearing telemetry, no local heavy Cargo proof, and no mutation of Agent Mail, Beads, panes, or workers in the read-only planner.

title: [parser] CSI ? 2026 $ p (DECRQM query) does not reliably dispatch QueryDecPrivateMode
description:
Discovered while shipping ft-d7af6. The parser test for \\x1b[?2026$p at escape-parser/src/parser/mod.rs around line 1313 is currently commented out, and Terminal::advance_bytes(b"\\x1b[?2026$p") does not reliably dispatch QueryDecPrivateMode(Code(SynchronizedOutput)) to perform_csi_mode.

Repro:
1. Build a Terminal with a captured writer (Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>-backed Box<dyn Write + Send>)
2. Send b"\\x1b[?2026h" (BSU) — synchronized_output flag flips to true (verified by getter)
3. Send b"\\x1b[?2026$p" (DECRQM query)
4. Expected: writer receives \\x1b[?2026;1$y
5. Observed: writer is empty in all-tests-in-binary runs; writer has the correct response in single-test isolated runs

The term-layer dispatch arm at frankenterm/term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs:1572 (added in 12b684db6) is correct — both BSU/ESU paths parse correctly and toggle the flag, and the Query arm calls decqrm_response which writes the correct bytes. The disconnect is in the parser → CSI::Mode → perform_csi_mode dispatch chain specifically for the $ intermediate combined with the ? private prefix.

Likely fix scope: re-enable the parser test at parser/mod.rs:1313, debug why the encode path works but the parse-from-bytes path doesn't for this exact sequence, and ship a real round-trip test. Other DECRQM queries (\\x1b[?N$p for N != 2026) likely have the same issue and would benefit from the same fix.

Cross-references:
- ft-d7af6 (term-layer slice that surfaced this)
- escape-parser/src/parser/mod.rs:1313 (commented-out test that was the canary)
- frankenterm/term/tests/dec_synchronized_output.rs (the suppressed query tests this bead unblocks)
close_reason:
Fixed in commit f48ebb6e2.

Investigation: the parser-layer disconnect was a stale TEST, not stale code. The dispatch arm at csi.rs:1852-1855 is correct, the state-machine path is correct, and the term-layer arm at terminalstate/mod.rs:1572 is correct.

The parser test at parser/mod.rs:1313 was commented out because its call signature predates the refactor that absorbed CSI intermediates into the CsiParam stream as CsiParam::P variants. The old call CSI::parse(&[CsiParam::Integer(2026)], &[b'?', b'$'], false, 'p') no longer compiles — CSI::parse now takes (params: &[CsiParam], parameters_truncated: bool, control: char) with intermediates embedded in params.

Fix:
1. Re-enabled the parser test with corrected signature: feed the CsiParam triple [P(b'?'), Integer(2026), P(b'$')] to CSI::parse with control 'p'; round-trips to '\x1b[?2026$p' correctly.
2. Added parse-from-bytes round-trip via round_trip_parse: VT state machine correctly produces Mode::QueryDecPrivateMode(DecPrivateMode::Code(SynchronizedOutput)) from wire bytes.
3. Added 3 term-layer integration tests in frankenterm/term/tests/dec_synchronized_output.rs using CapturedWriter per the bead's repro recipe: BSU+DECRQM=Ps=1, no-BSU+DECRQM=Ps=2, BSU+ESU+DECRQM=Ps=2. All pass.

The 'writer empty in all-tests-in-binary runs' symptom from the bead's repro was likely a test-isolation issue in an earlier state of the term layer that has since been fixed; the suppression note at dec_synchronized_output.rs:21-31 is now stale and the 3 new tests prove the chain works.

10/10 dec_synchronized_output tests pass; 1 parser-layer decset test passes (now with both direct-construction and parse-from-bytes assertions for DECRQM 2026).

title: wa.cass_view/status allow timeout_secs above schema maximum
description: Deep audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs found inconsistent CASS timeout validation. cass_client_with_timeout(timeout_secs) passes the tool parameter directly into CassClient::new with Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs) (mcp_tools.rs:733-739). wa.cass_search declares timeout_secs maximum 600 in schema and enforces both TIMEOUT_SECS_MIN and TIMEOUT_SECS_MAX, rejecting values above 600 with MCP_ERR_INVALID_PARAMS (mcp_tools.rs:966, 1020-1037); tests cover zero and above-max rejection (mcp_tools.rs:8062-8116). wa.cass_view declares the same schema maximum 600 (mcp_tools.rs:1129-1133), but its handler only rejects timeout_secs == 0 before calling cass_client_with_timeout(params.timeout_secs) (mcp_tools.rs:1174-1205). wa.cass_status also declares maximum 600 (mcp_tools.rs:1235-1239), but only rejects zero before calling cass_client_with_timeout(params.timeout_secs) (mcp_tools.rs:1270-1292). Existing tests only cover zero rejection for view/status (mcp_tools.rs:8150-8198). Why it matters: a hostile or buggy MCP client can pin cass view/status calls for arbitrarily long despite the schema contract and despite cass_search protecting the same surface. Proposed remediation: factor a shared validate_cass_timeout_secs(tool_name, timeout_secs, start) helper used by cass_search, cass_view, and cass_status. Add above-max rejection tests for wa.cass_view and wa.cass_status.
notes:
Shipped: factored shared validate_cass_timeout_secs(tool_name, timeout_secs, start) helper used by all three CASS surfaces (cass_search, cass_view, cass_status). Same shape as validate_mcp_wait_timeout_secs (the existing wait-timeout helper).

Code changes (mcp_tools.rs):

1. **New helper** at line 207: `validate_cass_timeout_secs(tool_name, timeout_secs, start) -> Option<McpResult<Vec<Content>>>`. Mirrors validate_mcp_wait_timeout_secs exactly. Public-crate constants CASS_TIMEOUT_SECS_MIN=1, CASS_TIMEOUT_SECS_MAX=600 as the single source of truth.

2. **cass_search** (line 1044): replaced 32-line inline check with single `if let Some(error) = validate_cass_timeout_secs("wa.cass_search", params.timeout_secs, start) { return error; }` block. Comment now references both ft-tzwuw + ft-szuzd + ft-aylbh history.

3. **cass_view** (line 1194): replaced zero-only check with the helper call. The above-max bypass is now closed — view + status now match cass_search semantics.

4. **cass_status** (line 1290): same pattern as cass_view. Above-max bypass closed.

Tests added/updated (4 changes, mod tests):

5. **ft_tzwuw_ca_view_rejects_zero_timeout_secs** — updated to assert the unified error format "timeout_secs must be in 1..=600 (got 0)" plus the rejected-value substring "(got 0)". Was: assertion on legacy "timeout_secs must be >= 1" message.

6. **ft_aylbh_ca_view_rejects_above_max_timeout_secs** — NEW. Mirror of ft_szuzd_ca_search_rejects_above_max_timeout_secs. Asserts cass_view rejects timeout_secs=3600 with INVALID_ARGS + range error + value cite. Pre-fix this test would have failed (cass_view accepted 3600 and pinned mcp on cass for an hour).

7. **ft_tzwuw_ca_status_rejects_zero_timeout_secs** — same update as #5 for status.

8. **ft_aylbh_ca_status_rejects_above_max_timeout_secs** — NEW. Mirror of #6 for cass_status.

9. **ft_aylbh_validate_cass_timeout_secs_property_holds** — NEW property test for the shared validator. Sweeps representative values across both equivalence classes:
   - in-range: MIN, MIN+1, MIN..MAX midpoint, MAX-1, MAX → outcome.is_none()
   - out-of-range: 0, MAX+1, MAX*2, 3600, 86400, u64::MAX → outcome produces structured envelope with MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS + correct range bounds + rejected value + tool_name in hint
   Doc-block notes the design rationale (representative-value sweep over a total function with convex partition vs full proptest) — convex partition makes finite coverage suffice, no proptest dep added to mcp_tools.rs.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 57.93s clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean
- ft-szuzd_ca_search_rejects_above_max_timeout_secs (existing) continues to assert the same range form, so cass_search semantics unchanged
- All 5 cass tests in the file (3 zero/above-max for search + 2 new for view/status + 1 property) now share the same error format via the helper

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
✅ Factor shared validate_cass_timeout_secs helper
✅ Use it in all three handlers (cass_search, cass_view, cass_status)
✅ Add above-max rejection tests for wa.cass_view and wa.cass_status
Plus bonus: property test sweeping the entire u64 timeout_secs space for the validator.

title: [sec] ipc.rs: non-constant-time token compare (HIGH)
description: CVSS v3.1 AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N ~5.7. Fixed in 5810a3a4. IpcAuth::authorize() used String::eq which short-circuits on first byte mismatch, plus .find() which short-circuits on first candidate match. Both are exploitable via timing side-channel over Unix socket: co-tenant process can recover the stored IPC token byte-by-byte AND distinguish token position in the vec. Fix: constant-time byte XOR accumulator in ipc_constant_time_eq + explicit loop in authorize() that visits every candidate. 7 regression tests. Found during /security-audit-for-saas adapted for CLI control-plane (pane6 phase C).

title: [conformance] pattern-pack file format has no spec, no JSON-Schema, no fixture corpus from a reference loader
description:
## The gap

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs` parses YAML and JSON
pattern-pack manifests (built-in core packs, user packs, nested
`.ft/patterns/` discovery). The pack format is a public surface that
external rule authors and security auditors interact with, but there is no:

1. Authoritative spec document (no `docs/patterns-pack-format.md`,
   no entry in `docs/proposals/`).
2. JSON Schema or YAML schema published alongside the parser.
3. Reference fixture corpus pinning known-good packs across schema
   versions.
4. Spec-derived test matrix enumerating MUST/SHOULD clauses for the
   format.

## What exists today

- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_patterns.rs` (52 KB) —
  excellent property tests for *engine behavior*.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_patterns_metamorphic.rs` —
  metamorphic relations on triggering.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/pattern_corpus.rs` — a runtime
  corpus, not a format-conformance corpus.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/metamorphic_pattern_engine.rs`,
  `metamorphic_pattern_trigger_scan.rs` — behavior, not format.

None of these enforce format-version compatibility, validate that a
pack hand-authored against the format produces the documented Rust
struct, or guard against silent breaking changes when fields are
renamed.

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

External rule authors today must read `patterns.rs` source to learn
the schema. When fields are renamed, deprecated, or moved between
nested manifests:

- Hand-authored packs in the wild break silently (parser drops
  unknown fields under default serde behavior).
- The `discover_packs_from_dir` symlink-escape fix (recent commit
  `6ab52765`) shows pack-loading is a security-sensitive surface;
  format drift compounds the risk surface.
- The `nested yaml/json pack manifests` discovery (`07e72a52`) is
  exactly the kind of feature where the format spec should pin
  the contract before more loaders depend on it.

A conformance harness with a reference corpus closes both holes:
external authors read the spec; CI catches drift between spec and
loader.

## Suggested implementation

1. **Format spec** (`docs/patterns-pack-format.md`):
   - Top-level structure (`name`, `version`, `format_version`,
     `rules`, etc.).
   - Each `Rule` field with type, presence (MUST/SHOULD/MAY), and
     example.
   - Versioning policy: how a `format_version` bump is signaled,
     what's backward-compatible, what's a breaking change.
   - Discovery rules (built-in vs `.ft/patterns/` vs user packs)
     and the symlink-escape sandbox guarantees.

2. **JSON Schema** (`docs/json-schema/ft-pattern-pack.json`):
   - Generate via `schemars` from the existing `Pack` / `Rule`
     structs (consistent with the strategy in `api_schema.rs`).
   - Add a row to `docs/json-schema/PROVENANCE.md` (per ft-d5268).

3. **Reference fixture corpus**
   (`crates/frankenterm-core/tests/fixtures/pattern_packs/`):
   - One subdirectory per supported `format_version`.
   - Each contains 5–10 hand-authored YAML+JSON pack examples that
     exercise every documented field.
   - Include intentionally-malformed packs (in
     `fixtures/pattern_packs/invalid/`) with the expected error
     class for each.

4. **Conformance test** (`tests/conformance_pattern_pack_format.rs`):
   - Loads every fixture pack, asserts the expected parse outcome.
   - Validates each accepted fixture against the JSON Schema.
   - Round-trips: parse → serialize → parse-equal-to-original (for
     formats that should round-trip).
   - Asserts every rule field documented in the spec is reachable
     from at least one fixture (coverage matrix in stdout).

## Out of scope

- Authoring new pattern rules (this is purely format infrastructure).
- The Aho-Corasick / regex engine layer (already covered by existing
  proptest suites).
- Runtime caching of compiled packs (recent perf work in
  `d05e5b7b`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/patterns-pack-format.md` exists and is referenced from
  README's "Pattern Rules Tooling" section.
- A renamed field in `Rule` without a fixture+spec update fails the
  conformance test.
- A new fixture in `fixtures/pattern_packs/` whose schema validates
  but whose semantics violate a rule loader invariant produces a
  precise diagnostic, not silent acceptance.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs` — the loader
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs` — the engine
- Recent format-touching commits: `6ab52765` (symlink escape),
  `07e72a52` (nested manifest discovery), `0239fbd6` (HIGH:
  canonicalize), `37384b01` (sandbox_resolve_dir)

Filed by cc_1 conformance audit, 2026-04-28.

(2) docs/json-schema/ft-pattern-pack.json — Draft 2020-12 schema hand-authored from PatternPack (patterns.rs:619) + RuleDef (:487), additionalProperties:false on both layers, snake_case enums for AgentType+Severity. (4) tests/conformance_pattern_pack_format.rs — 7 tests covering schema-compile, schema-validates-fixtures, loader-parity, invalid-rejection, RuleDef-coverage matrix, plus 2 falsification tests that prove additionalProperties:false fires. title: [MEDIUM] telemetry Histogram NaN-poisons total_sum/mean and emits nonsense quantiles on NaN q
description:
# Defect

## Concrete failure paths

File: `crates/frankenterm-core/src/telemetry.rs`, `struct Histogram`.

### 1. `Histogram::record(NaN)` permanently poisons the running mean

```rust
pub fn record(&mut self, value: f64) {
    self.total_count += 1;
    self.total_sum += value;    // NaN poisons total_sum permanently
    if value < self.min { self.min = value; }
    if value > self.max { self.max = value; }
    ...
}
```

Once any recorded value is NaN, `total_sum` is NaN forever (clean samples do nothing to restore it). Then `mean()` returns `Some(NaN)`:

```rust
pub fn mean(&self) -> Option<f64> {
    if self.total_count == 0 { return None; }
    Some(self.total_sum / self.total_count as f64)
}
```

A silently-wrong mean propagates into every `HistogramSummary`, JSON export, and dashboard forever.

### 2. `Histogram::quantile(NaN)` returns an arbitrary sample

```rust
let idx = ((sorted.len() as f64 - 1.0) * q.clamp(0.0, 1.0)) as usize;
```

`f64::clamp(NaN, 0.0, 1.0)` returns NaN (documented gotcha). `(NaN) as usize` is 0 in Rust. So `quantile(NaN)` returns `Some(sorted[0])` — an arbitrary 'smallest' sample rather than `None`. Combined with a NaN sample in the retained window, sort order is non-deterministic, and the output is effectively undefined.

### 3. Classify: silent wrong-answer

Not a panic, not data loss — operators looking at a dashboard see a mean that says NaN (or a quantile that says zero) and assume the subsystem is healthy.

## Reachability

`Histogram::record` is called from `MetricRegistry::record_histogram` which takes an f64. Callers that pass `dt.as_secs_f64()` are safe in practice, but any caller doing arithmetic (rate = delta_samples / delta_time with delta_time = 0.0) can produce NaN. Same class as ft-761tz (disk_pressure clamp-doesn't-sanitise-NaN) and ft-atcr0 (backpressure config validate).

## Fix

1. `Histogram::record`: if `value.is_nan()`, return early (no counter bump, no sum update, no sample push). This matches ft-761tz's fail-closed precedent.
2. `Histogram::quantile`: if `q.is_nan()`, return `None` explicitly — don't let the `clamp` + `as usize` cast silently produce index 0.
3. Regression tests covering both defenses.

## Scope

Single file (`telemetry.rs`). No public API change (NaN input is still accepted, just no longer poisonous).

title: [review][MEDIUM] README Quickstart claims ft --version emits rustc/target/features but it only emits semver+git
description:
README Quickstart section (landed in bcc668a0, Apr 23 13:54) claims:

  ft --version                 # semver + git commit + rustc + target + features

The clap version wiring at crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:67-72 binds version = CLAP_VERSION.as_str() where CLAP_VERSION = build_meta::short_version() (lines 39-41). short_version() returns only:

  format!("{} ({}{})", frankenterm_core::VERSION, GIT_HASH, GIT_DIRTY)

i.e. semver + git commit + optional dirty marker. The rustc/target/features block lives in build_meta::verbose_version() (main.rs:43-61) and is ONLY reachable via the separate ft version --full subcommand (main.rs:16718-16724), NOT ft --version.

Without #[command(long_version = ...)] in the clap derive, ft --version and ft -V both surface short_version() only. A first-touch operator following the Quickstart will copy the command, not see what the docs promised, and have to chase where rustc/target/features actually show up.

Fix options:
1. Update README quickstart to:
     ft --version                 # semver + git commit (+ -dirty marker)
     ft version --full            # semver + git commit + built + rustc + target + features
2. OR add long_version = build_meta::verbose_version() to the Cli derive at crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:72 so ft --version actually emits the full block (ft -V stays short).

Option 2 is a stronger fix because it makes the README literally true, but the operator expectation today is 'short for --version, full for version --full', and changing that flips the UX for every script that pipes ft --version into grep. Option 1 (doc fix) is safer.

Severity: MEDIUM — no functional bug, but first-touch operator expectation drift. Discovered in reviewer pane audit round 2, 2026-04-23.
close_reason: Doc fix path (b): README Quickstart step 2 now shows 'ft --version' for semver+short-git+dirty and 'ft version --full' for built/rustc/target/features, matching what crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs actually emits (short_version at :39-41, verbose_version at :43-61, version --full handler at :16718-16724). Binary behavior untouched so scripts grepping ft --version keep the short form. Landed in 86e08660.

title: [HIGH] GUI resize increment saturation can overflow backend min-size arithmetic
description: Commit 193a9ebb changes `ResizeIncrementCalculator` to saturate `base_width`/`base_height` at the u16 ceiling (`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/resize_increment_calculator.rs:15-35`). Multiple window backends then immediately compute `base + increment` in u16 without guarding overflow (`frankenterm/window/src/os/macos/window.rs:1410-1412`, `frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/window.rs:1892-1893`, `frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs:915-916`). With large padding/border/tab-bar geometry, the new saturation can produce `base_width == u16::MAX`, so `base_width + x` overflows before min-size clamping. This turns an intended overflow hardening change into a runtime panic/wraparound path on oversized layouts. Expected fix: clamp stored base dimensions to `u16::MAX - increment` (or widen backend arithmetic) and add a regression test that asserts `base + increment` stays representable.

title: [MEDIUM] wgpu readback poll loop has no test coverage for timeout, disconnect, or error-propagation paths
description:
Commit 6f41130c (br-43bbl fix wgpu readback polling) rewrites the
readback wait in crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/webgpu.rs:168-193
from:

\`\`\`rust
self.device.poll(PollType::Wait { submission_index: None, timeout: Some(WEBGPU_READBACK_TIMEOUT) })?;
receiver.recv_timeout(WEBGPU_READBACK_TIMEOUT)?...
\`\`\`

to a bounded poll loop:

\`\`\`rust
let deadline = Instant::now() + WEBGPU_READBACK_TIMEOUT;
loop {
    self.device.poll(wgpu::PollType::Poll)?;
    match receiver.recv_timeout(Duration::from_millis(10)) {
        Ok(result) => { result?; break; }
        Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) if Instant::now() < deadline => continue,
        Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => return Err(...),
        Err(RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => return Err(...),
    }
}
\`\`\`

Concerns with the new implementation:

1. \`PollType::Poll\` is non-blocking by contract in wgpu 25. The loop
   relies on \`Poll\` actually driving the \`map_async\` callback forward.
   If a future wgpu point release changes \`Poll\` to be strictly
   \"dispatch-only\" (no callback invocation), the loop would always
   hit the 5s timeout. There is no test pinning this behavior.

2. The \`Disconnected\` branch is reachable only if the \`map_async\`
   closure drops without sending — that happens e.g., if wgpu drops
   the submission without invoking the callback (device lost, internal
   error). No test exercises this path.

3. \`Instant::now() + WEBGPU_READBACK_TIMEOUT\` panics on overflow
   (impossible in practice for 5s, but worth noting as a latent
   concern). Prefer \`checked_add\`.

4. Busy-wait cost: on the timeout path, the loop spins ~500 iterations
   (5000ms / 10ms) calling \`device.poll\` each time. The prior
   \`PollType::Wait\` blocked in the driver. This is a CPU-efficiency
   regression on cancellation/device-loss paths, not a correctness
   regression.

Impact: readback behavior on wgpu failure paths (device lost, long
delay, map_async disconnect) is silently unverified. A correctness
regression in \`PollType::Poll\` semantics between wgpu versions would
silently break screenshots and readback-based features.

Fix direction:
- Add a unit-level test with a mock/stub Device that controls
  \`poll()\` return timing and can force a Disconnected on the mpsc
  channel. Assert each of the four loop outcomes.
- Consider moving the readback loop into a small helper function
  that takes a \`Fn()\` poll closure + channel receiver, to make it
  unit-testable without a real GPU.
- If unit isolation is impractical, at minimum add an integration
  test that triggers a readback and asserts completion within a
  tight CPU budget (regression test for busy-wait blow-up).

Severity: medium — latent risk in a GPU-facing path that typically
works and has no automated coverage for failure modes.

Evidence: commit 6f41130c diff;
crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/webgpu.rs:168-193 at HEAD.
close_reason: Added timeout/disconnect/cancel-style readback coverage and hardened the helper deadline with checked_add

title: [testing-conformance] Gate Robot ApiSurface docs/schema/golden coverage
description:
Follow-up conformance task discovered while clearing `ft-ns4by` and checking for a safe non-overlapping next bead.

Problem:
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_api_contracts.rs` enumerates 35 `ApiSurface::ALL` surfaces and has a strong in-memory contract matrix, but the repo does not mechanically prove that each surface is accounted for across the outward-facing documentation and artifact registries. Existing gates cover adjacent slices:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/schema_golden.rs` validates `docs/json-schema/` JSON, provenance, and `SchemaRegistry::canonical()` registry/disk consistency.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/conformance_robot_envelope_schema.rs` validates discovered `tests/golden_robot_envelope/wa_*.json` success envelopes against `wa-robot-envelope.json`.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/control_plane_golden_matrix.rs` validates the representative control-plane golden matrix.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/conformance_mcp_coverage.rs` gates explicit `docs/mcp-api-spec.md` MCP MUST/SHOULD clauses.

Gap:
None of those gates cross-check `ApiSurface::ALL` against all outward-facing coverage sources. A new or renamed robot surface can have an internal envelope/idempotency check while lacking a JSON schema, docs row, golden fixture/matrix entry, or an explicit documented reason why that particular artifact is not required. Snapshot examples seen during triage include surfaces such as `batch-get-text`, `search-pipeline-status`, `mission-state`, `mission-decisions`, `tx-*`, `replay-*`, and `health`, which are represented in code/tests unevenly rather than through one audited coverage ledger.

Why this depends on `ft-0elb9`:
`ft-0elb9` is the blocked contract/proof-matrix task that will update live fleet/profile mutation docs and golden matrices after the daemon mutation implementation lands. This bead should run after that task so it audits the final contract surface instead of fighting planned placeholder-to-live updates.

Scope:
1. Add a Robot API surface coverage matrix, preferably in `docs/robot-contracts/`, mapping every `ApiSurface::ALL` entry to:
   - robot CLI path or MCP tool/family where applicable,
   - JSON schema file or a precise justification that no schema artifact is expected,
   - docs location,
   - golden fixture or control-plane matrix entry,
   - unit/e2e/proof lane that exercises the contract.
2. Add a CI-gating conformance test, likely under `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/`, that parses the matrix and fails when:
   - any `ApiSurface::ALL` command name is missing from the matrix,
   - a matrix row points at a non-existent schema/docs/golden/proof artifact,
   - a row uses an undocumented exemption instead of an explicit tracked gap,
   - the matrix contains stale rows for surfaces no longer in `ApiSurface::ALL`.
3. For currently missing artifacts, either add the smallest correct schema/docs/golden coverage or mark the row as `DEFERRED` with a concrete follow-up bead id and rationale. Do not silently whitelist gaps.
4. Keep this as a coverage/audit harness only. Do not change daemon mutation behavior, profile/fleet actuators, or active worker files from `ft-269nf` / `ft-3yptk`.

Acceptance:
- The matrix accounts for every current `ApiSurface::ALL` surface and reports coverage by category.
- The conformance test has a falsification path or fixture proving it fails on an omitted surface/stale path.
- Existing registries remain consistent: `SchemaRegistry::canonical()`, `docs/json-schema/PROVENANCE.md`, golden envelope fixtures, and the control-plane matrix are all referenced rather than duplicated by hand where possible.
- `cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test conformance_robot_api_surface_coverage` (or the final chosen test target) passes through RCH only.
- Any shell proof helpers added for the matrix pass `bash -n` and `shellcheck -x`.
- `git diff --check` passes, and `bv --robot-insights` reports no dependency cycles after the bead graph update.

title: [idea-wizard] High-core swarm capacity autopilot and proof gauntlet
description:
## Background

Idea-wizard phase 2/3 found that FrankenTerm already has strong individual substrates for large swarms: resource-pressure cockpit, fleet memory controller, context horizon, capture fairness, herd-wave admission, blocker radar, target-class hardware gates, and release attestation. The remaining high-leverage gap is a composed capacity autopilot for operators running 50-500 agent panes on high-core/high-RAM machines.

This epic turns those separate surfaces into an operator-facing, proof-backed planning loop: predict safe fleet size and fanout, choose workload-class-specific admission and degradation policies, run deterministic high-scale simulations, prove the envelope on RCH/target-class hardware, and publish the result as attested release evidence.

## Idea-wizard shortlist represented here

Top ideas considered and folded into this graph:
- Core-aware swarm capacity planner for 64+ CPU / 256GB+ RAM hosts.
- Deterministic high-scale proof gauntlet instead of isolated microbenchmarks.
- Workload-class admission model that separates coding, review, build, idle, and stuck panes.
- Operator surface that explains why the next 100 panes are admitted, staggered, degraded, or refused.
- Release-attested capacity envelope tied to the existing trust graph.

Next-best complementary ideas included as child scope:
- Telemetry-gap fail-closed behavior.
- Per-family cross-invariant reuse rather than a parallel cockpit.
- Doctor/runbook remediation for operators.
- Regression gates over capacity envelopes.
- Completion dashboard that maps every claim to artifacts.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace the existing resource-pressure cockpit, context-horizon, herd-wave, capture-fairness, or blocker-radar surfaces.
- Do not add a second mux backend.
- Do not claim 200+/500-pane production safety without retained RCH/target-class artifacts.
- Do not run heavy Cargo locally; all substantial proof remains RCH-only.

## Acceptance

- Child beads define the signal inventory, workload-class model, core-aware budget model, simulation corpus, RCH gauntlet, operator surfaces, fail-closed behavior, attestation/regression gates, operator runbook, and final proof dashboard.
- Every child bead includes unit/integration/e2e expectations with structured logs.
- The dependency graph remains cycle-free under `br dep cycles --json`.
- The graph complements existing `ft-tf6g3`, `ft-tf6g3.46`, `ft-rz0eb`, `ft-n447z`, `ft-5bwjf`, `ft-9ntud`, and `ft-r920m` work instead of duplicating it.

title: [fuzz] add MCP request params parser harness
description:
Existing fuzz coverage already hits pattern-pack TOML/binary, config TOML, workflow YAML, robot envelope JSON, IPC auth envelope, snapshot deserialization, replay recordings, and term/escape parsers. But there is still no fuzz target for MCP request-param parsing.

Evidence:
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml` has no MCP parser target; current targets stop at `ipc_auth_envelope`, `robot_envelope_json`, and related config parsers.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_types.rs:25-170` defines the externally-controlled MCP request param structs (`StateParams`, `GetTextParams`, `SearchParams`, `EventsParams`, etc.), but they are `pub(super)` and only covered by unit/proptest deserialization checks.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_types.rs:1170-1845` has property tests over many `serde_json::from_value(...)` paths, but no byte-level fuzzing against malformed/truncated/oversized JSON.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_framework.rs:203-265` also round-trips untrusted remote MCP payloads through `serde_json::from_value(...)`.

Why it matters:
- MCP is a network/external-input surface with many optional/defaulted fields and multiple tool-specific param shapes.
- Proptests cover valid structured values, not adversarial raw JSON bytes, duplicate keys, deep nesting, type confusion, or truncation.

Fix:
- Add a fuzz seam plus harness that feeds raw JSON/Value payloads through the MCP request-param decode paths (or framework payload bridge) and asserts no panic / deterministic decode outcomes.

title: ft-d6nrd.cont: per-op FrameBudget try_execute + cost feedback + bulk_drain wiring at paint sites
description:
Continuation of ft-d6nrd (slice 1 shipped at 40047d02f).

Slice 1 wired begin_frame / end_frame + the doctor surface; per-op try_execute is item 2 of the parent bead and remains.

Each paint-pipeline op site needs:
1. Wrap with Instant::now() delta to measure cost_ns.
2. Call frame_budget.try_execute(OpKind, OpPriority, cost_ns) before the op runs.
3. If ExecutionDecision::Deferred or Dropped, skip the op + cosmetic_defer_outstanding.record_deferred(op_kind).

title: ingest.rs: extract_delta gap-reason conflates overlap_size_zero with current_empty
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs:1700-1705` in `extract_delta`:

```rust
if overlap_size == 0 || current.is_empty() {
    return DeltaResult::Gap {
        reason: "overlap_size_zero_or_current_empty".to_string(),
        content: current.to_string(),
    };
}
```

## Defect
Two semantically distinct failure causes share a single gap reason:

1. **overlap_size == 0** — caller deliberately disabled overlap (config). Recoverable by re-enabling overlap.
2. **current.is_empty()** — capture returned zero bytes. Symptom of capture-source error or terminal-clear.

Forensic observers reading Gap.reason from the captured-segment stream cannot distinguish these.

## Impact
- Operator dashboards aggregate causes into a single bucket — root-cause analysis blocked.
- Class P3 observability hygiene (no data loss).

## Fix shape
Split into:
- `overlap_size_zero` when overlap_size == 0
- `current_empty` when current.is_empty()
- Prefer `current_empty` if both hold (downstream symptom is the diagnosable cause).

## Tests
Update conformance_ingest_gap_semantics_are_explicit (line 3079+) to exercise both reasons separately.
close_reason:
Fixed at 54e9f0839 (commit message reads 'sec(ingest): observable counter for PaneCursor seq saturation (br-ft-g8nbu)' but the diff also contains the ft-baaex gap-reason split — known concurrent-edit commit-message-vs-content mismatch pattern, ft-4dhsm tracks the broader class).

## What landed

extract_delta at ingest.rs:1788 split the conflated 'overlap_size_zero_or_current_empty' reason into two semantically distinct causes ordered current_empty-first (downstream symptom wins when both hold):

- current_empty: capture returned zero bytes — diagnosable symptom of capture-source error or terminal-clear. Returns Gap with content=String::new() (the empty current had no bytes anyway).
- overlap_size_zero: caller deliberately disabled overlap via config — recoverable by re-enabling overlap. Returns Gap with content=current.to_string().

The test-mirror at ingest.rs:3115 mirrors the production split.

conformance_ingest_gap_semantics_are_explicit at ingest.rs:3263 was updated to exercise four cases:
- ('abc', 'zabc', 0, 'overlap_size_zero', 'zabc') — pure overlap-disabled
- ('abc', '', 1024, 'current_empty', '') — pure capture-empty
- ('abc', '', 0, 'current_empty', '') — both hold; current_empty wins
- Plus the two pre-existing content-discontinuity reasons (content_changed_without_append, overlap_not_found) for regression coverage.

## Verification

cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features clean (193 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors at HEAD).

Note: cargo test --lib hits pre-existing failures in events.rs test code (PaneDiscovered field rename in a sibling commit) that are unrelated to this fix; the lib compiles cleanly and the four conformance cases exercise the new ordered-check shape directly.
