# Continuation: smart-selection regex catalog + OSC 52 wiring

## Context
ft-2okh0.14 retired at substrate scope (commit f77a5e568):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/smart_selection.rs ships SelectionPatternKind 12-variant catalog (Url / HttpUrl / UnixPath / WindowsPath / ShellQuoted / Email / Ipv4 / Ipv6 / GitRef / PhoneNumber / HexColor / NumericLiteral) with priority() (URL=0 wins) + display_name() for AT, SelectionMatch with end-exclusive contains, classify_double_click + classify_triple_click widest-match-wins, Osc52Policy (Allow/Prompt/Deny) + Osc52PolicyConfig (default write=Prompt read=Deny per exfiltration vector rule) + paranoid()/permissive() variants, evaluate_osc52 with session_allowed override, SmartSelectionA11yMessage::render.
- 29 inline tests passing.

## What this bead carries

### Regex catalog
- New module `frankenterm/term/src/selection_patterns.rs`:
  - For each SelectionPatternKind variant, a compiled regex matching the wire format
  - Url: RFC 3986 (scheme + authority + path + query + fragment)
  - HttpUrl: more permissive http/https variant
  - UnixPath: `[/~]?[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*`
  - WindowsPath: `[A-Za-z]:\\\\[^\\s]+`
  - ShellQuoted: single/double/dollar-quoted
  - Email: RFC 5321 simplified
  - Ipv4 / Ipv6 / GitRef / PhoneNumber / HexColor / NumericLiteral

### Pre-filter for URL-inside-ShellQuoted
- Substrate's classify_double_click picks widest by default; integration's pattern engine pre-filters to drop ShellQuoted when a higher-priority match (URL/Email/UnixPath) is fully contained inside it
- Algorithm: for each ShellQuoted candidate, check whether any higher-priority candidate is fully contained; if so, drop the ShellQuoted

### GUI mouse handler
- frankenterm-gui mouse-double-click handler:
  - Get click cell coords → byte offset in line text
  - Run pattern engine → Vec<SelectionMatch>
  - Apply pre-filter (drop ShellQuoted-containing-higher-priority)
  - classify_double_click(matches, byte_offset) → Option<SelectionMatch>
  - On Some: select span, emit SmartSelectionA11yMessage to AT-tree
  - On None: fall back to existing word-boundary selection

### Triple-click wiring
- Same flow but classify_triple_click constrained to current line span

### User-extensible patterns
- frankenterm.toml `[[smart_selection.patterns]]` array:
  ```toml
  [[smart_selection.patterns]]
  name = "jira-ticket"
  regex = "[A-Z]+-[0-9]+"
  display_name = "Jira ticket"
  priority = 50
  ```
- Custom patterns get an integer priority that slots in between the built-in kinds

### OSC 52 escape-parser implementation
- Cross-link ft-jornq / ft-2okh0.1.5 OSC 22/8/52 continuation
- Parser for `\x1b]52;c;<base64>\x07` (write) and `\x1b]52;c;?\x07` (read query)
- Decode base64; pass through evaluate_osc52 gate; on Granted, dispatch to platform backend; on PromptUser, show UI; on Denied, log + drop

### Per-platform clipboard backends
- macOS: NSPasteboard via objc2 bindings
- X11: PRIMARY + CLIPBOARD selection via x11rb
- Wayland: wl-clipboard via wayland-client
- Windows: OpenClipboard / SetClipboardData via windows-rs

### Prompt UI for OSC 52
- Modal overlay: "App requested clipboard {direction}. Allow once / Allow for session / Deny"
- Operator's choice updates the session_allowed flag for subsequent requests in this session

### AT-tree integration
- SmartSelectionA11yMessage::render() output gets played through NSAccessibility / AT-SPI / UIA
- Cross-link ft-mpc9b.10.1 a11y_tree.rs for the announcement playback path

### Tests at integration layer
- E2E: double-click on `https://example.com/path?q=1` selects the full URL with query
- E2E: triple-click on `cat "hello world"` selects `"hello world"`
- E2E: OSC 52 write prompt → user clicks "Allow for session" → subsequent writes pass without prompt
- E2E: OSC 52 read default policy denies; logs the denial
- A11y test: AT receives "URL selected: https://example.com" within 16ms of selection commit
- Custom pattern test: jira-ticket pattern from config matches ABC-123

## Acceptance per the original bead
- Smart selection regex catalog at frankenterm/term/src/selection_patterns.rs
- Double-click + triple-click classification working
- OSC 52 implementation behind policy gate
- User-extensible patterns via config
- A11y announcements working
- ClipboardWrite ActionKind in policy.rs

- OSC 22/8/52 parser: ft-jornq (BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.1.5.cont)

title: Replay checkpointer resumes foreign or stale-schema checkpoints
description:
Reality-check audit of the replay checkpointer found that checkpoint resume does not validate checkpoint identity or schema before replacing live state.

Evidence:
- CheckpointState carries checkpoint_version and replay_run_id at crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_checkpoint.rs:91-116, and CHECKPOINT_VERSION is defined at crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_checkpoint.rs:120.
- ReplayCheckpointer stores its own replay_run_id at crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_checkpoint.rs:187-191.
- ReplayCheckpointer::resume_from at crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_checkpoint.rs:389-397 blindly clones the supplied checkpoint into inner.state, copies checkpoint_created_ms into last_checkpoint_wall_ms, and clears halted/completed. It does not check checkpoint.checkpoint_version, checkpoint.replay_run_id, event_position monotonicity, or whether the checkpoint belongs to this run.
- CheckpointState::from_json only parses JSON at crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_checkpoint.rs:146-149; no validation layer rejects a stale schema or foreign replay_run_id before resume_from consumes it.

Why it matters:
Replay checkpoints are a trust boundary for deterministic resume. A stale or foreign checkpoint can rewind/advance another replay run and clear halted/completed state, producing reports and resumed traces under the wrong replay_run_id instead of failing closed.

Proposed remediation:
Change resume_from to return Result and validate checkpoint_version == CHECKPOINT_VERSION, checkpoint.replay_run_id == self.replay_run_id, and sane monotonic counters for the current run. Add unit/property tests that arbitrary mismatched checkpoint_version/replay_run_id values are rejected and that valid checkpoints round-trip unchanged.
notes: Already shipped at a7e96816e (sibling-attributed but the impl + tests match the design exactly): CheckpointResumeError enum (SchemaMismatch + RunIdMismatch), resume_from now returns Result<(), CheckpointResumeError>, validates checkpoint.checkpoint_version == CHECKPOINT_VERSION and checkpoint.replay_run_id == self.replay_run_id BEFORE installing state, rejected resume leaves halted/completed flags untouched. 4 unit tests + 1 proptest pin: foreign run_id rejected with bead-id Display, stale schema rejected, matching checkpoint accepts, halted-flag-preserved-on-rejection, proptest covering arbitrary (ckpt_run, state_run, version_choice) ∈ all-fuzzed-combinations. Existing test callsites (lines 702 + 739 in replay_checkpoint.rs + line 178 in proptest_replay_checkpoint.rs) updated to call .expect or use matching run_id. Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core-replay --lib clean. My local diff matched HEAD; closing as sibling-shipped.

title: [policy.trauma_guard.fix] FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA bypass widened by substring match on var name
description:
Bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs (the user-requested security/correctness review pass — same pass that found ft-ftepl + ft-vgtab).

## Defect

has_trauma_bypass_prefix at policy.rs:2664+ scans leading shell-style var assignments to detect FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 prefixes. The check uses assignment.contains(...):

    if assignment.contains("FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1")
        || assignment.contains("FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=\"1\"")
        || assignment.contains("FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA='1'")
    {
        return true;
    }

The substring check matches any variable whose name ends with FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA (or whose name contains the exact bytes FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 anywhere).

## Repro

MY_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 dangerous_cmd
OTHER_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 dangerous_cmd
XFT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 dangerous_cmd

All three bypass the trauma guard. The string MY_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 contains the substring FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1; .contains() returns true; bypass granted. The user never set the documented variable; an unrelated variable with a colliding name suffix grants the override.

## Why it matters

Trauma guard blocks repeated-failure commands (a safety gate). The documented escape hatch is FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1. The substring match widens the escape hatch to any custom var with FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA in its name. An operator who legitimately uses an env var like MY_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA_AUDIT=1 (audit naming convention) accidentally bypasses every trauma block thereafter, with no warning that they triggered the bypass.

Worse: this enables a documented-bypass-via-typosquatting attack. A pasted command from elsewhere might contain MYFT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 (typo) and the operator would not notice their guards are off.

## Fix

Parse the var name explicitly. The VAR_ASSIGN regex already captures  — pull the var name out (everything before the first ) and check it's exactly FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA. Then check the value is 1 / "1" / '1'.

## Acceptance

- has_trauma_bypass_prefix correctly distinguishes FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 from MY_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 (and similar prefix collisions).
- Regression test reproduces all three attack vectors.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:2664-2706 (has_trauma_bypass_prefix)
- policy.rs:2414 (VAR_ASSIGN regex)
- ft-ftepl + ft-vgtab (sibling bugs from the same review pass — operator-facing safety signals where the underlying check is mechanically too permissive)
notes:
Security fix landed at commit 10359db69. Trauma-bypass check now parses var name explicitly (no substring widening).

Bug: has_trauma_bypass_prefix used assignment.contains("FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1") which matched any var name whose suffix contained those bytes. Attacks: MY_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1, OTHER_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1, AUDIT_FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1, XFT_BYPASS_TRAUMA=1 all bypassed silently.

Fix:
- New helper is_exact_trauma_bypass_assignment parses var name + value explicitly. Splits on '=', asserts LHS is exactly 'FT_BYPASS_TRAUMA', strips optional ' / " quotes from value, asserts value is exactly '1'.
- has_trauma_bypass_prefix now calls the helper.

2 new regression tests (4 trauma-bypass-related total):
- trauma_bypass_rejects_prefix_augmented_var_names: covers MY_/OTHER_/X/AUDIT_ prefix attacks.
- is_exact_trauma_bypass_assignment_unit: direct unit coverage.

Same review pass also found:
- ft-ftepl: is_safe monotonic-false in render_snapshot_audit
- ft-vgtab: record_write rubber-stamp in cold_tier_pipeline
- (this) ft-cof0r: substring-match security widening in policy

All three are operator-facing safety signals where the underlying check is mechanically too permissive. Pattern: a test/check returns 'pass' in the case the real-world condition is broken.

Plus picked up linter's defense-in-depth improvement: ChunkBytes::bytes field in scrollback_cold_tier_pipeline.rs made private (preventing mid-pipeline mutation that would bypass the redactor).

title: recording.rs and wire_protocol.rs epoch_ms_now silently substitute 0 on clock-before-1970
description:
Phase 3 audit found two more sites with the same defect family as ft-bn6qi (web/sse.rs::epoch_ms_now): production code uses unwrap_or_default() on duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH), silently substituting 0 timestamps when the system clock is before 1970-01-01.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:1009-1014: pub fn epoch_ms_now() -> u64 uses .unwrap_or_default(). This is the recorder's wall-clock helper, called by replay_capture.rs:291,293,347,407,465 and other capture paths to stamp event timestamps. A clock anomaly window during ingest produces a flat line of timestamp=0 for every captured event with no diagnostic.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/wire_protocol.rs:741-749: fn epoch_ms_now() -> i64 same shape, used by wire-protocol envelopes that get replayed and audit-traced.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs already shipped the fail-loud fix under ft-bn6qi (counter + tracing::warn). The recording/wire_protocol sites still have the silent-substitution pattern.
- Recording is the forensic-truth surface. A silent timestamp=0 on every event during clock skew turns the recorder's monotonic-sequence promise into 'all events claim the same instant' — operators correlating an incident lose temporal ordering across the anomaly window.

Why it matters: ft-bn6qi shipped the observability counter + tracing::warn pattern for the SSE path. Apply the same shape to these two production helpers so a clock anomaly is a single observability scrape away, not a forensic mystery.

Proposed remediation: replace unwrap_or_default() at both sites with explicit match. Bump a process-global counter (recording_clock_anomaly_count, wire_protocol_clock_anomaly_count) on the Err branch and emit structured tracing::warn at target ft.recording.clock / ft.wire_protocol.clock. Keep the scalar return contract (0 / i64::MAX-saturated) so callers don't need to handle Result. Add tests with pre-epoch SystemTime injection (UNIX_EPOCH - 100s) similar to ft-bn6qi's approach.
notes: Applied the ft-bn6qi observability pattern to recording.rs::epoch_ms_now and wire_protocol.rs::epoch_ms_now. Both replaced unwrap_or_default() with explicit match. New process-global counters: RECORDING_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT (recording.rs) + WIRE_PROTOCOL_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT (wire_protocol.rs) with pub observability surfaces (recording_clock_anomaly_count(), wire_protocol_clock_anomaly_count()) and cfg(test) reset helpers. Err branch bumps counter, emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.recording.clock / ft.wire_protocol.clock with pre_epoch_secs delta + br-ft-crpvd breadcrumb, returns scalar (0 / saturated i64::MAX) so callers don't have to handle Result. Both fns refactored into thin wrappers over epoch_ms_now_from(SystemTime) for testability. Added 4 tests (2 each): post_epoch_no_anomaly (sanity), pre_epoch_bumps_counter (Err branch returns 0 + bumps counter, second call bumps again per recording.rs). Recording is the forensic-truth surface; wire_protocol envelopes feed audit-traced replays — pre-fix a clock anomaly silently produced timestamp=0 across both, corrupting forensic ordering. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [codebase-audit][capture/storage] WAL checkpoint cost under sustained-write load is unmeasured + ungoverned
description:
## Domain gap

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs` opens SQLite in WAL mode
(per the existing benches and `recorder_storage.rs` — confirmed
by `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` patterns in the schema setup). WAL
mode trades disk-write durability for read concurrency: writes
go to a sidecar `.db-wal` file; checkpoints fold the WAL back
into the main DB on a periodic schedule (default: when the WAL
hits ~4MB).

## What's missing (not caught by prior audits)

- `benches/recorder_ingest.rs` (proposed in ft-9r82k) covers
  ingest CPU/serialize cost.
- `tests/storage_regression.rs` (34 KB) covers schema regression.
- 9 migration tests + proptest_recorder.* cover migration safety.

**None measure or govern WAL checkpoint cost.** Specifically:

1. **Checkpoint stalls under sustained writes.** SQLite's auto-
   checkpoint runs synchronously on the writer thread when the
   WAL crosses the threshold. At fleet scale (200 panes × 10
   events/sec = 2000 events/sec), the WAL fills in seconds; the
   checkpoint stalls every writer for the duration of the fold.
   p99 latency on the recorder hot path likely has an unbounded
   tail driven by checkpoint cadence.

2. **WAL grows unbounded if checkpoint blocks.** A single
   long-running read query holds the WAL "in use" — auto-
   checkpoint fails, WAL grows past the `journal_size_limit`
   pragma if not configured, and disk fills. ft has no
   explicit configuration of `wal_autocheckpoint`,
   `journal_size_limit`, or `synchronous` PRAGMAs.

3. **No adaptive throttle.** When checkpoints are running long
   (because of blocking readers or just disk pressure), the
   ingest path doesn't know to slow down. Per the README's
   backpressure hierarchy (Green/Yellow/Red/Black), there's
   no checkpoint-cost-aware tier.

This is exactly the SaaS pattern of "fail-open under sustained
load" — but for a local SQLite store rather than Redis.

## Why this catches real defects

Concrete failure scenarios:

- **Operator runs a swarm session for 8 hours.** The WAL
  accumulates because of a long-running `ft search` that
  pinned readers across a checkpoint. Disk fills overnight.
  Recorder writes start failing.
- **`ft session restore` reads from a 100 MB WAL.** Restore
  takes minutes because every read joins the main DB + WAL.
- **Tail latency on the recorder hot path** spikes every 30s
  as auto-checkpoint runs. Per the profiling skill's tail-
  latency discipline, p99 must be measured — today p50 is fine
  but p99 hides a checkpoint stall.

## Suggested approach

1. **Bench**: `benches/wal_checkpoint_cost.rs` —
   - Sustained-write workload (10K events/sec for 60s).
   - Measure: WAL size over time, checkpoint frequency,
     per-event p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency.
   - Compare three PRAGMA configurations: default,
     `synchronous=NORMAL+wal_autocheckpoint=10000`, manual
     checkpoint via `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.

2. **Configuration knobs in ft.toml**:
   ```toml
   [storage.wal]
   autocheckpoint_pages = 10000
   synchronous = "normal"   # or "full" / "off"
   journal_size_limit_mb = 64
   ```

3. **Telemetry counter** for checkpoint events:
   `counter!("storage.wal_checkpoint_ms")`. The diagnostic
   surface (per ft-40k1o's ft doctor goldens) shows the
   distribution.

4. **Backpressure integration**: when WAL size > threshold OR
   recent checkpoint took > N ms, raise to Yellow tier so
   ingest knows to throttle.

## Out of scope

- Migrating to a different storage engine (orthogonal — WAL is
  fine; the audit gap is the lack of measurement).
- The `frankensqlite` rollout-only backend (per README hedge).

## Acceptance criteria

- `benches/wal_checkpoint_cost.rs` exists and runs the three
  PRAGMA configurations.
- p99 latency under sustained 10K-events/sec load is documented
  in `docs/perf-ledger/wal-checkpoint.md`.
- `[storage.wal]` config block is wired to the production loader.
- Telemetry counter for checkpoint duration lands.
- Per the profiling skill's hand-off contract, this bead stops
  at the hotspot table; optimization (if needed) becomes a
  follow-on bead per `extreme-software-optimization` skill.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs` (WAL mode setup)
- ft-9r82k (sibling: recorder ingest bench — covers
  serialize/flush, NOT WAL checkpoint specifically)
- README §Replay & Forensics
- Skill: profiling-software-performance — IO-AND-TRADEOFFS.md
  ("disk is the bottleneck" trigger; biolatency for fsync)

Filed by cc_1 codebase audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: added WAL checkpoint sustained-write Criterion benchmark and perf ledger baseline

title: ft-2okh0.12: BlockStats avg_cmd_duration_ms denominator includes blocks without cmd_start_ts
description: block_mode_terminal.rs BlockStats::avg_cmd_duration_ms divides cmd_duration_sum_ms by blocks_completed_total. cmd_duration_sum_ms only increments when block.cmd_duration_ms() returns Some (cmd_start_ts AND output_end_ts present). blocks_completed_total increments for every CommandEnd that finalizes an active block, including blocks that completed without going through Command phase (e.g., PromptStart followed directly by CommandEnd). title: [redactor_coverage_matrix.fix] is_safe rubber-stamps cold-start (no vectors evaluated)
description:
## Defect

RedactorCoverageHealth::is_safe at redactor_coverage_matrix.rs:344-347:

    pub const fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        self.providers_below_recall_floor == 0
    }

baseline() returns providers_below_recall_floor=0 — so a fresh
RedactorCoverageHealth (zero vectors evaluated, zero TP, zero FN)
reports is_safe == true.

Same rubber-stamp family as ft-05poz (iterm2_osc_1337) and
ft-ftepl (render_snapshot_audit): zero-state must NOT be reported
as safe — it must be reported as 'no measurement yet' (false).

## Why it matters (P2)

This health is consumed by the doctor surface. In production:
- A fresh process reports redactor coverage safe BEFORE any
  probe has run.
- A process where the redactor coverage matrix harness has not
  been wired/scheduled reports safe.

Result: operator sees green, has no signal that the coverage
probe failed to run. The redactor could be silently degraded.

## Repro

    let health = RedactorCoverageHealth::baseline();
    assert!(!health.is_safe());  // FAILS today; should pass.

## Fix

    pub const fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        self.vectors_evaluated_total > 0

title: [EPIC] End-to-end swarm integration proof: demonstrate full observe-detect-react loop with live agents
description:
# Goal
Prove that FrankenTerm actually delivers on its core value proposition end-to-end: observing live AI agent panes, detecting state transitions, triggering automated workflows, and exposing actionable data through Robot Mode. Today every subsystem has unit tests, but nobody has proven the aggregate works.

# Background
The reality check (2026-04-06) found that individual subsystems are well-implemented:
- Ingest pipeline: real delta extraction with 4KB overlap matching
- Pattern detection: real Aho-Corasick + Bloom + regex
- Storage: real SQLite v23 + FTS5
- Robot Mode: fully implemented
- Policy engine: 40+ subsystems
- Fleet memory: 4-tier backpressure (Normal/Elevated/Critical/Emergency)

But there is NO evidence that someone has run: ft watch -> observed real panes -> detected a real pattern -> triggered a real workflow -> verified via ft robot. The individual subsystems are proven; the integration is not.

# Why This Matters
FrankenTerm promises a swarm-native terminal platform. Without E2E proof, it is a collection of well-tested libraries, not a platform.

# Architectural Intent
1. Start with a minimal proof: 3 panes, synthetic agent output, verify Robot Mode sees detection events.
2. Scale to realistic: 20 panes with mixed agent types, workflow triggers, policy gates, FTS search.
3. Scale to stress: 50+ panes with fleet memory engaged, prove tiered scrollback works under load.
4. Prove tx execution: ft tx run against real panes with policy gates and compensation.
5. For each scale tier, demonstrate the FULL loop: observe -> detect -> react -> audit.

# Acceptance Criteria
1. Minimal E2E (ft-d0ez0.1): ft watch + 3 panes + pattern detection + Robot Mode queries
2. 20-pane integration (ft-d0ez0.2): multi-agent detection, workflow, policy, FTS search
3. 50-pane stress (ft-d0ez0.3): fleet memory pressure transitions (Normal->Elevated->Critical), tiered scrollback eviction
4. Tx E2E (ft-d0ez0.4): ft tx run with real pane operations, compensation, audit trail
5. All tests produce structured JSON artifacts for reproducibility.
6. Tests run in CI or have clear manual reproduction instructions.
close_reason: done

title: Minimal E2E proof: ft watch + 3 mock panes + pattern detection + Robot Mode verification
description:
# Goal
Create the smallest possible E2E test proving the full observation-detection-query loop works against real (or simulated) panes.

# Background
Every subsystem has strong unit tests (46,633 total), but nobody has proven the aggregate works: ft watch observing panes -> pattern engine detecting state transitions -> Robot Mode returning detection events. This is the foundational proof.

# Design
## Test script: tests/e2e/e2e_minimal_loop.py

### Pane output (use ACTUAL corpus fixture text, not paraphrases)
- Pane 0: codex.usage.reached — echo the text from corpus/codex/usage_reached.txt:
  "You've hit your usage limit. Please try again at 2026-01-20 12:34 UTC."
- Pane 1: claude_code pattern — echo the text from corpus/claude_code/usage_reached.txt:
  "rate limit reached; try again in 15 minutes"
- Pane 2: normal text with no pattern matches (e.g. "hello world")

### Steps
1. Create temp workspace dir with minimal ft.toml:
   [general]
   log_level = "debug"
   [ingest]
   poll_interval_ms = 200
   [patterns]
   packs = ["core"]
   [storage]
   db_path = "<tempdir>/ft.db"
2. Build ft binary (or use prebuilt from PATH)
3. Start ft watch --foreground --workspace <tempdir> as subprocess
4. Create 3 panes (headless mux server or WezTerm CLI)
5. Write corpus text to each pane
6. Wait for 2x poll_interval (400ms + 1s buffer = ~1.5s)
7. Run assertions via ft robot:
   a. ft robot state → assert ok:true, >= 3 panes
   b. ft robot events --limit 20 → assert >= 1 event with rule_id containing "usage" for pane 0 or 1
   c. ft robot search "usage limit" → assert >= 1 search result
   d. ft robot get-text <pane_0_id> --tail 5 → assert contains "hit your usage limit"
8. ft stop or SIGTERM the watcher
9. Cleanup tempdir

### Fallback for no-backend environments
- If neither WezTerm CLI nor headless mux server available: skip with exit code 77 (TAP skip) and message
- CI should ensure headless mux server is available

## Logging
- JSON report: tests/e2e/output/e2e_minimal_loop_<timestamp>.json
- Per-assertion: { check: "robot_state", expected: "ok=true, panes>=3", actual: <raw>, pass: bool, elapsed_ms: N }
- On failure: dump ft watch stderr, ft.db stat, all robot responses
- Python logging with JSON formatter to both file and stderr

# Acceptance Criteria
1. Script runs from clean state (no pre-existing ft.db).
2. All 4 Robot Mode assertions pass.
3. Completes in under 30 seconds.
4. Idempotent (cleanup on exit via atexit or try/finally).
5. JSON report produced.
6. On failure, output sufficient to debug without re-running.

# Implementation Notes
- Pattern rules codex.usage.reached and claude_code.usage.reached are in the built-in "core" pack.
- The headless mux server binary is crates/frankenterm-mux-server — check if it provides a PTY creation API or needs wezterm cli compatibility.
- Existing tests/e2e/ directory has Python scripts — follow existing patterns (check for test runner conventions).

Remaining validation of the live-pane success path is blocked on this machine because no usable ft binary is available locally and wezterm is not present in PATH. The script records both preconditions explicitly and exits 77 as designed.

title: 50-pane stress test: fleet memory pressure transitions, tiered scrollback eviction, backpressure under load
description:
# Goal
Prove fleet memory management and tiered scrollback work under sustained 50-pane load, matching the advertised 200+ pane scale claims.

# Background
The README claims '200+ panes under 1GB' and describes a 4-tier fleet memory controller. The fleet_memory_controller.rs and scrollback_tiers.rs are implemented, but never tested at scale. This test proves they work.

# Design
## Test script: tests/e2e/e2e_50pane_stress.py
### Setup
- 50 panes via headless mux server, each generating ~1KB/sec continuous output via script
- Per-pane memory budget configured to trigger tier transitions within 5 minutes
- Total sustained throughput: ~50KB/sec

### Phase 1: Warm-up (0-60s)
- All panes generating output
- Verify: ft robot state shows 50 panes, ft doctor --json shows Normal pressure tier

### Phase 2: Pressure build (60-180s)
- Continue output generation
- Monitor: FleetPressureTier transitions via ft doctor --json (polled every 10s)
- Expected: Normal -> Elevated as scrollback accumulates

### Phase 3: Tier transitions (180-300s)
- Continue output generation with increased rate on 10 panes
- Expected: Elevated -> Critical on high-output panes
- Verify: tiered scrollback eviction events occur (warm tier activation)

### Phase 4: Detection under load (at 240s)
- Inject rate-limit pattern into pane 25
- Measure: time from injection to ft robot events showing the detection
- Expected: detection latency < 5 seconds

### Phase 5: Robot Mode under load (at 270s)
- Time ft robot state, ft robot search, ft robot get-text responses
- Expected: state < 2s, search < 5s

### Metrics collection
- Peak RSS of ft process (via ps or /proc/self/status)
- Detection latency (injection time vs event timestamp)
- Robot Mode response latency
- Pressure tier transition timestamps
- Scrollback tier eviction counts

## Logging
- JSON metrics report: tests/e2e/output/e2e_50pane_stress_<timestamp>.json
- Per-phase: phase_name, start_time, end_time, metrics_snapshot
- Timeseries: pressure_tier sampled every 10s
- On failure: full metrics dump + ft doctor --json + process info

# Acceptance Criteria
1. ft process RSS stays under 1GB with 50 panes over 5 minutes.
2. Pattern detection latency < 5 seconds under 50-pane load.
3. Robot Mode state query < 2 seconds, search < 5 seconds under load.
4. At least one FleetPressureTier transition above Normal observed.
5. At least one tiered scrollback tier transition (hot->warm) observed.
6. No crashes, panics, or data corruption during 5-minute run.
7. Machine-readable metrics report produced with all measurements.
8. On failure, report identifies which metric breached which threshold.

title: Runtime telemetry queue stats aggregation can overflow fail-open
description:
Subsystem: runtime_telemetry work-queue normalization

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:1393-1467` normalizes `QueueStats` into a unified runtime telemetry record used for queue health.
- The adapter computes `let terminal = stats.completed + stats.failed + stats.cancelled` with unchecked `usize` addition, then derives `failure_rate` and `blocked_ratio` from that value (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:1413-1424`).
- `QueueStats` is a public serializable struct with `usize` counters (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/swarm_work_queue.rs:250-261`), and live snapshots fill those counters by incrementing one field per work item (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/swarm_work_queue.rs:793-814`). Restored, synthetic, or corrupted diagnostic snapshots can therefore contain individually valid counters whose sum overflows.
- Existing adapter tests cover only small hand-written queues (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:15110-15188`), so there is no boundary test for terminal counts near `usize::MAX` or inconsistent `total_items` vs terminal totals.

Why it matters:
This is the health-classification path for `swarm.work_queue`. In debug builds, an overflow panics inside telemetry normalization. In release builds, the wrapped `terminal` value can produce a low/zero failure rate or a misleading `blocked_ratio`, causing a severely failed queue snapshot to be reported as Green or Yellow.

Proposed remediation:
Aggregate queue counters with checked/saturating `u128` arithmetic, mark inconsistent or overflowing snapshots explicitly, and force at least Red/Black health when terminal totals cannot be trusted. Add property tests over `QueueStats` with counters near `usize::MAX`, including terminal totals greater than `total_items`, asserting no panic and no lower-severity fail-open classification.
notes: Reality-check audit was out of date: the unchecked usize addition has been replaced with u128 accumulation (runtime_telemetry.rs:1446-1452), counter_overflow_detected and terminal_exceeds_total flags are emitted (lines 1450-1452), and the health_tier ladder forces Black/Corruption for overflow + Red/Configuration for terminal>total (lines 1482-1508). The existing proptest at line 15600+ already exercises any<usize>() counter values and asserts no-panic + correct Black/Red classification. Added 2 named regression tests pinning the bead's specific worry: queue_stats_at_usize_max_does_not_panic_and_is_black_ft_d4jyb (all three terminal counters at usize::MAX -> Black/Corruption, finite ratios) and queue_stats_terminal_exceeds_total_is_red_ft_d4jyb (terminal=50 > total_items=10 -> at least Red/Configuration). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [conformance] docs/json-schema/ has no PROVENANCE.md — generator + version of every committed schema is unrecorded
description:
## The gap

`docs/json-schema/` contains 19 committed JSON Schema files
(`wa-robot-*.json`, `wa-robot-envelope.json`, etc.). There is no
`PROVENANCE.md` recording how each one was generated.

The conformance skill mandates this exact artifact:

> **Fixture Provenance (Non-Negotiable):** Every fixture must record
> how it was generated. … When fixtures are regenerated 6 months later
> and results change, you need to know what version generated the
> originals to diagnose whether the change is a bug or a new feature.

## What exists today

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/api_schema.rs` documents the *strategy*
  ("Rust structs → JSON Schema via `schemars`") but doesn't record
  which committed files were generated this way vs hand-authored.
- The `wa-` prefix is a leftover from the project's pre-rename state
  (per ft-ijbql notes); nothing in `docs/json-schema/` records that
  decision either.
- `schema_golden.rs` enforces well-formedness but knows nothing about
  generator lineage.

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

A future contributor regenerates `wa-robot-state.json` via `schemars`,
the output differs slightly from the committed copy (field ordering,
new `description:` strings, etc.). They cannot tell whether:
1. The committed file was originally hand-authored and the schemars
   version is the new canonical source (accept the drift), or
2. The committed file was generated by an older schemars version and
   the diff is a regression they need to investigate, or
3. The committed file was generated, then hand-edited to relax a
   constraint, and the regeneration would lose that edit.

Without provenance metadata, every regeneration becomes archaeology.

## Suggested implementation

`docs/json-schema/PROVENANCE.md` with one row per committed schema:

```markdown
| File                          | Source       | Generator              | Generator version | Last regenerated |
|-------------------------------|--------------|------------------------|-------------------|------------------|
| wa-robot-envelope.json        | hand         | —                      | —                 | 2026-03-16       |
| wa-robot-state.json           | schemars     | schemars (Rust)        | 0.8.x             | 2026-04-23       |
| wa-robot-search.json          | schemars     | schemars (Rust)        | 0.8.x             | 2026-04-23       |
| wa-robot-mission-state.json   | hand→schemars| schemars; hand-edited L | 0.8.x             | 2026-04-23       |
| ...                           | ...          | ...                    | ...               | ...              |
```

Plus a one-time bead-implementation pass:
1. Audit each file's git history (`git log --oneline -- <file>`) to
   reconstruct provenance.
2. Where ambiguous, mark `Source: unknown — needs reconstruction`
   so the gap is visible rather than papered over.
3. Add a CI check that fails when a file in `docs/json-schema/`
   changes without a matching `Last regenerated` bump in
   `PROVENANCE.md`.

## Out of scope

- Migrating all schemas to schemars-generated (separate ft-* if
  desired).
- Renaming `wa-` → `ft-` in schema filenames (separate cosmetics bead).

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/json-schema/PROVENANCE.md` lists every `*.json` file in the
  directory.
- Every entry has `Source` ∈ {`hand`, `schemars`, `mixed`,
  `unknown — needs reconstruction`}.
- A CI check fails when a schema file is modified without a matching
  PROVENANCE.md row update.

## References

- Skill section "Fixture Provenance (Non-Negotiable)"
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/api_schema.rs` — the strategy doc
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/schema_golden.rs` — the existing
  well-formedness gate (does NOT cover provenance)

Filed by cc_1 conformance audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: documented schema provenance and added coverage test

title: Tantivy full reindex ignores clear_before_start after checkpoint
description:
Reality-check audit evidence:
- `ReindexConfig::clear_before_start` is documented as "Whether to clear the entire index before starting" and defaults to true (`crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_reindex.rs:147-164`). The `full_reindex` docs also say that if the flag is true, all existing documents are deleted before indexing begins (`tantivy_reindex.rs:337-342`).
- The implementation only clears when `storage.read_checkpoint(&consumer_id)` returns `None` (`tantivy_reindex.rs:356-363`). If any checkpoint exists, `clear_before_start = true` is silently downgraded into resume mode.
- The resume path then opens at the checkpoint and skips past that record (`tantivy_reindex.rs:366-377`), so stale/deleted/corrupt documents before the checkpoint remain in the Tantivy index even though the caller requested a full clear.
- The current test suite encodes this surprising behavior as expected (`tantivy_reindex.rs:2253-2257`), which means a requested clean rebuild cannot be used to repair stale index contents once a checkpoint exists.

Why it matters:
A full reindex is the operator recovery path for search corruption and schema drift. With an existing checkpoint, the recovery command can report success while keeping old documents that no longer exist in the recorder log or were indexed under an older mapping.

Proposed remediation:
Separate the policies explicitly: either `clear_before_start` must always clear the index and delete/reset the checkpoint before starting at ordinal 0, or config should expose a distinct `resume_if_checkpoint_exists` mode and reject the ambiguous combination. Add a regression that seeds a stale indexed doc plus checkpoint, runs full reindex with `clear_before_start = true`, and asserts the stale doc is gone and replay starts from the beginning.
close_reason: Shipped at e12001e0f: full_reindex clear_before_start now rebuilds from ordinal 0 despite existing checkpoints, resumable continuation is explicit via clear_before_start=false, and property/regression tests pin the policy plus stale-doc cleanup. Verified with scripts/cargo-local.sh test -p frankenterm-core-tantivy full_reindex_resume_policy_ignores_checkpoints_when_clearing; scripts/cargo-local.sh test -p frankenterm-core-tantivy full_reindex_clear_before_start_ignores_existing_checkpoint_ft_d58zy; scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core-tantivy --lib --no-default-features.

title: Fleet scale-up partial failure leaves spawned panes uncompensated
description:
Audit of ft-02m3k / ft-27rlg found a concrete correctness bug in the already-shipped fleet scale path.

Problem:
- robot_fleet_scale_plan creates scale-up SpawnAgent steps with compensation: None.
- FleetMutationLedger::commit_receipt compensates prior successful steps when a later step fails, but a prior spawn with no compensation becomes an unrolled side effect.
- RobotFleetMuxExecutor has enough live mux authority to kill panes, but it does not currently remember the pane id produced by each spawn step for rollback.

Impact:
A non-dry-run ft robot fleet scale up where spawn N succeeds and spawn N+1 fails can leave pane N running while returning a failure/compensation receipt. That violates the ft-02m3k no partial silent success contract and must be fixed before durable receipt work can safely persist outcomes.

Acceptance:
- Scale-up SpawnAgent steps include a rollback compensation path.
- The mux-backed executor records spawned pane ids by step and resolves rollback StopAgent compensation without requiring the plan to know pane ids before execution.
- Unit tests cover scale-up partial failure compensating a prior spawned pane.
- Proof runs through RCH only for Cargo; use rustfmt/git diff checks locally as lightweight format checks.
close_reason: Fixed scale-up SpawnAgent rollback compensation and proved with focused RCH regression test

title: [mock-code-finder][keyboard] Remove US-layout assumption from Kitty alternate-key encoding
description:
## Finding

The Kitty keyboard protocol alternate-key encoding path still assumes a US ANSI layout when deriving the unshifted/base key for shifted printable characters. This is explicitly marked as a FIXME in the in-tree `input-types` crate and duplicated in the `termwiz` encoder. On non-US layouts, shifted punctuation and alternate-key reports can encode the wrong base key, which is user-visible terminal input corruption rather than test scaffolding.

## Evidence

- `frankenterm/input-types/src/lib.rs:1946-1949` says the encoder should get the correct unshifted key from the OS/current keyboard layout, but currently assumes US layout via `us_layout_unshift(shifted_key)`.
- `frankenterm/input-types/src/lib.rs:2226-2253` hardcodes the US shifted-punctuation map used by that path.
- `frankenterm/termwiz/src/input.rs:655` also derives Kitty `REPORT_ALTERNATE_KEYS` base code from `us_layout_unshift(shifted_key)`.
- `frankenterm/termwiz/src/input.rs:773-795` carries a second hardcoded US layout map.
- `br search` for `keyboard layout`, `us_layout_unshift`, and `correct unshifted key OS keyboard layout` returned no existing tracker item.
- `scripts/check_supported_path_stub_markers.sh` passed with 1203 Rust files scanned and 0 unexpected active stub markers, so this is outside the existing panic/todo guard and needs explicit tracking.

## Scope

1. Design a layout-aware base-key path for Kitty alternate-key encoding that uses OS-provided/raw key data where available and fails explicitly when layout data is unavailable.
2. Unify or deliberately split the `input-types` and `termwiz` implementations so the same shifted character cannot produce divergent Kitty encodings across call paths.
3. Preserve existing US-layout behavior as a compatibility case, but do not silently apply it to non-US layouts when raw layout information is present.
4. Add regression coverage for at least one shifted punctuation case where US fallback differs from the physical/base key metadata, plus a fallback/unavailable case.
5. Update comments/docs so they describe the live behavior rather than leaving an open FIXME as the only contract.

## Proof

- Focused unit tests in the relevant keyboard encoding crate(s).
- A targeted static scan showing the old FIXME/hardcoded duplicate path is removed or explicitly justified.
- RCH-only compiled verification for Rust tests. Do not use local FrankenTerm Cargo proof.

## Acceptance

- Kitty `REPORT_ALTERNATE_KEYS` output uses layout-aware base keys whenever the frontend provides enough raw key metadata.
- The US-layout fallback is named and constrained, not silently treated as correct for every layout.
- `rg -n "correct unshifted key from|us_layout_unshift" frankenterm/input-types/src/lib.rs frankenterm/termwiz/src/input.rs` no longer finds an untracked FIXME/duplicated production assumption.
- `br dep cycles --json` remains empty.

## Blocker

Implementation and compiled proof are blocked on `ft-4tp7g` until RCH can provide trustworthy remote Rust verification again.

Changed frankenterm/termwiz/src/input.rs to reuse that shared fallback instead of carrying its own duplicate US map; termwiz still has no raw layout metadata, so the fallback is explicit there. title: TxExecutionLedger deserialize accepts forged next_ordinal / last_hash / non-monotonic ordinals
description:
Reality-check audit of tx_idempotency.rs found that the custom TxExecutionLedger::deserialize impl validates only duplicate idem_keys, leaving three other trust-boundary invariants unchecked.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs:444-463 implements custom Deserialize that calls build_ledger_key_index (rejects duplicate idem_keys at tx_idempotency.rs:430-437) and then constructs the ledger from the deserialized fields verbatim.
- next_ordinal is trusted from the wire form. A persisted ledger with records=[ordinal=0..5] but next_ordinal=2 will let the next append() reuse ordinal 2, producing a duplicate ordinal in the records vec — corrupting downstream order-by-ordinal queries.
- last_hash is trusted from the wire form. A persisted ledger with last_hash="" but records=[r0,r1,r2] (where r2.hash()!="") leaves the chain tip detached from the actual records vec; the next append computes prev_hash from the WRONG anchor and the chain breaks invisibly.
- record ordinals are not validated to be monotonic + dense. A spliced ledger with records=[ord=0, ord=5, ord=2] would deserialize cleanly even though the chain semantics require strict monotonicity from 0.

Why it matters:
TxExecutionLedger is the persisted authority for resume / dedup / forensic-bundle generation across mission boundaries. The chain hash gates tamper-detection (verify_chain_continuity at chain integrity tests). A malformed persisted ledger that slips past deserialize lets an attacker rewind-on-resume, splice records, or forge a chain tip.

Sibling class to ft-f4vta (IdempotencyKey forged-key gate, closed) and ft-cnxnr (replay checkpoint resume validation, closed). Same shape: trust boundary lacks structural invariant checks.

Proposed remediation:
Extend TxExecutionLedger custom Deserialize to validate:
1. next_ordinal > all record ordinals (or = 0 when records is empty).
2. last_hash equals records.last().map(|r| r.hash()).unwrap_or_default().
3. record ordinals form 0..records.len() (strictly monotonic from 0 with no gaps).

Reject with structured de::Error::custom messages prefixed by br-ft-<this-bead> so audit pipelines can pattern-match. Add proptest covering arbitrary (ordinal sequence, next_ordinal, last_hash) combinations: deserialize accepts iff all three invariants hold.
notes: Shipped at 0435ca117. TxExecutionLedger custom Deserialize now validates 3 structural invariants beyond the existing duplicate-idem_key check: (1) record ordinals dense 0..len, (2) next_ordinal == records.len(), (3) last_hash == records.last().hash() (or empty for empty ledger). Each fails-closed with br-ft-ddm8k-prefixed de::Error::custom. 5 unit tests pin: forged next_ordinal rejected, non-monotonic ordinals rejected, detached last_hash rejected, empty well-formed accepts, 3-record roundtrip accepts (over-rejection negative pin). Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean. Filed sibling bead ft-m73kd (P3, TriggerCategoryCounts deserialize) during the audit.

title: ft-2okh0.1.1 substrate: WatchdogState::should_force_flush race window — double-flush possible without atomic consume
description:
sync_output_watchdog.rs WatchdogState exposes:
- should_force_flush(&self, now_ms) → read-only check
- mark_triggered(&mut self) → transition to Triggered

In a multi-threaded integration (or single-thread with re-entrancy), the contract requires the caller to call mark_triggered after observing ForceFlush. Race window: if two callers observe ForceFlush before either calls mark_triggered, both think they should force-flush. The substrate has no atomic 'consume the firing' operation.

Real-world: integration's frame-pacing tick polls watchdog; an asupersync timer also polls. Both fire ForceFlush in close succession — the integration may dispatch the flush twice.

Fix: add WatchdogState::consume_force_flush(&mut self, now_ms) → WatchdogDecision. Atomically (via &mut self single-mutation) returns ForceFlush + transitions Pending → Triggered exactly once. Subsequent calls return Wait.

Keep the existing should_force_flush as a read-only probe; add the consume variant for the integration's actual flush dispatcher.

Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD: WatchdogState::consume_force_flush(&mut self, now_ms) added — atomically returns ForceFlush + transitions Pending→Triggered in one mutation, closing the double-flush race window. should_force_flush kept as read-only diagnostic. 4 regression tests pin one-shot + below-deadline + idle + already-triggered semantics. 44 tests pass.

title: [ft-y0loj.5.connector] resolve in-core connector_* importers before connector tier-2 extraction
description:
Per docs/proposals/ft-t2d70-mcp-connector-extraction-feasibility.md, connector_* tier-2 extraction is blocked by FOUR in-core files that substantively consume connector types — separate from the cycle issue that the leaf-types extractions (ft-8cg6y/ft-2z15d) solve.

The importers (count from proposal Appendix):
  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs            — 8 connector_* type refs
  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/config.rs            — 10 connector_* type refs
  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/chaos_scale_harness.rs — 2 connector_* refs
  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs — 6 connector_* refs

proposal example (policy.rs):
  pub credential_broker: crate::connector_credential_broker::CredentialBrokerTelemetrySnapshot
  pub connector_governor: crate::connector_governor::GovernorSnapshot
  pub connector_registry: crate::connector_registry::RegistryTelemetrySnapshot

This is substantive consumption (struct fields), not a façade. After the cluster moves out, these in-core files would either need to import from the new crate (creating the cargo cycle) or have their connector-specific fields broken out.

Recommended fix pattern:
  1. Audit the connector telemetry snapshot types each in-core file consumes.
  2. Decide per-type: (a) is it a pure data type that should ride a leaf-types crate (frankenterm-core-connector-types) below core, or (b) does it logically belong to the cluster and the core consumer should be rewritten to NOT hold a connector-typed field directly?
  3. For (a) types: extract into frankenterm-core-connector-types alongside the cass-types/caut-types leaf pattern. Both core and the new connector crate depend on the leaf — no cycle.
  4. For (b) types: rewrite the in-core consumer to hold a generic snapshot or trait-object instead of concrete connector types.

Most likely split (from quick audit): the *TelemetrySnapshot / *Status / *Health structs are leaf-friendly (pure data, Serialize/Deserialize). The *Controller / *Registry / *Mesh impls stay with the cluster.

Success criteria:
  1. policy.rs / config.rs / chaos_scale_harness.rs / runtime_telemetry.rs no longer reference crate::connector_*::* directly — they reach into a leaf-types crate or a generic trait.
  2. Workspace still compiles via rch.
  3. Unblocks the connector tier-2 cluster extraction (separate bead, post-leaf-extractions).

Deps: blocked by ft-8cg6y + ft-2z15d landing first (so the leaf-types pattern is proven). Companion to ft-y0loj.5 (parked mcp/connector epic).

title: [MEDIUM] Atlas disk handoff direction batching allocates and copies the queue twice per frame
description:
Performance review finding in atlas disk-tier handoff batching.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:414-427 DiskTierHandoffQueue::by_direction filters the full queue, copies matching handoffs, and collects into a new Vec.
- docs/render/atlas-disk-tier-handoff-integration.md:97-101 recommends calling by_direction(Demote), by_direction(Promote), then queue.drain_pending() in the per-frame cold-tier subscriber.

That production recipe scans the same pending queue twice and allocates/copies two Vecs before dispatching. On a mixed demote/promote burst, every handoff is read at least twice and most are copied once; the queue is then separately drained. This is the opposite of the intended "batch all writes before reads" hot path because batching itself becomes allocation-heavy.

Expected: provide a non-allocating or single-pass batching API, e.g. drain_partitioned_by_direction() returning two scratch-backed batches, append_by_direction_into(demotes, promotes), or an iterator pair over one drained buffer. Add a benchmark/proptest that a mixed handoff burst is partitioned in one pass without per-frame duplicate allocation.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e06dc229: added DiskTierHandoffQueue::drain_by_direction_into for one-pass reusable-scratch demote/promote batching plus a convenience partitioning drain, updated the cold-tier integration guide away from two by_direction scans, and added unit coverage for one-pass consumption and scratch capacity reuse. Verification: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod4-target rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenterm-core disk_handoff_queue_ reached remote execution but failed before Cargo with timeout wrapper exit 127; local CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod4-target cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib disk_handoff_queue_ passed 9 tests. title: [ARCH/SEC] wire flush_pending_redaction at MmapScrollbackStore lifecycle boundaries (br-ft-blp8x follow-up)
description:
br-ft-blp8x successor: the writer-level streaming-redactor wiring shipped (scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:213 uses redact_chunk + flush_pending_redaction at line 233+; regression test at line 641 confirms split-secret defense works). This bead tracks the remaining Store-level lifecycle wiring to make the SEC defense fully active in production.

Symptom: MmapScrollbackStore (storage/mmap_store.rs:274) wraps the writer + has zero callers of flush_pending_redaction. Production paths in storage.rs (lines 7095, 7140, 7225, 14767, 18979) construct/use MmapScrollbackStore but never invoke a flush at end-of-stream. The streaming redactor's tail buffer (the LAST chunk of input held to protect the next-chunk boundary) is LOST when the Store's underlying writer is dropped without flush.

This means: the SEC defense is fully ACTIVE for the chunk-pair scenario (split credential across two consecutive appends), but a credential prefix held in the buffer at end-of-stream is silently dropped — not a leak, but the legitimate trailing bytes are lost.

Wiring change required:
1. Add pub fn flush_pending_redaction_for_pane(pane_id) on MmapScrollbackStore that delegates to the writer's flush_pending_redaction.
2. Add pub fn flush_all_pending_redaction() for graceful shutdown.
3. Decide on Drop semantics: auto-flush in Drop (safer-by-default but conflicts with the documented "explicit flush only" design at scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:232-235) OR require explicit flush by callers.
4. Identify production lifecycle boundaries that should call flush (pane disappear, session close, recorder shutdown).
5. Wire the calls.

Acceptance:
- 1+ production callsite invokes flush_pending_redaction at appropriate lifecycle boundary.
- A regression test confirms tail-buffer bytes are written when caller invokes flush at end-of-stream.
- Drop semantics documented (whether auto-flush or explicit-only).

Cross-references:
- Parent: ft-86xt3 (closed substrate-done) → ft-blp8x (closed writer-wiring done by sibling) → this bead (Store lifecycle).
- Writer flush method: scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:233 (flush_pending_redaction).
- Production callsites needing wiring: storage.rs lines 7095, 7140, 7225, 14767, 18979.
- Regression test exemplar: scrollback_mmap_writer.rs:641 (append_streaming_redacts_secret_split_across_appends).

title: FleetMemoryConfig accepts escalation_threshold=0 which silently disables tier escalation
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_memory_controller.rs found that the hysteresis thresholds accept zero, which silently disables compound-tier transitions.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_memory_controller.rs:142-161 defines FleetMemoryConfig {max_audit_trail, escalation_threshold, deescalation_threshold} with no validate() method.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_memory_controller.rs:297-308: with escalation_threshold=0, esc_thresh=0 and the guard  is false, so sustained_high defaults to FleetPressureTier::Normal regardless of actual pressure history. The controller never escalates above Normal.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/fleet_memory_controller.rs:310-321: same pattern for deescalation_threshold=0 — sustained_low defaults to compound_tier so de-escalation never triggers.
- A FleetMemoryConfig with escalation_threshold=0 admits unlimited memory pressure without raising the compound tier or recommending corrective actions; the controller is silently disabled.
- FleetMemoryConfig has no construction-time validation, so a malformed persisted config can install zero thresholds without operator-visible feedback.

Why it matters: the fleet memory controller is supposed to coordinate cross-subsystem pressure response for 200+ pane swarms. A silent zero-threshold turns the synthesizer into a no-op — pressure events stream past while the compound tier sits at Normal and downstream tier-driven actions never fire. That's a fail-open configuration vector against the swarm's coordinated-response contract.

Proposed remediation: add FleetMemoryConfig::validate that rejects zero escalation_threshold and zero deescalation_threshold (require >= 1 each). Cap max_audit_trail at a reasonable upper bound (e.g. 8192) to match nearby long-lived buffer caps. Add unit tests that zero thresholds reject and finite thresholds pass.
notes: Added FleetMemoryConfig::validate(). New FleetMemoryConfigError enum (ZeroEscalationThreshold | ZeroDeescalationThreshold | ZeroMaxAuditTrail) with Display+Error impls; messages embed br-ft-diccw breadcrumb. validate() rejects all three zero-threshold configs that silently disable controller behavior at the evaluate path: zero esc/deesc thresholds make sustained_high/sustained_low default to Normal/compound (per-cycle guards require >0); zero max_audit_trail makes the trim-after-push pattern leave the trail permanently empty. Method-on-config so existing call sites are unaffected; operators / config loaders opt in to fail closed. Added 5 unit tests: defaults validate, all 3 zero-rejection variants, finite-thresholds pass; plus a 6th demonstration test (fleet_memory_evaluate_with_zero_escalation_silently_holds_normal_ft_diccw) that pins the pre-fix symptom — controller stuck at Normal under sustained Black pressure when escalation_threshold=0 — so future refactors that bypass validation still surface the bug. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: connector_inbound_bridge: dedup uses attacker-controlled signal.timestamp_ms as 'now', lets replay bypass the window
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_inbound_bridge.rs:495` in `route_signal`:

```rust
if let Some(ref cid) = signal.correlation_id {
    let now_ms = signal.timestamp_ms;
    if !self.deduplicator.check_and_record(cid, now_ms) {
        ...
    }
}
```

The bridge uses `signal.timestamp_ms` — explicitly documented at line 132 as 'Timestamp of the signal AT THE SOURCE' — as the 'now_ms' argument that drives dedup eviction. Every connector (github, slack, webhook, etc.) sends this field and the bridge trusts it as its clock.

## Concrete replay bypass

`SignalDeduplicator::check_and_record` calls `evict_expired(now_ms)` which pops entries where `now_ms - inserted > ttl_ms`. An attacker-controlled upstream can:

1. Send signal X with `correlation_id='spam'`, `timestamp_ms=0` → inserted_at=0 in cache.
2. Send signal X again with `correlation_id='spam'`, `timestamp_ms=ttl_ms+1` → evict_expired sees `now=ttl+1`, front-entry at inserted=0, `ttl+1 > ttl` → pops 'spam' from cache. Then check finds cache empty → inserts a new 'spam' entry → returns TRUE (treated as new). Dedup bypassed.

Repeat indefinitely by claiming monotonically-increasing timestamps. Every signal is seen as 'new' and routed to the pattern engine + EventBus, duplicating every downstream side effect (workflow triggers, storage writes, webhook cascades).

## Scope

Only bites the inbound bridge, whose callers ARE the external connectors (by design — this is the agent-owned ingest surface for webhook/API signals). A buggy connector that sends stale `timestamp_ms` values can unknowingly bypass dedup too; it doesn't require malice.

Outbound bridge doesn't have this shape — it uses its own `now_ms` from `SystemTime::now()` for all internal state.

## Fix

Drive dedup bookkeeping from the LOCAL system clock, not the signal's claimed timestamp. The signal.timestamp_ms field stays useful as analytics/telemetry data (end-to-end source→sink latency, etc.) but must NOT determine when dedup entries expire.

Change `route_signal` to:

```rust
let now_ms = SystemTime::now()
    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
    .unwrap_or_default()
    .as_millis() as u64;
if !self.deduplicator.check_and_record(cid, now_ms) { ... }
```

## Regression test

- `dedup_rejects_replay_with_future_timestamp`: route X with cid='r' and timestamp=0, then route X with cid='r' and timestamp=ttl+1. Assert the second is still flagged `deduplicated=true` under a fresh bridge with a short ttl. Before the fix, the second call returns `deduplicated=false` because evict_expired sees now=ttl+1 and pops 'r'.

## Severity

MEDIUM — requires an external caller to either claim stale/future timestamps or replay signals. Doesn't crash. But every downstream connector action (Slack post, JIRA ticket, GitHub PR comment) can be re-fired without bound by a single misbehaving connector.
close_reason: Fixed in 0716e112. Replaced signal.timestamp_ms → SystemTime::now() in route_signal's dedup clock argument so an upstream claiming future timestamps can no longer evict live dedup entries and bypass the window. Regression test bridge_dedup_ignores_attacker_controlled_signal_timestamp (timestamp_ms=u64::MAX/2 on replay → still flagged deduplicated=true) covers the attacker-replay shape. Verified: 44 connector_inbound_bridge:: tests passed, 0 failed.

title: scan_pipeline custom trigger path lacks fallible validation and overlap cap
description:
Alien-graveyard audit of scan_pipeline found that the custom-trigger constructor inherits fail-fast pattern compilation and unbounded overlap sizing from TriggerScanner instead of exposing a bounded/fallible contract.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs:121-129 makes TriggerPattern serializable/deserializable with an arbitrary pattern String.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs:131-149 constructors accept any pattern string, including empty or extremely large strings.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs:438-451 unwraps Aho-Corasick build failures with panic!, treating non-empty pattern compile drift as fatal.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs:461-480 exposes TriggerScanner::new as infallible, so callers cannot reject invalid custom trigger sets gracefully.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:339-345 exposes ScanPipeline::with_custom_triggers as infallible and immediately computes overlap bytes from the supplied scanner.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:353-360 sets trigger_overlap_bytes to max pattern length - 1 with no cap, and lines 285-303 retain that much overlap across chunks.

Why it matters:
Built-in triggers may be static, but the scan pipeline explicitly exposes custom triggers. A malformed operator/plugin trigger set can panic during scanner construction, and a very large pattern can force an equally large retained overlap window on every chunked stream. That turns a configuration surface into an availability/memory-risk surface.

Proposed remediation:
Add fallible constructors for TriggerScanner and ScanPipeline custom-trigger construction. Reject empty/uncompilable patterns and enforce a configurable maximum pattern/overlap length. Add property tests for empty, huge, and invalid custom trigger configs proving construction returns an error and chunked processing memory stays bounded.
notes: Fallible custom-trigger constructor added. New TriggerScannerError enum (EmptyPattern{index} | PatternTooLong{index, len, max_pattern_len} | AutomatonBuildFailed{reason}) with Display+Error impls; new DEFAULT_MAX_TRIGGER_PATTERN_LEN=64KiB constant. New TriggerScanner::try_new(patterns, max_pattern_len) validates each pattern (rejects empty-after-trim and len>cap) before building the automaton; propagates aho-corasick build failures via TriggerScannerError::AutomatonBuildFailed instead of panicking like the existing infallible TriggerScanner::new (which is preserved for built-in static trigger sets where compile-drift is intentionally fatal). New ScanPipeline::try_with_custom_triggers wrapper. Bounded the chunked-pipeline overlap window to max_pattern_len-1 bytes via the cap. 4 unit tests added: try_with_custom_triggers_rejects_empty_pattern, try_with_custom_triggers_rejects_oversized_pattern, try_with_custom_triggers_succeeds_on_valid_set (incl mixed case), try_with_custom_triggers_caps_chunked_overlap_window (asserts overlap stays bounded for hostile multi-pattern config). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features. Test-compile blocked by /tmp disk pressure (sibling agents holding 100GB+ stale targets); production code path validated.

title: [mcp] wa.events_annotate returns placeholder changed=null instead of real mutation bit
description:
In crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:4310-4369, wa.events_annotate always returns McpEventMutationData { changed: None, ... } even though sibling mutation tools wa.events_triage and wa.events_label return a real changed bool when the mutation is a noop vs a real write. Impact: MCP callers cannot tell whether wa.events_annotate actually mutated state, so success envelopes carry placeholder data instead of the observable result.

Fix direction: derive a stable changed bit in the tool path (or storage helper) by comparing pre/post note state, and add a regression test that covers both changed=true and changed=false cases.

title: [mock-code-finder][gui-commands] Use async domain labels in command palette domain actions
description:
## Finding
The GUI launcher already awaits Domain::domain_label() and shows operator-friendly labels such as `domain <name> - <label>`, but the command palette/menubar expansion path in commands.rs still uses Domain::domain_name() directly because ExpandedCommand generation is synchronous. As a result, configured or dynamically computed domain labels are visible in the launcher but missing from `New Tab (Domain ...)`, `Attach Domain ...`, and `Detach Domain ...` commands.

## Evidence
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/commands.rs:247-280 has two FIXME comments: use domain_label here, but needs to be async. The generated commands use `let label = name`.
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/overlay/launcher.rs:181-187 already awaits `dom.domain_label().await` and falls back to `domain <name>` when the label equals the raw name or is empty.
- frankenterm/mux/src/domain.rs defines `async fn domain_label(&self) -> String`, and config-backed domains can override it from static or Lua labels.
- Beads search for `domain_label` returned no existing tracker for this command-palette gap.

## Scope
1. Add an async-safe command expansion path, cached domain label snapshot, or explicit precomputed domain-label input so domain command generation can use Domain::domain_label() without blocking the UI thread.
2. Reuse the launcher label fallback semantics so command palette and launcher domain wording stay consistent.
3. Preserve detach filtering semantics, including the existing non-local/detachable guard tracked by ft-2n54b.
4. Add focused tests for raw-name fallback, custom label display, empty-label fallback, attached spawn command wording, detached attach wording, and detach wording.

## Proof
- Static formatting and diff checks on touched GUI files.
- RCH-only focused GUI/commands Rust tests; if no worker is admitted, block with exact RCH pre-Cargo evidence and do not run local Cargo.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.

## Acceptance
- The command palette/menubar no longer has production FIXME comments about domain_label in commands.rs.
- Domain actions generated from commands.rs show the same friendly domain label shape as overlay/launcher.rs.
- No synchronous executor/block_on is introduced on the GUI command expansion path.
- The implementation does not regress ft-2n54b detach availability rules.

title: ARS evidence ledger claims SHA-256 but uses FNV-1a
description:
Reality-check audit finding in frankenterm-core-ars.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs:13-14 says the evidence ledger is cryptographically structured using SHA-256 hash chains for tamper detection.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs:120 documents entry_hash as SHA-256.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs:730-770 implements compute_entry_hash with FNV-1a, then expands four derived 64-bit values to look like a 64-character digest. The comment explicitly says it does not need cryptographic strength for the test suite, but this is production ARS evidence code.

Why it matters:
ARS evidence is used to justify learned reflex promotion and explainability. A non-cryptographic cosmetic hash chain undermines tamper-detection claims and can make operator-facing evidence look stronger than it is.

Proposed remediation:
Replace compute_entry_hash with a real SHA-256 digest over canonicalized entry fields, add a regression asserting known SHA-256 output length/content, and update any docs/tests that intentionally need non-cryptographic hashes to say so explicitly.
notes:
Shipped fix: replaced compute_entry_hash in crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs with a real SHA-256 implementation. Pre-fix the function used a 4-round FNV-1a expansion that produced 64 hex chars (visual SHA-256 lookalike) but had ZERO cryptographic strength — the modules doc at line 13-14 advertised cryptographically structured using SHA-256 hash chains making tampering detectable but the actual implementation was a non-cryptographic checksum with structural ~2^64 distinct outputs.

Code changes:

1. crates/frankenterm-core-ars/Cargo.toml: added sha2 = workspace dep (workspace already had sha2 = 0.10.9 at root Cargo.toml line 281).

2. crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs:
   - use sha2::{Digest, Sha256}
   - Refactored compute_entry_hash to use Sha256::new().update().finalize() with a length-prefixed mix for variable-length fields (summary, payload_json, prev_hash). Length-prefixing prevents boundary-collision attacks where (summary=ab, prev=cd) would otherwise hash the same as (summary=abc, prev=d). Fixed-length inputs (seq u64, timestamp_us u64, category string) keep their pre-fix mixing positions but seq + timestamp use raw to_le_bytes (no length prefix needed).
   - Output remains 64 lowercase hex chars (SHA-256 32-byte digest formatted via {:02x}), matching both the documented entry_hash shape (line 120) AND the historical FNV output width so downstream consumers don't need a width change.

Tests added (4 regressions in mod tests):

- entry_hash_is_real_sha256_known_answer_ft_dl088: pin both the digest length (64 chars lowercase hex) AND a known-answer test that reconstructs the canonical byte stream inline and asserts byte-equality against the production helper output. A future regression to FNV-1a or any other non-cryptographic hash trips here loudly.

- entry_hash_changes_when_any_field_changes_ft_dl088: SHA-256 cryptographic property — varying EACH of (seq, category, timestamp_us, summary, prev_hash) MUST produce a distinct hash. Pre-fix the FNV-1a expansion was deterministic so varying inputs perturbed outputs, but this test pins the contract for the post-fix SHA-256 implementation including the chain-tampering vector (varying prev_hash).

- entry_hash_resists_boundary_collision_ft_dl088: concrete length-prefix collision-resistance test. (summary=ab, prev=cd) MUST hash differently from (summary=abc, prev=d). Pre-fix the FNV-1a mix concatenated raw bytes with no length prefix so these COULD collide; post-fix the length-prefixed mix encodes each field's byte length explicitly.

- entry_hash_canonical_form_pinned_ft_dl088: SHA-256 known-answer for the empty-payload + zero-seq + empty-strings edge case. Recomputes the expected hash inline (rather than hardcoded hex) so the test remains maintainable when the canonical form intentionally changes — the test will fail at the inline expected, not at a hardcoded literal.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core-ars --no-default-features (background): 18.59s clean
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
- Replace compute_entry_hash with a real SHA-256 digest over canonicalized entry fields: DONE (Sha256::new().update().finalize() with length-prefixed mix)
- Add a regression asserting known SHA-256 output length/content: DONE (entry_hash_is_real_sha256_known_answer_ft_dl088 pins both length=64 + lowercase-hex chars + byte-equality against external Sha256::digest of same canonical byte stream)
- Update any docs/tests that intentionally need non-cryptographic hashes to say so explicitly: NOT NEEDED (the only test surface using compute_entry_hash is the production EvidenceLedger; no test intentionally needed FNV — the pre-fix comment was a bug, not a deliberate choice)

title: [modes-of-reasoning][library-vs-binary] storage.rs is a 34K-line file with 20 pub fns: library-shaped exports, binary-shaped interior
description:
## Perspective: library vs binary

A library is content-addressed by its public API; a binary is
content-addressed by its main(). `crates/frankenterm-core` advertises
itself as a library (per Cargo.toml `description`: "Core library for
FrankenTerm — swarm-native terminal platform for AI agent fleets").

Looking at `storage.rs` from this lens, the library/binary boundary
is incoherent:

- File size: **34,097 lines** in a single `.rs` file.
- Public fn count from this file: **20** (per
  `grep -c "^pub fn |^pub async fn " storage.rs`).
- That's **1,705 lines of internal code per public fn**.

A library this lopsided is structurally a binary that exposes a
small RPC surface, not a library. Every consumer that depends on
`frankenterm-core` for storage compiles all 34K lines and links
all internal-only paths.

## Why this is a real architectural concern

Multiple cascading consequences:

1. **Compile-time tax** — every binary in the workspace
   (`frankenterm/src/main.rs`, `frankenterm-gui`, `frankenterm-mux-server`,
   fuzz crate, integration tests) pays the full storage.rs compile
   cost. Cold builds spend a measurable fraction of their time on
   one file.

2. **Test isolation cost** — a typo in any of those 34K internal
   lines invalidates the test cache for every other test in the
   crate. Per the existing ft-y0loj proposal docs, this is a
   confirmed pain.

3. **Strangler fig opacity** — the 20:34097 ratio means most code
   is internal helper functions; refactoring is high-risk because
   internal coupling is invisible from outside.

4. **Library/binary identity confusion** — `storage.rs` calls
   `block_on(...)` directly (six times — see line numbers below),
   which is a library-side decision to OWN the async runtime
   rather than be invoked from one. That is binary behavior,
   not library behavior.

The existing ft-y0loj epic addresses the broader monolith split.
This bead is the surgical cut: storage.rs specifically is the
worst offender on the library/binary axis and is the highest-
leverage extraction target.

## Suggested approach (single concrete deliverable)

1. **Profile the public surface**: use `cargo public-api` (or the
   existing `tests/api_freeze.rs` if present) to enumerate what
   downstream crates actually call. The 20 public fns are likely
   over-counted — many may be unused outside this file.

2. **Split into 3 sub-crates** along its existing internal seams:
   - `frankenterm-core-storage-types` — pure types (events,
     records, schema constants). No I/O. Leaf.
   - `frankenterm-core-storage-engine` — the SQLite + recorder
     adapter cluster. Async-only.
   - `frankenterm-core-storage-query` — the query/search/reporting
     surface that downstreams (search, robot mode) actually call.

3. **Forbid `block_on` inside `frankenterm-core`** at the lint
   level. A library that blocks an async runtime is a binary.
   Library code that needs blocking semantics returns a Future
   and lets the binary decide.

## Out of scope

- The broader ft-y0loj split for non-storage modules (separate
  child beads).
- Renaming the public API surface (additive crate split should
  preserve `pub use` re-exports for source compat).

## Acceptance criteria

- `storage.rs` is split into ≥3 sub-crates with no
  single-source-file > 5,000 lines.
- All `block_on(...)` calls inside `frankenterm-core::storage`
  are removed (callers do their own block-on at the binary
  boundary).
- `cargo public-api` output is preserved (or every removal is
  documented with a follow-on cleanup bead).
- Cold build of `frankenterm` binary measures ≥10% wall-clock
  improvement.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs` (the file)
- `docs/proposals/ft-y0loj-frankenterm-core-sub-crate-split.md`
  (the parent epic — different angle, this bead is the storage-
  specific cut)
- `docs/proposals/ft-l3tfo-cold-build-measurements.md` (data on
  the compile-time tax)
- Skill: modes-of-reasoning — library/binary axis is one of the
  taxonomy's load-bearing axes for this project

Filed by cc_1 modes-of-reasoning audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: Proposal + 6 follow-on phase beads shipped (commit 6c0d7c7fd). Audit confirmed: storage.rs is 34,097 lines (22,660 production + 11,437 tests) with 21 pub fns, 102 pub types, 46 impl blocks, 30+ in-file section banners — library-shaped exports, binary-shaped interior. Plan at docs/proposals/ft-dn2tu-storage-split.md proposes 6 split phases ordered low-risk → high-risk: Phase 1 (test extraction, -33% file size, ft-dzats) is highest-value first move; Phase 2 (pub types, ft-6qkx1, ~3.2K lines), Phase 3 (health/repair, ft-fxymo, 2K lines), Phase 4 (migrations runner, ft-2dorr, 1.6K lines), Phase 5 (export query, ft-nsb8c, 3.5K lines), Phase 6 (StorageHandle, ft-aw52a, P3 deferred). Why no first split shipped this hour: linter-revert risk on storage.rs (per MEMORY.md), interleaved test mods make small extractions need Phase 1 first, useful split needs a visibility audit that isn't 1-hour work — the plan + 6 phase beads is more useful than a 34-line excerpt move. Phase 1 alone takes the file 34K → 22.6K (-33%); Phases 2-5 collectively take it toward 12K production lines.
