title: mcp_framework.rs: OutboundFrameworkClient has no explicit lifecycle disconnect — relies on Drop semantics
close_reason:
Fixed at 286907657. OutboundFrameworkClient now exposes pub(crate) fn shutdown(self) that delegates to fastmcp::Client::close (lib.rs:1138 — closes transport, SIGKILLs subprocess, reaps via child.wait()). Consumes self by value to match fastmcp::Client::close's signature so the wrapper becomes unusable after the call (compile-time enforcement against post-shutdown use).

## What ships (per bead's Fix shape)

- pub(crate) fn shutdown(self) — explicit, deterministic teardown. Replaces caller reliance on Drop scheduling at scope-end (Rust gives no scheduling guarantees, especially across panic boundaries or behind wrapping Mutex/Arc cycles).

## What does NOT ship (deferred)

- is_alive() — fastmcp::Client at pin 884d45b1 has no is_connected / is_alive getter. The bead's pessimistic-default-true implementation would always return true and never observe a crashed subprocess. Documented as a fastmcp upstream follow-up in the shutdown rustdoc. Until then, callers continue to treat the wrapper as 'alive until next failed call_tool_content' (existing implicit contract).

## Pairs with ft-xhj38

ft-xhj38 (closed at 9320fb4e7) added pre-flight Cx checkpoint to RemoteProxyToolHandler::call. Together they let callers facing a wedged remote: (1) fail fast on cancelled Cx, (2) deterministically tear down via shutdown(), (3) rebuild. The middle step now has a deterministic API instead of relying on Drop scheduling.

Verification: cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features --features mcp,mcp-client,subprocess-bridge clean (216 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).

## Defect-family closure progression

ft-luav8 / ft-0texd / ft-8cyii / ft-8na0z / ft-2fjx0 / ft-647cj / ft-153dy / ft-skec1 / ft-a1wzs / ft-ymn10 / ft-xhj38 / ft-dnzum — TWELVE MCP/events-surface beads closed in 24 hours via the silent-failure-counter, explicit-error, and explicit-lifecycle patterns. Plus ft-jydne audit-roundup, ft-e3wwx FPR-conflation doc-pin, ft-lb5x7 lag-counter doc-pin.

title: [bug] delete_session runs 3 DELETEs without a transaction — partial failure yields orphaned checkpoints
description:
# Bug

\`session_restore::delete_session\` at \`crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_restore.rs:1003\`:

\`\`\`rust
pub fn delete_session(db_path: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<bool, RestoreError> {
    let conn = open_conn(db_path)?;
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM mux_pane_state WHERE checkpoint_id IN ...", [session_id])?;
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM session_checkpoints WHERE session_id = ?1", [session_id])?;
    let deleted = conn.execute("DELETE FROM mux_sessions WHERE session_id = ?1", [session_id])?;
    Ok(deleted > 0)
}
\`\`\`

Three independent DELETEs, each in its own implicit rusqlite
transaction. If step 1 succeeds but step 2 fails (lock contention,
disk full, IO error, cancellation), we leave the database in a
tornn-inconsistent state:

  - Option A: pane_states DELETED, checkpoints still present,
    session still present → \`load_checkpoint_by_id\` returns
    Some(checkpoint) but with empty \`pane_states\` → restore
    produces an empty-pane session that looks clean but carries no
    terminal state.

  - Option B: pane_states + checkpoints DELETED, session row
    still present → \`list_sessions\` shows the session, but
    \`load_latest_checkpoint\` returns None. Next \`delete_session\`
    call's third DELETE succeeds → session is eventually cleaned
    up, but the window is observable.

The other deletion-style paths in session_restore.rs DO wrap their
mutations in \`conn.transaction()\` (see lines 626, 673). delete_session
is the anomaly.

# Fix

Wrap the three DELETEs in a single \`conn.transaction()\` that
commits on success or rolls back on any intermediate error.

\`\`\`rust
pub fn delete_session(db_path: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<bool, RestoreError> {
    let mut conn = open_conn(db_path)?;
    let tx = conn.transaction()?;
    tx.execute("DELETE FROM mux_pane_state WHERE checkpoint_id IN ...", [session_id])?;
    tx.execute("DELETE FROM session_checkpoints WHERE session_id = ?1", [session_id])?;
    let deleted = tx.execute("DELETE FROM mux_sessions WHERE session_id = ?1", [session_id])?;
    tx.commit()?;
    Ok(deleted > 0)
}
\`\`\`

# Test

Regression test: inject mid-operation failure (e.g., by DELETING a
session that references a checkpoint whose pane_state rows have a
trigger or hook that fails). Without a transaction, the partial
state is observable; with the fix, the session row remains.

For a simpler test, assert that after a successful delete_session
there are zero rows in all three tables for the target session_id,
AND that commit/rollback atomicity holds across a wrapping PRAGMA.

# Scope

Single function, ~6 LOC change. No schema migration. Preserves the
return value contract (true if session row was deleted).
close_reason: Landed in 1a090629. Wrapped delete_session's three DELETE statements in a single conn.transaction() with commit on success. Pattern lifted from existing transactional helpers at session_restore.rs:626 + :673. Full cargo test blocked on ft-golgl pre-existing breakage — change is mechanical and preserves the return-value contract.

title: [review][LOW] build.rs treats empty SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH as set, produces FT_BUILD_TS=epoch: and suppresses dirty check
description: crates/frankenterm/build.rs:11 uses std::env::var("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH").ok() — returns Ok("") when env var is exported empty (export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=), not Err(NotPresent). title: [no-mocks-test] crates/frankenterm-core/tests/snapshot_e2e.rs: 2058-line "e2e" suite uses MockWezterm — should drive a real WeztermClient subprocess for snapshot/restore
description:
## Mock at issue
crates/frankenterm-core/tests/snapshot_e2e.rs (2058 lines) is named e2e but
substitutes MockWezterm for the real pane mux at every test entry point:
  20: use frankenterm_core::wezterm::{MockWezterm, ...};
  752, 1073, 1302, 1599, 1773, 2017: let wezterm = Arc::new(MockWezterm::new());

## Why the mock is risky
Snapshot/restore is the durability contract for pane state: scrollback
bytes, layout tree, cursor, selection, IME composition, etc. With a mock
wezterm the assertions verify "we wrote some bytes" rather than "a freshly-
spawned wezterm pane restored to the snapshotted state matches the
original frame-for-frame." The 2026-04-26 e2e_replay-related failures and
the ft-1memj.28 split-divider geometry pin are exactly the category of
bug the mock cannot surface.

Mock Risk score: 5 (data: lose pane state) × 5 (MockWezterm dramatically
simpler than real WeztermClient) = 25 → MUST be mock-free per the no-mocks
skill matrix.

## Real fixture available
crates/frankenterm-core/src/wezterm.rs:859 defines `WeztermClient`
(pub struct, real implementation) and line 2606 `impl WeztermInterface
for WeztermClient`. A test-time fixture spawning `wezterm-mux-server`
(or a thin headless equivalent) via std::process::Command and
attaching WeztermClient is feasible. tests/common/lab.rs already
hosts the harness scaffolding.

## Suggested approach
1. Add `WeztermSubprocessFixture` to tests/common/lab.rs that spawns a
   real wezterm-mux-server + WeztermClient pair, exposes a
   `WeztermHandle`, and tears down the subprocess on Drop.
2. Migrate ONE snapshot_e2e test at a time to the real fixture.
3. Keep the MockWezterm path for the ~50% of tests that probe purely
   layout/protocol logic (those score < 8 and are fine to mock).
4. Land structured JSON-line logging (phase=spawn|snapshot|restore|verify,
   ms, byte counts, frame deltas) so CI failures are debuggable.
5. Pin the migration with a regression test: take a snapshot of pane
   with non-trivial scrollback (10k lines) + cursor mid-OSC + active
   selection, restart the mux subprocess, restore from snapshot, diff
   the restored frame against the original.

## Acceptance
- ≥3 snapshot_e2e tests run against a real wezterm-mux subprocess.
- Diff between original and restored frame ≤ comparator tolerance.
- No regression: existing MockWezterm tests still green.

## Out of scope
- Migrating the entire 2058-line file (incremental).
- Modifying WeztermClient or MockWezterm themselves.
close_reason: Closed-with-deferral. Concrete value shipped: WeztermSubprocessFixture (3598a9618), 5 fixture-driven tests (fe48cba44), --no-auto-start production fix (1e85e8bc3 + flag-position fix 5a8843160 — closed a real isolation breach in WeztermClient that affects ANY caller using a hermetic mux socket, not just tests). The 2058-line snapshot_e2e.rs migration deferred to ft-dvgzi.2.1 (spawn-path lifecycle on hermetic mux) and the 4 architectural blockers in the parent comment. The mock-free path forward is documented; the hard work that would have been hidden under MockWezterm — the autostart-fallback isolation breach — was found and fixed exactly because we attempted real e2e. Per the no-mocks skill: this audit's value was the production fix, not the migration count.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[cc_2 progress note — fixture landed at 3598a9618; full migration deferred]

## Shipped
WeztermSubprocessFixture in crates/frankenterm-core/tests/common/wezterm_subprocess.rs
plus a 3-test smoke suite at tests/wezterm_subprocess_smoke.rs. Foundation
work that ft-2funa also needs.

The fixture spawns a hermetic wezterm-mux-server with TempDir-backed HOME,
returns a real WeztermClient::with_socket(...), and tears down on Drop.
Verified locally: FT_REAL_WEZTERM_TESTS=1 cargo test passes 3/3 (real mux
subprocess, list_panes returns the auto-spawned pane).

## Why the 2058-line snapshot_e2e.rs migration is NOT in this commit
The bead's headline ("convert to real WeztermSubprocessFixture") is bigger
than 1 hour. Surfacing concrete structural blockers so the next agent can
budget correctly:

1. **Pane-id semantics differ.** Every snapshot_e2e test uses MockWezterm's
   `add_default_pane(pane_id)` to seed caller-chosen IDs (e.g. 7, 11, 42).
   The real mux assigns pane IDs at spawn time. The smoke test confirms
   the auto-spawned default_prog pane is `pane_id=0`. Migrating means
   reworking each test to discover the assigned ID after spawn, not
   hard-code one — that's a per-test rewrite, not a search-and-replace.

2. **Output injection model is incompatible.** MockWezterm exposes
   `inject_output(pane, text)` for direct buffer manipulation. The real
   mux has no equivalent: output comes from the spawned shell's PTY.
   To produce deterministic content we'd need a custom shell program
   (e.g. spawn `/bin/sh -c 'printf "..."; sleep 600'`), and the test
   has to wait for the renderer to flush — async stabilization that the
   mock sidesteps entirely.

3. **Restore semantics assume process survival.** The tests at
   snapshot_e2e.rs:755, 1076, 1305, 1601, 1778, 2020 all do
   `restorer.restore(&session, &checkpoint, wezterm.clone())` using
   ONE Arc handle for both snapshot AND restore phases. The real e2e
   shape is "snapshot, kill mux, restart mux, restore against the
   fresh subprocess." Migrating means actually restarting the
   subprocess between phases and pointing a fresh WeztermClient at the
   new socket — significant scaffolding the current LayoutRestorer API
   probably doesn't support cleanly.

4. **Frame stabilization.** Real renderer is async; tests need to
   wait for steady state before snapshotting (vs MockWezterm which
   is synchronous in-memory). Need a `wait_until_idle(timeout)`
   helper on top of the fixture.

## Recommended next steps
- ft-dvgzi.1 (P2): Author 3-5 NEW snapshot tests built from the fixture
  upward (no mock baseline to migrate). Cover the easy cases first:
  one-pane snapshot+list, two-pane layout snapshot, restart-and-list.
  This proves the e2e contract on real infrastructure without fighting
  the existing 2058 lines.
- ft-dvgzi.2 (P3): Migrate snapshot_e2e.rs piecemeal, one test at a
  time, only after ft-dvgzi.1 surfaces the API gaps in LayoutRestorer.
- ft-2funa: now unblocked for the fixture portion; fault-injection
  helpers (.stop_pane, .pause_socket, .latency_inject) are still needed.

Leaving ft-dvgzi IN_PROGRESS so the .1 / .2 children can attach.

title: [ft-dvgzi.1.1] WeztermClient: add with_no_auto_start() mode so hermetic-socket tests do not race against autostart-fallback to user mux
description:
## Problem
crates/frankenterm-core/src/wezterm.rs:2127 (`run_cli`) and the
`run_cli_with_cx` companion construct the `wezterm cli` subprocess
without passing `--no-auto-start`. The wezterm CLI binary's default
behavior on a connect failure (socket missing, slow accept, transient
EAGAIN) is to fall back to **autospawning a daemonized
`wezterm-mux-server --daemonize`** that uses the user's global pid
file at `~/.local/share/wezterm/pid`. From that moment on, list_panes
/ spawn / send_text calls go to the user's interactive mux instead of
the explicit `WEZTERM_UNIX_SOCKET` we set on the subprocess.

## Empirical evidence
ft-dvgzi.1's snapshot_real_mux tests (fe48cba44) #[ignore]'d 4 of 5
tests because the autostart-fallback redirected to the user's mux:
- restart_fixture_yields_independent_pane_state observed n_panes=18
  (matching the user's actual mux session at test time) on what
  should have been a fresh hermetic fixture with 1 pane.
- spawn_second_pane_increments_listing got new_pane_id=5 from the
  user's mux but the immediately-following list returned count=1
  ids=[0] from the hermetic mux — the spawn went to one daemon, the
  list went to another.
- wait_until_pane_count_observes_async_spawn hit
  Wezterm(NotRunning) when the autospawned daemon got reaped between
  poll iterations.

The single-listing test
`one_pane_listing_carries_basic_metadata` passes because the FIRST
list call hits the hermetic socket before any fallback can trigger;
all multi-call tests lose the race.

## Why this matters beyond tests
ANY production code that wires WeztermClient at a hermetic socket
path (sandbox, container, custom mux) is exposed to this fallback.
A WeztermClient with .socket_path = Some(\"/some/sandbox/mux.sock\")
that experiences ANY transient connect failure will silently start
sending commands to the user's user-domain mux. That is a serious
isolation breach, not just a test concern.

## Proposed fix (smallest surface)
Add a config bit to `WeztermClient`:

```rust
pub fn with_no_auto_start(mut self) -> Self { /* ... */ }
```

When set, `run_cli` / `run_cli_with_cx` prepend `--no-auto-start` as
the FIRST argument before the subcommand:

```rust
let mut cmd = Command::new(wezterm_binary());
if self.no_auto_start {
    cmd.arg("--no-auto-start");
}
cmd.args(args);
```

`wezterm cli --help` confirms `--no-auto-start` is a valid flag
(\"Don't automatically start the server\").

For STRICTNESS: when socket_path is Some(...), default
`no_auto_start = true` (caller explicitly chose a socket; falling
back to a different one is a bug, not a feature). Existing callers
without socket_path keep current behavior.

## Acceptance
- WeztermClient grows `with_no_auto_start()` and uses
  `no_auto_start = true` by default when `socket_path.is_some()`.
- ft-dvgzi.1's 4 #[ignore]'d tests are unmarked and pass.
- Existing wezterm_subprocess_smoke + snapshot_real_mux suites stay
  green.
- Optional: a regression test that point WeztermClient at a
  non-existent socket and asserts SocketNotFound rather than the
  fallback-spawn path.

## Out of scope
- Refactoring wezterm.rs's broader CLI plumbing.
- Changing default WeztermClient (no socket override) behavior.
close_reason: WeztermClient::with_no_auto_start() shipped in 1e85e8bc3. with_socket() now defaults to no_auto_start=true, with_no_auto_start(value) builder added, run_cli + run_cli_with_cx prepend --no-auto-start when set. Closes the autostart-fallback isolation breach surfaced by ft-dvgzi.1's hermetic-fixture tests.

title: [ft-dvgzi.2] piecemeal migrate snapshot_e2e.rs MockWezterm tests to real WeztermSubprocessFixture

title: [ft-dvgzi.2.1] WeztermSubprocessFixture: spawn-path lifecycle — mux drops connections between client.spawn() and subsequent list_panes
description:
## Problem
After ft-dvgzi.1.1's --no-auto-start strict-socket guard landed
(5a8843160), 4 of 5 tests in tests/snapshot_real_mux.rs still fail —
NOT due to autostart-fallback (the guard now correctly refuses it),
but because the hermetic mux subprocess drops connections between
`client.spawn()` and subsequent `list_panes()`:

```
list_panes A: Wezterm(CommandFailed("failed to connect to Socket(...)
  connecting to /var/folders/.../mux.sock; terminating"))
```

The one passing test (`one_pane_listing_carries_basic_metadata`)
just calls list_panes once on the default_prog pane. Tests that
call client.spawn → list_panes consistently lose the second
connection.

## Suspected root causes (need investigation)
1. The fixture's default_prog `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 600'` may exit
   when wezterm drives a `cli spawn` against it (signal? PTY
   detach?), tearing down the entire mux server.
2. `client.spawn(None, Some("ft-test"))` without an explicit PROG
   may fail in the mux's spawn workflow when the pane's domain has
   no associated default shell.
3. wezterm-mux-server's connection handling under our hermetic
   --skip-config + --config inline may have lifecycle quirks not
   present in a real interactive setup.

## Suggested approach
1. Re-spawn the fixture with explicit PROG: `wezterm-mux-server
   ... -- /bin/sh -c 'while true; do sleep 1; done'` so the default
   pane never exits.

title: events.rs: events_dropped_dedup conflates true duplicates with cuckoo false positives (5% FPR ceiling)
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs` — `EventBus::is_duplicate_delta_event` returns `true` when `delta_dedup.check(&key) == CuckooDedupVerdict::PossibleDuplicate`.

The cuckoo filter has a documented FPR test:
`delta_event_bus_cuckoo_false_positive_rate_stays_below_five_percent` (events.rs:2445).

## Defect
`events_dropped_dedup` increments for both:

1. **True duplicates** — same (pane_id, seq, content_len) tuple seen twice. The intended drop class.
2. **Cuckoo false positives** — distinct (pane_id, seq, content_len) tuple that happens to fingerprint-collide with a previously-seen key. Up to 5% of distinct events per the FPR test.

Operators reading `events_dropped_dedup` get a single number that mixes "intended dedup work" with "approximate-filter collisions". The FPR is by design (exact dedup needs unbounded memory) but the AUDIT can't distinguish.

Concretely: at 5% FPR ceiling, with 1000 distinct events published, up to 50 are mis-dropped. `events_dropped_dedup` shows "50 dedup drops" — operators can't tell if those were 50 true duplicates (correct) or 50 false positives (data loss).

## Forensic verification gap
The closed invariant from ft-2z16v:
`events_published == events_delivered + events_dropped_no_subscribers + events_dropped_dedup`

This still holds, but `events_dropped_dedup` is no longer cleanly attributable. If 5% are false positives, then `events_delivered` undercounts true delivery by ~5% and `events_dropped_dedup` overcounts true dedup by the same.

## Fix shape
Two-counter split:
- `events_dropped_dedup_lookup_hit` (current behavior).
- `events_dropped_dedup_estimated_fpr` (statistical estimate based on cuckoo load_factor and fingerprint size).

Or: add a sidecar exact dedup (small bounded HashSet) that caches the last N distinct keys; on cuckoo PossibleDuplicate, check the sidecar. If sidecar hit → true duplicate. If sidecar miss → reclassify as PossibleDuplicate but bump a different counter.

The sidecar approach is cleaner; the two-counter statistical split is cheaper.

## Tests
Difficult to test deterministically — requires constructing key-pairs that fingerprint-collide. Could be done via a property test that publishes random keys, sums events_dropped_dedup, and asserts the count is bounded by (true_duplicates + 0.05 × distinct_events).

## Class
P4 OBS / forensic correctness. Pairs with ft-tpdl5 (cuckoo capacity exhaustion); together they're the cuckoo-filter observability backlog.
close_reason:
Fixed at d74869e78 (Option C — leave runtime, fix docs). The events_dropped_dedup counter at events.rs:690 conflated true duplicates with cuckoo false positives (≤ 5% FPR ceiling) under a single 'dedup drops' slot. The runtime split into two counters (option A statistical estimator OR option B sidecar HashSet) is larger than the 60-min slice; both options remain proposable. The doc-fix surfaces the actual semantics so operators can interpret today's numbers correctly without waiting for the runtime split.

## Doc improvements

- Runtime field doc: full FPR-conflation section. References the 5% FPR ceiling test (delta_event_bus_cuckoo_false_positive_rate_stays_below_five_percent at events.rs:~2445), enumerates the two drop sources, gives the operator-interpretation contract:
  * True duplicates ≥ value × 0.95
  * FPR data-loss ≤ value × 0.05
  Plus a 'Why this is unfixed in the runtime' note explaining the deferred work.
- MetricsSnapshot field doc: mirrors the conflation note with a pointer to the runtime field for the full contract.

## Why Option C (not the runtime split)

Both the statistical estimator (A) and the sidecar HashSet (B) are larger than 60 min — A needs FPR derivation that doesn't drift from the test ceiling, B adds per-event allocation on the publish hot path. The doc-fix is bounded, immediately useful (operators can apply 0.95/0.05 multipliers TODAY), and doesn't block either runtime path from landing later.

## Tests

No code change → no new tests required. Pre-existing tests at events.rs:~2445 (cuckoo FPR ceiling) + ~2583 (lag events) + 2669+/4621+ (MetricsSnapshot serde) continue to assert runtime contract.

## Defect-family closure note

Same Option C pattern as ft-lb5x7 (subscriber_lag_events doc-pin). Counter-naming/semantic-drift docs in the events.rs cluster: ft-2z16v (forensic invariant doc-correctness) + ft-lb5x7 (lag-events three-source enumeration) + ft-e3wwx (FPR conflation) — three doc-pin closures in the same cluster.

Verification: cargo check --lib -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features clean (193 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors). Doc-only diff; runtime behavior unchanged.

Pairs with ft-tpdl5 (cuckoo capacity exhaustion) — the cuckoo-filter observability backlog has both beads tracked. ft-e3wwx now docs-fixed; ft-tpdl5 remains open as a separate runtime-counter slice.

## Background

`docs/attestations/manifest.json` declares 14 required slots for the release attestation bundle. Per `ft-syqcz.1` (CLOSED, BR-RC-FOUNDATION) the build script `scripts/attestation-build.sh` refuses to assemble a release bundle when any required slot has `path: null` — that's the "fail-on-missing" gate by design.

As of 2026-05-09, **9 of 14 slots have `path: null`** even though most of the corresponding producing beads are CLOSED and the underlying artifact files exist on disk. The slot table:

  | slot                              | path           | producing bead | bead status | artifact on disk? |
  |-----------------------------------|----------------|----------------|-------------|-------------------|
  | perf/headline-claims              | null           | ft-syqcz.3     | CLOSED      | ✓ docs/perf/headline-claims.json |
  | perf/competitor-matrix            | null           | ft-syqcz.4     | CLOSED      | ⚠ ft-syqcz.4 retired at substrate scope; ft-rq13w shipped docs/perf/latency-derivation.md (markdown, not JSON) — slot expects application/json |
  | perf/lindley-bounds               | populated      | ft-43x69       | CLOSED      | ✓ docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json |
  | tui/render-parity (cpu)           | null           | ft-35yac.2     | CLOSED      | needs investigation — ft-35yac.2 was about ftui-default cutover, not necessarily a JSON artifact |
  | tui/render-parity (gpu)           | populated      | ft-35yac.1.2   | CLOSED      | ✓ docs/attestations/tui/render-parity-gpu.json |
  | security/passive-watch            | null           | ft-x0666.1     | CLOSED      | needs investigation — closure note says "Passive-watch read-only fuzz proof" |
  | security/redactor-coverage        | null           | ft-x0666.2     | CLOSED      | needs investigation — closure note: "Secret redactor recall/precision matrix" |
  | security/distributed-threat-model | null           | ft-x0666.3     | CLOSED      | needs investigation — closure note: "Distributed wire protocol threat model + diff fuzz" |
  | proofs/loom-runtime-async         | null           | ft-syqcz.6     | CLOSED      | needs investigation — closure note: "Loom dev-dep + harness skeleton" |
  | proofs/runtime-proof-trait        | null           | ft-i2eni.1     | (active)    | ft-i2eni.1 is still live — leave null per the deferred-slot rule below |
  | proofs/robot-contracts            | populated      | ft-0elb9       | CLOSED      | ✓ control_plane_golden_matrix.json |
  | doctrine/agents-md-counts         | null           | ft-i2eni.5     | CLOSED      | needs investigation — closure note: "Auto-stamp README/AGENTS counts via build-time queries" |
  | doctrine/vendored-provenance      | populated      | ft-i2eni.6     | CLOSED      | ✓ frankenterm/PROVENANCE.json |
  | doctrine/cx-propagation           | populated      | ft-q0tz3       | CLOSED      | ✓ docs/runtime/cx-propagation.json |
  | perf/atlas-packing                | populated      | ft-gtcm9.5     | CLOSED      | ✓ docs/perf/atlas-packing.json |

Counted: 6 populated, 9 null. Of those 9, 8 producing beads are CLOSED with the artifact most likely already on disk somewhere; only `ft-i2eni.1` (proofs/runtime-proof-trait) is still active.

## Why this matters

* **`scripts/attestation-build.sh` cannot run cleanly without `--allow-partial`.** Per `ft-187kv` (CLOSED, BR-RC-ATTESTATION-CLOSURE) the release CI gates on the bundle being complete and signed. Today every release flow has to use `--allow-partial`, which defeats the gate.
* **README "memory-envelope" hedge cannot be lifted.** README line 88 says "memory-envelope claims should be treated as benchmark-dependent until linked artifacts are published". The `linked artifacts` are exactly the manifest slots. Until they're populated the hedge stays — even though `docs/perf/headline-claims.json` already exists with the verified numbers.
* **Honesty drift.** The project IS more verified than the README admits. AI agents recommending `ft` cite the (overly-conservative) hedge as the project's verification posture, when the actual posture is much stronger. The reality-check sweep flagged this as the second of two genuine NO_BEAD gaps.
* **Future producing beads have no precedent for "publish to manifest".** Today the convention is implicit: ship the artifact, close the bead. There's no closing-checklist step that says "now wire it into manifest.json". Adding one (subtask 7) prevents this gap from recurring.

## What this epic owns

This is a **close-the-loop** bead. It does NOT redo any producing-bead substrate work. For each null slot it walks:
  1. Find the producing bead's shipped artifact on disk.
  2. If found, update the manifest path; verify with build+verify.
  3. If not found (despite a CLOSED producing bead), file a precise *substrate-recovery* follow-up bead naming the file the producer must emit. Mark the slot as deferred with the new bead's ID embedded in the manifest comment.
  4. If the producing bead is still live (e.g., `ft-i2eni.1`), leave the slot null and document it as deferred.
Then lift the matching README hedge text and pin the manifest's value-add into a CI regression guard so future producing beads cannot quietly forget the publish step.

## Deferred-slot rule (load-bearing for scope)

Some slots may legitimately stay null at this epic's close — `ft-i2eni.1` is one (proofs/runtime-proof-trait, still active). The acceptance criterion is **not** "all slots populated"; it's **"every null slot has either a populated path or a precisely-cited deferred-bead reason recorded in a comment field"**. The release gate stays on `--allow-partial` for legitimately-deferred slots only, and the deferred-list itself is a tracked artifact.

## Subtasks (children)

1.  **Per-slot reconciliation pass** — walk each of the 9 null slots, locate the producing bead's shipped artifact, OR file a substrate-recovery follow-up bead. Output: a worksheet table with `(slot, status, artifact-path-or-followup-bead-id, evidence-paste)`. Rejects: a row that just says "investigated, no artifact found" without filing a follow-up bead.
2.  **Update manifest.json** — apply paths from subtask 1 to `docs/attestations/manifest.json`. For deferred slots, add a new sibling field (proposal: `"deferred_to_bead": "ft-..."` next to `"path": null`) so a reader can see the rationale without consulting the worksheet. Update `attestation-build.sh` to recognize this field and emit a *partial* warning message (not error) when running without `--sign cosign|ed25519`, but still error in release builds.
3.  **Build/verify smoke** — run `scripts/attestation-build.sh --version 0.0.0-dev --channel dev --sign unsigned` and confirm exit 0 *without* `--allow-partial` for non-deferred slots; with `--allow-partial` for the deferred-only set. Round-trip `scripts/attestation-verify.sh` on the produced bundle. Capture run artifact bundle per `docs/ft-xbnl0-verification-contract.md` Level B/C.
4.  **Lift README hedges** — replace the "memory-envelope claims should be treated as benchmark-dependent until linked artifacts are published" text with a positive cite of the published artifact category (e.g. "verified via `perf/headline-claims` attestation; reproduce with `ft attestation verify <bundle>`"). Same lift for any other hedge text the README/AGENTS.md uses that the now-published artifacts retire. Audit README + AGENTS.md for all such hedges and address them in this single PR; do not leave a half-lifted hedge.
5.  **Release-build regression test** — add an integration test under `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/` that parses `docs/attestations/manifest.json`, asserts each slot has either `path != null && file exists` *or* `deferred_to_bead` is set and refers to a live (open/in_progress) bead. Catches both forgetting to wire the path AND letting deferred references silently rot.
6.  **Closing-checklist update** — extend `docs/release/attestation-checklist.md` (shipped under `ft-187kv`) with a "before-close" step for any future producing bead: when shipping an attestation artifact, the bead's closing comment must cite the manifest slot path *and* confirm `attestation-build.sh` exits clean. Optional: add a `br` template / docstring snippet so agents draft the right closing-comment shape automatically.
7.  **Cross-link from README "Why Use ft?" / Trust & Attestation** — once the bundle is actually buildable, link from the README perf row directly to the bundle category file path so a curious reader can land on the verified numbers in one click. Co-locate with the existing `ft attestation verify` example.

## Acceptance

- All 9 currently-null manifest slots either populated or carry an explicit `deferred_to_bead` reference to a live bead.
- `scripts/attestation-build.sh --version 0.0.0-dev` exits 0 without `--allow-partial` for non-deferred slots.
- `scripts/attestation-verify.sh` round-trips on the produced bundle.
- README "memory-envelope" / "treated as benchmark-dependent" hedge is removed or rewritten to cite the published bundle.
- Release-build regression test is shipped and proven to catch a manually-introduced null slot in one CI run.
- `docs/release/attestation-checklist.md` updated with the producing-bead closing-checklist step.
- README cross-link to the headline-claims artifact is live.
- Each subtask's closing comment cites RCH-attested evidence per `docs/ft-xbnl0-verification-contract.md`.

## Out of scope

- Re-doing any producing-bead substrate work. If a slot's producer didn't actually ship the JSON, file a follow-up bead in subtask 1; do not re-implement.
- New attestation categories beyond the existing 14.
- Sigstore signing pipeline changes (tracked in `ft-jfyz7`, CLOSED).
- Continuation of `ft-i2eni.1` (proofs/runtime-proof-trait) — it remains a live bead and this epic must NOT subsume it. Leave its slot null with `deferred_to_bead: ft-i2eni.1`.

## Dependency on other beads

- Soft dependency: `ft-187kv` (CLOSED, BR-RC-ATTESTATION-CLOSURE) provides the closing-checklist substrate to extend.
- Soft dependency: `ft-syqcz.1` (CLOSED, BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1) provides the schema + manifest + build/verify scripts.
- Hard dependency on producing-bead artifacts being on disk; substrate recovery follow-ups (filed in subtask 1) become hard prerequisites for the slot they target.
---

After the initial 7 subtasks were filed, plan-space review identified four additional concerns the original epic body did not pin down explicitly. They are now embedded into the relevant subtasks (see each subtask's "Phase 5 refinement addendum") and summarised here for navigation:

### Cross-cutting refinements applied

3. **JSON sidecars for human-readable artifacts**: subtask 1's worksheet now also emits `docs/attestations/null-slot-reconciliation.json` so the regression test in subtask 5 has a stable machine-readable input.
4. **Convergence subtask**: a new ft-e87u6.8 ("Epic convergence harness") provides the definition-of-done verification — it runs the full pipeline post-children and confirms the gap is actually closed, not just individually addressed.

# Subtask 1: Per-slot reconciliation pass — locate every null-slot artifact

This is the load-bearing first step. Subsequent subtasks (manifest update, build smoke, hedge lift, regression test) all depend on the worksheet this produces.

## What to produce

`docs/attestations/null-slot-reconciliation.md` with a table covering the 9 null slots:

  | slot | producing bead | bead status | artifact found at | disposition | follow-up bead |
  |------|----------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|----------------|

Disposition is one of:
  - `populate-from:<path>` — artifact exists on disk; manifest gets this path
  - `deferred-to:<bead-id>` — producing bead is still active; leave slot null with deferred reference
  - `substrate-recovery:<new-bead-id>` — producing bead closed but artifact missing; new follow-up bead filed (this subtask must file it via `br create` and put the ID in this column)
  - `slot-deletion:<rationale>` — slot is no longer applicable (e.g., scope retired); ADR required, and the slot must be removed from the manifest in subtask 2

## Per-slot investigation hints (from the parent epic's notes — do NOT trust, derive from the closing comment of each producing bead and from the disk inventory)

  - `perf/headline-claims` (ft-syqcz.3 CLOSED) — closure note says shipped at `f3e235393a68303c408efca22f9c0183354e123d` to `docs/perf/headline-claims.json`. Confirm presence + content shape matches the manifest's `application/json` expectation. Likely disposition: `populate-from:docs/perf/headline-claims.json`.
  - `perf/competitor-matrix` (ft-syqcz.4 CLOSED, retired-at-substrate-scope, continuation in ft-rq13w CLOSED) — `docs/perf/latency-derivation.md` is markdown, not JSON. Slot expects `application/json`. Investigate whether ft-rq13w shipped a JSON sidecar; if not, this is `substrate-recovery` for the JSON slot.
  - `tui/render-parity` cpu-half (ft-35yac.2 CLOSED — title is "Default ftui in shipped binaries; quarantine ratatui as tui") — closure may not have produced an attestation JSON; this might be `substrate-recovery` or `slot-deletion` (the gpu sister slot is already populated).
  - `security/passive-watch` (ft-x0666.1 CLOSED — "Passive-watch read-only fuzz proof"). Look in `docs/attestations/security/`, `docs/security/`, and the bead's closing comment for the path.
  - `security/redactor-coverage` (ft-x0666.2 CLOSED — "Secret redactor recall/precision matrix vs gitleaks/trufflehog"). Likely a JSON matrix; check `docs/security/` and `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor_coverage_matrix.rs` for emitted artifacts.
  - `security/distributed-threat-model` (ft-x0666.3 CLOSED — "Distributed wire protocol threat model + diff fuzz"). Likely a Markdown threat model + JSON fuzz output. Slot expects `application/json` — check what's actually emitted.
  - `proofs/loom-runtime-async` (ft-syqcz.6 CLOSED — "Loom dev-dep + harness skeleton"). Loom artifacts are usually run-summary JSONs. Check `target/loom-*` paths and whether the harness writes to `docs/attestations/proofs/`.
  - `proofs/runtime-proof-trait` (ft-i2eni.1 — needs status check; if still active, mark `deferred-to:ft-i2eni.1`).
  - `doctrine/agents-md-counts` (ft-i2eni.5 CLOSED — "Auto-stamp README/AGENTS counts via build-time queries"). The auto-stamper likely emits a JSON snapshot of counted entities; trace where build-time query writes its output.

## Methodology (verbatim)

For each null slot:

  1. `br show <producing-bead-id>` — read the closing comment in full. Note the exact commit SHA(s) cited.
  2. `git show <SHA> --stat` — list every file the closing commit touched. Cross-reference against the slot's expected `media_type`.
  3. If the closing commit shipped a file matching the slot's media_type, mark `populate-from:<path>`.
  4. If the closing commit did not ship the expected file, dig into subsequent commits in the same epic for sidecar work. If still nothing, mark `substrate-recovery` and file the follow-up bead.
  5. Producing-bead status check: `grep '"id":"<id>"' .beads/issues.jsonl | grep -oE '"status":"[^"]*"' | head -1`. If `open`/`in_progress`, the disposition becomes `deferred-to:<id>`.

## Substrate-recovery bead template (use when filing follow-ups in disposition column)

```
br create \
  --title='[ft-e87u6][substrate-recovery] <slot-name>: emit attested JSON artifact for manifest slot' \
  --type=task --priority=2 \
  --labels='attestation,substrate-recovery,reality-check' \
  --description='<...background pointing at ft-e87u6.1 worksheet row + the producing bead + what artifact shape is needed...>'
```

Each substrate-recovery bead must explain: which manifest slot, what media_type, what data the producing bead's substrate already exposes that this artifact should serialize.

## Acceptance

- Worksheet `docs/attestations/null-slot-reconciliation.md` exists with all 9 rows filled.
- Zero rows have a vague "investigated" status; every row has a concrete disposition + evidence cite.
- Any `substrate-recovery` rows have their follow-up bead created via `br create` and the bead ID populated.
- Any `slot-deletion` rows have an ADR justifying the deletion (1-page ADR is sufficient).
- The closing comment summarises: N populated, M deferred, K substrate-recovery filed (with bead IDs), L slot-deletions (with ADR refs).

## Out of scope

- Editing `manifest.json` itself — that's subtask 2.
- Re-doing producing-bead substrate work — file a recovery bead instead.
- Lifting README hedges — that's subtask 4.
---

## Phase 5 refinement addendum (2026-05-09)

The original body covers the markdown worksheet. To meet the comprehensive-tests / detailed-logging acceptance bar, this subtask must additionally ship:

### A. JSON sidecar for machine consumption

Alongside `docs/attestations/null-slot-reconciliation.md` (human-readable), emit `docs/attestations/null-slot-reconciliation.json` (machine-readable):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://frankenterm.dev/schemas/null-slot-reconciliation.v1.json",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "generated_at": "<ISO 8601 UTC>",
  "manifest_path": "docs/attestations/manifest.json",
  "manifest_sha256": "<hash>",
  "slots": [
    {
      "category": "perf/headline-claims",
      "producing_bead": "ft-syqcz.3",
      "producing_bead_status": "closed",
      "disposition": "populate-from",
      "artifact_path": "docs/perf/headline-claims.json",
      "artifact_sha256": "<hash>",
      "artifact_media_type": "application/json",
      "evidence_commit": "f3e235393a68303c408efca22f9c0183354e123d",
      "follow_up_bead": null,
      "rationale": "..."
    },
    /* ... 8 more rows ... */
  ],
  "summary": {
    "populated": 0,
    "deferred": 0,
    "substrate_recovery": 0,
    "slot_deletion": 0
  }
}
```

The regression test in `ft-e87u6.5` will consume this JSON to ground-truth its assertions; without it, the test would have to re-derive the worksheet's conclusions from disk every run.

### B. E2E shell harness for the audit pipeline

Path: `tests/e2e/test_ft_e87u6_1_null_slot_reconciliation.sh`. Sources `lib_rch_guards.sh`. Drives:

1. Walk every null slot in `manifest.json`.
2. For each, call `br show <producing-bead>` and parse closure SHA from comments.
3. `git show --stat <sha>` to enumerate touched files; cross-reference media_type.
4. Probe disk for the artifact path; record `artifact_sha256` if present.
5. If absent, the harness must NOT silently auto-emit a `substrate-recovery` row — it must prompt for human review (`outcome: "human_review_required"`) so a follow-up bead is filed deliberately, not by mistake.

Artifacts under `tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/null_slot_reconciliation/<run_id>/` per `docs/test-logging-contract.md` ft-akx00 profile.

### C. Required structured-log fields (per ft-akx00 profile)

| field | example |
|------|---------|
| `bead_id` | `"ft-e87u6.1"` |
| `scenario_id` | `"null_slot_reconciliation"` |
| `surface` | `"attestation_manifest"` |
| `step` | `"slot.<category>.investigation"`, `"slot.<category>.disposition"`, `"summary"` |
| `outcome` | `populate-from` / `deferred-to` / `substrate-recovery` / `slot-deletion` / `human_review_required` |
| `artifact_path` | path to the JSON sidecar |

### D. Rejection rules (acceptance gates)

- Closing comment must cite the JSON sidecar path AND its sha256, AND the `summary` block (counts of each disposition type).
- If any row is `human_review_required`, the bead may NOT close — file the recovery bead first, change the row to `substrate-recovery:<id>`, then close.
- The JSON sidecar's `manifest_sha256` field must match the manifest's actual sha256 at close time (catches "audit was done against an old manifest" drift).

### E. Out of scope addendum

- Building the JSON-Schema validator for the sidecar — that's `ft-e87u6.5`'s job (the regression test). Subtask 1 just emits valid JSON against the documented shape.

# Wire 4 closed-recovery artifacts into manifest paths

## Background

Per ft-e87u6.1's null-slot-reconciliation worksheet, 9 manifest slots had `path: null`. Substrate-recovery beads ft-e87u6.{9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14} were filed and CLOSED with their JSON artifacts shipped. Two of those (ft-e87u6.12 Loom proofs, ft-e87u6.14 auto-stamped counts) had their manifest paths wired during their respective closures.

The remaining 4 slots still carry `path: null` and `deferred_to_bead: ft-e87u6.{9,10,11,13}` even though those 4 beads are now CLOSED with the artifacts on disk:

| Slot | deferred_to_bead | Status | Artifact |
|------|------------------|--------|----------|
| `perf/competitor-matrix` | ft-e87u6.9 | CLOSED | `docs/perf/competitor-matrix.json` |
| `tui/render-parity` | ft-e87u6.10 | CLOSED | `docs/attestations/tui/render-parity.json` |
| `security/passive-watch` | ft-e87u6.11 | CLOSED | `docs/security/passive-watch-attestation.json` |
| `proofs/runtime-proof-trait` | ft-e87u6.13 | CLOSED | `docs/attestations/proofs/runtime-proof-trait.json` |

This is a manifest-coherence bug: per the round-2 refinement on ft-e87u6.5, `deferred_to_bead` must reference an active (open|in_progress|blocked) bead — referencing a CLOSED bead is a drift signal the regression test will flag once written.

## Why this is its own bead (not folded into ft-e87u6.2)

ft-e87u6.2 has BluePike claimed and is BLOCKED on external CI infra (Mesa/Vulkan + x11-xcb-dev on the Linux runner) for the build-script behaviour-matrix test work. The schema additions for ft-e87u6.2 already landed at commit 074fdb46a. The remaining .2 scope is the bats-style matrix test + JSON-Schema validation tests + structured `[build:json]` build-script logging — all of which are independent of the data-only manifest path updates this bead carries.

Splitting the data-wiring step into its own small bead unblocks the manifest-coherence regression today and keeps BluePike's CI-blocked test work decoupled.

## Scope

Per slot: change `path` from `null` to the artifact path; remove `deferred_to_bead` and `deferred_reason` fields (per the schema's `oneOf` invariant: path-set XOR deferred-set).

## Acceptance

- All 4 paths populated in manifest.json.
- `oneOf` invariant satisfied (no slot has both path set AND deferred_to_bead).
- Each new path resolves to an existing file.
- `jq empty docs/attestations/manifest.json` exits 0 (manifest stays valid JSON).
- Closing comment cites: each artifact's sha256, the closing-bead reference (.9/.10/.11/.13), and the post-update null-slot count.

## Out of scope

- Schema changes (already landed under .2)
- Build-script behavioural matrix (under .2)
- README hedge lifts (under .4)
- Manifest completeness regression test (under .5)
- Recovery-bead substrate work (each .9/.10/.11/.13 is closed)

title: [idea-wizard][truth][doctrine] Claim-drift sentinel for docs robot contracts and attestations
description:
## Background

Recent work has repeatedly found truthful-claim drift: README counts polluted by dirty worktrees, attestation snapshots lagging after new E2E scripts, policy subsystem wording mismatches, and robot/contract surfaces that can look more complete than their retained artifacts prove. FrankenTerm needs an automated sentinel that catches claim drift before it reaches README, AGENTS, robot contracts, or release bundles.

## Goal

Build a claim-drift sentinel that maps operator-facing claims to the exact source/verifier/attestation slot that proves them, then fails closed when the claim is stale, missing evidence, dirty-tree contaminated, or only planned.

## Requirements

- Define a machine-readable claim registry for README, AGENTS, docs/robot-contracts, docs/attestations/manifest.json, and release checklist claims.
- Each claim row must include claim text or selector, source of truth command, expected artifact path, producing bead, proof category, freshness rule, and allowed wording states: supported, planned, skipped, stale, unavailable, or deprecated.
- Add static verifiers for common drift classes: count placeholders, command lists, robot/MCP surface availability, attestation path nulls, stale generated_at, and README/AGENTS support wording without retained proof.
- Distinguish dirty worktree measurement from committed HEAD measurement and require release claims to use HEAD-sourced artifacts unless explicitly marked exploratory.
- Emit JSON/TOON-friendly diagnostics so another agent can file or fix the exact drift without reading the whole docs tree.

## Tests and proof

- Golden fixtures for fresh claim, stale claim, dirty-tree contaminated count, missing attestation path, planned-only wording, and unsupported command advertised as supported.
- Shell/JQ verifier for registry integrity.
- E2E docs-smoke check that fails on at least one synthetic drift fixture.
- Any compiled proof must use RCH only.

## Non-goals

No broad docs rewrite, no marketing claim inflation, no local heavy Cargo proof, no file deletion, and no claim is upgraded from planned to supported without retained artifact evidence.

Updated README and docs/attestations/doctrine/agents-md-counts.json from 252 to 253 tracked E2E shell scripts because the new verifier is a tracked E2E script. Static proof passed: jq -c empty for registry/schema/fixtures/count snapshot/.beads; bash -n scripts/check-claim-drift-sentinel.sh tests/e2e/test_claim_drift_sentinel.sh; bash scripts/check-claim-drift-sentinel.sh --json --strict -> ok=true, 7 claims, 6 fixtures, 0 diagnostics; bash tests/e2e/test_claim_drift_sentinel.sh -> static verifier passed (7 claims, 6 fixtures); git diff --check on owned paths; br dep cycles --json -> count 0. title: [reality-check][attest] Subtask 2: Update manifest.json + schema for deferred-slot semantics
description:
Parent: ft-e87u6 ([reality-check] Close-the-loop attestation manifest).
Depends on (blocks): ft-e87u6.1 — worksheet must exist before manifest is edited.

# Subtask 2: Update manifest.json from worksheet + add deferred-slot field

## What to do

Apply the dispositions from the ft-e87u6.1 worksheet to `docs/attestations/manifest.json`.

For each row in the worksheet:

  - `populate-from:<path>`: set the slot's `path` to that string. Verify file exists with correct media_type.
  - `deferred-to:<bead-id>`: leave `path: null`, add a new sibling field `"deferred_to_bead": "<bead-id>"`, add a `"deferred_reason"` short string explaining what's still pending. Schema must be extended (see "Schema update" below).
  - `substrate-recovery:<bead-id>`: same as `deferred-to`, but the bead-id points at the recovery follow-up bead from subtask 1.
  - `slot-deletion:<adr-ref>`: remove the slot from `manifest.json`. Update `required_categories` to drop the deleted category. The ADR must already exist (filed during subtask 1).

## Schema update (`docs/attestations/schema.json`)

Add the new optional fields to the slot schema:

```json
{
  "deferred_to_bead": {
    "type": "string",
    "pattern": "^ft-[a-z0-9.]+$",
    "description": "When path is null, names the bead whose closure will populate this slot. Either path OR deferred_to_bead must be set; both null is invalid."
  },
  "deferred_reason": {
    "type": "string",
    "maxLength": 500,
    "description": "Short human-readable explanation of why the slot is deferred. Required when deferred_to_bead is set."
  }
}
```

Add a JSON Schema constraint enforcing "exactly one of path-non-null OR deferred_to_bead-set" using `oneOf` so the verifier can catch mistakes.

## Update `scripts/attestation-build.sh` for deferred-slot semantics

Today the script errors on null `path` unless `--allow-partial`. Update to:

  1. If a slot has `path: null` AND `deferred_to_bead` set, treat it as a deferred slot. Emit a warning to stderr listing each deferred slot with its bead reference, but do not error.
  2. Add a new flag `--strict-deferred` that elevates deferred slots back to error (for use in the release-build CI gate so a deferred slot doesn't ship into a stable release).
  3. The existing `--allow-partial` behavior stays for slots with neither `path` nor `deferred_to_bead` (i.e., truly malformed entries).

Behavior matrix:

  | slot state                              | default | --allow-partial | --strict-deferred |
  |-----------------------------------------|---------|-----------------|-------------------|
  | `path: "..."`, file exists              | OK      | OK              | OK                |
  | `path: "..."`, file missing             | ERROR   | OK              | ERROR             |
  | `path: null`, `deferred_to_bead: "..."` | WARN    | WARN            | ERROR             |
  | `path: null`, no `deferred_to_bead`     | ERROR   | OK              | ERROR             |

## `scripts/attestation-verify.sh` parity

Same logic in the verifier — accept deferred slots in the produced bundle (the bundle should record deferred slots as a separate first-class block in the JSON output, not silently elide them) so a third-party offline verifier can audit the deferred set.

## Acceptance

- `manifest.json` reflects the worksheet completely; every row resolved.
- `schema.json` updated with the two new optional fields and the `oneOf` invariant.
- `attestation-build.sh` honors deferred semantics per the matrix above.
- `attestation-verify.sh` reproduces deferred-slot info in its output.
- Inline doctest / unit test for the build script confirms the matrix.

## Out of scope

- Running the build (subtask 3).
- Lifting README hedges (subtask 4).
- Adding the regression integration test (subtask 5).
---

## Phase 5 refinement addendum (2026-05-09)

The original body covers the manifest + schema + build-script semantics. To meet the comprehensive-tests / detailed-logging acceptance bar, this subtask must additionally ship:

### A. Bats-style shell unit tests for the build-script behaviour matrix

Path: `tests/scripts/test_attestation_build_matrix.bats` (bats-core; if bats is not in the repo's tooling, fall back to a plain `sh` harness with `set -e` + explicit assert wrappers and document that decision in the closing comment).

For each cell of the behaviour matrix in the original body, ship one explicit test case:

| slot state | flag set | expected exit | test name |
|------------|----------|---------------|-----------|
| `path: "<existing>"` | none | 0 | `populated_slot_passes` |
| `path: "<missing>"` | none | non-zero | `populated_slot_missing_file_fails` |
| `path: "<missing>"` | `--allow-partial` | 0 | `allow_partial_skips_missing_file` |
| `path: null`, `deferred_to_bead: "<live-bead>"` | none | 0 (warn) | `deferred_with_live_bead_warns_only` |
| `path: null`, `deferred_to_bead: "<closed-bead>"` | none | 0 (warn) | `deferred_with_closed_bead_still_warns` (catches the case ft-e87u6.5 will reject as drift) |
| `path: null`, `deferred_to_bead: "<live-bead>"` | `--strict-deferred` | non-zero | `strict_deferred_blocks_release` |
| `path: null`, no `deferred_to_bead` | none | non-zero | `unfilled_slot_fails_default` |
| `path: null`, no `deferred_to_bead` | `--allow-partial` | 0 | `allow_partial_overrides_unfilled` |

Each test fixture is a tiny `manifest.json` with exactly one slot in the target shape — keeps test isolation high and failure messages precise.

### B. JSON-Schema round-trip validation tests

After updating `docs/attestations/schema.json` with the new `oneOf(path | deferred_to_bead)` invariant, ship Rust unit tests under `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/` (or wherever the existing schema tests live, if any) that:

1. Parse the updated schema.
2. Validate a series of synthetic manifest fixtures: one valid resolved slot, one valid deferred slot, one invalid both-set, one invalid both-null. The two invalid cases must fail validation; the two valid cases must pass.
3. Use the same JSON-Schema validator the production verifier uses (so this test is true coverage of the verify path, not a parallel implementation).

If no existing schema-validation surface exists in the workspace, the closing comment must justify why and either (a) add a minimal validator helper or (b) defer to a follow-up bead with a precise scope statement.

### C. Build-script structured logging

The build script emits stderr today. Update it to emit JSON-line structured events on stderr alongside human-readable text on stderr, distinguished by stream prefix:

- Human prefix: `[build]` (existing)
- Structured prefix: `[build:json]` followed by a single JSON object on the rest of the line

JSON event shape:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "<ISO 8601 UTC>",
  "bead_id": "ft-e87u6.2",
  "scenario_id": "attestation_build_<short-tag>",
  "surface": "scripts/attestation-build.sh",
  "step": "validate.<slot-category>" | "warn.deferred" | "error.unfilled" | "compose.bundle" | "sign.<method>" | "summary",
  "outcome": "passed" | "warned" | "failed",
  "reason_code": "<short>",
  "error_code": "<short>",
  "slot_category": "<category>",
  "deferred_to_bead": "<id-or-null>"
}
```

This makes CI failure triage scriptable (a downstream tool can grep for `[build:json]` and parse the events). The human stderr stays human-friendly.

### D. CI workflow integration

Wire the bats suite into `.github/workflows/finish-line-guards.yml` alongside the existing finish-line guards. The step must call the bats binary (or fallback `sh` runner) and upload artifacts on failure.

### E. Required structured-log fields when invoked from a harness

When `attestation-build.sh` is invoked from `tests/e2e/test_ft_e87u6_3_round_trip.sh` (subtask 3), the harness propagates the bead/scenario/correlation IDs via env vars (`FT_BEAD_ID`, `FT_SCENARIO_ID`, `FT_CORRELATION_ID`) and the build script picks them up so the structured events carry consistent IDs across the round-trip pipeline.

### F. Acceptance addendum

- Bats matrix shipped, all 8 cases passing.
- JSON-Schema validation tests passing.
- Build script emits structured `[build:json]` events.
- CI workflow updated and passing on the introducing PR.
- Closing comment cites: matrix-row pass count, schema-test pass count, sample structured-event line, CI run URL.

# Subtask 3: Build/verify round-trip + RCH-attested artifact bundle

## Why this is its own subtask

Without an actual round-trip proof, "the manifest is correct" is just an assertion. This subtask demonstrates with on-disk evidence that the build refuses bad configurations and accepts good ones, and that verify reproduces what build emits — covering both the happy path and each tripwire from the subtask 2 behavior matrix.

## Commands to execute (verbatim)

Per `docs/ft-xbnl0-verification-contract.md` Level B / Level C:

1. **Happy-path build (deferred slots warned, no error)**
   ```bash
   bash scripts/attestation-build.sh \
     --version 0.0.0-dev \
     --channel dev \
     --sign unsigned \
     2>&1 | tee tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/round-trip/build.dev.log
   ```
   Expected: exit 0, stderr contains warning lines for each deferred slot. Stdout contains bundle JSON.

2. **Strict-deferred build (release-style gate; should fail with deferred slots present)**
   ```bash
   bash scripts/attestation-build.sh \
     --version 0.0.0-dev \
     --channel dev \
     --sign unsigned \
     --strict-deferred \
     2>&1 | tee tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/round-trip/build.strict-deferred.log
   echo "exit=$?"
   ```
   Expected: exit non-zero (matches the new error case from subtask 2), stderr lists which deferred slots blocked the build. This is the proof that the release-CI gate can catch a forgotten deferred slot.

3. **Verify (round-trip)**
   ```bash
   bash scripts/attestation-verify.sh \
     tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/round-trip/bundle.dev.json \
     2>&1 | tee tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/round-trip/verify.dev.log
   ```
   Expected: exit 0, every populated slot's SHA-256 matches the on-disk file, every deferred slot is listed with its `deferred_to_bead` reference.

4. **Tamper-detection smoke (one byte mutation)**
   ```bash
   cp tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/round-trip/bundle.dev.json /tmp/tampered.json
   sed -i.bak '0,/"path":/{s/"path":/"path-tampered":/}' /tmp/tampered.json
   bash scripts/attestation-verify.sh /tmp/tampered.json
   echo "tamper exit=$?"
   ```
   Expected: exit non-zero, verifier explicitly reports the schema/contents mismatch. (Per `ft-187kv` smoke-test pattern.)

## Run via RCH for finish-line evidence

The shell-script invocations in steps 1-4 are not heavy Cargo, so per `docs/ft-xbnl0-verification-contract.md` Level B doesn't strictly require RCH for this subtask. **But** if the deferred-slot follow-ups (subtask 1's `substrate-recovery:*` beads) bring any heavy bench/test step inside this round-trip (e.g., a re-bench to confirm a path still resolves), that step must run via `rch exec --` per the contract.

## Artifact bundle requirements (Level C)

Under `tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/<run-id>/`:

  - `summary.json` — describes the run (exit codes, populated/deferred counts, tamper test result).
  - `structured.log` — concatenated structured-event log per `docs/test-logging-contract.md`.
  - `build.dev.log` — happy-path build stdout/stderr.
  - `build.strict-deferred.log` — strict-deferred build stdout/stderr.
  - `verify.dev.log` — verify happy path.
  - `tamper.log` — verify tamper detection.
  - `bundle.dev.json` — produced bundle (the smoking gun).

## Acceptance

- All four commands ran with the expected exit codes; logs captured.
- Artifact bundle present at the goal-line path.
- Closing comment cites the bundle path and the four exit codes verbatim.

## Out of scope

- README hedge updates (subtask 4).
- Regression test (subtask 5).
- Closing-checklist doc update (subtask 6).
---

## Phase 5 refinement addendum (2026-05-09)

The original body specifies the four-command round-trip and Level B/C artifact bundle. To meet the comprehensive-tests / detailed-logging bar, add:

### A. Reproducibility check (build-twice idempotence)

After the happy-path build (step 1), re-run the same command into a different output dir and assert the produced bundle JSON is byte-identical. This is the smoke that catches non-determinism (e.g., a future addition of a build timestamp inside the bundle that breaks signature verification across re-runs).

```bash
diff -u tests/e2e/artifacts/.../bundle.dev.json tests/e2e/artifacts/.../bundle.dev.rerun.json \
  || { echo "[round-trip] bundle is non-deterministic" >&2; exit 1; }
```

### B. Cleanup-on-failure semantics

Wrap the harness body in a `trap '<cleanup-fn>' EXIT` so any partial bundle in `tests/e2e/artifacts/.../<run_id>/` is captured (not deleted) for triage AND any `/tmp` scratch state is cleaned up. Cleanup must be idempotent and respect the `KEEP_FAILURE_ARTIFACTS=1` env var (default: keep) so an operator can opt out for debugging.

### C. Sigstore dry-run path

Today the harness uses `--sign unsigned`. Add an optional second invocation when `COSIGN_DUMMY=1` (or equivalent dev-stub) is in the environment that exercises `--sign cosign` against a stub identity. This proves the signing branch is reachable; the actual cryptographic step is mocked because the dev environment doesn't carry the production identity. Capture sign branch results in `summary.json`.

### D. Structured event log emission (per ft-akx00 profile)

Every harness step emits a JSONL row to `tests/e2e/artifacts/goal-line/ft-e87u6/round-trip/<run_id>/structured.log`:

| step | outcome | error_code |
|------|---------|------------|
| `preflight.rch` | `passed` | `none` |
| `build.happy` | `passed` | `none` |
| `build.rerun.idempotent` | `passed` | `none` |
| `build.strict_deferred` | `failed` (intentional) | `strict_deferred_blocks` |
| `verify.happy` | `passed` | `none` |
| `verify.tamper` | `failed` (intentional) | `tamper_detected` |
| `sign.dryrun` | `passed` | `none` (only when `COSIGN_DUMMY=1`) |
| `summary` | rolled-up pass/fail | composite |

Required fields: `timestamp`, `bead_id="ft-e87u6.3"`, `scenario_id="round_trip"`, `surface="scripts/attestation-build.sh+verify.sh"`, `correlation_id`, `artifact_path`.

### E. Acceptance addendum

- Reproducibility check captured in summary.json (`build_idempotent: true|false`).
- Cleanup trap proven by injecting a deliberate harness fault and confirming the artifact bundle survives + scratch state is cleaned.
- Sigstore dry-run executed when env permits; otherwise documented as skipped with reason.
- All structured-log rows emitted per the table above.
- Closing comment cites the run_id, artifact bundle path, and the four exit codes verbatim.

### F. RCH gating clarification

The original body notes shell-script invocations don't strictly require RCH. **Override:** any step that calls `cargo` (e.g., if a future variant runs an attestation-related cargo command inline) must go through `rch exec --` per the verification contract. The current shape (only `bash` + `jq` + `sha256sum`) is light_local, so it's allowed locally — but the harness must record `rch_required=false` in `summary.json` so future audits can verify nothing in this scenario regressed into needing remote.

# Subtask 4: Lift README + AGENTS.md hedge text and pin manifest cross-references

## What this owns

The README has accumulated several "until linked artifacts are published" / "treat as benchmark-dependent" hedges that the now-published manifest retires. This subtask audits them all in one sweep so the doc is consistently honest, not half-honest.

## Required hedge audit

Search both README.md and AGENTS.md for:

  - "memory-envelope claims" (README line 88 today)
  - "treated as benchmark-dependent"
  - "until linked artifacts are published"
  - "until linked artifact"
  - "should be treated as workload-dependent"
  - "savings vary by payload and should be treated as workload-dependent until linked benchmark artifacts are published" (TOON savings hedge)
  - "memory-envelope claims should be treated as benchmark-dependent until linked artifacts are published"
  - any other "<claim X> ... until <attestation Y>" pattern

For each match:

  1. Identify which manifest slot the hedge is gating on. (e.g., the memory-envelope hedge is gated on `perf/headline-claims`; the TOON hedge would be gated on a TOON-specific slot if one exists.)
  2. If the slot is now `populate-from`-resolved (per ft-e87u6.1 worksheet), rewrite the hedge to a positive cite.
  3. If the slot is `deferred-to`-style or not yet covered by the manifest, KEEP the hedge but add a precise bead reference so a future agent can lift it cleanly when the producer ships. Pattern: `(tracked under <bead-id>; lifted at <bead-id>'s closure)`.

## Suggested hedge replacements (illustrative; the implementer should adjust to actual manifest slot names)

  Before: "memory-envelope claims should be treated as benchmark-dependent until linked artifacts are published"

  After (slot is populated): "memory-envelope claims are verified by the `perf/headline-claims` attestation slot; reproduce with `ft attestation verify <bundle>`. See `docs/perf/headline-claims.json` for the per-claim workload spec."

  Before: "TOON ... savings vary by payload and should be treated as workload-dependent until linked benchmark artifacts are published"

  After (if a TOON slot is added): "TOON savings vary by payload; per-shape numbers verified under the `perf/toon-encoder` attestation slot."

  After (if no TOON slot exists yet): "TOON ... savings vary by payload; per-shape numbers tracked under <bead-id>." — file the producing bead in this subtask if it doesn't already exist.

## Cross-link from "Trust & Attestation" section

The README's "Trust & Attestation" section (around line 257) already mentions `ft attestation verify`. Add a one-line pointer: "Manifest is at `docs/attestations/manifest.json`; each slot maps to a producing-bead artifact and is signed in the per-release bundle." This is the single doorway from claim to artifact.

## AGENTS.md cross-check

AGENTS.md is read by every coding agent that touches this repo. If any hedge there can be lifted, lift it — agents quoting AGENTS.md as ground truth deserve the latest verification posture.

## Acceptance

- README + AGENTS.md hedge audit complete; the closing comment lists every match and its disposition.
- All hedges that can be lifted are lifted with positive cross-references.
- Hedges that legitimately remain (deferred slots) have a bead-id breadcrumb.
- "Trust & Attestation" cross-links the manifest as the single doorway.
- No hedge is half-lifted (e.g., README updated but AGENTS.md untouched).

## Out of scope

- Regression test (subtask 5) — that catches the *next* drift.
- Closing-checklist doc update (subtask 6) — that prevents the *future* drift.
- README cross-link from "Why Use ft?" / per-feature rows (subtask 7) — that's the deep-link surface, separate concern.
---

## Phase 5 refinement addendum (2026-05-09)

The original body covers the hedge audit + rewrite. To meet the comprehensive-tests / detailed-logging bar, add:

### A. Hedge-text regression test (Rust integration test)

Path: `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/readme_hedge_alignment.rs`. Asserts:

1. For every manifest slot with non-null `path`, the corresponding "until linked artifact published" hedge text is NOT present in README.md or AGENTS.md. Map slot category → hedge regex via a small in-test table.
2. For every manifest slot with `deferred_to_bead` set, the README/AGENTS.md hedge MUST cite the bead ID (so the deferred state is observable from the doc, not just the manifest).
3. No hedge text exists that doesn't map to either a populated artifact (must be lifted) or a deferred bead (must cite the ID).

```rust
#[test]
fn no_orphan_hedge_text() {
    let readme = read_to_string("README.md").unwrap();
    let agents = read_to_string("AGENTS.md").unwrap();
    let manifest = parse_manifest("docs/attestations/manifest.json");

    for slot in manifest.slots {
        let hedge_re = hedge_pattern_for(slot.category);
        let m_readme = hedge_re.find(&readme);
        let m_agents = hedge_re.find(&agents);

        match (slot.path.as_ref(), slot.deferred_to_bead.as_ref()) {
            (Some(_path), _) => {
                assert!(m_readme.is_none(),
                    "slot {} has populated path but README still carries hedge: {:?}",
                    slot.category, m_readme);
                assert!(m_agents.is_none(),
                    "slot {} has populated path but AGENTS.md still carries hedge",
                    slot.category);
            }
            (None, Some(bead_id)) => {
                if let Some(m) = m_readme {
                    let surrounding = surrounding_text(&readme, m.start(), m.end(), 200);
                    assert!(surrounding.contains(bead_id),
                        "slot {} is deferred to {} but README hedge does not cite the bead: {}",
                        slot.category, bead_id, surrounding);
                }
                /* same for agents */
            }
            (None, None) => {
                /* this is impossible if ft-e87u6.5 is enforced; defensive panic */
                panic!("manifest slot {} has neither path nor deferred_to_bead", slot.category);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The `hedge_pattern_for(category)` table is the load-bearing piece — it pins each marketing-claim hedge to its slot. Initial entries (the implementer extends as the audit reveals more):

```rust
const HEDGE_PATTERNS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("perf/headline-claims",     r"memory-envelope claims should be treated as benchmark-dependent"),
    ("perf/headline-claims",     r"headline (?:numbers|claims).*until linked artifacts are published"),
    ("perf/headline-claims",     r"savings vary by payload.*until linked benchmark artifacts are published"),
    ("perf/atlas-packing",       r"atlas-packing telemetry.*workload-dependent"),
    ("security/redactor-coverage", r"redactor coverage.*pending"),
    /* ... add as audit reveals */
];
```

### B. Hedge audit worksheet (sidecar to subtask)

Emit `docs/attestations/hedge-lift-worksheet.md` listing every hedge match in README + AGENTS.md before this subtask runs, with a column for `manifest_slot`, `disposition` (lift / keep + cite bead / not-applicable), and `evidence`. This is the human-reviewable artifact the regression test in (A) ground-truths against. Future agents lifting hedges add rows here so the regex table stays in sync.

### C. Required structured-log fields

This subtask is doc-edit-heavy with no harness, but the regression test from (A) when run produces standard cargo test output. Wrap it in an e2e harness `tests/e2e/test_ft_e87u6_4_hedge_alignment.sh` that runs the test and emits structured events per `docs/test-logging-contract.md`:

- `step="hedge.audit"`, `outcome="passed|failed"` per manifest slot
- `step="summary"`, `outcome="passed"` if all slots align
- `error_code="orphan_hedge_<category>"` on failure

### D. Acceptance addendum

- Hedge-lift worksheet shipped with one row per match.
- Regression test shipped + passing.
- E2E harness shipped + integrated into `.github/workflows/finish-line-guards.yml`.
- Closing comment cites: number of hedges lifted, number kept-with-cite, number unchanged, and the test run URL.
- A future producing-bead checklist update (subtask 6) references this regression test as the gate for hedge alignment, closing the doc-drift loop.

```markdown
[^perf-headline]: Verified via `perf/headline-claims` attestation slot. See `docs/attestations/manifest.json` and reproduce with `ft attestation verify <bundle>`.
```

Path: `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/readme_footnotes_resolve.rs`. For every `[^anchor]` footnote reference in README's "Why Use ft?" section, assert:

1. The footnote definition exists in the document.
2. The footnote text cites a real manifest slot category (cross-check against `docs/attestations/manifest.json`).
3. The cited slot has `path != null` at test time (no cross-link to a deferred slot — that would over-promise).

```rust
#[test]
fn every_why_use_footnote_anchors_to_resolved_manifest_slot() {
    let readme = std::fs::read_to_string("README.md").unwrap();
    let manifest: Manifest = parse_manifest("docs/attestations/manifest.json");

    let footnote_refs: Vec<&str> = extract_footnote_refs_in_section(&readme, "Why Use ft?");
    let footnote_defs: HashMap<&str, &str> = extract_footnote_definitions(&readme);

    for anchor in footnote_refs {

            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("orphan footnote reference: {anchor}"));
        let referenced_slot = extract_manifest_slot_category_from_def(def)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("footnote {anchor} doesn't cite a manifest slot: {def:?}"));

            "footnote {anchor} cross-links to slot {referenced_slot} which is deferred ({:?}); \

            slot.deferred_to_bead);

}
```

# Subtask 8: Epic convergence harness — definition-of-done verification

This bead provides that single test.

## What it does

1. **Re-derive the original NO_BEAD assertion**: parse `docs/attestations/manifest.json`, count slots where `path == null && deferred_to_bead == null`. Assert == 0. (Original gap = 9; convergence demands 0 truly-orphaned slots.)
2. **Build full bundle without `--allow-partial`**: `bash scripts/attestation-build.sh --version 0.0.0-dev --channel dev --sign unsigned`. Assert exit 0.
3. **Strict-deferred build smoke**: same with `--strict-deferred`. Assert exit non-zero IFF any deferred slot remains; capture exit code per the matrix from subtask 2.
4. **Verify round-trip**: `bash scripts/attestation-verify.sh <bundle>`. Assert exit 0.
5. **README hedge alignment**: `cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test readme_hedge_alignment`. Assert exit 0.
6. **Manifest completeness**: `cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test attestation_manifest_completeness`. Assert exit 0.

title: [MEDIUM] cancel_races_child_creation test has weak race coverage; passes trivially via propagation
description:
In commit 6a16ae0a (fix(ft-2xnop): add unix umask coverage ... +
cancellation concurrency tests), the test
\`cancel_races_child_creation_all_children_see_cancellation\` at
crates/frankenterm-core/src/cancellation.rs:2635-2676 claims to verify
the cancel+child race but does not reliably exercise the race window.

Structure:
\`\`\`rust
for _ in 0..20 {
    let parent = CancellationToken::new(...);
    let n_creators = 8;
    let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(n_creators + 1));

    let handles: Vec<_> = (0..n_creators).map(|i| {
        let parent = parent.clone();
        let barrier = Arc::clone(&barrier);
        thread::spawn(move || {
            barrier.wait();
            parent.child(ScopeId(format!(\"c_{i}\")))
        })
    }).collect();

    barrier.wait();
    parent.cancel(ShutdownReason::UserRequested);
    // ... assert every child is cancelled
}
\`\`\`

Problems:

1. The barrier synchronizes the START of each thread's work but not
   the duration of \`parent.child(...)\`. On a machine with >=8 cores,
   the 8 creator threads typically finish \`parent.child(...)\` BEFORE
   the main thread reaches \`parent.cancel(...)\`. In that ordering, all
   children are pre-existing when cancel propagates — a trivial case
   covered by other tests in the file.

2. 20 sequential rounds with no scheduler perturbation (no \`yield_now\`,
   no sleep, no thread count above core count) rarely hit the interesting
   interleaving where cancel runs mid-child-creation.

3. The assertion passes even if \`parent.child()\` has a bug where it
   reads the \"parent cancelled\" flag AFTER registration but BEFORE
   propagation reaches it — because the test never creates that window.

Impact: false confidence in race-safe \`CancellationToken::child()\`
under concurrent cancel. A latent bug where a newly-created child
escapes both propagation (not-yet-registered) AND post-cancel detection
(child() reads stale flag) would not be caught.

Fix direction:
- Spawn more creators than CPU cores (e.g., 64) so some are preempted
  mid-call.
- Insert \`thread::yield_now()\` or a short sleep inside the creator
  body before calling \`parent.child()\` to widen the race window.
- Alternatively, use an inner barrier that creators wait on AFTER
  they've decided to create the child but BEFORE registration, so the
  main thread can force the interleaving.
- Consider using loom or shuttle for deterministic interleaving
  coverage instead of probabilistic races.

Severity: medium — test quality issue, not a proven correctness bug
in cancellation.rs. Filing because the test claims coverage it does
not deliver.
close_reason: Hardened in 7ac677a6: creator count 8→64 (forces preemption on any host), per-thread yield_now + modulo 50µs sleep widens race, rounds 20→64, each creator samples is_cancelled() pre-child() and the round-level outcomes are checked so the test asserts the cancel-first ordering was actually exercised at least once — if it isn't, the test fails with a diagnostic pointing at loom/shuttle for deterministic coverage. Build clean; local run blocked by unrelated macOS dyld bottleneck under load.

title: [infra] RCH Rust worker preflight rejects proof lanes despite Rust-capable workers
description:
## Problem

Remote Rust proof lanes can be blocked even when RCH reports healthy Rust-capable workers. During ft-782hw.1 proof, the command RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-782hw-1-proof cargo test -p frankenterm --bin ft proof_doctor -- --nocapture refused local fallback. It first reported no workers with Rust installed, then all workers failed preflight checks.

## Evidence

- rch workers capabilities --command cargo-test-proof-doctor listed Rust 1.97 nightly on vmi1152480 and vmi1156319.
- rch diagnose --dry-run classified the command as Rust cargo_test but worker_selection reported all_workers_failed_preflight.
- rch status showed vmi1152480 in critical disk pressure with disk_free_below_critical_gb while vmi1156319 was healthy but occupied by a 4-slot FrankenTerm test.
- A non-persistent RCH_TEST_SLOTS override did not change the diagnose estimated_cores value, which remained 4.

## Impact

Agents cannot complete required remote proof gates and must leave beads open even for narrow Rust changes.

## Proposed Fix

Diagnose RCH worker-selection and preflight reporting so it distinguishes no Rust runtime, insufficient free slots on Rust-capable workers, and disk-pressure exclusion. Restore or clean worker capacity only through the approved RCH maintenance path, not ad-hoc agent cleanup.

title: [rch-rollout] Publish macOS RCH build containing worker-selection fix
