## Goal

Make the source fix for ft-e8ghx consumable by the live macOS RCH daemon. The RCH source fix is already shipped in remote_compilation_helper as commit 35372ae and pushed to origin main plus origin master, but the installed FrankenTerm operator machine still reports RCH version 1.0.24 and the update check currently reports no newer packaged release.

## Context

The remaining live failure is packaging and rollout, not a FrankenTerm source diagnostic. Worker capabilities can list Rust-capable workers while remote-required proof lanes still fail in stale live-daemon states. A previous remote release build produced Linux artifacts only; those cannot replace the local macOS binaries.

## Scope

- Produce or publish a macOS aarch64 RCH package containing commit 35372ae or a later equivalent fix.
- Ensure the package includes both the CLI and daemon binaries and exposes a version or build marker distinguishable from the stale 1.0.24 binary if the semantic version is unchanged.
- Keep this non-destructive: do not overwrite live installed binaries until the safe drain and update bead is ready.
- Record package URL or local artifact path, SHA256, source commit, build host, target triple, and exact build command.

## Non-goals

- Do not restart the live daemon in this bead.
- Do not repair, restart, or touch Agent Mail.
- Do not claim FrankenTerm proof lanes are unblocked until live daemon update and validation pass.

## Acceptance

- A macOS aarch64 package containing the worker-selection fix exists and is reachable from the operator machine.
- SHA256 and source commit are recorded in the Beads comment.
- The next rollout step has either an advertised update package or an exact manual artifact path.

title: [rch-rollout] Safely drain and update live RCH daemon to fixed build
description:
## Goal

Install or activate the fixed macOS RCH build only after the shared daemon is safe to roll and the package from ft-e8ghx.1 is available.

## Context

The live daemon is shared by multiple agents. Restarting or replacing it while active proof lanes are running can invalidate RCH evidence. This bead owns the operational step that turns the packaged fix into the live daemon state, with an explicit drain and rollback record.

## Scope

- Wait for the RCH queue to drain, or record explicit operator approval if an emergency restart is unavoidable.
- Snapshot daemon status, queue state, worker capabilities, installed binary paths, version or build marker, and SHA256 before update.
- Install or activate the fixed macOS package from ft-e8ghx.1 using the least disruptive supported path.
- Restart or reload only through documented RCH commands, then verify the socket answers, worker inventory is available, and the installed marker matches the fixed package.
- Preserve logs showing whether any pre-existing rch exec clients were already stale before the update.

## Non-goals

- Do not build the macOS package here; that belongs to ft-e8ghx.1.
- Do not delete remote worker directories or local source trees.
- Do not count restarted sync or queue chatter as a FrankenTerm proof pass.

## Acceptance

- Live daemon reports the fixed build marker or equivalent source commit evidence.
- Post-update queue and worker capability checks pass.
- Any interrupted or stale pre-update proof lanes are documented as invalid and not used as source proof.
- The Beads comment includes exact commands, timestamps, package SHA256, daemon PID before and after, and active build count at restart time.

title: [rch-rollout] Validate live RCH proof admission after daemon update
description:
## Goal

Prove that the live daemon update actually fixes the FrankenTerm proof-admission failure, using remote-required validation commands and retained evidence.

## Context

ft-e8ghx should close only when the live daemon no longer collapses Rust-capable same-project exclusion or capacity cases into stale no-runtime errors. A package existing or a daemon restart is not enough; the live proof-admission path must produce the corrected reason shape and allow unrelated proof lanes to be classified accurately.

## Scope

- Run non-mutating diagnose or dry-run selection for representative FrankenTerm proof commands that previously returned no workers with Rust installed despite Rust-capable workers.
- Run a tiny remote-required RCH smoke that reaches the expected remote assignment path without using local fallback.
- If same-project workers are intentionally excluded, verify the live reason reports an admissibility or active-project exclusion summary rather than no runtime.
- Re-run or unblock the dependent FrankenTerm proof lane only when the smoke shows the live selection path is fixed.
- Attach exact command output, worker ID, queue state, and artifact paths in Beads comments.

## Non-goals

- Do not close source beads based only on RCH sync or transport logs.
- Do not run heavy local Cargo as proof.
- Do not mutate worker mirrors or delete remote source trees.

## Acceptance

- A live remote-required smoke passes or fails with the corrected stable reason code.
- The previous stale no-runtime reason is no longer reproduced for a command with Rust-capable workers present.
- Any dependent bead unblocking is justified with exact evidence and no proxy signals.
- ft-e8ghx receives a closeout comment that separates source fix, package rollout, daemon update, and live validation evidence.

title: [rch][preflight] Diagnose RCH-E324 dependency preflight blocker after full sync
description:
## Problem

A FrankenTerm docs-smoke proof lane for `ft-9ntud.1` selected a healthy Rust-capable worker and synced the workspace, then failed before Cargo/test execution with RCH dependency preflight `RCH-E324`.

Command:

```bash
RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 RCH_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 RCH_EXTERNAL_TIMEOUT_ENABLED=false rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-9ntud-1-docs-smoke CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test -p frankenterm --test docs_smoke blocker_radar_contract_docs_truth_gate -- --nocapture
```

Observed evidence:

- Selected worker: `vmi1153651` at `ubuntu@38.242.134.66`.
- Sync completed: 28,776 files, 13,973,213 bytes, 167,442 ms.
- Failure: `Remote dependency preflight blocked remote execution on vmi1153651 [RCH-E324] remediation='Ensure every dependency root in the closure is synced and Cargo.toml exists remotely.'`
- Local fallback was refused because `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1`.
- `rch diagnose --json -- env ... cargo test ...` classified the command as `cargo_test`, would intercept, and selected `vmi1153651` successfully.
- `rch status --workers --jobs --json` at 2026-05-10T19:49Z reported daemon posture `remote_ready`, version `1.0.24`, 7/7 workers healthy, and 28/46 slots available.

## Impact

FrankenTerm proof lanes can be blocked after full sync but before Cargo, leaving source-only/doc-only changes unable to receive required RCH-backed closeout. This is different from a source test failure and should not be counted as proof.

## Scope

Diagnose and fix the RCH dependency-preflight path so it emits the missing/stale dependency root report in normal machine-readable output and so a fully synced FrankenTerm workspace does not fail closed with opaque `RCH-E324` when required dependency roots exist locally.

This may belong in `remote_compilation_helper`; the Bead is tracked here because it blocks FrankenTerm proof closeout.

## Non-goals

- Do not restart, update, drain, or repair the live RCH daemon from this bead without explicit operator approval.
- Do not delete remote mirrors or mutate worker source trees as an ad hoc fix.
- Do not count local Cargo fallback as proof for FrankenTerm beads.
- Do not conflate this with GitHub Actions macOS package artifact rollout.

## Acceptance

- A reproduced `RCH-E324` case includes a retained dependency-preflight report naming the missing or stale roots, or the bug is fixed so the same FrankenTerm docs-smoke command reaches Cargo/test remotely.
- The reason-code taxonomy distinguishes dependency-preflight blockers from worker-selection no-runtime, queue timeout, remote mirror missing file, and source/test failure.
- A follow-up RCH proof for `ft-9ntud.1` either passes remotely or fails with a more specific machine-readable substrate artifact.
- Beads comments cite exact command, selected worker, artifact/report path, and whether Cargo/rustc/test binary was reached.
close_reason: Patched RCH preflight reached Cargo and the dependent FrankenTerm docs-smoke proof passed remotely with source-entrypoint verification.

title: [rch][rollout] Provide patched macOS launcher and validate live preflight classification
description:
## Background

ft-e8ghx.4 identified and fixed a remote_compilation_helper source bug: dependency preflight verified only Cargo.toml and missed required source entrypoints. The source fix is pushed as remote_compilation_helper commit 2fa1249a18dfd05ae5e319e8d10bfd3c9ea1af55, but the installed macOS launcher at /Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/rch is still version 1.0.24 and has not been updated from that source commit.

## Scope

Package or otherwise provide a macOS arm64 rch launcher containing commit 2fa1249a18dfd05ae5e319e8d10bfd3c9ea1af55, then validate a live FrankenTerm proof lane through that patched launcher. This is an operator-controlled rollout step, not a source patch.

## Guardrails

Do not restart, update, drain, or repair RCH or RCHD without explicit operator approval. Do not delete remote mirrors. Do not treat sync chatter as proof. Do not use local Cargo as FrankenTerm closeout evidence.

## Acceptance

- Patched macOS arm64 rch launcher is available or installed with explicit operator approval.
- Live rch --version or equivalent provenance proves the launcher contains remote_compilation_helper commit 2fa1249a18dfd05ae5e319e8d10bfd3c9ea1af55 or a later commit with the same fix.

- Beads comments cite exact command, selected worker, target dir, exit code, and whether Cargo/rustc/test binary was reached.

title: [rch-rollout] Package and validate RCH 5577caa floating-toolchain fix

Provide a macOS aarch64 RCH package or launcher that contains remote_compilation_helper commit 5577caa and then validate live FrankenTerm remote-required Cargo admission against it.

## Context

ft-e8ghx still blocks dependent FrankenTerm proof lanes because the live daemon rejects floating nightly rust-toolchain.toml commands with all_workers_failed_preflight. - Do not restart, update, drain, or repair live RCH without explicit operator approval or a documented safe rollout window.
- Do not delete local or remote mirrors.
- Do not count local Cargo or RCH sync chatter as source proof.
- Do not use PR59 or GitHub Actions queue state as a substitute for live RCH validation.

- Beads comment records exact artifact, SHA256, source commit, install status, daemon PID before and after if installed, and queue state at rollout time.

title: tx_idempotency ledger chain does not authenticate final record or risk/agent fields
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs found incomplete ledger authenticity coverage. StepExecutionRecord carries ordinal, idempotency key, execution_id, timestamp_ms, outcome, risk, prev_hash, and agent_id (tx_idempotency.rs:146-163). But StepExecutionRecord::hash canonicalizes only ordinal, idem_key, execution_id, timestamp_ms, outcome_json, and prev_hash (tx_idempotency.rs:186-201), omitting risk and agent_id entirely. TxExecutionLedger::verify_chain then walks records by checking each record.prev_hash against the previous computed hash and ordinal gaps (tx_idempotency.rs:417-442), but it never compares the final computed tip against self.last_hash (last_hash is stored separately at tx_idempotency.rs:268-269 and updated on append at tx_idempotency.rs:406-410). Consequences: tampering risk/agent_id is invisible for every record, and tampering the final record outcome/timestamp/key can be invisible because no subsequent record checks its computed hash and verify_chain ignores the stored tip. Existing property tests only verify append-built chains remain intact (proptest_tx_idempotency.rs:261-279) and serde+rebuild lookups (proptest_tx_idempotency.rs:321-345), not tamper detection. Why it matters: tx_observability builds forensic bundles from ledger records and chain verification (tx_observability.rs:705-718); a green chain can carry altered attribution/risk or altered final outcome evidence. Proposed remediation: include all safety/forensic fields in StepExecutionRecord::hash, compare the final computed hash to ledger.last_hash in verify_chain, and add tamper regressions for final-record outcome, risk, and agent_id mutations after serde roundtrip.

title: [bench_stats.fix] empirical_bernstein_ci accepts range=NaN
description:
## Defect

empirical_bernstein_ci at bench_stats.rs:457-461:

    pub fn empirical_bernstein_ci(samples: &[f64], range: f64, alpha: f64) -> Option<f64> {
        if samples.is_empty() || range <= 0.0 || !(0.0..1.0).contains(&alpha) {
            return None;
        }
        ...
    }

The `range <= 0.0` predicate rejects 0.0 and negatives but admits
NaN (NaN comparisons all return false). With range=NaN the function
proceeds and computes:

    bernstein = sqrt(2 * var * log_term / n) + 7/3 * range * log_term / (n-1)

The second term is NaN, so the function returns Some(NaN).

Sibling of ft-p2xmz / ft-gldyy (validator-logic-bug family). Same
root cause: float predicate doesn't catch NaN.

## Fix

    if samples.is_empty() || !range.is_finite() || range <= 0.0
        || !(0.0..1.0).contains(&alpha) {
        return None;
    }

Adding `!range.is_finite()` rejects NaN and ±infinity. The range
contract per the docstring is 'a-priori upper bound on each
observation' — implicitly finite.

(`(0.0..1.0).contains(&alpha)` already rejects NaN correctly because
Range::contains returns false for NaN.)

## Acceptance

- empirical_bernstein_ci(&[1.0], f64::NAN, 0.05) returns None
- empirical_bernstein_ci(&[1.0], f64::INFINITY, 0.05) returns None
- empirical_bernstein_ci(&[1.0], f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.05) returns None
- existing happy-path tests still pass

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/bench_stats.rs:457-477
- ft-p2xmz, ft-gldyy (sibling validator-logic-bug instances)
- 3rd instance in family — file is starting to look swept
close_reason: done

title: [5-lens audit / OBSERVABILITY] SwarmCapacityTelemetry::record_* methods have ZERO production callers — capacity certificates compute on empty data
description:
[HIGH] observability gap surfaced during Phase-2 5-lens analysis on runtime_telemetry.rs.

## Symptom

`SwarmCapacityTelemetry` exposes write-side methods (record_arrival, record_outcome, record_completion, record_cancellation, record_timeout, record_error, record_wait_time_ms, record_retry_latency_ms, record_service_time_ms, observe_queue_depth) at runtime_telemetry.rs:2516+. `grep -rn 'SwarmCapacityTelemetry::new\|SwarmCapacityTelemetry {' crates/` returns ONLY test/proptest sites in runtime_telemetry.rs itself — ZERO production callers.

`SwarmCapacityTelemetry::snapshot` (read path) feeds into `SwarmCapacityTelemetrySnapshot::compile_capacity_certificate` which has the fail-closed branch I noticed in the prior review pass:

```rust
// Fail-closed when no stage telemetry was available for any selected
// stage. `aggregate_capacity_status(&[])` would otherwise fall through
// to `Safe` (vacuous "no Unknown, no Unsafe ⇒ Safe")...
if stages.is_empty() {
    let assumption_flags = vec![
        SwarmCapacityAssumptionFlag::InsufficientSamples,
        SwarmCapacityAssumptionFlag::InvalidObservationWindow,
    ];
    return SwarmCapacityCertificate { status: Unknown, ... };
}
```

In production this fail-closed branch likely fires EVERY tick because the stage metrics are empty (no production writers). The capacity certificate is permanently Unknown; the admission controller treats Unknown as fail-closed; pressure cooldown was independently dead until ft-0ig2q.

## Why this matters

The ft-onheq epic's 'swarm capacity autopilot' is a multi-component system:
- Stage telemetry (writes by production hot paths)  ← MISSING
- Stage telemetry (reads by certificate compiler)   ← present
- Certificate (consumed by admission controller)    ← present
- Admission controller (decides plans)              ← present
- Plan (audit + evidence ledger persists)           ← present
- Cooldown (state recorder)                         ← MISSING (ft-0ig2q substrate landed; wiring follow-up)

Two of the six components have no production writers. The system 'works' end-to-end only because every consumer fail-closes on missing data. That's correct safety behavior but means the system never enters an Active state in production — the autopilot is not autopiloting.

## Fix shape

This is a per-call-site instrumentation pass. Each production hot path that the capacity certificate covers (capture/admission/storage/render stages per the SwarmCapacityStage enum) needs a `telemetry.record_arrival(stage, queue_depth)` at the start + `telemetry.record_completion/timeout/error(...)` at the end.

State ownership question (where does the long-lived `SwarmCapacityTelemetry` live?) needs design review — likely a per-process singleton + an Arc-Mutex shared across call sites. This is the same shape as the ft-0ig2q wiring follow-up.

## Acceptance

- Each `SwarmCapacityStage` variant has at least one production call site recording arrivals + outcomes.
- A regression test verifies that after running a representative production scenario, `SwarmCapacityTelemetry::snapshot()` returns non-empty stages.
- Capacity certificate transitions out of Unknown → Safe/Watch/Violated based on real data.

## Cross-references

- runtime_telemetry.rs:2485 (SwarmCapacityTelemetry struct).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:2516+ (record_* methods).
- ft-onheq.5 (parent — admission controller).
- ft-0ig2q (the parallel cooldown-state wiring gap I filed earlier today).

## Sweep

A reviewer should also confirm whether `SwarmTailRiskMonitor` and other sibling `SwarmCapacity*` controller-state types have the same write-side gap. The pattern (controller-state defined, consumers wired, but no production writers) was previously surfaced for SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerState in ft-0ig2q — strong signal there are more.

Avoiding edits to another pane's dirty file; proceeding to workflows runner conformance fallback.

title: Planner anti-thrash governor is resolved but not wired into mission loop
description:
Reality-check audit of planner_features.rs against mission_loop.rs found the anti-thrash governor surface is implemented, configured, and resolved, but the live mission loop never applies it before solving assignments.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:983-1014 defines GovernorConfig with reassignment cooldown, starvation boost, history window, flip threshold, and thrash penalty.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:1064-1246 implements ThrashGovernor::evaluate, record_cycle, record_agent_assignment, and register_bead. Lines 1083-1086 explicitly say callers should use adjusted scores in the solver instead of raw scores.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:1294-1296 includes governor_config in every MissionProfile, and lines 1864-1886 apply MissionRuntimeConfig governor overrides into ResolvedMissionConfig. Lines 1933-1941 return governor_config in the resolved config.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:31-35 imports planner extraction/scoring/solver types and functions but does not import GovernorConfig/ThrashGovernor/GovernorAction.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:272-296 MissionLoopConfig contains extraction_config, scorer_config, solver_config, safety_envelope, metrics, and conflict_detection, but no governor_config or governor state.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:578-636 scores candidates and immediately calls solve_assignments on scorer_report. There is no ThrashGovernor::evaluate step, no adjusted-score ScorerReport, and no record_cycle after assignment.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:679-740 applies a separate safety envelope after solving, which does not implement the planner_features anti-thrash semantics.

Why it matters:
The runtime profiles advertise cooldown/starvation/thrash behavior, but live mission decisions ignore those knobs. Operators can select SafetyFirst/Throughput/UrgencyDriven governor settings and receive assignments as if the anti-thrash governor did not exist.

Proposed remediation:
Thread GovernorConfig and ThrashGovernor state into MissionLoopConfig/MissionLoopState, apply ThrashGovernor::evaluate between scoring and solve_assignments, rebuild the scored report from adjusted scores, and call record_cycle/record_agent_assignment after final assignments. Add an integration test where a recently assigned bead is blocked by cooldown and a repeatedly skipped registered bead receives a starvation boost in the actual MissionLoop::evaluate path.
close_reason: Fixed in bec232bec. Wired MissionLoop through ThrashGovernor between scoring and solving, persisted governor state/report in loop state, enforced cooldown blocks via solver safety gate, reranked boosted/penalized scores before solve, recorded final post-envelope assignments back into governor state, and added focused ft_efxr6 regression tests. title: [BR-RC-RENDER-PERF] Atlas frame-budget gates over-admit via integer-rounding fractional loss
description:
Severity: MEDIUM.

Both `FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer` (br-ft-ktd19.3 slice 1 at bdd118ed8) and
`DiskBudgetEstimator` (br-ft-ktd19.3 slice at 494e31116) compute their
admit/defer decision via:

    handoff_cost = self.cost_microseconds(handoff.bytes);
    admitted_cost = self.cost_microseconds(self.admitted_bytes);
    if admitted_cost.saturating_add(handoff_cost) > budget_us { defer }

Where `cost_microseconds` is floor integer division (`bytes / bytes_per_microsecond`).

Bug: `floor(a/N) + floor(b/N)` can be 1 less than the accurate
`floor((a+b)/N)` due to fractional carry. Each admit call sheds up
to 1 µs of fractional cost. Over a frame with K handoffs, cumulative
over-admission can reach K × (N-1) bytes vs the accurate budget.

## Reproduction (NVMe N=3000, budget=2 µs, six 1500-byte handoffs)

Trace step-by-step:
- #1: admit_cost=0/3000=0, handoff_cost=1500/3000=0, 0+0=0 ≤ 2 → ADMIT. acc=1500
- #2: 1500/3000=0, 0, 0 ≤ 2 → ADMIT. acc=3000
- #3: 3000/3000=1, 0, 1 ≤ 2 → ADMIT. acc=4500
- #4: 4500/3000=1, 0, 1 ≤ 2 → ADMIT. acc=6000
- #5: 6000/3000=2, 0, 2 ≤ 2 → ADMIT. acc=7500
- #6: 7500/3000=2, 0, 2 ≤ 2 → ADMIT. acc=9000

After 6 admits: 9000 bytes (3 µs of accurate throughput) on a 2 µs
budget = 50% over-admission.

## Real-world impact

Frames carrying many small handoffs (typical: hundreds of glyph-
slot demotes per frame at 1-3KB each, well below NVMe N=3000 B/µs)
will systematically over-admit. The 10% disk-handoff budget reserve
(per docs/render/atlas-disk-tier-handoff-integration.md) becomes a
weaker guarantee than the runbook claims.

For a frame with 500 small handoffs at NVMe class (10% reserve =
1667 µs budget): worst-case over-admission ≈ 500 × 2999 = ~1.5MB
extra throughput dispatched, ~0.5ms additional dispatch time
(~30% of the budget consumed phantomly).

## Fix

Sum bytes BEFORE dividing, not after. Replace the per-call
floor-divide-then-add with a single accumulated-bytes check:

    let next_total = self.admitted_bytes.saturating_add(handoff.bytes);
    let next_cost = self.cost_microseconds(next_total);
    if next_cost > budget_us { defer }
    else { self.admitted_bytes = next_total; admit }

This gives the accurate `floor((a+b)/N) ≤ budget` check without
fractional loss.

## Acceptance

- Both `FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer::admit_or_defer` and
  `DiskBudgetEstimator::admit_or_defer` use the next-total
  cost computation.
- A new test exercises the 6×1500-byte / N=3000 / budget=2 µs
  scenario and asserts the 7th admit (which would push acc=10500
  → cost 3 > 2) is the FIRST to defer; the algorithm currently
  admits it.
- Existing 13 + 8 tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- ft-ktd19.3 slice 1 (FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer) at bdd118ed8.
- ft-ktd19.3 slice (DiskBudgetEstimator) at 494e31116.
- Runbook: docs/render/atlas-disk-tier-handoff-integration.md.
- Substrate: crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs
  (both estimator types).
close_reason: Fixed atlas frame/disk budget gates to charge ceil next-total transfer cost and defer zero-budget nonzero work; verified via atlas_tiered_swap_frame_budget and inline disk cost test.

title: MCP bridge composes remote proxy tools in no-db degraded mode without audit
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs found that degraded no-db server builds still compose remote MCP proxy tools after the local db_path split, and the proxy layer falls back to an unaudited wrapper when db_path is None.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:88-99 makes build_server route through build_server_degraded, and lines 381-390 route run_stdio_server(None) through the same no-db builder.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:337-365 handles the local no-db branch, then lines 367-370 unconditionally call super::mcp_proxy::compose_proxy_tools(builder, config.as_ref(), db_path.clone()) under the mcp-client feature. In degraded mode that db_path is None.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs:185-193 enters proxy composition whenever mcp_client.proxy_enabled is true.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs:426-436 wraps mounted remote handlers in AuditedToolHandler only when db_path is Some; otherwise it registers FormatAwareToolHandler::new(handler) with no audit DB.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:140-147 documents AuditedToolHandler as the wrapper that records every tool call, and lines 168-220 show the audit write.
- Existing mcp_proxy tests around lines 1030-1414 exercise compose_proxy_tools(..., None) mainly for selection/fallback counters; the bridge has no degraded-mode test that proxy_enabled either fails closed or emits a no-audit warning/counter.

Why it matters:
An operator can start the bridge in explicit degraded mode expecting a stripped local surface, but if MCP proxying is configured, remote tools can still be mounted and invoked without the normal MCP audit trail. That creates a cross-module fail-open path between mcp_bridge and mcp_proxy.

Proposed remediation:
Make proxy composition in build_server_degraded fail closed unless a real audit db_path is configured, or require an explicit config opt-in that logs/counts the unaudited proxy surface. Add bridge-level tests with mcp_client.proxy_enabled=true and db_path=None asserting remote proxy tools are rejected or that a dedicated unaudited-proxy degraded counter/warning fires and no mutation-capable remote tools mount.
notes:
Shipped fix: added cross-module fail-closed gate in compose_proxy_tools to prevent the bridge degraded mode from silently mounting unaudited remote proxy tools.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_proxy.rs):

1. New static MCP_PROXY_UNAUDITED_DEGRADED_SKIPS atomic counter + public mcp_proxy_unaudited_degraded_skip_count accessor + cfg(test) reset helper + private record helper. Same observability shape as MCP_PROXY_MOUNT_FAILURES (ft-59hlx), MCP_PROXY_DESTRUCTIVE_FILTERED (ft-153dy), MCP_BRIDGE_TOOLS_SKIPPED_NO_DB (ft-647cj).

2. New no-db gate in compose_proxy_tools placed after the mcp_client.enabled mismatch check but before discover_servers. When db_path is None and proxy is enabled, fails closed in strict mode (proxy_strict OR not proxy_fallback_to_local) returning ConfigError; otherwise bumps the counter, emits a structured tracing::warn (target ft::mcp_proxy, event mcp_proxy_unaudited_degraded_skip), and returns the unchanged builder.

title: [ARCH] HandoffAwareResumePlan wires HandoffCapsule into SessionResumer (ft-1650n.5 slice 3)
description:
Slice 3 of ft-1650n.5 shipped this commit at crate::session_resume_with_handoff (feature-gated session-resume).

Wires HandoffCapsule into the SessionResumer code path via a two-phase commit pattern that keeps capsule application isolated from the underlying casr subprocess:

PRE-RESUME plan.preflight_validate()
  → integrity check + destination-compatibility validation
  → returns Allowed sections (indices) + Skipped sections
  → on integrity mismatch / version mismatch → bail BEFORE any casr subprocess runs (no side effects from a tampered or incompatible capsule)

RESUME plan.invoke_resume(&SessionResumer)
  → delegates to SessionResumer::resume_session
  → runs the casr subprocess

POST-RESUME plan.apply_to_resumed_session(resume_output, validation, per_section_outcomes)
  → produces an AppliedHandoffSummary recording session_id, target_provider_slug, resumed_session_id (from CasrResumeOutput.target_session_id), capsule_version, accepted_indices, skipped_count, applied: Vec<SectionApplyOutcome>

SectionApplyOutcome carries section_index + section_label + SectionDisposition (Applied / SkippedByPolicy { reason } / Errored { error }) so operators can distinguish 'tried and failed' from 'preflight said no' for triage.

AppliedHandoffSummary.is_clean() returns false iff any section Errored. .disposition_counts() bins per category for dashboards. Three stable skip-by-policy reasons (REDUNDANT_WITH_DESTINATION / OPERATOR_OPTED_OUT / INHERITANCE_DISABLED_FOR_KIND) so consumers can filter consistently.

Bonus: section_kind_compatible_with_destination(section, LifecycleEntityKind) — pure-function predicate that gates PassportExcerpt to pane-scoped destinations (rejected at session-scoped or window-scoped destinations).

Coverage: 8 unit tests:
- preflight_validate_returns_full_acceptance_when_destination_satisfies_all + ProbeRunner sanity-check.
- preflight_validate_skips_sections_destination_cannot_satisfy.
- preflight_validate_short_circuits_on_integrity_mismatch_before_resume (proves casr subprocess never runs on tampered capsule).
- preflight_validate_no_destination_passport_skips_every_guarded_section (fail-closed).
- apply_to_resumed_session_records_per_section_dispositions (Applied + SkippedByPolicy + Errored mix).
- applied_summary_is_clean_when_no_errored.
- section_kind_compatible_with_destination_passport_excerpt_requires_pane.
- section_kind_compatible_unguarded_kinds_apply_anywhere.
- applied_summary_serde_roundtrip.

Verified: cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --features session-resume finished in 1m18s with 0 errors. cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features finished in 51s with 0 errors (module is correctly feature-gated). 

What's NOT in scope: the actual operator-side apply functions that consume each accepted section into the destination's stores (passport-store insertion for PassportExcerpt, mission-state inheritance, etc.). The planner produces the summary; the caller decides what to do with each accepted section. Those wiring beads can be filed per section type as the handoff CLI lands (ft-yk9lp follow-up).

title: fd_budget invalid config thresholds and leak window fail open
description:
Phase 3 audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/fd_budget.rs.

Evidence:
- FdBudgetConfig exposes public serde fields warn_threshold, refuse_threshold, fds_per_pane, min_nofile_limit, audit_interval_secs, and leak_detection_count with no validate method.
- can_admit_pane compares projected/limit against warn_threshold and refuse_threshold directly; NaN thresholds make both comparisons false and allow admission.
- audit() computes max_entries = leak_detection_count * 2, uses history.len() >= leak_detection_count, and indexes history[history.len() - leak_detection_count]. With leak_detection_count=0, the window predicate is vacuously true and the index can panic after history pruning.
- Existing fd_budget tests cover ordinary finite thresholds and large counters but do not cover NaN/Inf thresholds, warn > refuse, or leak_detection_count=0.

Why it matters:
FD budget is a fail-closed resource gate for large pane fleets. Malformed persisted/operator config should not silently allow pane admission or panic the audit loop.

Proposed remediation:
Add FdBudgetConfig validation requiring finite ordered thresholds in [0,1], nonzero fds_per_pane, nonzero min_nofile_limit, and leak_detection_count > 0. Constructors should reject invalid config or normalize to a fail-closed config. Add property tests for NaN/Inf/misordered thresholds and zero leak window.

description:

The 5 export query functions in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage/export.rs` accept `conn: &Connection` and use `Box<dyn ToSql>` dynamic-param builders. To complete the ft-l1jgo trait migration for export-domain callsites, refactor the submodule.

title: aegis_entropy_anomaly::EProcess::update propagates NaN e_value; permanently disables rejection
description: EProcess::update calls likelihood_ratio(h, baseline_mean, baseline_std, collapse_mean, collapse_std). If any f64 input is NaN, log_h0 and log_h1 both become NaN, log_lr = NaN - NaN = NaN, log_lr.exp() = NaN, and clamp(1e-6, 1e6) passes NaN through because f64::clamp does not reject NaN. self.e_value *= NaN = NaN. The final clamp(1e-100, max_e) at update:226 also passes NaN through. Future is_rejected() returns (NaN >= threshold) = false, silently disabling anomaly detection for the lifetime of this EProcess. Matches ft-b4l62 / ft-yskcu / ft-c17iw / ft-n4fdx pattern — fail-closed on non-finite inputs at the update() boundary.

title: latency memory pool high-water mark accepts non-finite and out-of-range thresholds
description:
Phase 3 audit finding in latency_stages::memory_pool.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages/memory_pool.rs:78-90 exposes PoolConfig as public serde data and documents high_water_mark as a fraction in 0.0..1.0.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages/memory_pool.rs:162-176 constructs MemoryPool directly from the supplied config without validation or clamping.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages/memory_pool.rs:223-225 compares utilization against high_water_mark directly. With NaN the comparison is always false; with negative thresholds the pool is immediately under pressure; with thresholds above 1.0 pressure may never fire.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages/memory_pool.rs:357-371 turns under_pressure into HighUtilization health, so malformed config can suppress or force degradation.

Proposed remediation: add PoolConfig validation for finite high_water_mark in 0.0..=1.0 and sensible block counts, then reject or normalize invalid config at MemoryPool construction with tests for NaN, infinity, negative, and above-one thresholds.
close_reason: Fixed in 44c9cd8a2: MemoryPool now normalizes PoolConfig.high_water_mark during construction; finite values clamp to [0,1] and non-finite values fail closed to 0.0 so NaN/Inf cannot suppress pressure degradation. Added unit and property coverage for arbitrary threshold inputs. `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:204-330` defines ~25
regex patterns (anthropic_key, openai_key, github_*, stripe_key
[recently extended at br-ft-76zp6 to cover rk_*/whsec_*], etc.)
plus generic api_key/token/password/secret patterns.

The repo has 230+ proptest_*.rs files; one of them
(`proptest_diagnostic_redaction.rs`) covers the
`diagnostic_redaction` field-policy layer but **none** exercises
the core `Redactor` invariants. Coverage gap means regex changes
land with only inline `#[test]` per-format tests; structural
invariants (idempotence, no-leak-past-redact, detect-span
non-overlap, concat boundary stability) are unaudited.

A regex regression that erodes one of these contracts (e.g., a
catastrophic-backtracking pattern that produces partial
replacements, or an alternation reorder that lets a secret slip
past on the second pass) would not surface in the current test
matrix.

## Contract surface to pin

The Redactor advertises the following invariants (from
documentation + call-site assumptions):

1. **Idempotence**: `redact(redact(t)) == redact(t)` — applying
   the redactor twice yields the same output as applying it once.
2. **No-leak-past-redact**: `contains_secrets(redact(t))` is
   false — once redact() ran, the catalog's own `contains_secrets`
   predicate must report clean (otherwise downstream gates that
   check the predicate before persisting will short-circuit
   incorrectly).
3. **Marker stability**: every replacement is the exact
   `REDACTED_MARKER` constant ("[REDACTED]" in default mode,
   "[REDACTED:<name>]" in debug mode). No partial replacements,
   no marker truncation.
4. **Detect span discipline**: `detect()` returns spans whose
   `start..end` slice the input UTF-8 cleanly (boundary-safe)
   and whose starts are monotonically non-decreasing (sorted).
5. **Empty-input invariant**: `redact("")` returns "".
6. **Plain-text passthrough**: text that contains no
   catalog-pattern matches must be returned verbatim — no
   spurious redactions from generic patterns biting innocuous
   alphanumeric strings shorter than the credential thresholds.

## Acceptance

- New `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_redactor_conformance.rs`
  hosts a proptest suite covering the 6 invariants.
- Per-pattern smoke tests: for each high-priority catalog format
  (anthropic_key, openai_key, github_*, stripe_*, aws_*,
  jwt_token), generate a synthetic-but-shape-conforming string
  and assert redact strips it AND contains_secrets reports
  clean post-redact.
- Suite runs under
  `cargo test --test proptest_redactor_conformance --no-default-features`.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs` (target)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_diagnostic_redaction.rs`
  (sister harness shape — field-policy layer)
- ft-76zp6 (recent regex catalog extension; would have been
  caught earlier had a stripe_key catalog-coverage proptest
  existed)

Composes with sibling proptest_diagnostic_redaction.rs (field-policy layer above) — together they cover the redactor stack end-to-end.

title: [ARCH/storage] §8.13 SuRF (Succinct Range Filters) for ts >= ? prefilter on retention queries
description:
Phase-3 alien-graveyard match for storage/search domain.

## Symptom

storage.rs:14219 / 14324 / 14447 (and similar sites) issue `WHERE ts >= ?` queries against the events / segments / audit tables for retention sweeps + range scans. SQLite uses its B-tree index on ts directly, which is fine for narrow ranges but degrades for very-old-cutoff sweeps (most of the table is read).

## Algorithm match

§8.13 from the alien-graveyard catalog: SuRF (Succinct Range Filters, Zhang et al. 2018). A succinct trie over the indexed column that answers range queries in O(k) where k is the key length, with bounded false-positive rate + zero false-negatives. Used as a PREFILTER before the SQLite scan: SuRF says 'this range MIGHT have matches' or 'definitely no matches'. False-positive case falls back to the SQLite scan; false-negative case never occurs.

## Integration point

A new `crate::storage_range_filter` (sibling module pattern, mirroring storage_cardinality_sketch.rs) wrapping the `surf` crate (or hand-rolled FST). Maintained per-table:
- `StorageRangeFilter::new(table)`
- `record_range(ts_min, ts_max)` — called by the writer thread on every insert.
- `could_have_match(ts_low, ts_high) -> bool` — called by the reader path BEFORE the SQLite query.
- Persistence: serialize to a sidecar file in `.ft/range_filters/<table>.surf` so SuRF state survives process restart.

## Why P3 not P2

The documented hot path (200-agent fleet) is dominated by point/narrow-range queries, not big retention sweeps. SuRF wins for the retention-sweep case which is operator-triggered + infrequent (daily/weekly cron). P3 because it's a real win but not on the 24/7 hot path.

## Proof obligations

1. False-negative rate: 0 (per SuRF design).
2. False-positive rate: bounded by the suffix-bits configuration (default 4 bits → ~6% FPR).
3. Range query is correct: `could_have_match(L, H)` returns true for every (L, H) covering at least one observed range.

## Cross-references

- alien-graveyard catalog §8.13.
- storage.rs:14219, 14324, 14447 (the range-query sites).
- The `surf` crate (LSM-fast-succinct-trie author's reference impl).

title: [ALIEN-UPLIFT] table-driven CRC32-IEEE (Sarwate 1988) sibling module
description:
[ALIEN-UPLIFT/SUBSTRATE] Sarwate 1988 table-driven CRC32-IEEE shipped as sibling module crate::crc32_table.

Replaces the bitwise reference impl's 8-iteration inner loop per byte with a single XOR + 256-entry table lookup. Per-byte cost drops from `8 × (cmp + xor + shr)` to `1 × (xor + shr + load)` — typically 3-5× wall-clock speedup on AArch64 / x86-64.

Reference: Sarwate, Dilip V. (1988) "Computation of cyclic redundancy checks via table look-up", Communications of the ACM 31(8):1008-1013.

Hotspot found during alien-graveyard sweep (cc1, 2026-05-03):
- crate::cell_consistency_crc::crc32_ieee (line 139) is the bitwise reference impl.
- The doc comment explicitly invites a tabled replacement: "the integration layer can swap in a tabled version if hot-path benchmarks demand it."
- Used by hash_cell_grid (line 166) which fuses FNV-1a + CRC32 in a per-byte inner loop on cell-grid data.

Substrate API:
- crc32_ieee_tabled(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32
- Output is BIT-FOR-BIT identical to the bitwise reference (verified on standard vectors + 50 pseudorandom inputs in equivalence_on_pseudorandom_inputs test).
- Table is `static [u32; 256]` generated at compile time via const fn (no precomputed-table-as-data dependency).

Coverage (7 unit tests, lib-level cargo check clean in 22s):
- empty_input_yields_zero
- single_byte_zero_yields_known_value (0x00 → 0xD202EF8D)
- classic_vector_quick_brown_fox ("The quick brown fox..." → 0x414FA339)
- classic_vector_123456789 ("123456789" → 0xCBF43926, the canonical CRC32 conformance vector cited in ITU-T V.42, IEEE 802.3, PNG, gzip)
- equivalence_with_bitwise_reference_on_diverse_inputs (9 inputs including binary, all-zeros, all-ones)
- equivalence_on_pseudorandom_inputs (50 LCG-generated buffers, lengths up to 1024)
- table_first_and_last_entries_match_polynomial (sanity-pin against hand-derivable values)

Ecosystem scan (per alien-graveyard methodology):
- crc32fast crate exists, widely used. Considered + rejected for this substrate: cell_consistency_crc.rs's design constraint is "dependency-free", which is satisfied by the const-fn-generated table here. Production callers can opt into crc32fast at the integration layer if SIMD speedup is needed beyond the 3-5× this provides.

Sibling-module pattern: top-level crate::crc32_table avoids contention on cell_consistency_crc.rs (32KB file with 14+ struct-literal callsites). Integration into crc32_ieee + hash_cell_grid is a follow-up bead.

EV score:
- Impact 3 (cell-grid hashing per-frame in consistency checks; 3-5× speedup on inner loop).
- Confidence 5 (Sarwate 1988 is textbook; identical output verified).
- Reuse 4 (any CRC32-IEEE callsite — also consider archive formats, PNG handling).
- Effort 2 (single-file substrate, ~180 LOC including tests + comprehensive coverage).
- Friction 2 (substrate-only; integration is follow-up bead).
- EV = (3 × 5 × 4) / (2 × 2) = 15.0 ≫ 2.0 ✓

Cross-references:
- Substrate: crates/frankenterm-core/src/crc32_table.rs (this commit).
- Module declaration: crates/frankenterm-core/src/lib.rs (between crash_persistence_gate and crdt).
- Integration follow-up: ft-IDtoBeFiled (replace cell_consistency_crc::crc32_ieee + inline in hash_cell_grid with crc32_ieee_tabled).
notes: Shipped this commit. crate::crc32_table::crc32_ieee_tabled available; library compile clean (cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features finished in 22s with 0 errors). 7 unit tests covering empty, single byte, 'The quick brown fox', '123456789' canonical conformance vector, equivalence with bitwise reference on 9 diverse + 50 pseudorandom inputs, table sanity. Integration follow-up filed as ft-IDtoBeFiled (replaces this in HEAD).

title: [mock-code-finder][storage] Implement Frankensqlite recorder and Tantivy event-reader path
description:
## Finding
The mock-code-finder pass found a real runtime placeholder, not just test scaffolding: Frankensqlite recorder support is exposed in selectors/descriptors and surrounding migration/audit/advisor surfaces, but live execution still rejects or falls back. This creates a truthfulness gap for operators evaluating storage migration and search indexing.

## Evidence
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_storage.rs:40 describes RecorderBackendKind::FrankenSqlite as follow-on work.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_storage.rs:52 rejects deserializing the frankensqlite backend with a not-yet-implemented error.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_storage.rs:611 returns BackendUnavailable when bootstrap_recorder_storage sees RecorderBackendKind::FrankenSqlite.
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_ingest.rs:833 chooses RecorderSourceDescriptor::FrankenSqlite but immediately returns frankensqlite_unsupported("ingest").
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_reindex.rs:53 likewise rejects Frankensqlite reindex sources.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_workload_advisor.rs:517 always recommends Rusqlite until this backend lands.
- Existing Beads searches for frankensqlite-recorder, ft-lzbkn, RecorderSourceDescriptor FrankenSqlite, and workload advisor Rusqlite returned no open tracker item for this exact recorder/indexer gap. ft-kcdqp is related but closed/deferred around the lower-level backend factory seam.

## Scope
1. Implement the Frankensqlite recorder storage backend behind the existing feature flag or remove the exposed selector until support is real.
2. Provide a RecorderEventReader for RecorderSourceDescriptor::FrankenSqlite usable by incremental ingest and deterministic reindex/backfill.
3. Replace fallback-only startup behavior with explicit configured behavior: either real Frankensqlite or a documented fail-closed migration gate that cannot be mistaken for active support.
4. Update the storage workload advisor so it can recommend Frankensqlite only from measured conditions and only when the backend is actually available.
5. Update operator/docs/error text so feature names, config names, and migration guidance describe the live state exactly.

## Tests and proof
- Unit tests for backend selection, bootstrap health, reader cursor ordering, checkpoint monotonicity, torn-tail/corruption behavior, and feature-disabled errors.
- Integration tests proving incremental ingest and reindex read the same recorder events from append-log and Frankensqlite sources.
- Golden JSON/TOON or structured logs for degraded startup, fallback/fail-closed, and advisor recommendation states.
- Heavy Rust proof must run through RCH only; if RCH worker health is unavailable, close or block with exact no-worker/topology reason and do not substitute local proof.

## Acceptance
- No production path emits a not-yet-implemented Frankensqlite recorder/indexer message unless the feature is intentionally disabled and the error says that precisely.
- Frankensqlite recorder source can be ingested and reindexed by Tantivy without using mock in-memory stand-ins.
- Advisor recommendations are tied to real backend availability and measured workload predicates.
- Existing append-log behavior remains unchanged and covered by parity tests.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty after dependencies are added.

title: [fuzz] add FtviIndex::from_bytes harness for vector index loader
description:
The FTVI vector-index binary loader is public and currently unfuzzed.

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/mod.rs:73` publicly re-exports `FtviIndex`.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/vector_index.rs:218-267` parses attacker-controlled bytes in `FtviIndex::from_bytes`, including magic/version checks, dimension/count headers, and per-record half-float decoding loops.
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml` has no target for `FtviIndex::from_bytes`.

Why it matters:
- This is a binary format loader over persisted search state, so malformed bytes can hit allocation pressure, unexpected EOF handling, half-float edge cases, and count/dimension loops.
- The surface is already public, synchronous, and easy to fuzz without extra seams.

Fix:
- Add a fuzz target that exercises both arbitrary raw bytes and structured valid FTVI buffers via `write_ftvi_vec` round-trips, asserting parse no-panics and round-trip sanity where applicable.

title: [MEDIUM] no semantic_schema_version marker; vector store not invalidated on storage schema migration
close_reason: Shipped in 821edfad: semantic store metadata records schema/embedder markers and invalidates stale embeddings on mismatch (verification partial; rch lane quiet after compile)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
# Gap

`ft_meta` (crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs, wa_meta→ft_meta rename
at line 4714) tracks the main storage schema version via `user_version`
and `record_migration`. The vector store in
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/search/chunk_vector_store.rs` tracks its own
`lexical_schema_version` per generation (line 57) but nothing ties the
two together.

There is NO `semantic_schema_version` / `vector_store_version` row in
ft_meta. If storage.rs migrations change the semantic contract
(for example: change how segment ordinals are assigned, change the
content_hash function, bump the chunk policy implicitly), the vector
store silently retains the old embeddings indexed under the old contract
and continues serving them from `semantic_search`.

Today's scenario is benign because migrations v18/v19/v21 don't touch
the semantic chunk surface. But the guardrail is missing.

# Why this matters

When storage schema bumps, the semantic store should either:
(a) be invalidated (DELETE all rows, mark generation Failed, force reindex),
(b) be version-gated (writes after bump must use the new contract, reads
    from old rows are filtered), or
(c) explicitly documented as schema-independent with a test that freezes
    the coupling.

None of (a)/(b)/(c) is present.

# Shape of fix

Smallest defensive move (≤30 LOC, safe to land):

* Add `semantic_schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` column to
  `semantic_generations` via a new migration.
* On orchestrator startup, if a generation's stored version < current
  const `SEMANTIC_SCHEMA_VERSION`, mark it inactive or Failed with a
  reason string and force a rebuild.

Larger defensive move: add a `semantic_schema_version` row to `ft_meta`
and enforce match at generation register time.

# Out of scope

Actually migrating the contract. This bead is the version-marker only,
so future contract changes HAVE a graceful invalidation path.

title: runtime telemetry fairness enabled with default budgets is effectively a no-op
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs found that enabling fairness without explicit finite budgets preserves effectively unlimited admission.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5084-5090 defines enabled plus admission_budget_units and reduced_admission_budget_units as the controls that should let fairness reorder/defer/shed requests.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5095-5101 defaults enabled=false, admission_budget_units=u32::MAX, reduced_admission_budget_units=u32::MAX / 2.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5279-5305 shows the disabled path admits every request and reports budget_units=u32::MAX.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5311-5339 shows the enabled path admits while admitted_units + requested_units <= budget_units.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:5125-5131 uses reduced_admission_budget_units.min(admission_budget_units) under ReduceAdmission, so enabled=true with otherwise-default budgets still leaves a 2B-unit budget and will admit all realistic request sets.
- Existing tests exercise finite explicit budgets at runtime_telemetry.rs:11772-11840, but there is no guard that enabled=true requires finite budgets or changes behavior from disabled defaults.

Why it matters: an operator can flip fairness_policy.enabled expecting request-level capacity control, while the default budgets make the enabled policy behave like pass-through for normal swarm sizes. That is a silent fail-open configuration surface and makes controller summaries imply fairness control that is not operationally constraining admission.

Proposed remediation: add validation/normalization for enabled fairness that requires explicit finite budgets, or derive finite budgets from queue pressure/request count when enabled. Add tests for enabled=true + default budgets to fail validation or produce a bounded plan, plus a summary/config warning reason code for legacy/unbounded fairness settings.
notes: Added validate_budgets() method on SwarmCapacityFairnessPolicyConfig. New FairnessBudgetError enum (UnboundedAdmissionBudget | ZeroAdmissionBudget | UnboundedReducedBudget | ReducedAboveAdmission{reduced,admission}) with Display+Error impls; all messages embed br-ft-f4njb breadcrumb. Disabled policy passes through (no validation needed since fairness does nothing). Enabled policy must carry: admission_budget_units < u32::MAX (catches the silent fail-open default), admission_budget_units > 0 (zero blocks all Allow paths), reduced_admission_budget_units < u32::MAX, reduced <= admission (the .min() in budget_for accidentally papered over misordered config but it's still operator-confusing). Added 6 tests: disabled+default passes, enabled+default rejects with UnboundedAdmissionBudget+breadcrumb, enabled+zero rejects, enabled+unbounded-reduced rejects, enabled+reduced>admission rejects with matches! variant pattern, enabled+finite passes. Method-on-config so existing call sites are unaffected; operators / config loaders opt in to fail closed. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: Serialized IdempotencyKey can forge raw key and step metadata mismatch
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs found that IdempotencyKey exposes derived state to serde without validation. The type derives Serialize/Deserialize over private key, plan_id, and step_id fields (tx_idempotency.rs:29-37). Normal constructors derive key from plan_id, step_id, and action content (tx_idempotency.rs:39-59), but deserialization can set key to any txk value while reporting an unrelated plan_id or step_id. Deduplication and ledger lookup trust only idem_key.as_str through key_index and DeduplicationGuard (tx_idempotency.rs:350-359, 539-540), while resume classification trusts idem_key.step_id from records to compute completed, failed, compensated, and remaining steps (tx_idempotency.rs:660-686). Existing tests only roundtrip constructor-built keys (tx_idempotency.rs:1017-1023; tests/proptest_tx_idempotency.rs:140-154), so they never exercise mismatched serialized fields. Why it matters: a malformed persisted ledger can alias a raw key from one step while claiming completion/failure for a different step, corrupting both dedup decisions and resume accounting. Proposed remediation: add custom Deserialize validation for IdempotencyKey, at minimum enforcing txk:16hex format and rejecting impossible/mismatched persisted forms; ideally persist a canonical source tuple or store only opaque raw keys and keep step metadata in the execution record. Add malformed JSON regression tests where raw key and step_id disagree and verify load fails or resume refuses the ledger.
notes:
Shipped full hash-input-authentication fix. Sibling had earlier shipped a minimum-viable form (format check + non-empty fields, 8 unit tests + 2 proptests) but the headline bead concern (cross-step alias attack: valid txk:HASH from step A claimed against step_id from step B) was NOT actually detected by format-only validation. cc1 extended to the bead body's ideal remediation per the proposed-remediation text.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs):

1. New private field hash_input on IdempotencyKey storing the post-plan_id|step_id| segment of the original FNV-1a hash input. For new() this is the action_fingerprint as-is; for_compensation() this is comp:{kind} with the comp: prefix included. Stored verbatim so the validator can re-derive without needing to know which constructor was used.

2. New private compute_key helper centralizing the canonical-form derivation. Used by both constructors and the deserialize validator (single source of truth).

3. Custom Deserialize impl now performs four checks in order: format check (txk:16hex lowercase), non-empty plan_id, non-empty step_id, and hash-match check (re-derive expected key from plan_id + step_id + hash_input and compare to persisted key). The hash-match is the load-bearing addition that catches cross-step aliasing.

Tests (mod tests):

4. 6 existing reject tests updated to include hash_input in JSON fixtures (validation order means earlier checks fire before hash check, so hash_input value is arbitrary for those reject paths).

5. Three new unit tests for the cross-step alias attack:
   - key_deserialize_rejects_cross_step_alias_ft_f4vta: keep step-as key + hash_input but alias step_id to step-b. Pre-fix slipped through; post-fix rejected.
   - key_deserialize_rejects_tampered_hash_input_ft_f4vta: keep real key + plan_id/step_id but tamper hash_input. Rejected.
   - key_deserialize_rejects_tampered_key_with_valid_format_ft_f4vta: tamper key to a different valid txk format string while keeping plan_id/step_id/hash_input intact. Format check passes; hash-match fires.

6. New proptest key_deserialize_rejects_cross_tuple_alias_property: for any pair of distinct (plan_a, step_a, action_a) and (plan_b, step_b, action_b) tuples, mixing one tuples key with the others source fields must reject. Skips the rare hash-collision case (where the two tuples coincidentally produce the same key) since those are not the alias attack.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 1m06s clean
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean
- Zero behavioral change for legitimate constructor-built keys (constructor outputs always round-trip through validator per existing key_constructor_output_always_round_trips proptest)
- Chain-format change (hash_input added to serialized form) — same kind of break as ft-e9r75 just shipped, operators regenerate ledgers

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
- Add custom Deserialize validation for IdempotencyKey: DONE
- At minimum: enforcing txk:16hex format: DONE (sibling minimum-viable + cc1 extension)
- Rejecting impossible/mismatched persisted forms: DONE (hash-match gate catches cross-step alias)
- Ideally: persist a canonical source tuple so step metadata can be re-verified: DONE (hash_input field)
- Add malformed JSON regression tests where raw key and step_id disagree: DONE (3 unit tests + 1 proptest)

title: [profiling] ARS evidence ledger: 41KB workflow forensics surface; zero benches
description:
## Hypothesis

`crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs` (41 KB) is the
evidence-ledger module — appends-and-verifies digests of robot/
mission/tx decision evidence so post-incident forensics can prove
"X happened in this order with this signature". Per the existing
proptest at `tests/proptest_ars_evidence.rs:6`, the surface includes
`EvidenceEntry`, `LedgerDigest`, `ChainVerification`.

`grep -lE "ars_evidence\|EvidenceLedger\|ChainVerification" benches/*.rs`
returns zero hits. Production cost is unknown.

## Why a profile + bench would deliver real perf gain

Evidence ledger writes happen on the workflow + mission + tx hot
paths — every step appends an entry. Verification runs at incident-
review time, but ALSO during checkpoint-resume and replay. Risk:

- **Append cost is in the workflow critical path.** A workflow
  with 50 steps × 100 panes × 5 evidence rows per step = 25K
  entries per session. If append is O(log N) with hashing
  per-entry, the per-step latency adds up.
- **Verification cost is O(N) chain-walk.** A session with 100K
  entries reverifying on resume could pin the resume path for
  seconds before the first action.
- **Hash + signature crypto** — what's the per-entry crypto cost?
  If using `ring` or `sha2` per entry, that's a measurable share
  of step latency.
- **Memory growth** — does the ledger keep all entries in memory
  for the session, or stream to disk?

The skill's hand-off contract says: rank these with evidence
before optimizing. Today we have NO evidence.

## Suggested instrumentation + bench

1. **Bench**: `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/ars_evidence_ledger.rs`
   (or place under `crates/frankenterm-core-ars/benches/`):
   - **append throughput**: 1K, 10K, 100K entries; measure
     ops/sec + p95.
   - **verification cost**: build a 10K-entry chain, run
     `verify()`; measure ms.
   - **chain-tail re-verification**: append 100 then verify only
     the tail vs full chain.
   - **memory**: peak RSS during a 100K-entry session (likely
     candidate for the RAM-for-speed tradeoff).

2. **Crypto attribution**: use `samply` to identify whether
   `sha2::Sha256::update` dominates the append flame. If so,
   batched hashing or a faster hash (e.g., Blake3) is the
   immediate optimization target.

3. **Allocation attribution**: dhat — `EvidenceEntry` per-row
   alloc count.

## Hypothesis ledger entries

```
append-cost-linear-in-chain   : pending — ops/sec at 1K entries
                                  vs 100K entries (should be flat)
verify-dominates-resume       : pending — checkpoint-resume p95
                                  is > workflow first-action p95
sha256-dominates-append-cpu   : pending — flame shows
                                  sha2::Sha256::update
                                  > 30% of append CPU
unbounded-memory-per-session  : pending — heaptrack shows linear
                                  growth across 100K entries
```

## Out of scope

- The `frankenterm-core-ars` workflow / drift / fst / federation
  sub-modules (each may need its own profile pass).
- ARS schema validation (covered by proptest_ars_evidence).

## Acceptance criteria

- `benches/ars_evidence_ledger.rs` exists with four workloads.
- Profile run produces hotspot table — top-3 cost centers
  attributed.
- Memory growth over 100K-entry session captured via `heaptrack`.
- Hypothesis ledger entries marked with evidence paths.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs` (41 KB)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_ars_evidence.rs:6`
  (existing proptest — shape coverage, not perf)
- Skill: profiling-software-performance — operator card "Attribute"
  for crypto-vs-allocation cost split

Filed by cc_1 profiling audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: added ARS evidence ledger Criterion baseline, perf ledger, and artifacts

title: [ft-cnil8.4 review] RecorderHandle and ContractRecorder are parallel/uncoordinated a11y recorders
description:
[MEDIUM] integration gap discovered during cc_2's review pass.

## Symptom

Two independent in-memory accessibility recorders ship in the same crate, with overlapping purpose but incompatible APIs:

1. `frankenterm_core::a11y_tree::ContractRecorder` (a11y_tree.rs:229) — implements the `AccessibilityRecorder` trait (a11y_tree.rs:212). Consumed by the GUI bridge at crates/frankenterm-gui/src/smart_selection_a11y.rs (cc_3's commit 6bd3b34c1) via `&mut dyn AccessibilityRecorder`.

2. `frankenterm_core::smart_selection_a11y_recorder::RecorderHandle` (cc_2's commit d99d6d0f4) — `Arc<Mutex<Vec<AccessibilityEvent>>>` cloneable. Does NOT implement `AccessibilityRecorder` (different `&mut self` vs `&self` shape).

## Why this is a defect

The recorder I shipped (`RecorderHandle`) was positioned as the "companion test fixture for the AT-tree announcement assertion" per the substrate's commit message. But the actual production-side bridge does not use it — the bridge takes a `&mut dyn AccessibilityRecorder` and the GUI fixture-side tests (per the bridge's test imports) use `ContractRecorder`.

Net result: `RecorderHandle` is orphaned substrate. New tests that want to assert against a smart-selection announcement choose between two parallel recorders, and there's no way for one test to use both surfaces.

## Affected files

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/smart_selection_a11y_recorder.rs (RecorderHandle)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/a11y_tree.rs (ContractRecorder + AccessibilityRecorder trait)
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/smart_selection_a11y.rs (bridge — uses AccessibilityRecorder)

## Fix paths

Two options:

1. **Implement `AccessibilityRecorder` for `RecorderHandle`.** Requires reconciling the `&mut self` (trait) vs `&self` (handle's shared-arc design) split — likely needs a `RecorderHandle::lockable_mut(&self) -> impl AccessibilityRecorder` adapter. Preserves both APIs so existing tests on either side keep working.

2. **Retire `RecorderHandle`** and migrate its test users to `ContractRecorder`. Smaller surface, single recorder, but loses the cloneable-handle ergonomic for cross-thread test fixtures.

Option 1 is the cleaner one if the cloneable shared-handle pattern is load-bearing for any GUI test. Option 2 is right if `ContractRecorder` already covers the use case.

## Acceptance

- One canonical recorder type for AT-tree assertions in smart-selection contexts.
- The chosen recorder implements both: (a) the `AccessibilityRecorder` trait the bridge consumes, (b) the convenience accessors my recorder added (`find_announcement_for_kind`, `assert_announcement_for_kind`).
- The bridge's test at crates/frankenterm-gui/src/smart_selection_a11y.rs and the recorder's inline tests use the same type.

## Cross-references

- d99d6d0f4 (cc_2 RecorderHandle).
- 6bd3b34c1 (cc_3 GUI bridge using AccessibilityRecorder).
- ft-cnil8.4 (parent).
close_reason: RecorderHandle now implements AccessibilityRecorder and GUI bridge tests use it as the smart-selection recorder

title: Route mux-layout E2E cargo lanes through RCH only
description:
Audit finding from CoralBeaver after the ready queue was empty.

Problem:
- scripts/e2e_mux_layouts.sh runs cargo test through rch when RCH_BIN is present, but silently falls back to local cargo test when rch is missing.
- Heavy Cargo lanes must not run locally in this repo; local fallback can overload the shared host during swarm work.
- The RCH path also does not set a per-script CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so repeated or parallel runs can collide with default targets.

Scope:
1. Remove the local cargo test fallback from scripts/e2e_mux_layouts.sh.
2. Require RCH_BIN/rch for the cargo-test lanes, failing or skipping with an explicit prerequisite message when unavailable.
3. Run remote cargo tests with an isolated target dir such as /tmp/ft-e2e-mux-layouts-target.
4. Preserve dry-run output, per-filter log files, and pass/fail/skip accounting.

- scripts/e2e_mux_layouts.sh --dry-run shows rch exec with env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-e2e-mux-layouts-target.
- rg proves scripts/e2e_mux_layouts.sh no longer has a local cargo test fallback.
- git diff --check passes for the edited script.

title: pattern pack discovery followed symlinks out of tree
description:
# [HIGH] pattern-pack loader: symlink-escape via discover_packs_from_dir

**Subsystem:** patterns / scan_pipeline
**File:** crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs

## The hole

`load_pack_from_file(path, root)` routes through `sandbox_resolve` only when a
`Some(root)` is supplied. `discover_packs_from_dir`, used for
`.ft/patterns/**` discovery from a workspace root, was calling
`load_pack_from_file(path, None)` for every file + rules.toml it iterated —
so the sandbox check was **skipped** even though the dir itself was
workspace-attacker-controlled.

A hostile repo could ship:

    .ft/patterns/config.yaml -> /Users/victim/.ssh/id_rsa

`path.is_file()` follows the symlink (returns true), `load_pack_from_file`
opens the target, feeds its contents to `serde_yaml::from_str`, and on parse
failure emits:

    tracing::warn!("Skipping invalid user pack {}: {e}", path.display());

Which can echo excerpts of the target file via serde's error reporting
(`mapping expected, found: …`).

## Pre-conditions

* victim clones a hostile repo that contains a symlink under
  `.ft/patterns/`;
* frankenterm loads user packs at session start.

## Fix

`discover_packs_from_dir` now passes `Some(dir)` as the sandbox root to
`load_pack_from_file`. `sandbox_resolve` canonicalizes and rejects any
resolved path outside `dir`. Added regression test
`discover_packs_rejects_symlink_escape`.

## Residual risk

A top-level symlink replacing `.ft/patterns` itself would still escape
because the caller (`load_packs_from_config`) builds `ws_dir =
root_path.join(".ft").join("patterns")` without canonicalizing. That's a
follow-up — tracking separately.

## Sibling work

- 33e84436 security(patterns): add sandbox_resolve helper (helper introduction)
- e8397747 / 8e57c8e0 fix(limits): MAX_PACK_BYTES 16 MiB cap (orthogonal DoS layer)
close_reason: Fixed in 6ab52765 — canonicalize + in-tree check applied to pack discovery

title: [patterns] rate-limit regexes can pair distant anchors with unrelated retry text
description: Reasoning mode: statistical. The engine uses anchors only to select candidate rules, then applies a rule regex across the entire text segment. Builtin Codex and Claude rate-limit rules have anchors such as rate limit/429/529, but regexes that only look for retry/reset/wait/back off plus a duration (patterns.rs:1573-1588 and 1719-1731). A segment containing one rate-limit phrase and an unrelated 'wait 5 minutes' elsewhere can emit a false rate_limit.detected. Fix: require regex evidence to overlap or be near the matched anchor, or make these regexes include the rate-limit anchor terms; add a regression covering distant unrelated retry text.

title: [disk_pressure.fix] EwmaEstimator::new accepts NaN alpha and poisons all samples
description:
## Defect

EwmaEstimator::new at disk_pressure.rs:308-314:

    pub fn new(alpha: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            alpha: alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
            value: 0.0,
            initialized: false,
        }
    }

`f64::clamp` propagates NaN unchanged. So new(f64::NAN) stores
NaN as the alpha field. Then update() at line 325 computes:

    self.alpha.mul_add(sample, (1.0 - self.alpha) * self.value)

With self.alpha = NaN, mul_add returns NaN regardless of sample.
Every subsequent update returns NaN.

The update() function has an explicit NaN guard for the sample
(per the docstring about ft-761tz), but the same guard is
missing on the alpha field at construction.

## Fix

    pub fn new(alpha: f64) -> Self {
        let alpha = if alpha.is_nan() { 0.0 } else { alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0) };
        ...
    }

NaN alpha → 0.0 (no smoothing, treat as 'always use new sample
verbatim'). This is the same conservative choice the linter just
made for chaos::FaultMode::sanitize_probability.

Alternative considered: panic on NaN — but the rest of the
ewma surface is forgiving (NaN samples skip update), so the
constructor should match.

## Acceptance

- EwmaEstimator::new(f64::NAN).update(0.5) returns a finite
  value (not NaN).
- Existing tests with valid alpha still pass.
- New regression test pinning NaN alpha → finite output.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/disk_pressure.rs:308-314
- ft-761tz (sibling — update() NaN sample guard)
- ft-6qs6x, ft-eebc9, ft-p2xmz, ft-gldyy (validator-logic family)
- linter-shipped chaos.rs sanitize_probability (concurrent same-family fix)
close_reason: done

title: Tantivy quality InTopN assertion accepts n=0 which is unsatisfiable
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_quality.rs found InTopN relevance assertion has a degenerate case that always fails silently.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_quality.rs:76-77 defines InTopN{event_id, n: usize} as 'A specific event_id must appear within the top N results'.
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_quality.rs:364-385 implements the check as pos.is_some_and(|p| p < *n). When n==0, p < 0 is never true (usize positions are always >= 0), so the assertion always fails regardless of search results.
- No GoldenQuery validate / RelevanceAssertion validate path catches n==0 at config time. The assertion fires only at evaluate_assertion time, so a misconfigured n=0 only surfaces as a CI failure with a confusing 'event_id X not found in top 0' message.
- Existing tests at crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_quality.rs:791+ exercise n=1, n=5, etc but never the n=0 boundary.

Why it matters: golden-query suites are CI quality gates. A typo of n=0 (vs n=10) silently fails every run on that assertion and the failure message ('not in top 0') is operator-confusing — does it mean the suite is broken or the search engine regressed? Catching n==0 at GoldenQuery validate time produces a clear configuration-error path.

Proposed remediation: add a GoldenQuery::validate (or RelevanceAssertion::validate) method that rejects n==0 for InTopN with a structured error citing the assertion index. Add a unit test that constructing a suite with n=0 surfaces the validation error before any runner.run() call.
close_reason: Fixed in 982d48a50: QualityHarness construction now rejects InTopN assertions with n=0 using a structured QualityConfigError before any search run.

title: [SEC-hardening] RobotResponse envelope has no schema_version field — forward-compat detection impossible
description:
[SEC-hardening] RobotResponse envelope has no schema_version — forward-compat detection impossible across ft versions

## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_types.rs:51` defines:

    pub struct RobotResponse<T> {
        pub ok: bool,
        pub data: Option<T>,
        pub error: Option<String>,
        pub error_code: Option<String>,
        pub hint: Option<String>,
        pub elapsed_ms: u64,
        pub version: String,    // ft binary version (semver of the binary)
        pub now: u64,
    }

The envelope tracks `version` (the ft binary's semver) and `now`
(timestamp), but has NO `schema_version` field for the envelope
shape itself. Forward-compat across protocol versions is
unachievable:

- `version` describes the binary that emitted the response, not
  the envelope contract. The envelope shape can change without
  the binary version bumping (a bug-fix release that adds a
  field; a client running an older binary reading a newer
  server's envelope).
- A client reading a future envelope with new fields would
  silently drop them (serde default-skip-unknown). It can't
  surface "this envelope is from a newer schema; some fields
  may be missing from my view".
- A server reading a client's older envelope (e.g., for
  storage-replay forensic verification) can't anchor decoding
  against a known schema version — it has to guess from
  `version` which is at best a coarse proxy.

## Severity

P3 hardening. Not a security defect on its own — but the
audit_table chain stores robot envelopes, and forward-compat
verification on persisted envelopes (e.g., "decode a 6-month-old
audit row") needs a stable anchor that's separate from the
binary version. Same shape as ft-nucbz's tamper-evidence
watermark — exposing the structural anchor instead of leaving
it implicit.

## Fix

Add `pub schema_version: u32` field with
`#[serde(default = "default_robot_response_schema_version")]`
so:
- Outgoing envelopes always carry the constant (currently 1).
- Incoming envelopes that pre-date the field decode cleanly
  with `schema_version = 1` via the default.
- Future envelope shape changes bump the constant; clients
  can compare against their own constant and route through
  a compat layer if needed.

Add `RobotResponse::SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1` const so the
constant is operator-visible + tests can assert against it.

## Acceptance

- `RobotResponse<T>::SCHEMA_VERSION == 1`.
- `RobotResponse::success(data, elapsed_ms)` sets
  `schema_version = SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- Round-trip: serialize → deserialize → schema_version preserved.
- Forward-compat: parse a JSON envelope without `schema_version`
  field → `schema_version = 1` via serde default.
- Existing struct-literal constructors in tests continue to
  compile (use the default expression or explicit value).

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_types.rs:49-72 (RobotResponse)
- ft-nucbz (sibling — AuditChain tamper-evidence watermark, same
  "expose the anchor" pattern)
- ft-uesdi (sibling — envelope classification fail-closed)
close_reason: Shipped at 23abf63d3. RobotResponse now carries pub schema_version: u32 with #[serde(default = 1)] for forward-compat. RobotResponse::SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 const exposed; success() sets it; existing struct-literal tests updated. 5 tests pass: constant pinned, success ctor populates, round-trip preserves, wire JSON includes field, forward-compat decodes pre-fix envelopes (without schema_version) as version 1. Migration plan documented in commit message: bump constant + serde-default + test assertion in lockstep on shape change. Same shape as ft-nucbz tamper-evidence watermark.

title: [MEDIUM] Atlas tiered-swap frame loop lacks a production-shape performance bench
description:
Bench-vs-production gap from atlas tiered-swap performance review.

Evidence:
- Recent atlas tiered-swap commits added hot frame-loop pieces: DiskTierHandoffQueue, StagingTransferQueue, FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer, DiskBudgetEstimator, and AtlasBlitPlan.
- crates/frankenterm-core/Cargo.toml registers atlas_packing and heavy_burst benches, but no bench target exercises atlas_tiered_swap.rs or atlas_staging_blit_plan.rs.

The new atlas budget/queue/blit path is performance-sensitive, but current benches do not measure the production-shaped sequence or allocation behavior. That leaves regressions like repeated drain/refill allocation, admitted/deferred Vec churn, and command-plan allocation invisible to Criterion.

close_reason:
Shipped atlas_tiered_swap_frame_loop bench at 61e365a49. Drives the production-shape per-frame loop from docs/render/atlas-tiered-swap-wgpu-integration.md:72-85 (take carry-over → drain StagingTransferQueue → partition through FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer → emit AtlasBlitPlan::from_events → carry deferred → reset deferrer). Five workload shapes cover the envelope per the bead's expected criteria: empty, steady_small, mixed_promote_demote, carry_over_heavy, zero_budget_recovery. Each scenario records p50 + p95 over 240 frames (after 16 warmup) and panics if p95 > 200 µs — assertion-bearing pattern mirrors heavy_burst.rs.

Smoke (--quick) measurements, per-frame (per-iter timing / 240):
- empty: ~46 ns
- steady_small: ~122 ns
- mixed_promote_demote: ~311 ns
- carry_over_heavy: ~7.2 µs (worst case; 27× under budget)
- zero_budget_recovery: ~0.98 µs

All five scenarios pass. The bench exposes partition()'s per-frame Vec allocation (admitted + deferred) plus AtlasBlitPlan::from_events()'s command-Vec allocation — regressions like quadratic carry-over scans, repeated drain/refill churn, or O(N²) command-plan growth would surface here before reaching production.
