title: ARS compiler accepts incomplete evidence digests
description:
Reality-check audit finding in frankenterm-core-ars.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs:179-194 models LedgerDigest with entry_count, categories_present, and is_complete.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_evidence.rs:379-383 computes is_complete from required categories.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_compile.rs:247-255 only rejects EvidenceVerdict::Reject; it does not reject is_complete=false, entry_count=0, missing required categories, or malformed root_hash.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_compile.rs:590-630 builds a default digest with entry_count=0, categories_present=[], is_complete=false, and Neutral verdict. That fallback can still flow into compile.
- crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_ars_compile.rs:250-259 codifies that Neutral evidence always succeeds, with no completeness check.

Why it matters:
The ARS compiler is the promotion boundary from evidence to executable workflow. Incomplete or fallback digests can produce workflow descriptors even though the ledger says required proof categories are missing. That is a fail-open evidence gate.

Proposed remediation:
Make compile reject incomplete digests and empty/malformed roots before descriptor generation, add property tests that incomplete Support/Neutral digests fail, and consider passing a verified EvidenceLedger/ChainVerification result instead of a freely constructible LedgerDigest at the trust boundary.
notes: Shipped at f9f8d504f. ArsCompiler::compile now rejects incomplete digests (is_complete=false) and empty root_hash before descriptor generation via two new CompileError variants (IncompleteEvidence, MalformedEvidenceRoot) with bead-id-prefixed Display. Pre-fix only Reject verdict was gated; Neutral/Support on incomplete or default-constructed digests silently passed through. 3 new property tests pin: (1) incomplete digest with Support/Neutral verdict rejected with IncompleteEvidence, (2) empty root_hash rejected with MalformedEvidenceRoot, (3) complete + 64-char root_hash + Support/Neutral happy path still succeeds (negative pin against over-rejection). Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core-ars --lib and -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features both clean.

title: [fuzzing] simd_scan::scan_newlines_and_ansi: SIMD bytes path on every captured pane delta with no fuzz target
description:
## Attack surface

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/simd_scan.rs` contains the SIMD-
optimized scanner that runs against every byte of pane output ft
ingests:

```rust
pub fn scan_newlines_and_ansi(bytes: &[u8]) -> OutputScanMetrics    // line 194
pub fn logical_line_count(self, bytes: &[u8]) -> usize              // line 25 (impl method)
```

Existing fuzz coverage:
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/scan_pipeline_chunked.rs` (8.1 KB) — drives
  the full scan pipeline including `process(bytes)`, but at the
  pipeline level not the SIMD primitive.
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/scan_pipeline_quick.rs` (458 B) — drives
  `quick_scan(bytes)` which is the public bucket-counting path.

Neither calls `scan_newlines_and_ansi` directly. The pipeline
fuzzers exercise it transitively but the strongest coverage —
direct fuzz of the SIMD core with raw byte input — is missing.

## Why fuzzing finds real defects here

SIMD code is a known panic + UB hotspot:

- **Out-of-bounds read on chunk-tail handling** — SIMD scanners
  typically vectorize 16/32/64-byte chunks then handle the tail
  in a scalar loop. An off-by-one in the tail loop is a classic
  UB that ASan would catch immediately.
- **Integer overflow in ANSI parameter accumulator** — ANSI
  sequences contain numeric parameters; an attacker pane outputting
  `\x1b[99999999999999999m` could overflow the 32-bit accumulator
  before the bounds check.
- **Alignment crash on architectures without unaligned vector loads**
  — macOS arm64 tolerates unaligned, but the `simd_scan` may have
  fallback paths for x86 with stricter requirements.
- **Quadratic blowup on adversarial patterns** — `\x1b[\x1b[\x1b[`
  recursive escape introducer prefixes can drive worst-case scan
  cost.

This code runs against every pane delta — bytes from agent
output, which IS untrusted (a malicious agent process could emit
crafted bytes). Every byte of every captured agent goes through
this function.

## Suggested implementation

`fuzz/fuzz_targets/simd_scan_bytes.rs`:

```rust
#![no_main]
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use frankenterm_core::simd_scan::scan_newlines_and_ansi;

fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    if data.len() > 16 * 1024 * 1024 { return; }

    // Crash detector
    let metrics = scan_newlines_and_ansi(data);

    // Invariant: counts are bounded by length
    assert!(metrics.newlines as usize <= data.len(),
        "newlines count exceeds input length");
    assert!(metrics.ansi_sequences as usize <= data.len(),
        "ansi sequences count exceeds input length");
});
```

Seed corpus:
- `samples/simd_seed/empty` — empty input
- `samples/simd_seed/just_newlines` — `\n` * 1024
- `samples/simd_seed/just_ansi` — `\x1b[m` * 256
- `samples/simd_seed/realistic_terminal` — 4KB of real `vim`/`htop`
  output (already in the corpus tree under `tests/corpus/`)
- `samples/simd_seed/long_param` — `\x1b[` + `9` * 1024 + `m`
- `samples/simd_seed/recursive_csi_intros` — `\x1b[\x1b[\x1b[\x1b[\x1b[m`

Bonus: differential against a scalar reference impl (Pattern 3)
to catch SIMD/scalar divergences. The `simd_scan` module
likely already has a fallback scalar path under `#[cfg(not(target_feature))]`.

## Out of scope

- The `pattern_detect_with_context_streaming` fuzzer at the
  detection layer (different surface).
- Optimizing the SIMD code itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/simd_scan_bytes.rs` exists + registered.
- Seed corpus has ≥6 diverse entries.
- 24h ASan+UBSan campaign produces zero unique crashes.
- Differential variant (if scalar fallback exists) produces zero
  divergences.
- Crashes (when found) convert to regression tests under
  `tests/simd_scan_fuzz_regressions.rs`.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/simd_scan.rs:25, 194`
- Skill: testing-fuzzing Hard Rule #5 ("ASan without UBSan is half
  a tool" — UBSan catches the integer-overflow class for ANSI
  parameter accumulators)

Filed by cc_1 fuzzing audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: simd_scan fuzz harness shipped at 9c9acfaee. The harness file (previously untracked from earlier agent work) is now committed with material enhancements: (1) added multi-split state-stitching invariant — original single-split coverage PLUS up to 8 chunk boundaries per input via Arbitrary-driven multi_split_seeds, ANSI state machine carried forward across all chunks via one OutputScanState (matches production streaming model). (2) seeded fuzz/corpus/simd_scan/ with 10 adversarial inputs (csi_basic, osc_then_csi, dcs_st_terminator, recursive_csi_intro, integer_overflow_param, long_osc_payload, plain_newlines, empty, lone_esc, csi_intro_only). Four contracts pinned: SIMD vs scalar reference equivalence, logical_line_count consistency, ansi_density finite+bounded, multi-chunk stitching equivalence. cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bin simd_scan → exit 0. Long-running campaign (cargo +nightly fuzz run simd_scan -- -runs=5000) is the deployment step; harness compiles clean and is registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml. Mirrors ft-h8v8v's Archetype 5 + Archetype 1 shape, with SIMD/scalar differential as the primary crash-detector oracle.

title: [PHASE3/redactor] detect() double-counts overlapping priority patterns
description:
## Finding

`Redactor::detect()` reports every regex match independently, while `Redactor::redact()` applies the patterns in priority order. The source comments explicitly rely on priority ordering to avoid broad patterns stealing specific provider tokens, but the detection/evidence path does not coalesce overlaps or honor the same priority contract.

Concrete evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:395-401` — comments state order matters because broad `openai_key` can also match Anthropic-shaped `sk-ant-...` tokens.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:402-545` — `SECRET_PATTERNS` is an ordered priority list.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:621-633` — `detect()` pushes every match from every pattern and only sorts by start offset; it does not drop lower-priority overlaps.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:660-680` and `874-893` — redaction evidence uses `detect().len()` for `matches`, so duplicate overlaps inflate telemetry.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:1529-1566` — tests pin that Anthropic variants redact as `anthropic_key`, but there is no detect/evidence test requiring one prioritized span rather than multiple overlapping spans.

Concrete failure shape: an Anthropic `sk-ant-api03-...` token is matched by the specific Anthropic regex and can also match the broader OpenAI `sk-...` regex noted in the source comment. `redact()` produces one marker, but `detect()`/evidence can count/report overlapping detections for one secret.

## Alien-graveyard match

This is an evidence-ledger correctness gap: the runtime makes a correct redaction decision but records incoherent evidence. The FrankenSuite graveyard summary repeatedly calls for explainable decisions and observability ledgers that match the actual decision surface.

## Impact

P3: no direct leak in the replacement path, but telemetry/audit evidence can overcount matches and mislabel pattern coverage. That undermines operator trust and can hide actual coverage gaps behind inflated counters.

## Proposed remediation

1. Make `detect()` use the same priority semantics as `redact()`: keep the first/highest-priority match for an overlapping span and discard lower-priority overlaps.
2. Preserve deterministic output by sorting by `(start, priority_index, end)` before coalescing.
3. Add regression tests with `sk-ant-api03-...` showing exactly one detection named `anthropic_key` and `matches == 1` in `redact_bytes_with_evidence` for a single token.
4. Add a multi-secret test proving adjacent non-overlapping tokens are still counted separately.

## Acceptance

- Overlapping matches for one secret produce one detection/evidence count using the highest-priority pattern.
- Non-overlapping secrets still produce one detection per secret.
- `Redactor::redact()` output stays byte-for-byte compatible for existing fixtures.
notes: Detect() priority dedup shipped. Walks SECRET_PATTERNS in priority order; drops lower-priority overlaps via half-open interval check. Higher-priority match wins by virtue of being processed first. Tests: detect_anthropic_token_counts_once_not_twice (literal token), detect_redact_evidence_match_count_consistency (evidence pipeline), detect_disjoint_secrets_count_independently (no over-collapse), detect_anthropic_token_in_arbitrary_noise_counts_once (proptest with arbitrary prefix/suffix/tail). ## Phase 2 top five

1. No-mock PTY/mux loopback harness, because it proves the real session boundary instead of only unit helpers.
2. Terminal protocol differential corpus, because protocol regressions are subtle and transcript-backed fixtures are debuggable.
3. Feature coverage matrix for CSI/OSC/DCS/graphics/input modes, because it prevents broad claims with missing artifacts.
4. Transcript minimizer and quarantine workflow, because large failure logs need a route to small committed repros.
5. Resource/performance budget for replaying large agent-swarm transcripts, because correctness must not become unusably slow at scale.

## Phase 3 next ten

Supporting ideas kept for later integration: kitty graphics corpus; resize storm loopback; hyperlink/OSC 8 parity; bracketed paste and focus replay; UTF-8/grapheme edge corpus; fuzz-to-golden promotion; upstream WezTerm differential sampling; proof-ledger terminal records; render-state snapshot diffing; operator docs for terminal failure triage.

## Overlap check

Searches for terminal protocol differential, no-mock mux loopback, docs claim scanner, Agent Mail fallback drill, and related terms found only the broad ft-ilxky idea list, not a concrete bead graph for this terminal/mux conformance lane. This epic is intentionally separate from active proof-ledger and fleet-mutation work, and implementation children should re-check dirty paths before claiming.

## Goal

Create a no-mock, transcript-driven terminal and mux conformance lane that proves real PTY/mux/session behavior, promotes minimized failures into durable fixtures, and records proof in the repository evidence style without weakening RCH-only heavy verification.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace the existing mux backend or add a second backend.
- Do not bulk-import upstream WezTerm tests without manual review.
- Do not run local heavy Cargo as proof.
- Do not touch active proof-ledger, fleet mutation, or broad dirty test files without claiming a matching child bead.
- Do not delete or rewrite existing fixtures; additive/minimal changes only unless explicitly approved.

## Acceptance

- Child beads define the contract/matrix, no-mock loopback harness, transcript corpus, minimizer workflow, performance budget, and docs/proof closeout.
- The graph has no active dependency cycles.
- The first implementation child can be claimed without overlapping current dirty proof-ledger/fleet files.
- Heavy Rust validation runs through RCH only; static shell/docs checks may run locally.

title: [terminal-conformance] Build no-mock PTY/mux loopback harness
description:
## What

Build the first no-mock loopback harness for terminal/mux behavior using real process, PTY, mux/session, and pane read/write surfaces where the repository architecture permits.

## Why

Unit tests can miss boundary bugs in PTY IO, mux attach/detach, pane state transitions, resize propagation, and transcript capture. A no-mock harness gives future protocol fixtures a real execution path.

## Scope

- Start with one deterministic smoke scenario: spawn a controlled program, send text, resize, read output, and validate pane/session state.
- Emit structured logs with scenario id, command receipt, target dir, worker id when RCH is used, and artifact paths.
- Fail closed if RCH falls back locally for any heavy Cargo or e2e proof.
- Keep fixtures additive and do not delete existing tests.

## Acceptance

- Harness passes a narrow RCH-backed smoke proof.
- Failure logs distinguish source/test failure from RCH infrastructure failure.
- The contract bead row for the harness is updated with exact artifact paths.

title: [terminal-conformance] Add differential terminal transcript corpus
description:
## What

Create the first transcript corpus for protocol-differential terminal behavior and bind it to the no-mock harness or existing parser/render tests.

## Why

Terminal regressions often hide in escape-sequence interactions. Curated transcripts make failures reproducible and reviewable.

## Scope

- Start with a small manually reviewed set: bracketed paste, focus events, OSC 8 hyperlink, alt-screen enter/exit, resize plus wrapped text, UTF-8/grapheme edge, and one graphics-negative fixture.
- Include expected state/output artifacts with enough metadata to explain provenance and update rules.
- Do not bulk-copy upstream directories; sample or adapt manually with provenance.

## Acceptance

- Corpus has at least six scenarios with metadata, expected artifacts, and proof commands.
- Existing or new tests consume the corpus and fail with scenario ids.
- Heavy Rust proof runs through RCH only.

title: [terminal-conformance] Add transcript minimizer and quarantine workflow
description:
## What

Define and implement a workflow for turning large failing terminal transcripts into minimized committed repro fixtures, with quarantine rules for flaky or environment-sensitive cases.

## Why

No-mock terminal tests can produce large logs. Without minimization and quarantine, failures become expensive to understand and agents either overfit or ignore them.

## Scope

- Add a script or documented manual procedure for reducing transcript logs while preserving the failing assertion.
- Record scenario id, original artifact path, minimization steps, and residual risk.
- Quarantine only with explicit reason and follow-up bead; no silent skip.

## Acceptance

- At least one synthetic failing transcript fixture demonstrates minimization metadata.
- Docs explain when quarantine is allowed and how to promote a minimized case into the main corpus.
- Static checks pass; any executable test proof uses RCH for heavy work.

title: [terminal-conformance] Add large-transcript performance and resource budget
description:
## What

Add a performance/resource budget for replaying large terminal transcripts representative of massive agent swarms.

## Why

Correct terminal replay is not sufficient if conformance fixtures become too slow or memory-heavy for 64+ CPU / 256+ GiB swarm operators. The budget should catch accidental quadratic behavior and unbounded allocations.

## Scope

- Define one or more large transcript fixtures or generators with stable scale factors.
- Measure wall time, memory proxy, artifact size, and scenario count.
- Keep the lane RCH-backed and structured so slow workers or queue failure are not misclassified as source regressions.

## Acceptance

- Budget thresholds are documented and justified.
- RCH-backed proof emits structured logs and fails with actionable messages when limits are exceeded.
- The lane is optional/operator-gated if it is too heavy for normal CI, but still reproducible.

title: [idea-wizard] Ready-queue truth gate and claimability reconciler
description:
## Background

Idea-wizard pass after a Beads-only coordination snapshot on 2026-05-11. Agent Mail list/inbox are degraded, `br ready --json` returns an empty ready queue, and the shared worktree has unrelated dirty source files. `bv --robot-triage` still recommends blocked beads as actionable: for example `ft-e87u6.2` is reported as status `blocked` but the reasons include `Currently unclaimed - available for work`, while `br show ft-e87u6.2 --json` shows assignee `BluePike`, status `blocked`, and fresh PR 59 CI-wait comments.

This graph turns that operational failure mode into a first-class read-only contract and proof lane. The goal is to stop agents from acting on stale or internally inconsistent tracker recommendations before they claim work, touch files, or spam Beads comments.

Nearby existing work is not duplicated:
- `ft-9ntud` blocker radar tracks external substrate blockers and operator runbooks.
- `ft-782hw` proof-handoff tracks durable proof attempt records.
- `ft-5bwjf` herd-wave tracks synchronized swarm pressure.
- `ft-e87u6` attestation tracks manifest closeout.
- RCH repair beads track live remote proof infrastructure.

This graph specifically reconciles claimability across Beads, BV, fallback snapshots, PR/check evidence, Agent Mail degradation, and dirty-path risk.

## Phase 2: thirty ideas considered

Ideas considered before winnowing: ready-queue truth gate; BV/BR consistency checker; pre-claim safety oracle; stale top-pick suppressor; dependency-state validator; owner/assignee conflict detector; fresh-comment external-wait detector; PR check rollup classifier; Agent Mail degraded-mode classifier; dirty-path overlap guard; tracker-inconsistency structured event; no-ready operator cockpit; claim dry-run command; Beads comment anti-spam gate; RCH proof blocker import; blocker-radar adapter; proof-doctor adapter; GitHub PR waiting-state adapter; orphaned-assignee stale detector; dependency-cycle smoke gate; parent/child readiness audit; BV command-hint modernizer; stale `bd` hint detector; robot TOON claimability packet; MCP read-only claimability resource; e2e fixture corpus for misleading BV output; JSONL structured logs for coordination decisions; AGENTS/runbook closeout docs; CI/static guard for stale classifications; and upstream beads_rust bug report or patch lane.

## Phase 2 top five

1. A pre-claim claimability reconciler, because agents currently need to manually compare `br ready`, `br show`, `bv`, GitHub PR status, and dirty paths before they know whether work is actually safe.
2. A deterministic fixture corpus for misleading BV output, because the current observed case has enough evidence to become a regression test instead of tribal knowledge.
3. A structured verdict vocabulary, because `blocked`, `actionable`, `available`, `external_wait`, and `dirty_overlap` must mean the same thing across robot output, docs, comments, and future automation.
4. A read-only robot/script surface, because the first safe product should never claim, assign, comment, restart services, or mutate queues.
5. A docs/runbook adoption path, because this only helps if future agents can use the verdict before acting when Agent Mail is degraded and the ready queue is empty.

## Phase 3 next ten

Retained follow-up ideas: GitHub check-suite materialization detector; stale owner contact advice; PR head drift detector; blocked-child claim denial explainer; dirty-file ownership overlap table; Beads/BV graph consistency metrics; upstream `bv` issue/patch handoff; claimability MCP resource; `scripts/swarm-tick.sh` integration; and a release/CI guard that fails if known fixture states are mislabeled as claimable.

## Goal

Ship a read-only ready-queue truth gate that produces a machine-readable claimability verdict before an agent claims work. It must reconcile `br ready`, `br show`, `bv --robot-triage`, degraded Agent Mail/fallback state, dirty worktree paths, and optional GitHub PR/check evidence into exact next actions.

## Verdict vocabulary

At minimum, the contract must distinguish:
- `claimable`: ready, unassigned or explicitly claimable, dependencies satisfied, no conflicting dirty-path risk.
- `no_ready`: tracker ready queue is empty and no safe new work was selected.
- `dependency_blocked`: dependencies or parent blockers prevent claim.
- `owner_blocked`: another owner/assignee has active or fresh evidence on the bead.
- `external_wait`: GitHub Actions, RCH, Agent Mail, or another substrate is waiting without a source failure to fix.
- `dirty_overlap`: local dirty paths overlap the candidate's owned files.
- `mail_degraded`: Agent Mail list/inbox cannot be trusted, so Beads/git are the handoff surface.
- `tracker_inconsistent`: `bv` and `br` disagree in a way that would mislead an agent.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace blocker-radar or proof-doctor.
- Do not restart, repair, drain, or update Agent Mail/RCH.
- Do not claim or comment automatically.
- Do not mutate Beads except through explicit human/agent commands outside the read-only check.
- Do not run heavy Cargo locally.

## Acceptance

- Child beads define the contract, fixtures, implementation surface, upstream/tooling diagnosis, runbook integration, and proof closeout.
- The observed `ft-e87u6.2` mismatch is captured as a fixture: BV says actionable/available while BR says blocked/assigned/fresh external wait.
- The output includes candidate id, source timestamps, dependency verdict, assignee/owner verdict, dirty-path verdict, optional PR/check verdict, final claimability verdict, exact next action, and forbidden actions.
- A future agent can run one command before claiming and get a stable JSON/TOON answer.
- `br dep cycles --json` reports no active cycle after graph creation.

title: [claimability] Define ready-queue truth states and safety invariants
description:
## Goal

Define the v1 claimability contract before implementation. The contract must make it impossible for a blocked, assigned, or externally waiting bead to be described as safe to claim just because a graph score is high.

## Scope

- Define the input sources: `br ready --json`, `br show <id> --json`, `bv --robot-triage`, `scripts/swarm-tick.sh --agent-mail-fallback frankenterm`, `git status --short --branch`, and optional GitHub PR/check metadata when a candidate names a PR or external wait.
- Define the canonical verdicts: `claimable`, `no_ready`, `dependency_blocked`, `owner_blocked`, `external_wait`, `dirty_overlap`, `mail_degraded`, and `tracker_inconsistent`.
- Define precedence rules. Safety blockers must dominate score-based recommendations. A candidate that is blocked, owned by another active assignee, fresh-comment externally waiting, or dirty-overlapping is not claimable.
- Define required JSON/TOON fields and reason-code vocabulary.
- Define forbidden actions: no claiming, no commenting, no Agent Mail/RCH repair, no service restart, and no source edits from the read-only check.

## Acceptance

- A contract doc or existing docs section specifies all verdicts, precedence, source freshness requirements, required output fields, and forbidden actions.
- The observed `ft-e87u6.2` case is explicitly represented as `tracker_inconsistent` plus `owner_blocked` or `external_wait`, not `claimable`.
- The contract explains how to act when `br ready` is empty and BV still recommends blocked work.
- Static docs checks for the touched docs pass.

title: [HIGH] GUI resize increment saturation can overflow backend min-size arithmetic
description: Commit 193a9ebb changes `ResizeIncrementCalculator` to saturate `base_width`/`base_height` at the u16 ceiling (`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/resize_increment_calculator.rs:15-35`). Multiple window backends then immediately compute `base + increment` in u16 without guarding overflow (`frankenterm/window/src/os/macos/window.rs:1410-1412`, `frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/window.rs:1892-1893`, `frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs:915-916`). With large padding/border/tab-bar geometry, the new saturation can produce `base_width == u16::MAX`, so `base_width + x` overflows before min-size clamping. This turns an intended overflow hardening change into a runtime panic/wraparound path on oversized layouts. Expected fix: clamp stored base dimensions to `u16::MAX - increment` (or widen backend arithmetic) and add a regression test that asserts `base + increment` stays representable.

title: [ARCH] integrate bounded_edit_distance into output_compression::lines_similar (br-ft-88cka follow-up)
description:
[ARCH] integrate bounded_edit_distance into output_compression::lines_similar (br-ft-88cka follow-up)

Substrate ft-88cka shipped Ukkonen 1985 bounded edit distance as crate::bounded_edit_distance. This bead tracks the production integration into the pairwise similarity hot path.

Current code (crates/frankenterm-core/src/output_compression.rs:169):
```rust
pub fn lines_similar(a: &str, b: &str, threshold: f64) -> bool {
    let max_len = a.len().max(b.len());
    if max_len == 0 {
        return true;
    }
    let dist = edit_distance(a.as_bytes(), b.as_bytes());
    (dist as f64 / max_len as f64) < threshold
}
```

Migration:
1. Compute bound up-front: `let max_distance = (max_len as f64 * threshold).floor() as usize;`
   - Note `<` not `≤` in original — care with `floor` vs `ceil` semantics.
2. Replace edit_distance call: `crate::bounded_edit_distance::within_edit_distance(a.as_bytes(), b.as_bytes(), max_distance)`
3. Result is the same boolean.

Suitable additional callsites:
- Any pairwise similarity scan in compress() at output_compression.rs:383.
- Other approximate-string-match callers across the codebase (run grep `edit_distance|levenshtein` to find).

title: events::NotificationCooldown::check: insertion_order not refreshed on cooldown-expired send, LRU evicts actively-used keys
description: crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs:1015-1064 NotificationCooldown::check has a subtle LRU-staleness bug: when a key's cooldown has EXPIRED and we emit Send (line 1036-1043), we update entry.last_notified to now and reset entry.suppressed_since_notify, but we do NOT move the key to the back of self.insertion_order. The key stays at its ORIGINAL insertion position. Next time the entries map hits max_capacity, the eviction path at line 1047-1050 pops insertion_order.pop_front() — which picks a key by ORIGINAL INSERTION ORDER, not by last-use. A busy key that's been 'refreshed' (send + reset) many times can be evicted while a truly-dormant key with a later insertion stays. Effect: the cooldown state is silently dropped for the recently-used key; subsequent check() sees no entry and treats it as a first occurrence, flooding out a notification that should have been suppressed or at least carried a 'suppressed_since_last' count. Same pattern already fixed in sibling EventDeduplicator at events.rs:867-870 (refresh insertion_order on window-expired reset). Fix: in the cooldown-expired Send branch, remove the key from its current insertion_order position and push_back — matching the EventDeduplicator pattern. Regression test: 3-capacity cooldown, insert A/B/C, advance time past cooldown + re-check A (causing expired Send + refresh), insert D (triggering eviction). Pre-fix A is evicted; post-fix B is evicted (truly oldest-by-use).

title: [cell-image] Make animated image memory accounting empty-frame safe
description:
## Finding
`frankenterm/cell/src/image.rs::ImageData::len` computes animated-image memory as `frames.len() * frames[0].len()`. `ImageDataType::AnimRgba8` is publicly constructible and serde-derived, so an empty frame vector can reach this method even though decoder-produced animations normally have at least one frame. - Account animated images by summing frame buffer lengths without indexing frame 0.
- Preserve zero retained bytes for empty animations.
- Add focused regression coverage for empty and non-uniform frame vectors.

## Context

## What this bead carries

### BinPacker trait wiring
- `frankenterm/window/src/bitmaps/atlas.rs`: replace the existing alloc path with a `Box<dyn BinPacker>` field selected via `select_packer(atlas_size, thresholds)` at atlas construction time
- `BinPacker` trait surface: `try_alloc(&mut self, glyph: GlyphSize) -> AllocationOutcome` (matches ShelfPacker/SkylinePacker method signatures already)

### Full MaximalRectanglesPacker
- Implement BSSF (Best Short Side Fit): maintain `Vec<FreeRect>` of remaining free rectangles
- For each alloc, scan `FreeRect`s, score each as `min(free.w - glyph.w, free.h - glyph.h)`, pick minimum (best short-side fit)
- After placement: split the chosen FreeRect into up to 2 new FreeRects (the area to the right and below the placed glyph)
- Remove FreeRects fully contained in others (degenerate state pruning)
- ~2% wasted per Jylänki; O(N²) per alloc in FreeRect count

- `crates/frankenterm-core/benches/atlas_packing.rs`: pack 4 corpora through all 3 packers

### ft doctor surface

title: Mission loop active operator overrides are unbounded
description:
Reality-check audit finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs.

Evidence:
- OperatorOverride supports permanent overrides when expires_at_ms is None at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:1928-1933.
- OperatorOverrideState stores active overrides in an unbounded Vec while only history has MAX_HISTORY at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:1955-1967.
- activate() blindly pushes every override at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:1969-1972, and apply_override() only rejects duplicate active override_id values at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:2101-2113.
- Each evaluation drains/scans active overrides for expiry, exclusions, reprioritize deltas, and pins at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:2137-2215.
- Tests assert history is bounded at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:5463-5480, but there is no analogous active override cap or required TTL test.

Why it matters:
A control-plane caller can accumulate many unique permanent overrides. That grows serialized mission state and makes every mission evaluation scan more work before solving, which is a denial-of-service vector against the scheduler/control plane.

Proposed remediation:
Add an active override cap in config with a conservative default, require TTL for externally sourced overrides unless explicitly privileged, and reject or coalesce overrides by target/action. Add tests that active override insertion fails closed at the cap and that large expired batches cannot leave active/history over configured bounds.
notes: Bounded the active operator-overrides vec. Added MAX_ACTIVE=100 const on OperatorOverrideState (matches MAX_HISTORY order). Added new fallible try_activate that returns OperatorOverrideRejection::ActiveCapReached{cap, rejected} when at cap; rejected override is returned to caller so it can be logged/surfaced rather than silently dropped. The infallible activate is preserved for internal helpers that already validated capacity. MissionLoop::apply_override now uses try_activate so the cap propagates to the public surface. OperatorOverrideRejection enum + Display + Error impls carry br-ft-i4brq breadcrumb. Added 3 tests: override_active_cap_rejects_overflow_ft_i4brq (fills to cap, asserts reject + count unchanged), apply_override_propagates_active_cap_error_ft_i4brq (wrapper error contains breadcrumb + id), override_clear_frees_slot_for_new_activation_ft_i4brq (clear() frees a slot so subsequent try_activate succeeds). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [no-mocks-test] crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_replay_artifact_registry.rs: MockFs (test-only trait) hides fsync/metadata/race bugs — use tempdir + std::fs
description:
## Mock at issue
crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_replay_artifact_registry.rs:
  43: struct MockFs { files: Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>> }
  59: impl FsBackend for MockFs
The MockFs is the only implementer of FsBackend in the workspace
(grep confirms no real FsBackend impl exists in src/), meaning the
trait abstraction was introduced solely for testing.

## Why the mock is risky
Replay artifacts (recordings, metadata, golden refs) are persistent
data. The MockFs uses a HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>> and ignores:
- Filesystem metadata (mtime, size-on-disk vs len of bytes)
- Atomic-rename semantics (rename(temp, target))
- Fsync ordering — production code that writes-then-fsyncs is
  indistinguishable from the buggy write-without-fsync under MockFs
- Disk-full / EROFS / EACCES error paths
- Concurrent writer races (the Mutex serializes; real fs does not)
- Path-canonicalization edge cases (./, .., symlinks)

The artifact registry decides which replay artifacts are durable and
which to garbage-collect. A bug in size accounting under MockFs is
silent because the Mutex guarantees atomicity that real disk does not.

Mock Risk score: 3 (data: replay artifacts lost) × 4 (mock collapses
all I/O complexity) = 12 → MUST be mock-free.

## Real fixture available
std::fs + tempfile::TempDir. Trivial — already used in 72 other tests
under crates/frankenterm-core/tests/.

## Suggested approach
1. Inline-delete the FsBackend trait abstraction (test-only; no
   production impl exists). The artifact-registry production code
   already uses std::fs directly.
2. Update the proptests to drive the registry against a per-test
   tempfile::TempDir.
3. proptest's #![proptest_config(...)] already runs fast; tempdir
   create/teardown adds <1ms per case.
4. Add proptest properties the MockFs cannot exercise:
   - prop: writing artifact-A then crashing before sync still leaves
     a recoverable directory (we should detect partial writes via
     the `*.partial` rename pattern)
   - prop: concurrent writers on disjoint paths never corrupt either
5. Drop MockFs entirely once tests are migrated.

## Acceptance
- proptest_replay_artifact_registry.rs uses no MockFs.
- ≥10 properties run against tempdir.
- Suite wall time still < 5s.
- Crash-mid-write recovery property added.
close_reason: proptest uses tempdir-backed real artifact registry filesystem path

title: runtime_async.rs: 4 JoinHandle production sites panic on abort_waker Mutex poison — every spawned-task poll cascades runtime-wide
description:
## Sites
\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_async.rs\` inside \`pub mod task { ... }\` — 4 production sites use \`.expect("abort waker mutex poisoned")\` on \`JoinHandle.abort_waker\` (Arc<Mutex<Option<Waker>>>):

- **L851** \`JoinHandle::poll\` storing waker — HOT PATH (every poll of every spawned task)
- **L863** \`JoinHandle::poll\` clearing waker on abort path
- **L871** \`JoinHandle::poll\` clearing waker on success path
- **L898** \`JoinHandle::abort\` waking the stored waker

(Plus 2 timer-lock sites at L2789/2798 inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests; out of scope.)

## Defect

\`JoinHandle\` is the asupersync runtime spawned-task handle wrapping every \`asupersync::runtime::JoinHandle<T>\`. \`poll()\` is called by the executor on EVERY task wakeup. If any thread panics while holding the abort_waker Mutex, every subsequent \`poll()\` re-panics → the executor dies → the entire runtime is unavailable.

The blast radius is even higher than ft-h2vyr (cancellation): cancellation Mutexes are touched on cancel/checkpoint, but JoinHandle.poll is the executor primitive — every task completion (success, abort, pending) goes through this lock.

A typical poison trigger: a panic in a Future poll fn that runs while another thread holds the abort_waker. The poison propagates next time anything polls a JoinHandle anywhere in the runtime.

## Comparison to sibling-shipped pattern

ft-skec1 (events.rs), ft-4pxzi (policy rate-limiter), ft-h2vyr (cancellation.rs) all converted similar `.expect()` panic-cascades into fail-soft + observable counter recovery via \`PoisonError::into_inner()\`. Same pattern applies here:

- Recovery cost: an inconsistent abort_waker Option (a stale Waker stored, a Waker dropped before being woken). Wakers are designed to be safely droppable; a stale Waker is wasted memory but causes no runtime defect.
- Cascade cost (status quo): runtime death.

Recovery wins.

## Fix shape

Add \`JOIN_HANDLE_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT: AtomicU64\` static + public accessor + #[cfg(test)] reset helper + private bump helper, scoped INSIDE \`pub mod task\` so the JoinHandle observability is colocated with JoinHandle.

Add a private helper \`lock_abort_waker_recovering(...)\` that handles the unwrap_or_else(|p| { counter.fetch_add(1, Relaxed); p.into_inner() }) pattern.

Replace each \`.lock().expect("abort waker mutex poisoned")\` with the helper. No signature changes.

## Forensic verification contract

\`\`\`text
total_polls_attempted == polls_completed
                          + join_handle_lock_poisoned_count()
\`\`\`
The right side becomes observable. Non-zero values mean a prior thread panicked while holding a JoinHandle abort_waker; the runtime recovered and continued instead of cascading.

## Tests

- Counter starts at 0 after reset.
- Force a poisoned abort_waker via panic-injection in a child thread; assert subsequent abort() recovers + bumps counter.
- Negative test: 5 clean spawn+await cycles do NOT bump the counter.

## Class

P2 — runtime hot-path crash recovery. Highest blast radius of the panic-recovery family — every spawned task poll touches this lock, and the executor itself depends on it. Pairs with ft-h2vyr (cancellation) and ft-4pxzi (rate-limiter) as the runtime-level Mutex-poison-recovery suite.
close_reason: Shipped at 75f287ac9: added JOIN_HANDLE_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT counter + accessor + reset helper + private lock_abort_waker_recovering() helper, all scoped inside pub mod task. Replaced .expect('abort waker mutex poisoned') at all 4 production sites in JoinHandle: poll (waker store, hot path), poll (abort-path clear), poll (success-path clear), abort (waker wake). Fail-OPEN recovery rationale: stale Waker is wasted memory but causes no runtime defect; cascade cost is runtime death. 2 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline, unchanged-for-clean-spawn-await (5 cycles). Deterministic panic-injection test deferred — requires exposing test-only constructor on JoinHandle or asupersync spawn refactor; recovery path is structurally identical to ft-h2vyr (cancellation) which has end-to-end panic-injection tests. Highest blast radius of the panic-recovery family — every spawned task poll touches this lock. Pairs with ft-h2vyr + ft-4pxzi as runtime-level Mutex-poison-recovery suite. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (53.33s, 0 errors).

title: [gh-52] build.rs must populate FT_WEZTERM_VENDORED_REV for path-dep workspace layout
description:
## Problem (GitHub #52)

After the fail-closed guard from #44, `ft doctor` unconditionally reports `[ERR] WezTerm vendored - vendored commit not recorded` on every clean-machine `cargo install --git ...` build. Root cause:

- `crates/frankenterm-core/build.rs` only extracts vendored commit from `Cargo.lock` entries whose `source = "git+...#<hash>"` fragment carries a commit.
- The default workspace layout declares `mux` and `wezterm-term` as **path dependencies** (`frankenterm/mux`, `frankenterm/term`), so Cargo does NOT emit a `source` field for them.
- `select_vendored_metadata` returns `(None, None, None)`, no `cargo:rustc-env=FT_WEZTERM_VENDORED_REV=...` is emitted, `option_env!("FT_WEZTERM_VENDORED_REV")` resolves to `None`, and `vendored.rs` reports `Incompatible` at runtime.

Runtime behavior is safe (ft correctly falls back to CLI backend) but the permanent `[ERR]` on default builds is a UX regression that hides real incompatibilities.

## Fix direction

In `crates/frankenterm-core/build.rs`, add a path-dep fallback branch to `select_vendored_metadata`:

1. If `mux.source.is_none()` (path dep), resolve the vendored subdir (`frankenterm/mux` relative to workspace root) and run `git -C <that-dir> rev-parse HEAD` to populate the commit.
2. Handle the case where the workspace is not a git checkout (e.g. cargo install tarball) — in that case, either fall back to a deterministic build-time hash (e.g. `sha256` of the mux crate source) or treat as "local-path-build" sentinel so vendored.rs can accept it without [ERR].
3. Add `cargo:rerun-if-changed=` entries for `frankenterm/mux/Cargo.toml` and `frankenterm/term/Cargo.toml` so the metadata refreshes on vendored bumps.
4. Emit `FT_WEZTERM_VENDORED_VERSION` + `FT_WEZTERM_VENDORED_SOURCE` in the path-dep branch too.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `cargo install --git https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm.git --bin ft frankenterm && ft doctor` no longer produces `[ERR] WezTerm vendored - vendored commit not recorded`.
2. `ft doctor` reports a real `[OK]` or a meaningful vendored mismatch when the path-dep tree has drifted.
3. Runtime vendored compatibility guard (`vendored.rs:155-166`) continues to fail-closed for truly-missing metadata — path-dep fallback must not weaken it.
4. Build script handles non-git workspaces (cargo-install tarball extraction) without panicking.
5. Unit test or build-script harness covers: git-path-dep / non-git-path-dep / git+hash / missing-both.

## Reporter

GitHub user JordanChoo — https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm/issues/52
close_reason: Fixed in 3174399d (build.rs path-dep fallback + non-git sentinel + 8-test harness)

title: [MEDIUM] ActivityProfile::new allows NaN alpha/default_activity past clamp; poisons all hourly_ewma slots
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/survival.rs:437-438` — `ActivityProfile::new`.

ft-26k3h just hardened `update_hour` against NaN input. The construction-time path is the **complement**: `alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` and `default_activity.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` both still let NaN through because `f64::clamp(NaN, _, _)` returns NaN.

Two independent failure modes:

1. **NaN `default_activity`**: all 24 `hourly_ewma` slots are initialised to NaN. `predict_hour` returns NaN for every slot until the first clean `update_hour` overwrites the bucket via the `sample_count == 0` branch. Until then, every hazard/survival score computed from `predict` silently produces NaN (matches the ft-26k3h failure shape but from a different path).

2. **NaN `alpha`**: `self.alpha = NaN`. `update_hour` at line 460 computes `alpha.mul_add(sample, (1.0 - alpha) * prev) = NaN` on every non-first sample. `hourly_ewma[idx]` stays NaN from the second sample onward. ft-26k3h's entry guard doesn't catch this because the caller passes a clean `normalized_activity` — the NaN is stored in `self.alpha`, not in the input.

Both are the same `f64::clamp(NaN)` gotcha shipped across ft-761tz / ft-b4l62 / ft-jz40p / ft-0p5q5 / ft-x50ce / ft-26k3h. This closes the pair's construction-time counterpart.

## Fix

Snap NaN to sensible defaults at the boundary:
- `alpha` → 0.1 (a conservative EWMA coefficient; config-adjacent code uses 0.3 as the common default but 0.1 is safe for an unspecified sentinel).
- `default_activity` → 0.5 (neutral midpoint — if operator didn't supply a meaningful default, 0.5 is the least-surprising fallback).

Both `.is_nan()` checks happen **before** the clamp so the clamp still trims out-of-range finite inputs normally.

## Tests

* `ft_icreu_new_sanitises_nan_alpha` — alpha=NaN → stored α=0.1, EWMA updates stay finite.
* `ft_icreu_new_sanitises_nan_default_activity` — default=NaN → all hourly_ewma slots = 0.5, predict_hour returns 0.5.

## Scope

Single file (`survival.rs`).
close_reason: done

title: ft-l0oe3 substrate: SoakSummary.meets_acceptance integer-truncation false-positive on warnings-per-pane-per-hour
description:
triple_buffer_fleet_health.rs SoakSummary::meets_acceptance computes warnings rate as total_warnings / panes / hours (integer division). With 199 total warnings across 200 panes over 24h, division yields 199/200=0, 0/24=0. Compared to max=0 → returns true even though warnings are present.

Fix: use cross-multiplication. total_warnings > max_warnings_per_pane_per_hour * panes * hours_u64 catches the threshold directly without integer-truncation false-positives.

Real-world: bead's release-gate threshold is 0 warnings/pane/hour. Current code lets 199 warnings slip through on a 200-pane 24h soak; gate stays green when it should fail.

Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD: cross-multiplication threshold catches truncation case; 2 regression tests pin 199-warning failure + exact-boundary semantics. 34 tests pass.

title: [MEDIUM] defer_fts_triggers=false is not reversible: triggers stay dropped after enabling once (ft-wk5fo follow-up)
description:
# Defect

## Concrete failure path

File: `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs`.

d74401c6 landed `StorageConfig.defer_fts_triggers` (ft-wk5fo). The intent is a reversible opt-in: flip to `true` to trade FTS freshness for write-path latency, flip back to `false` to restore synchronous indexing. The inline comment at line 6006 says as much:

> The triggers can be re-created by re-opening with `defer_fts_triggers: false`

That claim is wrong. Concrete interleaving:

1. Operator opens DB with `defer_fts_triggers: true` on an up-to-date schema (`user_version == SCHEMA_VERSION`).
2. `initialize_schema` returns early at line 4315 (no SQL executed, up-to-date path).
3. The explicit `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS output_segments_ai/ad/au` at line 6010 runs — triggers gone.
4. Operator flips config to `defer_fts_triggers: false` and restarts.
5. `initialize_schema` again short-circuits at line 4315.
6. Line 6010 is skipped (flag is false). **No `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS` runs.**
7. Database silently stays in deferred mode; the operator's `false` setting is a no-op.

The inline comment at line 6007 hints the author knew: 'this commit ships the opt-in direction only; reverting would require re-running SCHEMA_SQL or the operator dropping the DB.' That matches reality but contradicts the line-6006 'can be re-created by re-opening' claim — and leaves the config behaving non-intuitively for operators.

## Severity rationale

- Not a crash or data loss.
- Silent wrong answer: operator flips back to `false`, expects synchronous FTS, gets deferred.
- One-way-door config is a known anti-pattern. Easy fix.

## Fix sketch

Make the open path truly bidirectional. On every open, after `initialize_schema` returns:

* If `defer_fts_triggers == true`: `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS ...` (idempotent).
* If `defer_fts_triggers == false`: `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS ...` using the same SQL the SCHEMA_SQL block defines.

Factor the trigger SQL into one private const referenced by both branches so SCHEMA_SQL and the re-create branch cannot drift.

## Tests

* ft_ih4tm_defer_fts_triggers_roundtrip — open with true, verify triggers dropped, close, reopen with false, verify triggers re-created.
* ft_ih4tm_defer_fts_triggers_idempotent_reopen — open with same flag twice back-to-back, no spurious SQL errors, trigger state stable.

## Scope

Single file (`storage.rs`). No API break (`defer_fts_triggers` already public, default `false`).
close_reason: done

[MEDIUM] ft-cnil8.2 closed but smart_match_in_line never called from triple-click GUI path
description:
[MEDIUM] ft-cnil8.2 closed but smart_match_in_line never called from triple-click path

## Defect

ft-cnil8.2 ("Triple-click wiring for smart-selection (line span)")
was closed by cc_1 with this acceptance summary:

> Acceptance criteria for ft-cnil8.2 are met: classify_triple_click
> in line span exists; ClickKind dispatcher routes Triple to it;
> tests cover the path.

The substrate (classify_triple_click + ClickKind::Triple dispatcher
+ smart_match_in_line at c1cfbb435) is well-tested in isolation.
But the bead's actual scope is broader:

> Sub-task 4 of ft-cnil8. **Same flow as sub-task 3** but
> classify_triple_click constrained to current line span.
> **Composes with the mouse handler from sub-task 3.**

```
$ grep -rn 'smart_match_in_line\|classify_triple_click' --include='*.rs' \
    crates/frankenterm-gui/
(zero references)

$ grep -n 'SelectionMode::Line\|line_around' \
    crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/selection.rs
202:  let end_line = SelectionRange::line_around(SelectionCoordinate::x_y(x, y), &**pane);
209:  let start_line = SelectionRange::line_around(start_coord, &**pane);
256:  let selection_range = SelectionRange::line_around(start, &**pane);
```

The `SelectionMode::Line` arm of the mouse handler uses the legacy
`SelectionRange::line_around` (full physical-line span), not a
smart-selection variant. There is no `smart_or_line_around` sister
to `smart_or_word_around` (which cc_1's commit at 24e8a9092 added
for double-click). Triple-click on a line containing a URL selects
the entire line, not the URL.

## Why it matters

Bead's stated acceptance: triple-click on a URL inside text should
select the URL span (per "Same flow as sub-task 3 but constrained
to current line span"). Without the GUI wiring, triple-click is
identical to legacy line-around: it picks the full line. The
substrate's `widest-pattern-fully-contained-in-line` logic never
fires.

## Repro

1. Open frankenterm.
2. In a pane: `echo 'see https://example.com/long-path?param=value'`
3. Triple-click on the URL.
4. Observe: full line selected (`echo 'see https://...'`), not just
   the URL.

Expected per bead: URL span selected (the widest smart-pattern fully
contained in the line).

## Fix sketch

Mirror the `smart_or_word_around` pattern at
`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/selection.rs:312`:

```rust
pub fn smart_or_line_around(start: SelectionCoordinate, pane: &dyn Pane) -> Self {
    for logical in pane.get_logical_lines(start.y..start.y + 1) {
        if !logical.contains_y(start.y) { continue; }
        let line_text = logical.logical.as_str();
        if let Some(m) = smart_match_in_line(&line_text, 0, line_text.len()) {
            // map m.span_start..m.span_end to physical coords + return
        }
    }
    Self::line_around(start, pane)
}
```

Then route `SelectionMode::Line` calls at termwindow/selection.rs:202,
:209, :256 through `smart_or_line_around`.

## Acceptance

- Triple-click on a line with a URL selects the URL span (widest
  smart-pattern fully contained in the line wins).
- Triple-click on a line with no smart-pattern matches falls back
  to the full physical line (current behavior).
- Behavior covered by GUI integration tests (sister to the existing
  smart_match_logical_x_range_selects_url_inside_quotes test in
  selection.rs).

## Cross-references

- ft-cnil8.2 (this — closed prematurely; substrate at c1cfbb435 has
  zero GUI callers)
- ft-cnil8.1 (sibling; double-click wired but mouse handler never
  emits a11y — see ft-weglh)
- ft-cnil8.3 (sibling; SmartSelectionConfig.compile() never called —
  see ft-qhhb3)
- ft-cnil8.4 (sibling; smart_selection_a11y bridge never called —
  see ft-weglh)
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/selection.rs:312 (smart_or_word_around,
  the model the line-mode equivalent should mirror)
- crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/selection.rs:202,209,256
  (SelectionMode::Line call sites)
close_reason:
Duplicate of ft-t5j0a — both beads were filed for the same triple-click ghostwiring defect (ft-cnil8.2 closed but smart_match_in_line never called from the GUI mouse handler). Likely a double-file from the round-2 review pass when the beads DB hit busy and the create command was retried. The fix landed under ft-t5j0a at 9f8a22065 and satisfies every acceptance item of ft-iiqb8 verbatim:

(1) Triple-click on a line with a URL selects the URL span — verified via smart_match_in_line_picks_url_in_full_line_span + smart_match_in_line_url_inside_quotes_wins_over_shell_quoted tests.
(2) Triple-click on a line with no smart-pattern falls back to the full physical line — verified by smart_or_line_around's None-pick branch routing through SelectionRange::line_around (test smart_match_in_line_returns_none_on_plain_text_only_line covers the substrate side).
(3) Behavior covered by GUI integration tests — 16 tests pass via cargo test -p frankenterm-gui --bin frankenterm-gui selection, including the 5 new smart_match_in_line_* tests filed under the fix-sketch's exact recipe.

The implementation matches the bead's fix sketch verbatim: smart_or_line_around walks logical lines, calls smart_match_in_line(text, 0, text.len()), maps the byte span to physical coords via logical_x_for_byte_offset, and falls back to line_around when no smart pattern is matched. Both SelectionMode::Line call sites in termwindow/selection.rs route through the new function. AT-tree announcement composes with the br-ft-weglh recorder.

No additional code change required. Closing as duplicate.

title: [reality-check] README workspace-structure counts are stale (vendored 47→42, fuzz 4→37, docs 114→258)
description:
## Gap

README.md's 'Workspace Structure' section (around lines 855-868) makes three
specific count claims that are off by enough to mislead readers about scale.

| Claim | README line | README says | Reality | Drift |
|-------|-------------|-------------|---------|-------|
| Vendored crates | 857 | `frankenterm/  # In-tree vendored workspace crates (47 crates)` | 42 | -5 |
| Fuzz targets | 865 | `fuzz/  # 4 fuzzing targets` | 37 | +33 |
| Doc files | 866 | `docs/  # 114 documentation files` | 258 | +144 |

## Reality (HEAD verification)

```bash
$ find frankenterm -maxdepth 2 -name Cargo.toml | wc -l
42
$ find fuzz/fuzz_targets -name "*.rs" | wc -l
37
$ find docs -name "*.md" | wc -l
258
```

The fuzz and docs counts are dramatically understated; the vendored count is
slightly overstated.

## Why this matters

- The README's "How ft Compares" table (line 258) and "Why Use ft?" pitch
  rely on scale credibility. Telling readers there are 4 fuzz targets when
  there are 37 sells the project short.
- "114 documentation files" suggests the docs tree is small/manageable;
  258 is a different conversation about what's worth indexing.
- Users following `find frankenterm -maxdepth 2 -name Cargo.toml | wc -l`
  (the README itself recommends this exact command at line 38 of the
  'Platform Model' subsection) will see 42, not 47.

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. **Replace static counts with the live commands** the README already
   recommends elsewhere (`find ... | wc -l`). Self-updating, no future drift.
2. **Update the static counts** to match HEAD (42 / 37 / 258) and add a
   build-time check (a small CI step that re-runs the counts and fails if
   they drift by more than ±10%).

Option 1 is preferred: zero maintenance burden, and the user gets the truth
at the moment they read it.

## Out of scope

- Reorganizing the workspace itself.
- Reducing the number of fuzz targets or doc files.
- The 'tests/e2e # 149 end-to-end test harnesses' line at line 867 — that
  count needs separate verification (tests/e2e currently has 198 .sh scripts
  and 1 .py harness, but 'harness' may have a narrower meaning here).

## Verification

After fix, the three commands above must agree with the README text (or
the README must use the commands themselves).

Filed by cc_1 reality-check audit, 2026-04-28.

title: [idea-wizard] RCH worker-targeted proof reproducibility and mirror attestation
description:
## Background

The current swarm has strong RCH policy direction and an active proof-ledger graph, but the ft-3yptk.2 closeout exposed a separate operational gap: when a failure is worker-specific, agents cannot reliably reproduce it on the exact worker without either waiting for scheduler luck, running broad RCH jobs that disturb shared capacity, or using weaker self-test evidence that may fail before the target proof runs. In that incident, the eventual decisive proof selected the affected worker naturally, while a worker-targeted self-test timed out at the local daemon boundary. That is good enough for that closeout, but not good enough as an operator capability.

## Idea-wizard pass

Thirty ideas considered before winnowing: worker-targeted RCH reproducibility; worker mirror/source-closure attestation; queue-aware proof preflight; proof-ledger worker evidence; stale mirror negative fixtures; active RCH job telemetry in robot health; dirty-tree ownership guards; Agent Mail outage fallback drills; macOS heap vs graphics residency classifier; high-core scale artifacts; durable fleet receipts; daemon mutation substrate; Robot API coverage matrix; direct-tokio gates; proof-doctor reason-code expansion; stuck-agent recovery automation; transcript redaction gates; terminal protocol differential corpus; shared-worktree staging leases; safe shell-command catalog; per-worker source snapshot fingerprints; non-repairing environment doctor; RCH capacity estimator; safe target-dir cleanup review; benchmark bisection; MCP denial observability; fleet resource autopilot; pane crash snapshots; docs claim scanner; no-mock mux loopback harness.

Top five selected:
1. Worker-targeted RCH proof reproducibility, because it removes ambiguity when one remote host, source mirror, or daemon path is suspect.
2. Source mirror and tracked-file attestation, because missing or stale source files invalidate otherwise green proof logs.
3. Queue-aware proof preflight, because massive swarms should avoid saturating all workers or falling back locally when a remote-only lane is required.
4. Proof-ledger worker evidence fields, because closeout artifacts need durable worker identity, repo snapshot, and mirror status rather than prose.
5. Negative fixtures for stale/missing worker mirrors, because the system must prove it fails closed instead of turning an infrastructure problem into a source verdict.

Next ten supporting ideas kept for later integration: active RCH job telemetry in robot health; Agent Mail fallback drills; dirty-tree ownership summaries; macOS memory residency classification; safe target-dir cleanup review; proof-doctor reason-code alignment; shared-worktree staging leases; benchmark bisection hooks; docs truthfulness scanning; no-mock mux loopback proof.

## Overlap and merge notes

This is intentionally not a replacement for ft-uz1bl proof ledger, ft-3yptk representative harness migration, ft-p7un0 proof-ledger docs, ft-uz2gg proof-lane operations hardening, or ft-wik9p proof-doctor taxonomy. It is the missing worker-reproducibility layer that those systems can consume. Child beads should depend on the active proof-ledger tasks where they need ledger schema or migrated harness surfaces, but the first design/runbook slice can proceed independently.

## Goal

Make worker-specific RCH incidents reproducible, diagnosable, and auditable without restarting shared services, draining shared workers, running local heavy Cargo, or treating RCH setup/sync chatter as proof.

## Non-goals

- Do not modify the RCH daemon or external RCH binary unless that code is explicitly in this repository.
- Do not restart, repair, or kill Agent Mail or RCH services.
- Do not run local heavy Cargo as proof.
- Do not weaken existing fail-closed RCH guards.
- Do not touch active proof-ledger or warning-cleanup files without claiming the matching child bead and checking current ownership.

## Acceptance

- Child beads define the operator contract, mirror/source attestation, queue-aware preflight behavior, proof-ledger integration, negative fixtures, and closeout docs.
- At least one early child remains implementable without editing active dirty proof-ledger files.
- Later implementation proof uses RCH only and records worker identity, queue state, repo snapshot, mirror convergence status, target dir, elapsed time, and whether Cargo/rustc was actually reached.
- `bv --robot-triage` reports no active ft-* dependency cycles after the graph is filed.

title: Define worker-targeted RCH proof contract and no-repair runbook
description:
## What

Define the worker-targeted proof contract for FrankenTerm agent workflows: what counts as a valid worker-specific RCH proof, what metadata must be captured, what is only preflight/sync chatter, and what actions are forbidden during incident response.

## Why

A single-worker RCH failure is currently hard to close cleanly. Agents can see missing files or daemon timeouts on a named worker but may only be able to prove a later command that happened to schedule there. Operators need a documented contract that distinguishes target-worker proof, scheduler-selected proof, worker self-test, mirror attestation, local fallback, and inconclusive daemon failure.

## How

Create or update the narrowest existing operator documentation surface. Reuse the ft-wik9p proof-doctor taxonomy and ft-uz1bl proof-ledger vocabulary. Do not invent a separate build system. The runbook should include exact allowed commands, forbidden service actions, RCH-only heavy proof requirements, shared-worker etiquette, and when to reopen a blocker bead.

## Risks

The main risk is documenting behavior that the tooling cannot yet prove. Mark unsupported target-worker operations explicitly as capability gaps and link the later child beads instead of implying they already work.

## Success criteria

- Fresh agents can classify worker-specific incidents without consulting this planning discussion.
- The contract requires worker identity, command class, queue state, repo snapshot, mirror/source status, target dir, elapsed time, exit status, and whether Cargo/rustc was reached.
- The runbook forbids Agent Mail repair/restart, RCH service disruption, local heavy Cargo fallback, and broad worker draining.
- Examples cover valid target-worker proof, scheduler-selected proof with weaker confidence, self-test-only inconclusive evidence, missing tracked source files, and local fallback rejection.
- Validation uses docs/static checks only unless Rust code changes are made; any Cargo proof must run through RCH.

title: [rch] Repair stale or incomplete worker mirrors blocking terminal-conformance proof
description:
## What

RCH terminal-conformance proof for ft-hme39.2 is blocked by stale/incomplete worker source mirrors. The failing run was `tests/e2e/logs/terminal-conformance/ft-hme39.2/20260509T182946Z/summary.json`; RCH selected `vmi1153651` and returned `RCH-REMOTE-MIRROR-MISSING-FILE` before the loopback test binary could run.

## Evidence

- Harness: `RCH_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECS=3600 tests/e2e/test_ft_hme39_2_mux_loopback.sh`
- Artifact dir: `tests/e2e/logs/terminal-conformance/ft-hme39.2/20260509T182946Z/`
- Meta: `loopback_test.log.rch_meta.json` has `selected_worker=vmi1153651`, `remote_exit_code=101`, `timed_out=false`, `fail_open_detected=false`, `failure_reason_code=RCH-REMOTE-MIRROR-MISSING-FILE`.
- Cargo error: remote compile could not read `crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/lib.rs`. That file is tracked and present locally.
- Read-only mirror attestation for `vmi1153651` reported project path `/home/ubuntu/rch/frankenterm/5405212fb4cef0ff`, unreadable HEAD, missing `crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/lib.rs`, and present `Cargo.toml`.
- Additional read-only attestations: `vmi1152480` and `vmi1293453` were clean; `vmi1149989` had unreadable HEAD with required files present; `vmi1156319` missed the replay lib; `vmi1167313` and `vmi1264463` had stale HEADs; `vmi1227854` pointed at `/home/ubuntu/rch` with required files missing.

## Why

The scheduler can select a stale/incomplete worker even when other workers are healthy, so heavy proof lanes fail before source tests execute. Treating that as a source failure would create false negative/false proof ambiguity.

## Acceptance

- Worker mirrors either converge to the local repo HEAD with required tracked files present, or RCH preflight excludes/blocks stale workers before proof lanes run.
- Re-run `tests/e2e/test_ft_hme39_2_mux_loopback.sh` reaches the test binary on an attested worker.
- Do not delete remote source trees or restart shared services as part of the fix without explicit operator approval.

Execute a compilation command on a remote worker

This command is typically invoked by the PreToolUse hook to perform the actual remote compilation. The hook returns immediately with `rch exec -- <command>` to avoid timeout issues.

Usage: rch exec [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <COMMAND>...
          The compilation command to execute remotely

Options:
  -v, --verbose
          Enable verbose output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-error output

  -j, --json
          Output as JSON for machine parsing

  -F, --format <format>
          Machine output format: json or toon
          
          [env: RCH_OUTPUT_FORMAT=]
          [possible values: json, toon]

      --color <COLOR>
          Color output mode: auto, always, never
          
          [default: auto]

      --schema
          Emit JSON Schema for command output format
          
          When specified with a command, outputs the JSON Schema for that command's JSON output format. Use to validate output or understand structure programmatically.
          
          Examples: rch --schema config lint    # Schema for 'config lint' output rch --schema workers list   # Schema for 'workers list' output rch --schema daemon status  # Schema for 'daemon status' output

      --help-json
          Emit help text as JSON for machine parsing
          
          Outputs the CLI structure as JSON, including all subcommands, arguments, and descriptions. Useful for agents to discover available functionality.
          
          Examples: rch --help-json             # Full CLI structure as JSON rch --help-json workers     # Workers subcommand structure

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

EXAMPLES:
    rch exec -- cargo build --release
    rch exec -- cargo test
    rch exec -- bun test

USAGE:
    This command is primarily used internally by the PreToolUse hook.
    The hook intercepts compilation commands and rewrites them as:
        cargo build --release  →  rch exec -- cargo build --release

    This allows the hook to return immediately (<50ms) while the actual
    compilation runs as a normal command invocation. exposes no worker-target/exclude flag, so I did not attempt scheduler steering or remote mutation.

description:
# Continuation: TripleBuffer integration into render path

## Context
ft-2okh0.3 retired at substrate scope:
- 3.1 (TripleBuffer<T>): shipped in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/triple_buffer.rs` (br-ft-d0ol8, commit 7802549a0)
- 3.4 (Loom proof): shipped in `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/loom_triple_buffer.rs`
- Watchdog policy substrate: shipped in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/triple_buffer_watchdog.rs` (commit 498f07a61) — TripleBufferWatchdog state machine with Idle/Active/Warned states, Warn/ForceRecycle decisions, lifetime stats. Pure-logic; integration uses it.

## What this bead carries
The integration work the substrate enables:

### Sub-task 3.2 — Render thread migration
- Wire `TripleBuffer::acquire()` into the renderer's hot path, replacing the current mutex-protected single-buffer access
- Drop guard around `acquire()` that calls `record_acquire(now)` on entry and `record_release()` on drop, feeding into a per-pane `TripleBufferWatchdog`
- Periodic `watchdog.poll(now)` driven from the same timer cadence that runs `IdleDetector::poll` (br-ft-mpc9b.5.3)
- On `WatchdogDecision::ForceRecycle`, invoke `TripleBuffer::force_recycle()` and bump the `force_recycle_invocations` counter
- On `WatchdogDecision::Warn`, log structured warning with `outstanding_for` duration + acquire site

### Sub-task 3.3 — Persistent rope composition
- Once br-ft-mpc9b.2.5 (persistent rope) lands a non-prototype, retire the 3× memory overhead by sharing rope structure across slots — slots become rope version pointers, not full state copies
- Memory accounting: `WriterOverrunsTotal` + per-slot rope-version-id telemetry

title: perf(storage): avoid per-pane no-op FTS catchup on healthy startup
description:
Hot path: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:16959-16983 lists every distinct pane_id and calls sync_fts_for_pane for each pane on every healthy startup. sync_fts_for_pane then does progress lookup plus an unindexed-segment query even when the pane has no new output, making startup O(number_of_panes) SQL round trips for a fully caught-up FTS index. title: [BR-RC-STORAGE-PERF] storage.rs backend-trait refactor bypasses read pool + opens RW mode for read paths
description:
Severity: HIGH (perf regression) + MEDIUM (concurrency model violation) + LOW (silent overflow truncation).

Commit a13e86226 (refactor(storage): route embedding reads through
backend trait, br-ft-l1jgo) migrates six storage.rs reader paths
from `PooledReadConn::acquire(db_path)?` to a new helper:

    fn open_rusqlite_backend(db_path: &str, context: &str) -> Result<RusqliteBackend> {
        RusqliteBackend::open(db_path, &OpenConfig::default())
            .map_err(|err| storage_backend_error(context, err).into())
    }

This opens a FRESH `rusqlite::Connection` on every call + runs the
WAL pragma every time + uses READ_WRITE mode. Three distinct defects:

## [HIGH] Connection-pool bypass

`PooledReadConn::acquire` returned a pre-warmed connection from a
pool — the pool exists exactly because SQLite connection setup
(open file handle, WAL probe, schema cache, page cache warm-up) is
expensive. The new path opens a brand-new connection per call and
discards it after the query. In hot paths (embedding lookup during
search, gap queries during recovery, retention metrics) this is a
real regression — easy 10-50× slowdown on the per-query overhead.

## [MEDIUM] READ_WRITE mode for read-only queries

`OpenConfig::default()` has `read_only: false` + `wal_mode: true`.
`RusqliteBackend::open` then chooses
`SQLITE_OPEN_READ_WRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE`. The original
`PooledReadConn` was the dedicated read-only pool. New behaviour:

- READ_WRITE connections enter the writer-pool contention model
  (multi-writer-readers WAL design); previously these paths were
  guaranteed not to compete with the writer thread for the
  database write-lock.
- SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE is wrong intent for read paths — a missing
  database silently creates a fresh one instead of erroring.
- Each open re-runs `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, which under
  contention with the writer can cause SQLITE_BUSY transitions
  during checkpoint.

## [LOW] Silent integer truncation in embedding_stats

```rust
dimension: reader.i64(1)? as i32,
```

Pre-refactor used `row.get(1)?` which returned `Err` on overflow
via rusqlite typed conversion. The `as i32` silently wraps. Realistic
SQLite column values fit, but the defensive contract regressed.
Should be `i32::try_from(reader.i64(1)?).map_err(|_| BackendError::Query(...))`.

## Affected call sites (all in commit a13e86226)

1. `StorageHandle::store_embedding` — INSERT path now via execute_typed
   (also bypasses the canonical writer-thread dispatch, but that was
   already pre-existing pattern using PooledReadConn for INSERT).
2. `StorageHandle::get_unembedded_segments` — read.
3. `StorageHandle::get_embedding` — read.
4. `StorageHandle::embedding_stats` — read + the [LOW] silent
   truncation site.
5. `StorageHandle::get_gaps` — read.
6. `StorageHandle::retention_cleanup_count` — read.
7. `StorageHandle::segment_time_range` — read.

The refactor pattern (replace 6 sites of PooledReadConn with
open_rusqlite_backend) is also present at commit 6e711f8d1
(refactor(storage): route saved-search reads through backend trait)
— the same defects likely apply there.

## Fix

Three coordinated changes:

1. Extend `RusqliteBackend` to accept an existing
   `rusqlite::Connection` (it already does via `RusqliteBackend::new`).
   Add a helper that wraps a `PooledReadConn` into a borrowed
   `RusqliteBackend` — likely a new `RusqliteBackend::wrap_pooled(&PooledReadConn)`
   method or a `BorrowedRusqliteBackend<a>` newtype that doesn`t own
   the connection.

2. Update `open_rusqlite_backend` callers to acquire a pooled read
   conn first, then wrap it into the backend:

   ```rust
   let conn = PooledReadConn::acquire(db_path.as_str())?;
   let backend = RusqliteBackend::wrap_pooled(&conn);
   // existing typed-trait calls work unchanged
   ```

3. For the (rare) read-paths that genuinely need a fresh connection,
   pass `OpenConfig { read_only: true, wal_mode: false, ..default }`
   so the SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY flag fires + no WAL pragma.

4. Replace `as i32` truncations with `i32::try_from(...)`.

## Acceptance

- All 7 reader sites in a13e86226 + 6e711f8d1 use the pooled
  connection path.
- A regression test asserts that calling `get_embedding` 100×
  does NOT open 100 separate connections (use a probe via
  `Connection::is_busy` or a counter wrapper).
- Existing storage tests still pass.
- `dimension: i32` truncation replaced with try_from; new test
  asserts overflow input → error.

## Cross-references

- a13e86226 — refactor(storage): route embedding reads (this bug)
- 6e711f8d1 — refactor(storage): route saved-search reads (likely
  same bug pattern, audit during fix)
- ft-l1jgo — parent (call-site migration epic)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs (RusqliteBackend
  + OpenConfig)
- PooledReadConn module in storage.rs (around line 8310+)
close_reason: done

comments.text: cc_1 (closing): all three findings resolved. [HIGH] pool bypass — fixed at 61ce1883a (ft-3twzm) by routing all 9 sites through pooled_rusqlite_backend. [LOW] embedding_stats silent i32 truncation — fixed at 47b1b9cd8 with i32::try_from + BackendError::Query on overflow. [MEDIUM] dead open_rusqlite_backend helper removed at 47b1b9cd8 — eliminates the foot-gun where a future refactor could re-introduce the per-call Connection::open + PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL regression. Note re the bead's READ_WRITE claim: PooledReadConn was never read-only — open_read_storage_conn uses Connection::open which defaults to SQLITE_OPEN_READ_WRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE, and the pool is shared by writer paths (store_embedding, etc). title: [lock_manager_health.fix] is_safe returns true when only force-releases have happened
description:
Bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/lock.rs:145-163 (the LockManagerHealth::is_safe method the linter added during this session's review pass).

## Defect

is_safe checks force-release ratio:

    if self.releases_total == 0 {
        return true;  // ← wrong if force_releases_total > 0
    }
    let force_ratio = self.force_releases_total as f64 / self.releases_total as f64;
    force_ratio <= 0.05

When releases_total == 0 but force_releases_total > 0, the function returns true. But that means ONLY force-releases have happened — a 100% pathological rate, not healthy.

## Repro

let mut h = LockManagerHealth::default();
h.force_releases_total = 10;  // 10 stuck workflows force-released
h.releases_total = 0;          // no normal releases
assert!(h.is_safe());          // returns TRUE — wrong

## Why it matters

The docstring says 'force-release rate is non-pathological (≤5% of total releases)'. The early return for releases_total == 0 silently treats the worst case (pure force-release) as healthy.

Operator scenario: a stress storm causes every workflow to panic, leaving stuck locks. Operator runs force_release on each. is_safe still returns true → ft doctor reports green → operator misses the smoking gun.

## Fix

Reject the case where force_releases_total > 0 && releases_total == 0:

    if self.releases_total == 0 {
        return self.force_releases_total == 0;  // healthy iff truly idle
    }

OR move the empty-case check below the 5% ratio check so the threshold is uniformly applied (treat 0 releases + N force_releases as 100% force ratio).

## Acceptance

- is_safe returns false when force_releases > 0 and releases == 0.
- is_safe still returns true when both counters are 0 (truly idle, no operations yet).
- Regression test reproduces the bug + asserts the fix.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/lock.rs:145-163 (the buggy is_safe)
- ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r (the same is_safe-rubber-stamp pattern; this is the 4th instance found this review pass)
notes:
Fix landed via commit bbe7aaf67 (concurrent agent absorbed). LockManagerHealth::is_safe now rejects the pure-force-release case: when releases_total == 0, returns true iff force_releases_total is also 0.

5 regression tests (verified passing):
- lock_manager_health_is_safe_rejects_force_releases_without_normal_releases (load-bearing — proves the fix)
- lock_manager_health_is_safe_accepts_truly_idle (boundary)
- lock_manager_health_is_safe_accepts_low_force_ratio
- lock_manager_health_is_safe_rejects_high_force_ratio
- lock_manager_health_is_safe_rejects_mutex_poisoning

4th instance of the is_safe-rubber-stamp pattern this review pass:
- ft-ftepl: render_snapshot_audit is_safe monotonic-false
- ft-vgtab: cold_tier_pipeline record_write rubber-stamp
- ft-cof0r: policy.rs trauma_bypass substring widening
- ft-ismxr (this): lock_manager_health is_safe edge-case rubber-stamp

The pattern is now well-established. Worth a codebase-wide audit pass on similar shapes.

ft-1dq8h substrate: evaluate_buffer_admission Truncated decision overflows cap when incoming_bytes > cap
description:
sync_output_buffer_orchestrator.rs evaluate_buffer_admission produces a Truncated{dropped_bytes} result that, when followed by the integration, can still overflow the buffer cap.

Repro: cap=4096, current_used=1000, incoming=10_000.
- after = 11_000, overflow = 11_000 − 4096 = 6904.
- dropped_bytes = min(6904, 1000) = 1000.
- Integration drops 1000 (all current), appends 10_000 → buffer holds 10_000 bytes, exceeding 4096 cap.

The substrate's contract says 'drop dropped_bytes worth and append incoming' but the result violates the cap when incoming alone exceeds cap.

Fix: when incoming_bytes > config.effective_max_bytes(), return Refused (substrate can't trim incoming bytes it doesn't see; integration must chunk large PTY bursts). When incoming ≤ cap, Truncated semantics work correctly.

Tracked under self-review pass.
