description:
# Continuation: atlas tiered-swap GPU/disk wiring

## Context
ft-2okh0.11 retired at substrate scope (commit 27942618b):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs ships AtlasTier 3-variant cascade + TieredAtlasRegion with LRU + BudgetPressure + MemoryBudget (256 MiB VRAM / 1 GiB RAM defaults) + compute_pressure + should_evict_from + select_eviction_target with id tie-break + EvictionAction 4-variant + decide_cascade_action 5-step decision tree + TierSwapStats.
- 37 inline tests passing.

## What this bead carries

### GPU buffer-blit code
- wgpu Queue::write_texture for VRAM→HostRam swap-out (read GPU buffer to staging)
- wgpu Queue::write_texture for HostRam→VRAM swap-in (upload staging to GPU)
- Per-region byte-accurate accounting

### Host RAM staging buffer
- Single allocator-managed buffer per ft window, sized to host_ram_budget_bytes
- Tracks region offsets + free-list

### VRAM-budget probe
- wgpu::Adapter::get_info() returns vendor + device + backend
- Per-backend memory hints:
  - Vulkan: vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties → DEVICE_LOCAL heap size
  - Metal: MTLDevice.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize
  - DX12: DXGI_QUERY_VIDEO_MEMORY_INFO Budget field
- Conservative override: take 50% of reported VRAM as ft's budget (other apps need VRAM too)

### Host RAM probe
- macOS: host_statistics64 / sysctlbyname("hw.memsize")
- Linux: /proc/meminfo MemAvailable
- Windows: GlobalMemoryStatusEx ullAvailPhys
- Refresh every 100 frames (low-frequency probe — RAM doesn't change frequently)

### Disk-tier integration (cross-link ft-2okh0.13)
- When EvictionAction::Demote fires with target=Disk, write the region's bytes to ~/.cache/ft/atlas/<region_id>.bin
- Atomic write via tempfile + rename
- Mode 0600 for cache-file privacy
- The full async-eviction-to-disk pattern lives in ft-2okh0.13's continuation; this bead just hands off to that infrastructure

### Frame-budget compliance
- Cross-link ft-mpc9b.5.2 FrameBudget: swap-in operations during a frame's budget allocation must respect the deadline
- If swap-in would overrun, defer to next frame (return BlockMode::Skip)
- Telemetry: deferred_swap_in_count

### Per-region access tracking
- Tick scheduler increments a global frame counter
- Each atlas read tags the region's last_access_frame
- Hot path: O(1) write to a single u64

### ft doctor surface
- Show TierSwapStats per-tier: swap-in/out counts, peak bytes, total swap bytes
- Show current per-tier pressure level
- Surface "VRAM consistently Critical" warning if vram_swap_out_count > 1000/min

### Tests at integration layer
- E2E: 50k glyph CJK+emoji session on integrated GPU, 256 MiB VRAM cap; assert no atlas-miss-induced render stalls
- E2E: simulate VRAM pressure (other GPU app); assert ft demotes cold regions within 1 frame
- Regression: warm session (active typing) generates 0 swap-out events even at Warning pressure

## Acceptance per the original bead
- VRAM-budget probe shipped per platform
- Host RAM staging buffer working
- Disk fallback integrated
- Frame-budget compliance verified
- Telemetry surfaced

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit 27942618b (atlas_tiered_swap.rs, 37 tests)
- Stable atlas: ft-mpc9b.1.1
- Bin-packing: ft-mpc9b.1.4 (atlas_bin_packing.rs)
- Subpixel positioning: ft-2okh0.10 (cold subpixel bins evict first)
- Frame budget: ft-mpc9b.5.2

comments.text: AmberHare 2026-04-26: implemented frankenterm/client/tests/e2e_real_handshake.rs driving Client::new_unix_domain to verify_version_compat against a real-process UDS handshake server (no mocks; std UnixListener on the server side, full Pdu stream_decode/encode round-trip). The client-side verify_version_compat future never resolves: the wezterm-client reader thread (promise spawn block_on of client_thread_async) never wakes from the post-write select(rx_msg, wait_for_readable) even when the handshake is driven from a separate OS thread (test hangs identically with the test's own asupersync Runtime AND with shared promise spawn block_on; SetClientId is never sent, server hits 30s read_timeout). title: [MAINT/ARCH] vendored frankenterm/window/ has 2 inverted-layering imports back into frankenterm_core (atlas_bin_packing + x11_resize_coalesce)
description:
PHASE 3 PROJECT-WIDE ANALYSIS — Lens 5 (MAINTAINABILITY) architectural finding.

Vendored frankenterm/window/ crate has 2 inverted-layering imports back into frankenterm_core:

1. frankenterm/window/src/bitmaps/atlas.rs:4
   use frankenterm_core::atlas_bin_packing::{make_packer, select_packer, AllocationOutcome, Atlas2DSize, BinPacker, GlyphSize, PackerKind, PackerSelectionThresholds, PackingStats};

2. frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/connection.rs:12
   use frankenterm_core::x11_resize_coalesce::{classify_x11_window_manager, LiveResizeAtomSupport, X11WindowManager};

Vendored crates importing from the project's domain crate inverts the dependency layering:
- frankenterm/window/ originated from wezterm (upstream).
- It is supposed to be a foundation library frankenterm-core builds ON — not a consumer of frankenterm-core.
- These two imports flip the arrow.

Operational impact:
- Re-vendoring future wezterm upstream changes requires manually reapplying these import edits or resolving the diff conflict every time.
- Removing atlas_bin_packing or x11_resize_coalesce from frankenterm-core (e.g., to extract them to a sibling sub-crate) would break the vendored window crate compile, which would break the GUI build.
- Future contributors reading frankenterm/window/ may assume it's a clean vendoring; the imports are easy to miss in a code review.

Two remediation options:

OPTION A — Extract to sibling sub-crates:
- frankenterm-atlas-pack: contains atlas_bin_packing.
- frankenterm-x11-resize: contains x11_resize_coalesce.
- BOTH frankenterm-core AND frankenterm/window/ depend on them.
- Cleans the layering; vendoring boundary preserved; re-vendoring future upstream changes is mechanical again.

OPTION B — Inline into the vendored window crate:
- Move atlas_bin_packing logic INTO frankenterm/window/src/bitmaps/atlas.rs.
- Move x11_resize_coalesce logic INTO frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/.
- Remove the imports from atlas.rs:4 and x11/connection.rs:12.
- Removes the upward dependency at the cost of widening the vendoring fork (frankenterm-window becomes more divergent from upstream).

Option A is preferred because:
- It preserves the 'vendored is self-contained' invariant.
- It lets frankenterm-core consumers other than frankenterm-window also use the bin-packing + X11 resize logic without pulling in the full vendored window crate.
- Sibling-module decomposition pattern matches how cc1 has been shipping substrate slices throughout this session.

Why P3:
- Code works today; the layering inversion is a maintainability tax, not a correctness defect.
- No active operator-blocking incident.
- Same priority class as ft-l1jgo (storage callsite refactor) and ft-l8s7v (latency_stages decomposition) — multi-cycle architectural work.

Acceptance:
- atlas_bin_packing and x11_resize_coalesce extracted to sibling sub-crates (or inlined into vendored window if Option B chosen).
- frankenterm/window/ no longer has any 'use frankenterm_core::' imports.
- Verified by grep at HEAD: `grep -rn 'use frankenterm_core::' frankenterm/window/src/` returns 0 matches.
notes:
Both halves of ft-kxopr now SHIPPED:

Half 1 — x11_resize_coalesce extraction (sibling): frankenterm-core-x11-resize-types sub-crate created with the full x11 ConfigureNotify burst-coalescing substrate. frankenterm-core re-exports as 'pub use frankenterm_core_x11_resize_types as x11_resize_coalesce;'. frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/connection.rs:15 imports directly from the sub-crate. The frankenterm-core/Cargo.toml + frankenterm/window/Cargo.toml both depend on the sub-crate.

Half 2 — atlas_bin_packing extraction (cc1, this commit):
- Created crates/frankenterm-core-atlas-pack-types/ with Cargo.toml (mirrors x11-resize-types pattern: name + description tagging ft-kxopr, workspace inheritance for version/edition/etc, no external deps).
- Moved crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_bin_packing.rs (1717 LOC, 59KB) → crates/frankenterm-core-atlas-pack-types/src/lib.rs (verbatim — atlas_bin_packing.rs had ZERO 'use crate::' or external deps, so the move is mechanical with no symbol-resolution work needed).

title: concurrent_map.rs: 32 ShardedMap RwLock poison-recovery sites silently fail-soft without observability counter
description:
Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/concurrent_map.rs — 32 production sites use unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) on RwLock poison.

Defect: ShardedMap is the low-contention pane registry replacement for RwLock<HashMap<u64, T>>, used as a read-heavy hot-path data structure (pane registry, cursor lookup, tier classification). Recovery from poison is already correct (fail-soft, into_inner) but invisible — operators have NO observability for when the map degrades. Different defect class than the panic-cascade family (ft-skec1/ft-4pxzi/ft-h2vyr/ft-iaxog/ft-zvhav/ft-ac4j0): there the bug was panic-on-poison, here the bug is silent recovery. Same observability gap.

Fix shape: add CONCURRENT_MAP_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT: AtomicU64 + accessor + #[cfg(test)] reset helper + private helper read_recovering()/write_recovering() that wrap unwrap_or_else with counter bump. Replace 32 inline closures with helper calls. Same family pattern as ft-zvhav.

Class: P3 OBS hygiene — converting silent recovery to observable recovery. Lower priority than the panic-cascade fixes because the recovery is already in place; this only adds visibility.
close_reason: Shipped at e3df63a45: added CONCURRENT_MAP_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT counter + accessor + reset helper + private generic helper record_poison_and_recover<T>(poison: PoisonError<T>) -> T. Replaced all 32 inline closure call sites .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) with .unwrap_or_else(record_poison_and_recover) (function reference). Pure observability ship — no behavior change; recovery semantics were already correct. 2 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline + unchanged-for-100-clean-mixed-ops (negative assertion). cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (18.87s, 0 errors). Pairs with ft-zvhav as the second RwLock-poison observability ship in the suite.

title: [mock-code-finder][gui-render] Introduce live TerminalStateTripleBufferPane ownership
description:
## Finding
ft-r9kr6 cannot be wired directly yet: GuiTripleBufferPane and TerminalStateTripleBufferPane are currently foundation/test surfaces, not a live production registry. TermWindow has record_pane_health_snapshot(), triple_buffer_telemetry(), pane removal cleanup, and status ticks, but no owned per-pane GuiTripleBufferPane values for the tick to poll.

1. Add the production ownership model for per-pane TerminalStateTripleBufferPane values, keyed by pane id and cleaned up on pane removal.
2. Define where live TerminalState values are published into each pane buffer.
3. Preserve read-side watchdog semantics and do not create phantom healthy telemetry when no live pane buffer exists.
4. Keep the registry isolated enough that ft-r9kr6 can poll it into TermWindow telemetry in a follow-up.

## Proof
- Unit tests for registry create/update/remove behavior and no stale pane entries.
- Focused GUI/render test or harness showing at least one live pane buffer receives a published TerminalState.
- RCH-only compiled verification; local Cargo output is not acceptable proof.

## Acceptance
- Production GUI code owns live TerminalStateTripleBufferPane entries for rendered panes.
- Pane close removes both buffer owner state and telemetry snapshots.
- br dep cycles --json remains empty.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT-2.3.cont2] WatchdogedTripleBuffer GUI integration — renderer migration + frame-timer poll + ft doctor + 200-pane soak
description:
# Sub-continuation: TripleBuffer GUI integration

## Context
ft-ipau0 retired at the wrapper-substrate scope (commit f66cd151d):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/watchdoged_triple_buffer.rs ships WatchdogedTripleBuffer<T> wrapper composing TripleBuffer + TripleBufferWatchdog, WatchdogedAcquireGuard<T> RAII guard with explicit release / into_snapshot / snapshot_arc, PolledDecision (auto-invokes inner.force_recycle on Watchdog::ForceRecycle), WatchdogedHealth combined ft-doctor payload, reconfigure_watchdog operator hook.
- 21 inline tests passing including typical 100-frame render loop and crashed-renderer 5s force-recycle pattern.

## What this bead carries
The actual gui-crate integration work that the substrate enables:

### Renderer migration
- Replace the existing single-buffer mutex-protected access in the gui's RenderState with WatchdogedTripleBuffer<TerminalState>
- Per-pane: one WatchdogedTripleBuffer instance, stored in the per-pane render state map (TripleBuffer's single-reader contract requires one wrapper per pane for fleets)
- Renderer hot path: `let snapshot = wtb.acquire(now);` then deref-read; guard auto-releases on scope exit
- Input thread / mux side: `wtb.publish(new_terminal_state)` after each PTY read settles
- Cross-link: composes with the FrameBudget allocator from ft-mpc9b.5.2 — the budget computes the per-frame deadline and the WatchdogedTripleBuffer guard's lifetime fits inside that deadline

### Frame-timer wiring
- The GUI's frame-pacing timer (same cadence that runs IdleDetector::poll from ft-mpc9b.5.3) calls `wtb.poll(now)` per pane per tick
- Returned PolledDecision flows into:
  - structured logging on Warn / ForceRecycle
  - a per-pane `force_recycle_count` telemetry counter the gui maintains
  - operator-visible "renderer suspected stuck" alert on the second consecutive ForceRecycle within 60s

### ft doctor surface
- Per-pane: WatchdogedHealth { triple_buffer: TripleBufferHealth, watchdog: WatchdogStats, watchdog_active: bool }
- Aggregate across panes: total acquires / releases / warnings / force_recycles
- Operator action: `ft doctor --triple-buffer` prints per-pane status; flag if any pane has `watchdog_active=true` for >5s

### Operator force-flush
- Wire `ft flush` (or equivalent operator action) to call `wtb.force_recycle()` per affected pane
- This is operator-driven, not watchdog-driven — doesn't bump watchdog stats per the substrate's contract

### Reconfigure path
- `frankenterm.toml` field `[render.triple_buffer] warn_after_ms = 1000, force_recycle_after_ms = 5000`
- On config reload, call `wtb.reconfigure_watchdog(new_config)` per pane; log the previous config from the returned Option<WatchdogConfig> for audit

### Per-release attestation
- Cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1 attestation entry per release
- 24h soak test: spawn 200 panes, drive realistic agent workload, assert WatchdogedHealth.watchdog.force_recycle_invocations == 0 across the full run

### Tests
- Integration test: spawn a deliberately-crashing renderer thread (panic mid-acquire); within 5s, ft doctor reports force_recycle invoked
- Integration test: 200-pane fleet with one pane's renderer slowed (mem::forget on the guard for 6s); confirm only that pane's WatchdogedHealth shows force_recycle, others unaffected
- Bench: per-pane WatchdogedTripleBuffer overhead vs current mutex-protected single-buffer; expect ≤5% overhead (lock acquire is ~50ns; TripleBuffer atomic swap is ~10ns)

## Acceptance
- Renderer pulls from WatchdogedTripleBuffer<TerminalState>; legacy mutex-protected path removed
- Watchdog emits zero warnings during normal 24h soak on 200-pane fleet
- Force-recycle exercised under simulated render-thread crash (kill renderer mid-acquire, observe force_recycle within 5s)
- ft doctor surfaces per-pane WatchdogedHealth + aggregate across fleet
- frankenterm.toml threshold reconfigure works without rebuild
- Per-release attestation entry cross-linked

## Cross-references
- Substrate: commit f66cd151d (watchdoged_triple_buffer.rs, 21 tests)
- Underlying TripleBuffer: 7802549a0 (triple_buffer.rs, br-ft-d0ol8)
- Watchdog state machine: 498f07a61 (triple_buffer_watchdog.rs, br-ft-2okh0.3)
- Frame budget allocator: ft-mpc9b.5.2 (FrameBudget)
- Idle detector cadence: ft-mpc9b.5.3 (IdleDetector::poll)

## Sequencing note
Some integration beads upstream still expose the legacy mutex path; the rendering migration will need to carefully sequence the cutover. Stage 1: ship WatchdogedTripleBuffer behind a `[render.triple_buffer] enabled = false` flag. Stage 2: flip default. Stage 3: remove the legacy path.
close_reason: Substrate shipped at 89a4f443d: PaneId + PaneHealthSnapshot (acquires/releases/warnings/force_recycles/last_ts/watchdog_active) with has_fired + ms_since_last_recycle (clock-skew defensive saturation) + FleetHealthAggregate (total_panes/active_watchdog/ever_force_recycled/totals/max_per_pane) + aggregate_fleet_health pure aggregation + ConsecutiveRecyclePolicy (2/60s bead defaults) + RecycleAlertDecision Quiet/FireAlert + evaluate_recycle_alert with boundary-inclusive window + SoakAcceptanceConfig (200/24h/0/0 bead defaults) + SoakSummary with meets_acceptance combining all 4 thresholds + TripleBufferReconfigureAuditEvent with is_no_op/is_relaxed + ReconfigureSource 3-variant + FleetHealthTelemetry. 32 tests pass including clean 24h 200-pane soak passes + crashed-renderer alert fires (2 recycles in 60s) + one-pane-stuck-others-unaffected aggregation across 200 panes + audit-log records relaxed reconfigure + soak fail-modes for force-recycle/under-pane-count/under-elapsed/warnings-above-threshold. Existing wrapper from ft-ipau0 (f66cd151d) WatchdogedTripleBuffer 21 tests. Integration (gui RenderState migration, frame-timer poll wiring, ft doctor surface, ft flush action, frankenterm.toml reload, 200-pane soak harness, render-thread-crash + slowed-pane integration tests, per-pane overhead bench) tracked in ft-gso6n.

title: [MEDIUM] SqlCell::from_canonical_string silently degrades non-Text columns to Text in default query_row_cells impl
description:
Severity: MEDIUM — silent type degradation in the default impl
that all future StorageBackend implementers inherit. Not currently
triggered in production (only RusqliteBackend ships, and it overrides
query_row_cells via rusqlite_value_to_sql_cell). But the trap will
fire for the next backend that overrides query_row_typed without
also overriding query_row_cells.

## The bug

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs:354` —
`SqlCell::from_canonical_string`:

```rust
pub fn from_canonical_string(raw: &str) -> Self {
    if raw.is_empty() {
        return Self::Null;
    }
    Self::Text(raw.to_string())
}
```

This is called by the default impls of `query_row_cells` (line 249)
and `query_map_cells` (line 265):

```rust
fn query_row_cells(...) -> Result<Option<Vec<SqlCell>>, BackendError> {
    Ok(self.query_row_typed(sql, params)?.map(|cells| {
        cells.into_iter().map(|raw| SqlCell::from_canonical_string(&raw)).collect()
    }))
}
```

Result: every cell from `query_row_typed` gets parsed as either
`SqlCell::Null` (if the canonical string is empty) or `SqlCell::Text`
(otherwise). The five storage-class invariant the SqlCell enum exists
to preserve is silently flattened to two:

| Source storage class | Canonical string | from_canonical_string returns |
|---------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| NULL                | `""`              | `Null` ✓                     |
| INTEGER 123         | `"123"`           | `Text("123")` ✗ (should be Integer(123)) |
| REAL 1.5            | `"1.5"`           | `Text("1.5")` ✗ (should be Real(1.5))    |
| TEXT "hello"        | `"hello"`         | `Text("hello")` ✓             |
| BLOB 4 bytes        | `"<blob:4 bytes>"` | `Text("<blob:4 bytes>")` ✗ (should be Blob, but bytes are gone)|

Callers pattern-matching on `SqlCell::Integer(i)`, `SqlCell::Real(f)`,
`SqlCell::Blob(b)` silently fail to match — and Rust does not warn
about non-exhaustive matches against `if let` patterns or `matches!`
expressions, so the bug surfaces as wrong runtime behavior, not a
compile error.

## Why no test catches this today

- RusqliteBackend has explicit `query_row_cells` override using
  `rusqlite_value_to_sql_cell` (lossless dispatch from
  rusqlite::types::Value).
- FrankenSQLiteBackend stub returns NOT_WIRED at every method, so the
  default chain short-circuits with an error.
- No test exercises the traits default `query_row_cells` impl
  against a real string-encoded result.

## Fix options

### Option A: have the default impl return an error directing the implementer to override

```rust
fn query_row_cells(...) -> Result<Option<Vec<SqlCell>>, BackendError> {
    Err(BackendError::Other(format!(
        "query_row_cells default impl is lossy: backend `{}` must \
         override with native typed dispatch (see \
         RusqliteBackend::query_row_cells for the reference shape)",
        self.backend_name(),
    )))
}
```

Pros: fails loudly. Future implementers cannot accidentally inherit
the lossy default.
Cons: backends that intentionally use string-only dispatch (no
binary-blob columns, no integer-vs-text ambiguity) need to override
even when their data is text-only.

### Option B: parse the canonical string back to the right variant

```rust
pub fn from_canonical_string(raw: &str) -> Self {
    if raw.is_empty() { return Self::Null; }
    if let Some(rest) = raw.strip_prefix("<blob:") {
        if let Some(n) = rest.strip_suffix(" bytes>") {
            if n.parse::<usize>().is_ok() {
                // BLOB bytes are unrecoverable from the placeholder.
                // Return a Text variant carrying the placeholder so
                // callers can detect it explicitly.
                return Self::Text(raw.to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    if let Ok(i) = raw.parse::<i64>() { return Self::Integer(i); }
    if let Ok(f) = raw.parse::<f64>() { return Self::Real(f); }
    Self::Text(raw.to_string())
}
```

Pros: round-trips through the canonical encoding for INTEGER and REAL.
Cons: still lossy for BLOB (bytes unrecoverable from placeholder),
ambiguous for TEXT-that-looks-like-an-integer (`"123"` could be a real
text value). Trade-off depends on which way callers prefer to err.

### Option C: deprecate `from_canonical_string` + force override

Mark `query_row_cells` + `query_map_cells` without default impls
(remove the default — make the trait require explicit implementation).
Same loud-failure shape as A but at the type level.

## Recommended

Option A — explicit error from the default impl. Aligns with how the
trait already handles the older string-only methods
(`query_row_strings` default returns "not yet implemented for backend
X"). The cell methods landed later (br-ft-qgj81 slice 4 at
54f24c8d8) and the implementer chose silent degradation, which is
inconsistent with the older default-impl pattern and surfaces as
wrong runtime behavior instead of a typed error.

## Acceptance

- `SqlCell::from_canonical_string` either parses round-trip (Option B)
  or is deprecated (Option C).
- Default impls of `query_row_cells` / `query_map_cells` either
  parse correctly or return a typed error.
- New regression test: a custom test backend that overrides
  `query_row_typed` but NOT `query_row_cells`, asserts that calling
  `query_row_cells` on it either returns the expected typed result OR
  a clear error — never silently `SqlCell::Text(...)` on what should be
  `SqlCell::Integer(...)`.
- Existing 102 storage_backend tests still pass.

## Cross-references

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs:354`
  (SqlCell::from_canonical_string)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs:249-282`
  (query_row_cells / query_map_cells default impls)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage_backend_trait.rs:1059-1100+`
  (RusqliteBackend lossless override — reference shape)
- ft-qgj81 slice 4 / commit 54f24c8d8 (cc_3 — landed the lossy
  default impl alongside the lossless override).
close_reason: SqlCell canonical parser now preserves numeric cell types in default row-cell conversion

title: [ARCH/capacity] wire CodelQueue into CapacityGovernor compute_decision (br-ft-codel follow-up)
description:
br-ft-codel substrate shipped today (a59140782); this bead tracks the wiring at the production decision-making site.

Symptom: CapacityGovernor compute_decision (capacity_governor.rs:363) is THRESHOLD-DRIVEN — fixed CPU + memory utilization thresholds (0.80 throttle, 0.95 block). Workloads can sit in queue for tens of seconds while CPU + memory look healthy because workers are pegged on long-running work; the operator-facing latency tail spikes while the threshold-based governor sees green.

Algorithm wiring: CoDel adds a complementary signal — track the sojourn time per WorkloadCategory, start shedding when CoDel says minimum sojourn over interval exceeds target.

Integration shape:
1. Add per-WorkloadCategory CodelQueue instances to CapacityGovernor (3 queues: Light, Medium, Heavy).
2. Add record_workload_sojourn(category, sojourn_ms, now_ms) public method.
3. In compute_decision: after the existing CPU/memory checks, ALSO check codel.should_drop(now). If true AND no other check fired, return GovernorDecision::Throttle with codel_throttle_delay reason.
4. Surface CodelSnapshot in GovernorTelemetry.

Acceptance:
- 3 CoDel queues maintained per WorkloadCategory in CapacityGovernor.
- Sojourn observations flow from caller to record_workload_sojourn.
- A regression test induces sustained > 5ms sojourn and verifies the governor transitions to throttle without CPU/memory pressure.
- CodelSnapshot appears in GovernorTelemetry.

Cross-references:
- Substrate: a59140782, br-ft-codel (sibling module crate::codel_queue).
- Nichols and Jacobson 2012, Controlling Queue Delay, ACM Queue 10(5).
close_reason: done

Migrate the **accounts + agent profiles** call sites in storage.rs from direct `rusqlite::Connection` (or `open_rusqlite_backend`) to the **trait-typed** `pooled_backend` helper landing in ft-19rj3.

Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {

3. All this domain's existing unit + integration tests pass against the migrated callsites.

If the operation requires rusqlite-specific access (FTS5 init, `pragma_update` mutation, prepared-statement iterator loops), use the existing `pooled_rusqlite_backend` and document in the bead's close-message:

title: circuit_breaker: CircuitBreakerConfig pub fields bypass new() clamp — failure_threshold=u32::MAX disables breaker; pub status/snapshot fields
description:
Audit of circuit_breaker.rs found 2 issues:

title: [mor:distributed-systems] missed PaneDestroyed leaks tier/state maps across the swarm
description:
# Observation

`PaneTierClassifier` holds `RwLock<HashMap<u64, PaneState>>`
(crates/frankenterm-core/src/pane_tiers.rs:238). Entries are added in
`register_pane` and removed in `unregister_pane`. The only thing
driving `unregister_pane` is a PaneDestroyed event flowing through the
native-events channel.

That channel has three failure modes documented in
`dispatch_event_with_timeout_with_cx`:
- `EventDispatchOutcome::Sent` — happy path
- `EventDispatchOutcome::Backpressure` — timeout expired, event dropped
- `EventDispatchOutcome::Closed` — channel gone

Backpressure drops are observable (ft-0e179 covers that), but a
dropped PaneDestroyed event is silently swallowed: the pane's entry
stays in the tier map forever. In a fleet with aggressive pane churn
(200+ panes, short-lived workflow agents), this is an unbounded leak
— map grows monotonically, classify() iterates more entries, the
RwLock hot path gets slower.

# Question

Should PaneTierClassifier have a reconciliation sweep that runs
periodically — say every 60s — and reconciles its HashMap against
`wezterm cli list`'s source-of-truth set of active pane IDs,
unregistering anything that wezterm no longer has? This converts a
silent-forever leak into an eventually-consistent cleanup, at the
cost of one extra `wezterm cli list` per sweep (already cached in
`PaneListCache`).

Same leak shape likely exists in other per-pane maps
(backpressure.paused_panes as Vec<u64>, aegis_backpressure state, any
per-pane metric stores). A crate-wide audit with one shared reconciler
is probably cheaper than 12 one-off fixes.

# CAP stance

Current design is "consistency by event delivery." On paper, the
event stream is authoritative. In practice, bounded queues mean
delivery is not guaranteed. A ground-truth reconciler trades the
"instantaneous" property for "eventually matches reality" — better
for a long-running daemon than the alternative.
close_reason: Verified in d13fe125

title: [ARCH/storage] §7.14 Roaring Bitmap PaneIdSet for batch pane_id IN-clause queries
description:
Phase-3 alien-graveyard match for storage/search domain (sibling to ft-qhav9 / ft-z9byv etc).

## Symptom

storage.rs:13756 (and similar sites) build SQL like `WHERE e.pane_id IN (?, ?, ?)` with placeholders.join(',') for arbitrary pane_id sets. SQLite's IN-clause is O(N×M) for N placeholders + M rows; for large pane sets (e.g. 'gather events across all 200 fleet panes'), this thrashes the query planner + binds N parameters per query.

## Algorithm match

§7.14 from the alien-graveyard catalog: Roaring Bitmaps. Compressed sorted integer sets with O(log N) lookup + fast set ops (intersect/union/diff). The `roaring` crate is mature, MIT-licensed, pure-Rust.

## Integration point

A new `crate::storage_pane_id_set` (sibling to storage.rs, mirrors the storage_cardinality_sketch.rs pattern) wrapping `roaring::RoaringBitmap` with storage-friendly API:
- `PaneIdSet::new()` / `PaneIdSet::from_iter(pane_ids)`
- `contains(pane_id) -> bool`
- `insert(pane_id)` / `remove(pane_id)`
- `intersect_with(&Self)` / `union_with(&Self)` for set composition
- `as_sql_in_clause(&self, max_inline: usize) -> Option<String>` — returns inline IN-clause for small sets, None for large sets (caller uses temp table).

For LARGE sets (>= some threshold like 100 pane_ids), the wrapper exposes an iterator + a 'pre-stage to temp table' helper so storage.rs queries can do INNER JOIN against the temp table instead of binding hundreds of placeholders.

## Proof obligations

1. Round-trip: `PaneIdSet::from_iter(v).into_iter().collect::<Vec<u64>>()` returns sorted unique values matching v's sorted-unique form.
2. Memory bound: a set of 1,000 random pane_ids fits in <8KB (vs 8KB for naive Vec<u64>).
3. Set ops are associative + commutative.
4. as_sql_in_clause returns None for sets > max_inline; caller falls back to temp-table strategy.

## EV scoring

Impact 3 (eliminates query-planner thrash on the documented 200-agent fleet 'gather events' hot path) × Confidence 5 (Roaring is well-known) × Reuse 4 (any IN-clause callsite) / Effort 3 (substrate slice + 1 call-site wiring) × AdoptionFriction 2 (mature pure-Rust crate, drop-in)
= 60 / 6 = 10.0 → Tier S.

## Cross-references

- alien-graveyard catalog §7.14.
- storage.rs:13756 (the documented hot path).
- crate::storage_cardinality_sketch (sibling module shipped today; mirrors the pattern this bead would adopt).

Substrate (storage_pane_id_set.rs) was already shipped at an earlier sibling commit; this slice adds the property-test coverage that promotes the unit tests to randomized invariants. Verification: cargo test --test proptest_storage_pane_id_set --no-default-features — 13 passed in 0.04s (64 cases each). The substrate is now ready for that work without further changes.

title: Recording FrameWriter can emit corrupt WAR frames with mismatched payload_len
description:
Subsystem: recording/replay WAR frame producer

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:54-64` exposes `FrameHeader.payload_len` and `RecordingFrame.payload` as public fields, so callers can construct a frame whose declared length differs from the actual payload bytes.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:66-77` encodes `header.payload_len` into the stream and then appends all bytes from `payload`, with no equality check.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:119-126` accepts arbitrary `RecordingFrame` values in `FrameWriter::write_frame`; `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:139-143` and `:222-230` flush them via `frame.encode()` unchanged.
- The reader trusts the declared length when advancing offsets (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/replay.rs:46-80`), so a short declared length leaves extra payload bytes to be interpreted as a subsequent frame header, and a long declared length makes the stream look truncated.
- Existing proptest generation only creates well-formed frames with `payload_len = payload.len()` (`crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_recording.rs:207-221`), so the producer-side invariant is not tested.

Why it matters:
Normal `Recorder::record_output` and `record_event` build sane frames, but `FrameWriter` is a public producer API. A bad or future caller can create recordings that the replay path rejects or misparses, turning a local invariant violation into corrupted forensic artifacts.

Proposed remediation:
Make malformed frames unrepresentable or rejected at the write boundary: add a checked `RecordingFrame::new`, make fields private where feasible, and have `RecordingFrame::encode`/`FrameWriter::write_frame` return an error when `header.payload_len != payload.len()`. Add property tests that generate mismatched lengths and assert producer-side rejection before any bytes hit disk.
notes: Producer-side guard at FrameWriter::write_frame rejects RecordingFrame with mismatched header.payload_len vs payload.len(). Added: RecordingFrame::new(timestamp_ms, frame_type, flags, payload) -> Result<Self> as the safe constructor that derives payload_len from the bytes; pub(crate) RecordingFrame::check_payload_len_matches() guard called from write_frame; 4 unit tests (recording_frame_new_derives_payload_len_from_payload, write_frame_rejects_short_declared_payload_len, write_frame_rejects_long_declared_payload_len, write_frame_accepts_consistent_zero_length_payload); 1 proptest recording_frame_new_keeps_header_payload_len_in_sync (200 cases) pinning the constructor invariant. Error message embeds br-ft-l88j0 + both lengths for forensics. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: DistributedHttpClient response-read path does not observe mid-flight cx-cancel
description:
# DistributedHttpClient mid-flight cx-cancel gap

## Background
Discovered during ft-xbnl0.2.4 tick 380 verification work. When a caller fires
`cx.cancel_with(...)` WHILE a `DistributedHttpClient::get` is in flight (blocked
reading response bytes from a stalled server), the cancel does NOT propagate to
the HTTP client's read loop.

## Reproduction
The ft-xbnl0.2.4 test
`distributed::tests::distributed_http_client_mid_flight_cancel_does_not_hang`
exercises this. Observed behavior:

    elapsed = 10.02s
    result = Err("deadline has elapsed at Time(10000000041ns)")

The elapsed = ~10s matches the test's DEFENSIVE outer timeout ceiling
(`crate::runtime_compat::timeout(10s, client.get(...))`), not the 50 ms
cx-cancel fire. The cancel went through (cx.is_cancel_requested() would return
true) but the HTTP client's await points didn't observe it.

## Relation to other findings
- **Tick 328** documented that `timeout_with_cx` observes cx *budget deadline*
  but not direct cx *cancel*. This is the same shape of gap at a different
  layer — the HTTP client wraps asupersync::http::h1 whose await points
  don't poll cx.
- **ft-kfkyi** (closed tick 351) was a distinct concern (3xx redirect
  exfil). This finding is lower-severity: not a security issue, just an
  operational-ergonomics gap.

## Impact
- Hung distributed RPC calls will eventually time out via internal limits
  (if any configured) but won't observe operator-initiated cancel.
- Agent workflows that fire cx.cancel to abort a slow peer call will wait
  the full internal-timeout window before the call returns.

## Fix approach (candidate paths)
1. Extend `DistributedHttpClient::get/post` to race the inner future against
   a cx-cancel future (tokio::select! or similar race).
2. Patch asupersync::http::h1 to thread cx through its await points and
   honor cancel at read/write boundaries. Bigger scope; upstream change.
3. Wrap the DistributedHttpClient inner calls in `timeout_with_cx` —
   but per tick 328, that only observes budget, not cancel. So this
   doesn't help unless the caller sets a short budget.

Option (1) is the narrowest change; aligns with the cx-first migration
pattern and doesn't require upstream asupersync work.

## Verification
The existing tick-380 snapshot test is the flip trigger. When the fix lands:
1. Observed elapsed drops from ~10s to << 10s (cx-cancel observed mid-read).
2. `result` shape changes from the outer-timeout Err to the HTTP client's
   own cancel-shaped Err.
3. Update the snapshot assertions to require the faster behavior.

## References
- Finding: ft-xbnl0.2.4 tick 380 (commit 4d925607)
- Related: `docs/ft-xbnl0-2-4-completion-evidence.md §5` out-of-scope carve-out
  for primitive-doc-only coverage (timeout_with_cx / sleep_with_cx — ticks
  328 / 331).
close_reason: Fixed by tick 387 (commit 99640e41): DistributedHttpClient::{get,post} now race inner call against cx-cancel watcher (50ms poll). Mid-flight cancel surfaces as Ok(Err(Cancelled)) in ~70ms. Tick-380 snapshot test tightened to assert the new fast-cancel behavior (elapsed < 1s, exact Cancelled variant).

title: events.rs: subscriber_lag_events counter is fanout-weighted, not unique-event count — naming and docstring misleading
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs`:
- struct field doc (line 695): `Total lag events (slow consumer missed messages)`
- bumped at recv_cx Lagged arm (line 1284-1286): `fetch_add(n)` per Lagged event per subscriber.
- bumped at try_recv Lagged arm (line 1314-1316): same.
- bumped at send_routed broadcast_send Err arm (line 1156-1158): fixed +1 (different semantic).

## Defect
The counter is incremented by `n` (the missed_count from each subscriber's Lagged error) every time ANY subscriber observes lag. With N subscribers all lagging on the same M events, the counter shows `N×M`, not `M`.

The struct doc-comment calls it "Total lag events (slow consumer missed messages)". This conflates two quantities:
- **Lag events**: distinct messages that lagged out of the channel.
- **Subscriber-missed messages**: the fanout-weighted sum.

Operators reading the metric assuming "how many events did I lose?" get a wildly inflated answer when N > 1.

Compounding: `send_routed` Err arm bumps by +1 (line 1158), but the comment says "all lagging" — tokio broadcast_send only fails on zero receivers, not on lagging. So this bump fires on a different condition than the recv-side bumps. Mixing two semantics into one counter.

## Fix shape
Rename or split:

### Option A — rename + clarify
Rename to `subscriber_lag_messages` and document it as fanout-weighted. Add a separate `distinct_events_lagged` derived from per-channel lag-tracker state.

### Option B — add a per-channel "events_lagged" counter
Add three new counters (one per subscribable channel):
- `delta_events_lagged: AtomicU64`
- `detection_events_lagged: AtomicU64`
- `signal_events_lagged: AtomicU64`

Bump each by 1 per `record_send` call where queued_len exceeds capacity (or some threshold).

### Option C — leave runtime, fix docs
Keep the counter as-is. Update the docstring to clearly state it's fanout-weighted and explain the relationship to per-subscriber Lagged events.

## Tests
- 1 publisher, 1 subscriber, 1 lag event with missed_count=5 → counter == 5 (matches today's behavior).
- 1 publisher, 3 subscribers all lagging on same 5 events → with current code counter == 15. Document this is fanout-weighted.
- send_routed Err arm: distinct semantic — separate test or merge into a single counter with explicit rules.

## Class
P3 OBS / docs. Operationally similar to ft-2z16v (events_dropped_dedup invariant doc-correctness).
close_reason:
Fixed at a0e7eb25a (commit message reads 'fix(events): close forensic invariant — events_delivered counts events not fanout (br-ft-2z16v)' but the diff also contains the ft-lb5x7 docstring rewrite — known concurrent-edit commit-message-vs-content mismatch pattern, ft-4dhsm tracks the broader class).

## What landed (Option C — leave runtime, fix docs)

Three documentation surfaces now pin the three-source semantics of EventBusMetrics::subscriber_lag_events:

1. **Runtime field doc** at events.rs:717 — replaces the misleading 'Total lag events' lead with 'Fanout-weighted subscriber-missed-message + send-failure counter' and enumerates all three bump sources (recv_cx Lagged + missed_count, try_recv Lagged + missed_count, send_routed Err + 1) with their exact fetch_add shapes. Operator-facing meaning paragraph + semi-formal forensic invariant.

2. **MetricsSnapshot field doc** at events.rs:869 — mirrors the three-source enumeration with a pointer to the runtime field for the full contract.

3. **Inline comments at all three bump sites** (events.rs:1256 send-side #3, ~1391 recv_cx Lagged #1, ~1424 try_recv Lagged #2) — annotates each fetch_add call with its source number and fanout-weighted contribution shape so future refactors that drop or merge a bump can't slip past review.

## Why Option C (not A or B)

The bead's three options were:
- A: rename to subscriber_lag_messages + add a separate distinct_events_lagged counter

title: [idea-wizard][demo-lab] Replayable bundled swarm demo/scenario proof pack
description:
## Idea-wizard result

Phase 1 research found a concrete product/testing gap that is not covered by the existing capacity autopilot (`ft-b94bx`), flight recorder (`ft-ogr3n`), fleet/profile mutation (`ft-02m3k`), renderer-SLO (`ft-tf6g3.3`), or attestation-closure (`ft-e87u6`) graphs: `ft demo` advertises `quickstart`, `usage_limit`, and `compaction`, but the command currently reports that demo scenario files are not bundled and points users at custom `ft simulate run <file.yaml>` input.

The selected idea is a replayable bundled scenario lab: turn the advertised demos into deterministic, redacted, versioned scenario assets that double as no-mock regression/proof fixtures for swarm onboarding, product demos, and release evidence.

## Ideas considered before selection

The phase-2 pool included scenario demos, live swarm heatmaps, cross-pane deadlock prediction, proof-log compaction, RCH worker health modeling, policy explainability, replayable chaos labs, semantic pane clustering, operator trust dashboards, snapshot migration tests, rate-limit early warning, action receipt auditors, profile libraries, secure transcript sharing, multi-host trace stitching, automatic README claim validators, stuck-agent triage macros, GPU/renderer visual diff packs, terminal conformance bundles, and target-class capacity drills.

The top five after overlap review were:
- Replayable bundled swarm scenario lab.
- Policy explainability notebooks for approvals/denials.
- Action receipt auditor for robot/MCP mutation claims.
- Stuck-agent triage macro packs.
- Multi-host trace stitching preflight.

This epic chooses the scenario lab because the code has an explicit missing-bundle path today, it improves first-run usability, and it creates reusable golden artifacts without colliding with active RCH/renderer work.

## Goal

Bundle deterministic scenarios for the advertised `ft demo` commands, wire the demo runner to execute/validate them through existing `ft simulate`/robot surfaces, retain structured JSON/TOON/golden artifacts, and make every outward-facing demo claim proveable through RCH-only heavy checks.

## Non-goals

- Do not create a marketing-only demo that bypasses real `ft` surfaces.
- Do not depend on Agent Mail availability, remote service repair, destructive git cleanup, or local heavy Cargo proof.
- Do not send input to live panes except in an explicit approval-gated live-demo follow-up.
- Do not claim production 200+ pane safety from demo fixtures; target-class capacity claims remain under the existing capacity/proof beads.

## Acceptance

- Child beads define the scenario schema/manifest, bundle the advertised scenarios, wire `ft demo` to real assets, ship a no-mock golden proof harness, update operator docs truthfully, and add a convergence artifact.
- Every child includes unit/integration/e2e expectations with structured logs and redaction requirements.
- The graph stays cycle-free under `br dep cycles --json`.
- README/demo language only graduates after retained artifacts exist.

- Invalid, unredacted, or unbounded fixtures fail closed with typed reason codes.
- The manifest contract states that demo fixtures are not evidence for target-class 200+ pane production capacity.

title: Define resource-pressure chaos verdict schema and coverage matrix
description:
Foundation bead for `ft-lmg3g` resource-pressure chaos suite. Before individual chaos scenarios are implemented, define the mechanical conformance contract every scenario must satisfy.

Specification source:
- Parent `ft-lmg3g` requires deterministic memory pressure, IO stalls, search daemon stalls, MCP proxy stalls, queue saturation, and clock/timer anomalies.
- Parent acceptance requires local reduced mode plus high-scale proof mode, structured logs, machine-readable verdicts, and coverage of at least one CPU, memory, IO, and external-service pressure path.
- `ft-tn6cw` truthfulness contract requires planned/simulated evidence to stay distinct from real 64-core/256GB hardware evidence.

Scope:
1. Define a stable machine-readable chaos verdict schema, likely JSON/JSONL, with scenario_id, pressure_class, mode, preconditions, injected_fault, observed_mitigation, fail_closed_decision, diagnostics, logs_path, proof_level, skip_reason, and pass/fail/skipped status.
2. Define reduced-mode and high-scale-mode semantics. Reduced mode may run locally or on small workers and can prove harness behavior; high-scale mode may only report PROVEN when hardware predicates are met and captured in the verdict.
3. Define a coverage matrix with rows for CPU/admission, memory/tiering, storage IO/search, external-service/MCP/search-daemon stalls, queue saturation, and clock/timer anomalies.
4. Define common assertion vocabulary: fail-closed, bounded queue growth, no panic, diagnostic emitted, mitigation logged, and recovery/rollback observed where applicable.
5. Provide fixtures or sample verdict records for PASS, FAIL, SKIPPED_NOT_PROVEN, and EXPECTED_BLOCKED_BY_INFRA outcomes.

Acceptance:
- Future scenario beads can reference this schema instead of inventing per-test output formats.
- Coverage accounting makes it impossible to claim the parent complete without at least CPU, memory, IO, and external-service rows passing or explicitly marked skipped with reasons.
- The schema distinguishes local/reduced proof from real high-scale proof.
- Unit tests or schema validation tests cover required fields and reject missing proof-level/skip-reason combinations.

title: [reality-gap] tui/ftui_stub.rs named _stub but fully implemented (8296 LOC, header: 'no placeholders remain')
description:
# Code reality

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui/ftui_stub.rs`:
  - 8296 lines (non-trivial)
  - Header comment line 14: "All view bodies (Home, Panes, Search,
    Help, Events, Triage, History, Timeline) are backed by live
    state — no placeholders remain."
  - `crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui/mod.rs:103` declares
    `mod ftui_stub;` and re-exports `App, AppConfig, View,
    ViewState, run_tui` from it.

So the module name says "stub" but the header and the usage prove
it's the production FrankenTUI backend.

# Why this is a reality-check gap

Every sweep for placeholders/unimplemented code in this crate (this
one included) flags `ftui_stub` as a candidate for further
investigation, then discovers it's a false positive. Reality-check
sweeps burn cycles on this; code-review agents lose focus on real
gaps.

The naming is a legacy from when the file genuinely was a stub. The
content has grown into the real backend. The file name didn't
follow.

# Recommended disposition

```bash
git mv crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui/ftui_stub.rs \
       crates/frankenterm-core/src/tui/ftui_backend.rs
```

…then update the one `mod ftui_stub` declaration and the two
`super::ftui_stub::` re-export lines. 15-second edit, preserves
git history via `git mv`.

# Risk

- `git mv` preserves blame + history.
- No external dependency on the file name (it's a sibling module).
- Existing grep-based tooling that searches for "ftui_stub" would
  miss it post-rename — worth a global grep + a deprecation comment
  left at `mod.rs` during the rename window.

# Severity

Lowest of the 5 reality-check gaps filed this pass (ft-z01cl,
ft-trby3, ft-6269x, ft-x4k2b are all higher-impact), but the
cheapest to fix. Good first-issue material.
close_reason: Verified in a68246b7 (fix(tui): wire ftui_backend module rename follow-through) + 8c8f505b which completed the git mv ftui_stub.rs → ftui_backend.rs and updated mod.rs/keymap.rs/rollout.rs references.

title: [LOW] diag bundle environment.json leaks absolute workspace cwd; tracing fields leak operator paths
description:
Found during /security-audit-for-saas pass #6 (pane 5, 2026-04-21).

## Summary
Three logging/telemetry surfaces all come out clean on the obvious
secret-leak vectors (no bearer-token / API-key / pane-content
fields in tracing calls; no /etc/ or .ssh/ reads in diag
collection). One defense-in-depth gap remains: path privacy.

## Findings

### F1 [LOW] diag bundle environment.json includes absolute cwd
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/diagnostic.rs:87-89
  ```rust
  cwd: std::env::current_dir()
      .ok()
      .map(|p| p.display().to_string()),
  ```
- Diag bundles (`ft diag bundle`) are often attached to bug reports
  and shared outside the host. An absolute cwd reveals:
  - the user's home path segment (`/Users/<username>/...` or
    `/home/<username>/...`),
  - the project path (`/Users/alice/projects/secret-startup-pitch-deck/`),
  - on some setups, mount points that hint at filesystem layout.
- Severity: LOW. Users implicitly share the workspace when
  debugging, but the current behavior removes the choice.

### F2 [LOW] tracing fields log operator-private paths
- Multiple `tracing::[info|warn|debug]!(..., path = %X.display(), ...)`
  call sites scatter socket paths, DB paths, and workspace paths
  through structured logs. Representative hits (non-exhaustive):
    - crates/frankenterm-core/src/native_events.rs:258, 302, 331,
      362, 401 — unix socket paths.
    - crates/frankenterm-core/src/telemetry.rs:1118 —
      `info_span!("telemetry_store_open", path = %db_path.display())`.
    - crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime.rs:1375, 2658, 2814 —
      socket paths on accept failures.
    - crates/frankenterm-core/src/build_coord.rs:265 —
      `meta_path = %self.meta_path.display()`.
- Severity: LOW. These logs land in the user's local log file,
  not network-visible by default, but they do end up in diag
  bundles when `collect_recent_log_lines` is called.

## Non-findings verified in the same pass
- Bearer tokens in structured logs: grep across
  `tracing::{info,debug,warn,error}!` call sites for
  `token|bearer|secret|password|api_key` returned zero production
  hits. Clean.
- Pane content in tracing fields: no production code logs
  `segment.content`, `delta_text`, or `pane_text`. Only test
  `assert_eq!(segment.content, ...)` references found. Clean.
- Diag bundle reading privileged files: no `/etc/`, `.ssh/`,
  `.aws/`, `.gnupg/` reads in `diagnostic.rs`. The bundle only
  reads the ft SQLite DB (already redacted via `redact_events`)
  and writes to the workspace-local `diag_dir`. Clean.
- Environment variables in diag bundle: `gather_environment`
  captures only OS / arch / rust_version / wa_version / cwd —
  no `std::env::vars()` dump. Clean.
- Summarize_config: the docstring already calls out "no paths or
  secrets" and the implementation confirms — only numeric/boolean
  config values are copied over. Clean.

## Fix direction
- F1: replace absolute cwd with just the basename, or gate
  inclusion behind `DiagnosticOptions.include_cwd: bool` default
  `false`. Concretely at diagnostic.rs:87:
  ```rust
  cwd: if opts.include_cwd {
      std::env::current_dir().ok().map(|p| p.display().to_string())
  } else {
      std::env::current_dir()
          .ok()
          .and_then(|p| p.file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned()))
  },
  ```
- F2: when a log line is included in a diag bundle via
  `collect_recent_log_lines` (or equivalent), run it through the
  existing `Redactor` path-aware rules. Non-bundle in-process logs
  stay as-is since they aid operator debugging on the local box.

## Severity rationale
- LOW (P2): neither finding reveals a secret, and both sit behind
  an operator action (`ft diag bundle` + sharing it). The fix
  shrinks the unintentional-share footprint but doesn't close a
  live exploit.

## Related
- ft-ybtyg (598a7c13) — snapshot/checkpoint hashing honesty.
- ft-2guux (doc reality-check) — complementary; this bead is the
  diagnostics-exfil counterpart.

Filed per /security-audit-for-saas pass #6.
close_reason: Closed by e790f481. F1 (cwd leak) fixed: DiagnosticOptions gains include_full_cwd:bool (default false). gather_environment now routes through new scrub_path_to_basename helper which returns only the final path component; opt-in via include_full_cwd:true restores absolute path for legitimate mount-point/multi-host repro cases. Both production entry points (generate_bundle + generate_bundle_with_cx) forward opts. 8 regression tests cover basename-only default, root/empty fallback to <scrubbed> sentinel, relative paths, opt-in restore, and the strongest guarantee: default environment.json output cannot contain /Users/ or /home/ segments. F2 (tracing field path-leak via collect_recent_log_lines) deferred as follow-up — requires routing log-line bundling through the existing Redactor infrastructure, out of scope for the 25-min cap but documented inline in the commit body for the next pass.

title: Extend proof-ledger records with worker and mirror evidence
description:
## What

Extend the repository proof-ledger contract so remote proof entries can carry worker-specific evidence: worker id, scheduler mode, queue/preflight verdict, repo snapshot, source-mirror attestation result, selected target dir, whether Cargo/rustc was reached, and residual confidence when worker selection was indirect.

## Why

The proof ledger should make closeout claims auditable without prose-only reconstruction. For worker-specific incidents, a ledger entry that says remote pass is not enough unless it also says which worker ran, what source snapshot it saw, and whether the command proved the suspected failure mode.

## How

Build on ft-uz1bl schema/validator work and ft-3yptk representative harness migration. Add fields conservatively so existing proof entries remain classifiable as weaker or legacy evidence rather than silently upgraded. Include redaction rules for host paths/env and stable reason codes for unavailable worker-selection data.

## Risks

This can overlap active proof-ledger files. Do not start until the relevant proof-ledger implementation slice is safe to edit, and avoid mixing schema evolution with unrelated warning cleanup.

## Success criteria

- Proof-ledger schema and validator can represent direct target-worker proof, scheduler-selected proof, mirror-attested proof, mirror-failed proof, local fallback rejection, and inconclusive worker self-test.
- Existing ledger fixtures either migrate or receive explicit legacy/unknown fields with truthful residual risk.
- Negative fixtures fail when worker id or source snapshot is required but absent.
- Docs explain confidence levels for direct vs indirect worker proof.
- RCH-backed validation covers schema self-test and at least one representative migrated harness when Cargo is involved.
close_reason: Implemented in b6f175a47. Proof-ledger schema/validator now carries worker_evidence_confidence, selected/intended worker ids, queue state, repo snapshot, source mirror status/reason, and remote Cargo/rustc/test reachability. The validator enforces target_worker_remote_proof and scheduler_selected_remote_proof requirements, accepts mirror-failed static attestation as diagnostic residual-risk evidence, and keeps fallback/timeout/inconclusive records out of clean proof. Shared RCH guard emission and the E2E fixtures were migrated. Proof passed: bash -n; shellcheck -x; jq empty docs/asupersync-rch-evidence-schema.json; validator --self-test; tests/e2e/test_asupersync_rch_execution_policy.sh.

title: Document worker-specific RCH incident closeout workflow
description:
## What

Document the final closeout workflow for worker-specific RCH incidents after the attestation, preflight, proof-ledger fields, and negative fixtures exist.

## Why

Future agents need a self-contained path from observed worker-specific failure to bead update, proof artifact, residual-risk language, and closeout decision. Without a closeout workflow, the new evidence fields can still be misread or cited inconsistently.

## How

Update the proof-ledger and verification-contract docs that own proof terminology. Include examples for reopening a worker blocker, closing a mirror blocker, recording an inconclusive self-test, and citing a scheduler-selected proof with weaker confidence. Tie the examples back to `bv --robot-triage`/`br` workflow and RCH-only heavy verification.

## Risks

Do not duplicate large runbooks in multiple docs. Prefer one canonical workflow plus short links from adjacent docs.

## Success criteria

- A fresh agent can close or reopen a worker-specific RCH bead using only the docs and emitted artifacts.
- The workflow names exact evidence required for close, block, reopen, defer, and residual-risk outcomes.
- Docs explicitly reject local heavy Cargo, service restart/repair, and RCH sync chatter as sufficient proof.
- Examples include realistic JSON/TOON or JSONL snippets but no secrets or host-sensitive paths.
- Validation includes docs static checks and, if proof-ledger fixtures are touched, the ledger validator through the appropriate RCH-backed gate.

title: [Audit] storage.rs workflow_executions row reader silently drops 3 serde failures per row
description:
Phase 3 audit found three silent serde drops on every workflow_executions row read.

Sites: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15308, 15313, 15318

```rust
let wait_condition_str: Option<String> = row.get(6)?;
let wait_condition = wait_condition_str
    .as_ref()
    .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(s).ok());

let context_str: Option<String> = row.get(7)?;
let context = context_str
    .as_ref()
    .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(s).ok());

let result_str: Option<String> = row.get(8)?;
let result = result_str
    .as_ref()
    .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(s).ok());
```

When a workflow_executions row has a malformed wait_condition / context / result column (schema drift between writers and readers), the row is constructed with that field set to None — indistinguishable from "the column was actually NULL". Workflow consumers reading these rows lose the WHY of the workflow's wait/context/result with no diagnostic.

Why it matters: workflow_executions rows feed mission planner, replay, and audit consumers. A schema-skewed row silently corrupts ALL THREE consumer paths because the consumer can't tell missing-data from bad-data. Audit-fidelity defect.

Note: ft-zhnaw shipped a parse-drop counter for the in-memory WorkflowDecision::parse path. This site is the storage-layer counterpart — different path, different operator response (DB schema migration vs runtime consumer schema fix).

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-k6uwb, ft-zhnaw, ft-94cdu, ft-0n4nx, ft-crpvd.

Remediation:
1. Add WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ROW_PARSE_DROP_COUNT AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset.
2. Refactor the 3 sites into a shared helper parse_workflow_execution_column(value, column_name) that bumps + emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.storage.workflow with column tag ("wait_condition" | "context" | "result").
3. NULL column is NOT a drop (legitimate absence); only column-present-but-fails-to-parse bumps.
4. Tests: each column tag bumps the counter; null column does not.
notes: Replaced 3 .ok() drops in workflow_executions row reader with shared parse_workflow_execution_column<T>(value, column) helper. New WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_ROW_PARSE_DROP_COUNT counter + pub fn workflow_execution_row_parse_drop_count() observability surface + cfg(test) reset helper. Helper returns Some(parsed) on Ok, bumps counter and emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.storage.workflow carrying column tag ("wait_condition" | "context" | "result") + error %display + br-ft-lqj5g breadcrumb on Err, returns None so scalar contract stays the same. NULL column is intentionally NOT counted (legitimate absence). The workflow_executions row reader appears in 2 places (get_workflow + a sibling list reader); both now route through the helper via the replace_all edit. Added 3 tests in inline workflow_execution_row_parse_drop_tests mod: null_column_does_not_bump (legitimate absence sanity), well_formed_column_does_not_bump (happy path), malformed_column_bumps_counter (bumps twice across two distinct columns -> count=2). Same observability defect family as ft-zhnaw (the in-memory WorkflowDecision::parse counterpart), ft-yygus, ft-k6uwb, ft-94cdu, ft-bn6qi, ft-crpvd, ft-0n4nx. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: native_events: decode errors logged at debug, invisible in production
description:
# [MEDIUM] native_events: malformed wire events logged at debug

**Subsystem:** native_events / protocol_recovery
**File:** crates/frankenterm-core/src/native_events.rs (`handle_connection_with_cx`)

## The hole

When wire-event decoding fails (invalid JSON, bad base64, unknown event
type), the handler emitted:

\`\`\`rust
Err(err) => {
    debug!(error = %err, "failed to decode native event (cx path)");
}
\`\`\`

A malformed wire event is a protocol anomaly — version skew between
frankenterm and the mux-server, on-wire corruption, or a hostile peer
writing into the native-events socket. Operators routinely filter
`debug!` in production, so the signal was effectively lost.

Contrast with the `MAX_EVENT_LINE_BYTES` path a few lines above, which
already emits at `warn!`. Same class of anomaly, inconsistent level.

## Fix

Promoted the decode-error log to `warn!`. The `warn!` import was already
present — no dependency change.

Future work (separate bead): attach a telemetry counter for
decode-failure rate so it can drive a SLI rather than relying solely on
log sampling.
close_reason: done

title: [SEC] mcp_helpers audit-write paths swallow failures via tracing::warn only — no observable failure counter
description:
[SEC] mcp_helpers audit-write paths swallow failures via tracing::warn only — no observable failure counter

## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_helpers.rs` exposes three MCP
audit-recording entry points:
- `record_mcp_audit_with_cx` (line 505)
- `record_mcp_audit` (line 531)
- `record_mcp_audit_sync` (line 580)

The functions are documented as fire-and-forget: "failures are
logged but never propagated to the caller". Currently four
distinct failure sites swallow the error with only a
`tracing::warn!`:

1. `record_mcp_audit:568` — storage write error.
2. `record_mcp_audit_sync:602` — asupersync runtime build error.
3. `record_mcp_audit_sync:638` — storage open after 10s retry
   exhaustion.
4. `record_mcp_audit_sync:650` — OS thread spawn error.

`tracing::warn` is appropriate for live diagnostics but is NOT
sufficient for cumulative audit-completeness verification. An
operator running a forensic verification — "did every MCP tool
call this quarter produce an audit row?" — has no way to
quantify how many writes failed. The audit table's row count
≠ tool-call count under any non-zero failure-count regime.

This is the same shape as ft-nucbz (silent state loss on the
audit path without observability). For ft-nucbz the fix was
the AuditChain `first_retained_sequence` watermark; for this
finding the equivalent is a process-wide failure counter.

## Severity

P2. Same as ft-nucbz — defends an operator-visible
audit-completeness assertion, not a Deny-bypass. Without the
counter, there is NO upper bound an operator can put on
audit incompleteness from log scraping alone.

## Repro

```rust
use frankenterm_core::mcp_helpers::mcp_audit_failure_count;
let before = mcp_audit_failure_count();
// trigger a tool call against a closed StorageHandle (forced
// write failure)
let after = mcp_audit_failure_count();
assert!(after > before); // FAILS today — counter doesn't exist
```

## Fix

Add a process-wide `static MCP_AUDIT_FAILURE_COUNT: AtomicU64`
in mcp_helpers. Increment at all four silent-failure sites
listed above. Expose `pub(super) fn mcp_audit_failure_count()
-> u64`. Tests cover storage-error increment.

## Acceptance

- Counter starts at 0 on process load.
- Increments by 1 on storage write failure in record_mcp_audit.
- Increments by 1 on each of the three sync-path silent failure
  sites.
- Accessor returns the cumulative count.
- Test verifies storage-error increments the counter (sync-path
  failures cover by inspection).

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_helpers.rs:531-655 (audit-write
  family)
- ft-nucbz (sibling — AuditChain tamper-evidence watermark)
close_reason: Shipped at 194087f8b. mcp.rs's record_mcp_audit + record_mcp_audit_sync now bump a process-wide AtomicU64 failure counter at all 4 silent-failure sites (storage write, runtime build, storage-open retry exhaustion, OS thread spawn). Public accessor mcp_audit_failure_count() exposes the cumulative count for forensic verification: audit_table.row_count + mcp_audit_failure_count() == cumulative_mcp_tool_calls should hold. 4 tests pass including the storage-shutdown acceptance test that proves the counter bumps on a real write failure. Discovered during the fix that crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_helpers.rs is orphaned (no mod declaration) — flagged in commit message for separate bead.

title: Implement safe telemetry-driven auto-tuning with rollback
description:

title: [security] dcg failure output can leak command secrets into policy denial audit
description:
Scope: policy.rs gate decisions and policy_denied_audit persistence.

Finding: run_dcg sends the full command text to the external dcg process, copies failing dcg stderr/stdout into DcgError, then Required mode embeds that detail in the policy decision reason. policy_denied_audit stores reason without re-redaction.

Evidence: crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:2883-2887 forwards command text to dcg; crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:2913-2924 copies dcg stdout/stderr into the error detail; crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:2848-2858 embeds the detail in CommandGateOutcome.reason; crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:13573-13597 stores PolicyDeniedAuditRecord.reason without redaction.

Repro: place a fake dcg earlier in PATH containing `#!/bin/sh; cat >&2; exit 1`, configure safety.command_gate.enabled=true and dcg_mode=required, then run a gated robot/MCP send with command text `echo sk-ant-api03-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`. The denial reason contains the JSON payload with the raw command, and the same reason is returned/persisted in denial/audit paths.

Impact: any failing/noisy dcg helper can leak command secrets into policy errors, tracing, and policy_denied_audit.

Fix: never include raw dcg stdout/stderr in policy reasons; redact dcg details before returning/logging/persisting, and add a regression with a failing dcg runner that echoes the input command.
close_reason: Redacted dcg failure details before command gate approval reasons and added regression coverage

title: mcp_client.rs: map_mcp_error collapses 7 distinct FrameworkMcpErrorCode variants into ERR_PROTOCOL with no hint — operators cannot distinguish ResourceNotFound from ParseError from Custom remote codes
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_client.rs:395-438` — `map_mcp_error` translates `FrameworkMcpError` to `McpClientError` via an exhaustive match on `FrameworkMcpErrorCode`.

## Defect
Six explicit framework variants + the open `Custom(_)` catch-all all fall through to `ERR_PROTOCOL` (`mcp_client.protocol`) with NO hint:

```rust
FrameworkMcpErrorCode::ParseError
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::InvalidRequest
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::InternalError
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::ResourceNotFound
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::ResourceForbidden
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::PromptNotFound
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::Custom(_) => McpClientError::new(ERR_PROTOCOL, base),
```

Operators surveying `mcp_client.protocol` errors cannot distinguish:

- **ResourceNotFound** (operator should verify the resource URI exists on the remote server)
- **ResourceForbidden** (operator should check authorization scope)
- **PromptNotFound** (operator should verify prompt name on remote)
- **ParseError** (remote returned malformed JSON-RPC; version skew likely)
- **InvalidRequest** (request shape rejected — protocol contract drift)
- **InternalError** (uncatched, after timeout/spawn-failure detection runs first)
- **Custom(code)** (server-defined code; the inner code is silently DISCARDED)

All 7 land in the same bucket with the same generic code and no hint. The 4 framework variants in pre-fix lines 411-416 (MethodNotFound, InvalidParams, ToolExecutionError, RequestCancelled) DO get distinct codes + hints, plus the message-pattern fallthroughs for InternalError+"timed out" → ERR_TIMEOUT and InternalError+"failed to spawn" → ERR_SPAWN. The catch-all is the gap.

## Production exposure
`map_mcp_error` is the sole bridge from fastmcp framework errors to the typed `McpClientError` surface. It feeds:
- `tracing::warn` log entries with the `code` field at list_tools / call_tool failure paths.
- `RobotResponse.error_code` when proxied through robot mode.
- Operator alerting + retry middleware classification.

Operators investigating proxy failures see `code=mcp_client.protocol` and have to dig into the remote message text — which has been redacted (br-ft-qde8p) so secrets don't leak — to figure out whether they have a missing resource, a forbidden access, or a parse-error from a misbehaving server. The classification gap defeats the typed-error contract.

## Fix shape

### Add 4 distinct codes
```rust
const ERR_PARSE: &str = "mcp_client.parse_error";
const ERR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND: &str = "mcp_client.resource_not_found";
const ERR_RESOURCE_FORBIDDEN: &str = "mcp_client.resource_forbidden";
const ERR_PROMPT_NOT_FOUND: &str = "mcp_client.prompt_not_found";
```

### Restructure match
```rust
FrameworkMcpErrorCode::ParseError =>
    McpClientError::new(ERR_PARSE, base).with_hint(
        "Remote returned malformed JSON-RPC; check protocol/version compatibility."),
FrameworkMcpErrorCode::ResourceNotFound =>
    McpClientError::new(ERR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, base).with_hint(
        "Verify the requested resource URI exists on the remote server."),
FrameworkMcpErrorCode::ResourceForbidden =>
    McpClientError::new(ERR_RESOURCE_FORBIDDEN, base).with_hint(
        "Check authorization scope; the remote server denied resource access."),
FrameworkMcpErrorCode::PromptNotFound =>
    McpClientError::new(ERR_PROMPT_NOT_FOUND, base).with_hint(
        "Verify the requested prompt name on the remote server."),
FrameworkMcpErrorCode::InvalidRequest
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::InternalError
| FrameworkMcpErrorCode::Custom(_) =>
    McpClientError::new(ERR_PROTOCOL, base).with_hint(
        "Generic protocol-layer error; inspect the redacted remote message + remote server logs."),
```

### Preserve Custom code in message
For Custom(code), include the inner code in the message so forensic correlation works:
`base = format!("server '{server}' [custom_code={code}]: {redacted_remote}")`

ERR_PROTOCOL still exists — pre-existing test at `mcp_framework.rs:364` (icon decode failure) still asserts `code == \"mcp_client.protocol\"` and goes through a different code path (`into_framework`), unaffected by this change.

## Tests
- map_mcp_error_resource_not_found / _forbidden / _prompt_not_found / _parse_error: each pins the new code + non-empty hint.
- map_mcp_error_invalid_request: still maps to ERR_PROTOCOL; pin the new hint.
- map_mcp_error_custom_preserves_code_in_message: assert the custom code appears in `message`.
- All EXISTING map_mcp_error tests (method_not_found, tool_execution, spawn_failure) keep passing — their codes are unaffected.

## Class
P3 OBS / classification correctness. Same family as ft-tzolj (robot.* hint registry) but at the internal mcp_client error boundary.
close_reason: Shipped at 5d613e8af: added 4 dedicated error codes (ERR_PARSE/RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND/RESOURCE_FORBIDDEN/PROMPT_NOT_FOUND) for distinguishable framework variants. Restructured map_mcp_error match: ParseError/ResourceNotFound/ResourceForbidden/PromptNotFound each get typed code + targeted hint; Custom(code) preserves inner code as 'custom_code=N' in message + remote-docs hint; InvalidRequest+InternalError stay under ERR_PROTOCOL (catch-all) but now carry a hint. ERR_PROTOCOL retained — pre-existing test at mcp_framework.rs:364 (icon decode via into_framework) and external dependents at frankenterm-core-mcp + proptest_mcp_client_boundary unaffected. 6 new tests pin code+hint per variant, 3 pre-existing tests untouched. cargo check --lib --features mcp-client clean (34.13s, 0 errors). Pivoted from ft-nfk94 orphan via ft-jydne audit-pivot meta-bead.

title: [ARCH/Composition-B follow-up] §0.14 BOCPD drift detection for adaptive admission controller (regime-shift reset)
description:
Composition B follow-up #2 of 3 (ft-84mht parent, closed first-slice).

This bead adds §0.14 Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection (BOCPD, Adams & MacKay 2007) on the SwarmCapacityCertificate's status time series. When a regime shift is detected — e.g., new workload class, sudden traffic spike, sustained latency increase — reset the adaptive controller to the conservative baseline for one observation window so the e-process restart sees fresh data not contaminated by the prior regime.

## Algorithm

BOCPD maintains a posterior over run-length r_t (time since last change point). The probability of a change is P(r_t = 0). A simple BOCPD with hazard rate H = 1/100 (expected segment length 100 ticks) + Gaussian observation model is sufficient for capacity-status drift.

## Integration point

A new SwarmCapacityDriftDetector type that ingests certificate snapshots over time + emits a Drift event when P(change_point) > 0.5. The SwarmCapacityAdmissionController subscribes; on Drift, it resets the controller stage to Shadow + clears the e-process accumulator.

## Acceptance

- BOCPD updates per tick on certificate snapshot stream.
- Drift event fires on synthetic regime shift within bounded ticks.
- Controller resets to Shadow + clears e-process on Drift.
- False-positive rate < 5% on a stable-regime synthetic test.

## Cross-references

- ft-84mht (parent, closed first slice).
- alien-graveyard catalog §0.14.
