title: mcp.rs: redact_mcp_args loses shape info for non-Object args — audit summary cannot distinguish null/array/scalar tool calls
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs:705-715`:

```rust
fn redact_mcp_args(tool_name: &str, args: &serde_json::Value) -> String {
    let keys = args
        .as_object()
        .map(|m| m.keys().map(|k| k.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(","))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    if keys.is_empty() {
        format!("mcp:{tool_name}")
    } else {
        format!("mcp:{tool_name} keys=[{keys}]")
    }
}
```

## Defect
The function only enumerates KEYS when args is an Object. For any other JSON shape — `Null`, `Array`, `String`, `Number`, `Bool`, or `Object{}` — the summary degrades to bare `mcp:{tool_name}` with no shape indicator. Audit observers cannot distinguish:

- `tool_name(null)` (call with explicit null arg)
- `tool_name([1,2,3])` (array of length 3)
- `tool_name("raw_string")` (scalar)
- `tool_name({})` (empty object)
- `tool_name(<missing>)` (no args at all)

All five collapse to `mcp:tool_name` in the audit row. Forensic answers like "how many calls had null args this quarter?" are unanswerable from the audit log alone.

## Fix shape
Match all six `Value` variants and emit a shape-aware suffix that preserves the no-values-logged contract:

```rust
match args {
    Value::Object(m) if !m.is_empty() =>
        format!("mcp:{} keys=[{}]", tool_name, m.keys().map(|k| k.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",")),
    Value::Object(_) => format!("mcp:{} args=empty_object", tool_name),
    Value::Array(a)  => format!("mcp:{} args=array(len={})", tool_name, a.len()),
    Value::Null      => format!("mcp:{} args=null", tool_name),
    Value::String(_) => format!("mcp:{} args=string", tool_name),
    Value::Number(_) => format!("mcp:{} args=number", tool_name),
    Value::Bool(_)   => format!("mcp:{} args=bool", tool_name),
}
```

Array length is non-PII shape info (matches the spirit of "keys list, no values"). Scalar variants log only the type, never the contents.

## Tests
- Object with keys → `mcp:foo keys=[a,b]`
- Empty object → `mcp:foo args=empty_object`
- Null → `mcp:foo args=null`
- Array len 3 → `mcp:foo args=array(len=3)`
- String → `mcp:foo args=string`
- Number → `mcp:foo args=number`
- Bool → `mcp:foo args=bool`

## Class
P3 OBS hygiene. No data loss (audit row still recorded), but observability of call shape was lost.
close_reason: Shipped at 52e76f9e5: redact_mcp_args now matches all six serde_json::Value variants and emits a shape-suffixed summary (Object/Array/Null/String/Number/Bool) preserving the no-values-logged contract. Five formerly-collapsed call shapes are now distinct in the audit log. 8 tests total (2 updated existing, 6 new) including explicit no-leak assertions for string and numeric values. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (1m00s, 0 errors).

title: [PHASE3/policy_diagnostics] Connector governor health check ignores throttle-only incidents
description:
## Finding

`policy_diagnostics::check_connector_governor` only degrades health when rejections are nonzero:

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy_diagnostics.rs:368-390` — warn branch is `if snap.telemetry.rejections > 0`, with evidence including throttles.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy_diagnostics.rs:391-400` — otherwise the check returns `pass`, even if `snap.telemetry.throttles` is high.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_governor.rs:1011-1020`, `1035-1044`, `1046-1077` — queue pressure, adaptive backoff, global rate, and per-connector rate all produce `GovernorVerdict::Throttle` without incrementing rejections.

Concrete failure path: a connector storm can result in every action being throttled by queue pressure/adaptive backoff/rate limit, but if nothing reaches hard rejection, runtime health still reports `PASS`. The evidence string in the warn branch already knows about throttles, but the branch predicate ignores them.

## Alien-graveyard match

Matches the graveyard/FrankenSuite observability-first and evidence-ledger rules for runtime controllers: adaptive/admission decisions must expose why actions were taken, and operability gaps should be fixed before clever controller tuning. This is not an algorithmic rewrite; it is a health-contract gap.

## Impact

P3: no direct data loss, but an operator health surface can rubber-stamp a degraded connector system as healthy during throttle-only incidents. That undermines the controller evidence ledger and makes rate-limit/backoff storms harder to diagnose.

## Proposed remediation

1. Change the health predicate to warn on `rejections > 0 || throttles > 0`, or use severity tiers: throttle-only = warn/degraded, rejection = warn/critical depending on count/rate.
2. Include top reason counters if available, or add lightweight reason counters to `GovernorTelemetry` as a follow-up.
3. Add tests in `proptest_policy_diagnostics.rs` or connector-governor diagnostics coverage:
   - throttle-only governor snapshot returns non-pass status.
   - rejection path remains warning with rejection evidence.
   - zero-evaluation or all-allow snapshots still pass.

## Acceptance

- A throttle-only connector governor incident no longer reports pass.
- Health evidence includes evaluations/allows/throttles/rejections and global rate fill.
- Existing no-incident pass behavior remains unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in e12ae9cb2: policy.connector_governor health now warns on throttle-only incidents as well as rejections, with evidence preserving evaluations/allows/throttles/rejections and global rate fill. Added proptest coverage that drives a real connector governor into throttle-only telemetry and asserts WARN plus throttle/rejection evidence. title: Tantivy SearchFilter range filters silently match nothing on misordered min > max
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs found that the four range filter variants accept misordered bounds and silently match no documents.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs:187-208 defines four range filters: TimeRange{min_ms, max_ms}, RecordedTimeRange{min_ms, max_ms}, SequenceRange{min_seq, max_seq}, LogOffsetRange{min_offset, max_offset}, each with independent Option<T> bounds.
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs:244-298 implements matches() for each by checking each bound independently with < / > comparisons. No invariant ties min <= max.
- A filter like TimeRange{min_ms: Some(2000), max_ms: Some(1000)} produces a predicate that requires occurred_at_ms >= 2000 AND occurred_at_ms <= 1000, which no document satisfies.
- crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_query.rs:119 SearchQuery::validate validates pagination/snippet/boosts but does not iterate filters or call any per-filter validate.
- impl SearchFilter at line 224 has matches() but no validate() method.

Why it matters: a misordered range filter is a silent zero-result query. Operators chasing a forensic incident or running golden-query tests get an empty page that looks like 'no documents matched' rather than 'your filter is malformed'. Pre-fix this also prevents debugging tools from surfacing the configuration error.

Proposed remediation: add SearchFilter::validate that rejects misordered bounds for all four range variants (min > max). Wire the call into SearchQuery::validate so callers see the error before backend dispatch. Add unit tests for each variant with min > max producing a structured InvalidQuery error.
notes: Added SearchFilter::validate() that rejects misordered min > max bounds for all 4 range variants (TimeRange, RecordedTimeRange, SequenceRange, LogOffsetRange). Wired into SearchQuery::validate so the InvalidQuery error fires at config time rather than at silent zero-result dispatch. Other filter variants pass through (no order invariant). Errors carry br-ft-m5bne breadcrumb + offending min and max values. Added 7 tests: time/recorded/sequence/log-offset misordered rejection, min == max accepted (single-value boundary), one-sided bounds (only min OR only max) accepted, SearchQuery::validate propagates filter errors. Crate check clean -p frankenterm-core-tantivy --no-default-features.

title: scrollback_cold_tier: PRIVACY BYPASS — ChunkMetadata.redaction pub allows skipping redactor; EvictionPolicy + ChunkId pub fields
description:
Audit of scrollback_cold_tier.rs (cold-tier eviction substrate) found 3 issues including a HIGH-severity privacy bypass:

1. (HIGH PRIVACY BYPASS, ChunkMetadata.redaction) The field is pub. The substrate's docstring CLAIMS 'redactor MUST apply before chunks land on disk. Substrate enforces at the type level.' But should_evict_to_disk only checks chunk.redaction == Required — any caller can set chunk.redaction = RedactionStatus::Applied WITHOUT running the redactor, bypassing the privacy gate. The docstring's 'type-level enforcement' claim is FALSE — it's a runtime-checkable enum field, not a type-state. Same exploitable pattern as the OSC 52 + ChunkBytes typed-state holes I fixed earlier (ft-vesy5, ft-vzk2n). Fix: pub → pub(crate) on the redaction + encryption fields; add transition methods that take a 'RedactorRan' typed witness or require a builder method that internally validates.

2. (pub-field, EvictionPolicy) disk_budget_bytes (1 GiB security cap), retention_days (privacy-relevant), min_compression_ratio, min_warm_idle_ms all pub mutable. Same recurring pattern (now in 12 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + builder API + read accessors.

3. (pub-field, ChunkMetadata + ChunkId) All ChunkMetadata fields pub including tier (state machine!), bytes_compressed (telemetry), etc. ChunkId(pub u64) allows arbitrary id construction outside the next() allocator — id-forgery / collision possible. Fix: pub → pub(crate) on ChunkMetadata fields + private inner u64 on ChunkId with constructor + accessor.

title: FTS search misses tokens split by streaming redactor retained tails
description: While proving ft-cgpz4 hybrid_search.rs on 2026-05-07, the broad test filter `cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features hybrid_search -- --nocapture` persistently failed `storage::storage_handle_tests::storage_handle_hybrid_search_blends_lexical_and_semantic` at `bundle.lexical_candidates >= 2`. Inspecting the leftover test DB showed output_segments/FTS rows split by the streaming persistence redactor tail: row 1 was `needle appears in lexical l`, row 2 was `aneneedle appears in both l`, row 3 was `anestotally different wordi`, row 4 was `ng`. Querying FTS for `needle` matched only row 1 because the token at the start of the second logical segment had been prefixed with the retained `ane` tail from the prior segment. Diagnosis: `dispatch_write_command_raw` routes every AppendSegment through `redact_segment_for_persistence`, which reuses a per-pane `StreamingRedactor`; `StreamingRedactor::redact_chunk` intentionally withholds a bounded suffix to catch cross-boundary secrets, but the withheld suffix is emitted as part of the next durable segment, so per-row FTS tokenization can miss words that cross these artificial storage boundaries. Proposed fix: design a persistence/search strategy that preserves cross-boundary redaction without corrupting per-segment FTS tokens, e.g. store/search a separate FTS-safe logical content field, flush retained tails with explicit boundary metadata, or make search index the reconstructed stream with mapping back to segment ids. This is larger than the clippy slice and should be fixed deliberately with redaction/security tests plus FTS regression coverage.
close_reason: Fixed storage persistence redaction so retained streaming tails no longer corrupt per-segment FTS tokens. Added split-secret regression coverage and restored the hybrid-search needle assertion. Proof: cargo fmt --check; git diff --check; rch remote storage::storage_handle_tests:: 41 passed on vmi1227854; rch remote cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed on vmi1227854; rch remote cargo clippy -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features -- -D warnings passed on vmi1227854.

title: TriggerCategoryCounts deserialize lacks length + sum + monotonicity invariants
description:
Reality-check audit of pattern_trigger.rs found that TriggerCategoryCounts custom Deserialize at line 274 does not validate the array-form invariants documented on the type.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs:274 implements Deserialize for TriggerCategoryCounts as an array-backed [u64; 6] indexed by TriggerCategory::as_index (per ft-6db1t).
- The deserialize impl reads the raw array but does not validate that the input length matches the const NUM_CATEGORIES, leaving deserialize behavior depending on the upstream serde shape.
- No range check on per-category counts; saturating arithmetic is used at insert time but a deserialized value that exceeds the documented monotonicity contract (e.g., one-category total > total_matches) would slip through.

Why it matters:
TriggerCategoryCounts feeds error-class telemetry; a forged deserialize value can bias trigger summaries or cross-cycle aggregation. Lower severity than the tx-ledger / replay-checkpoint cases because trigger counts are operational telemetry rather than authoritative state.

Proposed remediation:
Validate (a) array length matches NUM_CATEGORIES constant, (b) per-category count <= total_matches, (c) total_matches equals sum of per-category counts. Add proptest covering arbitrary array values asserting deserialize rejects iff invariants are violated.
close_reason: Fixed TriggerCategoryCounts/TriggerScanResult deserialize invariants in crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs: duplicate category keys now reject; TriggerScanResult deserialization rejects category counts above total_matches, count-sum overflow, and sums that do not equal total_matches while preserving sparse legacy map counts. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs; git diff --check -- crates/frankenterm-core/src/pattern_trigger.rs; rch exec -- bash -lc 'env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-web-target cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features' passed. title: intervention_console: emergency stop can be bypassed by later resume/release actions
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/intervention_console.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/intervention_console.rs:318-337 sets emergency_stop/emergency_scope and pauses panes, but it does not install a guard around later actions while the emergency remains active.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/intervention_console.rs:258-262 lets ResumePane move a Paused pane back to Active.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/intervention_console.rs:277-280 and 296-299 release ManualTakeover/Quarantined panes back to Active without checking emergency_stop or emergency_scope.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/intervention_console.rs:49-53 defines agent_can_act as Active-only, so a resumed pane can act while the console still reports emergency_stop active.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/intervention_console.rs:800-847 tests emergency activation/release, but no test asserts that resume/release is blocked while the emergency stop is active.

Impact:
The kill switch is only a one-time state mutation, not an enforcement gate. A later resume or release action can reactivate a pane under a still-active global or pane-scoped emergency stop. This is a fail-open safety-controller bug.

Proposed remediation:
Add a pre-action emergency guard in execute(): while global emergency is active, reject or no-op state transitions that would make any pane Active; while pane-scoped emergency is active, reject Active transitions for that pane. Keep ReleaseEmergencyStop as the only action that clears the gate. Add tests for ResumePane, ReleaseTakeover, and ReleaseQuarantine under both global and pane-scoped emergency stops.
close_reason: Emergency-stop reactivation gate is present at HEAD; follow-up fixed intervention_console test imports and pane-scoped release test setup. Verified rustfmt --check and git diff --check for intervention_console; rch cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib passed with warnings. rch cargo test -p frankenterm-core intervention_console --lib is blocked by unrelated dirty test compile errors in tx_observability, storage/policy_decision_tests, and shadow_mode_evaluator, with no remaining intervention_console compile errors.

title: ft-h8s0p substrate: sanitize_alt_text misses DEL (0x7F) and C1 controls (0x80-0x9F)
description:
kitty_graphics_alt_text.rs sanitize_alt_text scrubs only C0 (0x00-0x1F) via . Misses:

- DEL (0x7F) — screen readers choke on it.
- C1 control characters (0x80-0x9F) — including CSI (0x9B), ANSI escape lead.

A malicious actor could emit alt-text with embedded DEL or C1 codes that bypass substrate's scrub and reach the screen reader / status bar. Bead's threat model includes this.

Fix: extend the scrub predicate to: . Add regression test with DEL + C1 input.

Also minor: control_chars_scrubbed and whitespace_collapsed counters use plain  (not saturating). With 256-char cap this never overflows in practice, but defensive substrate should saturate.

Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD: scrub now covers C0/DEL/C1 (0x00-0x1F + 0x7F + 0x80-0x9F). Counters use saturating_add. 2 regression tests pin DEL+C1 scrub + high-Unicode-not-scrubbed. 35 tests pass.

title: [MEDIUM] escape-parser robustness suite contains vacuous CSI MR and missing concatenation property
description:
[MEDIUM] Recent commit f3242133 (test: proptest robustness suite for escape-parser) overstates the protection added by frankenterm/escape-parser/tests/proptest_parser_robustness.rs.

Evidence:
- The file header claims property 3: `Concatenation consistency — parse(a++b) == parse(a) ++ parse(b)` (lines 9-10), but there is no corresponding test anywhere in the file. The suite advertises a metamorphic relation it never checks.
- The new `csi_roundtrip_via_display` property is partially vacuous (lines 170-184). It only asserts equality when `actions1.len() == 1` AND `actions2.len() == 1`; otherwise it silently skips the case. A regression that starts emitting zero or multiple actions for generated CSI sequences would therefore pass this property instead of failing.
- The generated inputs in `arb_csi_sequence()` are always syntactically complete CSI byte strings (lines 30-47), so a non-singleton parse result is exactly the kind of behavioral drift this MR should catch, not skip.

Why this matters:
- This commit is framed as a robustness/metamorphic suite, but two of the strongest claimed relations are currently absent or weak enough to miss structural parser regressions.
- Escape parsing is a streaming state machine; vacuous MRs give false confidence around output-shape stability.

Requested fix:
- Add the missing concatenation-consistency property or remove the claim from the suite header/commit description.
- Tighten `csi_roundtrip_via_display` so generated complete CSI inputs must roundtrip to exactly one action on both parses, and fail otherwise.
close_reason: Already fixed by db835e7b — csi_roundtrip_via_display tightened with arb_singleton_csi_sequence + hard asserts, concatenation_consistency_for_printable added

title: [HIGH] Atlas frame/disk budget partition skips over deferred head-of-line work
description:
Review finding in GUI/render atlas tiered-swap commits.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:514-516 documents DiskBudgetEstimator::partition as returning admitted prefix + deferred suffix.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:646-649 documents FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer::partition the same way.
- Implementations at crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:527-533 and :661-667 keep scanning after a Defer, so a later small item can be admitted after an earlier over-budget item is deferred.
- Existing inline tests encode this skip-ahead behavior: events/handoffs #3 deferred while #4 admitted in the same frame.

Impact:
The integration docs say deferred events are re-enqueued FIFO for the next frame. Skipping over a deferred head item breaks prefix/suffix/FIFO semantics, can reorder cold-region priority, and can repeatedly service newer small swaps while older large swaps stay deferred.

Expected:
Once an item defers, partition should stop admitting later items for that frame and return the original suffix as deferred, or the docs/tests must explicitly state non-prefix work-conserving scheduling and the carryover queue must preserve that contract.
close_reason: Fixed DiskBudgetEstimator and FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer partition to stop at first deferral and return the original deferred suffix; added prefix/suffix proptests. Verified atlas_tiered_swap_frame_budget and inline partition tests.

title: [mock-code-finder][mission] Metrics cite missing ignored mission logs
description:
## Finding

The retained mission metric JSON files cite raw `tests/e2e/logs/mission_*` logs as proof artifacts, but every cited path is absent from the checkout and the log directory is ignored by repo policy. The JSON therefore preserves pass counts and scenario summaries without retaining the raw evidence it points at.

## Evidence

- `docs/metrics/mission_chaos_evidence.json:26-30` cites five `tests/e2e/logs/mission_chaos_20260227_031811.*.stdout.log` files.
- `docs/metrics/mission_soak_chaos_evidence.json:6-7` cites `mission_soak_20260227_031416.jsonl` and `mission_chaos_20260227_031811.jsonl`; lines 71-75 cite the same missing chaos stdout logs.
- `docs/metrics/mission_tx_rollout_readiness.json:15,22,29,36` cites four `mission_tx_chaos_perf_20260227_025927.*.stdout.log` files.
- `jq -r '.. | strings | select(startswith("tests/e2e/logs/mission_"))' docs/metrics/mission_chaos_evidence.json docs/metrics/mission_tx_rollout_readiness.json docs/metrics/mission_soak_chaos_evidence.json | sort -u` finds eleven cited mission log paths.
- An existence/tracking check reports all eleven cited paths as `MISSING` and no path as tracked.
- `rg --files tests/e2e/logs | rg 'mission_(chaos|tx_chaos_perf|soak)_20260227|tx_scenario_matrix|tx_observability|resume_recovery_[ab]'` returned no matches.
- `.gitignore:52-53` ignores `*.log` and `logs/`, so `tests/e2e/logs` output is not a durable retained artifact location unless files are copied into a tracked artifact tree with hashes.
- Duplicate checks `br search "mission chaos evidence missing logs" --json` and `br search "mission_chaos logs unavailable" --json` returned `[]`.

## Scope

1. Either rerun the mission chaos, soak, and TX chaos perf harnesses through RCH and retain their raw logs/JSONL in a tracked artifact directory with hashes, worker identity, source commit, command, target dir, and exit status, then update the metrics JSON to point to those artifacts; or downgrade the metrics JSON to explicitly mark these raw logs as unavailable instead of citing missing paths.
2. Add or extend validation so every `artifact_log`, `chaos_log`, `tx_matrix_log`, `tx_observability_log`, `resume_run_*_log`, and mission `*_jsonl` path in these metric files either exists as a tracked retained artifact or is explicitly marked unavailable/external with storage details.
3. Preserve the current mission test/harness behavior; do not replace the missing proof with local Cargo runs or untracked local logs.
4. If RCH admission remains unavailable, keep this blocked on `ft-4tp7g` and record the exact no-worker evidence before attempting material proof.

## Acceptance

- All cited mission metric evidence paths resolve to tracked retained artifacts, or the JSON schema/status explicitly says the raw evidence is unavailable/external and stops presenting the missing paths as local retained proof.
- Regenerated evidence includes RCH worker identity, source commit, command, target dir, exit status, and artifact hashes.
- A static/path validation lane fails if future mission metrics cite missing local artifacts.
- `git diff --check -- docs/metrics/mission_chaos_evidence.json docs/metrics/mission_soak_chaos_evidence.json docs/metrics/mission_tx_rollout_readiness.json` passes for any doc/metric edits.
- `br dep cycles --json` remains empty.
- Any Cargo/test execution is RCH-offloaded only.

Proof: bash -n on the touched shell scripts; jq empty on mission metric JSON; scripts/validate_mission_metrics_artifacts.sh passed; targeted rg found no remaining metric artifact fields directly citing tests/e2e/logs strings; br dep cycles clean. No local Cargo/RCH material proof was needed for this truthfulness repair.

title: wa.workflow_run force flag is advertised but ignored
description: Deep audit of the MCP workflow path found a reality gap between the tool contract and execution. WorkflowRunParams includes force: bool (crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_types.rs:282-289). wa.workflow_run schema describes force as Force run (bypass handled guard) (crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:2969-2975). WaWorkflowRunTool::call deserializes params, runs policy checks, handles dry-run, finds the runner, then explicitly discards the flag with let _ = params.force (mcp_tools.rs:2992-3006, 3142). The actual call runner.run_workflow(params.pane_id, workflow, &execution_id, 0).await never receives force state (mcp_tools.rs:3155-3158). WorkflowRunner::run_workflow and run_workflow_with_cx accept pane_id, workflow, execution_id, and start_step, but no force or handled-guard override (crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:659-669, 2075-2082). Why it matters: MCP clients can set force=true believing they are bypassing a handled guard, but behavior is identical to default. Because this is a mutating operator surface, the mismatch can cause false confidence during recovery or incident workflows. Proposed remediation: either remove force from WorkflowRunParams/schema until semantics exist, or plumb it through the workflow runner/guard decision with policy/audit visibility. Add a regression showing force=true changes the handled-guard path, or that the schema no longer advertises the option.
close_reason: Landed 68401c59d. Removed ignored force from WorkflowRunParams and wa.workflow_run schema, deny unknown force inputs, and added schema/property coverage. Verified rustfmt, diff --check, and scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features. title: robot_types.rs: ErrorCode::category() and is_retryable() are stringly-typed — robot.send/state/nonexistent silently classify as Internal
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_types.rs:220-286` — `ErrorCode::category()` and `is_retryable()` use `match self.as_str()` over string literals with a wildcard `_ => ErrorCategory::Internal` and `matches!()` falsy-default respectively.

## Defect
69 unique `robot.*` codes are emitted across the production codebase. The category() function recognizes ~35 by exact-match plus 3 prefix patterns (workflow_/mission_/tx_). The remaining ~30 fall through to `ErrorCategory::Internal`, including codes that have a clearer category:

- **robot.send** — emitted by send-text path. Currently classified Internal; arguably Wezterm or a new IO category.
- **robot.state** — emitted by state-query path. Currently Internal; arguably Wezterm.
- **robot.nonexistent** — test/dev placeholder; should not silently be Internal.
- **robot.tx_lock_failed** — workflow_/mission_/tx_ prefix catches it as Workflow ✓ — but `is_retryable()` does NOT include it, despite lock-failed being a textbook retry candidate.

There is NO compile-time exhaustiveness check. A new code added in any module silently defaults to Internal+non-retryable until someone remembers to update this file. Pre-existing classification gaps are invisible.

## Impact
- Operators triaging by category get bucketed-into-Internal noise that hides real subsystem issues.
- Retry middleware misses retryable codes (e.g. tx_lock_failed) that should auto-retry.
- Class P3 OBS / classification correctness.

## Fix shape (option A — typed)
Replace the `String` newtype with a non_exhaustive enum + a fallback `Custom(String)` variant. category() and is_retryable() become exhaustive matches with compiler-enforced coverage. Larger fix, ~1 day.

## Fix shape (option B — minimal)
1. Add the missing classifications:
   - `robot.send` → Wezterm (or new `Io` category)
   - `robot.state` → Wezterm
   - `robot.tx_lock_failed` → add to is_retryable() list
2. Add a CI lint that grep-extracts all `"robot.*"` literals and asserts category() recognizes each by exact-match ("unknown — expected default Internal — please confirm").
3. Document in module docs that NEW codes MUST be added to BOTH category() AND is_retryable() per design review.

## Tests
Per missing code, add an `ErrorCode::parse(\"robot.send\").unwrap().category()` assertion against the chosen category.

## Class
P3 classification correctness — observability-only, no data loss but observability/retry-routing impacted.

Audit sweep showed the wider stringly-typed concern over robot.send/state/nonexistent was over-broad — those are capability/operation/test identifiers, not error codes. title: [ssh][sftp] Fail closed on libssh SFTP adapter edge cases
description:
## Finding
The mock-code scan started from the stale SftpChannelError::NotImplemented member. That enum variant is dead, but the same SFTP adapter has real fail-open/panic edges in production libssh-backed code.

## Evidence
- frankenterm/ssh/src/sftpwrap.rs converts OpenOptions::mode and create_dir mode with try_into().unwrap() for libssh-rs sys::mode_t.
- frankenterm/ssh/src/sftpwrap.rs expects every libssh read_dir metadata row to have name(), while the libssh-rs API returns Option<&str>.
- frankenterm/ssh/src/sftp/types.rs converts libssh SystemTime to Unix seconds with duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).expect(...), which can panic if a remote server reports pre-epoch timestamps.

## Scope
Replace those panics with typed SftpChannelError::FileIo/InvalidData or Unsupported-style errors, preserving normal ssh2 behavior and libssh happy paths. Add focused tests/helpers where they can run without a live SSH server.

## Proof
- rustfmt check on touched Rust files.
- git diff --check on touched files.
- br dep cycles --json.
- RCH-only Cargo proof for frankenterm-ssh when worker admission is available; local Cargo is not valid proof in this repo.

title: Add macOS system probes to environment auto-config

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT] Dramatically improve ft as a terminal emulator — close the wezterm-vs-ghostty/rio gap
description:
# BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT

## Origin
Reality-check audit (2026-04-30, docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md) found that ft is "wezterm + 460k LOC of agent-orchestration scaffolding bolted on top — but the *terminal emulation itself* hasn't meaningfully improved on WezTerm." This epic is the explicit mandate to close that gap.

## Mission
Make ft's terminal-emulator core *better* than WezTerm (and competitive with ghostty/rio) along three measurable axes:
1. Resize/repagination smoothness — no flicker, no stutter, sub-frame frame times during live-resize gestures
2. Steady-state input-to-photon latency — sub-vsync where the OS allows
3. Visual quality — no artifacts, no scroll glitches, no color/cell consistency bugs

Plus a fourth, cross-cutting axis added in Phase 6 refinement:
4. Do NOT regress accessibility, IME, color-management, or BiDi correctness for users who depend on them

## Source mining
- legacy_ghostty (`legacy_ghostty/src/renderer/`) — stable versioned atlas, triple-buffered swap chain, conditional redraw, Metal-direct backend
- legacy_rio (`legacy_rio/rio/sugarloaf/`) — retained-mode rendering, per-line dirty tracking, elastic instance buffer, sugar layer compositor
- legacy_zellij (`legacy_zellij/zellij-server/src/`) — floating panes, WASM plugins, stacked tabs, status bar tile system

## Sub-epics
- **1**: Render-path overhaul (stable atlas + per-line dirty + elastic instance buffer + bin-packing + quad cache + visual regression)
- **2**: Live-resize fast path + reflow-aware terminal model (gesture detection + draft mode + incremental reflow + snap-back + persistent-rope evaluation)
- **3**: Platform-direct backends (macOS Metal-direct + Wayland frame-callback batching + X11 burst coalescing)
- **4**: Layered compositor + zellij feature uplift (compositor + floating panes + WASM plugins + status tiles + stacked tabs)
- **5**: Conditional redraw + frame-pacing budget allocator (predicate + budget + idle dropdown)
- **6**: Lower-priority renderer enhancements (instanced rendering + CRC + latency-pinned input + SDF + predictive font + cell-delta + tearing-free + compute shaping)
- **A11Y (10)**: Cross-cutting accessibility protections (AT integration + IME + color-mgmt + BiDi + preferences) — guards every other sub-epic from regressing assistive tech

## Standalone beads
- **SLO (7)**: Resize Quality SLO catalog
- **COMPETITOR (8)**: ft vs WezTerm/Ghostty/Rio per-release proof
- **ROLLOUT (9)**: Feature-flag rollout strategy with absolute version markers (m0/m1/m2/...)

## Cross-references
- Reality-check beads ft-ombfl + ft-35yac.1.2 = the visual regression proof harnesses that validate this work
- Reality-check bead ft-syqcz.5 = the competitor bench matrix where new numbers publish
- Reality-check bead ft-syqcz.1 = the attestation graph this work publishes into

## Sequencing
Sub-epic 1 (render-path overhaul) is the foundation — everything else either depends on it or is independent. Sub-epic 2 (live-resize) shares state-machine work with 1 but ships independently after. A11Y epic runs in parallel with 1 + 2 (no blocking deps from sub-epics 1-6 to A11Y, but renderer-touching beads cross-link to A11Y test fixtures).

## Phase 6 refinement convergence
After 5 deep-refinement passes, the bead corpus has:
- Structured JSON-line logging spec on every test section
- Accessibility / IME / color-management / BiDi / preferences cross-links from every renderer-touching bead
- Rollback paths on every major change (Metal-direct, persistent rope, draft mode, frame-budget)
- Telemetry (exposed via `ft doctor`) on every state-machine bead
- Per-platform test matrices for resize-related work (Wayland compositors, X11 WMs, macOS chips)
- AGENTS.md doctrine alignment (asupersync, forbid(unsafe_code) waivers, no file proliferation, no backwards compat)
- Absolute version markers (m0/m1/m2...) replacing abstract r0/r1/...
- 18 canonical visual-regression scenarios enumerated (vs prose "≥6 scenarios")
- 12 SLOs in the consolidated catalog with source bench files

## Bead totals
- 1 root epic
- 7 sub-epics (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, A11Y)
- 30+ leaf tasks
- 0 cycles
- ≥6 ready entry points (no blockers, P1)

## Acceptance for the epic as a whole
- Resize benchmark: ≥60 FPS sustained on 200-pane fleet during 5-second live-resize gesture (currently <30 FPS)
- Input-to-photon p95 latency: <16ms on macOS, <20ms on Wayland (current: 32-50ms p95 under load)
- Visual artifact rate: zero bugs from a 24-hour adversarial fuzz (random resize + scroll + content streams)
- Differential bench (vs WezTerm/Ghostty/Rio) shows ft ≥ ghostty on resize-FPS metric
- Zero accessibility regressions on AT regression suite
- All work publishes through reality-check attestation graph (per-release signed bundle)

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.1.1] Stable versioned atlas (ghostty pattern) — never rebuild on resize
description:
# Stable Versioned Atlas (Ghostty Pattern)

## Background
Current atlas (`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/glyphcache.rs` + `frankenterm/window/src/bitmaps/atlas.rs`) is rebuilt on every scale/DPI change at `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/resize.rs:124`. This is the single biggest source of resize stutter.

Ghostty solved this with versioned per-region modification flags (`legacy_ghostty/src/renderer/generic.zig:1534-1549`):
```zig
// Only sync if modified > frame.grayscale_modified (incremental)
if (state.atlas_grayscale.modified.load(.acquire) > frame.grayscale_modified) { ... }
```

## User-perceived value
- Resize never causes visible flicker (atlas stays warm; no rebuild flash)
- DPI change (e.g., dragging between monitors) doesn't restart glyph cache
- Battery drain during resize drops ~50% (no atlas re-rasterize work)

## Concrete actions
1. Add a `version: AtomicU64` field to the atlas struct
2. On every glyph upload, bump the version
3. Per-frame state tracks `last_synced_version: u64`
4. Resize only re-uploads glyph regions whose version changed since last sync (zero on a pure window-size resize)
5. Atlas growth (when out of texture space) is incremental: allocate a new texture, copy old contents via blit pass, *retain* the version map
6. Remove the `recreate_texture_atlas(None)` call from `scaling_changed()` path
7. Add per-glyph version stamp for fine-grained sync
8. Telemetry: atlas_uploads_total, atlas_rebuilds_total (should stay at 0 under normal use), atlas_grow_count, atlas_size_bytes

## AGENTS.md doctrine reminder
- Code lives in frankenterm-core or frankenterm-gui (forbid(unsafe_code) applies); use safe Rust
- asupersync primitives only — no raw tokio in any new threading
- Edit the existing files in place; no glyphcache_v2.rs or similar (per AGENTS.md "no file proliferation")

## Structured logging
JSON-line emissions in tests/atlas_stability/logs/:
- Per atlas op: ts, op (upload/grow/sync), version_before, version_after, bytes
- Per resize: ts, glyphs_re_uploaded (should be 0), atlas_size_bytes_before/after, sync_duration_ms

## Tests
- Unit: atlas-version monotonic invariant (proptest on op sequences)
- Unit: resize without glyph additions → zero re-upload bytes
- Unit: atlas grow preserves version map (proptest)
- Unit: blit-on-grow correctness — new texture's contents byte-equal old's
- E2E: run a 10-pane terminal, resize 100 times, assert atlas content hash stays identical
- Bench: resize-storm benchmark (50 resize events / sec) — assert <1ms p99 atlas-sync time
- Regression: WezTerm pre-fix reproducer (atlas rebuild on resize) — confirms bug present without fix
- Telemetry: atlas_rebuilds_total stays at 0 across the test suite

## Acceptance
- `recreate_texture_atlas` no longer called from resize paths
- Atlas-version test suite passes
- Resize-storm bench passes p99 target
- Visual regression harness (cross-link ft-mpc9b.1.6) reports zero artifacts
- Telemetry exposed via ft doctor
- Per-release attestation entry: atlas_stability metric (cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1)

## Why P1 + Foundation
Foundation for everything in this epic. Sub-epic 2 (live-resize fast path) needs per-line dirty + stable atlas. Sub-epic 3 (Metal-direct) needs storage-agnostic atlas. Sub-epic 4 (compositor) needs per-layer atlas regions. Sub-epic 5 (conditional redraw) doesn't pay off if atlas keeps rebuilding.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.1.2] Per-line dirty bitmap (rio pattern) — replace coarse quad_generation counter
description:
# Per-Line Dirty Bitmap (Rio Pattern)

## Background
Current coarse invalidation: `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/resize.rs:51` increments a `quad_generation` counter that triggers full-screen rebuild. There is no per-line or per-cell granularity.

Rio's pattern (`legacy_rio/rio/sugarloaf/src/layout/content.rs:151-155`):
```rust
pub fn mark_dirty(&mut self) { self.dirty = true; }
pub fn mark_line_dirty(&mut self, line: usize) { self.dirty_lines.insert(line); }
```

## User-perceived value
- 200-pane fleet typing 1 char/sec rebuilds 1 line/frame, not 200 lines/frame
- CPU usage during light typing drops ~95%
- Battery life on laptop with active ft-watch session improves significantly

## Concrete actions
1. Add `dirty_lines: BitSet` to the screen state (one bit per visible row)
2. Source dirty events (enumerate all):
   - PTY output writes a cell → mark line dirty
   - Cursor moves → mark old + new line dirty (cursor-blink also marks cursor-row)
   - Selection changes → mark spanned lines dirty
   - Resize (per sub-epic 2) → mark only lines whose content shifted
   - Pane focus change → mark border-row(s) dirty
   - Theme change → mark all rows dirty (rare)
   - Font change → mark all rows dirty (rare)
   - Status-tile updates (post-4.4) → mark status-bar row dirty
3. Render pass iterates only over dirty lines; clean lines reuse last frame's quads
4. Frame end clears the dirty set
5. Migrate `quad_generation` to be a lower-bound version on top of per-line dirty (kept for whole-screen events like font change)
6. Telemetry: dirty_lines_per_frame (histogram), clean_lines_skipped (counter)

## Data structure choice (alien-artifact uplift)
Use a roaring bitmap (`roaring` crate) for sparse dirty sets when there are many panes — efficient union/iter for >64 lines. Evaluated as part of the implementation.

## AGENTS.md doctrine reminder
- forbid(unsafe_code) — use safe Rust; bitset crate must be safe
- Edit terminalstate/mod.rs in place; no fork

## Structured logging
JSON-line per frame at tests/dirty_tracking/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- ts, frame_idx, dirty_lines_count, dirty_line_indices, trigger_events_count_per_kind
- Frame summary: clean_skipped, dirty_processed, total_quad_rebuild_time_ns

## Tests
- Unit: dirty-line propagation from cell mutation (proptest)
- Unit: cursor-move dirties exactly old+new line, nothing else
- Unit: selection-extend dirties spanned rows, nothing else
- Unit: resize-from-2.3 dirties only shifted lines
- E2E: type into a single line, assert frame metric "lines_redrawn=1"
- Bench: 200-pane fleet with 1 cell change per frame — assert <0.1ms quad-rebuild time
- Bench: 200-pane fleet with full-screen mutation (font swap) — full rebuild should be O(N) and within budget
- Regression: dirty-event source enumeration is comprehensive (no missing dirty source causes a stale frame)

## Acceptance
- Per-line dirty bitmap shipped
- Lines-redrawn frame metric exposed
- Bench passes 0.1ms target
- Lines untouched are observably skipped (instrumentation count)
- All dirty-event sources enumerated and tested

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.1.3] Elastic instance buffer (rio pattern) — decouple from atlas size
description:
# Elastic Instance Buffer (Rio Pattern)

## Background
Current quad batching (`crates/frankenterm-gui/src/quad.rs`) is per-cell with 4 vertices. Buffer size is implicitly tied to the atlas state, which means atlas changes ripple into vertex buffer reallocations.

Rio's pattern (`legacy_rio/rio/sugarloaf/src/components/core/buffer.rs:40`): instance buffer grows independently with explicit doubling strategy.

## User-perceived value
- No frame stall when atlas grows or window resizes
- Predictable memory footprint (high-water mark held during gestures)
- Independent tuning: VRAM use scales with screen size, not atlas size

## Concrete actions
1. Define `ElasticBuffer<T>` wrapper around wgpu buffer with capacity-doubling growth
2. Initial capacity: cells-per-screen at default size (e.g., 200×80 cells = 16k entries)
3. Growth: double when full; align to 64k for power-of-two GPU efficiency
4. Track high-water mark; never shrink during resize gestures (only after gesture end + idle for 1s)
5. Replace per-cell vertex batching with instance buffer of cell-instance-data records
6. Ensure buffer lifetime is independent of atlas lifetime (atlas can resize without touching buffer; buffer can grow without touching atlas)
7. Telemetry: buffer_capacity, buffer_used, buffer_grow_count, buffer_shrink_count

## AGENTS.md doctrine reminder
- forbid(unsafe_code); wgpu's buffer API is safe
- No file proliferation; integrate into quad.rs in place

## Structured logging
JSON-line at tests/elastic_buffer/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- Per buffer op: ts, op (alloc/grow/shrink), capacity_before, capacity_after, bytes
- Per resize: ts, capacity_at_start, capacity_at_end, allocs_during_resize (target: 0 during gesture)
- Per session: high_water_mark, total_grow_count, total_shrink_count

## Tests
- Unit: elastic buffer doubling correctness (proptest on push sequences)
- Unit: shrink only after gesture end + idle (state-machine test)
- Unit: capacity invariant: capacity ≥ used always
- E2E: resize from 80×24 to 200×60 to 80×24, assert buffer capacity stays at high-water mark until idle
- Bench: 10× rapid resize, assert zero buffer reallocs during the burst
- Bench: 1-hour idle session, assert eventual shrink to capacity ≈ used
- Regression: previous buffer-realloc-storms reproducer fails on pre-fix; passes on post-fix

## Depends on
- 1.1 (stable atlas — buffer is independent of atlas; this dep ensures atlas APIs are storage-agnostic)
- 1.2 (per-line dirty — buffer needs to know what to write per frame)

## Acceptance
- ElasticBuffer abstraction shipped
- Vertex/instance buffer growth decoupled from atlas
- Resize-burst bench shows zero allocs during gesture
- Idle shrink works
- Telemetry exposed via ft doctor

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.1.4] Atlas bin-packing — skyline or maximal-rectangles algorithm
description:
# Atlas Bin-Packing — Skyline or Maximal-Rectangles Algorithm

## Background
Once the atlas is stable (sub-task 1.1), efficient packing matters more — glyphs accumulate over a session and the atlas should make best use of texture VRAM.

## User-perceived value
- Lower VRAM usage for the same glyph set
- Long sessions don't run out of atlas space (reduces atlas-grow events)
- Especially valuable for CJK + emoji users (many glyphs)

## Algorithm choice (alien-artifact uplift)
Per Jukka Jylänki's "A Thousand Ways to Pack the Bin":
- **Skyline** — simple, ~5% wasted space, fast. Default for small atlases (<2048²)
- **Maximal rectangles** — tighter packing (~2% wasted space), slower. Default for atlases >4096²
- **Shelf-packing** — fastest, ~10% wasted, fine for small static atlases (legacy fallback)

Pick adaptive: size-based threshold (configurable via tuning_config).

## Concrete actions
1. Add a pluggable `BinPacker` trait in frankenterm/window/src/bitmaps/atlas.rs
2. Implement skyline + maximal-rectangles
3. Bench harness comparing packing efficiency on representative glyph corpus (Latin + CJK + Nerd Font + emoji)
4. Wire into atlas alloc path
5. Default selection by atlas size
6. Telemetry: packing_efficiency_pct, fragmentation_pct, packer_in_use

## Structured logging
JSON-line per atlas op at tests/atlas_packing/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- ts, glyph_id, glyph_size, allocation_pos, packer, wasted_space_after_alloc, total_atlas_bytes

## Tests
- Unit: packing is non-overlapping (proptest)
- Unit: free-and-realloc maintains invariants (proptest on op sequences)
- Bench: pack 10k random glyphs, measure wasted space % per algorithm
- Bench: pack a real-world glyph corpus (English text, CJK doc, emoji-rich chat, mixed) — validate which algorithm wins per workload
- Regression: known WezTerm packing bugs (if any) reproduce + fix

## Depends on
- 1.1 (stable atlas — packing is a strategy plug-in to the atlas allocator)

## Acceptance
- Two pluggable packers shipped
- Default selection by atlas size + workload
- Wasted-space metric exposed via ft doctor
- Bench artifact published per release (cross-link BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1 attestation)
- Per-real-world-corpus comparison documented at `docs/perf/atlas-packing-comparison.md`

## Why P2
Compounds with 1.1; not blocking strategic work.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.1.5] Per-line quad cache — only rebuild changed lines' quad lists
description:
# Per-Line Quad Cache

## Background
Now that we have per-line dirty (1.2) + elastic buffer (1.3), the missing piece is a per-line quad cache. The render pass iterates dirty lines, rebuilds those lines' quads, and concatenates with the cached quad lists from clean lines.

## User-perceived value
- Steady-state CPU usage near-zero (no per-frame full screen rebuild)
- Frame time variance drops dramatically
- Bench: 200-pane fleet typing 1 char/sec → frame time within 1ms of 0

## Concrete actions
1. Replace the global quad list with a per-line `Vec<Quad>` indexed by row
2. On dirty event: invalidate that row's quad list
3. Frame build: walk row-by-row, generate quads for dirty rows, copy quads from clean rows
4. Final upload: single concat into the elastic instance buffer (1.3)
5. Telemetry: cache_hit_rate (per-frame), cache_capacity, cache_evictions

## Cache invalidation triggers (ordered by frequency)
- Per-cell mutation → that line's row dirty (most common; sub-task 1.2 source)
- Cursor blink → cursor row dirty (every cursor-blink-period)
- Selection extension → spanned rows dirty
- Pane focus change → pane border row dirty (just 4 rows)
- Theme change → all rows dirty (rare; full rebuild)
- Resize → reflow-driven dirty (sub-epic 2's incremental reflow)
- Font change → all rows dirty (rare)
- Status-tile update (post-4.4) → status-bar row dirty
- Floating-pane move (post-4.2) → row range under floating pane dirty

## AGENTS.md doctrine reminder
- forbid(unsafe_code); use Vec<Quad> + Box, no unsafe
- asupersync if any concurrent access (tile updates from background plugin)
- Edit existing file in place

## Structured logging
JSON-line per frame at tests/quad_cache/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- frame_idx, cache_hits, cache_misses, hit_rate_pct, total_quads_assembled, time_to_concat_ns

## Tests
- Unit: per-line cache hit rate after random mutations (proptest)
- Unit: cache invariant: quads from cache + quads from rebuild = identical to full rebuild
- Unit: invalidation triggers — every enumerated trigger correctly marks dirty
- E2E: type 1 char per second for 60 sec, assert ≥95% rows are cache hits per frame
- Bench: 200-pane fleet steady-state — assert per-frame quad-rebuild work is O(active_panes), not O(visible_rows)
- Regression: cache-staleness reproducer (e.g., theme change without invalidating all rows) fixed

## Depends on
- 1.2 (per-line dirty) — this is what triggers cache invalidation
- 1.3 (elastic buffer) — this is where the concat'd output lands

## Acceptance
- Per-line quad cache shipped
- Cache-hit-rate metric exposed
- Bench passes O(active_panes) target
- All cache invalidation triggers enumerated + tested
- ft doctor reports cache state

description:
# Visual Regression Harness for Renderer Changes

## Background
Sub-epic 1 changes are foundational. Without a hard regression catch, the next agent who touches the renderer can silently regress every gain. WezTerm shipped resize/scroll artifacts for years that nobody caught at PR time; ft must make this class of bug structurally unshippable.

## User-perceived value
- Future agents (and the maintainer) can refactor the renderer with confidence; CI catches drift
- Users never see a regression released — every shipped frame is byte-comparable to the golden

## Cross-references (deps, not just comments)
- **ft-ombfl** ("headless visual GPU regression harness" — already open) — extend it for this purpose; this bead reuses its CI infra
- **ft-35yac.1.2** ("Headless GPU-renderer parity test (visual regression catch)") — borrow the pixel-diff infrastructure
- **ft-syqcz.5** ("Differential bench matrix vs WezTerm/Zellij/Ghostty") — publish numbers here
- **ft-syqcz.1** (attestation graph schema) — render-parity artifact published per release

## Canonical test scenarios (enumerate, don't gesture)
Each scenario is a deterministic input script (vhs/asciinema-derived). All must produce byte-identical render frames before+after a renderer change. Stored at `tests/renderer_golden/scenarios/<name>/`.

1. **steady-typing**: 60s of `cat /usr/share/dict/words` at moderate rate
2. **vim-edit**: open vim, navigate, type, save, quit (heavy ANSI movement + cursor)
3. **htop-top**: 30s of htop with sort changes (heavy redraw, partial-screen updates)
4. **neofetch-banner**: ANSI art with 24-bit color, transparency, Unicode box-drawing
5. **resize-step**: 80×24 → 200×80 → 80×24 in 1px steps (live-resize stress)
6. **resize-burst**: 50 resize events in 1 second (frame-callback stress)
7. **scroll-stress**: scroll up/down 1000 lines, page-up/down, jump-to-end
8. **selection-drag**: click+drag selection across full screen
9. **scrollback-search**: open search, type query, navigate matches
10. **multi-pane-split**: split into 8 panes, focus-cycle, type into each
11. **dpi-change**: simulated DPI change mid-session (scaling_changed path)
12. **font-change**: live font swap (atlas should retain on swap-back; SE1.1)
13. **alt-screen**: enter/exit alt-screen via vim/less repeatedly
14. **mouse-tracking**: mouse-mode-on, hover, click, drag, mouse-mode-off
15. **wide-gamut**: 24-bit color + DCI-P3 color profile (color-management regression catch)
16. **rtl-script**: Arabic/Hebrew text rendering (BiDi correctness)
17. **cjk-mixed**: ASCII + CJK + emoji + zero-width joiner sequences
18. **screen-reader-active**: assistive-tech announcements present (accessibility regression catch)

## Structured logging requirement
The harness emits **JSON-line structured logs** at `tests/renderer_golden/logs/<scenario>/<frame_n>.jsonl`:
- One log line per rendered frame with: frame_idx, ts_ns, ssim, pixel_diff_count, atlas_version, dirty_lines_count, quad_count, gpu_time_ns, paint_pass_count
- One summary line at scenario end with: total_frames, ssim_min, ssim_p99, pixel_diff_total, atlas_rebuild_count
- Failure mode: failed scenarios drop a `failure.json` with the offending frame index, before/after PNGs (lossless), and the structured-log slice covering the regression

Per AGENTS.md frozen template clause: "great, detailed logging so we can be sure that everything is working perfectly after implementation."

## Concrete actions
1. Build deterministic test scenarios per the enumerated list above
2. Capture rendered output via headless GPU pipeline (lavapipe / softpipe / Metal headless)
3. Compute SSIM ≥0.99 (lossy threshold) + exact pixel diff (lossless mode for the scoreboard)
4. Golden artifact storage in `tests/renderer_golden/` with content-hash naming
5. CI lane runs all scenarios on every renderer-related PR
6. Failure mode: clear before/after diff image with offending pixel highlighted, plus structured-log diff
7. Publishes `docs/attestations/render-parity-<version>.json` per release (cross-link ft-syqcz.1)

## Adversarial fuzz lane
24-hour fuzz CI lane:
- Random resize stream + random content stream + random scroll
- Captures any frame where SSIM <0.99 or pixel-diff finds nonzero in pristine area
- Failure → bug report with reproducer script (deterministic seed) + structured-log slice

## Accessibility regression catch
Scenario 18 specifically targets: do screen-reader announcements still fire correctly when the renderer is in draft mode (sub-task 2.2)? Renderer changes that bypass the platform accessibility tree silently break VoiceOver/Orca/Narrator.

## Acceptance
- Harness exists, runs in CI on every renderer PR
- 18 deterministic scenarios cover the major code paths (enumerated above)
- 24h adversarial fuzz lane reports zero artifacts on default branch
- Per-release artifact published to attestation graph
- Cross-link to ft-ombfl + ft-35yac.1.2 documented in their bead comments
- Structured JSON-line logs stored per scenario per frame; reviewable post-hoc

  -> ft-mpc9b.1 (parent-child)

# Accessibility, IME, Color-Management — Cross-Cutting Protections

## Background
Sub-epics 1-6 elevate raw rendering performance, but a fast renderer that breaks assistive tech is a regression for blind users, IME users, color-managed-display users, and BiDi-script users. This epic is the cross-cutting protective layer that ensures the renderer overhaul does NOT silently regress these populations.

## User-perceived value
- Blind users: VoiceOver/Orca/Narrator continues to work through every renderer change
- IME users (Pinyin, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, etc.): composition windows track caret correctly even in Draft mode
- Color-managed-display users: Display-P3, Rec.2020, ProPhoto-RGB profiles apply correctly through every render path
- Right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew): BiDi rendering correct, no glyph reordering bugs
- High-contrast / dark-mode / reduce-motion users: preferences honored regardless of RenderQuality

## Sub-tasks
- A11Y.1: Accessibility tree integration audit + regression test fixture
- A11Y.2: IME composition window correctness across renderer modes
- A11Y.3: Color-management correctness audit (gamut + ICC profile support)
- A11Y.4: BiDi rendering regression test
- A11Y.5: Reduce-motion + high-contrast preference plumbing through all RenderQuality levels
- A11Y.6: Screen-reader-active detection that opts out of idle-mode (cross-link 5.3)

## Cross-cutting checks applied to renderer beads
Each renderer-touching bead must pass these gates:
- Does Draft mode still emit accessibility tree updates?
- Does the change preserve IME caret-anchor invariants?
- Does the change preserve ICC color profile application?
- Does the change preserve BiDi reordering?
- Does the change honor reduce-motion preference?

## Concrete actions
1. Build accessibility test fixture: simulated AT-SPI / NSAccessibility / UIAutomation client that records all accessibility events from ft for a scenario corpus
2. IME test fixture: scripted Pinyin / Japanese composition + caret-tracking assertion
3. Color-management corpus: ICC test patterns through render pipeline; pixel-exact color match
4. BiDi corpus: Arabic + Hebrew + mixed RTL/LTR input; visual + structural assertions
5. Reduce-motion corpus: animation-disabled scenarios; assert no animations occur
6. Cross-link these tests as required gates on all renderer-touching beads (1.1, 1.2, 1.5, 2.2, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 5.3)

## Structured logging
- Per-scenario log: ts, scenario, accessibility_events_emitted, ime_anchor_correctness, color_match_count, bidi_correctness, reduce_motion_honored
- Summary log: scenario, pass/fail, evidence path

## Acceptance
- 6 sub-tasks shipped
- Cross-cutting checks integrated into renderer-touching beads
- AT regression suite runs in CI on every renderer-touching PR
- Per-release attestation entry for accessibility coverage
- README has an "Accessibility & Internationalization" section linking to the test corpus

## Why P1
Foundation for the whole epic — ensures we don't trade users for FPS.

## Background
Modern displays support wide-gamut profiles (Display-P3, Rec.2020, ProPhoto-RGB). Apple Pro Display XDR users, photographers, and developers using HDR-aware tools rely on correct color profile application. Renderer changes that drop/skip profile application produce wrong colors silently.

   - shader output color space
   - ICC profile detection per-display
2. Build test corpus:
   - sRGB test pattern (canonical 24-bit color cube)
   - Display-P3 test pattern (wider gamut, P3-only colors)
   - Rec.2020 test pattern (HDR-aware)
3. Per-render-path verification:
   - Standard quality: full color management
   - Draft quality (from 2.2): full color management still applies
   - Metal-direct backend (from 3.1): identical color match to wgpu backend
4. Pixel-exact color match: render → screenshot → ICC-aware compare
5. CI runs on a calibrated color-managed test machine (set up once, golden-corpus thereafter)

## Structured logging

## Tests
- Per-color-pattern: ΔE ≤ 1.0 (perceptually identical) across all render paths
- Wide-gamut: P3-only colors render correctly on P3-capable display
- Profile-mismatch fallback: sRGB content on P3 display renders within sRGB gamut
- Surface format: shader output matches surface format declared color space

## Acceptance

- ICC profile correctness verified across all render paths
- Per-release attestation entry: color-management coverage report

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.2.1] Detect live-resize gesture on macOS/Wayland/X11
description:
# Live-Resize Gesture Detection on macOS/Wayland/X11

## Background
Need a unified `LiveResizeState` enum signaled to the renderer:
- Idle (default)
- ResizeBegin (gesture started)
- Resizing (drag in progress, may emit many size deltas)
- ResizeEnd (gesture released)

## User-perceived value
- The whole sub-epic 2 fast path depends on this signal being right
- Users get smooth resize on every platform; no platform feels "chunky"

## Per-platform sources
- **macOS**: `NSWindowWillStartLiveResizeNotification` + `NSWindowDidEndLiveResizeNotification`. Wire via `frankenterm/window/src/os/macos/window.rs`. Note: macOS sometimes skips the End notification on extremely fast gesture release; need watchdog (see "Failure modes" below)
- **Wayland**: xdg_toplevel `configure` events with state including `Resizing`. Wire via `frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs`. Some compositors (sway/Hyprland) emit different cadences than mutter/kwin — test on multiple
- **X11**: `_NET_WM_STATE_LIVE_RESIZE` (some WMs only) + ConfigureNotify burst detection (16ms-window heuristic) for fallback. Wire via `frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/window.rs`

## Failure modes + recovery
1. **Stuck-in-Resizing**: if no state change for 5s during Resizing, force ResizeEnd. Watchdog runs in `frankenterm/window` event loop.
2. **macOS skipped Did-End**: detect via mouse-up event correlation; force ResizeEnd if mouse-up arrives during Resizing.
3. **Wayland configure storm**: if >100 configures in 100ms, coalesce to one ResizeBegin + final config (avoid dirty-flood).
4. **X11 fake-positive**: ConfigureNotify can fire from window-manager workspace switches, not user resize. Heuristic: only treat as live-resize if dimension changed (not just position).

## Structured logging
Test fixtures emit JSON-line logs at `tests/live_resize/logs/<platform>-<scenario>.jsonl`:
- One log per state transition: ts_ns, prev_state, next_state, source_event, dimensions
- Failure: `failure.json` with full event sequence

## Concrete actions
1. Add `LiveResizeState` enum to platform window abstraction in `frankenterm/window/src/os/mod.rs` (or platform-agnostic location)
2. Per-platform plumbing per the sources above
3. State changes broadcast to the renderer via existing event channel (asupersync mpsc, NOT raw tokio per AGENTS.md)
4. Test fixture for fake-driven gesture sequences (deterministic, replay-able)
5. Watchdog timer using runtime_async::sleep_with_cx (Cx-aware cancel-correctness)
6. Per-platform integration test
7. Structured JSON-line logging on all transitions

## Tests
- Unit: state machine transitions (proptest on event sequences)
  - Invariants: state diagram is acyclic when projected on (Idle→Begin→Resizing*→End→Idle); Begin always preceded ResizeEnd
  - Each transition emits a JSON log line
- Manual / E2E: real gesture on each platform produces correct state sequence; recorded via vhs where possible
- Regression: gesture-end always fires (no stuck-in-Resizing bug)
- Adversarial: random kill-and-retry mid-gesture; assert state recovers to Idle within 5s

## Cross-references
- BR-RC-RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.G14 (Cx propagation) — watchdog is a Cx-aware async path
- ft-syqcz.5 (competitor matrix) — resize-detection latency is part of the bench suite

## Acceptance
- LiveResizeState plumbed end-to-end on all 3 platforms
- Renderer receives state changes via event channel (asupersync mpsc)
- Stuck-in-Resizing watchdog: 5s timeout enforced
- macOS skipped-Did-End recovery works
- Wayland configure-storm coalescing works
- X11 ConfigureNotify dimension-change heuristic works
- Per-platform integration test passes
- Structured logs reviewable post-hoc

## Why P1
Sub-epic 2's other tasks (draft mode + reflow) all need this signal. Foundation for the whole sub-epic.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.2.3] Incremental terminal grid reflow (O(damage) not O(N))
description:
# Incremental Terminal Grid Reflow (O(damage) not O(N))

## Background
Current resize causes O(N) terminal grid recalculation. For a 200-pane fleet, that's expensive enough to feel.

The right algorithm: **incremental reflow** — only re-line content whose visual position actually changed.

## User-perceived value
- Resize is fast on huge scrollback (10k+ lines per pane)
- Low-end devices (integrated GPU, battery-saving mode) handle resize without stuttering
- Multi-byte / CJK / emoji / RTL text reflows correctly under width changes (no glyph-order corruption)

## Algorithm
On width change `W → W'`:
1. For each line, compute its new wrap-set under W'
2. If the new wrap-set is identical to the old (i.e., the line fit in both W and W'), skip
3. If it changed, mark all visually-shifted rows dirty (sub-task 1.2 picks them up)
4. Cursor coordinates remap proportionally

For height change `H → H'`: trivial — just reveal/hide rows from scrollback. No reflow needed.

## Multi-byte + wide-character correctness
Reflow MUST preserve:
- Multi-byte UTF-8 sequences (ASCII, Latin, CJK, Arabic, emoji)
- Zero-width-joiner sequences (emoji families like 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦)
- Combining marks (base + diacritic must travel together)
- Wide-character cells (CJK take 2 cells; can't split mid-cell on wrap)
- ANSI styling spans (color/attr that crosses wrap point preserved)
- BiDi paragraph integrity (RTL paragraph reflows without LTR/RTL mixing corruption — cross-link A11Y.4)

## Concrete actions
1. Audit `frankenterm/term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs` reflow path; find current algorithm
2. Replace with incremental algorithm
3. Per-line wrap-set computation function (deterministic, pure)
4. Add unit tests covering edge cases:
   - Lines that fit in both widths (no work)
   - Lines that wrap differently (re-line)
   - Multi-byte / wide characters (CJK, emoji, ZWJ)
   - Combining marks
   - ANSI styling preserved across reflow
   - BiDi: RTL + mixed-direction paragraphs
5. Cursor remap correctness

## Alien-artifact uplift (alternative impl, see 2.5)
- Persistent rope (HAMT or RRB-Tree) for O(log n) reflow + structurally-shared scrollback. Evaluated separately in 2.5.

## Structured logging
JSON-line per reflow: ts, old_width, new_width, lines_reflowed, lines_skipped, total_lines, duration_ms

## Tests
- Proptest: random content + random resize sequence; assert post-reflow content matches deterministic reference (compared cell-by-cell)
- Bench: 1000-line scrollback, resize 80→200, target <5ms
- Bench: 10k-line scrollback, resize 80→200, target <50ms
- Regression: known WezTerm reflow bugs (issue references in commit messages) reproduce in test suite, must be fixed
- CJK-correctness: 1000 lines of CJK + emoji, resize, assert no glyph reordering
- BiDi-correctness: Arabic paragraph, resize, assert paragraph reorders correctly
- Cursor-remap: cursor at (r,c) before resize, assert (r',c') after is correct under wrap-change

## Depends on
- 1.2 (per-line dirty)
- A11Y.4 (BiDi correctness corpus)

## Acceptance
- Incremental algorithm replaces O(N) algorithm
- 1000-line bench passes 5ms target
- 10k-line bench passes 50ms target

description:
# Snap-Back Repaint + Adversarial Resize Fuzz

## Background
On ResizeEnd, switch from Draft to Standard/Fancy in one full-quality repaint. Verify quality matches what would have been rendered without ever entering Draft mode (no quality drift).

## User-perceived value
- Quality transition feels instantaneous on gesture release
- No visible "settling" period after resize ends
- Resize-then-pause-then-resize cycles work cleanly

## Concrete actions
1. ResizeEnd handler triggers single full-quality repaint of the visible viewport
2. Skip animation: the quality transition should be visually instantaneous (within 1 frame)
3. Adversarial fuzz harness:
   - Random gesture sequences (begin/resize/end/begin/end-without-resize/etc.)
   - Random content streams during resize
   - Assert: at any quiescent state (Idle), rendered output equals reference rendering
4. Property test: `Draft → Standard transition is idempotent` (multiple ResizeEnd events produce same output)
5. Adversarial corpus reuses 1.6's fuzz infrastructure but specifically targets resize state-machine

## DO NOT BREAK
- A11Y: AT updates fire on snap-back (focus state, screen-reader announcements consistent)
- IME: composition window stays anchored across snap-back
- Color: gamut preserved across Draft→Standard

## Structured logging
JSON-line per fuzz run at tests/snap_back_fuzz/logs/<seed>.jsonl:
- ts, fuzz_seed, gesture_sequence (compact list), content_stream_hash
- Per-frame: ts, render_quality, dirty_lines, frame_time_ns

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.2.5] Persistent rope (HAMT/RRB-Tree) for terminal grid — alien-artifact uplift
description:
# Persistent Rope (HAMT/RRB-Tree) for Terminal Grid — Alien-Artifact Uplift

## Background
Round-3 alien-artifact uplift mentioned in 2.3. Promoted to its own bead because it's substantial and orthogonal to the basic incremental reflow algorithm.

## User-perceived value
- Reflow on huge scrollback (10k+ lines) becomes O(log n) instead of O(N)
- Undo/scrollback queries / snapshots become near-free (structurally shared)
- Concurrent read against last-good snapshot — render thread reads while input thread mutates without locks

## Mathematical foundation
Persistent (functional) data structures share structure across versions. For a terminal grid:
- **HAMT (Hash Array Mapped Trie)** — O(log n) random access; structurally shared subtrees
- **RRB-Tree (Relaxed Radix Balanced)** — O(log n) split/concat; ideal for line operations
- **Rope** — classical text-editor data structure; concatenation-friendly

The rope wins because terminal operations are predominantly line-based (insert line, delete line, scroll up = drop top line + append bottom line).

## Why this matters for ft
1. **Reflow is tree-rebalancing** — O(log n) instead of O(N) for many cases
2. **Old/new states share structure** — undo, scrollback queries, snapshots are nearly free
3. **Concurrent reads against last-good snapshot** — render thread can read the previous frame's grid while the input thread mutates the next, without locks
4. **Session restore + replay** — checkpoints become rope-version-pointers, not full state copies

## Decision rubric (rollback path)
Ship rope-backed grid if AND ONLY IF:
- Reflow benchmark improvement ≥2× on 200-pane fleet
- Memory overhead ≤30% vs current
- Render thread unaffected (read-side performance unchanged)

If the prototype fails any of these, KEEP the existing flat-grid implementation and document the negative result. The repo retains both data structures behind a feature flag for future re-evaluation.

## Concrete actions
1. Audit `frankenterm/term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs` to identify the cell-grid data structure currently in use
2. Evaluate `im` crate (Bodil Stokke's Rust persistent collections) and `imbl` (fork) for fit
3. Build a prototype rope-backed grid + benchmark vs current
4. If prototype shows ≥2× speedup on representative workloads, promote to default
5. Otherwise: archive prototype + write evaluation doc; keep flat-grid

## AGENTS.md doctrine reminder
- forbid(unsafe_code); im/imbl crates are safe Rust
- No file proliferation; prototype lives behind feature flag in same file (or separate module if substantial)

## Structured logging
JSON-line at tests/persistent_rope/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- Per op: ts, op (insert_line/delete_line/scroll/reflow), tree_size, time_ns
- Per snapshot: ts, snapshot_id, shared_bytes, total_bytes

## Tests
- Property test: rope-backed grid produces identical observable behavior to flat grid (1000-op random sequences)
- Bench: reflow on 1000-line scrollback, rope vs flat
- Bench: reflow on 10k-line scrollback, rope vs flat
- Bench: concurrent read/write — assert read latency unaffected by writer rate
- Memory: peak memory in 1-hour heavy-output session, rope vs flat

## Why P3
Speculative — only ships if the benchmark wins. Don't commit until prototype validates.

## Depends on
- 2.3 (incremental reflow algorithm — rope is an alternative implementation, evaluated against it)

## Acceptance
- Prototype + bench results checked in (regardless of ship/no-ship)
- Decision documented at `docs/perf/persistent-rope-evaluation.md`
- If shipping: rope-backed grid replaces flat-grid as default
- If not shipping: prototype + negative result archived; rationale documented
close_reason: Implemented in 2ee688adc: persistent-rope prototype + flat-grid baseline behind common TerminalGridOps trait + Criterion bench harness + decision doc. Rubric FAILS on gate 1 (rope is 21× SLOWER than flat on pure reflow at 1000 lines — allocation overhead per per-line tree path-clone dominates at terminal-grid sizes). Verdict: ARCHIVE prototype, keep flat-grid as default. Constructive alternative documented: ft-d0ol8's TripleBuffer<Arc<FlatGrid>> already captures the rope's load-bearing snapshot win (~115,000× faster on 10k lines) without paying the reflow penalty. 13 lib tests pass including 1000-random-op observational-equivalence sweep + Arc::ptr_eq clone-O(1) verification. Bench numbers in docs/perf/persistent-rope-evaluation.md. Sub-epic 2 status: 2.1/2.2/2.3/2.4/2.5 all ✓ at contract layer; GUI integration beads remain.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.3] Sub-epic 3 — Platform-direct backends (macOS Metal-direct + Wayland frame-callback fix)
description:
# Sub-epic 3: Platform-Direct Backends

## Idea origin
Idea #3 from idea-wizard ranking. Two platform-specific fixes for the actual broken code the investigation flagged.

## Part A: macOS Metal-direct backend
Skip wgpu on macOS for rendering. Use CAMetalLayer directly with `presentDrawable:afterMinimumDuration:` for sub-vsync latency. Ghostty's pattern (`legacy_ghostty/src/renderer/Metal.zig`) with `swap_chain_count = 3` triple-buffer pattern hides resize stalls completely.

Why: macOS is where most ft users live, and wgpu's overhead hurts most there. wgpu is great for portability but cannot match Metal-direct latency.

## Part B: Wayland frame-callback batching
Bug at `frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs:1146-1179`:
- Line 1153: if frame_callback pending, sets `invalidated=true` and returns early
- Line 1157-1158: invalidation under compositor pressure
- Line 1168: re-requests frame_callback on EVERY paint attempt → callback chaining under fast resize

Fix: batch invalidations into a single per-vsync paint; only re-request callback after successful compose.

## Sub-tasks
- 3.1 Audit current wgpu macOS pipeline; map to equivalent Metal-direct API
- 3.2 New backend crate `frankenterm-renderer-metal` with CAMetalLayer + triple buffering
- 3.3 Backend abstraction layer so wgpu and Metal-direct coexist (feature-gated)
- 3.4 macOS-direct atlas integration (sub-epic 1's stable atlas, but Metal-side)
- 3.5 Latency benchmark: input-to-photon p95 <8ms target on M2/M3/M4
- 3.6 Wayland frame-callback batching fix (small bead; <500 LOC change)
- 3.7 Wayland resize regression test corpus
- 3.8 Cross-platform frame-pacing parity tests

## Acceptance
- macOS Metal-direct: input-to-photon p95 <8ms, p99 <12ms
- Wayland: resize no longer smears; frame-callback chain depth always ≤2
- Both backends share the renderer abstractions from sub-epic 1
- Differential bench publishes to ft-syqcz.5

## Why P2 not P1
Sub-epic 1 (foundation) and 2 (live-resize) ship value on every platform; this gives extra wins on macOS/Wayland specifically. Land it after sub-epic 1 to share its abstractions.
