title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.3.1] macOS Metal-direct backend skeleton + CAMetalLayer integration
description:
# macOS Metal-Direct Backend

## Background
Skip wgpu on macOS. Use CAMetalLayer directly with `presentDrawable:afterMinimumDuration:` for sub-vsync latency. Triple-buffered swap chain (`swap_chain_count = 3` per `legacy_ghostty/src/renderer/Metal.zig:37`) hides resize stalls.

## User-perceived value
- macOS users get sub-8ms input-to-photon latency (vs ~16-32ms on wgpu today)
- Resize gestures feel native — equal-or-better than ghostty
- Battery-life improves on M-series chips (Metal direct path is more efficient)

## Scope
- **In scope**: Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4)
- **Out of scope**: Intel Macs — wgpu backend remains the only option there
- **Rollback safety**: wgpu backend remains feature-gated for 1+ release after Metal-direct ships as default; runtime switch via `FT_MACOS_BACKEND=wgpu|metal-direct`

## AGENTS.md doctrine — `forbid(unsafe_code)` waiver
The frankenterm-core lib.rs has `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Metal-direct backend WILL need unsafe code (CAMetalLayer is Objective-C, FFI-driven via metal-rs). 

**Approach**: the new `frankenterm-renderer-metal` crate is a SEPARATE crate from frankenterm-core. It can declare `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` at its own crate level — frankenterm-core's `forbid` only applies to its own tree. The unsafe code is contained:
- Wrapped behind a safe Rust API
- Each unsafe block has a comment explaining the invariant
- Crate-level audit: every `unsafe` block reviewed during code review
- Loom proofs from BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8 do NOT cover this crate (Loom can't model FFI)
- Instead: integration tests run under address-sanitizer + thread-sanitizer in CI

This separation is justified by AGENTS.md "no file proliferation" doctrine: the new crate is "genuinely new functionality that makes zero sense to include in any existing file" — Metal-direct is a separate backend, not a refactor.

## GPU compatibility matrix
| Hardware | Status |
|---|---|
| M1 | Tier-1 supported (CI tested) |
| M1 Pro/Max/Ultra | Tier-1 supported |
| M2 / Pro / Max / Ultra | Tier-1 supported |
| M3 / Pro / Max | Tier-1 supported |
| M4 / Pro / Max | Tier-1 supported |
| Intel Mac | Out-of-scope (wgpu fallback) |
| ARM-based external GPU (eGPU) | Best-effort (not CI tested) |

macOS version baseline: 13.0+ (Ventura). Earlier versions get wgpu fallback automatically.

## Concrete actions
1. New crate `crates/frankenterm-renderer-metal` (cfg(target_os="macos") + cfg(target_arch="aarch64"))
2. CAMetalLayer setup, drawable acquire pattern, frame-pacing via `presentDrawable:afterMinimumDuration:`
3. Triple-buffered swap chain with `dispatch_semaphore_t` synchronization
4. Metal shader compilation (.metal source files); shaders mirror the wgpu WGSL shaders functionally (golden-test parity, see Tests below)
5. Backend abstraction trait so wgpu and Metal-direct coexist behind a feature flag
6. Atlas integration: the stable atlas from sub-task 1.1 must be storage-agnostic
7. Runtime backend switch via env var for emergency rollback
8. unsafe-block audit doc at `crates/frankenterm-renderer-metal/UNSAFE-AUDIT.md`

## Code targets
- New: `crates/frankenterm-renderer-metal/src/lib.rs` + shader sources
- Touch: `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/webgpu.rs` (wgpu now opt-in on Apple Silicon, default on Intel)
- Touch: `crates/frankenterm-gui/Cargo.toml` (cfg-gated dep)
- New: unsafe-audit doc

## Structured logging
- Init: log Metal device name, family, version
- Per-drawable acquire: log latency from request to grant
- Per-frame: log GPU command-buffer encode/commit/present timings
- Failure: log Metal validation errors with full stack

## Tests
All tests must emit structured JSON-line logs (per AGENTS.md frozen template).
- Unit: backend trait conformance (shared test suite runs against both wgpu and Metal-direct backends, asserts identical observable results)
- Visual: SSIM ≥0.999 vs wgpu backend on golden corpus from 1.6 (cross-link)
- Bench: input-to-photon p95 <8ms on M2/M3/M4 (compare to wgpu p95 baseline)
- Stress: resize-storm 50 events/sec, 60s — no frame drops, no GPU hangs
- Rollback test: env var swap mid-session works without crash
- Cx-cancel: drop the render task at any await point, no Metal resource leaks
- ASan: integration tests run under address sanitizer; zero leaks
- TSan: thread-sanitizer pass on the swap-chain semaphore code

## Risk + mitigation
This is a substantial new backend (~5-10k LOC). Risk: timeline slippage. Mitigation:
- Land sub-epic 1 + 2 first; they ship value on every platform without this
- Metal-direct opt-in via `--features metal-direct` initially; default later
- 1-release deprecation window with diagnostic warning before removing wgpu fallback (we keep wgpu, just downgrade default)

## Rollback runbook
- If Metal-direct regresses post-default: set `FT_MACOS_BACKEND=wgpu` to bypass at runtime
- Bug report includes: Metal device info, macOS version, scenario, structured logs
- Code rollback: revert the cargo feature flag default — wgpu code path is preserved

## Depends on
- 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5 (the rendering abstractions must be storage-agnostic first)

## Acceptance
- crate compiles + shaders work on M1+M2+M3+M4
- backend abstraction trait shipped
- p95 latency target hit (input-to-photon <8ms)
- Visual regression passes (SSIM ≥0.999 vs wgpu)
- Rollback path works (env var switch)
- ASan/TSan tests pass
- unsafe-audit doc reviewed
- Per-release competitor bench (BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.COMPETITOR) shows ≥ ghostty on macOS

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.3.2] Wayland frame-callback batching fix (window.rs:1146-1179)
description:
# Wayland Frame-Callback Batching Fix

## Background
Bug at `frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs:1146-1179`:
- Line 1153: if frame_callback pending, set `invalidated=true` and return early
- Line 1168: re-request frame_callback on EVERY paint attempt
- Effect: under fast resize, frame callbacks chain, compositor floods, paint stutter

## User-perceived value
- Wayland users get smooth resize on every compositor (mutter, kwin, sway, hyprland, wayfire, weston)
- Resize stops smearing
- Compositor doesn't get flooded by ft's misbehavior

## Reproducer
1. Run ft on Wayland (any major compositor)
2. Drag window edge rapidly back and forth for 5 seconds
3. Observe: text smears / lags behind cursor / phantom frames
4. Symptom: frame_callback chain depth grows beyond expected bound

| mutter (GNOME) | Tier-1 |
| kwin (KDE) | Tier-1 |
| sway | Tier-1 |
| hyprland | Tier-2 (best-effort) |
| wayfire | Tier-2 |
| weston | Reference (Wayland upstream) |

CI runs Tier-1 tests; Tier-2 manually verified.

## Concrete actions
1. Replace per-paint frame_callback re-request with: only re-request after a successful compose
2. Coalesce multiple invalidations into a single per-vsync paint
3. Add a chain-depth guard: if frame_callback chain ≥3, skip new requests until current callback fires
4. Audit similar bug at line 578 (XXX comment about combined configure/window_configure paths) — likely related; either fix or document explicitly

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4] Sub-epic 4 — Layered compositor + zellij uplift (floating panes, WASM plugins, stacked tabs)
description:
# Sub-epic 4: Layered Compositor + Zellij Uplift

## Idea origin
Idea #4 from idea-wizard ranking. Where ft can *exceed* zellij's value while keeping its swarm orchestration moat. Zellij users love floating panes + plugins; WezTerm doesn't have either.

## Architectural uplift: layered render pipeline
Steal from rio's sugar layer system (`legacy_rio/rio/sugarloaf/src/components/layer/mod.rs`):
- Layer 0: backdrop (image, blur, transparency)
- Layer 1: tiled grid (current pane layout)
- Layer 2: floating panes
- Layer 3: status tiles (zellij-style status bar)
- Layer 4: modal overlays (pickers, prompts)

Each layer has its own dirty tracking (cross-link sub-epic 1). Compositing is a final pass.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4.1] Layered compositor abstraction (rio sugar-layer pattern)
description:
# Layered Compositor Abstraction (Rio Sugar-Layer Pattern)

## Background
Layer the render pipeline (steal rio's `legacy_rio/rio/sugarloaf/src/components/layer/mod.rs`):
- Layer 0: backdrop (image, blur, transparency)
- Layer 1: tiled grid (current pane layout)
- Layer 2: floating panes
- Layer 3: status tiles
- Layer 4: modal overlays

Each layer has independent dirty tracking + independent rendering.

## User-perceived value
- Floating overlays + tiled panes + status bar + modal pickers all coexist without redrawing each other
- New rendering features (transparency, blur, plugin-rendered overlays) compose cleanly
- Render perf scales with layer dirty rate, not full-screen frequency

## Concrete actions
1. Define `Layer` trait + `LayerStack` abstraction in frankenterm-gui (or new frankenterm-compositor crate)
2. Layer trait API:
   ```rust
   trait Layer {
       fn render(&mut self, ctx: &LayerContext) -> Vec<DrawCmd>;
       fn dirty_rect(&self) -> Option<Rect>;
       fn z_order(&self) -> u8;
       fn opaque(&self) -> bool; // optimization: opaque layers below it can skip render
   }
   ```
3. Migrate current tiled grid rendering into Layer 1 of the new compositor
4. Layer-stack render pass: traverse layers bottom-up, composite at end
5. Per-layer dirty tracking (cross-link 1.2)
6. Per-layer atlas (or shared atlas with per-layer regions — TBD evaluation; default: shared)
7. Z-order management
8. Compositor render strategy: front-to-back early-Z if opaque; back-to-front for transparency

## DO NOT BREAK
- A11Y: each layer contributes to the platform accessibility tree (cross-link A11Y.1)
- Color-management: composition happens in linear space; final output gamut-converted (cross-link A11Y.3)
- Reduce-motion: layer transitions disabled (cross-link A11Y.5)

## Concrete code targets
- New: `crates/frankenterm-compositor/src/lib.rs` (or under frankenterm-gui)
- Touch: `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/paint.rs` to use layer-stack render path

## Structured logging
JSON-line per frame at tests/compositor/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- frame_idx, layer_count, layers_rendered, layers_skipped (clean), composite_time_ns

## Tests
- Unit: layer composition is associative + commutative for non-overlapping
- Unit: opaque-layer-below skip optimization (proptest)
- Visual: known WezTerm rendering reproduces under the new compositor (compare to pre-fix golden)
- Visual: floating-pane + tiled + status tile + modal compose correctly
- Bench: layer-stack overhead <0.5ms per frame (vs single pass)
- A11Y: accessibility tree includes layers from all 5 levels
- Color: P3 gamut preserved through composition

## Depends on
- 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5 (foundation must be in place)
- A11Y.1 (accessibility tree integration)
- A11Y.3 (color-management correctness)

## Acceptance
- Layer trait + stack shipped
- Current tiled grid migrated to Layer 1
- Bench passes overhead target
- Visual regression passes (cross-link 1.6)
- A11Y test passes
- Color test passes

## Why P2
Foundation for sub-epic 4 (floating panes, plugins, status tiles, stacked tabs). Land after sub-epic 1 ships.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4.2] Floating panes (zellij pattern) — tiled or floating, z-order, drag/resize
description:
# Floating Panes (Zellij Pattern) — Tiled or Floating, z-order, drag/resize

## Background
Steal `legacy_zellij/zellij-server/src/screen.rs:236-240`:
- `floating_layouts: Vec<FloatingPaneLayout>`
- Panes can be tiled OR floating
- Floating panes have z-order, drag handles, resize handles, snap-to-edge

## User-perceived value (swarm-native)
- Pin `ft status --health` overlay over an agent grid
- Floating workflow execution log next to the running agents
- Pop-out a pane during deep debugging without disrupting the tiled layout
- AI agents can request a floating overlay programmatically (e.g., from the robot mode)

## Accessibility — DO NOT BREAK
- **Keyboard-only navigation**: every drag/resize/move must have a keyboard equivalent (no mouse-required path)
  - Move: e.g., Cmd+Shift+Arrow when floating focused
  - Resize: e.g., Cmd+Ctrl+Arrow when floating focused
  - Pin/unpin: e.g., Cmd+Ctrl+P
  - Z-order: e.g., Cmd+Ctrl+] / [ for raise/lower
- **Focus order**: tab navigation must include floating panes in a consistent order (z-order, top to bottom)
- **Screen reader**: announce "floating, position X,Y, size W×H, z-order N" when focused
- **High-contrast mode**: floating-pane border is visible in high-contrast (don't rely on shadow alone)

## Drag/resize paths (mouse + keyboard)
1. Drag handle (title bar grab + drag) — mouse
2. Resize handles (8 hot zones — corners + edges) — mouse
3. Snap-to-edge (Aero-snap-style) on drag near screen edge — mouse OR keyboard via "snap-to-edge" command
4. Pin/unpin (toggle floating ↔ tiled) — keyboard + menu
5. Z-order: alt-click cycles among overlapping floating panes — also keyboard via raise/lower

## Concrete actions
1. Extend Pane abstraction with `position: PanePosition::Tiled | PanePosition::Floating(Rect)`
2. Wire into Layer 2 of the compositor (4.1)
3. Drag handle (mouse) + keyboard move command
4. Resize handles (mouse) + keyboard resize command
5. Snap-to-edge logic (mouse + keyboard)
6. Pin/unpin toggle (keyboard + context menu)
7. Z-order management (raise/lower commands; alt-click cycle)
8. Accessibility tree integration (screen-reader announcements)
9. Session-restore: floating-pane state preserved across save/restore

## Structured logging
- State transitions per floating pane: ts, pane_id, prev_state (Tiled/Floating(rect)), next_state, trigger
- Z-order changes: ts, pane_id, old_z, new_z
- Accessibility tree updates per state change

## Tests
- Unit: PanePosition state machine
- Property: drag-and-snap is idempotent (proptest on drag sequences)
- E2E: float a pane, drag it, snap it, unpin it; assert state preserved across save/restore (cross-link session_restore)
- **Accessibility**: keyboard-only test — float, move, resize, snap, pin/unpin, raise/lower, all via keyboard only; assert no mouse required
- **Screen reader**: announcement test on macOS VoiceOver, Linux Orca
- **High-contrast**: floating border visible in high-contrast color profile
- Bench: 10 floating panes simultaneously, no frame drops

## Cross-references
- 4.1 (compositor)
- session_restore module — floating state must persist across restart
- BR-RC-DOCTRINE.G15 (provenance) — new code is original ft, not wezterm-derived

## Acceptance
- Floating panes work via mouse AND keyboard
- Snap-to-edge works
- Pin/unpin works
- Session-restore preserves floating state
- Accessibility test passes (keyboard-only path complete)
- Screen-reader announcements correct
- High-contrast theme renders floating borders correctly

## Why P2
Strategic differentiation feature; depends on 4.1 compositor.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4.3] WASM plugin system (zellij pattern) using existing wasmtime dep
description:
# WASM Plugin System

## Background
Steal `legacy_zellij/zellij-server/src/screen.rs:296-506`. ft already has wasmtime as a workspace dep. Plugins render status bar tiles, side panels, modal pickers, custom workflow visualizers.

## Plugin API (proposed, WIT-described)
```wit
interface plugin {
    record state { ... }
    record event { ... }
    enum lifecycle-stage { init, reload, shutdown }
    enum layer { ... }

    render: func(state: state) -> layer
    handle-event: func(event: event)
    lifecycle: func(stage: lifecycle-stage)
    declare-capabilities: func() -> list<capability>
}
```

## Plugin capability enumeration (sandbox boundary)
Plugins must declare capabilities at load time; host enforces via policy.rs ActionKind gate.

**Permissive (no approval needed)**:
- `read-state`: read pane metadata (id, title, cwd, agent_type, state)
- `read-events`: read detection events stream
- `render-tile`: render into status bar tile slot
- `render-side-panel`: render into side panel slot
- `render-overlay`: render modal overlay (hover/click only, no input capture)
- `read-config`: read plugin's own config (sandboxed file under ~/.config/ft/plugins/<name>/)

**Restricted (requires user approval token)**:
- `read-pane-text`: read scrollback content (sensitive — secrets!)
- `send-input`: send text/keys to a pane
- `spawn-pane` / `close-pane`
- `launch-workflow`
- `network`: outbound HTTP (rate-limited by policy engine)

**Forbidden**:
- File-system access outside plugin sandbox dir
- Direct PTY access
- Direct mux-server IPC
- Spawn arbitrary subprocesses

## Sandboxing details (cross-link reality-check G11 threat model)
- WASI subset only
- Per-plugin resource limits: 50ms render budget, 16MB memory cap, 100MB disk cap (sandboxed)
- Audit chain: every plugin action logs through policy_audit_chain
- Plugin signatures (sigstore/cosign) for "verified plugins" badge in registry

## Concrete actions
1. Plugin API stable trait + WIT bindings
2. Host loader using wasmtime
3. Plugin discovery: ~/.config/ft/plugins/*.wasm
4. Lifecycle hooks
5. Capability declaration + gate enforcement (policy.rs ActionKind integration)
6. Plugin registry CLI: `ft plugin list/install/remove/update`
7. Plugin signing tool: `ft plugin sign <plugin.wasm>` for verified-plugin badge
8. ≥3 example plugins:
   - clock-tile (status bar clock)
   - fleet-status-tile (agent state breakdown)
   - git-branch-tile (current pane's git branch)

## Tests
All tests emit structured JSON-line logs.
- Unit: plugin lifecycle state machine
- Sandbox tests: malicious plugin attempts (file write, network, infinite loop, fork bomb) → caught and logged
- Capability gate test: restricted-capability use without approval token → policy denial
- Conformance: same plugin .wasm runs identically across all 3 platforms (golden artifact comparison)
- Resource-limit test: plugin exceeding 50ms render budget → kill + restart with backoff

## Depends on
- 4.1 (compositor), 4.4 (status tile API for the canonical use case)
- BR-RC-SAFETY-PROOFS.G11 (threat model informs sandbox design)

## Acceptance
- Plugin API documented + WIT spec stable (semver-pinned)
- Loader + sandbox shipped
- Capability subset enumerated and enforced
- ≥3 example plugins ship
- Plugin SDK + docs at docs/plugins/
- Plugin signing tool works
- Sandbox stress test passes (24h fuzz of malicious plugins)

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.4.4] Status bar with pluggable tiles (zellij pattern)
description:
# Status Bar with Pluggable Tiles (Zellij Pattern)

## Background
Zellij has a status bar with pluggable tiles. ft can expose the same with stronger AI-swarm relevance: agent count, fleet health, current rate-limit status, active workflow count, etc.

## User-perceived value
- At-a-glance fleet status without leaving the terminal
- Customizable per user (built-in + plugin-provided tiles)
- Useful for swarm operators (cost meter, agent state distribution)

## Tile API
```rust
trait StatusTile {
    fn render(&self, ctx: &TileContext) -> Vec<Cell>;
    fn on_click(&mut self, x: u16) -> Option<TileAction>;
    fn on_hover(&self, x: u16) -> Option<String>; // tooltip
    fn min_width(&self) -> u16;
    fn max_width(&self) -> u16;
    fn priority(&self) -> u8; // truncation order
    fn accessibility_label(&self) -> String; // for screen readers
}
```

## Built-in tiles (default config)
1. Mode indicator (normal/copy/visual)
2. Active session name
3. Pane count + active-pane indicator
4. Agent state breakdown (cc/cod/gmi green/yellow/red counts)
5. Fleet memory tier (Normal/Elevated/Critical/Emergency)
6. Cost meter (per agent / per session)
7. Network activity (PTY bytes/sec aggregate)
8. Clock (local + UTC)

## Tile API exposed to plugins (4.3 cross-link)
- Plugins implement StatusTile trait via WIT bindings
- Plugin tiles get same API surface as built-in tiles
- accessibility_label is REQUIRED — screen readers must announce tile content

## Tile layout
- Left/center/right with priority-based truncation
- Truncation: if total tile width > status bar width, drop tiles by priority order
- Truncation rules deterministic: documented at `docs/status-bar/truncation-rules.md`

## Accessibility — DO NOT BREAK
- Tiles announceable via screen reader (accessibility_label is REQUIRED)
- High-contrast: tile separators visible
- Reduce-motion: tile-content animations (e.g., spinning icons) disabled

## Concrete actions
1. Define StatusTile trait + TileContext + TileAction
2. Wire status tiles into Layer 3 of the compositor (4.1)
3. Built-in tiles (8 listed above)
4. Tile API exposed to plugins (4.3)
5. Tile layout: left/center/right with priority-based truncation
6. ft config exposes tile selection + ordering
7. Accessibility integration

## Structured logging
JSON-line at `tests/status-tiles/logs/<scenario>.jsonl`: ts, tiles_rendered (list), total_width, truncation_applied, hover_events, click_events

## Tests
- Unit: tile rendering produces predictable cell output
- E2E: built-in tiles update reactively to fleet state changes
- Visual: tile layout truncation works when window is narrow
- A11Y: screen reader announces every tile's accessibility_label
- Plugin-tile parity: plugin-provided tile has full API surface

## Depends on
- 4.1 (compositor)
- 4.3 (plugin system for plugin-provided tiles)
- A11Y.1 (accessibility tree integration)

## Acceptance
- StatusTile trait shipped
- ≥8 built-in tiles in default config
- Plugin-provided tiles work
- Truncation rules predictable + documented
- A11Y test passes

# Conditional-Redraw Predicate (Ghostty Pattern)

## Background
Current paint_impl runs the full pass every frame (`paint_pass()` at `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/paint.rs:38`). Ghostty's pattern (`legacy_ghostty/src/renderer/generic.zig:1440-1444`):
```zig
needs_redraw = size_changed || cells_rebuilt || hasAnimations() || sync
```

## User-perceived value
- Idle CPU usage drops from ~5% to <1% (60Hz × 16ms × no work = ~0% CPU)
- Battery savings on laptop with active ft-watch
- Heat reduction; fan stays quiet

## Predicate inputs (enumerate all causes of "we need to repaint")
1. Any dirty line in any pane (1.2)
2. Cursor blink due (within blink period)
3. Active animation (selection animation, dialog fade, modal transition)
4. Pending invalidate from input/scroll
5. Mouse hover state changed
6. Focus state changed
7. Window-size changed (resize handler)
8. Theme changed
9. Floating-pane moved (post-4.2)
10. Status-tile updated (post-4.4)
11. Plugin requested redraw (post-4.3)
12. Live-resize gesture in progress (force redraw at draft quality regardless)
13. Bell character (BEL) received

- Bell: BEL must trigger a redraw even if no cells dirty (bell visual indicator)

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.5.2] Per-frame budget allocator with deferred-cosmetic queue
description:
# Per-Frame Budget Allocator with Deferred-Cosmetic Queue

## Background
Each frame gets a 16.67ms budget (60Hz) or 8.33ms (120Hz). When work exceeds budget, defer cosmetic operations to next frame. Self-recovers from heavy bursts.

## User-perceived value
- Heavy bursts of agent output never cause UI lag
- Input latency stays predictable under load
- Frame-time variance drops; smoother feel

## Algorithm
```
budget = 1.0 / refresh_rate  // seconds
spent = 0
priority_order = [
   Required: dirty quad rebuild,
   Required: cursor + selection,
   Cosmetic: ligatures,
   Cosmetic: subpixel AA,
   Cosmetic: decorations,
   Cosmetic: animations,
]
for op in priority_order:
   if spent > budget * 0.9: defer to next frame
   else: spent += execute(op)
```

## Cosmetic-queue overflow protection (failure mode)
Without backpressure, the deferred-cosmetic queue can grow unboundedly under sustained burst load. Failure modes:
1. **Memory growth**: queue grows → RAM usage climbs → OOM kill
2. **Quality regression**: a cell deferred for 1000 frames is effectively "rendered without ligatures forever"
3. **Recovery**: when burst ends, the queue must drain in finite time

Protections:
1. Queue capacity cap: 4 frames worth of cosmetic ops (i.e., ~4 × 16ms budget); excess oldest entries dropped
2. Drop-oldest with telemetry: log when drop happens (`cosmetic_dropped_count`)
3. Bulk-drain when budget surplus: if a frame finishes ≤50% budget, drain extra cosmetic ops
4. User-visible signal: `ft doctor` reports cosmetic-queue depth + drop rate

## DO NOT BREAK accessibility
- Required ops (dirty quad rebuild, cursor) are NEVER deferred — only cosmetic
- Animations may be deferred but NOT skipped if prefers-reduced-motion is OFF
- See A11Y.5 (preferences) for cross-link

## Concrete actions
1. Implement `FrameBudget` in `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/frame_budget.rs`
2. Wire into paint_impl
3. Per-op timing instrumentation
4. Deferred queue persists across frames
5. Queue capacity cap with drop-oldest
6. Telemetry: cosmetic_queue_depth, cosmetic_dropped_count, deferrals_per_frame, bulk_drain_count
7. ft doctor surface

## Structured logging
JSON-line per frame: ts_ns, budget_ms, spent_ms, deferrals, drops, queue_depth, ops_executed (list of op_kind + duration_ns)

## Tests
- Unit: budget overrun → cosmetic ops deferred (proptest)
- Unit: queue cap → drop-oldest works
- Unit: bulk-drain works when budget surplus
- E2E: 1MB/s output stream into 50 panes — assert input latency p95 <50ms
- E2E: sustained heavy burst (5 minutes) — queue depth stays bounded; drop rate logged
- Bench: budget tracking overhead <1% of frame time
- A11Y: animation respects prefers-reduced-motion (cross-link A11Y.5)

## Depends on
- 5.1 (predicate)
- A11Y.5 (preferences)

## Acceptance
- Budget allocator shipped
- Queue cap + drop-oldest works
- Heavy-burst test passes input-latency target
- Per-op timing exposed for diagnostics
- ft doctor reports queue state
- Sustained-burst test (5 min) passes without OOM
- A11Y.5 preference plumbing honored

## Why P1
Compounds with sub-epic 1; load-bearing for the heavy-burst story.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.5.3] Idle frame-rate dropdown — 60Hz → 5Hz when nothing happens for >500ms
description:
# Idle Frame-Rate Dropdown — 60Hz → 5Hz When Idle

## Background
When ft is idle (no animations, no input, no PTY output for >500ms), drop frame rate from refresh_rate to 5Hz (or pause entirely). Massive battery savings.

## User-perceived value
- 24-hour battery life on M2 MacBook for users running ft + 50 panes (current ~12 hours)
- Laptop fan stays quiet during long agent-watch sessions
- No perceived performance loss — wake-up is sub-frame

## Idle detection
1. Idle detector tracks last-event timestamp per category (input, PTY, animation, focus)
2. Threshold-based mode switch:
   - 0-100ms: full rate (60-120 Hz)
   - 100-500ms: half rate (30-60 Hz)
   - 500ms-5s: 5 Hz (mostly cursor blink)
   - >5s: paused, wake on event

## DO NOT BREAK accessibility / assistive tech
- **Screen-reader-active detection**: if VoiceOver / Orca / Narrator is announcing, do NOT drop frame rate. Assistive tech sometimes drives screen updates that the visual side doesn't see.
- Detection: macOS NSAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning, Linux AT-SPI bus presence, Windows ScreenReaderRunning
- Fallback: if detection unreliable, leave a config flag `idle_dropdown_disabled = true` for users to opt out

## DO NOT BREAK other interactions
- Mouse hover state changes wake immediately
- Mouse-tracking mode (program is asking for mouse events) wakes immediately
- Bell character (BEL) wakes immediately
- Window focus change wakes immediately

## Wake-up plumbing
Any event resumes full rate immediately:
- PTY data
- Mouse move/click
- Keyboard input
- Window focus
- IPC from sibling ft processes
- Animation tick due

Wake-up latency target: <16ms from event to first painted frame at full quality.

## Concrete actions
1. Idle detector module in `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/idle_detector.rs`
2. Per-platform assistive-tech detection
3. Threshold-based mode-switch state machine
4. Wake-up event channel (asupersync mpsc per AGENTS.md doctrine)
5. Config flag for opt-out
6. ft doctor reports current idle state for debugging
7. Wake-up latency benchmark

## Structured logging
- State transitions: ts_ns, prev_state, next_state, trigger_event_kind
- Wake-up: ts_ns_event_received, ts_ns_first_paint, latency_ms
- Per-second summary in idle: avg_fps, gpu_pct

## Tests
- E2E: 60-second idle test on M2 MacBook, measure GPU activity → near-zero in idle phase
- E2E: assistive-tech-active test — VoiceOver running, ft must NOT enter idle mode
- Battery test: 24-hour idle test with ft watching 50 panes — laptop should not exceed 5% battery drain on a healthy battery
- Wake-up latency: <16ms p99 from event to first painted frame
- Mouse-tracking-active test: program asking for mouse events, ft does NOT enter idle (mouse events still observable)
- Bell-during-idle test: BEL wakes ft immediately

## Depends on
- 5.1 (predicate)
- 5.2 (budget allocator)

## Acceptance
- Idle detector shipped
- Assistive-tech opt-out works (auto-detected + config flag)
- Battery test passes 24h target
- Wake-up latency target hit (<16ms p99)
- Bell + mouse-tracking + focus-change all wake immediately
- Structured logging exposed via ft doctor

Big QoL improvement; depends on 5.1 + 5.2 foundation; not blocking other work.

- 6.7 Tearing-free immediate-mode present (X11 + Wayland tearing-control protocol) for input-latency-critical frames
- 6.8 Compute-shader text shaping — shape glyph runs on GPU compute shader during heavy output bursts
- 6.9 Sugar-layer compositor for transparency/blur/background images (foundation for sub-epic 4's Layer 0)

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.1] Instanced quad rendering — cut vertex bandwidth ~75%
description:
# Instanced Quad Rendering — Cut Vertex Bandwidth ~75%

## Background
Current per-cell 4-vertex batches at `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/quad.rs:10-16`. Modern GPU best practice: one indexed quad with per-cell instance buffer (rio + alacritty both do this).

## User-perceived value
- Lower GPU bandwidth → cooler chip, longer battery life
- Lower frame time → headroom for higher refresh rates (120Hz+)
- More frames per second on integrated GPUs

## Concrete actions
1. Replace per-cell vertex buffer with: 1 quad index buffer + 1 instance buffer of `CellInstance` records
2. CellInstance fields: `position: vec2`, `glyph_id: u32`, `fg_color: u32`, `bg_color: u32`, `attributes: u8` (italic, bold, underline, etc.), `cursor_flags: u8`
3. Vertex shader reads instance buffer, computes screen-space position from instance ID
4. Fragment shader unchanged (still samples atlas)
5. Atlas integration: glyph_id is an index into the stable atlas (cross-link 1.1)
6. Telemetry: instance_count_per_frame, vertex_bandwidth_gbps

## Bench target
- Vertex bandwidth reduction: ~75% (4 verts/cell → 1 instance/cell)
- Frame time reduction: visible on 200-pane fleets

## AGENTS.md doctrine reminder
- forbid(unsafe_code); use safe wgpu API
- Edit quad.rs in place

## Structured logging
JSON-line per frame at tests/instanced/logs/<scenario>.jsonl:
- frame_idx, instance_count, bandwidth_bytes_per_frame, frame_time_ns

## Tests
- Unit: instance-data-record encoding correctness (proptest)
- Visual: SSIM ≥0.999 vs current per-cell rendering on golden corpus
- Bench: vertex bandwidth measurement; assert ≥75% reduction
- Bench: frame time on 200-pane fleet; visible improvement
- Regression: edge cases (empty cells, wide cells, cursor cells, selection cells)

## Depends on
- 1.1 (stable atlas — instance buffer references atlas indices)
- 1.3 (elastic instance buffer — this IS the buffer)
- 1.5 (per-line quad cache — this is what populates the instance buffer)

## Acceptance
- Instanced rendering shipped
- Bench shows bandwidth reduction
- Visual regression passes (cross-link 1.6)
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit 22a4df407 — crates/frankenterm-core/src/instanced_cell.rs.

Pure-logic substrate shipped:

1. CellInstance — 32-byte #[repr(C)] per-cell record (compile-time-asserted size). Carries row/col (u16), glyph_id (u32), fg_color/bg_color (RGBA8 u32), attributes (u8), cursor_flags (u8), and a 4-byte extra slot for IME caret offset / ligature group id.

2. CellAttributes + CursorFlags — packed u8 bitflags. CellAttributes uses all 8 bits (italic / bold / underline / strikethrough / dim / reverse / blink / conceal); disjoint-bits invariant asserted. CursorFlags uses bits 0-3 (cursor-visible / cursor-blinking / insert-mode / selection); bits 4-7 reserved for future IME / search-highlight / mouse-hover without wire-format change.

3. pack_color_rgba8 / unpack_color_rgba8 — u32 ↔ [f32; 4] round-trip; bounded 1/255 quantisation error; idempotent re-pack tested.

4. Bandwidth math — legacy_bytes_per_cell = 272 (computed from quad.rs Vertex layout: 2+2+4+4+3+1+1 = 17 f32 fields = 68 bytes × 4 verts), instance_bytes_per_cell = 32, bandwidth_savings_pct ≈ 88%. The ≥75% headline target is asserted as a hard floor so a future regression in either CellInstance or quad.rs::Vertex fails the test.

5. InstanceBufferConfig + decide_buffer_action — per-frame capacity policy mirroring the ElasticBuffer pattern. Submit / Grow (with grow_factor + max_capacity clamp + meet-the-request floor) / Shrink (after consecutive_low_frames threshold, floored at min_capacity AND request) / Split (request > max_capacity). fill_pct counter for the integration layer's running tally.

40 inline tests passing: full attribute-flag matrix, cursor reserved-bits, color clamp + idempotent round-trip, CellInstance 32-byte invariant + extra-field independence + 256-bit attr round-trip, bandwidth math vs the actual quad.rs Vertex layout, all InstanceBufferConfig decision branches, and 3 cross-cut scenarios (200-pane fleet bench sanity, grow-then-shrink cycle, split actionable chunk size).

Continuation tracked in ft-ady7w: wgpu::VertexBufferLayout + glium implement_vertex! macro wiring (gui crate), vertex shader rewrite that derives screen-space corners from instance ID + cell metrics, atlas integration mapping glyph_id to TextureRect, capacity policy dispatcher in RenderState, telemetry counters (instance_count_per_frame, vertex_bandwidth_gbps), SSIM ≥0.999 regression test, vertex-bandwidth bench asserting ≥75% reduction, structured logs, and the staged migration path (feature flag → default-on → legacy removal).

User-visible value of substrate: the encoding correctness, attribute/cursor disjoint-bits invariants, color round-trip, bandwidth math, and capacity policy decisions are all correctness-tested at the data-structure layer, eliminating the most error-prone surface (data layout choices and capacity hysteresis) before the integration layer touches a single GPU API.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.5] End-of-frame cell consistency CRC (debug mode) — catch artifacts at CI time
description:
# End-of-Frame Cell Consistency CRC (Debug Mode)

## Background
The bug class WezTerm shipped for years (resize artifacts, scroll glitches, cell-color desync) is detectable via a cheap end-of-frame hash over the rendered cell grid. Debug-mode-only; zero production overhead.

## User-perceived value
- Future agents touching the renderer cannot ship cell-grid corruption silently
- CI catches regressions before they reach users
- The "WezTerm has cell artifacts" complaint becomes "ft does not have cell artifacts" — measurable

## Concrete actions
1. Add `--features debug-cell-crc` to frankenterm-gui
2. After each frame, compute fast hash (xxhash or FNV-1a) over (visible_cell_grid_state)
3. Compare to expected hash computed from terminal model state
4. If mismatch: dump both states to `~/.local/share/ft/debug/cell-mismatch-<timestamp>.json`
5. CI runs the debug feature on the visual regression corpus (1.6) — any mismatch fails CI

## Hash collision considerations
- xxhash 64-bit for the rendered grid (collision rate ≈ 2^-64 per frame)
- For added safety in debug mode: dual-hash (xxhash + crc32) — false-negative probability vanishes
- For pristine debug scrutiny: full diff option (--features debug-cell-diff) that compares the entire grid byte-by-byte

## DO NOT BREAK
- Production builds: zero overhead (feature-gated)
- A11Y tree: not affected by this bead

## Structured logging
JSON-line per frame in debug builds at `~/.local/share/ft/debug/cell-crc-<timestamp>.jsonl`:
- frame_idx, expected_hash, actual_hash, match (bool), grid_size

Failure dump:
- expected_grid (full state)
- actual_grid (full state)
- diff_cells (list of (row, col, expected, actual))
- repro_seed (if from fuzz)

## Tests
- Unit: hash is deterministic + identical-input → identical-hash
- Unit: known-mismatch reproducer → CRC catches it
- Regression: known historical WezTerm artifacts reproduce → mismatch caught
- CI integration: debug feature runs on the visual regression corpus from 1.6
- Adversarial fuzz integration: 24h fuzz from 1.6 also runs CRC; any mismatch fails
- Per-release attestation entry: zero CRC mismatches on default branch

## Depends on
- 1.6 (visual regression harness — CI integration point)

## Acceptance
- Debug feature shipped
- CI integration catches injected artifacts
- Cross-link to ft-ombfl + ft-35yac.1.2 documented
- Per-release attestation entry

## Why P2
Compounds with 1.6; structurally unshippable bugs.
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit 8eaa513da — crates/frankenterm-core/src/cell_consistency_crc.rs.

Pure-logic substrate shipped:

1. CellRecord — 16-byte big-endian-encoded row/col/glyph_id/fg/bg record. BE chosen so cross-platform repro files are byte-identical regardless of host endianness. Composes with CellInstance from ft-mpc9b.6.1.

2. fnv1a_64 + crc32_ieee — two independent hash functions, no dependencies. CRC32 verified against industry test vectors ('123456789' = 0xcbf43926, quick-brown-fox = 0x414fa339).

3. CellGridHash { fnv: u64, crc: u32 } — dual-hash payload; both halves must equal. Combined false-positive probability ≈ 2^-96.

4. hash_cell_grid — single-pass over the data, FNV+CRC update simultaneously per byte (verified equivalent to separate calls).

5. MismatchClass (Match / BothDiffer / OnlyFnvDiffers / OnlyCrcDiffers) — telemetry routing. Single-half mismatches are statistically expected at <2^-32 per frame and shouldn't fail CI on their own; logged with rare-event marker so operator triage can decide whether to investigate.

6. classify_mismatch + diff_grids (with GridSizeMismatch err for length mismatch).

7. MismatchPolicy + MismatchAction — operator-tunable. Default = LogOnly (single-half) + DumpAndContinue (BothDiffer); ci_strict() = Fail (BothDiffer) + DumpAndContinue (single-half).

8. CellCrcStats — lifetime counters + is_clean predicate (per-release attestation entry asserts is_clean on default branch).

37 inline tests passing: CellRecord BE-encoding layout, FNV-1a known vectors + avalanche, CRC32 industry test vectors, hash determinism + sensitivity to single-cell change + position swap, hash_cell_grid single-pass = separate-call equivalence, classify_mismatch full matrix, diff_grids identical / single-change / multi-change / size-mismatch-err, MismatchPolicy default vs ci_strict + action_for routing, CellCrcStats record-per-class + is_clean invariant + mixed-run, plus 3 cross-cut scenarios (clean frame full pipeline / resize artifact caught with diff + CI Fail / 24h fuzz lane assertion).

Continuation tracked in ft-6t1vy: debug-cell-crc / debug-cell-diff / fail-on-cell-mismatch feature flags in frankenterm-gui, per-frame paint.rs instrumentation (post-Present hash compare + dispatch via MismatchPolicy::action_for), mismatch dump file format + path (~/.local/share/ft/debug/cell-mismatch-<ts>.json), CI hookup running debug feature on visual-regression corpus (ft-n0hpo / 1.6), 24h adversarial fuzz integration, structured JSON-line schema cross-link ft-ombfl + ft-35yac.1.2, per-release attestation asserting is_clean.

User-visible value of substrate: the dual-hash with single-half-rare-event classification means the integration layer can't accidentally false-positive itself into red CI on the statistically expected (~2^-32) collision events; the policy table's ci_strict variant draws a bright line between 'real corruption that must redden CI' and 'rare-but-statistically-expected single-hash collision logged for triage'.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.6] Latency-pinned input loop — input → PTY <1ms via dedicated low-latency thread
description:
# Latency-Pinned Input Loop

## Background
Decouple input → PTY write from render thread. Steal alacritty/ghostty pattern: dedicated low-latency input handler.

## Per AGENTS.md async runtime doctrine
**Use asupersync, NOT raw tokio or std::thread.** The latency-pinned input loop runs in an asupersync task with its own runtime priority class. The Cx-aware primitives (mpsc, watch) carry input events to the render thread.

## Concrete actions
1. Create dedicated input-handler asupersync task in frankenterm-gui, spawned via runtime_async::spawn
2. Set OS-level thread scheduling priority on the underlying carrier thread:
   - SCHED_FIFO on Linux (with sane priority, not -20)
   - QoS user-interactive on macOS (via dispatch_set_qos_class_self)
   - REALTIME_PRIORITY_CLASS sparingly on Windows
3. Input event loop: read OS input → translate → write to PTY in a single tight async loop
4. Render thread observes PTY output via the existing capture pipeline
5. Bench: input → PTY write latency p99 <1ms

## Concrete code targets
- `frankenterm/window/src/os/macos/window.rs` — input event handler currently dispatches synchronously
- `frankenterm/window/src/os/wayland/window.rs` — equivalent
- `frankenterm/window/src/os/x11/window.rs` — equivalent
- New: `crates/frankenterm-gui/src/input_loop.rs`

## Tests
- Bench: synthetic input flood, measure input → PTY p50/p95/p99
- E2E: typing burst doesn't drop characters under heavy renderer load
- Stress test: 1000 keystrokes/sec for 60s, assert zero drops
- Cx-cancel test: dropping the input task at any await point cleans up correctly (LabRuntime virtual time)

## Cross-link
- BR-RC-RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.G14 (Cx propagation) — input loop is a high-priority Cx-threaded path
- BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2 (Loom proofs) — Loom must verify the input→render mpsc primitive

## Acceptance
- Input task shipped via runtime_async::spawn (no raw tokio)
- Per-platform priority hint applied
- Bench passes p99 <1ms
- No keystroke drops under load
- Cx cancellation test passes

## Why P2
Compounds with sub-epics 1+5; not blocking but big input-feel improvement.
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit be9050165 — crates/frankenterm-core/src/input_priority.rs.

Pure-logic OS scheduling-priority policy shipped:

1. InputPriorityClass (LowLatency / Normal) + Platform (Linux / MacOs / Windows / Other) — request and runtime context.

2. OsPriorityHint enum — per-platform descriptor the integration layer translates to libc / Mach / Win32 calls. Linux uses SCHED_FIFO with safe priority 30 (range 1..=49 to avoid kthread collision at >=50). macOS uses UserInteractive QoS via dispatch_set_qos_class_self. Windows uses TimeCritical inside HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS (NOT REALTIME, per the kernel-driver-lockout caveat noted in the bead).

3. negotiate_priority — pure-logic table lookup, side-effect-free.

4. Three safety clamps: safe_sched_fifo_priority (0→1, >49→49, with clamp flag), safe_qos_class (Default/Utility/Background → UserInteractive), safe_windows_thread_priority (Normal → TimeCritical). Used when an operator-tuned priority comes from a config file.

5. PriorityFallbackReason (NormalRequested / UnsupportedPlatform / OsCallRejected) — telemetry routing.

6. PriorityOutcomeStats — lifetime counters (grants_total, fallback_unsupported_platform_total, fallback_os_call_rejected_total, normal_requests_total, clamps_engaged_total) + is_healthy predicate (any grant + zero rejections).

7. record_priority_outcome — composer feeding stats from a negotiation + integration apply result.

28 inline tests passing: full negotiation matrix (4 platforms x 2 classes), all sched_fifo clamp paths, all QoS clamp paths, all Windows clamps, OsPriorityHint::is_default, stats default-empty + record_grant running-total + per-reason fallback routing + is_healthy invariant, record_priority_outcome composition (grant / OS-rejected / Normal / Unsupported), and 3 startup scenarios (macOS UserInteractive grant + healthy, Linux EPERM fallback unhealthy, unsupported platform).

Companion to the existing input-latency *measurement* framework at input_latency.rs (ft-1memj.25, 765 LOC) — that module measures stage latencies; this module sets the OS-priority policy that lets the input task hit those budgets.

Continuation tracked in ft-96zes: asupersync input task at frankenterm-gui/src/input_loop.rs (runtime_async::spawn, NOT raw tokio per AGENTS.md), per-OS priority application via the substrate's OsPriorityHint dispatch (Linux pthread_setschedparam, macOS dispatch_set_qos_class_self, Windows SetThreadPriority), per-platform window-crate hook updates (macos/wayland/x11), bench harness (1000 keystrokes/sec for 60s; p99 <1ms via existing input_latency::InputLatencyCollector), Cx-cancel test (LabRuntime virtual time, drop-at-every-await), 200-pane stress test (zero keystroke drops), ft doctor surface for PriorityOutcomeStats, Loom mpsc proof at tests/loom_input_render_mpsc.rs (BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2).

User-visible value of substrate: the per-platform safety clamps (sched_fifo<=49, never REALTIME on Windows, QoS clamped to UserInteractive) prevent the most catastrophic foot-guns at the type level — a future operator config that asks for SCHED_FIFO=99 gets clamped to 49 with a logged 'clamp engaged' flag rather than deadlocking the host's scheduler. The is_healthy predicate gives ft doctor a one-line verdict on whether the latency target is achievable on the running host.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.2] SDF (signed distance field) glyph atlas — single texture serves all sizes
description:
# SDF Glyph Atlas

## Background
Signed-distance-field rendering: one texture serves all glyph sizes. Eliminates atlas rebuild on DPI/scale changes (compounds with sub-task 1.1's stable atlas).

## Risk
Small-text rendering quality. SDF can produce blurry text at <14px without careful tuning.

## Concrete actions
1. Spike: implement SDF rendering for a single glyph; visually compare to bitmap at 12-18px sizes
2. Decision: ship if quality is acceptable at 14px+; defer if not
3. If shipping: SDF generation in glyphcache.rs (uses fontdue or similar SDF rasterizer)
4. WGSL/Metal shader for SDF rendering with anti-aliasing
5. Hybrid path: bitmap glyphs at <14px, SDF at ≥14px

## Tests
- Visual: SDF vs bitmap at sizes 10/12/14/16/18/24/32 — manual review checklist
- Bench: SDF render time per glyph vs bitmap path
- Memory: total atlas VRAM saved (single SDF texture vs N bitmap textures for N sizes)

## Acceptance
- Spike report (decision artifact) at `docs/perf/sdf-evaluation.md`
- If shipping: visual regression passes; per-pixel SSIM ≥0.97 vs bitmap golden

## Why P3
Research-grade. Don't commit until spike validates.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.4-cell-delta] Differential cell streaming to GPU — push only diffed cells
description:
# Differential Cell Streaming

## Background
Push only diffed cells per frame as `(row, col, glyph_id, fg, bg, attrs)` deltas to GPU instance buffer. Steady-state bandwidth drops 10-100×.

## Concrete actions
1. Per-frame: walk dirty lines (1.2), compute changed-cell list
2. Append cell-delta records to a ring buffer in the instance buffer
3. Vertex shader reads ring; old cells preserved across frames
4. Periodic compaction: every N frames, full rewrite to avoid ring fragmentation

## Tests
- Bench: 1MB/s output, 50 panes — bandwidth-to-GPU measurement
- Property: full-rewrite + delta-stream produce identical visible output

## Depends on
- 1.1, 1.2, 1.5 (full foundation)
- 6.1 (instanced rendering — delta stream IS instanced)

## Acceptance
- Delta streaming shipped
- Bench shows expected bandwidth reduction
- Visual regression passes

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.6.7] Tearing-free immediate-mode present (X11 + Wayland tearing-control)
description:
# Tearing-Free Immediate-Mode Present

## Background
Where compositor allows, use immediate present for input-latency-critical frames. Sub-vsync latency.

## Per-platform
- X11: `_NET_WM_BYPASS_COMPOSITOR` hint; Present extension's allow_tearing flag
- Wayland: tearing-control protocol (proposed standard)
- macOS: not supported (CAMetalLayer + Metal handle this differently)

## Concrete actions
1. Detect compositor support via doctor checks
2. Per-frame decision: "is this a latency-critical frame?" (input event in last 16ms → yes)
3. If yes + supported: use immediate present
4. Else: use vsync present
5. Tearing artifacts only on input frames; user-perceived latency drops to ~ms-level

## Tests
- Bench: input-to-photon p99 with vs without tearing-free mode
- Visual: assert no tearing on non-input frames (vsync still applies)
- Compatibility: doctor reports compositor support correctly

## Acceptance
- Tearing-free path shipped on supported compositors
- Doctor surface accurate
- p99 input latency improvement measurable

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.COMPETITOR] Competitor delta proof — ft vs WezTerm/Ghostty/Rio published per release
description:
# Competitor Delta Proof — ft vs WezTerm/Ghostty/Rio

## Background
Epic acceptance says "ft ≥ ghostty on resize-FPS metric." Without published per-release proof, that's a claim, not a fact.

## User-perceived value
- Users can verify ft is competitive with ghostty/rio for their workload
- Operators choosing a terminal can compare apples-to-apples
- AI agents calling ft can verify the latency budget

## Concrete actions
1. Hook into BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.5 (existing competitor matrix bead)
2. Per release, run the resize-storm benchmark on:
   - ft (current build)
   - WezTerm (head)
   - Ghostty (latest tagged)
   - Rio (latest tagged)
3. Workload: 50-pane grid, 5s continuous resize gesture, capture: FPS p50/p95/p99, frame-time distribution, GPU memory peak, CPU peak
4. Produce `docs/perf/competitor-resize-<version>.json` per release
5. Same hardware baseline as G3.5 (specific GitHub Actions runner SKU + specific local mac/Linux box)
6. Failure mode: if ft is ≥10% slower than ghostty on any p95 metric for 2 consecutive releases, file a P1 regression bead automatically

## Hardware baseline (declared once, used per release)
- Local macOS: M2 MacBook Pro (16GB unified memory, 10-core)
- Local Linux: Framework 13 (i7-1370P, 32GB RAM, integrated graphics — common laptop class)
- Local Linux: Threadripper workstation (24-core, RTX 4070 — high-end class)
- CI: GitHub Actions runner spec documented in benchmark file

## Workload definition (deterministic, reproducible)
1. Spawn 50 panes via tmux (consistent multiplexer across all 4 terminals)
2. Each pane runs `cat /usr/share/dict/words` in a loop (consistent input shape)
3. Resize gesture: simulated via X11/Wayland mouse synthesis (xdotool/wayland-utils) for 5 seconds
4. Capture: ftrace (Linux) / Instruments (macOS) for frame-by-frame timing

## Differential bench harness
- Each terminal launched via shell script with consistent environment (PATH, locale, color profile)
- Timing measured by an external observer (tracker process), not the terminal itself (avoids self-bias)
- Output: machine-readable JSON per terminal per metric

## Structured logging
JSON-line at docs/perf/competitor-resize-<version>.json:
- terminal, version, hardware, workload_hash, fps_p50/p95/p99, frame_time_ms_distribution, gpu_mem_peak_mb, cpu_peak_pct
- Provenance: bench-harness commit, terminal binaries' SHA256

## Tests
- Reproducibility: re-running the bench produces results within ±5% (validate harness fairness)
- Hardware baseline reachable: CI / local box accessible to maintainer
- Per-release run completes in <30 minutes

## Acceptance
- Per-release competitor artifact published
- Automated regression detection wired
- README "How ft Compares" links to the artifact
- Workload definition checked into repo at scripts/bench/competitor-resize.sh

## Cross-link
- BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.5 (this is the implementation arm of that bead)
- BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.SLO (SLO doc embeds the comparison)

## Depends on
- BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.5 must define the matrix infrastructure first
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit 07df024f8 — crates/frankenterm-core/src/competitor_delta.rs.

Pure-logic substrate shipped:

1. Competitor (Ft / WezTerm / Ghostty / Rio) with label() and all() iter helper — bead's reference set.

2. Metric (FpsP50/P95/P99 + FrameTimeP95Ms + GpuMemoryPeakMb + CpuPeakPct) with kind() classifier returning HigherIsBetter or LowerIsBetter per axis. The kind drives the sign of delta_pct so the regression detector doesn't need per-metric special cases.

3. delta_pct sign-correct comparator: positive means ft is *better*, negative means *worse*, regardless of metric kind. Math splits on MetricKind. Returns None on div-by-zero or non-finite — defensive.

4. MAX_REGRESSION_PCT = -10.0 exactly matches the bead's '≥10% slower' threshold.

5. classify_regression: Clean when delta > -10% / Regressed when ≤ -10% / Clean defensively when delta is None (bench bug, not code regression).

6. RegressionState 3-state machine (Clean / SingleRegression / ConsecutiveRegression) with should_file_p1 predicate. observe() advances per the bead's '2 consecutive releases' rule; Clean observation resets from any state.

7. CompetitorMatrix registry with insert (overwrites existing key) / get / ft_vs (computes delta against any competitor on any metric, returns None when either sample missing).

8. HardwareBaseline (M2MacBookPro16Gb / FrameworkLaptop13 / ThreadripperRtx4070 / GithubActionsRunner) per the bead's table.

9. CompetitorMatrixSnapshot per-release output with classify_all walking 6 metrics × 3 non-ft competitors = 18 classifications.

31 inline tests passing: Competitor / Metric labels match bead, kind classification (3 HigherIsBetter + 3 LowerIsBetter), delta_pct sign correctness (4 directions), div-by-zero / non-finite return None, classify_regression at-or-below threshold + inside threshold + None-defaults-Clean, RegressionState lifecycle (default Clean / Clean→Single→Consecutive walk / Clean reset from Single / Clean reset from Consecutive / Consecutive stays until Clean), CompetitorMatrix insert/get/overwrite/ft_vs/None-on-missing, classify_all emits 18 classes per snapshot + finds single regression correctly, HardwareBaseline labels match bead, plus 3 cross-cut scenarios (bead's exact -10% threshold = Regressed, two-release-pipeline files P1, one-release-then-recovery does not).

Continuation tracked in ft-t101b: actual bench harness (spawn 4 terminals via shell script, xdotool/wayland-utils/cliclick resize storm, ftrace/Instruments capture), per-release GitHub Actions runner, 3 local-baseline lanes (M2 MacBook / Framework / Threadripper), JSON output writer at docs/perf/competitor-resize-<version>.json, auto-file-P1-regression-bead-on-2-consecutive-regressions wiring (substrate's RegressionState::ConsecutiveRegression variant is the policy-decision payload; integration's release script reads it and runs br create), cross-link to BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.5 baseline data.

User-visible value of substrate: the sign-correct delta_pct means a future agent reading the matrix can't accidentally invert the comparison for LowerIsBetter metrics — frame-time deltas come out with the same sign convention as FPS deltas, so 'ft is +5%' always means 'ft is better' regardless of metric kind. The 2-consecutive-regression state machine prevents single-release noise from filing spurious P1 beads — only sustained regression triggers the alarm, matching the bead's exact policy. The Clean-resets-from-any-state rule means a one-time blip doesn't leave the detector stuck in alarm state across releases.

title: [BR-TERM-EMULATOR-UPLIFT.ROLLOUT] Feature-flag rollout strategy + deprecation timeline
description:
# Feature-Flag Rollout Strategy + Deprecation Timeline

## Background
Each large renderer change has rollout/regression risk. Defining an explicit strategy upfront prevents shipping surprises.

## Per-feature rollout phases
1. **Hidden**: built but disabled by default; enable via `--features <name>` and `FT_RENDERER_<name>=1`
2. **Opt-in**: documented; default off; users can opt in via config
3. **Default**: shipped as default; legacy path still compilable via flag for emergency rollback
4. **Cleanup**: legacy path deleted (AGENTS.md "no backwards compatibility" doctrine — done aggressively after 1 release of being default)

## Version markers (absolute, not abstract)
Per `git log --oneline | head -1` ft is at v0.1.0-pre. The mapping below uses milestones from the next-release cycle.

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **m0** | First release including any of the SE1 foundation work (≈ v0.2.0) |
| **m1** | First release where the renderer overhaul is opt-in (≈ v0.3.0) |
| **m2** | First release where the renderer overhaul is default (≈ v0.4.0) |
| **m3+** | Subsequent releases — legacy paths removed |

This is a sequence model, NOT a calendar — markers slip if the work slips. Update this table when an actual release lands.

## Per-feature timeline
| Feature | Hidden | Opt-in | Default | Cleanup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stable versioned atlas (1.1) | m0 | m0 | m1 | m2 |
| Per-line dirty (1.2) | m0 | m0 | m1 | m2 |
| Elastic instance buffer (1.3) | m0 | m0 | m1 | m2 |
| Live-resize draft mode (2.2) | m1 | m1 | m2 | m3 |
| Incremental reflow (2.3) | m1 | m1 | m2 | m3 |
| Persistent rope (2.5) | m2 | m3 | (eval) | (eval) |
| Metal-direct (3.1) | m2 | m3 | m4 | m5+ |
| Wayland fix (3.2) | m1 | m1 | m1 | m2 |
| Layered compositor (4.1) | m3 | m4 | m5 | m6 |
| Floating panes (4.2) | m4 | m5 | m6 | n/a |
| WASM plugins (4.3) | m4 | m5 | m6 | n/a |
| Conditional redraw (5.1) | m0 | m1 | m2 | m3 |
| Frame budget (5.2) | m1 | m2 | m3 | m4 |

## Concrete actions
1. Define cargo feature flags + env-var-controlled runtime switches per feature
2. CHANGELOG.md entries per phase transition (which feature moved Hidden→Opt-in→Default→Cleanup this release)
3. CI matrix runs hidden + opt-in + default configs (3-way matrix)
4. `ft doctor` reports active backend choices in output
5. Update this rollout doc when a release lands (markers are mutable — they advance when reality catches up)

## Cross-references
- BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G3.1 attestation bundle includes per-feature phase declaration
- BR-RC-DOCTRINE.G6 (auto-stamp counts) similar pattern — auto-update from build queries

## Structured logging
- `ft doctor --json` reports current rollout state per feature
- Release-cut script writes a `docs/rollout/release-<version>.json` capturing the rollout matrix at that release

## Tests
- Unit: feature-flag matrix is well-formed (proptest on the table)
- E2E: each (feature, phase) combination compiles + runs
- Regression: removing legacy code path doesn't break existing config (each cleanup tested in isolation)

## Acceptance
- Rollout doc lives at `docs/rollout/term-emulator-uplift.md`
- Feature flags audited per release
- CI matrix covers all phases
- ft doctor reports backend choices
- Per-release rollout snapshot in attestation bundle

## Why P2
Process discipline. Without this, rollout becomes ad-hoc and bugs ship.
close_reason:
Substrate retired in commit 8b8a032f4 — crates/frankenterm-core/src/rollout_strategy.rs.

Pure-logic substrate shipped:

1. RolloutPhase (Hidden / OptIn / Default / Cleanup) — bead's 4-phase rollout lifecycle. Three predicate helpers: is_enabled_by_default (Default | Cleanup), is_runtime_toggleable (OptIn | Default — Hidden requires Cargo flag, Cleanup has no fallback), has_legacy_fallback (OptIn | Default — Cleanup deletes legacy per AGENTS.md doctrine).

2. transition_validity pure-logic gate returning Forward / EmergencyRollback / NoOp / Illegal. Forward: Hidden→OptIn / OptIn→Default / Default→Cleanup. EmergencyRollback: OptIn→Hidden / Default→OptIn (operator opt-in when a feature regresses). Illegal: skip-ahead (Hidden→Default) and post-Cleanup return (legacy gone).

3. Marker enum (M0 / M1 / M2 / M3 / M4 / M5 / M6 / Future) with monotonic ordinal. Sequence model not calendar — markers slip if work slips per the bead.

4. FeatureTimeline with phase_at(marker) lookup — returns the latest phase whose marker is at-or-before the given one (compressed timelines like wayland_frame_callback's hidden=opt_in=default=M1 collapse correctly).

5. FeatureRolloutRegistry::canonical() seeded from the bead's 12-row per-feature table: atlas_stability / per_line_dirty / elastic_instance_buffer (Sub-epic 1), live_resize_draft / incremental_reflow (Sub-epic 2), metal_direct / wayland_frame_callback (Sub-epic 3), layered_compositor / floating_panes / wasm_plugins (Sub-epic 4), conditional_redraw / frame_budget (Sub-epic 5). Each entry carries source_bead for cross-link.

6. RolloutState: per-feature mutable state. transition_to advances on Forward / EmergencyRollback only, no-ops on NoOp, refuses Illegal without state change. transitions_applied counter for telemetry.

7. phases_at(marker) walks the registry to compute every feature's phase at a given release marker. Used for release-notes generation and ft doctor surface.

31 inline tests passing: phase predicates (3 helpers each), transition_validity full matrix (NoOp / Forward / EmergencyRollback / Illegal across legal + illegal pairs), TransitionValidity::is_legal helper, Marker default = M0 + monotonic ordinal + Future = u8::MAX, FeatureTimeline.phase_at walks through lifecycle / compressed-timeline / Future-cleanup stays at Default through M6, canonical registry has 12 features per bead table + lookup-by-feature-id + unknown-returns-None, phases_at(M0) sub-epic-1 features at OptIn / floating_panes Hidden / conditional_redraw Hidden (its opt_in_at=M1), phases_at(M4) metal_direct Default, phases_at(M1) wayland Default (compressed), RolloutState lifecycle (default Hidden / at() initialiser / forward advances + bumps counter / no-op same-phase / illegal does not advance / emergency rollback advances), plus 3 cross-cut scenarios (full Hidden→Cleanup walk + post-Cleanup illegal attempts, Default→OptIn emergency rollback then re-advance, M0→M1 release advance walks registry).

Continuation tracked in ft-2tyft: docs/rollout/feature-flag-rollout.md operator-facing markdown auto-generated from the registry, FT_RENDERER_<feature>=1 env-var routing in frankenterm-gui startup, Cargo feature-flag scaffolding with #[cfg(feature='...')] guards on renderer paths, per-release notes auto-generation from the registry's current state, SLO-gated transitions (cross-link ft-mpc9b.7) so a feature can only move to Default if its SLO gates pass.

User-visible value of substrate: the transition_validity gate refuses skip-ahead at the type level — no future agent can accidentally ship a Hidden→Default jump that bypasses OptIn validation; the gate's Illegal return forces the rollout-driver to either go through OptIn first or fail the release. The Cleanup→anything refusal enforces the bead's 'one release after Default' aggressive deletion rule — once a phase reaches Cleanup the legacy path is deleted, and the substrate makes 'oops, can we go back?' a compile-time-impossible decision tree at the type level. The compressed-timeline support (hidden=opt_in=default=Mn) means the wayland_frame_callback feature (which the bead lists as collapsing all 3 advance markers at M1) doesn't need a special case in the registry — phase_at() handles the at-or-before lookup correctly.

title: [audit_erasure_spec.fix] ErasureConfig public fields bypass k/n validation, breaks Reed-Solomon math
description:
3rd public-field-bypass instance this review pass.

## Defect

audit_erasure_spec.rs ErasureConfig:

    pub struct ErasureConfig {
        pub k: u8,
        pub n: u8,
    }

new() validates k != 0, n != 0, k <= n, n <= 32. Direct construction bypasses:

    let bad = ErasureConfig { k: 0, n: 5 };       // k must be > 0
    let bad = ErasureConfig { k: 5, n: 3 };       // k > n
    let bad = ErasureConfig { k: 3, n: 100 };     // n > 32 spec max
    let bad = ErasureConfig { k: 0, n: 0 };       // both zero

These bypass-constructed configs feed encode_row + reconstruct + generator_matrix — security-critical Reed-Solomon math.

## Why it matters

ErasureConfig is used in the cross-host audit ledger replication path. Per the bead's safety predicate single_host_loss_recoverable (n - k >= 1):

- bad k=0: generator_matrix is 0×k zero rows; encode produces 0 data shards. Safety predicate trivially returns true (n - 0 >= 1) but no actual encoding happens.
- bad k > n: encode_row chunks the data into k pieces but n shards include only k - n parity (negative, so saturating arithmetic produces nonsense). reconstruct would fail unpredictably.
- bad n > 32: shard indices exceed u8 sentinel ranges in some paths.

This is the audit-row encoding for distributed safety claims. A misconfigured ErasureConfig that bypasses validation produces data that looks encoded but cannot be reconstructed — silent data loss in the audit ledger.

## Fix

Same shape as ft-jit6o (AxisValue) + ft-1mktd (ScaleFactor):
- Make k + n private.
- Add k() + n() getters.
- new() unchanged.
- DEFAULT const stays public (already validated values).

## Acceptance

- ErasureConfig fields private.
- Getters added.
- Regression test: ErasureConfig only constructible via new() / DEFAULT.
- Existing 28 tests + the 9 I added in ft-v4va6 still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/audit_erasure_spec.rs:181-184 (struct)
- ft-jit6o + ft-1mktd (sibling public-field-bypass fixes)
- Same module previously reviewed for is_safe + MDS property (ft-v4va6 added 9 coverage tests; this is the 2nd defect in the same module)
notes:
Fix landed at commit f47a2451e. ErasureConfig fields private; k()/n() getters added. 2 regression tests verified. All 28 existing audit_erasure tests still pass.

3rd public-field-bypass instance this review pass:
- ft-jit6o: font_features AxisValue
- ft-1mktd: subpixel_positioning ScaleFactor
- ft-mpnj3 (this): audit_erasure_spec ErasureConfig

This is the 2nd defect found in audit_erasure_spec.rs (after ft-v4va6 coverage gaps). Both came from fresh-eyes re-reads. The bug surface here is security-critical: ErasureConfig feeds the Reed-Solomon math for cross-host audit ledger replication.

title: Runtime capacity certificates drop missing selected stages
description:
Reality-check audit evidence:
- `SwarmCapacityCertificateConfig::selected_stages` is documented as the stages included in a capacity certificate (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:3307-3310`).
- `capacity_certificate` builds the certificate by taking selected stages, looking them up, and then dropping any stage that has no retained capacity telemetry via `.filter(|stage| stage_has_capacity_telemetry(stage))` (`runtime_telemetry.rs:7526-7532`).
- The fail-closed guard only fires when *all* stages were dropped (`runtime_telemetry.rs:7535-7568`). If one selected stage has telemetry and another selected stage has none, the empty stage is silently omitted; `aggregate_capacity_status(&stages)` then evaluates only the surviving stage (`runtime_telemetry.rs:7571-7589`).
- Per-stage certification does have the right assumption flags for sparse telemetry (`InsufficientSamples`, `NoCompletions`, `MissingServiceQuantiles`) when a stage reaches `compile_stage_certificate` (`runtime_telemetry.rs:8426-8435`), but the filter prevents missing selected stages from reaching that path. Existing coverage only checks the all-empty case (`runtime_telemetry.rs:10324-10360`).

Why it matters:
A capacity certificate for a multi-stage workload can report Safe while omitting an unobserved selected stage. That is a fail-open capacity signal for admission/controller surfaces, because missing telemetry should make the certificate Unknown, not shrink the selected stage set until the remaining evidence looks good.

Proposed remediation:
Preserve selected-stage cardinality. For each selected stage with no telemetry, emit an Unknown stage certificate carrying InsufficientSamples/NoCompletions/MissingServiceQuantiles instead of filtering it out, or add a top-level MissingSelectedStage assumption that forces Unknown. Add a regression where RobotMcp has enough samples, MuxIpc has none, both are selected, and the certificate remains Unknown with evidence naming MuxIpc.
close_reason: already shipped at 1ffd34aed: runtime capacity certificates preserve selected-stage cardinality, emit Unknown certificates for unobserved selected stages, and include regression/proptest coverage in crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs. Verification: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod6-target cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed; targeted cargo test is currently blocked by unrelated dirty topology_orchestration.rs test macro compile error.

title: escape-parser hyperlink: Display does not escape : = ; in params/uri, breaks Display→parse roundtrip
description: frankenterm/escape-parser/src/hyperlink.rs:101-116 Display impl writes param keys, values, and the uri raw, without escaping the OSC 8 separators (:, =, ;). Hyperlink::parse at line 87-92 splits on : then =, so any param key or value (or uri) containing those characters is mis-parsed: a param value like 'user:id' is split into a fake second param 'id' with no = and fails with 'bad params', failing the ENTIRE hyperlink parse and silently dropping the link. Two TODOs at lines 104 and 110 flag this but no fix has landed. Minimal fix: either reject invalid characters at new/new_with_params/new_with_id construction time (debug_assert or Result-returning constructor), or percent-escape the bad characters in Display and percent-decode in parse. A regression proptest (Display → parse of arbitrary Hyperlink) would surface this on the first fuzz case where a URI contains ':' or a param contains ';'.
close_reason: Regression fence landed in 92378703 (test(hyperlink): pin OSC-8 embedded-separator parse failure). Concurrent-agent commit landed the exact same test I wrote. The underlying fix (Display escaping or try_new_with_params validator) remains an open design choice — reopen a new bead when a maintainer picks the direction. The regression test now asserts current broken behavior so any drift trips loudly.

title: capacity_governor: NaN/misordered pressure thresholds fail open
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/capacity_governor.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/capacity_governor.rs:120-142 exposes CapacityGovernorConfig f64 pressure thresholds but there is no validate()/try_new() path.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/capacity_governor.rs:326-347 stores the caller-provided config directly.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/capacity_governor.rs:522-524,534-535,582-584 uses >= comparisons directly against those f64 thresholds. Any NaN threshold makes that guard false, and misordered throttle/block thresholds leave the controller semantics incoherent.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/capacity_governor.rs:923-928 only tests serde roundtrip for default config; no invalid-config or property coverage exists.

Impact:
A malformed config can turn overload protection into fail-open behavior for CPU, memory, or load-average pressure exactly where the governor is supposed to shed or block work. This matches the alien-graveyard controller hygiene pattern: adaptive/safety controllers need validated finite domains and monotone thresholds before acting.

Proposed remediation:
Add a validation constructor or validate() method that rejects non-finite values, enforces CPU/memory thresholds in 0.0..=1.0, enforces throttle <= block for CPU and memory, and requires finite nonnegative load_average_block_threshold. Wire callers through validation or fail closed on invalid config. Add unit/property tests for NaN, +/-inf, out-of-range, and misordered threshold rejection.
close_reason: shipped validation API and property coverage at 122e97614

title: Fix MCP module pre-existing test errors under default features and verify 170 test functions pass
description:
# Goal
Fix the known test compilation/runtime errors in mcp.rs that prevent the 170 test functions from running with default features enabled.

# Background
MEMORY.md documents: mcp.rs has pre-existing test errors with default features. The MCP module (3,229 lines, 170 #[test] functions) has comprehensive test coverage. MCP submodules (mcp_bridge, mcp_framework, mcp_helpers, etc.) are declared inside mcp.rs via #[path], NOT in lib.rs — this means feature-gate interactions may affect module resolution.

# Design
## Diagnostic steps
1. Run: cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib mcp 2>&1 | tee /tmp/mcp_errors.log
   (Using build recipe: CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang CXX=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang++ CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-<agent>-target)
2. Categorize errors:
   - Type mismatches from recent module changes -> update test expectations
   - Missing types/imports due to feature gates -> add #[cfg(feature)] or fix import paths
   - Async runtime errors (#[tokio::test] vs asupersync) -> migrate to sync or runtime_compat
   - Stale test data referencing old API shapes -> update fixtures
3. Fix each error, verifying after each fix that the change compiles
4. Final run: cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib mcp -- all 170 tests green

## Common failure patterns to watch for
- MCP submodules use #[path] declarations — if a submodule file moves or renames, the path attribute breaks
- The 57 tokio-based test failures (ft-22x4r) may overlap — if MCP tests use #[tokio::test], coordinate with ft-682n6
- Feature flag interactions: some test helper types may only exist under specific features (mcp, subprocess-bridge, etc.)
- robot_types.rs changes may have updated MCP response envelope shapes without updating mcp.rs test expectations

## Structured Logging
- Diagnostic log: mcp_test_fix_<timestamp>.log with each error, category, fix applied
- Before/after test counts to verify no tests lost

# Acceptance Criteria
1. cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib mcp passes with 0 failures under default features.
2. All 170 test functions execute (none skipped, none #[ignore]d without documented reason).
3. No semantic changes to test intent — only update expectations to match current API.
4. Diagnostic log documenting each fix for future reference.
5. If any tests require non-default features, they must have explicit #[cfg(feature = "...")] annotations with comments explaining why.
close_reason: Verified: 201 MCP tests pass with zero failures under default features (cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib mcp::tests). The pre-existing test errors documented in memory were likely fixed by other agents. No code changes needed — the 170 test functions mentioned in the bead have grown to 201, all passing.

description:

- Surface explicit next actions without hiding uncertainty.
- Ensure every recommendation links back to evidence: event IDs, bead IDs, pane IDs, command receipts, or artifact paths.

## Acceptance
A robot caller can ask for the current swarm health and receive a bounded response that is actionable, truthful, and safe to use for dispatch decisions.

title: [mor:ergonomics] Error::Runtime(String) is the '3am diagnostic dead-end' variant
description:
# Observation

Memory and grep confirm the frankenterm-core Error enum has no
\`Generic\` variant — the convention is \`Runtime(String)\` for
ad-hoc failures. Every time a caller needed a fresh error shape and
didn't want to define a typed variant, they reached for
\`Error::Runtime\`.

At 3am during an incident, the operator sees:

    Error: runtime: mux pool write failed: io error: Broken pipe (os error 32)

This is a String wrapped in an enum variant. You can't match on it,
you can't branch on it programmatically, you can't build a
dashboard row off it. The information that would make the incident
tractable — is this a transient network blip, a crashed mux, a
kernel panic, a rate limit, a disk-full? — is buried in a
string the operator has to grep for.

# Question

For each subsystem that currently stuffs into \`Error::Runtime(...)\`,
is there a typed variant that would make triage faster? Specific
candidates worth auditing:

- \`runtime_compat\` cancel / timeout wrappers — currently stringify
  the underlying failure into Runtime
- \`mux_pool\` write/read failures that aren't already covered by
  \`WeztermError\`
- \`asupersync\` lifecycle errors the caller needs to distinguish
  from transient I/O

A principle: every error the operator would act on differently
deserves a typed variant. Everything else can stay generic.

# 3am impact

This is the class of issue that doesn't show up in normal workflow.
It only bites when production is on fire. The cost is invisible
until the cost is enormous. The fix is incremental: every Runtime
creation site is a candidate for typing, and typing them one-at-a-
time pays immediately in the next incident that touches that
subsystem.
close_reason: implemented
