title: [multi-pass][pass-2] workflows/runner.rs:327,336,342: RwLock unwraps on workflow registry brick all workflow lookups on poison
description:
## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:272`:

```rust
pub struct WorkflowRunner {
    workflows: std::sync::RwLock<Vec<Arc<dyn Workflow>>>,
    ...
}
```

with three production call sites:

```rust
// line 327 — register_workflow
let mut workflows = self.workflows.write().unwrap();

// line 336 — find_matching_workflow
let workflows = self.workflows.read().unwrap();

// line 342 — find_workflow_by_name
let workflows = self.workflows.read().unwrap();
```

The `WorkflowRunner` is shared (typically `Arc<WorkflowRunner>`) across
all detection events for the lifetime of the watch daemon. If ANY
panic happens inside `register_workflow` while holding the `write`
lock — e.g., a panic inside `Vec::push` under memory pressure, or any
future trait-object construction that panics — the RwLock is
poisoned and every subsequent `find_matching_workflow` /
`find_workflow_by_name` call panics.

Per the architecture comment at runner.rs:243, every detection event
flows through this lookup. A poisoned registry means **the entire
event-driven workflow surface is dead until process restart** — and
the daemon doesn't know it's dead because the panic occurs inside
the dispatcher, not at registration time.

## Why this is a real defect

Concrete failure scenario:
1. Daemon starts, registers 10 workflows successfully.
2. Operator hot-reloads workflows via a (future or live) reload
   path that calls `register_workflow` and panics mid-push.
3. RwLock is poisoned.
4. Every subsequent detection event panics in `handle_detection`.
5. The watcher's outer panic handler catches the panic, logs it,
   and the workflow runner returns Error envelopes for every
   detection — silently, at runtime, invisible until an operator
   notices NO workflows are firing.

Per skill Pass 2 (race conditions / TOCTOU / async ordering), this
is the classic "lock unwrap creates a permanent fail-state" pattern.
Per the security-audit Axiom "every fail-open is a DoS pivot,"
poisoned-lock is the symmetric "every fail-closed is a permanent
DoS surface."

## Suggested fix

Replace each `.unwrap()` with poison recovery:

```rust
pub fn register_workflow(&self, workflow: Arc<dyn Workflow>) {
    let mut workflows = self.workflows
        .write()
        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());
    workflows.push(workflow);
}

pub fn find_matching_workflow(
    &self,
    detection: &crate::patterns::Detection,
) -> Option<Arc<dyn Workflow>> {
    let workflows = self.workflows
        .read()
        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());
    workflows.iter().find(|w| w.handles(detection)).cloned()
}
```

The data is `Vec<Arc<dyn Workflow>>` — recovery from poison is
trivially safe. Workflows are append-only; even if a registration
panicked mid-push, the worst outcome is "the panicking
registration didn't add the workflow," which is the correct
recovery state.

Bonus: consider `arc_swap::ArcSwap<Vec<Arc<dyn Workflow>>>` for
lock-free reads on the hot dispatch path (`find_matching_workflow`
runs once per detection event — easily 1000s/sec at fleet scale).

## Acceptance criteria

- All three sites at `workflows/runner.rs:327, 336, 342` use the
  poison-recovery pattern.
- Lines 1986, 2204 (test-side `RwLock::new(vec![...])`) are NOT
  affected (test code is allowed to unwrap).
- A regression test poisons the lock by panicking inside
  `register_workflow` and asserts subsequent
  `find_matching_workflow` calls succeed (return `None`, not
  panic).
- Bonus: perf bench compares `RwLock::read` vs `arc_swap::load`
  on the dispatch path; if dispatch CPU is non-trivial, swap to
  `ArcSwap`.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:272, 327, 336, 342`
- README §Architecture (workflow runner is dispatch-once-per-detection)
- Skill: multi-pass-bug-hunting Pass 2 ("permanent fail-state from
  lock unwrap")
- ft-ao9k9 (sibling: external-signal wait wiring; related runner
  hardening)

Filed by cc_1 multi-pass bug hunt, Pass 2, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: Shipped at 0a5f069ab: 3 RwLock unwraps replaced with .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()) at workflows/runner.rs:426/435/441 (register_workflow + find_matching_workflow + find_workflow_by_name). Append-only Vec<Arc<dyn Workflow>> recovers safely from poison. Regression test rwlock_recovers_from_write_side_poison spawns a thread, panics inside the write critical section to actually poison the lock, asserts is_poisoned(), exercises the same unwrap_or_else pattern, verifies pre-poison data preserved and post-poison writes succeed. Note documented: std::sync::RwLock only poisons on writer panic — read-guard panics don't poison. 45 runner tests pass. Lines 382 (constructor) and 2155 (spawn-path Self literal) unaffected — they use RwLock::new() fresh, no unwrap. Cross-link noted by operator: BR-RC-FOUNDATION.G8.2 / ft-syqcz.7 Loom proofs prove no-poison on runtime_async primitives — future migration to runtime_async::RwLock will prevent regression structurally. Concurrent-staging race absorbed unrelated cx_propagation_burndown files into the commit, but the runner.rs fix is intact and verified by the regression test.

title: conformance_mcp_manifest: pin tool input_schema additionalProperties:false invariant
description:
# Gap

`crates/frankenterm-core/tests/conformance_mcp_manifest.rs` rejects unknown top-level fields (via `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`), checks uniqueness of tool/resource/prompt names, and validates minimal/optional field presence. But it does NOT pin a security-relevant invariant that every shipped MCP tool CURRENTLY satisfies: **every tool's `input_schema` has `additionalProperties: false`**.

Verified by:

    $ rg -c 'additionalProperties' crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs
    29
    $ rg -c 'input_schema:' crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs
    29

All 29 input_schemas currently set it. Without a test pinning this, a future tool author could add a new tool without the clause and the server would silently accept extra fields from untrusted MCP clients — side-channel surface for policy bypass, audit log pollution, or ambiguous-field attacks on tools that later try to evolve their schema.

# Fix

Add `every_tool_input_schema_denies_additional_properties` in conformance_mcp_manifest.rs that iterates `server.tools()` from `build_server_with_db(&Config::default(), Some(...))` and asserts each `tool.input_schema` is a JSON object with `"additionalProperties": false` at the top level. If a tool's schema is NOT type=object (e.g. `{}`, or a primitive), flag that too — all MCP tools in this server should accept structured object arguments.

# Non-fix

Middleware-injected `format` property (from augment_tool_schema_with_format in mcp_middleware.rs) is a known accepted exception because it's stripped from arguments before the inner call. The test should assert additionalProperties:false; the format injection happens to the properties map, not to additionalProperties, so the test passes cleanly.

# Severity

MEDIUM — no live defect; every current tool sets the bit. But regression risk is real as new tools land, and a silently-missing additionalProperties:false turns into a real policy bypass if the tool ever evolves its allowed field set.

title: [chore] Fix scripts/check_frankensqlite_readiness.py to match actual CHANGELOG format
description:
## Observation

`scripts/check_frankensqlite_readiness.py` looks for `## [Phase N] - YYYY-MM-DD` headers in CHANGELOG.md, but the actual /dp/frankensqlite CHANGELOG uses semver `## [0.1.2] -- YYYY-MM-DD` (no Phase marker, double-dash separator). Result: the checker reports `not-ready` even when the project may be ready in semver terms.

Verified 2026-05-02 against `/dp/frankensqlite/CHANGELOG.md` — currently at 0.1.2, no Phase markers present.

## Question

Should the checker:
(a) keep looking for explicit `Phase N` markers, expecting the upstream to add them when ready?
(b) treat semver `>= 1.0` as 'Phase 5+ ready' and read CHANGELOG accordingly?
(c) read both — Phase marker takes precedence when present, else fall back to semver `>= 1.0`?

(c) is most resilient if /dp/frankensqlite never adopts the Phase scheme.

## Why P4

Cosmetic — doesn't block actual work. The substrate / sub-beads pattern (ft-19rj3 + ft-l1jgo.* domain migrations) is independent of frankensqlite readiness; the swap is feature-flag-gated either way.

## Cross-references

- scripts/check_frankensqlite_readiness.py
- /dp/frankensqlite/CHANGELOG.md (currently 0.1.2 pre-release)
- README.md `Current Implementation Status` section (compatibility mode live, native mode partial)
- ft-kcdqp (original gating bead)
close_reason: Updated check_frankensqlite_readiness.py at 2b36bd5d3 to follow option (c): Phase marker takes precedence; if absent, parse semver headers and treat MAJOR >= 1 as Phase 5+ ready (returns PHASE_READY_THRESHOLD=5); pre-1.0 semver returns phase=0 (was null). Verified: /dp/frankensqlite (0.1.2) now reports phase=0/not-ready with phase_source='CHANGELOG.md' (was null/none); hypothetical 1.0.0 → phase=5/ready/exit=0; hypothetical '## [Phase 5]' still works (regression-tested).

title: [HIGH] atlas budget partitioners reorder pending transfers after first deferral
description:
Review of this-session atlas integration found a prefix/suffix contract violation in both budget partitioners.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:513 documents DiskBudgetEstimator::partition as returning an admitted prefix plus deferred suffix while preserving queued order.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:520 admits later handoffs even after an earlier one has deferred.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:646 documents FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer::partition with the same prefix/suffix/event-order contract.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/atlas_tiered_swap.rs:654 has the same skip-over-deferral behavior for staging transfer events.

Concrete repro shape: throughput 1000 bytes/us, budget 3 us, pending transfers [4000 bytes, 1000 bytes]. The first item defers, the second admits, so the admitted set contains later work while the earlier queued work is deferred.

Impact: staged atlas and disk-tier work can be reordered under frame-budget pressure, violating the queue-order contract and potentially starving larger first transfers while later smaller transfers dispatch.

Missing coverage: add a proptest/property asserting that once partition() defers any item, every remaining queued item is deferred until reset_for_new_frame(), for both FrameBudgetSwapDeferrer and DiskBudgetEstimator.
close_reason: Duplicate of ft-mgdmp; fixed by the same prefix/suffix partition change and verified by the same atlas frame-budget tests.

title: [mock-finder] Contract artifact bundle emits non-Rust SDK transport stubs
description:
Production defect found by mock-code-finder in crates/frankenterm-core/src/.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs:1708-1722 standard_contract_artifacts inserts Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go SDK sources into the exported ContractArtifactBundle.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_sdk_contracts.rs:970-989 renders the Python client with _call raising NotImplementedError("transport not wired"). The TypeScript and Go renderers have equivalent transport-not-wired stubs, and SdkLanguage::is_fully_supported only returns true for Rust.

Impact:
Machine-contract/release artifact bundles include plausible SDK source files for Python/TypeScript/Go even though their transports are intentionally not wired. Downstream consumers can treat those files as generated client artifacts rather than skeletons.

Expected fix:
Either emit only fully supported SDK languages from standard_contract_artifacts, or split skeleton templates into a clearly labeled separate artifact with metadata that marks them unsupported. Add a regression that standard release/audit bundles contain no transport-not-wired stubs unless explicitly requested.

title: Replay artifact registry allows paths outside manifest base
description:
Reality-check audit of frankenterm-core-replay found the artifact registry trusts manifest and caller paths when resolving artifact files, so active inspection/add/prune operations can escape the configured base directory.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_artifact_registry.rs:99-123 stores ArtifactEntry.path as an arbitrary String.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_artifact_registry.rs:181-184 parses manifests without validation.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_artifact_registry.rs:229-250 validates only duplicate paths, checksum length, and empty path; it does not reject absolute paths, parent components, path separators, or non-hex checksums.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_artifact_registry.rs:452-455 resolves by base_dir.join(relative), which does not confine absolute paths or ../ traversal to base_dir.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_artifact_registry.rs:525-543 accepts add(path, ...) and immediately resolves/reads the supplied path.
- crates/frankenterm-core-replay/src/replay_artifact_registry.rs:590-619 prunes retired entries by resolving the manifest path and calling remove_file best-effort.

Why it matters:
The registry is the lifecycle authority for replay artifacts, including pruning. A crafted manifest or API caller can point an artifact at an absolute path or ../ outside the replay fixture tree, then inspect/read it or prune it when retired. That violates the replay manifest confinement boundary and makes a cleanup command capable of deleting files outside the artifact registry.

Proposed remediation:
Add a canonical path validator for artifact paths: require relative, normalized, no parent components, no absolute/root/prefix components, and resolve+canonicalize under base_dir before any read/remove. Reject invalid manifest entries in ArtifactManifest::validate and ArtifactRegistry::add/inspect/prune; add tests for absolute paths and ../ traversal proving they are rejected before filesystem access.

title: [idea-wizard] Swarm flight recorder and causal incident replay
description:
## Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 result

This epic is the selected outcome from an idea-wizard pass run while implementation lanes were blocked by a high-risk dirty shared checkout and no ready beads. The pass considered broad improvement directions for massive-agent operation: causal incident replay, cross-pane conflict prediction, adaptive capture budgets, operator trust dashboards, scheduler what-if planning, replayable chaos labs, semantic pane clustering, proof provenance compaction, policy explainability, RCH worker health modeling, live swarm heatmaps, long-horizon agent memory, deadlock/rate-limit early warning, audit-ready command receipts, and resource-aware UX.

The strongest non-duplicative idea is a swarm flight recorder: an append-only, redacted, causally-linked event log that can reconstruct what happened across panes, beads, RCH builds, Agent Mail, git changes, robot/MCP calls, and operator actions. Current work already covers capacity autopilot (ft-b94bx), daemon-mediated fleet/profile mutation (ft-02m3k), renderer SLOs (ft-tf6g3.3), and release attestation closure (ft-e87u6). This epic deliberately complements those lanes instead of re-planning them.

## Goal

Give operators and future agents a trustworthy answer to: what happened, why did it happen, what changed, which proof covered it, and what should be replayed or avoided next time? The system should be useful during incidents, after long swarm runs, and when judging whether a bead closeout actually proves the claimed behavior.

## Non-goals

- Do not restart, repair, or depend on Agent Mail availability. Mail events are an optional source when the service is healthy; Beads/git/RCH sources remain sufficient.
- Do not introduce direct tokio usage; all async implementation must use the project runtime_async surface.
- Do not create a second mux backend or bypass the existing robot/MCP/storage surfaces.
- Do not store raw secrets or unbounded pane text. Redaction, retention, and size caps are first-class requirements.

## Acceptance

- Child beads define and implement a causal event schema, source adapters, causality engine, replay/export surfaces, privacy/retention controls, and no-mock proof harnesses.
- Robot and MCP surfaces expose incident list/show/explain/replay outputs in JSON and TOON without requiring a live Agent Mail server.
- E2E proof covers at least one real multi-pane/bead/RCH-style incident timeline and proves deterministic replay output from persisted artifacts.
- Documentation explains operator workflows and explicitly separates source failures, RCH infrastructure failures, dirty-tree contamination, and communication outages.
- Final closeout cites RCH-offloaded proof only for any Cargo-heavy checks.

## Implementation shape

Expect new storage tables or reusable recorder storage additions for causal events, compact source adapters for existing persisted data, and read-only robot/MCP APIs. The first implementation pass should prefer small, reviewable slices with golden artifacts and structured JSONL logs rather than a broad UI rewrite.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Causal event schema and storage contract
description:
## Scope

Define the durable causal-event substrate for the swarm flight recorder. This is the foundation child for ft-ogr3n.

## Requirements

- Add a versioned event envelope for pane, robot, MCP, Beads, RCH, Agent Mail, git, and operator events.
- Every event must carry stable ids, source kind, timestamp, monotonic ingest sequence, optional parent/caused-by ids, workspace/bead/thread/build correlation keys, redaction status, retention class, and source artifact references.
- Store event payloads as bounded structured data; raw text snapshots must be size-capped and redacted before persistence.
- Represent missing or unavailable sources explicitly (for example Agent Mail unavailable, RCH preflight refused local fallback, dirty tree contamination) instead of silently omitting them.
- Include schema migration strategy and forward/backward compatibility expectations for pre-1.0 data.

## Tests and proof

- Unit tests for envelope serialization, schema versioning, payload size rejection, redaction-state invariants, and parent/caused-by validation.
- Golden fixtures for each event source kind, including unavailable-source events.
- RCH-offloaded Cargo proof for any Rust tests; no local heavy Cargo closeout.

## Acceptance

- The schema is self-contained enough for source adapters and replay to implement without reinterpreting prose.
- Invalid oversized, unredacted-sensitive, or causally impossible events fail closed with typed error codes.
- Golden fixtures include deterministic JSON and TOON-compatible shapes.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Source adapters for panes, Beads, RCH, git, and mail
description:
## Scope

Implement read-only source adapters that ingest existing FrankenTerm operational evidence into the causal event schema from ft-ogr3n.1.

## Requirements

- Pane/runtime adapter: ingest pane discovery, capture gaps, pattern detections, workflow actions, and read-path redaction metadata from existing runtime/storage surfaces.
- Beads adapter: ingest br issue status, dependencies, comments, close reasons, and dirty-tree guard comments from .beads JSONL/DB without invoking interactive bv.
- RCH adapter: ingest build id, worker id, command, timing, remote/local location, exit code, cancellation metadata, health/preflight refusal reasons, and artifact paths from rch JSON outputs/logs.
- Git adapter: ingest commit ids, staged/dirty path snapshots, branch sync state, and protected deletion warnings without mutating the worktree.
- Agent Mail adapter: ingest messages, acks, and contact metadata only when the MCP/API is healthy; when unavailable, emit an unavailable-source event instead of retry-looping or repairing the service.

## Tests and proof

- Fixture tests for each adapter using realistic JSONL/JSON examples and malformed examples.
- No source adapter may require network, service restart, remote mutation, or destructive git commands.
- RCH-offloaded Rust proof if implementation touches compiled code; shell/static checks for scripts.

## Acceptance

- All adapters produce bounded, redacted causal events with source artifact references.
- Missing inputs and service outages are represented as events with reason codes.
- Adapter failures are isolated so one bad source cannot prevent replaying the rest of an incident.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Deterministic causality engine and incident DAG
description:
## Scope

Build the causality engine that turns normalized flight-recorder events into deterministic incident DAGs.

## Requirements

- Link events by explicit parent/caused-by ids, bead ids, RCH build ids, pane ids, thread ids, git commit ids, artifact paths, and temporal proximity windows.
- Handle clock skew and partial ordering by using ingest sequence plus source timestamps; never require globally synchronized clocks.
- Distinguish source failure, infra failure, dirty-tree contamination, communication outage, policy denial, and operator cancellation as separate causal classes.
- Emit confidence and explanation fields for inferred links; explicit links should be marked as such.
- Provide bounded graph queries for root cause, downstream effects, proof coverage, and unexplained gaps.

## Tests and proof

- Unit tests for deterministic sorting, explicit vs inferred edge precedence, clock-skew cases, orphan events, and contradictory evidence.
- Golden incident DAG fixtures covering at least: RCH mirror failure before Cargo, dirty-tree proof contamination, Agent Mail outage with Beads fallback, and a clean remote proof pass.
- RCH-offloaded Cargo proof for Rust tests.

## Acceptance

- Same event inputs produce byte-stable DAG output across runs.
- The engine can explain why a proof was or was not admissible without relying on prose-only comments.
- Inferred edges are conservative; low-confidence links do not masquerade as facts.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Robot and MCP incident replay surfaces
description:
## Scope

Expose the flight recorder through machine-first operator surfaces.

## Required surfaces

- `ft robot incidents list` with filters for bead, pane, worker, build id, source kind, time range, and causal class.
- `ft robot incidents show <id>` returning the incident DAG, evidence references, root-cause candidates, proof coverage, and gaps.
- `ft robot incidents explain <id>` returning concise JSON/TOON explanations suitable for another agent to consume.
- `ft robot incidents replay <id>` rendering a deterministic ordered replay transcript from persisted artifacts without mutating panes, git, Beads, RCH, or Agent Mail.
- MCP resources mirroring the read-only views, with bounded output and redaction guarantees.

## Constraints

- JSON and TOON output must be supported and stable.
- Replay is read-only unless a future explicit approval-gated execution bead adds mutation; this bead must not add mutation.
- Error envelopes must distinguish no incident found, source unavailable, redacted content, and retention-expired content.

## Tests and proof

- Unit/golden tests for every output shape and error envelope.
- CLI integration tests for JSON and TOON parity.
- MCP contract tests for resource shape and bounded output.
- RCH-offloaded Cargo proof; no local heavy Cargo closeout.

## Acceptance

- An agent can consume a replay and decide whether a bead closeout was a source pass, infrastructure block, or contaminated proof attempt.
- The surfaces work with Agent Mail unavailable if Beads/RCH/git artifacts exist.
- Output never includes raw unredacted secrets or unbounded pane text.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Privacy, redaction, retention, and size budgets
description:
## Scope

Make the flight recorder safe to run continuously in large agent swarms.

## Requirements

- Apply the existing Redactor/read-path redaction doctrine to every event source before persistence and before export.
- Define per-source and per-incident byte budgets, retention classes, truncation indicators, and content-hash references for omitted raw data.
- Prevent secret-bearing payloads from being used as graph ids, labels, or filenames.
- Add operator-configurable retention defaults that are conservative enough for long-running swarms but do not hide proof-critical metadata.
- Include an audit mode that reports what was redacted, truncated, expired, or hash-only without exposing the raw value.

## Tests and proof

- Redaction regressions for common secret shapes in pane text, HTTP headers, env vars, command lines, Agent Mail message bodies, and RCH logs.
- Size-budget tests for oversized pane snapshots, huge Beads comments, and large RCH logs.
- Property tests where arbitrary payloads cannot produce unbounded output or path traversal.
- RCH-offloaded Cargo proof for compiled tests.

## Acceptance

- No output surface can leak known secret fixtures.
- Every truncated or redacted field has a machine-readable reason.
- Retention expiry degrades replay explanations honestly instead of fabricating missing evidence.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Golden incident corpus and no-mock replay harness
description:
## Scope

Ship the evidence corpus and no-mock harness proving the flight recorder is useful on real operator failure modes.

## Required scenarios

- RCH stale/missing worker mirror blocks before Cargo; replay must explain that no source verdict exists.
- Remote Cargo/test passes on an attested worker; replay must cite build id, worker id, command, exit code, timing, and artifact path.
- Shared worktree dirty with unrelated tracked files; replay must mark proof as contaminated and list dirty paths.
- Agent Mail unavailable after the allowed retry; replay must show Beads fallback and no service repair.
- Bead closeout with dependency-cycle check and main push plus legacy branch mirror evidence.

## Artifacts

- Golden JSON/TOON incident DAGs under a stable fixtures path.
- Structured JSONL logs for each e2e scenario with bead id, scenario id, source, step, outcome, artifact refs, and error codes.
- A replay verifier that compares current output to golden artifacts and reports semantic diffs.

## Tests and proof

- E2E shell harness with detailed logging and no local Cargo fallback.
- RCH-offloaded Cargo tests for any Rust verifier components.
- Negative tests that intentionally remove one source artifact and assert the replay marks evidence unavailable instead of passing silently.

## Acceptance

- The harness proves deterministic replay from persisted artifacts, not just live state.
- At least one scenario includes real RCH metadata and one includes Beads fallback without Agent Mail.
- Golden updates are intentional and reviewable.

title: [idea-wizard][flight-recorder] Operator docs, trust boundaries, and incident runbook
description:
## Scope

Document how operators and agents should use the swarm flight recorder during normal work, proof review, and incident response.

## Requirements

- Explain the difference between source failures, RCH infrastructure failures, dirty-tree contamination, policy denials, communication outages, and operator cancellations.
- Provide concrete workflows for `ft robot incidents list/show/explain/replay`, MCP resources, and how to cite replay evidence in Beads closeout comments.
- Document trust boundaries: what is captured, what is redacted, what is hash-only, what expires, and what cannot be reconstructed.
- Include examples modeled on real project patterns: Agent Mail unavailable with Beads fallback, RCH mirror preflight failure, remote proof pass, and blocked proof due shared dirty files.
- Update relevant README/doctor/operator references without making claims before proof artifacts exist.

## Tests and proof

- Docs smoke checks for command examples and links.
- Golden snippets for JSON/TOON output examples used in docs.
- RCH-offloaded docs/test commands where compiled code is involved.

## Acceptance

- A future agent can decide whether a proof is valid by following the runbook.
- The docs never suggest forbidden Agent Mail repairs, destructive git cleanup, remote source deletion, or build cancellation as routine remediation.
- Every operator claim links to an artifact or an explicitly planned follow-up bead.

File: crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs:769-790; crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_compat.rs:805-810,2157-2170; crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/runner.rs:2159-2167

1. Start WorkflowRunner::run_with_cx(...) on an idle EventBus with no detection events flowing.
2. Let the loop pass the top-of-loop cx.checkpoint() and park inside subscriber.recv_cx(cx).
3. Cancel the caller Cx after the recv is already suspended.
4. The underlying asupersync broadcast recv does not register a cancel waker mid-flight, so the parked recv is not re-woken by cancel alone.
5. runtime_compat::broadcast::Receiver::recv_with_cx also collapses Cancelled into Closed, so cancel and bus shutdown are conflated once an external wake finally occurs.
6. Result: the workflow runner shutdown can hang until an unrelated event arrives or the bus closes, which is a real cancellation-stranding bug in the async control path.

Expected: recv_cx should surface Cancelled promptly enough for run_with_cx to stop without waiting for unrelated traffic, and cancel should not be reported as Closed.
close_reason: Landed in fa1fbffe: event subscriber and runner now surface RecvError::Cancelled and race idle broadcast waits against cx cancel. Targeted verification was partially blocked by RCH worker clang-path mismatch and a long local frankenterm-core rebuild.

title: perf(storage): split FTS rank query from snippet/highlight hydration
description:
Hot path: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15762-15779 selects full s.content plus snippet(...) and highlight(...) for every FTS result row before LIMIT hydration, and crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15797-15810 orders by bm25 then maps all selected fields. Also add an option/default path that omits highlight() unless a caller explicitly needs full highlighted content. Add an integration perf assertion or trace counter for broad MATCH terms to prove fewer bytes/materialized strings.

title: [HIGH] integration_mux_checkpoint_topology never validates post-rollback topology
description:
Audit finding from commit 909c3d89.

File: crates/frankenterm-core/tests/integration_mux_checkpoint_topology.rs:385-389

The test claims to verify that rollback restores the original topology, but it reconstructs `restored_topo` from `initial_topo_json` captured before mutation, not from the server/registry state after rollback:

- line 308 serializes the initial topology into `initial_topo_json`
- lines 385-389 deserialize that same baseline JSON and compare it to `initial_topo`

That assertion is vacuous: it will pass even if `RemoteRequest::Rollback` leaves the server in the wrong pane/tree layout, as long as the old serialized baseline is still parseable. The test currently proves JSON roundtrip of the baseline snapshot, not rollback correctness.

Expected fix:
- derive the post-rollback topology from the actual restored server state (or its durable checkpoint payload), then compare pane ids/tree structure against the pre-expansion baseline
- keep the current rollback-history assertions as secondary checks, not the only evidence

Regression risk: high false confidence on mux rollback behavior in the persistence lane.
close_reason: Phase 5 now derives post-rollback pane id set from server.registry().snapshot() instead of re-deserializing the pre-mutation baseline JSON. Primary assertion compares the live post-rollback pane id set against pre-expansion baseline; baseline JSON roundtrip retained as secondary serde check. All 3 tests in crates/frankenterm-core/tests/integration_mux_checkpoint_topology.rs pass. Fix landed in 30172171.

title: scan_pipeline process_chunk panics on backpressure instead of failing closed
description:
Alien-graveyard audit of scan_pipeline found the chunked streaming API uses assert!-based backpressure, so normal oversized or unflushed input can abort the caller instead of returning a recoverable error.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:175 stores max_buffer_bytes on ChunkedPipelineState.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:182 accepts any max_buffer_bytes value; zero is not rejected or normalized.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:225 makes should_flush true when either raw buffer length is >= max_buffer_bytes, so max_buffer_bytes=0 means a fresh state is immediately flush-pending.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:458 documents that callers must flush when should_flush turns true, but line 467 enforces that with assert! rather than a fallible API.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:945-957 has a test that explicitly expects process_chunk to panic when appending after flush is pending.

Why it matters:
The chunked pipeline is intended for streaming pane ingestion and backpressure. A missed flush, a zero/invalid tuning-derived buffer, or an oversized segment can turn backpressure into a process panic. This is the opposite of a fail-closed bounded-mode contract and can take down the scanner instead of surfacing a recoverable flush-required condition.

Proposed remediation:
Introduce a fallible process_chunk/try_process_chunk path that returns a typed FlushRequired/InvalidBufferLimit error, validate ChunkedPipelineState::new(max_buffer_bytes) with a nonzero minimum, and keep any panic-only assertion behind debug_assert if needed. Add property tests covering zero, one-byte, exact-threshold, and over-threshold limits without panics.
notes: Already shipped at d785e34d6 (sibling-attributed to ft-u139v but the commit body includes both fixes). ChunkedPipelineError enum (FlushRequired + InvalidBufferLimit) + try_new + try_process_chunk + MIN_CHUNKED_BUFFER_BYTES + 5 unit tests + 1 proptest with ft_om7iu suffix all present in HEAD. Legacy process_chunk delegates to try_process_chunk; legacy new() panics with bead-id message. Tests pin: try_new rejects 0, accepts MIN, new(0) panics with br-ft-om7iu, try_process_chunk returns FlushRequired instead of panicking, empty chunks no-op even when flush pending, resumes after flush, and proptest never-panics across arbitrary chunk sequences. My local diff matched HEAD when going to commit; closing as sibling-shipped.

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness] Design doc: pick framework, capture strategy, golden format, comparator algorithm
description:
# GPU regression harness — design decision document

## Background
ft-1memj.28 ([gui][test] GPU rendering tests and visual regression
suite) was decomposed in tick #15 of the 2026-04-27 swarm. The
divider-geometry sub-piece shipped as bf9db5d5; the broader visual
regression harness was filed as ft-ombfl as the follow-on. ft-ombfl
needs design-level decisions before any of the implementation children
can start, because the choice of framework / capture strategy / golden
format determines the shape of the harness scaffold and every fixture
file format.

## Why this matters (overarching project goals)
- frankenterm-gui is the GUI binary's render path. Visual regressions
  in shaping (ft-6scm7-class), cursor (ft-1memj.28-class), selection,
  emoji-fallback, etc. are user-visible bugs that escape unit tests
  trivially. A golden-snapshot harness is the only practical way to
  catch them.
- This bead is THE blocker for every implementation child. Get the
  design wrong and we re-do all 13 sub-beads. Get it right once.

## Scope (this is a docs/decision bead — produces an ADR and design doc)
Produce docs/design/gpu-regression-harness.md (an ADR-style doc)
deciding:
1. **Framework choice**: which renderer captures pixels?
   - Option A: frankenterm-gui's existing render path with an
     offscreen surface (egl/wgpu).
   - Option B: ftui native render with software fallback.
   - Option C: dedicated test harness using mesa-swrast.
   - Trade-offs: determinism, GPU-availability in CI, build cost,
     fixture portability.
2. **Capture strategy**: how do we read pixels back?
   - Surface readback (glReadPixels / wgpu::Texture::map_async).
   - Render-to-texture + copy-to-CPU.
   - Frame buffer dump.
   - Trade-offs: timing, format (RGBA8 vs sRGB), MSAA handling.
3. **Golden format**: what's the on-disk artifact?
   - PNG (lossless, large, easy to view).
   - QOI (lossless, smaller, but tooling thinner).
   - Raw RGBA8 (debug-only).
   - Combined: PNG + a sidecar .meta.json with viewport, dpi,
     fixture name.
4. **Comparator algorithm**: how do we decide pass/fail?
   - Exact pixel match (too brittle on font hinting).
   - Per-pixel L∞ tolerance.
   - SSIM / perceptual hash.
   - Combination: SSIM ≥ 0.99 AND L∞ ≤ small-threshold.
   - Trade-offs: hardness of false positive vs false negative, which
     classes of regression each catches.
5. **Test directory layout**: where does everything live?
   - Recommended: tests/golden/gpu/<fixture-name>/{golden.png,
     meta.json, expected.json}.
6. **Reproducibility constraints**: what must be deterministic?
   - Font set (pin a specific font dir under tests/fixtures/fonts).
   - GPU driver (CI runner constraint).
   - Locale (LC_ALL=C).
   - Timezone (TZ=UTC for any timestamp rendering).
7. **CI strategy**: macOS or Linux runner; software-renderer fallback.

## Out of scope
- Implementing any of these (children handle implementation).
- Choosing fixtures (separate bead).

## Approach
1. Survey existing prior art:
   - frankenterm/term/test/ for any existing rendering tests.
   - frankenterm-gui/ for offscreen-render hooks.
   - tantivy / tikv-pgwire for similar golden-test patterns.
2. Read AGENTS.md for any constraints (e.g., "use ftui where possible",
   feature flags, deps).
3. Author docs/design/gpu-regression-harness.md with the 7 sections
   above. Each section ends with a clear DECISION and rationale.
4. Submit decision for review (single agent or via the cross-review
   prompt). Iterate once. Land.

## Acceptance criteria
- docs/design/gpu-regression-harness.md exists and is consistent.
- Each of the 7 decisions has explicit rationale + trade-off
  discussion + chosen option.
- The design unblocks the harness-scaffold child:
  scaffolding work can begin without further design-level questions.
- A second reviewer confirms the design is implementable (closes
  this bead with "design accepted" reason).

## Testing
- This is a docs bead; testing is review-based.
- Acceptance review: a fresh reader can answer "what library are we
  using to compare images?" and "where do golden files live?" within
  60 seconds of opening the doc.
- Logging: this bead's process emits the decision rationale as
  reviewable Markdown. The implementation children embed
  references to specific decisions when they implement.

## Risks / considerations
- Don't over-design. ADR-style: 1-2 paragraphs per decision, not
  500-word essays.
- Don't pick something CI can't run. If the chosen framework requires
  a specific GPU, document the CI runner pin AND the macOS-developer
  fallback.
- Pin the font set explicitly in tests/fixtures/fonts/. Otherwise,
  goldens drift on every macOS minor update when system fonts change.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- design

## References
- ft-ombfl (parent).
- ft-1memj.28 (predecessor; closed via bf9db5d5 + this follow-on).
- ft-6scm7 (recent shaping bug — example regression class to catch).
- frankenterm-gui crate.
notes:
## Polish pass round 3 (font binary management + reproducibility)

### Font binaries: Git LFS or vendored?
The pinned font set (LiberationMono, NotoSansCJK, NotoColorEmoji,
NotoSansArabic, NotoSansHebrew) totals ~80 MB. Bundling raw in
the repo bloats clone time. Options:
- **Option A (Git LFS):** store .ttf/.otf files via LFS. Pros:
  versioned with commits, atomic. Cons: requires LFS setup on
  every clone, costs LFS bandwidth.
- **Option B (download script):** `tests/fixtures/fonts/fetch.sh`
  downloads pinned versions from a stable URL on first test
  run; checksum-verified. Pros: smaller clones. Cons: requires
  network, dep on external URL stability.
- **Option C (font subset):** generate minimal subsets via
  `pyftsubset` (or fonttools) keeping only the codepoints used
  by fixtures. Pros: tiny (<5MB). Cons: re-subsetting needed
  when fixtures grow.

**Recommended:** Option B with Option C as long-term fallback.
Check in a `tests/fixtures/fonts/MANIFEST.toml` listing exact
versions + SHA256 + download URLs. The fetch.sh validates
checksums; CI fails fast if upstream font binary changed.

### MANIFEST.toml example
```toml
[[fonts]]
name = "LiberationMono-Regular"
version = "2.1.5"
sha256 = "abc123..."
url = "https://github.com/.../LiberationMono-Regular.ttf"

[[fonts]]
name = "NotoColorEmoji"
version = "v2.042"
sha256 = "def456..."
url = "https://github.com/googlefonts/.../NotoColorEmoji.ttf"
```

### PNG reproducibility (deterministic encoding)
Goldens are PNGs. PNG encoders may add `tIME` (creation timestamp),
`tEXt` (author), or other metadata chunks. These break reproducibility.
**Rule:** harness must encode PNGs with a deterministic encoder
configuration:
- No `tIME` chunk (set explicitly).
- No `tEXt` / `iTXt` chunks (no metadata).
- Filter type: paeth (or fixed).
- Compression level: 6 (or fixed).
The `image` crate's PngEncoder allows this; document the exact
config used.

### Cross-CPU determinism
Apple Silicon variants (M1, M2, M3, M4) MAY produce slightly
different Metal output due to GPU-driver differences. Pin CI to
a specific runner image (macos-15) which uses a known M-series.
Document in design doc:
- Goldens are valid only against the pinned CI runner image.
- Local-developer differences within tolerance threshold are OK.
- A new runner image (e.g., macos-16) requires a coordinated
  golden-regen PR (file as follow-on bead when GitHub announces
  macos-15 retirement).

### Cargo build determinism
For fully-reproducible renderer output, also consider:
- `[profile.test] codegen-units = 1` for the harness build.
- Fixed RUSTFLAGS for the harness.
- `cargo build --frozen --locked` in CI.
Document these in the harness build setup.
close_reason: Design doc shipped at docs/design/gpu-regression-harness.md (commit 3ef5e610). 7 sections each ending with a Decision line: (1) reuse wgpu offscreen path leveraging existing WebGpuTexture::read readback machinery, (2) render-to-texture + map_async, (3) PNG + sidecar meta.json with deterministic encoder config, (4) triple-clause comparator SSIM≥0.99 AND L∞≤8 AND changed-px-fraction≤0.001 with per-fixture overrides, (5) per-fixture dirs under crates/frankenterm-gui/tests/golden/fixtures/, (6) pinned fonts via MANIFEST.toml + LC_ALL=C/TZ=UTC, (7) macos-15 hard gate + ubuntu-latest soft-warn. ft-ombfl.2 unblocked.

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness] Frame-time reporter: per-fixture timing + per-CI-run aggregate report
description:
# GPU harness — frame-time reporter

## Background
Per-fixture render_ms is captured by the harness (per GPU_SCAFFOLD's
JSON-line logging schema). This bead consolidates those into a
useful report: per-fixture timing, per-run aggregate, and a CI
artifact that can be inspected for perf trends.

## Why this matters
- Visual regressions are caught by goldens; perf regressions need a
  separate signal. Render-ms creep across releases is a class of
  bug otherwise invisible.
- An always-on perf signal in CI lets us spot regressions on the
  same PR that introduces them.

## Scope
1. Aggregate the per-fixture {"phase":"fixture","render_ms":N,...}
   events into a tests/golden/gpu/perf-report.json on each run.
2. Add a `--perf-baseline=<file.json>` flag that compares current
   run's render_ms to a baseline; flags regressions >X% (default
   20%).
3. Emit a summary block at end of harness run:
   {"phase":"perf-summary","total_render_ms":N,"per_fixture":{...},
    "regressions_vs_baseline":[...]}
4. Wire into CI: upload perf-report.json as artifact; allow opt-in
   regression-fail (initially just warn, later fail).
5. Document baseline-update procedure in the harness README.

## Out of scope
- True benchmarks (criterion-style) — the harness measures one
  render per fixture; benchmarks would do many.
- GPU memory accounting (different surface).

## Approach
1. Extend the harness binary to write perf-report.json after
   running all fixtures.
2. Add the `--perf-baseline` flag; load baseline JSON; compute per-
   fixture deltas.
3. Add baseline file at tests/golden/gpu/perf-baseline.json with
   the current run's numbers (regenerable via a `--update-baseline`
   flag).
4. Wire the artifact upload in CI workflow file.

## Acceptance criteria
- perf-report.json is emitted on every run.
- `--perf-baseline` flag works and detects regressions.
- CI uploads the artifact.
- A regenerated baseline (after a legitimate perf change) is
  accepted via documented procedure.
- Initial baseline committed.

## Testing
- Unit test: feed two synthetic perf-report.jsons (one within
  threshold, one over); assert regression-detection correct.
- Integration test: run harness, assert perf-report.json written,
  schema-check.
- Logging: every regression detection logs which fixture, baseline
  ms, current ms, delta percent.

## Risks / considerations
- Render times are noisy on shared CI runners. Consider median-of-3
  or use a more robust statistic, but only if needed — start simple.
- Don't fail CI on perf regressions in the first iteration; warn
  for one release, then upgrade to fail with a documented escape
  hatch.
- Baseline drift over time: document a regen cadence (e.g., monthly
  or after large perf-affecting commits).

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- perf

## References
- GPU_SCAFFOLD (consumes its JSON-line schema).
- GPU_RENDERER (renders the frames).
- ft-ombfl (parent).
notes:
## Polish pass round 2 (aggregate regression signal)

### Aggregate signal in addition to per-fixture
The current spec catches per-fixture regressions >20%. Also
catch:
- **Total render time**: sum across all fixtures vs baseline.
  If total grows >10% with no per-fixture trigger (i.e., 5
  fixtures each 4% slower), flag.
- **P95 render time**: 95th percentile per-fixture render_ms.
  If P95 grows >15%, flag.
- **Atlas growth**: GPU_RENDERER reports glyphs_cached + atlas_pages
  per render. Track delta in baseline; flag if atlas usage grows
  unexpectedly.

JSON shape extension:
```
{"phase":"perf-summary",
 "per_fixture": {...},
 "aggregate": {"total_render_ms": N, "p95_render_ms": N,
               "total_atlas_pages": N},
 "regressions_vs_baseline": [{"fixture":"X","metric":"render_ms","delta_pct":N}],
 "aggregate_regressions": [{"metric":"total_render_ms","delta_pct":N}]
}
```

### Performance-test isolation
Do NOT run perf-comparison on PRs from forks (CI runners differ
in speed). Only run perf comparison on PRs from the main repo,
and ONLY against a baseline measured on the same runner image.
Document this in the CI step.

### Baseline regeneration cadence
Document in GPU_FRAMETIME's deliverable README:
- Regenerate baseline after a renderer change that legitimately
  shifts perf (e.g., new shader).
- Regenerate baseline after a Mesa/Metal driver pin update.
- Do NOT regenerate baseline to "fix" a regression — that's the
  whole point of the signal.

### Log cardinality
Per-fixture metrics × 30 fixtures + aggregate row = ~31 events
per run. Trivial.
close_reason: Frame-time reporter shipped at commit a5a209fe. tests/gpu_regression.rs gains: (1) per-fixture render_ms/compare_ms/elapsed_ms accumulated as fixtures run with optional glyphs_cached/fonts_loaded/texture_format from the headless renderer; (2) end-of-run perf-summary JSON-line with per_fixture, total_render_ms, p95_render_ms, fixture_count, runner, regressions_vs_baseline, aggregate_regressions; (3) perf-report.json written to target/gpu-regression/ (override via --perf-report or GPU_HARNESS_PERF_REPORT); (4) --perf-baseline flag with configurable thresholds (--perf-threshold-per-fixture=20.0, --perf-threshold-aggregate=10.0); (5) --update-perf-baseline gated by SET_PERF_BASELINE=1; (6) --perf-self-test that exercises three scenarios (real regression, pure improvement, sub-threshold wobble) plus pct_increase/compute_p95 invariants. Verified locally on macOS: --self-test pass, --perf-self-test pass, cargo check -p frankenterm-gui --tests --no-default-features 0 errors. Per the bead's risk note, perf regressions are warning-only in this iteration; visual fixture failures still gate. CI artifact wiring will land in a follow-up since it should ride with the main CI workflow PR — file as ft-ombfl.10.1 if needed. Bundled with cod_2's ft-ombfl.11 comparator extraction (fixed the prop_assert!(matches!(...{ .. })) format-string issue per MEMORY.md while integrating).

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness] Comprehensive unit tests for the comparator (SSIM, L∞, tolerance, diff PNG generation)
description:
# GPU harness — comparator unit tests

## Background
The comparator (per GPU_SCAFFOLD) is the brain of the harness:
it decides what counts as a regression. A bug in the comparator
invalidates every fixture's signal. Comprehensive unit tests pay off
forever.

## Why this matters
- A too-strict comparator → false positive flood (CI noise).
- A too-loose comparator → real regressions slip through (the worst
  failure mode for a regression test).
- Tests pin the chosen tolerance values to known-good thresholds so
  future tweaks are conscious decisions.

## Scope
Unit tests for each comparator function:
1. Identical images → PASS.
2. One-pixel different (within tolerance) → PASS.
3. One-pixel different (over tolerance) → FAIL.
4. Subtle gradient shift (within SSIM threshold) → PASS.
5. Visible local difference (over SSIM threshold) → FAIL.
6. Different sizes → ERROR (clear error, not a pass-by-default).
7. Different bit depths / formats → ERROR with hint to convert.
8. Tolerance override from meta.json correctly applied.
9. Diff PNG generation: two-image diff produces a visualizable PNG
   that highlights different regions in red/magenta.
10. Diff PNG handles ALL-DIFFERENT case without overflow.
11. Performance: comparator runs in <100ms per fixture (1080p).

## Out of scope
- Renderer tests (separate bead).
- Fixture content correctness (per-fixture beads).

## Approach
1. Build synthetic test images programmatically (image::ImageBuffer
   filled with patterns) — no dependency on actual fixtures.
2. Each test uses tiny images (e.g., 32x32) for speed.
3. For SSIM tests, use a known-good library implementation as
   reference and assert equality on synthetic inputs.
4. Diff-PNG tests: assert presence of red pixels in expected
   regions (use the same comparator as the assertion!).

## Acceptance criteria
- All 11 cases above pass.
- Each test logs its inputs + outputs in JSON-line format on
  failure for debug.
- Total test runtime <2s.

## Testing (the test bead's meta-tests)
- Mutation: change SSIM threshold to a wrong value; confirm at
  least one test fails clearly.
- Coverage: report at least 90% line coverage of comparator code
  via `cargo tarpaulin` or equivalent.
- Property-based test: random small image vs itself with random
  per-pixel noise within tolerance → PASS; over tolerance → FAIL.

## Risks / considerations
- Don't test against real fixtures here — keep this hermetic.
  Fixtures have their own tests via the harness binary.
- Test images should be small to keep CI fast.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- test

## References
- GPU_SCAFFOLD (the code under test).
- ft-ombfl (parent).
notes:
## Polish pass 2026-04-27 (perf budget + edge cases)

### Performance budget correction
Original "<100ms per fixture (1080p)" was wrong-scaled. Terminal
fixtures are typically 800x600 or 960x720 (a viewport-cell grid).
Budget:
- 800x600: <30ms per fixture.
- 1280x800: <50ms per fixture.
- Stress fixtures (50-pane 4K): <500ms acceptable.

### Additional edge cases to test
12. **NaN/Inf handling**: synthetic image with f16 NaN values
    (in case a future shader emits them) — comparator should
    detect-and-error, not silently pass.
13. **Alpha-channel blending edge**: identical RGB but different
    A → comparator should detect (or document tolerance).
14. **One-pixel width image**: degenerate-but-valid input.
15. **Unicode-named fixture path**: Path with Cyrillic / CJK
    characters; comparator must handle non-ASCII paths.

### Property-based test detail
Use `proptest` crate. Generators:
- Random 32x32 RGBA image.
- Random per-pixel noise of variable magnitude.
- Property: `compare(img, img + noise(M)) == PASS iff M <= tolerance`.

### Coverage gate
- 90% line coverage minimum on comparator code.
- 95% branch coverage minimum on the decision tree.
- Fail CI if either drops.
close_reason: 30 unit tests for the comparator landed (28 from cod_2 swept up by linter into a5a209fe + 2 boundary tests in 869773dd). Coverage: identical/diff (within/at/over l_inf), SSIM properties (identical/constant/local-block-degrades), threshold override (loose l_inf, structural fraction note), dimension-mismatch error path, diff-PNG red marking + all-different overflow guard, perf budget, alpha-channel detection, degenerate (1x1, 1xN, 0-height) sizes, serde roundtrip, metrics JSON-key contract, plus 4 proptest properties (zero-delta, uniform-delta-l_inf-counter, single-overshoot-fail, dimension-mismatch). Mutation-test verified: flipping the l_inf gate from <= to < trips the boundary test.

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness] E2E test script with structured JSON-line logging: full harness run + diff artifact emission + summary report
description:
# GPU harness — e2e test script

## Background
The harness binary runs in cargo test, but a thin wrapper script
provides:
- A single command (`scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh`) developers can run
  locally.
- Structured JSON-line logs that are CI-friendly.
- Automatic diff-PNG artifact collection on failure.
- Summary-report generation.

This bead authors that wrapper.

## Why this matters
- Cargo test's default output isn't structured well for CI artifact
  handling.
- Local developers want a one-liner that mirrors what CI does.
- Failure triage is dramatically faster when diff PNGs are
  auto-collected (rather than developers having to manually export
  them from cargo test cache).

## Scope
1. `scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh` — a Bash wrapper that:
   - Sets up a hermetic temp dir for the run.
   - Runs `cargo test --test gpu_regression -- --nocapture
     --format=json` (or similar).
   - Tees stderr/stdout to a per-run log file
     /tmp/gpu-harness-<timestamp>/run.log.
   - Collects all diff PNGs into /tmp/gpu-harness-<timestamp>/diffs/.
   - Generates a summary.html (lightweight static page) with each
     failed fixture's golden + actual + diff side-by-side.
   - Exits 0 if all pass; non-zero with a single-line summary if any
     fail.
2. Each phase emits JSON-line events to stderr:
   {"phase":"setup","tmpdir":"<path>"},
   {"phase":"run","exit_code":N},
   {"phase":"collect-diffs","count":N,"dest":"<path>"},
   {"phase":"summary-html","path":"<path>"},
   {"phase":"exit","code":N,"failed_fixtures":[...]}.
3. Document usage in scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh header and in
   tests/golden/gpu/README.md.
4. CI workflow uses this script (so local + CI behavior is
   identical).

## Out of scope
- Replacing cargo test as the test runner.
- Cross-fixture concurrency (cargo test handles).

## Approach
1. Author the script with `set -uo pipefail`.
2. Use a per-run timestamp dir to keep history.
3. Use `jq` for JSON-line parsing if needed for the summary HTML.
4. Test locally with all-pass and one-fail scenarios.
5. Wire into CI (the ci-wiring bead consumes this script).

## Acceptance criteria
- scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh exists and works locally.
- All phases emit JSON-line logs.
- Failure path produces a usable summary.html.
- shellcheck passes on the script.
- Documented in scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh header + tests/golden/
  gpu/README.md.

## Testing
- Pass-path: run on a known-passing fixture set; assert exit 0,
  no diffs collected, summary.html shows zero failures.
- Fail-path: run with a temporarily-mutated fixture; assert non-zero
  exit, diffs collected, summary.html shows the failure.
- Logging: capture all JSON-line events, assert phase ordering.
- shellcheck: pass.

## Risks / considerations
- The summary.html should be minimal-deps (no external CDN); use
  inline CSS/JS so it works offline.
- Be careful with quoting: failing fixture names may contain
  spaces or special chars; use null-byte-safe shell idioms.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- test
- e2e

## References
- GPU_SCAFFOLD (the binary this wraps).
- GPU_RENDERER (the renderer the harness invokes).
- ft-ombfl (parent).
notes:
## Polish pass 2026-04-27 (e2e wrapper details)

### summary.html scope (clarification)
The summary.html artifact is NICE-TO-HAVE, not required for v1.
Required: a summary.json with shape:
```json
{
  "run_id": "<timestamp>",
  "total": N, "passed": N, "failed": N,
  "duration_ms": N,
  "failures": [
    {"fixture": "X", "ssim": 0.94, "linf": 12,
     "golden": "tests/golden/gpu/X/golden.png",
     "actual": "/tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/diffs/X.actual.png",
     "diff": "/tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/diffs/X.diff.png"}
  ]
}
```
The HTML wrapper is a follow-on if useful (a thin Tera/handlebars
template over summary.json — file as separate ticket if v1 ships
without it).

### Bash quoting for fixture names
Fixture names must NOT contain spaces or shell metachars (enforce
in scaffold via fixture-loader validation: fail-fast if a fixture
dir name contains anything outside [a-zA-Z0-9-_]).

### CI artifact upload pattern
- /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/ → upload as a single tarball
  (`actions/upload-artifact@v4`) to keep the UI clean.
- Retain artifacts for 7 days minimum (longer for release-tag
  builds).

### Local-developer ergonomics
After a failure, print to terminal:
```
✗ X fixture(s) failed. Diff artifacts:
    /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/diffs/X.diff.png
    /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/diffs/Y.diff.png
  Open with: open /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/diffs/
  Summary: /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/summary.json
```
This shaves ~30 sec off triage.
close_reason: gpu harness e2e wrapper added

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness] CI wiring: dedicated GPU-test job + diff artifact upload + perf-report artifact
description:
# GPU harness — CI wiring

## Background
The harness binary (GPU_SCAFFOLD), e2e wrapper (GPU_E2E),
fixtures (multiple beads), and frame-time reporter (GPU_FRAMETIME)
all need to run in CI. This bead is the integration into GitHub
Actions.

## Why this matters
- Tests that don't run in CI don't catch regressions.
- Diff artifacts uploaded on failure make triage immediate.
- Perf reports archived per CI run enable historical trend analysis.

## Scope
1. Add a dedicated CI job (or extend existing ci.yml):
   - Job name: `gpu-regression`.
   - Runner: macOS (per design doc — pinned for determinism).
   - Steps: checkout + cache cargo + run scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh.
   - On failure: upload /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/diffs/ and
     /tmp/gpu-harness-<ts>/summary.html as artifacts.
   - Always: upload tests/golden/gpu/perf-report.json as artifact.
2. Pin the macOS runner version (e.g., macos-15) so renderer
   determinism doesn't drift.
3. Add a "release-blocker" status: if gpu-regression fails on a
   release tag, block the release workflow.
4. Document the renderer-determinism caveat in the workflow
   YAML and in tests/golden/gpu/README.md.

## Out of scope
- Linux GPU CI (renderer determinism on llvmpipe is a separate
  effort).
- Self-hosted GPU runners (premature optimization).

## Approach
1. Read existing .github/workflows/ to find the right insertion
   point (extend ci.yml or add a new file).
2. Add the gpu-regression job.
3. Wire artifact upload via actions/upload-artifact@v4 (if-no-files-
   found=ignore for the perf report; warn for diffs since absence
   means all passed).
4. Test by inducing a regression PR; confirm CI fails and artifacts
   are uploaded.

## Acceptance criteria
- gpu-regression job exists in CI; runs on every PR + main push.
- Failure uploads diffs + summary.html.
- Always uploads perf-report.json.
- Job runs in <10 min on the pinned macOS runner.
- Release workflow respects gpu-regression status.

## Testing
- CI dry-run: open a PR with a one-pixel mutation in a fixture;
  confirm CI fails, artifacts uploaded.
- Performance: assert wall time <10 min.
- Logging: CI log contains the JSON-line events from
  scripts/test-gpu-harness.sh.

## Risks / considerations
- macOS runners are slower and more expensive than Linux. Make
  sure cargo caching is aggressive.
- Pinning macos-15 means we'll need to update annually when GitHub
  retires that image.
- If goldens drift on a runner image update, treat that as a
  separate ticket — don't accept goldens silently.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- ci

## References
- GPU_SCAFFOLD, GPU_E2E, GPU_FRAMETIME (prerequisites).
- .github/workflows/ (existing CI infra).
- ft-ombfl (parent).
notes:
## Polish pass 2026-04-27 (CI specifics)

### Runtime budget
Target <5 min wall (was <10). With caching:
- Restore cargo cache: <30s.
- Build harness binary (incremental): <2 min.
- Run harness (≤30 fixtures × 50ms): <5s.
- Upload artifacts: <30s.
- Total: ~3 min.
If first-build (no cache), bump to <8 min.

### Job name and YAML location
- Workflow file: extend existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (don't
  proliferate workflow files unless needed).
- Job name: `gpu-regression`.
- Required-status: yes (block PRs that fail this).

### macOS runner deprecation handling
- Pin `runs-on: macos-15` initially.
- Document a "runner-image-update" follow-on bead due in ~12 months
  (when macos-15 retires).
- The runner-update follow-on must regenerate goldens (font/driver
  drift) — file as `[ft-ombfl][maintenance]` follow-on with explicit
  steps.

### perf-baseline file management
- Initial baseline: committed by GPU_FRAMETIME bead.
- Updates: only via `--update-baseline` flag with explicit reviewer
  approval.
- CI does NOT update baseline automatically.

### Caching strategy
- `actions/cache@v4` keyed on Cargo.lock + harness source hash.
- tests/fixtures/fonts/ as a separate static asset (rarely changes;
  cache aggressively).
close_reason: Added required GPU regression aggregate check with macOS 15 Metal lane, Linux llvmpipe lane, and uploaded wrapper artifacts

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness][stretch] Stress fixtures: many panes / rapid resize / dpi changes / extreme content
description:
# GPU harness — stress fixtures (stretch)

## Background
Once the core fixtures + comparator + CI are landed, this bead adds
stress-class fixtures that exercise the renderer at scale: many
panes (50+), rapid synthetic resize sequences, DPI scaling
transitions, extreme content (1MB scrollback).

## Why this matters
- Real swarm sessions run 6-15 panes routinely; stress at 50+ surfaces
  a different class of bug (texture cache eviction, glyph atlas
  reflow, font cache pressure).
- DPI transitions (drag window between Retina + non-Retina monitors)
  are a known regression class.
- Extreme content (huge scrollback, very long lines) can crash naive
  renderers.

## Scope
Author 4 stress fixtures under tests/golden/gpu/stress/:
1. **stress-50-panes/**: 50-pane grid layout, deterministic content
   per pane.
2. **stress-rapid-resize/**: a sequence of viewport sizes (smoke-
   test the renderer doesn't crash on rapid changes; pin a final-
   state golden after the sequence).
3. **stress-dpi-1.0-2.0/**: same content rendered at dpi=1.0 and
   dpi=2.0; verify no glyph regression at scale.
4. **stress-1mb-scrollback/**: a pane with 1MB of generated content;
   render the bottom-of-scrollback view.

## Out of scope
- Real-time animation testing (timing-sensitive).
- Multi-monitor span fixtures.

## Approach
1. Each fixture's input.json may need a generator script (especially
   stress-50-panes and stress-1mb-scrollback). Use a one-off Python
   or Rust generator stored under tests/golden/gpu/stress/_generators/.
2. Generate goldens via --update-goldens.
3. Verify each runs in <5s wall time (so stress doesn't slow the
   main suite).
4. Decide whether stress runs on every PR or only on release-tag
   builds — recommend release-only for cost.

## Acceptance criteria
- All 4 stress fixtures committed.
- Each runs to PASS.
- stress-50-panes render <5s.
- DPI transition fixture detects glyph regressions at 2x scale.

## Testing
- Each fixture self-tests.
- Stress-50-panes: capture per-fixture render_ms; assert
  proportional to baseline 5-pane fixture (sanity).
- Mutation: introduce a glyph cache regression (force eviction
  every frame); confirm stress-50-panes detects it via render_ms
  spike or visual diff.

## Risks / considerations
- Generator scripts must be deterministic (seed any RNG).
- Stress fixtures should NOT block the main CI lane — run them on
  a separate label-gated workflow or on release tags only.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- stretch

## References
- GPU_SCAFFOLD, GPU_RENDERER, GPU_CI (prerequisites).
- ft-ombfl (parent).
notes:
## Polish pass round 2 (stress-class regression detection)

### Stress regressions are different from fixture failures
A stress fixture might pass the SSIM check but fail because:
- It rendered in 5x baseline time (perf regression).
- It used 10x baseline atlas pages (resource regression).
- It allocated 50x baseline heap (memory regression).

The stress-fixture run must compare against a stress-specific
baseline (NOT the regular fixture-run baseline).

### Stress baseline file
Add tests/golden/gpu/stress/perf-baseline.json with:
- Per-stress-fixture render_ms (median of 3 runs).
- Per-stress-fixture atlas_pages, glyphs_cached.
- Per-stress-fixture max RSS during render (via /usr/bin/time
  or platform equivalent).

Stress regression thresholds:
- render_ms: 30% (stress is more variable).
- atlas_pages: 20%.
- max_rss: 25%.

### Memory leak detection via repeat-render
For stress-rapid-resize: the harness should run the resize
sequence 10x in a single process. If max_rss grows monotonically
across iterations, that's a leak. Flag if growth >10% from first
to tenth iteration.

This is a substantial extra deliverable — moves stress from "P3
stretch" to "P3 with concrete value". OK either way; if you
want to keep stress lean, file the leak-detection as a separate
follow-on under stress.

### Run schedule
- Stress fixtures: run on RELEASE TAG builds only (not every PR)
  to avoid CI cost.
- On main-branch pushes: run stress weekly via cron-scheduled
  workflow.
- On release tags: run stress as a release-blocker.

### Logging
Stress runs emit detailed per-iteration logs to make leak
detection feasible. Log volume larger here:
~10 iterations × 4 fixtures × ~10 events = 400 events per
stress run. Cap at 5000 lines / 5MB; archive via CI artifacts.
close_reason: GPU stress fixtures shipped and verified

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness] Fixture authoring guide: how to add a new visual regression fixture
description:
# GPU regression harness — fixture authoring guide

## Background
After GPU_SCAFFOLD lands and the first batch of fixtures (text,
CJK, box, cursor, selection, multi-pane) is in place, future
agents will want to add new fixtures (for new bug classes, new
features, new edge cases). Without a guide, each new fixture
becomes an exercise in spelunking through existing fixtures.

## Why this matters
- Onboarding cost: a new agent should be able to author a fixture
  in <30 min from reading the guide alone.
- Consistency: pinned font set, meta.json schema, golden-update
  procedure must stay uniform across all fixtures.
- Coverage: the guide should encourage filing a fixture every
  time a regression slips through (catch bug → file fixture →
  prevent recurrence).

## Scope (single docs file)
docs/gpu-fixture-authoring.md with sections:
1. **Anatomy of a fixture**:
   - input.json schema (required fields, optional fields, examples).
   - meta.json schema (viewport, dpi, color_space, tolerance,
     font_set, blink_disabled, cursor_blink_disabled,
     ime_disabled, etc.).
   - expected.json (optional sanity-check schema).
   - golden.png format expectations (sRGB, RGBA8, dimensions).
2. **Authoring procedure** (step-by-step):
   - Decide what regression class the fixture catches.
   - Pick a fixture name (kebab-case, descriptive, ≤40 chars).
   - Author input.json + meta.json by hand.
   - Run `cargo test --test gpu_regression --features gpu-headless
     -- --update-goldens <fixture-name>` to generate golden.png.
   - Manually inspect golden.png in an image viewer.
   - Run the test without --update-goldens to verify it passes.
   - Commit fixture directory + reference the bug class in commit.
3. **Determinism checklist** (mandatory pre-commit gates):
   - Font set pinned (subset of tests/fixtures/fonts/).
   - cursor_blink_disabled=true.
   - ime_disabled=true.
   - LC_ALL=C, TZ=UTC enforced.
   - No system-fonts fallback.
4. **Common mistakes**:
   - Trailing whitespace in input.json strings (renders differently
     than expected).
   - Mixing sRGB and linear color spaces.
   - Forgetting to disable cursor blink.
   - Using non-OFL fonts.
   - Path with spaces or non-ASCII chars (rejected by loader).
5. **Updating an existing fixture** (when behavior intentionally
   changes):
   - Document why in PR body.
   - Use --update-goldens with manual review.
   - Diff inspect old vs new golden side-by-side.
6. **Adding a fixture for a real regression**:
   - Workflow: bug filed → reproduce locally → create fixture
     that captures the BROKEN state in a "broken-golden.png" →
     fix the bug → re-generate golden against fixed state →
     commit fixture + fix together.

## Out of scope
- Test runner internals (covered by GPU_SCAFFOLD docs).
- CI configuration (covered by GPU_CI).
- Renderer internals (covered by GPU_RENDERER).

## Approach
1. After GPU_SCAFFOLD, GPU_RENDERER, and at least 2 fixture beads
   land, draft this guide using those as concrete reference cases.
2. Test the guide by having a fresh agent author one new fixture
   (e.g., "tab-character handling") using only the guide.
3. Iterate based on the friction points.
4. Cross-link from tests/golden/gpu/README.md and from
   docs/operator-runbook.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- docs/gpu-fixture-authoring.md exists.
- All 6 sections present.
- A fresh agent can author a NEW fixture (not in the original 14
  beads) using only the guide. Success criteria: the new fixture
  passes CI on first attempt.
- Cross-links from tests/golden/gpu/README.md.

## Testing
- Validation walkthrough: have a fresh agent author one new
  fixture from the guide alone. Document any friction in this
  bead's notes.
- Render check: open the markdown in a previewer; section
  hierarchy is clean.
- Cross-link integrity: each "see X" resolves.
- Logging: validation walkthrough emits a JSON-line trace per
  guide step the new agent follows; document any step that
  needed clarification.

## Risks / considerations
- This guide should be SHORT (≤8 KB). Longer = readers skip.
- Keep examples concrete: include a complete worked example of
  authoring a fixture from scratch (input.json + meta.json
  shown in full).
- Don't duplicate content from GPU_SCAFFOLD's README — link.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- docs

## References
- GPU_SCAFFOLD (the harness this guide explains).
- GPU_RENDERER (the renderer behind the harness).
- ft-ombfl (parent).
- All fixture beads (concrete examples).
close_reason: Added GPU harness fixture authoring guide and linked it from the fixture README

title: [ft-ombfl][gpu-harness][stretch] Explore Linux GPU CI: llvmpipe/swrast determinism + cost analysis vs macos-15
description:
# Linux GPU CI exploration

## Background
GPU_CI (ft-ombfl.13) pins macOS-15 as the GPU regression test
runner. macOS runners are ~5x more expensive than Ubuntu runners
on GitHub Actions ($0.08/min vs $0.016/min as of 2026-Q1).
For a project that runs CI on every PR, the cost adds up.

This bead explores running GPU regression tests on Linux via
llvmpipe (Mesa software rasterizer) or swrast. The renderer-
determinism question is non-trivial: software rasterization
may produce slightly different output from Metal due to
floating-point rounding, AA strategy, etc.

## Why this matters
- CI cost reduction (5x cheaper compute).
- Linux runners are faster to provision (less queue time).
- A Linux-portable harness is more portable in general.

## Scope (P4 stretch — do NOT block other work)
1. **Determinism investigation**: render the same fixtures on
   macOS-Metal vs Linux-llvmpipe. Measure SSIM / L∞ across
   platforms. Decide:
   - Tight enough → run on Linux primarily.
   - Loose → run separately on each, with platform-specific
     goldens.
   - Hopelessly different → keep macOS-only and accept cost.
2. **Cost-benefit analysis**: model the per-month CI cost
   for the project's PR volume; project savings.
3. **Determinism work** (if go-decision):
   - Pin Mesa + llvmpipe versions in CI runner image.
   - Pin LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 and similar env vars.
   - Possibly: use Vulkan + lavapipe instead of OpenGL +
     llvmpipe (more deterministic).
4. **Recommendation**: file a decision bead with the result.

## Out of scope
- Hardware-GPU CI runners (premature optimization).
- Cross-vendor renderer determinism (Intel vs AMD vs NVIDIA
  drivers — out of scope for software-only path).

## Approach
1. Build the harness with a feature flag for software-renderer
   path on Linux.
2. Render the existing fixture set on a Linux dev box; compare
   SSIM / L∞ to macOS goldens.
3. Document the determinism delta in a spike doc:
   docs/spike/gpu-ci-linux-feasibility.md.
4. Cost-benefit table.
5. Go/no-go recommendation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Determinism spike doc exists with concrete SSIM/L∞ numbers
  for ≥5 representative fixtures.
- Cost-benefit table exists with ($/month) projections.
- Go/no-go recommendation lands as a follow-on bead (one of:
  (a) implement Linux CI, (b) keep macOS-only with cost
  acceptance, (c) defer indefinitely with conditions for
  re-evaluation).
- This bead closes with a clear outcome.

## Testing
- The spike runs the existing fixture set on Linux; goldens
  are NOT updated (it's an investigation, not a CI change).
- Logging: per-fixture comparison output recorded as JSON-line:
  {"fixture":"X","platform":"linux","ssim_vs_macos_golden":F,
   "linf_vs_macos_golden":N,"determinism_class":"tight|loose|broken"}.

## Risks / considerations
- llvmpipe quality varies by Mesa version; pin a specific
  version to make the spike reproducible.
- Intermediate results are not actionable by themselves;
  present a clear recommendation, not raw numbers.
- This is a stretch — do NOT block tier-1 GPU work on it.

## Labels
- postswarm-2026-04-27
- gpu-harness
- linux
- stretch
- cost

## References
- GPU_CI (ft-ombfl.13) — the macOS-pinned baseline.
- Mesa llvmpipe documentation.
- GitHub Actions runner pricing.
