title: MCP degraded bridge still exposes mutating mission/tx tools without audited wrapper
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs found that degraded no-db mode is broader than the file claims and still exposes mutation-capable tools without the AuditedToolHandler success/failure audit wrapper.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:88-99 routes build_server through build_server_degraded, so legacy/default builds enter the no-db path.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:148-212 registers the base catalog before the db_path split. That catalog includes WaTxRunTool, WaTxRollbackTool, WaMissionPauseTool, WaMissionResumeTool, and WaMissionAbortTool at lines 167-205 even when db_path is None.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:216-325 wraps only the storage-backed branch in AuditedToolHandler; the base mutation tools are registered only through FormatAwareToolHandler.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:140-147 documents AuditedToolHandler as the wrapper that records every tool call, and lines 168-220 show the audit write path. The degraded base mutation tools bypass that wrapper.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs:3801-4021 shows wa.tx_run performs policy-gated tx execution and storage writes, and lines 5277-5398/5424-5536/5562+ show mission pause/resume/abort are side-effecting control tools.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs:423-470 tests only the degraded counter, not the actual degraded tool catalog or audit wrapper coverage.

Why it matters:
A database-less MCP bridge can still advertise and execute mission/tx mutation controls while the normal audited tool-call wrapper is unavailable. That violates the degraded-mode expectation created by br-ft-647cj and makes successful mutation calls invisible to the MCP audit stream.

Proposed remediation:
Classify bridge registrations by read-only, storage-backed, and mutation-capable surface. In build_server_degraded, either omit mutation-capable tx/mission tools or replace them with fail-closed audit-unavailable handlers. Add a catalog regression test that asserts the no-db server exposes only the explicitly allowed degraded tools and that every mutation-capable MCP tool is audit-wrapped or unavailable when no db_path is present.
notes:
Shipped fix: classified MCP bridge tool registrations into degraded-safe (read-only/no-storage) and db-gated (mutation-capable) tiers. The 5 mutation-capable mission/tx tools that pre-fix were registered unconditionally in the base catalog with NO audit wrapper are now gated to the if-Some(db_path) branch and wrapped in AuditedToolHandler — every mutation call lands in the audit stream.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_bridge.rs):

1. New pub(crate) const DEGRADED_MODE_BASE_TOOL_NAMES (12 names) — authoritative degraded-mode tool catalog (read-only diagnostics + no-storage tools).

2. New pub(crate) const DB_GATED_MUTATING_TOOL_NAMES (5 names: wa.tx_run, wa.tx_rollback, wa.mission_pause, wa.mission_resume, wa.mission_abort) — mutation-capable tools that REQUIRE storage + audit wrapper.

3. MCP_BRIDGE_DEGRADED_MODE_SKIPPED_ENTRIES bumped from 20 to 25 (was: 14 audited tools + 7 resources - 1 no-db get_text = 20; now: 14 + 5 newly-gated mutating + 7 - 1 = 25).

4. Removed WaTxRunTool, WaTxRollbackTool, WaMissionPauseTool, WaMissionResumeTool, WaMissionAbortTool from the unconditional base catalog (build_server_inner lines ~167-205). Replaced with a comment block referencing the relocation.

5. Added the 5 mutating tools to the if-Some(ref db_path) branch each wrapped in AuditedToolHandler::new(...). The tools themselves don't read db_path (their constructors take Config + rate_limiter), but AuditedToolHandler needs it to write audit records.

6. Updated the degraded-mode tracing::warn message to enumerate the 5 newly-gated mutating tools alongside the existing 14 storage-backed names.

Tests added (5 regression tests at end of mod tests):

- degraded_server_does_not_expose_mutating_tools_ft_p4y8d: builds a degraded Server, introspects via Server::tools(), asserts NONE of the DB_GATED_MUTATING_TOOL_NAMES appear.
- degraded_server_exposes_exactly_base_catalog_ft_p4y8d: builds degraded Server, asserts every DEGRADED_MODE_BASE_TOOL_NAMES entry IS present, and (when mcp-client feature is off) the count matches exactly.
- full_server_exposes_mutating_tools_when_db_path_set_ft_p4y8d: builds a full Server with tempdir db_path, asserts ALL 5 DB_GATED_MUTATING_TOOL_NAMES appear (round-trip — what's withheld in degraded IS exposed in full).
- degraded_and_mutating_catalogs_are_disjoint_ft_p4y8d: contract-level invariant test independent of any runtime build — pins that the two const lists are disjoint.
- every_degraded_tool_appears_in_documented_catalog_ft_p4y8d: property-style sweep — for every tool actually registered in degraded mode, that name MUST be in DEGRADED_MODE_BASE_TOOL_NAMES (catches drift in either direction).

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 1m11s clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new) — mcp_bridge.rs is feature-gated so unchanged behavior at this build
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features --features mcp,subprocess-bridge: 1m18s clean (226 pre-existing warnings, none new) — natural feature set for mcp_bridge.rs
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
- Classify bridge registrations by read-only, storage-backed, mutation-capable: DONE (two pub(crate) const lists)
- In build_server_degraded, either omit mutation-capable tx/mission tools OR replace with fail-closed handlers: DONE (omitted from degraded catalog)
- Wrap mutation-capable tools in AuditedToolHandler when db_path is present: DONE
- Add catalog regression test asserting no-db server exposes only allowed tools: DONE (5 tests covering both directions)
- Assert every mutation-capable MCP tool is audit-wrapped or unavailable when no db_path: DONE (degraded_server_does_not_expose_mutating_tools_ft_p4y8d)

title: [infra][rch] Make workers capabilities --refresh satisfy CLI response budget
description:
## Problem

The FrankenTerm proof substrate is restored, but the exact installed command `rch --json workers capabilities --refresh` still fails with `Timed out waiting for daemon response` even though remote workers are reachable and direct long-timeout daemon refresh returns all workers.

## Evidence

- Direct Unix-socket request to `/workers/capabilities?refresh=true` with a longer client timeout returned all 8 worker IDs.
- The installed CLI path `rch --json workers capabilities --refresh` still exits 1 after its daemon response timeout.
- RCH source diagnosis: `rch/src/commands/helpers.rs` has a 10s `DAEMON_COMMAND_IO_TIMEOUT` for the whole daemon response; `rch/src/commands/workers.rs` sends `GET /workers/capabilities?refresh=true`; `rchd/src/api.rs` parses the flag; `rchd/src/workers.rs` refreshes by looping over workers serially; `rchd/src/health.rs` gives each SSH capability probe a 10s timeout. On an 8-worker fleet this can exceed the CLI budget even when the endpoint eventually succeeds.
- Split from `ft-1iboz` after the remote-only smoke and the ft-rz0eb.4 resource-cockpit conformance harness passed through RCH.

## Acceptance

- `rch --json workers capabilities --refresh` returns a JSON response under the installed CLI path on the current 8-worker fleet, or returns a structured partial/stale response instead of timing out.
- The fix preserves live worker reachability evidence for operators; it must not silently treat stale cache as a fresh refresh.
- Add focused tests or upstream RCH evidence in the owning RCH repository if the implementation fix lands outside FrankenTerm.

## Non-goals

- Do not restart or kill the shared RCH daemon as part of diagnosis.
- Do not run heavy Cargo locally.

title: [ft-l1jgo.approvals] Migrate approval/plan storage.rs callsites to trait-typed pooled_backend
description:
## Scope (carved from ft-l1jgo, BLOCKED on ft-19rj3 substrate)

Migrate the **approvals + prepared plans** call sites in storage.rs from direct `rusqlite::Connection` (or `open_rusqlite_backend`) to the **trait-typed** `pooled_backend` helper landing in ft-19rj3.

## Methods in scope

consume_approval_token, consume_approval_token_by_code, consume_prepared_plan, count_active_approvals (+ `with_cx` siblings)

## Migration target pattern (default — swap-ready)

```rust
Self::spawn_blocking_storage(move || {
    pooled_backend(db_path.as_str(), |backend: &dyn StorageBackend| {
        // existing closure body, byte-identical, but using
        // ONLY trait methods + module-level helpers
        // (count_table_where, query_row_typed, query_map_typed,
        //  execute_typed, list_user_tables, etc).
    })
})
```

## Acceptance (trait-only contract)

1. `grep -c open_rusqlite_backend storage.rs` decreases by the migration count for this domain.
2. **Closure body uses ONLY trait methods or module-level `*_backend` helpers.** No `conn.execute(`, `conn.prepare(`, `conn.query_row(`, `conn.query_map(`, no `RusqliteBackend::` concrete-type calls. Type-erasure via `&dyn StorageBackend` enforces this at compile time.
3. All this domain's existing unit + integration tests pass against the migrated callsites.

## Escape hatch (rusqlite-typed) — document if used

If the operation requires rusqlite-specific access (FTS5 init, `pragma_update` mutation, prepared-statement iterator loops), use the existing `pooled_rusqlite_backend` and document in the bead's close-message:
- which callsite(s) used the escape hatch
- the specific rusqlite feature that has no trait equivalent
- (optional) propose a trait-widening sibling-bead if it's worth lifting

The maintenance domain (ft-gz4dt) is the most likely to need carve-outs; this domain is expected to migrate cleanly.

title: [codebase-audit][robot/MCP] error-envelope schema is unvalidated — runtime gate (ft-5ikbd) only covers success_envelope
description:
## Domain gap

ft-5ikbd (commit 04911fff7) shipped the runtime jsonschema validator
for robot envelopes. The fixture loader at
`tests/conformance_robot_envelope_schema.rs:116` extracts the
**`success_envelope`** field from each `wa_*.json` golden.

The MCP/robot envelope schema (`docs/json-schema/wa-robot-envelope.json`)
covers BOTH success and failure shapes via the `if/then` clause:

```json
"if": { "properties": { "ok": { "const": true } } },
"then": { "required": ["data"] }
```

…and the schema separately requires `error` + `error_code`
fields with a `^robot\\.[a-z_]+$` pattern when `ok=false`.

**The runtime validator never exercises the `ok=false` branch
against real fixtures.** The `wa_*.json` fixtures only carry a
`success_envelope` field. Error envelopes ARE produced in
production (`MCP_ERR_PANE_NOT_FOUND`, `MCP_ERR_POLICY`,
`MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS` per `mcp_tools.rs`), but no golden pins
their shape and no test validates them.

## Why this is a real defect

Concrete failure scenarios:

1. **A new error variant ships with a malformed `error_code`.**
   The schema requires `^robot\\.[a-z_]+$`. A code like
   `robot.not-implemented` (hyphen) or `robot.NotFound` (caps)
   would slip through today because no test runs an error
   envelope through the validator.

2. **A `data: null` leak.** Per the schema's `if/then`,
   when `ok=true`, `data` MUST be present. The complement —
   when `ok=false`, the `data` field is OPTIONAL but if
   present it must be parseable. A handler that returns
   `ok=false` PLUS a malformed `data` slips by.

3. **Hint string contains a secret.** The `hint` field is
   free-form. ft-3se13 (security audit) catches this for
   the decision log; the same risk exists at the response
   surface but no current test asserts the hint goes through
   redaction.

ft-5ikbd's three falsification gates
(`missing-required-field`, `malformed-error-code`,
`ok-true-without-data`) prove the validator works on
SYNTHETIC error envelopes — but no REAL production error
path is tested.

## Suggested approach

1. **Extend the fixture corpus** at
   `tests/golden_robot_envelope/`:
   - Add a sibling `error_envelope` field to each `wa_*.json`
     fixture that has a known error path (e.g., `wa_state.json`
     with the "wezterm not running" error).
   - Or: add new `wa_*_error.json` fixtures that pin specific
     error variants (one per error_code constant in
     `mcp_tools.rs`).

2. **Extend the runtime validator** at
   `tests/conformance_robot_envelope_schema.rs`:
   - Add a parallel `every_golden_error_envelope_validates_against_schema`
     test that loads `error_envelope` (or the new error fixtures)
     and validates each against the schema.
   - Add a coverage assertion: every error_code constant in
     production code (`mcp_tools.rs::MCP_ERR_*`) MUST appear
     in at least one fixture (so adding a new error_code
     forces a fixture update).

3. **Production hint redaction**: route every `McpEnvelope::error`
   call through `engine.redact_secrets()` for the `hint` field
   before it leaves the process. Mirror ft-3se13's audit-log fix.

## Out of scope

- The synthetic falsification gates already in ft-5ikbd (they're
  fine; this bead extends real-fixture coverage).
- The MCP coverage matrix (ft-zaqi8 — that's a higher-level
  spec/test-mapping work).

## Acceptance criteria

- ≥10 error envelope fixtures pinned (one per error_code constant
  used in production).
- A new test validates each against the schema.
- The coverage assertion fails red when a new `MCP_ERR_*` constant
  is added without a fixture.
- Production `McpEnvelope::error` redacts the hint field.

## References

- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/conformance_robot_envelope_schema.rs:116`
  (the success-only fixture loader)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs` (`MCP_ERR_*`
  constants)
- `docs/json-schema/wa-robot-envelope.json` (schema covers both
  branches)
- ft-5ikbd (sibling: runtime success-envelope validator —
  already shipped)
- ft-3se13 (sibling: secrets in audit log — same
  redactor-on-write principle applies to hint field)

Filed by cc_1 codebase audit, 2026-04-28.

title: [Audit] storage pane_bookmark tags reader silently drops malformed JSON
description:
PHASE 3 AUDIT — silent serde drop in storage pane_bookmark tags reader.

Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:10578

```rust
let tags_raw = reader.optional_string(3).map_err(...)?;
let tags = tags_raw.and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(&s).ok());
```

The pane_bookmark.tags column stores a JSON Vec<String>. On parse failure (malformed tag JSON, schema-skewed shape), the reader silently returns tags=None — indistinguishable from "no tags set". Operators running tag-based filtering see bookmarks missing from queries with no signal.

Why it matters: bookmarks are a search/recall affordance. Tag-based filtering relies on the JSON Vec round-tripping. A silent drop hides the bookmark from every tag-filtered query, making it appear deleted even though the row is present.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-ncijf, ft-r3d4e, ft-jtcrv, ft-zs9v0.

1. Add PANE_BOOKMARK_TAGS_PARSE_DROP_COUNT AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset.
2. Replace .ok() with explicit match: bump counter + emit structured tracing::warn carrying bookmark_id, pane_id, error, raw_len.
3. Tests: well-formed JSON array parses; malformed bumps; null/missing column doesn't bump.

Note: storage.rs has 8 silent-drop sites in this same file — this one is the most operator-facing (bookmarks → user-facing queries). Other 7 may warrant separate beads if they affect operator workflows.

title: [OBS/SEC] mcp_tools.rs has 4 silent record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx swallows (sibling-class to ft-luav8)
description:
Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs at SHA cf8143498 found 4 silent audit-write swallows that bypass the ft-luav8 mcp_audit_failure_count counter.

## Sites

| Line | Tool | Pattern |
|------|------|---------|
| 5973 | wa.events_annotate | let _ = storage.record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx(&audit_cx, audit).await |
| 6199 | wa.events_triage | same |
| 6427 | wa.events_label (insert) | same |
| 6475 | wa.events_label (remove) | same |

`storage.record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx` returns `Result<i64>` (audit row id). The let _ = swallow drops both the Ok success and the Err failure silently.

## Why it matters

Same defect class as ft-luav8 (closed at 194087f8b — added MCP_AUDIT_FAILURE_COUNT counter for the 4 silent-failure sites in mcp.rs's record_mcp_audit + record_mcp_audit_sync helpers). But ft-luav8's scope was only the record_mcp_audit* helpers in mcp.rs / mcp_helpers.rs. These 4 sites in mcp_tools.rs use the storage method DIRECTLY, bypassing the helpers, so the existing counter does NOT bump on these failures.

Result: a wa.events_annotate / wa.events_triage / wa.events_label call that successfully mutates storage but fails to write the audit record returns success to the MCP client. The audit row is missing. Operators have no signal — no tracing::warn, no counter bump.

This is a fail-open path on a security-relevant surface (event annotation = operator action that should ALWAYS be audited).

## Suggested remediation

Two options:

**Option A** (preferred — matches ft-luav8): replace each let _ = with explicit match. On Err, call crate::mcp::record_mcp_audit_failure() (already pub(crate), used by the existing record_mcp_audit_failure pattern) AND emit a structured tracing::warn with target ft.security.audit, the tool name, and the error.

**Option B**: refactor the 4 sites into a single helper fn record_event_mutation_audit_or_log that wraps the pattern. Single point of policy enforcement for future audit-write fail-open cases.

Recommended: Option A is the smallest single-cycle fix that mirrors ft-luav8's established pattern.

## Acceptance

- All 4 sites replaced with explicit match + counter bump + tracing::warn
- Existing mcp_audit_failure_count() reflects the bumps
- Regression test: force a storage error (or use a test-mock that returns Err), assert the counter increments + the MCP tool's response still succeeds (audit failure does NOT propagate to the client; audit is fire-and-forget per ft-luav8's contract)
notes:
Shipped fix: routed 4 silent record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx swallows in mcp_tools.rs through the existing ft-luav8 MCP_AUDIT_FAILURE_COUNT counter via a new private helper.

Audit context: cc1 PHASE 3 audit on mcp_tools.rs (10K LOC / 6515 prod lines) at SHA cf8143498. mcp_missions.rs + mcp_resources.rs swept clean concurrently. Found 4 silent storage-audit-write swallows that bypass the ft-luav8 counter.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs):

1. Promoted record_mcp_audit_failure() from private to pub(crate) so mcp_tools.rs can call it. Doc-block (br-ft-pgjat) explains: the audit-failure metric is intended to be the single observable signal across ALL silent MCP audit-write paths; siblings of the ft-luav8 sites should use the same counter.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs):

2. New private helper record_event_mutation_audit_or_log(storage, audit_cx, audit, tool_name) that wraps storage.record_audit_action_redacted_with_cx with explicit Err handling. On Err: bumps MCP_AUDIT_FAILURE_COUNT via crate::mcp::record_mcp_audit_failure() AND emits structured tracing::warn (target ft.security.audit) with the tool name + error. Preserves the fire-and-forget contract (audit failures must NOT propagate to the MCP client per ft-luav8's design — client succeeded, audit fidelity gap surfaced via counter + log).

title: [HIGH] full_pipeline_mux_checkpoint_topology still cannot verify pane-tree rollback
description:
Commit 30172171 fixes the vacuous baseline roundtrip, but the test still reduces "topology" to a pane-id set derived from LifecycleRegistry records rather than the restored topology payload.

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/integration_mux_checkpoint_topology.rs:392-423` now compares only `server.registry().snapshot()` pane IDs/count against the baseline and then re-parses `initial_topo_json` as a secondary serde check.

- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/durable_state.rs:159-167,288-314` shows HeadlessMuxServer checkpoints/rollback persist and rebuild only `LifecycleRegistry::snapshot()` entities; there is no topology JSON in the checkpoint path for the test to compare after rollback.

- The test name and comments still claim topology restoration coverage, so this is false confidence on the checkpoint/rollback surface.

Expected fix:
- Either persist/restore topology payloads in the checkpoint path and compare a post-rollback `TopologySnapshot` against the baseline,
- or explicitly narrow/rename this test to registry-membership rollback and add a separate topology persistence/restore integration test.

title: codec: buffered_frame_len accepts oversized tagged_len, allowing memory-exhaustion before MAX_PDU_SIZE fires
description: frankenterm/codec/src/lib.rs:240 buffered_frame_len validates only that the leb128-decoded payload_len fits in usize. It does NOT check against MAX_PDU_SIZE (256 MiB at lib.rs:106). An attacker who sends a frame whose outer tagged_len advertises e.g. 10 GiB forces try_read_and_decode at lib.rs:763-792 into a read loop that keeps extending the caller's buffer 4 KiB at a time until buffer.len() >= total_len — because stream_decode's first step is if buffered_frame_len(buffer)?.is_none() { return Ok(None); }, which short-circuits to 'need more bytes' and never rejects oversize. decode_raw at lib.rs:395-403 DOES reject via MAX_PDU_SIZE, but by then the process has already OOM'd or swapped. Fix: in buffered_frame_len, after decoding payload_len, early-bail if payload_len > MAX_PDU_SIZE so stream_decode returns Err immediately on an oversize header and callers stop accumulating.
close_reason: Landed in 22965865 (fix(codec): reject oversize tagged_len before accumulation in buffered_frame_len). Concurrent-agent commit landed the identical fix + regression test I wrote: MAX_PDU_SIZE early-reject in buffered_frame_len before try_read_and_decode accumulates attacker-advertised gigabytes. Test buffered_frame_len_rejects_oversize_tagged_len_ft_phz7x passes in the 117-test codec suite.

title: Separate Windows socket descriptors from generic handles
description: Mock-code scan found frankenterm/filedescriptor/src/windows.rs still has FIXME comments on FileDescriptor's AsRawSocket/IntoRawSocket impls: they cast a generic RawHandle into RawSocket even when the FileDescriptor owns a pipe/file/console handle. The crate docs for poll correctly say Windows uses WSAPoll and only works with sockets, but the public FileDescriptor type can hold both sockets and non-socket handles. Evidence: OwnedHandle tracks HandleType and can probe Socket vs Pipe, but as_raw_socket/into_raw_socket only debug_assert is_socket_handle and then cast; release builds silently produce invalid SOCKET values for pipes. Tests in frankenterm/filedescriptor/src/lib.rs also include pipe_as_socket_descriptor and poll_pipe_write_end_is_writable assumptions that are valid on Unix but invalid for Windows WSAPoll. Fix shape: add fallible socket-descriptor accessors or a distinct socket wrapper/path, audit Windows callers of as_socket_descriptor/as_raw_socket/into_raw_socket, gate or rewrite Unix-only pipe-as-socket tests, and keep standard AsRawSocket/IntoRawSocket impls only where the type invariant guarantees a socket. RCH-only proof required for the Windows target; if RCH admission is unavailable, record exact blocker.

title: policy RateLimiter pane_counts leak still present: ft-yjt9e methods unwired in PaneDestroyed handler
description: Follow-up to ft-yjt9e (closed in 27ef45e1 + f97e6cac): the tools were added (RateLimiter::remove_pane, gc, gc_at, tracked_pane_entry_count and PolicyEngine::remove_pane/gc_rate_limiter forwarders) but nothing in the runtime teardown path actually calls them. Confirmed by reading runtime.rs:3406 (NativeEvent::PaneDestroyed handler): it tears down cursors, detection_contexts, pane_activity_tracker, and backpressure.cleanup_pane but never touches PolicyEngine. Consequence: the original memory leak ft-yjt9e described (every (pane_id, ActionKind) pair in RateLimiter.pane_counts lingers forever after pane destroy, estimated ~48 MB per 10k destroyed panes in long-running watchers) is still present in production. Two wiring options: (a) thread an Arc<Mutex<PolicyEngine>> through to the runtime so PaneDestroyed can call engine.remove_pane(pane_id) directly; (b) fan out a PaneDestroyed event via the event bus and have the workflow/policy layer subscribe. Option (b) matches the existing fanout architecture and avoids coupling runtime to the policy layer, but requires adding a subscriber. Option (a) is surgical and runtime-local. Recommend (b) for layering. Test: after wiring, a 1000-pane-churn loop must show tracked_pane_entry_count() stays bounded, not linear in total-panes-ever-destroyed.
notes: Investigation finding (2026-04-22): grep across production (non-test) code found NO long-lived PolicyEngine that sees per-pane authorize calls. ConnectorOutboundBridge::policy is instantiated only in tests (1695+). mcp_tools.rs creates fresh engines per tool call (not persistent). workflows/mod.rs PolicyEngine::permissive() uses are also in tests. The actual pane_counts leak described in this bead is therefore LATENT in production — the shape exists but no callsite currently accumulates enough volume to matter. Priority can stay at P2 as defense-in-depth; if a long-lived production holder is added later (direct ConnectorOutboundBridge usage, or a workflow runner that persists its engine), the wiring becomes urgent. See new commit 1f3ae436 which lands the lifecycle event emission (Event::PaneDisappeared) — that primitive is now available for any future policy-layer subscriber.

Regression tests 41cab3bb (runtime emission), policy.rs:7566 (adapter contract), policy.rs:7622 (self-gc bounds pane_counts under unbounded churn). The emitter + adapter contract is now end-to-end; long-lived PolicyEngine holders (ConnectorOutboundBridge et al.) close the leak with a one-liner over EventBus::subscribe.

title: context_budget: compaction events do not update peak token evidence
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:171-174 defines estimated_tokens and peak_tokens as separate tracker fields.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:205-212 update_tokens updates peak_tokens when the observed estimate increases.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:214-238 record_compaction records tokens_before/tokens_after and sets estimated_tokens = tokens_after, but never updates peak_tokens from tokens_before or tokens_after.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:291-305 includes peak_tokens in PaneContextSnapshot, making it operator-visible evidence.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:537-547 tests record_compaction only after update_tokens(90_000), and crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:601-614 covers the same pre-update pattern; no test covers compaction as the first high-water observation.

Impact:
If the pattern engine detects compaction markers with token estimates before any update_tokens call, the snapshot can report total_compactions > 0 while peak_tokens remains 0 or stale. Operators lose the high-water context evidence needed to judge compaction severity.

Proposed remediation:
In record_compaction, update peak_tokens with max(existing peak, tokens_before, tokens_after). Add tests for a fresh tracker receiving record_compaction(90_000, 40_000, ...) and for repeated compactions preserving the maximum observed before/after count.
notes: record_compaction now updates peak_tokens via .max(tokens_before).max(tokens_after). Tests: tracker_record_compaction extended to assert peak_tokens=90_000 (before-call); tracker_record_compaction_first_observation_sets_peak (fresh tracker, no prior update_tokens, peak must reflect tokens_before); tracker_record_compaction_repeated_preserves_max (4-step ladder pinning that lower-pressure events don't overwrite peak, higher-pressure lift it, and unusual after>before events still contribute). Lib check clean (scripts/cargo-local.sh check, 191 warnings, 0 errors).

title: [security] Agent-mail bridge logs raw message bodies through subprocess args
description:
Scope: agent-mail bridge in agent_mail_bridge.rs and subprocess_bridge.rs.

Finding: AgentMailBridge::send_message passes the full subject/body as argv to agent_mail, and SubprocessBridge logs the complete args vector before spawning. Failure and parse-error paths also log raw stdout/stderr previews. No redaction is applied.

title: connector_outbound_bridge: dedup uses OutboundEvent.timestamp_ms as clock — same replay-bypass shape as ft-dijpe (inbound)
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/connector_outbound_bridge.rs:1027` in `process_event`:

```rust
if event.correlation_id.is_some()
    && !self
        .deduplicator
        .check_and_record(&correlation_id, event.timestamp_ms)
{ ... }
```

And line 1080:

```rust
let now_ms = event.timestamp_ms;
```

Both use `event.timestamp_ms` as the dedup/processing clock. `OutboundEvent` is `Serialize + Deserialize` (line 207) with `pub timestamp_ms: u64` (line 216, documented 'Timestamp at source') — any deserialized event carries an attacker-controllable field.

## Shape

Identical to ft-dijpe (connector_inbound_bridge, closed in 0716e112). An OutboundEvent with:

1. correlation_id='spam', timestamp_ms=0 → inserted_at=0 in OutboundDeduplicator.
2. correlation_id='spam', timestamp_ms=ttl_ms+1 → `evict_expired(now=ttl+1)` pops the live entry, `check_and_record` finds cache empty, inserts + returns `true` (new). Replay accepted.

Repeat indefinitely by monotonically increasing the claimed timestamp. Every replay re-fires every matched routing rule → every downstream connector action (Slack post, JIRA ticket, webhook, etc.) fires again without bound.

## Severity

MEDIUM — same as inbound. In the normal path OutboundEvent is constructed internally via `::new()` which uses SystemTime::now(), so a well-behaved caller never triggers this. But any replay path (serde roundtrip from disk, wire-level deserialization, test fixtures promoted to fixtures, misbehaving producer) propagates untrusted timestamps straight into the dedup clock.

## Fix

Mirror ft-dijpe: replace `event.timestamp_ms` with `SystemTime::now()` at the dedup call site so the eviction window is driven by the local clock, not by the event's wire-claimed timestamp. Leave `let now_ms = event.timestamp_ms` at line 1080 alone if it's only used for non-security accounting (history, telemetry); change only the dedup-clock input.

## Test

`outbound_dedup_ignores_attacker_controlled_event_timestamp` mirror of `bridge_dedup_ignores_attacker_controlled_signal_timestamp` (added in 0716e112 for inbound):

* Route event A with cid='replay', timestamp_ms=0 → not deduplicated.
* Route event A with cid='replay', timestamp_ms=u64::MAX/2 → must be flagged deduplicated=true.

Pre-fix, the second route slips past because the attacker's huge timestamp evicts the live entry. Post-fix, the local clock catches both in the same real-time window and dedup works.
close_reason: Fixed in 85a0f350. Mirror of ft-dijpe (inbound, 0716e112): dedup_now_ms now comes from SystemTime::now() instead of the Serialize+Deserialize OutboundEvent.timestamp_ms wire field. Regression test connector_outbound_bridge_dedup_ignores_attacker_controlled_event_timestamp (timestamp_ms=u64::MAX/2 on replay → still flagged deduplicated=true) covers the same attacker-replay shape. Verified: 53 connector_outbound_bridge:: tests passed, 0 failed.

title: Runtime telemetry log sequence counters can wrap
description:
Subsystem: runtime_telemetry in-memory event log

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:2087-2092` stores `sequence`, `total_emitted`, and `total_evicted` as `u64` counters in `RuntimeTelemetryLog`.
- `RuntimeTelemetryLog::append` uses unchecked increments for all three long-lived counters: `self.sequence += 1`, `self.total_emitted += 1`, and `self.total_evicted += 1` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:2118-2134`).
- The snapshot exports these counters directly as operator diagnostics (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:2246-2273`).
- Existing tests only exercise small sequences: `log_fifo_eviction` emits 5 events (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:14343-14365`) and `log_sequence_monotonic` emits 10 events (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_telemetry.rs:14762-14774`). There is no boundary coverage near `u64::MAX`.

Why it matters:
The telemetry log is explicitly long-lived and monotonic. At counter boundaries, debug builds panic and optimized builds wrap, breaking the monotonic sequence contract and making snapshots report smaller totals after more events. That can confuse consumers that dedupe or checkpoint on sequence/total counters.

Proposed remediation:
Use checked or saturating counter updates for `sequence`, `total_emitted`, and `total_evicted`. Prefer fail-closed diagnostics: preserve monotonicity until saturation, emit an overflow marker/attribute, and avoid wrapping to zero. Add tests that seed the log near `u64::MAX` and assert append/eviction never panics or decreases the exported counters.
notes: RuntimeTelemetryLog::append now uses saturating_add for sequence, total_emitted, total_evicted. Counters plateau at u64::MAX rather than panicking (debug) or wrapping to zero (release). Added sequence_saturated, total_emitted_saturated, total_evicted_saturated booleans to TelemetryLogSnapshot (with #[serde(default)] for backwards-compat with persisted snapshots) so consumers can detect plateaued counters rather than silently assuming 'no new events'. Test-only seed_counters_for_test helper avoids needing to emit 1.8e19 events. Added 4 unit tests: append_at_u64_max_does_not_panic_or_wrap (staggered saturation), snapshot_exports_saturation_flags_false_by_default (negative path), total_evicted_saturates_independently (eviction-only saturation with capacity=1 trick), snapshot_counters_never_decrease_after_saturation (operator-facing contract). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [ft-l1jgo regression] storage migration to trait bypasses PooledReadConn — per-call SQLite opens under fleet load
description:
[HIGH] performance regression introduced by the storage.rs callsite migration to the StorageBackend trait.

Detected during cc_2's review pass on commits a13e86226 (embedding reads) and 6e711f8d1 (saved-search reads).

## Symptom

10 callsites in crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs replaced PooledReadConn::acquire(db_path) with open_rusqlite_backend(db_path, _) which calls RusqliteBackend::open(path, &OpenConfig::default()) directly. Each call now does a fresh SQLite Connection::open (file open + page cache warmup + 5s busy_timeout PRAGMA) instead of taking a pre-warmed connection from the LIFO pool.

The pool was specifically introduced as ft-bhyxz with the comment at storage.rs:8324-8341 calling out:

> Every `StorageHandle::*_with_cx` reader path used to call `open_read_storage_conn(db_path)` inside a `spawn_blocking_storage` closure. With ~78 call sites and a per-call `Connection::open` (file open + page cache warmup + 5s busy_timeout PRAGMA), a 200-agent fleet hammering `wa.search` / `wa.get_text` / web `/search` could rack up hundreds of SQLite-open syscalls per second.

The migration unwound that fix for the 10 affected reader paths.

## Affected callsites

10 `open_rusqlite_backend(...)` calls in storage.rs vs 66 surviving `PooledReadConn::acquire(...)` calls. Counts via:

  grep -c "open_rusqlite_backend" crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs   # → 10
  grep -c "PooledReadConn::acquire" crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs # → 66

Specific sites (line numbers approximate):
- 2162 get_saved_search_by_name
- 2185 list_saved_searches
- store_embedding (one of the 5 embedding-reads paths)
- get_unembedded_segments
- get_embedding
- (5 more in the embeddings refactor; analyzer can enumerate)

## Why this matters

The pool was load-bearing for the 200-agent fleet scenario. Under that load, hundreds of open() syscalls per second exhaust kernel file-descriptor budgets + thrash the SQLite page cache. The 10 converted sites all live on the read path that the documented fleet workload (`wa.search` / `wa.get_text` / web `/search`) hammers.

## Fix shape

The trait abstraction needs a pool-aware constructor. Two paths:

1. **Easier:** add a `PooledRusqliteBackend` newtype that wraps `PooledReadConn` and implements `StorageBackend`. The migration calls swap `open_rusqlite_backend(...)` → `PooledRusqliteBackend::acquire(db_path)`. Keeps the pool intact + keeps the trait migration green.

2. **Harder:** add a `with_pooled_backend(db_path, |&dyn StorageBackend| -> Result<T>)` helper on the pool itself. Avoids the wrapper but requires every callsite to pass a closure.

Option 1 is the clean one + matches how RusqliteBackend already works (a thin newtype over a Connection).

## Acceptance

- 0 callsites in storage.rs call `open_rusqlite_backend` for read paths that previously used `PooledReadConn::acquire`. (open_rusqlite_backend may stay for one-shot writer paths that did not pool.)
- The 10 converted sites either use the pooled backend wrapper OR are documented as "intentionally not pooled" (with the rationale in a comment + the load-test evidence).
- A regression test in storage.rs exercises the pool-acquire path under load and asserts the pool's hit-rate stays > 80% after migration.

## Cross-references

- a13e86226 — embedding reads migration (5 sites).
- 6e711f8d1 — saved-search reads migration (2 sites).
- ft-l1jgo (parent — call-site migration epic).
- ft-bhyxz (PooledReadConn substrate the migration regressed).
- scripts/storage_backend_callsites.py (cc_2's analyzer at bbf5762b7 — does NOT detect this category yet; the gap is "open path is via the trait, but the trait open is unpooled").

## Sweep

Reviewer should run `git log --grep='br-ft-l1jgo' --since='6 hours ago' --name-only | sort -u` and audit every `open_rusqlite_backend` introduction; if any of the 10 converted sites was a frequently-hit reader, escalate that callsite to [CRITICAL].
close_reason: done

title: Shadow phase health ignores unexpected executions
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/canary_rollout_controller.rs found a fail-open case in Shadow phase health. The module docs define Shadow as observe-only with no assignments dispatched (canary_rollout_controller.rs:31-35), and filter_assignments enforces that by moving every assignment to rejected in Shadow (canary_rollout_controller.rs:474-493). But compute_health_check only checks diff.missing_executions and diff.unexpected_executions when self.phase.dispatches() is true (canary_rollout_controller.rs:557-565), and CanaryPhase::dispatches is false for Shadow (canary_rollout_controller.rs:60-65). Therefore a Shadow cycle with unexpected executions can still be marked healthy if fidelity/conflict/rejection thresholds pass, and auto_advance can move to Canary on top of evidence that the observe-only phase dispatched work. Existing tests cover zero recommendations and simply assert no panic (tests/canary_shadow_integration.rs:551-570), and the property unhealthy diff includes missing_executions mostly with low fidelity, not a Shadow-phase unexpected-execution-only case (tests/proptest_canary_rollout_controller.rs:173-192, 459-477). Why it matters: unexpected executions in Shadow are the strongest signal that the canary gate leaked dispatch or that telemetry is misattributing live actions. Ignoring it can advance rollout after a phase that violated its core safety contract. Proposed remediation: always treat unexpected_executions as unhealthy, and in Shadow also treat any emitted execution evidence or nonzero emissions_count as a ShadowDispatchLeak/UnexpectedExecutions failure reason. Add regression tests where phase=Shadow, fidelity is high, warmup is satisfied, unexpected_executions is non-empty, and evaluate_health holds/marks unhealthy instead of advancing.
notes: Shipped at 4d990fbc7. compute_health_check now: (1) always flags UnexpectedExecutions when non-empty (dropped phase.dispatches() gate); (2) new HealthFailureReason::ShadowDispatchLeak variant; (3) Shadow phase additionally flags ShadowDispatchLeak when execution evidence present (execution_rejections_count > 0 OR missing_executions OR unexpected_executions non-empty) — emissions_count alone NOT a leak (recommendations are Shadow's purpose); (4) MissingExecutions still phase-dispatches-only (no expected executions in Shadow). 4 unit tests + 1 proptest (covers all tuples of execution evidence in Shadow). Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh check clean.

title: ARS replay ignores trigger and timeout validation surfaces
description:
Reality-check audit finding in frankenterm-core-ars.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_replay.rs:36-47 defines ReplayConfig::max_replay_ms.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_replay.rs:65-84 stores each incident trigger_pattern, and FailReason has PatternMismatch and Timeout variants at lines 128-143.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_replay.rs:219-297 validate() loops incidents and computes pass rate without checking elapsed time or max_replay_ms.
- crates/frankenterm-core-ars/src/ars_replay.rs:299-348 replay_incident() only skips failed originals, compares proposed_commands to actual_commands, and computes text_similarity(output_before, output_after). It never reads trigger_pattern and never emits PatternMismatch or Timeout.
- crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_ars_replay.rs:17-27 and repeated incident builders populate trigger_pattern, while the tests only serde the unused failure variants at lines 388-409.

Why it matters:
Replay is described as the validation gate before promoting an ARS reflex. Currently a reflex can validate without proving that its trigger would match the historical incident or that replay stayed inside the configured time budget. The exposed failure reasons make the API look stricter than the implementation.

Proposed remediation:
Thread trigger matching into replay_incident, enforce max_replay_ms or remove the field until real timing exists, add tests that mismatched trigger_pattern produces PatternMismatch and over-budget replay produces Timeout, and update pass-rate accounting so inconclusive/timeout cases cannot silently validate a reflex.
notes: Threaded trigger matching + timeout enforcement into ars_replay. New validate_with_trigger(reflex_id, reflex_trigger, ...) public entry point; legacy validate() delegates with None trigger (preserves pre-fix contract). replay_incident now accepts Option<&[u8]> reflex_trigger and emits FailReason::PatternMismatch when the reflex's trigger byte-mismatches the historical incident's trigger_pattern. New maybe_timeout(incident_id, started) helper checks per-incident wall-clock against max_replay_ms; emits FailReason::Timeout{elapsed_ms, max_ms} on overrun, treats max_replay_ms=0 as infinite-budget sentinel. Timeout check runs before pass/fail emission and on the cmd-mismatch fast path (a degenerate input can't blow past budget without surfacing). Added 6 tests: matching trigger passes, mismatched trigger emits PatternMismatch on all incidents and rejects assessment, legacy validate skips pattern check, max_replay_ms=0 disables timeout, maybe_timeout fires on overrun (1ms budget + 5ms sleep), maybe_timeout returns None within budget. Crate check clean -p frankenterm-core-ars --no-default-features.

title: context_budget: malformed compaction estimates are accepted without anomaly evidence
description:
Subsystem audit: crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:82-98 models CompactionEvent with tokens_before and tokens_after, implying a before/after budget transition.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:214-238 record_compaction accepts tokens_before/tokens_after without validating monotonicity or plausibility, pushes the event, increments total_compactions, and sets estimated_tokens = tokens_after.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:253-288 recovery_guidance then acts on the resulting pressure tier without any indication that the compaction estimate was malformed.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:537-574 only tests normal decreasing compactions and FIFO eviction; it does not test tokens_after > tokens_before or other implausible estimates.

Impact:
A parser/estimator glitch can record a compaction that increases context usage as a normal compaction, skewing compaction counts and recovery guidance without leaving an anomaly marker. This is an evidence-ledger quality gap: control-plane telemetry should distinguish successful compaction from suspicious accounting input.

Proposed remediation:
Validate compaction estimates in record_compaction. If tokens_after > tokens_before, either reject the event, record it with an explicit anomaly flag/status, or classify it as PatternDetectedAnomaly rather than a normal compaction. Add tests for increasing estimates and for saturated/implausible values near u64::MAX.
close_reason: Marked malformed context compaction estimates as explicit anomaly evidence when tokens_after exceeds tokens_before; added deterministic and property coverage over normal, increasing, and extreme before/after values.

title: [ARCH/cleanup] runtime_async.rs has 3 pub fns with zero production callers
description:
[LOW] dead-code cleanup surfaced during Phase-3 codebase-archaeology pass on runtime_async.rs.

## Symptom

Three public functions defined + self-tested in runtime_async.rs have ZERO production callers anywhere in the workspace:

| Function | Location | Production refs | Self-test refs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `broadcast_len` | runtime_async.rs:2422 | 0 | 1 (`broadcast_len_grows_after_send`) |
| `broadcast_try_recv` | runtime_async.rs:2401 | 0 | 2 (`broadcast_try_recv_empty_channel`, `broadcast_try_recv_closed_channel`) |
| `current_runtime_handle` | runtime_async.rs:45 | 0 | 1 (`current_runtime_handle_tracks_install_and_clear`) |

Verification (run today):
```text
$ for fn in broadcast_len broadcast_try_recv current_runtime_handle; do
    grep -rn "$fn" crates/ | grep -vE '/runtime_async\.rs|test|proptest' | wc -l
  done
0
0
0
```

## Why this is a defect

- 30+ lines of `BroadcastTryRecvError` enum + impl exists solely to support `broadcast_try_recv`. With no callers, the enum is dead too.
- Each pub fn carries doc + test maintenance burden (the `broadcast_*` tests reach into a 6,800-line file via `use super::*`).
- The migration-era reasoning ('complete the API surface so future callers find what they need') has aged poorly — the API surface inflates without payoff.

## Fix shape

Three options per fn:

1. **Delete + retire tests + cross-refs**. Cleanest for true dead-code.
2. **`#[allow(dead_code)]`** + a pointer to this bead. Defers the decision; preserves the test scaffolding for the day someone needs it.
3. **`#[deprecated]`** + retire in N+1 release. Honors the public-API contract for any out-of-tree consumer (if any exists).

Recommend Option 1 for all three — the public API contract is workspace-internal (no published crate), and the migration-era reasoning is documented as resolved in ft-7iof6.

## Acceptance

- The three pub fns + their self-tests are deleted.
- `BroadcastTryRecvError` enum is deleted (no other consumers).
- `grep -rn 'broadcast_len\|broadcast_try_recv\|current_runtime_handle' crates/` returns zero matches.
- Workspace builds clean after deletion.

## Cross-references

- runtime_async.rs:2422 / 2401 / 45 (the three fns).
- ft-7iof6 (closed; the rename + ledger-retirement that aged this code).
- See cc1's runtime archaeology map at `~/.claude/.../project_runtime_archaeology_2026_05_03.md` for the full surface audit.

## Sweep

A reviewer should also audit runtime.rs and runtime_telemetry.rs for similar dead pub fns. The audit command:
```text
for fn in $(grep -E '^pub (async )?fn ' crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime*.rs | sed -E 's/.*pub (async )?fn ([a-z_]+).*/\2/' | sort -u); do
    count=$(grep -rn "$fn" crates/ 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '/runtime_async\.rs|/runtime\.rs|/runtime_telemetry\.rs|test|proptest' | wc -l)
    [ "$count" = "0" ] && echo "  $fn: 0 external refs"
done
```

title: [HIGH] ft-ybtyg incomplete: session_checkpoints.state_hash is written but never verified on load
description:
Follow-up from ft-ybtyg (closed in 598a7c13).

## Gap

The ft-ybtyg fix replaced the placeholder `'restore'` literal with a real SipHash via `compute_restore_state_hash` and documented the intent: 'a later integrity check can recompute and compare'. But grep across session_restore.rs + snapshot_engine.rs + storage.rs finds ZERO callers that read the stored state_hash, recompute from the current inputs, and assert equality. The hash is written on INSERT, never verified on SELECT/load.

Result: the on-disk state_hash column now contains useful-looking SipHash values but is still effectively unverified — an attacker who tampers with the session_checkpoints row (flipping hash + any other field) is not detected, because no read path compares the stored hash against the recomputed hash.

## Reproducer
```
grep -rn 'compute_restore_state_hash\|compute_state_hash' crates/frankenterm-core/src/ | grep -iE 'verify|check|compare|assert_eq'
```
Expected matches: any call site that does `recomputed == stored`.
Actual: (empty).

## Fix direction
1. In the session-load path (session_restore.rs load fn + snapshot_engine.rs open/restore), after reading a session_checkpoints row, call compute_restore_state_hash on the current inputs and compare with the stored state_hash column.
2. On mismatch, return a typed Error (new StateHashMismatch variant) and refuse to restore from a tampered checkpoint.
3. Add regression test with a deliberately-tampered row that must produce StateHashMismatch and NOT a silent restore.

## Severity
MEDIUM → HIGH. The fix closed the docs-drift half but left the verification half open. A partial integrity check is worse than no check because it signals a stronger trust story than actually exists.

## Priority
P1 — this closes a real hole that ft-ybtyg was supposed to close.
close_reason: fixed in ca3d3fe2 — state_hash verification wired into load_checkpoint_by_id for startup rows; StateHashMismatch error + 5 regression tests (tampered hash, tampered pane_id_map, legacy 'restore' literal, null metadata, non-startup skip). Periodic/capture checkpoints remain a documented follow-up since their hash is over PaneInfo not reconstructable from session_checkpoints alone.

title: [VALIDATION] SearchBridgeRequest accepts unbounded limit + Duration::ZERO/MAX timeout without validation
description:
Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/search_bridge.rs at SHA 4688195f2 found that SearchBridgeRequest constructors and setters accept any usize / Duration without validation, leaving operators able to construct requests that misbehave silently.

## Sites

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/search_bridge.rs:45-71`:

```rust
impl SearchBridgeRequest {
    pub fn new(query: impl Into<String>, limit: usize) -> Self {
        Self { query: query.into(), limit, timeout: None, cancellation: None, text_provider: Arc::new(|_| None) }
    }
    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {
        self.timeout = Some(timeout);
        self
    }
    // ...
}
```

## Defect classes

1. **limit=0**: silently produces a search request that asks for zero results. The bridge happily executes (paying the search cost) and returns an empty result set. Operators see no error, no warning, no signal that they accidentally passed 0.

2. **limit=usize::MAX**: caller can request unbounded results. The bridge passes this through to frankensearch which will allocate space proportional to the limit. On a 64-bit system that's a 18-quintillion-element ask — likely OOM or other failure further down the stack. No upstream validation cap.

3. **timeout=Duration::ZERO**: with_timeout(Duration::ZERO) sets a zero-second deadline. The bridge's timeout machinery will fire immediately, before any real work happens, returning a confusing 'timeout' error on every call.

4. **timeout=Duration::from_secs(u64::MAX)**: caller can effectively disable the timeout. No upper-bound cap — a misconfigured caller could pin the bridge on a slow query for ~584 billion years.

These are config-level invariants that the bridge currently delegates entirely to upstream callers. None of the existing wa.cass_* tools (which validate similar bounds at the MCP layer per ft-aylbh) call SearchBridgeRequest directly, so there's no inherited validation — but anyone instantiating SearchBridgeRequest from a non-MCP path (e.g., embedded library use) gets no protection.

## Why it matters

The bridge is the kernel between MCP/operator surfaces and frankensearch. Validation upstream is per-tool; the bridge itself accepts anything. A future tool that forgets to validate (e.g., a new wa.search variant) inherits the unvalidated bridge surface — same fail-open class as ft-aylbh (which fixed wa.cass_view/status timeout_secs upstream).

## Suggested remediation

1. Add SearchBridgeRequest::validate(&self) -> Result<(), ValidationError> method that enforces:
   - limit >= 1 (zero is structurally meaningless)
   - limit <= SEARCH_BRIDGE_MAX_LIMIT (cap at e.g., 10000 — same as wa.cass_search's LIMIT_MAX)
   - timeout >= Duration::from_millis(1) when Some (zero is structurally meaningless)
   - timeout <= Duration::from_secs(SEARCH_BRIDGE_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECS) when Some (cap at e.g., 600 — same as wa.cass_*)

2. Call validate() at the top of the bridge's execute / dispatch fn so invalid requests are rejected before any side effect.

3. Add new public-crate constants SEARCH_BRIDGE_MAX_LIMIT and SEARCH_BRIDGE_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECS as the single source of truth.

4. Mirror the wa.cass_* validate_cass_timeout_secs helper pattern (ft-aylbh).

## Acceptance

- validate() helper that checks all 4 invariants
- SearchBridgeRequest::execute or equivalent rejects invalid requests at the boundary
- Unit tests for each invariant + each boundary value (limit=0, limit=MAX, timeout=ZERO, timeout=MAX)
- Property test sweeping representative values
notes:
Shipped fix: added SearchBridgeRequest::validate() pre-flight gate with 4 boundary invariants, wired into search_direct so every dispatch path runs through it.

Audit context: cc1 PHASE 3 audit on mcp_helpers.rs + replay.rs + search_bridge.rs at SHA 4688195f2. mcp_helpers + replay clean (filed ft-w5j4f informational, self-closed). search_bridge had 4 unvalidated input fields — this bead.

Code changes (crates/frankenterm-core/src/search_bridge.rs):

1. New SearchBridgeError::ValidationError(String) variant for pre-flight rejections.

2. Four new public-crate constants as the single source of truth for the bounds:
   - SEARCH_BRIDGE_MIN_LIMIT = 1 (zero is structurally meaningless)
   - SEARCH_BRIDGE_MAX_LIMIT = 10_000 (prevents unbounded result allocation; matches MCP-layer wa.cass_search LIMIT_MAX of 1000 with 10x headroom for non-MCP callers)
   - SEARCH_BRIDGE_MIN_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_millis(1)
   - SEARCH_BRIDGE_MAX_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_secs(600) (matches the MCP-layer wa.cass_* CASS_TIMEOUT_SECS_MAX shipped at ft-aylbh)

3. New SearchBridgeRequest::validate(&self) -> Result<(), SearchBridgeError> method enforcing all 4 bounds. Returns structured ValidationError with the bead breadcrumb + the rejected value + the offending bound.

4. Wired request.validate()? at the top of SearchBridge::search_direct (the canonical entry point that all public search_* methods funnel into). Catches misconfigurations before any side effect (timeout-thread spawn, cancellation-thread spawn, underlying searcher).

Tests added (7 regressions in mod tests):

- validate_rejects_zero_limit_ft_qfklb: limit=0 must reject with breadcrumb + lower-bound message + cited value
- validate_rejects_above_max_limit_ft_qfklb: limit > MAX must reject with upper-bound message
- validate_rejects_usize_max_limit_ft_qfklb: practical worst case pinned explicitly
- validate_rejects_zero_timeout_ft_qfklb: timeout=ZERO must reject (structural-meaning case)
- validate_rejects_above_max_timeout_ft_qfklb: timeout > MAX must reject (caps unbounded asks)
- validate_accepts_well_formed_request_ft_qfklb: vacuous-regression guard. Default + valid timeout + boundary-MIN + boundary-MAX values all validate cleanly.
- validate_property_sweep_ft_qfklb: cross-product sweep over the 4 equivalence classes (in-range limit, out-of-range limit, in-range timeout, out-of-range timeout) pinning the contract against drift in either constant.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features (background): 1m19s clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean

Bead acceptance per the original Suggested remediation:
- validate() helper that checks all 4 invariants: DONE
- SearchBridgeRequest::execute or equivalent rejects invalid requests at the boundary: DONE (search_direct?)
- Unit tests for each invariant + each boundary value: DONE (5 dedicated tests + 1 happy-path + 1 sweep)
- Property test sweeping representative values: DONE (validate_property_sweep_ft_qfklb)

title: [mor:security-engineering] wa.send trust boundary is 'which agent', not 'what bytes'
description:
# Observation

`WaSendTool` (mcp_tools.rs:1819) caps payload at 4 MiB (ft-05hfm) and
gates via the policy engine. Everything the authenticated agent
submits as \`text\` is then forwarded through
\`wezterm cli send-text -- <text>\` to the target pane.

The Command-args layering is safe from shell injection: args are
passed directly, not through \`sh -c\`. But send-text is typing
bytes into a terminal, and those bytes include the full control-char
space:

- \\x03 (Ctrl+C) kills the foreground process
- \\x04 (Ctrl+D) sends EOF, often exiting shells/REPLs
- \\x1a (Ctrl+Z) suspends
- Escape sequences can fake prompt text (`\\x1b[H\\x1b[2J$ `)
- Bracketed-paste wrappers can be forged

Trust model today: "if the agent is authenticated and policy allows
scope, arbitrary bytes are fine." This is appropriate for the
normal case (an agent typing \`npm test\` into its own pane). It is
less obviously appropriate for:

- agent A sending into agent B's pane (policy gates scope but not
  content)
- a compromised/misconfigured agent signing off its scope with a
  ghost Ctrl+C
- typing \`\\x1bc\` (reset terminal) into a neighbor pane to mask
  the audit trail of whatever just scrolled off

# Question

Would a lightweight content class — "does this payload contain
control characters outside the normal typing range?" — as a
separate policy capability be worth the complexity? The default
policy could allow control chars (current behavior); a hardening
toggle could require an explicit \`send-control-chars\` capability.

Agents that need to Ctrl+C their own long-running commands would
declare the capability up front; the 99% of typing-plain-text cases
would run without it and be structurally incapable of sending
Ctrl+C into another pane.

# Trust boundary

Current boundary: authenticated identity + policy scope + size cap.
Open question: should the boundary also include "which byte classes
can flow"? For security platforms, the answer is usually yes; the
tradeoff is ergonomics cost during normal agent operation.

comments.author: content-trust-audit
comments.text: answered — investigation found content-aware gating already exists via PolicyEngine::analyze_content_risk (policy.rs:4792) + PredicateKind::CommandPattern (policy.rs:3296). Trust boundary IS identity + bytes, not identity alone. Specific extension to cover terminal-control bytes (Ctrl+C/D/Z, ESC, bracketed-paste wraps) filed as child ft-qgk35.1 (P2) with ~10-line patch + 5 tests.

title: [security] wa.send: extend analyze_content_risk to flag terminal-control bytes
description:
# Parent

ft-qgk35 asked whether wa.send's trust boundary should include "what
bytes flow," not just "which agent is authenticated." Investigation
found the policy engine **already has content-aware gating** — the
question collapses from "should we add a mechanism?" to "should we
extend the existing mechanism to cover a specific blind spot?"

# Mechanism already in place

`PolicyEngine::analyze_content_risk` (crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:4792)
runs on every `ActionKind::SendText` with non-empty `command_text`.
It flags:

- **content.destructive_tokens** (40 pts): rm -rf, DROP TABLE, dd if=, …
- **content.sudo_elevation** (30 pts): sudo / doas / run0
- **content.multiline_complex** (15 pts): multi-line heredoc
- **content.pipe_chain** (10 pts): ≥ 2 pipes

And `PredicateKind::CommandPattern { patterns }`
(crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:3296) lets operators write
regex-match rules on `command_text`.

So content-aware gating **exists**. The parent bead (ft-qgk35)'s
framing of "trust boundary is identity, not bytes" is incorrect —
the boundary already inspects bytes for a specific class of risks.

# The actual gap

`analyze_content_risk` is **shell-command aware** (rm -rf, sudo,
pipes) but not **terminal-control aware**. It does not flag:

- \x03 (Ctrl+C) — can kill another agent's foreground process
- \x04 (Ctrl+D) — can exit another agent's REPL/shell
- \x1a (Ctrl+Z) — can background another agent's work
- \x1b prefix (escape sequences) — can fake prompts, scramble
  the scrollback, clear the screen to mask evidence
- Bracketed-paste wrappers (\x1b[200~ ... \x1b[201~) — can be
  forged to make injected text read as human-pasted by agent
  detection heuristics

On the fleet of 200+ panes described in README.md, a compromised or
misconfigured agent that has scope to wa.send into a neighbor pane
today has unrestricted ability to type control bytes. The risk
surface is not hypothetical — agent A releasing its reservation on
pane B via a ghost Ctrl+C is a known class of coordination failure
in multi-agent terminal systems.

# Proposed tightening

Add a new risk factor to `analyze_content_risk`:

```rust
// Terminal-control bytes
let has_control_byte = text.bytes().any(|b|
    b == 0x03 || b == 0x04 || b == 0x1a  // Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Z
    || b == 0x1b                           // ESC (escape sequences)
);
if has_control_byte {
    self.add_factor(
        factors,
        "content.terminal_control_bytes",
        RiskCategory::Content,
        25,  // between multiline (15) and sudo (30)
        "Payload contains terminal-control bytes (Ctrl+C/D/Z or ESC)",
    );
}
```

Point value 25 chosen so default `risk_config.allow_max` still
permits typical interactive use (which should not contain control
bytes; agents that type `npm test` don't include \x03). Agents that
DO need Ctrl+C for long-running workflows trip the factor and
either:
  - pass through (if policy's allow_max accommodates 25), or
  - land in require-approval (if allow_max is below 25).

Either way the event is **visible in the audit trail** — which is
the actual ask from the parent bead.

# Alternative (higher-cost)

Introduce `PaneCapability::AcceptControlBytes` as a separate gate.
Richer but requires:
  - schema change to PaneCapabilities
  - migration for existing PaneState rows
  - config surface for operators to declare which panes accept
    control bytes

The risk-factor approach above is a ~10-line change with no schema
impact; the capability approach is ~150 lines and a migration. Pick
risk-factor unless a future bead explicitly wants per-pane
structural gating.

# Tests that should land with the fix

1. `analyze_content_risk_flags_ctrl_c`: "npm test\x03" triggers
   terminal_control_bytes factor.
2. `analyze_content_risk_plain_text_unchanged`: "npm test" does NOT
   trigger it (false-positive guard on printable ASCII).
3. `analyze_content_risk_flags_esc_prefix`: "\x1bc" (reset
   terminal) triggers.
4. `analyze_content_risk_flags_bracketed_paste_wrap`: the literal
   bytes `\x1b[200~...\x1b[201~` trigger (agent forging a paste).
5. `wa_send_dry_run_reports_control_byte_risk`: end-to-end from
   the MCP tool layer; dry-run with a Ctrl+C payload surfaces the
   factor in the injection preview.

# Disposition on parent

ft-qgk35 can be closed as `answered`: the mechanism exists; this
sub-bead tracks the specific extension. Keeping ft-qgk35 open risks
re-discovery of the same insight.

title: [ARCH/Composition-B follow-up] §12.1 conformal-promotion wrapper for SwarmTailRiskMonitor (distribution-free coverage guarantee)
description:
Composition B follow-up #3 of 3 (ft-84mht parent, closed first-slice).

SwarmTailRiskMonitor exists today and emits a TailRiskStatus + nonconformity score. This bead promotes its output to a CONFORMAL prediction with distribution-free coverage guarantee: P(true tail risk ≤ predicted) ≥ 1 - α, finite-sample.

## Algorithm

Conformal prediction (Vovk, Gammerman, Shafer 2005): given a calibration set of past observations + a nonconformity score, the (1-α) conformal prediction interval is guaranteed to contain the true value with probability ≥ 1-α regardless of the underlying distribution. Online conformal (Gibbs & Candès 2021) updates the calibration set on each new observation.

## Integration point

A new SwarmTailRiskConformalLayer type that wraps SwarmTailRiskMonitor. The layer maintains a sliding calibration window of past nonconformity scores + computes the (1-α) quantile. The wrapped monitor's output is annotated with the conformal interval bound.

The expected-loss decision layer (already shipped) consumes the bound: if the conformal-bounded tail risk is in the Watch zone, the loss matrix's Watch column is used; if Violated, the Violated column. This makes the loss-matrix decision distribution-free-bounded rather than threshold-bounded.

## Acceptance

- Conformal layer wraps SwarmTailRiskMonitor without changing its surface.
- Calibration window is bounded (e.g., last 1000 nonconformity scores).
