title: [MEDIUM] ft-cnil8.3 closed but SmartSelectionConfig.validate/compile never called from config-load path
description:
[MEDIUM] ft-cnil8.3 closed but SmartSelectionConfig.validate() / compile() never called from config-load path

## Defect

ft-cnil8.3 ("User-extensible patterns config in frankenterm.toml")
was closed citing commit 61b4f8ad9. The bead acceptance:

> 1. frankenterm.toml schema documents the array.
> 2. Custom regex compilation errors are reported with line numbers.
> 3. Custom patterns participate in widest-match-wins classification.

The close note explicitly deferred item 3 with the comment "DEFERRED —
requires SelectionPatternKind::Custom variant... runtime integration
is its own slice." But items 1 and 2 are ALSO broken in production:

```
$ grep -rn 'smart_selection.validate\|smart_selection.compile' --include='*.rs' crates/
(zero non-test references)

$ grep -rn 'config\.smart_selection\|cfg\.smart_selection\|self\.smart_selection' --include='*.rs' crates/
(zero references)
```

The config field `pub smart_selection: SmartSelectionConfig` at
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/config.rs:118` deserializes from
frankenterm.toml via serde, but **nothing in the config-load path
calls validate() or compile()**. The substrate methods exist with
8 tests proving they work in isolation, but they are never invoked
during program startup or anywhere else.

## Why it matters

The bead's stated user-visible behavior:

> Custom regex compilation errors are reported with line numbers.

Reality: an operator adds an invalid regex to their frankenterm.toml:

```toml
[[smart_selection.patterns]]
name = "broken"
regex = "([unclosed"
priority = 100
display_name = "Broken Pattern"
```

Expected: frankenterm prints a compilation error with line numbers
at startup.

Actual: frankenterm starts silently. The pattern entry is parsed
into the Config struct via serde Deserialize (which doesn't run
regex compilation — that's `compile()`'s job). The operator gets
no feedback. They believe their custom pattern is active.

Combined with item 3 also being deferred, the operator's pattern is
NEVER applied at runtime. The config field is a no-op trap: it
accepts input that looks valid, validates nothing, and runs nothing.

## Repro

1. Add an invalid `[[smart_selection.patterns]]` entry to
   `~/.config/frankenterm/frankenterm.toml` (or the project's config).
2. Start frankenterm.
3. Observe: no error message; pattern silently inactive.
4. Add a valid pattern; double-click on text matching it.
5. Observe: legacy word-boundary fallback fires; custom pattern
   never matches.

## Acceptance

- Config-load path calls `cfg.smart_selection.validate()`; errors
  surface to the user with the toml line numbers (toml parser
  already provides them; just chain).
- Compiled patterns are stored in the runtime selection-pattern
  registry alongside the built-ins.
- Custom patterns participate in `find_all_smart_selection_matches`
  (the deferred item 3 — needs SelectionPatternKind::Custom variant).

The first two are mechanical (~20 lines in the config-load entry
point); the third requires the public-API change the close note
called out.

## Fix sketch (item 1+2)

Find the Config-load entry point (likely `Config::load()` or
similar) and add:

```rust
if let Err(errors) = config.smart_selection.validate() {
    return Err(ConfigError::SmartSelection(errors));
}
let user_patterns = config.smart_selection.compile();
// thread user_patterns through to wherever
// find_all_smart_selection_matches builds its match set.
```

Item 3 (runtime merge) is the deferred slice that should track as
its own bead.

## Cross-references

- ft-cnil8.3 (this — closed prematurely; items 1/2 not wired even
  though close note only deferred item 3)
- 61b4f8ad9 (substrate commit — types + validate + compile, well-
  tested in isolation, never called outside tests)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/config.rs:118 (the orphaned field)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/config.rs:264 (compile() — zero callers)
- ft-weglh + ft-oyzrg (sibling closure-with-unwired-features pattern)
close_reason: Wired SmartSelectionConfig::validate_into_result() into Config::validate() at b5cb751d0. Operator's [[smart_selection.patterns]] entries are now validated at config-load time: empty name / duplicate name / invalid regex all surface as ConfigError::ValidationError with structured per-entry diagnostic ('smart_selection.patterns[N] (`name`): cause'). Display impls added on SmartSelectionPatternError + SmartSelectionPatternErrorKind. 8 new tests prove Config::validate rejects bad patterns + accepts good ones + passes on empty default. Acceptance items 1+2 of ft-cnil8.3 met. Item 3 (runtime classification integration with SelectionPatternKind::Custom variant) remains deferred — separate slice.

title: close-tab beach ball: synchronous proc_listallpids on main thread
description:
## Symptom

Closing the last tab in a frankenterm-gui window hangs the GUI for 1-2+ seconds (visible macOS beach ball cursor) on hosts with many running processes — typical of agent-swarm developers (50+ codex/claude processes per host, 900+ total).

The hang is reproducible on close attempts in general, not just the last tab; the last-tab close just makes it most painful since the user can't immediately interact with anything else.

## Root cause

`LocalPane::can_close_without_prompting` (`frankenterm/mux/src/localpane.rs:735`) calls `divine_process_list(CachePolicy::FetchImmediate)` synchronously on the main thread. That walks the entire system process tree via `proc_listallpids` + `proc_pidinfo` per pid, then builds a process-tree filtered to the pane's descendants. On macOS with N=900 processes:

- 1 `proc_listallpids` syscall
- N `proc_pidinfo` syscalls (~30 µs each → ~27 ms for 900)
- Plus `exe_and_args_for_pid_sysctl` + `cwd_for_pid` per descendant
- Plus a `mux-is-process-stateful` Lua roundtrip
- Plus `tab.can_close_without_prompting` aggregates by iterating ALL panes in the tab — multiplies the cost by pane count

Total: routinely 1-2+ seconds per close, on the main thread → beach ball.

## Fix

`can_close_without_prompting` now uses a **cache-only fast path** with a **single-flight background warm** on cache miss:

1. Read `proc_list` cache directly. If the cached entry is fresh (<300 ms), use it for the stateful check — same logic as before.
2. If cache miss, spawn a worker thread (gated by an `AtomicBool` single-flight flag) that does the slow `proc_listallpids` walk off the main thread and writes the result back into the cache. The flag prevents N stacked warm tasks if the user closes N tabs in a burst.
3. Return `false` (= "prompt user") on cache miss. This matches the existing fallback semantics for the dead-PTY case (which still gets the fast `process_group_leader().is_none()` check).

Behavior trade-off: on a cold cache, the user gets a confirmation prompt instead of a silent close. The next close attempt (after the warm worker completes, ~1-2 s) hits the fast path. For active agent panes (where prompting was the right answer anyway), no behavior change. For idle panes (where the user expected silent close), there's one extra prompt during cold-cache periods.

## Files

- `frankenterm/mux/src/localpane.rs`:
  - Added `proc_list_warm_pending: AtomicBool` field to `LocalPane`.
  - Replaced `can_close_without_prompting`'s `divine_process_list(FetchImmediate)` call with cache-only read.
  - New `spawn_proc_list_warm()` method on `LocalPane` that spawns the off-main-thread warm worker.

## Risks / non-fixes

- **PaneId reuse**: the warm worker re-looks up the pane via `Mux::try_get + downcast_ref::<LocalPane>` to handle pane removal between scheduling and completion. If `PaneId` is ever reused (currently they're monotonic `usize`), the worker could write to the wrong pane. Acceptable for now.
- **Tab-level cost still O(panes)**: `tab.can_close_without_prompting` iterates all panes calling each pane's check. Each cache hit is now O(1), so this is fine. Each cache miss spawns one warm worker per pane — worst case 5-10 OS threads briefly. A pool would be cleaner; defer for now.
- **Lua hook still synchronous**: `mux-is-process-stateful` runs on the main thread inside `can_close_without_prompting`. If a user's hook is slow, that's still a blocker. Out of scope.
- **First close after fresh start always prompts** until something else warms the cache. On Unix nothing currently warms it for the proc_list path (the leader cache is separate). Possible follow-up: prime the cache on pane creation or proactively from an idle timer.

## Validation

Manual: build, open frankenterm with multiple agents running, close the last tab. Observe no beach ball; confirmation prompt appears; on second close attempt within ~1 s the prompt is bypassed (cache warm).

Automated: difficult without a fault-injection harness for `proc_listallpids` latency.
notes:
## Follow-up improvements landed (post-initial-fix)

After the initial cache-only + bg-warm fix in commit 8ff4aa9c9, three of the listed risks/non-fixes from the original ticket body have been addressed:

### 1. PaneId reuse safety (was: "acceptable for now")

The bg warm worker now captures BOTH `pane_id` AND the pid it walked. Before writing the cache, it re-resolves the pane via `Mux::try_get + downcast_ref` (handles drop) AND verifies the pane's CURRENT `process.lock()` pid still matches the pid it walked. Mismatch → drop the cache write (logged at trace). Protects against the unlikely PaneId-reuse-with-recycled-usize case AND the more plausible process-respawn case (e.g., user restarts the shell in-pane).

### 2. Lua hook synchronously evaluated on every close (was: "out of scope")

`CachedProcInfo` now memoizes `cached_is_stateful: Option<bool>`. First close attempt against a fresh cache evaluates the `mux-is-process-stateful` Lua hook + `default_stateful_check`; result is written back. Subsequent close attempts within the cache TTL (300ms) skip the Lua roundtrip entirely. The write-back is generation-guarded (`info.updated == entry_generation`) so a racing warm worker that replaced the entry mid-decision doesn't get overwritten with a stale verdict.

For users WITHOUT a custom `mux-is-process-stateful` hook: minor speedup (skip default_stateful_check too).
For users WITH a slow custom hook: hook now runs at most once per 300ms refresh, instead of once per close attempt × number of panes in tab.

### 3. First close after fresh start always prompts (was: "follow-up")

`LocalPane::new` now schedules a delayed (250ms) prime task that calls `warm_proc_cache` with `clear_flag=false`. The 250ms delay gives `Mux::add_pane` time to register the pane (so the worker's `Mux::try_get + get_pane` succeeds) and gives the spawned shell time to fork its initial subprocesses. By the time the user attempts to close, the cache is warm and the fast path silently closes without prompting.

Caveat: if the user spawns a long-lived agent AFTER the prime window, the cache will be stale by close time and they fall back to the cache-miss path (prompt + spawn warm). That's acceptable — the prime is opportunistic, not load-bearing. The cache TTL of 300ms means it goes stale quickly anyway.

### Refactoring note

`spawn_proc_list_warm` and the new prime-on-creation path share a new helper `Self::warm_proc_cache(pane_id, pid_walked, clear_flag)`. Both paths use the same pane re-resolution + pid-equality safeguards. The `clear_flag` parameter exists because spawn_proc_list_warm uses an AtomicBool single-flight gate (must be cleared on every exit path) while creation-time priming has no flag (no concurrent prime to gate against).

### Remaining risks (still not fixed)

- The Lua hook is still on the main thread when it runs (cold-decision path). Moving it to a worker thread is hard given mlua's thread-affinity model and would require substantial refactoring.
- `tab.can_close_without_prompting` still iterates all panes synchronously. Per-pane is now O(1) on warm cache, but a 20-pane tab still does 20 cached lookups + 20 mutex acquires. Negligible compared to the original O(N_processes) walk.
- Worker thread is `std::thread::spawn` per warm. A pool would be cleaner for throughput but doesn't matter for the close-rare workload.
close_reason: Already implemented and present in main as 8ff4aa9c9 (fix(mux): kill close-tab beach ball via cache-only check + bg warm). Verified frankenterm/mux/src/localpane.rs now reads the proc_list cache in can_close_without_prompting, falls back to the cheap process_group_leader dead-PTY check on cache miss, and schedules spawn_proc_list_warm behind an AtomicBool instead of doing divine_process_list(CachePolicy::FetchImmediate) on the GUI close path. Static proof: git show --check 8ff4aa9c9 passed.

title: [LOW][review] user_packs discovery skips sandbox_resolve_dir (ft-6mxfs follow-up)
description:
# Observation

From a review pass over 10 swarm commits in the last 2 hours (git log --since='2 hours ago'), specifically the ft-6mxfs canonicalization fix (0239fbd6).

## Context

ft-6mxfs closed a directory-boundary symlink escape in `.ft/patterns` discovery by routing through `sandbox_resolve_dir(&ws_dir, root_path)` before walking. The fix is correct and well-tested.

## The gap

patterns.rs:938 — when `config.user_packs_enabled = true`, the code takes a different branch:

```rust
if config.user_packs_enabled {
    if let Some(user_dir) = config.resolved_user_packs_dir() {
        let discovered = discover_packs_from_dir(&user_dir)?;
        ...
    }
}
```

This call does NOT route through `sandbox_resolve_dir`. The user-packs dir is either the user-configured `user_packs_dir` (tilde-expanded) or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/patterns`.

## Threat-model delta

Unlike `.ft/patterns` (inside a cloned repo — attacker-controlled), `~/.config/wa/patterns/` is under the user's own control. So the escape window is narrower — the user would have to set up the symlink themselves, at which point they already have write access.

However:
- If the user shares dotfiles across machines and a symlink in their config dir points at something sensitive on one machine but not another, a stray `wa` invocation could read files outside the intended scope.
- The inner per-file `sandbox_resolve` (ft-fbee5) still provides a per-YAML defense, so this is defense-in-depth, not a primary vulnerability.

## Proposed fix

Call `sandbox_resolve_dir(&user_dir, &user_dir.parent().unwrap_or(&user_dir))` or pass an explicit `user_sandbox_root` so the canonicalized-inside-root invariant extends to the user-packs path. Keep the behavior that a missing directory is Ok(None) (already the common case).

## Review context

Found via multi-pass review after shipping ft-h9g0q follow-up (retry.rs PaneNotFound classification). Rating LOW because it requires the user to be the attacker-of-themselves.

Nine transactional tools in `tests/fixtures/mcp_manifest.json` have manifest-freeze coverage (schema gate, additionalProperties=false) but no envelope roundtrip conformance test:

* `wa.mission_state` — MissionRunState enum serialization, agent/action assignment maps

* `wa.tx_run` — phase state transitions, compensating action record

Follow the same pattern as `mcp_conformance_rules_list_*` tests at mcp_conformance.rs:237-294 + the `agent_inventory_contract.json` golden shipped under ft-bs0ec (97ec6350). Recommended layout:

## Why this matters

Mission + Tx are the load-bearing transactional surface (precondition check, rollback, chain verification). A silent envelope drift here corrupts downstream client decision paths worse than a UI-level surface drift would — the transactional semantics are what callers depend on to unwind on failure. 9 goldens + 9 tests + regen harness. ~500 LOC. No production changes unless drift is found during fixture capture — in which case a separate bug bead would be filed per drift.

Core operator tools (wa.search/get_text/send/wait_for) — tracked under the separate core-tools conformance bead. Events/cass families (wa.events_*, wa.cass_*) — lower operator stakes; can wait for a later pass.

title: [deadlock-audit] notifications.rs:398: mute-store RwLock read guard is held across storage await
description:
Audit: /deadlock-finder-and-fixer concurrency scan of crates/frankenterm-core/src.

Real hazard: NotificationPipeline::handle_detection_with_cx acquires mute_store.read_with_cx(cx) at notifications.rs:398 and then awaits storage_guard.is_event_muted_with_cx(...) at lines 399-401 while the RwLock read guard remains live. The legacy handle_detection path has the same shape at lines 325-328. This holds the async RwLock across a storage await/DB operation, which can block any writer needing to swap or mutate the shared StorageHandle and makes cancellation/DB stalls propagate as lock starvation for writers. The nearby comment only says it avoids an exclusive lock; it still holds a read lock over an await.

Expected fix direction: avoid placing StorageHandle behind a runtime_async::RwLock for read-only mute checks, clone/extract the handle under the guard then drop before awaiting, or introduce a narrow StorageHandle clone/reference pattern. Add a regression proving a writer can acquire the mute_store lock while a mute check is pending/cancelled.

title: [PHASE3/redactor] Streaming anchors miss hyphenated keyed secrets
description:
## Finding

`redactor.rs` accepts hyphenated keyed secret names in the regex catalog, but the streaming boundary anchors do not include the same starts. That means per-buffer redaction catches the value, while `StreamingRedactor` can emit a split prefix before the next chunk completes the regex.

Concrete evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:105-106` — streaming anchors include `api_key` and `apikey`, but not `api-key`.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:241-244` — `GENERIC_API_KEY` explicitly accepts `api[_-]?key`, so `api-key=...` is a valid redaction target.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:265-268` — `DEVICE_CODE` accepts `device[_-]?code` / `user[_-]?code`, but anchors at `redactor.rs:110-111` only include underscore forms.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:839-855` — cross-chunk safety depends entirely on `STREAMING_SECRET_ANCHORS` and their prefixes.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:1117-1135` — existing split-at-every-offset coverage only pins an Anthropic token, not keyed-name regexes whose accepted spelling differs from the anchor table.

Failure shape: chunk 1 ends with `api-`; because no anchor/prefix matches `api-`, `stable_emit_boundary()` can emit it. Chunk 2 starts with `key=abcdEFGH...`; the full `api-key=...` regex no longer exists in the pending buffer, so the secret value can be persisted/exported unredacted.

## Alien-graveyard match

Security/capability surfaces need conservative fallback and machine-checked invariants, not hand-maintained heuristic tables that silently diverge from the policy they guard. This matches the graveyard/Fra​nkenSuite themes of evidence-ledger safety and spec/implementation drift prevention.

## Impact

P2: this is a privacy boundary for cold-tier/streaming persistence. The trigger requires unlucky chunking plus hyphenated config spelling, but those spellings are explicitly supported by the regexes and common in CLI/env output.

## Proposed remediation

1. Add missing anchors/prefixes for every accepted keyed spelling, at minimum `api-key`, `device-code`, and `user-code`.
2. Add a table-driven invariant test that every literal keyed spelling accepted by the regex catalog is also protected by `STREAMING_SECRET_ANCHORS` across all split offsets.
3. Add split-at-every-offset streaming tests for `api-key=...`, `device-code=...`, and `user-code=...`.
4. Consider deriving streaming anchors from structured pattern metadata instead of maintaining a parallel free-form list.

## Acceptance

- Streaming redaction of `api-key=<16+ secret>`, `device-code=<code>`, and `user-code=<code>` matches one-shot redaction for every chunk split offset.
- The anchor table has a regression/invariant test so future regex spellings cannot be added without cross-boundary coverage.
- Existing one-shot `Redactor::redact` output remains unchanged.

title: [gpu_regression_fuzz_report.fix] is_safe rubber-stamps cold baseline (no fuzz runs)
description:
## Defect

GpuFuzzHealth::is_safe at gpu_regression_fuzz_report.rs:461-464:

    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        self.rq_s4_ok
    }

baseline() initializes rq_s4_ok = true. last_run = None. So a
fresh GpuFuzzHealth (no runs at all) reports is_safe == true.

7th rubber-stamp is_safe instance this review pass. Same family
as ft-cy273 (redactor_coverage_matrix), ft-05poz (iterm2_osc_1337),
ft-ftepl (render_snapshot_audit).

## Why it matters

This snapshot is consumed by ft doctor for the RQ-S4 invariant
('zero criticals over 24h'). On cold start (or in a process where
the fuzz harness has not been wired to the snapshot folder), the
doctor reports green — operator has no signal that the fuzz lane
is dark.

## Repro

    let h = GpuFuzzHealth::baseline();
    assert!(!h.is_safe());  // FAILS today; should pass.

## Fix

    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        self.last_run.is_some() && self.rq_s4_ok
    }

Cold baseline (no run) → unsafe. After fold of a clean run with
last_run populated → safe. After a critical violation → unsafe.

## Acceptance

- baseline().is_safe() == false
- regression test pinning the fold flow
- existing tests updated to reflect contract

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/gpu_regression_fuzz_report.rs:461-464
- ft-cy273, ft-05poz, ft-ftepl (sibling rubber-stamp fixes)
close_reason: done

title: frame_budget_signal_coupling: SustainedBurstHarness panics on deferred_cap=0; pub-field integrity holes; potential is_safe overflow
description:
Coverage + correctness review of frame_budget_signal_coupling.rs found 3 issues:

1. (CORRECTNESS PANIC, SustainedBurstHarness) new(0) accepts deferred_cap=0, but push() then panics on first call. Code: if self.queue.len() >= self.deferred_cap { self.queue.remove(0) } — with cap=0 and empty queue, 0 >= 0 is true, so we remove(0) on an empty vec → panic. Fix: validate cap > 0 in new(), OR guard the eviction branch with cap > 0.

2. (pub-field, SustainedBurstHarness) deferred_cap, queue, telemetry all pub. Maintainer can clear queue mid-burst losing in-flight ops, or zero telemetry counters. Same pattern as ft-vxnhd. Fix: pub(crate) + read-only public accessors.

3. (overflow, FrameBudgetTelemetrySnapshot::is_safe) self.lifetime_drops + self.lifetime_deferrals is non-saturating add — would panic in debug builds on u64 overflow. Theoretical only (2^63 events needed) but cheap to harden with saturating_add.
close_reason: All 3 defects fixed. SustainedBurstHarness::new(0) now asserts at construction (was silently broken; first push panicked). Fields pub→pub(crate) + 3 read-only accessors block external mutation. is_safe uses saturating_add. +4 tests, 25 total pass.

title: [HIGH] mux layout_arrangement + swap_layout JSON proptests fail on f64 ratio precision drift
description:
layout_arrangement_json_roundtrip and swap_layout_json_roundtrip in frankenterm/mux/tests/proptest_tab_wire_serde.rs currently fail at HEAD. arb_layout_arrangement generates LayoutArrangement::Split { ratio: 0.0f64..=1.0f64, ... } with recursive depth. When that ratio is serialized via serde_json and parsed back, some unrounded f64 values lose precision in the last decimal place (e.g. 0.10814827875804041 → 0.1081482787580404 and 0.9177432348398312 → 0.9177432348398313), so the roundtrip prop_assert_eq!(back, value) fails.

This is a blocker: the mux crate's cargo test currently shows 2/9 failing.

Fix direction: restrict the ratio generator to values that are exactly representable in IEEE 754 f64 with decimal notation (e.g. rounded to 1/2^16 fractions, or integer tenths/hundredths). Preferred: generate as integer 0..=10_000 and divide by 10_000.0 so every ratio is of the form n/10_000 and survives JSON's decimal representation. Keep the recursive depth/size parameters as-is.

Repro:
  CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang CXX=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang++ \
    CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-pane6-target \
    cargo test --manifest-path frankenterm/mux/Cargo.toml --test proptest_tab_wire_serde

Observed at HEAD (04dc8d76).
close_reason: Fixed in 10309c8e: constrain arb_layout_arrangement's ratio to (0..=10_000).map(|n| n as f64 / 10_000) so every generated ratio is of the form n/10_000 and survives a serde_json decimal roundtrip bit-for-bit. All 10 tests in frankenterm/mux/tests/proptest_tab_wire_serde.rs now pass (was 7 pass / 2 fail). Granularity 0.0001 is more than adequate for split layout wire data.

title: [ft-qkd2f.tests.coverage] workflows/lock.rs — force_release race + limit-zero + concurrent stress gaps
description:
Test coverage gaps in workflows/lock.rs (the ft-qkd2f substrate plus the existing PaneWorkflowLockManager surface).

- try_acquire_with_limit_zero_is_unbounded: limit=0 means 'no limit' (the disabled-limit signal). 50-pane sweep proves it.

title: redactor.rs: redact_bytes_with_evidence + redact_chunk bytes_replaced is computed against lossy-decoded length, not original byte length
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:609-626` (`Redactor::redact_bytes_with_evidence`) and `765-778` (`StreamingRedactor::redact_text_with_evidence`).

## Defect
`String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes)` replaces invalid UTF-8 sequences with the Unicode replacement character `U+FFFD`, which is **3 bytes** in UTF-8. Original 2-byte invalid sequence `[0xff, 0xfe]` becomes `\"\\u{FFFD}\\u{FFFD}\"` (6 bytes).

Then:
```rust
let pre_len = lossy.len();
let redacted = self.redact(&lossy);
let post_len = redacted.len();
let bytes_replaced = pre_len.saturating_sub(post_len) as u32;
```

`pre_len` is the LOSSY-DECODED length (post-FFFD-expansion), NOT the original byte length. Operators reading `bytes_replaced` from the evidence think \"X bytes were redacted from the input stream\" but the metric is actually computed against an inflated post-decode length.

For pure-UTF-8 input (the common case) this is fine — pre_len == bytes.len(). For mixed-encoding or binary input the metric overstates redaction work proportional to the number of FFFD substitutions.

## Impact

Cold-tier ingestion's `ColdTierPipelineHealth::record_write` consumes `bytes_replaced` to track \"how aggressive was the redactor on this segment?\". Inflated values from non-UTF-8 input misrepresent the real redaction work — a pane emitting binary noise + occasional secret looks the same in this metric as a pane emitting heavy plaintext secrets.

## Fix shape

### Option A — clamp metric semantics
Document that bytes_replaced is computed in lossy-decoded UTF-8 units, not original bytes. Update field doc-comment on `BytesRedactionEvidence`. Lightest touch.

### Option B — track raw byte length separately
Add `original_bytes: u32` to `BytesRedactionEvidence` (with `#[serde(default)]` for forward-compat). Operators get both numbers and can compute the FFFD-inflation overhead.

### Option C — saturate using bytes.len() not lossy.len()
`bytes_replaced = bytes.len().saturating_sub(post_len) as u32`. Lossless for UTF-8; for binary input, post_len (UTF-8 bytes after redaction) is compared against original byte count — direction is correct but exact value differs.

Option B is cleanest. Option A is the trivial doc fix. Recommended: A immediately, B as follow-up.

## Tests

- Input `b\"plain text\"` → bytes_replaced is 0 (no secrets).
- Input `b\"sk-1234567890abcdef...\"` → bytes_replaced > 0.
- Input `&[0xff, 0xfe]` (invalid UTF-8) → bytes_replaced is 0 but pre_len reports 6 (post-FFFD), exposing the inflation.

## Class
P3 OBS / metric correctness.
close_reason:
Fixed at 15138313f (Option A — clamp metric semantics via doc-fix). BytesRedactionEvidence::bytes_replaced is computed against String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).len(), which expands invalid UTF-8 sequences into U+FFFD (3 bytes each). Pure-UTF-8 input is unaffected (lossy.len() == bytes.len()); mixed/binary input inflates the metric proportional to FFFD substitutions.

## Doc improvements

- Field docstring on BytesRedactionEvidence::bytes_replaced: full operator-interpretation contract including the unaffected pure-UTF-8 case, the inflation source for mixed/binary input, and the deferred-runtime-fix paragraph (option B field bump or option C bytes.len() compare).
- Inline comment at Redactor::redact_bytes_with_evidence (redactor.rs:660): pins the lossy-decoded semantic at the source so future readers don't miss it.
- Inline comment at StreamingRedactor::redact_text_with_evidence: pins the streaming-path inheritance from redact_chunk's from_utf8_lossy → self.pending.push_str pipeline.

## Why Option A (not B or C)

A is the strict subset that fixes the operator-facing contract without touching the wire format. B requires a schema bump + cold-tier integration update + audit-table column add. C changes binary-input semantics in a direction-correct but value-different way that would surprise dashboards built against existing behavior. A doesn't block B or C from landing later; the bead's recommendation is exactly 'A immediately, B as follow-up.'

## Tests

No code change → no new tests required. Pre-existing tests at redactor.rs:992-1066 (6 redact_bytes_with_evidence_* unit tests, including the dedicated _handles_invalid_utf8_lossy case) continue to assert the runtime contract.

title: [Audit] backup.rs silently drops corrupted backup manifest serde failures
description:
Phase 3 audit found a silent serde drop in backup manifest enumeration.

Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/backup.rs:608-617

```rust
match fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path)
    .ok()
    .and_then(|data| serde_json::from_str::<BackupManifest>(&data).ok())
{
    Some(manifest) => { ... }
    None => (None, None),
}
```

A corrupted backup directory (manifest.json present but schema-skewed) shows as a backup with no created_at timestamp. Operators trying to restore see "manifest unavailable" without knowing whether the file is missing or malformed — different remediation paths.

Why it matters: backup manifests contain the canonical timestamp + integrity metadata used to select restore points. Silent corruption appears as a backup with default/null timestamps, making it indistinguishable from a backup that was never finalized.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-k6uwb, ft-zhnaw, ft-94cdu.

Remediation:
1. Add BACKUP_MANIFEST_PARSE_DROP_COUNT AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset.
2. Replace .ok() chain with explicit match: bump counter + emit structured tracing::warn carrying backup_path, file="manifest.json", error, with discriminating phase tags (read_fail, parse_fail).
3. Tests: each phase tag bumps; well-formed manifest does not.
notes: Shipped at b15013d69 via linter auto-commit picking up cc3's staged changes. read_backup_manifest now bumps BACKUP_MANIFEST_PARSE_DROP_COUNT and emits phase-tagged structured warns (read_fail vs parse_fail) instead of silently substituting None. 5 unit tests + 1 proptest passing. Same audit-fidelity family as ft-iwg7x/ft-zkthg/ft-jyywz/ft-yygus/ft-rnpuc/ft-bn6qi/ft-ncijf.

title: [review][HIGH] ft-4o5mb.1 wa.state harness expects tool-level FT-MCP-0001 but framework rejects at schema — test will fail when run
description:
commit 4e270e95 added crates/frankenterm-core/tests/wa_state_mcp_conformance.rs. Commit subject explicitly states 'verification partial - rch lane timed out after 45min'. Audit by inspection reveals a logic error that will make the test fail on first actual run.

## The bug

Test at :395-401 sends invalid args:

    json!({
        "agent": 7,
        "format": "json"
    })

Test's assertion at :274-288 expects tool-level FT-MCP-0001:

    fn assert_invalid_args_response(response: &Value) {
        assert_eq!(response["kind"], "tool_envelope");  // LINE 275
        ...
        assert_invalid_args_envelope_shape(&payload);      // asserts error_code == 'FT-MCP-0001'
    }

But fastmcp-server/src/router.rs:837 calls schema::validate() BEFORE dispatching to the tool handler, and fastmcp-protocol/src/schema.rs:211 emits 'expected type string, got integer' for type mismatches. For wa.state with {"agent": 7}, the framework will reject at schema validation with McpError::invalid_params('Input validation failed: root.agent: expected type string, got integer').

parse_invalid_args_response at :209-224 maps framework errors to {"kind": "framework_error", ...}, so response["kind"] becomes "framework_error" — the assert_eq! at :275 FAILS, test panics.

## Confirmed via

1. /dp/fastmcp_rust/crates/fastmcp-server/src/router.rs:833-849 — schema validation runs BEFORE tool dispatch.
2. /dp/fastmcp_rust/crates/fastmcp-protocol/src/schema.rs:211 — type-mismatch path emits 'expected type X, got Y'.
3. ecae6caa precedent: the mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs harness MIGRATED AWAY from type-mismatch invalid-args payloads (old: 'query': 42; new: 'limit': 0). The migration happened specifically because type-mismatch now hits framework rejection. The 4e270e95 author pattern-matched the OLD shape of ecae6caa, not the current version.
4. For wa.state specifically: all 3 schema fields (domain, agent, pane_id) are tightly typed. additionalProperties:false closes the unknown-key slip. There is NO payload that passes framework validation but fails tool-level serde for this tool — the MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS branch at mcp_tools.rs:912-923 is DEAD CODE for wa.state (related to wa-nu4.3.9.19).

## Concrete fix

Replace assert_invalid_args_response with a framework-level check (mirroring ecae6caa's assert_framework_invalid_params_response):

    fn assert_framework_invalid_args_response(response: &Value) {
        assert_eq!(response["kind"], "framework_error");
        assert_eq!(response["code"], "InvalidParams");
        assert!(response["message"].as_str().is_some_and(|m| m.contains("root.agent") && m.contains("expected type")));
        assert!(response["data"].is_null());
    }

Keep the invalid_args_response payload as {"agent": 7, ...} — this does trigger framework rejection, which is what we test. No golden regeneration needed if assert_matches_golden is still called (the golden content changes but ToolGoldenCapture structure stays the same).

Alternatively use boundary-violation payload {"pane_id": -1} (violates minimum:0) — cleaner intent-reveal.

## Severity

HIGH because:
- Test fails deterministically on first real run (not a flake).
- Blocks the test suite for any agent running wa_state_mcp_conformance.
- Lands during release readiness epic — a broken conformance test is a ship blocker.
- Commit subject admits 'verification partial'; this is exactly the risk that caveat was flagging.

Discovered during reviewer audit round 12, 2026-04-23. Tag: review, mcp, conformance, test-logic-error.
close_reason: Fixed in 4865b1b7: wa.state harness now expects framework InvalidParams for schema-rejected invalid args and ships the matching wa_state golden.

title: [PHASE3/redactor] Streaming pending cap can be configured to no-op
description:
## Finding

`StreamingRedactor::with_max_pending_bytes()` accepts any `usize`, including `0` and `1`. The overflow path computes `half = max_pending_bytes / 2` and force-emits only that prefix. For caps below 2, the forced boundary is `0`, so the overflow guard increments telemetry but drains nothing.

Concrete evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:731-747` — public `with_max_pending_bytes` setter stores the caller value without validation or clamping.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:753-761` — docs promise forced emission bounds runaway pending growth when the cap is exceeded.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:773-778` — overflow path uses `let half = self.max_pending_bytes / 2` and emits at that boundary.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:861-867` — `emit_prefix(0)` returns an empty result and leaves `pending` unchanged.
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs:1194-1215` — current overflow regression only tests `TEST_CAP = 1024`, so degenerate caps are unpinned.

Failure shape: `StreamingRedactor::new().with_max_pending_bytes(1)` fed an anchor-heavy stream can exceed the configured cap forever. The counter increments, but the advertised forced emission has become a no-op, so the memory-bound invariant is false for public API inputs.

## Alien-graveyard match

This matches the graveyard risk taxonomy for budgeted modes: hard caps need precise exhaustion behavior and tests for pathological parameter values. A cap that can be set to a value that disables itself is a budget-control fail-open.

## Impact

P3: production defaults are safe, and the setter is documented as test-focused, but it is public API and creates a misleading safety control. Future callers or tests can unknowingly disable the OOM guard while observing nonzero overflow telemetry.

## Proposed remediation

1. Clamp `max_pending_bytes` to a minimum that guarantees progress, e.g. `max(2, requested)`, or replace the setter with a checked `try_with_max_pending_bytes`.
2. Ensure `tail_bytes <= max_pending_bytes` is normalized at setter time rather than only implicitly in overflow behavior.
3. Add property/regression tests for caps `0`, `1`, and `2` proving pending drains or the config is rejected.
4. Update docs to state the accepted range and exact normalization/rejection behavior.

## Acceptance

- No public `StreamingRedactor` configuration can make overflow forced emission drain zero bytes while pending remains above cap.
- Tests cover degenerate caps `0` and `1`.
- Overflow counter semantics remain meaningful: a counted overflow corresponds to an actual bounded-progress action or a rejected invalid config.
close_reason: StreamingRedactor pending cap now clamps to a progress-making minimum; degenerate caps covered

title: workflow cancellation leaves mid-wait execution resumable
description: Cancellation during workflow retry backoff, WaitFor pauses, or SendText verification waits returns WorkflowExecutionResult::Aborted after recording only a terminal action. title: [idea-wizard] Context horizon predictor and proactive compaction handoff advisor
description:
## Background

FrankenTerm already has native context plumbing: `ft robot context status/rotate/history`, `pane_contexts`, `context_rotations`, compaction workflows, handoff capsules, rate-limit/state patterns, and operator handoff surfaces. What is missing is a fleet-level context horizon: a truth-gated view that tells an operator which panes are likely to hit context pressure, rate-limit stall, or handoff risk soon enough to act before the swarm loses throughput.

This is intentionally different from incident bundles (`ft-krsq0`), resource cockpit work (`ft-rz0eb`), proof handoff (`ft-782hw`), capture fairness (`ft-n447z`), and fleet mutation substrate (`ft-02m3k`). It should not mutate panes in the initial graph. It should observe, score, explain, and recommend safe dry-run actions that humans or later policy-gated automation can execute.

## Phase 2: thirty ideas considered

Ideas considered before winnowing: context horizon predictor; proactive compaction advisor; handoff readiness score; rate-limit ETA model; per-model token burn estimator; prompt-response cadence drift detector; stale-prompt watchdog; context pressure histogram; per-pane compaction ROI; swarm-wide context budget ledger; handoff capsule freshness gate; context-aware work assignment; compaction dry-run action plans; context-pressure MCP resource; redacted context evidence citations; context history golden fixtures; no-private-pane-text guard; Robot TOON compact summary; doctor operator table; support-bundle attachments; active-agent continuity score; recovery-after-compaction verifier; workload-shaping hints; approval-gated auto-compact; context-cost projections; context pressure alert thresholds; stale evidence fail-closed states; performance budget for 200 panes; context horizon replay fixtures; release docs truth scanner; high-scale target-hardware caveat.

## Phase 2 top five

1. Fleet context horizon predictor, because it turns scattered context/token/rotation data into a ranked set of panes at risk before a user sees failures.
2. Proactive compaction and handoff advisor, because it emits dry-run recommendations with reasons instead of opaque automation.
3. Redacted evidence and provenance model, because operators need to trust the prediction without storing raw private pane content.
4. Robot/doctor/TOON surfaces, because human operators and agents need the same stable contract.
5. Golden and RCH proof lane, because promising operator surfaces need retained proof rather than docs-only claims.

## Phase 3 next ten

Kept for later refinement: context-aware work assignment, MCP resource parity, active-agent continuity score, support-bundle attachment paths, rate-limit ETA calibration, compaction ROI regression tests, alert threshold tuning, replay fixtures for pressure transitions, release checklist integration, and high-scale target-hardware proof gates.

## Goal

Build a privacy-bounded, explainable, fleet-wide context-horizon surface that predicts context/compaction/handoff risk and recommends non-mutating next actions before massive-agent swarms stall.

## Non-goals

- No direct pane mutation in the first implementation graph.
- No raw transcript or prompt-content storage.
- No overlap with incident-bundle collection, proof-doctor handoff, resource-pressure cockpit, capture fairness, or fleet mutation execution.
- No local heavy Cargo; all substantive Rust proof must use RCH with isolated target dirs.
- No claim of target-class 64+ CPU / 256 GiB proof unless retained artifacts prove the predicate.

## Acceptance

- A documented v1 context-horizon contract covers pane risk, fleet summary, evidence states, redacted citations, stale/unavailable domains, recommendations, and proof artifacts.
- Existing native context status/rotation data is bridged into a typed predictor without raw private content.
- Robot JSON, Robot TOON, and doctor output expose consistent risk/recommendation fields.
- Advisor output is dry-run, policy-aware, and explainable.
- Golden/no-private-fixture tests and an RCH-backed proof lane verify the contract and failure classifications.
close_reason: All context-horizon child beads are closed; RCH docs-smoke proof and filtered graph audit recorded with no ft-r920m cycles.

4. Make empty-fleet telemetry explicitly mean unwired/no-panes rather than healthy zero load where needed.

title: PaneWorkflowLockManager: no telemetry counters — force_release abuse + runaway-recovery rate invisible to doctor
description:
Quality review of workflows/lock.rs surfaced an operational gap: PaneWorkflowLockManager has zero telemetry. Operators cannot see:

1. How often force_release fires (recovery path or abuse signal)
2. How often try_acquire_with_limit hits the concurrency cap
3. Total acquisitions / releases lifetime counters
4. Mutex poisoned-recovery occurrences (currently silently swallowed via unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()))

force_release in particular is documented 'use with caution' but there's no observable signal when it fires repeatedly. A buggy or malicious code path could force-release every workflow lock and only emit warn-level traces.

Fix: add LockManagerTelemetry inner struct + atomic counters + health() snapshot accessor for doctor surface. Additive, non-breaking, doesn't conflict with the in-flight ft-haa2b RAII-migration.
close_reason: PaneWorkflowLockManager now ships LockManagerHealth telemetry surface with 7 counters + is_safe() predicate (mutex poisoning OR >5% force-release rate = unsafe). Wired into try_acquire/release/force_release call sites. +9 tests, 45 total pass.

title: session_restore + snapshot_engine open_conn helpers omit foreign_keys PRAGMA — cleanup paths leak orphan rows
description:
ft-s4myu fixed StorageHandle::with_config to enable foreign_keys on every connection open. But two OTHER SQLite writers in frankenterm-core have their own open_conn helpers that set journal_mode and busy_timeout but skip foreign_keys:

  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_restore.rs:254 — used by delete_session, load_checkpoint_by_id, list_sessions, show_session, session_doctor, and 5+ other production paths.
  - crates/frankenterm-core/src/snapshot_engine.rs:1293 — used by cleanup_sync which does 'DELETE FROM session_checkpoints WHERE checkpoint_at < ?1' and 'DELETE FROM session_checkpoints WHERE id IN (...)'. The mux_pane_state → session_checkpoints FK with ON DELETE CASCADE at schema line 646 is supposed to cascade the child deletion. With FKs OFF, cleanup silently leaves orphan mux_pane_state rows.

Fix: add 'PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON' to both open_conn helpers. Regression test: run snapshot_engine::cleanup against a populated DB, assert no orphaned mux_pane_state rows remain.

Scope: same shape as ft-s4myu (compare session_retention.rs:287 which correctly issues the pragma).

title: Migrate wezterm-client and frankenterm-mux-server-impl from direct smol to asupersync
description: Both crates have direct smol::Async<T>, smol::channel, smol::future::or, and async_io::IoSafe usage that needs asupersync equivalents. Key challenge: smol::Async<T> wraps blocking FDs with reactor - asupersync uses capability-based IoCap model instead. Needs design work for the I/O wrapping layer. Blocked by: understanding asupersync IoCap API and creating an Async<T>-like adapter.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: TopazHarbor research: asupersync uses IoRegistration (per-type, not generic Async<T>). TcpStream/UnixStream each embed Option<IoRegistration> directly. To build generic Async<T>: wrap T:AsRawFd + IoRegistration + implement AsyncRead/AsyncWrite with rearm pattern. Alternative: add feature-gated conditional compilation (async-smol vs async-asupersync) like SSH crate, keeping smol path until native mux replaces these legacy crates.

comments.author: OliveDesert
comments.text:
Code-grounded execution split after validating current sources and Asupersync primitives on 2026-04-03.

What the code says now
- `frankenterm/client` and `crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl` are the direct Smol entrypoints.
- Support crates already partially know about native Asupersync:
  - `codec` defaults to `async-asupersync` and only stays on Smol when callers force `async-smol`.
  - `frankenterm-ssh` defaults to `async-asupersync` and already exposes a runtime shim (`runtime::block_on`, channel/io reexports).
  - `frankenterm-uds` and `async_ossl` default to `async-asupersync`, but today they only expose blocking `Read`/`Write` wrappers plus optional `async_io::IoSafe`.
- The hard blockers are therefore not abstract runtime folklore; they are concrete call sites and wrapper gaps:
  1. local Unix / mux-server dispatch path
  2. SSH proxy / pipe path
  3. TLS/OpenSSL path

Important design correction
- The first idea in this bead description about creating an Async<T>-like generic adapter should NOT be the default architecture.
- Asupersync's native pattern is per-type `Option<IoRegistration>` plus `rearm(...)` on `WouldBlock`, as seen in its own `net::unix::UnixStream` and `process` pipe wrappers.
- The finish-line-safe approach is: use concrete per-type native adapters where the project owns the type, and only fall back to a narrow local adapter when there is no better owned boundary.

Recommended implementation slicing
1. Local Unix + mux-server dispatch first.
   files: `frankenterm/uds/src/lib.rs`, `crates/frankenterm-mux-server-impl/src/dispatch.rs`, `frankenterm/client/src/client.rs`, relevant `Cargo.toml` files.
   plan: add native Asupersync `AsyncRead`/`AsyncWrite` + readiness registration to `frankenterm-uds::UnixStream`; stop forcing `codec`/`uds`/`async_ossl` into Smol mode from client and mux-server manifests; replace `smol::Async` + `smol::channel` + `smol::future::or` in dispatch and the local client path with native Asupersync-shaped loops.

2. SSH proxy / pipe path second.
   files: `frankenterm/client/src/client.rs`, possibly `frankenterm/ssh/*` only if needed.
   plan: remove direct `smol::block_on` in favor of the SSH runtime shim immediately; then decide whether `SshStream` should gain a small local Asupersync pipe-registration adapter or reuse an existing process-pipe pattern from Asupersync. This path is not the same problem as Unix sockets and should not be conflated with them.

3. TLS/OpenSSL path third, coordinated with finish-line networking work.
   files: `frankenterm/client/src/client.rs`, `frankenterm/async_ossl/src/lib.rs`.
   plan: either give `AsyncSslStream` a native Asupersync readiness wrapper using the same `IoRegistration`/`WouldBlock` pattern, or deliberately hand this slice to the broader native-network/TLS lane if the correct answer is to stop using this wrapper entirely. Do not hide TLS behind another executor-neutral shim.

Immediate low-risk cleanup opportunities once the first slice starts
- direct `smol::block_on(sess.exec(...))` in `client.rs` should route through `frankenterm-ssh`'s runtime shim rather than calling Smol directly.
- `smol::Timer::after(...)` in `client.rs` should move to a native timer path (`asupersync::time` or a repo-local native shim) rather than survive as a stray holdout.

This bead should now be read as: concrete per-transport native cutover, not "invent a new generic Async<T> compatibility layer".

title: mcp_tools.rs has 11 i64::try_from(now_ms()).unwrap_or(0) sites with no observability counter
description:
mcp_tools.rs has 11 sites with the pattern:

    ts_ms: i64::try_from(now_ms()).unwrap_or(0),

When the u64 → i64 conversion fails (now_ms() corrupted to a value > i64::MAX), the timestamp silently collapses to 0. The audit row records ts_ms=0 and the operator has no signal that the clock cast failed — same observability gap that ft-fp6st (invalid regex) and ft-z2nve-style policy_clock_anomaly_count addressed in policy.rs.

In practice this never fails (now_ms() is monotonic time-since-UNIX_EPOCH, currently ~1.7 trillion ms; i64::MAX is ~9.2 quintillion). But the silent fallback to 0 is a code smell and the observability gap is real — if a future code path corrupts now_ms() (e.g., subtraction underflow yielding u64::MAX, or a 2's-complement bug), the audit chain accumulates ts=0 entries with no counter to surface the anomaly.

Sites in mcp_tools.rs:
- line 471: pane query audit row
- line 511: another audit row
- line 3803, 4021, 5253: workflow / mission / approval audit rows
- + 6 more (grep -c reports 11)

Fix shape: helper  that does the conversion AND bumps a  AtomicU64 on collapse to 0. Replace all 11 sites with the helper. Same shape as policy.rs's  + POLICY_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT (policy.rs:1878 and surrounding helpers).

Cross-references: ft-fp6st (policy regex compile counter, same pattern), policy.rs:1899 record_policy_clock_anomaly (the helper-bump idiom).
notes: Counter shipped at 89ee68c4e. mcp_clock_anomaly_count + accessor + reset + mcp_now_ms_i64 helper; all 11 i64::try_from(now_ms()).unwrap_or(0) sites in mcp_tools.rs replaced with the helper. 3 tests pin the counter contract. Same shape as policy.rs's POLICY_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT (ft-fp6st pattern). Lib check clean.

title: [ARCH] integrate PhiAccrualFailureDetector into headless_mux_server::check_peer_health (br-ft-nll8a follow-up)
description:
[ARCH] integrate PhiAccrualFailureDetector into headless_mux_server::check_peer_health (br-ft-nll8a follow-up)

Substrate ft-nll8a shipped the φ-accrual failure detector as crate::phi_accrual_failure_detector. This bead tracks the production-side migration from the current hard-threshold timeout to the adaptive accrual approach.

Current code (crates/frankenterm-core/src/headless_mux_server.rs:518):
```rust
pub fn check_peer_health(&mut self) {
    let now = epoch_ms();
    let timeout = self.config.peer_timeout_ms;
    for peer in self.peers.values_mut() {
        if peer.status == PeerStatus::Connected
            && now.saturating_sub(peer.last_heartbeat_at) > timeout
        {
            peer.status = PeerStatus::Unreachable;
        }
    }
}
```

Migration shape:
1. Add `failure_detector: PhiAccrualFailureDetector` field to PeerInfo (struct at line 68).
2. On heartbeat receipt (locate sites: search for assignments to `peer.last_heartbeat_at`), call `peer.failure_detector.record_heartbeat(now_micros)`.
3. In check_peer_health, replace the hard threshold check with:
   `peer.failure_detector.is_unreachable(now_micros, self.config.suspicion_threshold)`
4. Add `suspicion_threshold: f64` to ServerConfig (default DEFAULT_SUSPICION_THRESHOLD = 8.0).
5. Update tests that exercise check_peer_health to drive heartbeats through record_heartbeat first.

Rollback: keep peer_timeout_ms field for one release as fallback; gate on suspicion_threshold being Some.

Acceptance:
- check_peer_health uses PhiAccrualFailureDetector::is_unreachable.
- Regression test confirms a peer with steady-state 1s heartbeats followed by 30s silence transitions to Unreachable.
- Regression test confirms a peer with high-variance heartbeats (1s±500ms jitter) does NOT flip Unreachable on a single 5s gap (false-positive rate down).
- All ServerConfig defaults documented; default threshold matches Akka/Cassandra (8.0).

Why P3:
- Substrate is shipped; this is integration only.
- Current hard-threshold behavior is functionally correct for the common case; this improves correctness in variance-prone topologies.
- No active SEC or correctness incident; soft win.

Cross-references:
- Substrate: ft-nll8a (closed in same commit).
- Substrate code: crates/frankenterm-core/src/phi_accrual_failure_detector.rs.
- Production callsite: crates/frankenterm-core/src/headless_mux_server.rs:518 (check_peer_health).
- Heartbeat-receipt sites to wire (TBD by integrator): grep `last_heartbeat_at` in headless_mux_server.rs and any RemoteRequest handler.
notes: Shipped this commit. PhiAccrualFailureDetector wired into PeerInfo (#[serde(skip)] field) + ServerConfig (suspicion_threshold f64, default 8.0). check_peer_health now uses peer.failure_detector.is_unreachable(now_micros, threshold) instead of fixed timeout vs elapsed. Heartbeat handler + JoinFederation handler call record_heartbeat. Legacy peer_timeout_ms field retained for serde back-compat but no longer consulted. Regression test check_peer_health_phi_accrual_tolerates_variance_ft_roacq drives 200 bursty heartbeats (alternating 0.5s/2s) and confirms 5s gap does NOT flip Unreachable (suspicion < 8.0). Existing check_peer_health_marks_timeout test preserved by seeding detector with one heartbeat at last_heartbeat_at = 0 — saturated suspicion still trips threshold. server_config_serde + server_config_roundtrip tests updated to include suspicion_threshold field. cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features clean in 22s.

title: [SEV] CommandBuilder env_map_serde silently collides duplicate keys after to_string_lossy
description: frankenterm/pty/src/cmdbuilder.rs env_map_serde (added in 803356bf) maps BTreeMap<OsString, EnvEntry> -> JSON via OsString::to_string_lossy for keys. Two distinct OsString keys whose non-UTF-8 bytes differ but collapse to the same String under lossy conversion will (1) produce a JSON map containing duplicate keys during serialize (most JSON parsers keep last, silently dropping one entry), and (2) on deserialize the BTreeMap::insert loop overwrites on collision, again silently dropping entries without returning an error. The adapter offers no detection or rejection of this case — a corrupted env set roundtrips to a smaller env set with no diagnostic. Metamorphic property: |deserialize(serialize(m))| == |m| — currently violated for any m with keys that collide under to_string_lossy. Conformance concern: the commit message asserts 'POSIX env names are ASCII-only' but setenv(3) on Linux accepts non-ASCII bytes (LC_*=ja_JP.UTF-8 etc.), and libc-level execve passes raw bytes. Fix by either (a) erroring on lossy conversion in both directions, or (b) serializing as an array of [key_bytes, value] pairs via serde_bytes / base64 so the roundtrip is lossless. At minimum add a proptest that asserts roundtrip preserves map size when two synthesized OsString keys share a lossy-equivalent representation.
close_reason: Fixed in 7a452b96: replaced map adapter with sequence-of-pairs adapter so every distinct OsString key survives serde roundtrip losslessly (via OsString's native byte/UTF-16-preserving enum encoding in value position). Added 2 regression proptests: one generates arbitrary byte keys (many non-UTF-8) and asserts all distinct keys roundtrip with paired values intact; the other injects two different invalid-UTF-8 sequences that both lossy-render to U+FFFD and asserts both survive. Test-binary run is blocked by pane6-target lock contention; fix is structurally complete and compiles clean at my previous build pass.

title: [OBS] ingest.rs has 6 silent set_tracked_bytes swallows; upstream None-return semantics undocumented
description:
cc1 PHASE 3-style audit of patterns/* + ingest/* domain at SHA fcac90e08 found one maintainability gap.

## Site
6 production sites in `crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs` all swallow the `Option<PaneArenaStats>` return of `pane_arenas.set_tracked_bytes(...)` without explanatory comment:

- ingest.rs:922 (after `re_evaluate_observation`)
- ingest.rs:975 (after setting priority_override)
- ingest.rs:988 (after clearing priority_override)
- ingest.rs:1009 (loop over tracked_byte_updates batch)
- ingest.rs:1082 (after entry update in main pump)
- ingest.rs:1095 (after vacant.insert in main pump)

All six are uniform: `let _ = self.pane_arenas.set_tracked_bytes(pane_id, tracked_bytes);`

## Why this matters

`set_tracked_bytes` returns `Option<PaneArenaStats>` where:
- `Some(stats)` = pane was reserved, accounting updated
- `None` = pane not reserved (released or never allocated)

The `let _ =` swallow means: "if pane_id is no longer reserved, silently skip this accounting update." This is correct best-effort behavior because the next `discovery_tick` reconciles state, BUT:

1. The upstream doc at `crates/frankenterm-alloc/src/lib.rs:313` reads "Update the logical tracked byte count for a pane arena" — does NOT document the `None`-return semantics.

2. None of the 6 callsites have an inline comment explaining the swallow. Future readers either re-derive the semantics or worry that this is a swallowed bug.

3. Counter-example: comparable swallows in workflows/runner.rs:3053 (`let _ = cx;`) and workflows/mod.rs:229 (`let _ = std::panic::catch_unwind(...)`) BOTH have explanatory WHY comments.

## Suggested fix (single commit)

1. Upstream: extend the rustdoc on `set_tracked_bytes` to document the `None`-return semantics: `Returns None if pane_id is not reserved (no current allocation; usually means the pane was released between the upstream event and this update).`

2. Downstream: add ONE clarifying comment block above the first swallow site (line 922) referencing the upstream contract: `// pane_arenas returns None when the pane is no longer reserved; silent skip is intentional — the next discovery_tick reconciles if the pane comes back.`

This is doc-only — zero runtime change, zero behavioral change. Single commit, <30min.
notes:
Shipped doc-only fix: upstream rustdoc on `PaneArenaRegistry::set_tracked_bytes` now documents the `None`-return semantics, and ingest.rs adds a `br-ft-rsv5b` doc-block on the `pane_arenas` field that explains the swallow strategy applying to all 6 callsites uniformly.

Verification:
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on both files: clean
- cargo check -p frankenterm-alloc: 4.43s, clean
- Zero behavioral change (doc-only)

Audit context: cc1 PHASE 3-style multi-lens audit of patterns/* + ingest/* domains found this single maintainability gap. patterns/* (3 files) was clean — the only panic + expect sites in pattern_trigger.rs:451 + smart_selection_patterns.rs:61 are static-config fail-fast / build-time validation patterns with explicit WHY comments. ingest.rs production code (lines 1-2833 before mod tests) had 0 unwrap/expect, 0 panic!, 0 Vec::remove(0), 0 TODO/FIXME — only the 6-site set_tracked_bytes swallow without WHY breadcrumb.

title: [ft-q4udk follow-up] PooledReadConn lacks hit-rate counter; add for regression-test verifiability
description:
ft-q4udk acceptance criterion #3 asked for a regression test that 'asserts the pool's hit-rate stays > 80% after migration.' That requires PooledReadConn to expose hit-rate telemetry. Today the pool has no per-acquire hit/miss counters — only the silent LIFO recycle path.

## Substrate gap

`PooledReadConn::acquire` (storage.rs:8485) takes the recycled connection from the LIFO if present, else opens a fresh one. The branch is taken silently — no AtomicU64 counter increments, no tracing event, no exposed metric.

## Fix shape

Add to PooledReadConn module:
- `static POOL_HITS: AtomicU64` (or per-db_path map) bumped when `recycled` is Some.
- `static POOL_MISSES: AtomicU64` bumped when fallthrough to `open_read_storage_conn`.
- `pub fn pool_telemetry_snapshot() -> (u64, u64)` for tests + diagnostics.
- New regression test in tests/storage_pool_regression.rs: spawn N concurrent reader tasks against same db, assert hits/(hits+misses) > 0.80 after migration.

## Why follow-up not blocker

The structural regression ft-q4udk identified is FIXED by ft-3twzm (61ce1883a) + ft-ir23j (47b1b9cd8). Hit-rate counters are a verification mechanism, not a fix. Filing as P3 because the underlying pool contract is already restored.

Cross-refs: ft-q4udk (parent), ft-3twzm + ft-ir23j (the actual fixes), ft-bhyxz (original pool substrate).
close_reason: done

title: watchdoged_triple_buffer: WatchdogedHealth + PolledDecision pub fields; reconfigure_watchdog loses stats
description:
Audit of watchdoged_triple_buffer.rs (TripleBuffer + Watchdog wrapper) found 3 issues:

1. (pub-field, WatchdogedHealth) triple_buffer, watchdog, watchdog_active are pub. Even after the TripleBufferHealth/WatchdogStats inner fixes, the wrapper struct fields can be replaced wholesale by external code (h.triple_buffer = TripleBufferHealth::baseline() zeros recovered-event signal). Pure-math, deterministic.' but the implementation is the Euclidean algorithm using modulo (not bit shifts). Both produce correct GCD; doc is misleading. title: headless_mux_server: JoinFederation has no peer-count cap (unbounded DoS) + clobbers first_seen_at on rejoin
description:
crates/frankenterm-core/src/headless_mux_server.rs:402-416 RemoteRequest::JoinFederation blindly inserts into self.peers without checking a cap, and overwrites the existing PeerInfo entirely on every re-join — losing first_seen_at. Two distinct defects:

1. **Unbounded peer-map growth (DoS)**: ServerConfig has max_connections (for clients) and max_panes, but NO max_peers. A hostile or buggy counterparty spamming JoinFederation with distinct node_ids grows self.peers without bound, eventually OOM'ing the mux server. prune_unreachable_peers only fires after peer_timeout_ms + an external caller — a burst of N spurious JoinFederation requests can bloat the map before any prune runs. Parallel shape to ft-kfy99 (tmux_cc line cap), ft-phz7x (codec oversize tagged_len), ft-8ihuz (scrollback unbounded read).

2. **first_seen_at lost on rejoin**: Every JoinFederation fully replaces PeerInfo at line 404-414, including setting first_seen_at to epoch_ms(). A peer that legitimately rejoins (e.g. partition heal after the Heartbeat ft-lekgj path tells it to re-JoinFederation) loses its original first_seen_at — making 'how long has this peer been federated' observability lie.

Fix: add max_peers: u32 to ServerConfig (default 512, twice max_connections as headroom). In JoinFederation, if the node_id is NEW and self.peers.len() >= max_peers, return RemoteResponse::Error { code: "peer_registry_full" }. If the node_id already exists, preserve first_seen_at from the existing entry and only update the re-join-time fields (node, status, last_heartbeat_at, capabilities). Regression tests: (a) 512-peer cap rejects the 513th distinct JoinFederation with peer_registry_full; (b) a rejoin keeps first_seen_at of the original insert.
close_reason: Landed in 78721403 (fix(headless_mux_server): cap JoinFederation peer registry + preserve first_seen_at on rejoin). Added ServerConfig.max_peers (default 512) + JoinFederation rejects new peers past cap with peer_registry_full; re-joins of known node_ids still succeed (they don't consume a slot). Also preserves existing first_seen_at on rejoin. Two regression tests pin both contracts. Verification blocked by pre-existing frankenterm-core build blockers (ft-kqidb/uigpj/s2u51/zv3u9).

title: [idea-wizard] Resource cockpit v1 conformance and live proof convergence
description:
## Background

The ready queue is empty, Agent Mail is unavailable, and the active dirty worktree belongs to other lanes. Existing resource-pressure work is closed: `ft-gl0n0` shipped the first operator resource cockpit, and `ft-p3457` added the schema contract, macOS residency classifier, pressure receipts, and reduced RCH soak proof. A follow-up gap remains: `docs/json-schema/ft-resource-pressure-cockpit.json` requires a full v1 root envelope (`contract_id`, root `evidence_state`, `run_identity`, required `domains`, `residency_buckets`, `queue_backpressure`, `admission_decisions`, `action_receipts`, `artifact_paths`), while the live `SwarmResourceCockpitSnapshot` currently emits the legacy subset (`schema_version`, source/status/proof gate, summary/next move, memory tiers, slowest latency cohorts, capacity/resource decisions, storage IO, auto-tune decisions, mitigation history, drilldowns). The receipt and residency models exist in `memory_pressure.rs`, but they are not yet bridged into the live cockpit envelope.

## Phase 2: thirty ideas considered

Ideas considered before winnowing: contract-conforming cockpit DTO; root evidence-state synthesizer; required-domain fail-closed rows; run-identity hardware predicate rows; residency-bucket adapter; action-receipt adapter; queue-backpressure normalizer; admission-decision merger; storage-IO domain parity; worker-pool unavailable/measured rows; artifact-path retention; schema validation e2e; Robot JSON/TOON parity; doctor JSON parity; compact human table preservation; redaction invariant tests; stale telemetry freshness budgets; mixed-evidence root state; high-scale target-hardware proof gate; local/reduced proof classification; MCP resource endpoint parity; support-bundle attachment pointers; incident drilldown query rows; receipt persistence handoff to fleet mutation receipts; regression golden matrix; fuzz/property tests for missing telemetry; replay fixture for pressure transitions; docs claim scanner; operator runbook closeout; release scoreboard integration.

## Phase 2 top five

1. Full v1 contract-conforming live cockpit envelope, because the docs/schema already promise a shape that Robot/doctor consumers cannot currently rely on from the live Rust serializer.
2. Evidence-state and domain synthesis, because missing memory, worker, queue, or receipt telemetry must fail visibly instead of disappearing from the object.
3. Residency and action-receipt bridge, because the classifiers/receipts are useful only when they feed the canonical cockpit rather than living as separate helper models.
4. Robot/doctor/TOON conformance proof, because machine consumers need stable output and detailed reason codes without parsing raw logs.
5. RCH-backed schema/golden closeout, because any Rust output claim must prove Cargo/test/runtime was reached remotely and must preserve high-scale truth gates.

## Phase 3 next ten

Supporting ideas kept for later refinement: MCP endpoint parity; action receipt persistence handoff; cross-run pressure regression snapshots; incident support-bundle attachment paths; target-hardware run identity; stale/freshness property tests; resource what-if replay fixtures; operator drilldown search; release scoreboard integration; docs claim scanner for cockpit fields.

## Overlap check

This graph does not reopen `ft-p3457`; it treats that closed epic as the contract and helper-model foundation. It does not duplicate `ft-gl0n0`; that bead shipped the first cockpit subset and compact rows. It does not claim real 64-core / 256 GiB proof without target-class artifacts. It should avoid current dirty attestation and policy paths unless a child explicitly claims them later.

## Goal

Converge the live resource cockpit emitted by `ft doctor --json` and `ft robot capacity --level 2` with the documented v1 schema, while preserving truth-gated evidence states, redaction, compact operator rows, and RCH-only proof discipline.

## Non-goals

- No local heavy Cargo; Rust builds/tests/e2e proof use RCH.
- No synthetic high-scale `PROVEN` wording without 64+ CPU / 256+ GiB target hardware artifacts.
- No live process attach in ordinary tests.
- No Agent Mail repair/restart and no RCH worker mutation.
- No deletion or broad rewrite of existing cockpit, proof, or memory-pressure files.

## Acceptance

- The live cockpit can emit every required v1 schema field or a documented unavailable/stale row for unavailable domains.
- `memory_pressure.rs` residency classifications and action receipts have a clear adapter path into the canonical cockpit.
- Robot JSON, Robot TOON, and doctor JSON preserve reason codes, evidence states, and redaction invariants.
- A retained RCH proof lane shows schema/golden/e2e checks reached Cargo/test/runtime as appropriate, or blocks with precise RCH substrate artifacts.

title: [resource-cockpit-v1] Add contract-conforming DTO and evidence-domain synthesizer
description:
## Goal

Add the Rust model/adapter needed for the live resource cockpit to satisfy the documented v1 root envelope instead of only the older `SwarmResourceCockpitSnapshot` subset.

## Current evidence

`docs/json-schema/ft-resource-pressure-cockpit.json` requires `contract_id`, root `evidence_state`, `run_identity`, required domain rows, `queue_backpressure`, `admission_decisions`, `action_receipts`, and `artifact_paths`. `runtime_telemetry.rs::SwarmResourceCockpitSnapshot` currently serializes schema/version/source/status/proof gate, summaries, memory tiers, slowest latency cohorts, capacity/resource decisions, storage IO, auto-tune decisions, mitigation history, and drilldowns. Missing domains should not disappear or look green.

## Scope

- Add a v1 contract DTO or extend the existing cockpit snapshot so every required schema field is represented.
- Introduce a root evidence-state synthesizer: `measured`, `simulated`, `unavailable`, `stale`, or `mixed`.
- Add required domain rows for memory, rss_residency, pane_budget, queue_backpressure, storage_io, worker_pool, capacity_admission, resource_admission, and action_receipts.
- Missing telemetry must produce unavailable/stale/unknown domain rows with reason codes and drilldowns.
- Preserve existing compact human rows and existing field names where practical.

## Non-goals

- Do not wire live macOS process attachment here.
- Do not add high-scale proof claims.
- Do not weaken redaction or admission fail-closed behavior.

## Tests / proof

- Unit tests for measured, unavailable, stale, and mixed root evidence states.
- Serialization tests pin all required schema keys and required domain rows.
- RCH Cargo proof only: for example `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rz0eb-v1-dto cargo test -p frankenterm-core swarm_resource_cockpit_v1 --lib -- --nocapture`.

title: [resource-cockpit-v1] Bridge residency buckets and action receipts into cockpit inputs
description:
## Goal

Connect the already-implemented macOS residency classifier and pressure action receipt model to the v1 resource cockpit envelope so incident evidence and mitigation receipts appear in the canonical output.

## Current evidence

`memory_pressure.rs` contains `classify_macos_residency` and `evaluate_resource_pressure_action_receipts` plus tests. The live `SwarmResourceCockpitSnapshot` does not yet expose schema-level `residency_buckets` or `action_receipts`, and unavailable receipt/residency evidence is not synthesized into the required `rss_residency` or `action_receipts` domains.

## Scope

- Add adapter functions from `MacosResidencyClassification` to v1 `residency_buckets` plus the `rss_residency` domain row.
- Add adapter functions from `ResourcePressureActionReceiptReport` to v1 `action_receipts`, action-receipt domain summaries, mitigation history, and drilldowns.
- Preserve correlation ids, affected pane/agent/resource attribution, policy decisions, evidence freshness, and reason codes.
- When no live residency or receipt inputs exist, emit explicit unavailable/unknown rows instead of omitting the domain.
- Keep live process attachment optional and outside unit tests.

## Non-goals

- Do not build fleet mutation or persistence here; daemon-mediated mutation is tracked separately.
- Do not collect vmmap/heap/sample in tests.
- Do not treat a dry-run/planned receipt as a completed side effect.

## Tests / proof

- Unit tests for missing residency evidence, mixed residency evidence, unavailable receipts, stale receipts, and simultaneous pressure domains.
- Serialization tests prove the adapter output lands under the v1 fields with stable reason codes.
- RCH Cargo proof only, with a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` under `/tmp`.

title: [resource-cockpit-v1] Wire doctor, robot JSON, and robot TOON to the v1 envelope
description:

Make the user-facing and machine-facing capacity surfaces emit the same v1 resource cockpit semantics without forcing operators or agents to parse ad hoc rows.

title: [audit] chaos.rs: NaN probability silently disables fault, unbounded delay_ms DoS, probability=1.0 has 1/2^32 false-negative
description:
Audit findings in crates/frankenterm-core/src/chaos.rs:

(A) NaN probability silently disables fault injection. FaultMode::fail_with_probability calls .clamp(0.0, 1.0) which propagates NaN unchanged. Then 'if rand_val < probability' with NaN probability is always false — tester thinks they configured fault injection but no faults fire. Detection masquerade. Fix: sanitize NaN to 0.0 in the builder + the constructor.

(B) Unbounded delay_ms in FaultMode::Delay / DelayThenFail. delay_ms: u64 → std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(u64::MAX)) freezes the worker thread for ~584M years. Effective DoS via fault config; trivially set via set_fault. Cap at sane bound (e.g., 300_000ms = 5min) — fault injection legitimately needs delays measured in seconds, not hours.

(C) FaultMode::FailWithProbability uses 'rand_val < probability' strict inequality. With probability=1.0 and rand_val=1.0 (occurs when hash >> 32 == u32::MAX, ~1/2^32 of the time), the fault does NOT fire. Subtle false-negative when tester uses FailWithProbability(1.0) instead of AlwaysFail. Fix: special-case probability>=1.0 → always fail.
close_reason: All 3 findings landed in d06ef64d1. NaN probability sanitization (sanitize_probability) + delay_ms cap (MAX_DELAY_MS = 5min) + probability=1.0 short-circuit. Builder + evaluator both apply guards (defense against struct-init bypass). 7 regression tests added; all 62 chaos lib tests green.

- The gui's tick loop maintains a `LastRendered { tile_id, last_render_at }` map.
- Per-tile: if `now - last_render_at >= TileRefreshHint::EveryMs`, re-render and update.
- OnEvent tiles: re-render only when an explicit signal fires (e.g. mode change, session rename).
- Layout recomputed on any change to (specs, renders, bar_width).

### Layout caching
- Cache `LaidOutBar` per (specs, renders, bar_width) hash.
- Invalidate when any tile's RenderedTile changes or bar_width changes.
- Hot-path optimisation: hash_cell_grid-style FNV-1a over the layout inputs.

### Painter integration
- After layout, walk `LaidOutBar.placements` left-to-right and render each tile at `x_start..x_start + width`.
- Tile content lives in a row of `Cell` records; status bar occupies one row at the bottom of the window.

### Mouse handler
- Mouse-move over status bar: `bar.hit_test(x)` → if `Some(hit)`, call `tile.on_hover(hit.x_in_tile)` for tooltip.
- Mouse-click: `tile.on_click(hit.x_in_tile)` → `Option<TileAction>` (e.g. ToggleMode, OpenAgentList, ShowCostBreakdown).

### A11y / screen-reader integration
- On tile render-content change: post `accessibility_label` via NSAccessibility / AT-SPI.
- Cross-link a11y_tree.rs / ft-mpc9b.10.

### frankenterm.toml config
- `[[status_bar.tile]]` array: id, alignment, min_width, max_width, priority, source = "builtin:ft.mode" | "plugin:cost".
- Operator can rearrange / hide tiles by editing config (no rebuild).

### Plugin discovery
- Plugin tiles loaded from `~/.config/ft/plugins/*.wasm` via wasmtime.
- Cross-link ft-mpc9b.4.3.

### docs
- Author docs/status-bar/truncation-rules.md per the bead.

## Acceptance per the original bead
- 8 built-in tiles shipped + plugin trait surface
- Truncation rules documented + deterministic
- A11y labels mandatory; screen-reader announces tile content changes
- Operator config in frankenterm.toml

title: retry::RetryPolicy::delay_for_attempt panics on NaN backoff_factor or jitter_percent (no fail-closed)
description: RetryPolicy::delay_for_attempt computes base_ms = initial_ms as f64 * backoff_factor.powi(exp); then jitter_range = base_ms * jitter_percent; then rng.random_range(-jitter_range..=jitter_range). If backoff_factor or jitter_percent is NaN (from a malformed config, a fuzz harness, or a direct struct-literal construction bypassing new()), base_ms / jitter_range become NaN, and rng.random_range(NaN..=NaN) panics. Matches the fail-closed pattern already applied to disk_pressure (ft-761tz), continuous_backpressure (ft-yskcu), telemetry::Histogram (ft-b4l62). Fix: sanitize backoff_factor and jitter_percent inside delay_for_attempt — if either is not finite or out-of-range, substitute a safe default and return a non-NaN delay. Add proptest: any RetryPolicy with any f64 in backoff_factor/jitter_percent must produce a finite, non-panicking Duration for any attempt in 0..=63.
