title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G35] TLA+/Stateright state-space coverage measurement
description:
Background: Round 2 critique. TLA+ TLC and Stateright explorers report 'states explored' but no bead measures *coverage of the reachable state space*. A spec that explores 0.01% gives spurious confidence — a TLC run that terminates in 5 seconds either means the spec is small or TLC gave up.

Why this matters: 'we ran TLC, 0 violations' is meaningful only when 'we explored X% of reachable states' is also reported. Without a coverage metric, formal-method proofs become a ritual.

Acceptance criteria:
- A scripts/measure-tla-coverage.sh that, per spec, computes: declared invariants, max-depth, states explored, distinct-states explored, state-space estimate (from depth + branching factor), %-coverage estimate, time budget consumed
- Same for Stateright models (Stateright already exposes a stats API; wrap it)
- docs/specs/<name>.tla and tests/<name>_model.rs gain a // coverage-metric: comment block consumed by the script
- A coverage threshold per spec (declared in docs/specs/<name>.tla): below threshold = warning in CI; below half threshold = CI fail
- Release attestation bundle lists per-spec coverage under proofs/<subsystem>.json (extends G33)
- proof_category: 6 (formal-method) augmented with category 2 (property/proptest) for the random-sampling component

References: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md G13, G33 (TLA+ doctrine), Stateright API docs.

proof_category: 6 (formal-method) + 2 (property)
notes:
## Refinement enrichments (Phase 5)

### Test companion
- Unit: tests/tlc_coverage_estimate.rs — synthetic small spec (3-state ring buffer) with known reachable state count; assert measure-tla-coverage reports the correct count within tolerance. Logs each invocation's metrics to target/test-logs/tlc-coverage/<spec>/<ts>.jsonl.
- Integration: tests/stateright_coverage.rs — wrap Stateright's stats API for the work-family model (G28), assert reported state-count matches BFS-explored count under a known seed.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_spec_coverage_release_gate.sh — drive scripts/measure-tla-coverage.sh + scripts/measure-stateright-coverage.sh, assert each spec's coverage emits a JSONL row, assert below-threshold specs trigger CI warning, below-half-threshold trigger CI failure.
- Property: proptest random spec sizes, assert coverage estimator returns monotone increasing values as TLC depth grows.
- Negative: tests/spec_explosion.rs — deliberately construct a state-space-explosion spec, assert coverage runner times out gracefully with state: 'space-explosion' rather than hanging.

### Operator surface
- 'ft robot specs coverage' lists per-spec { coverage_pct, threshold, states_explored, time_consumed, status }.
- 'ft robot specs coverage --spec <name>' single-spec detail.
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .spec_coverage.
- MCP: wa://specs/coverage, wa://specs/coverage/<spec>.

### Degradation behavior
- TLC OOM: emit state: 'oom-during-exploration' with last-recorded state count; do NOT silently truncate. Operator surface reports 'partial-coverage' for the affected spec.
- TLC version skew (CI runner has different TLC release than dev): test asserts spec parses + minimum-required-features supported; if not, surface state: 'tlc-version-incompat' with required-version hint.
- Stateright API breaking change: integration test is the canary; if the wrapper fails to build, CI fails the coverage-gate step explicitly rather than silently skipping.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G36] Continuous differential check against WezTerm upstream rendering
description:
Background: Round 2 critique. AGENTS.md lines 172-220 formalize a 10-step deliberate-port doctrine for WezTerm upstream commits. This is a *governance* invariant. But there is no *continuous differential* check confirming that on any input common to both upstreams, FrankenTerm and WezTerm render IDENTICALLY (modulo deliberate FrankenTerm divergences documented in legacy_wezterm/PROVENANCE).

Why this matters: WezTerm is the rendering-correctness oracle for the 4 vendored crates still under wezterm-* names AND for the renderer / surface / mux trees. A silent rendering regression in FrankenTerm relative to upstream is the kind of bug that breaks long-tail terminal applications without anyone noticing for months. Differential testing makes the divergence visible.

Acceptance criteria:
- A nightly CI lane that:
  - Checks out the current WezTerm upstream HEAD
  - Builds both binaries side-by-side
  - Runs a fixed corpus of terminal-conformance scripts (the existing tests/fixtures/terminal-conformance/ corpus is the seed)
  - Diffs the rendered output frame-by-frame (using existing SSIM-parity infra from G18)
  - Reports SSIM-divergent inputs to a dashboard
- Deliberate-divergence allow-list: docs/wezterm-divergence-allowlist.md per input pattern + rationale + bead ID
- Any new divergence not on the allow-list = CI failure
- Release attestation bundle gains tui/wezterm-divergence.json slot with the latest run's divergence count, allow-listed count, novel divergences (must be 0)
- proof_category: 9 (differential)
- This pairs with the existing weekly backport doctrine: backport = legitimate divergence ON PURPOSE; this fuzz check = divergence WE DIDN'T MEAN

References: AGENTS.md:172-220 (backport doctrine), G18 (SSIM infra), tests/fixtures/terminal-conformance/, frankenterm/{client,font,open-url,toast-notification}/.

proof_category: 9 (differential)
notes:
## Refinement enrichments (Phase 5)

### Test companion
- Unit: tests/wezterm_upstream_clone.rs — assert the clone-and-build helper produces a working WezTerm binary from a pinned upstream rev; logs build steps to target/test-logs/wezterm-upstream/<rev>/.
- Integration: tests/wezterm_differential_corpus.rs — for a small fixture corpus (5 terminal-conformance scripts), run both binaries, compute SSIM per output frame, assert ≥ floor. Emits per-script divergence report.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_wezterm_differential_nightly.sh — full nightly flow: clone upstream HEAD, build, run full corpus, diff, post results to dashboard, fail if any divergence not on allow-list. Per-stage structured logging.
- Adversarial: fuzz/wezterm_differential/fuzz_target.rs — generates random terminal escape sequences via Arbitrary, runs both binaries, asserts SSIM ≥ floor (or input is added to known-incompatible list). Catches escape sequences where upstream and FrankenTerm intentionally diverge.
- Known-divergence drill: scripts/test-divergence-detection.sh — deliberately inject a 1-pixel rendering difference in a controlled scenario, assert the gate detects it and reports the affected glyph.

### Operator surface
- 'ft robot wezterm-divergence' returns latest run summary { ts, upstream_rev, total_scripts, divergent_scripts, allow_listed_count, novel_divergences }.
- 'ft robot wezterm-divergence --detail <script>' single-script diff.
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .wezterm_differential.
- MCP: wa://wezterm/divergence, wa://wezterm/divergence/<script>.

### Degradation behavior
- WezTerm upstream is unreachable / clone fails: gate reports state: 'upstream-unavailable' with timestamp; CI passes (we don't punish ourselves for upstream availability) but flags the staleness window.
- WezTerm upstream introduces a breaking change to its build: gate emits state: 'upstream-build-failure' with the build log preserved; manual review required before allow-listing.
- SSIM float-drift across runs (non-determinism in either binary): emit deterministic_warning: true; if persistent, file as a sub-bead investigating the source.

### Proof category
9 (differential).

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G37] Sigstore/cosign keyless signing for release attestation bundles
description:
Background: Round 2 critique. G16 plans to ship docs/attestations/0.X.Y.json signed with ed25519, keyed off docs/attestations/signing-key.pub. But who signs signing-key.pub? A bundle-with-no-key-provenance is a single point of forgery: anyone who compromises the build environment can substitute a key and a matching bundle.

Why this matters: ft is sold as the control plane for AI agents. An AI agent verifying a bundle wants to know: 'is this bundle signed by a key whose provenance I can chain back to a trusted authority?' Sigstore/cosign keyless signing provides exactly this via the Fulcio root CA + Rekor transparency log: every signature is bound to a CI run identity, every signature is logged, anyone can verify the chain offline against the Fulcio root.

Acceptance criteria:
- The release build pipeline signs each docs/attestations/0.X.Y.json with cosign keyless, producing a .sigstore bundle file alongside
- The bundle includes the Fulcio cert + Rekor inclusion proof
- docs/attestations/verify.sh / 'ft attestation verify' both validate the sigstore bundle (not just the ed25519 sig)
- A docs/attestations/SIGNING.md doc explains: which CI run identity is allowed to sign (the .github/workflows/release.yml run on tag push), the Fulcio root, the Rekor log URL, how a third party validates
- The bundle's own schema validates a 'sigstore_bundle' field with hash of the .sigstore file
- proof_category: 10 (cryptographic attestation)
- This replaces the bridge-plan G16 acceptance criterion 'signed with ed25519 keyed off signing-key.pub' (which has the SPOF problem). The ed25519-only path stays as a fallback for offline builds.

References: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md G11 (signing requirement), https://docs.sigstore.dev/, https://github.com/sigstore/cosign.

proof_category: 10 (cryptographic)
close_reason: Implemented Sigstore keyless attestation binding: release build now records signature.sigstore_bundle path/sha256/size, verifier validates the .sigstore bytes before cosign verify-blob, release gate uses --strict-deferred, SIGNING.md documents CI identity/Fulcio/Rekor/manual verification, and schema/tests cover the new field. Proof: shellcheck; bash -n; jq schema; tests/scripts/test_attestation_build_matrix.sh (10/10); scripts/attestation-verify.sh docs/attestations/0.0.0-dev.json --json; cargo fmt --check --package frankenterm-core; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-rch-attestation-sigstore cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test attestation_manifest_schema (4 passed). title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G38] Stochastic network calculus for p99.99 latency bounds under heavy-tail arrivals
description:
Background: Round 3 alien-graveyard pass. latency_stages.rs implements classical min-plus algebra (deterministic network calculus). For a swarm running 200+ panes with bursty agent-generated output, arrivals are heavy-tail (Pareto / Lévy-stable, exponent < 2). Classical Lindley bounds break down — the tail is asymptotically infinite, the bound becomes vacuous. Stochastic Network Calculus (SNC, Jiang 2008; Ciucu 2007) extends to time-varying probabilistic envelopes and gives end-to-end p99.99 latency bounds even under heavy-tail arrivals.

Why this matters: A single p99.99 spike strands an agent for 10s and *users notice*. Bounding p99.99 mathematically — not just sampling it — is a competitive moat. Competitors sample; we can prove.

Acceptance criteria:
- An extension to crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages.rs implementing the stochastic-arrival-envelope and stochastic-service-curve types (Jiang's MGF-based formalism)
- A docs/perf/snc-derivation.md showing, for each stage in the <50ms capture path: arrival-envelope estimation from headline-claims-evidence (G19), service-curve estimation, computed p99.99 bound, agreement check with empirical p99.99 (G25/G26 dependency for the empirical side)
- Per-release bundle slot perf/snc-bounds.json with content hash of the derivation + per-stage bounds
- Heavy-tail detection: a fitness test (Hill estimator or other) that auto-classifies arrival distributions as light-tail vs heavy-tail, picks the appropriate envelope
- proof_category: 8 (network-calculus) + 7 (information-theoretic for the MGF/tail estimation)
- This bead supersedes G23 for the heavy-tail case; G23 remains for the light-tail/Lindley case

References: Jiang & Liu 'Stochastic Network Calculus' (Springer 2008), Ciucu 'Network Calculus Delay Bounds in Queueing Networks with Exact Solutions' (TR-2007), crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages.rs.

proof_category: 8 (network-calculus) + 7 (information-theoretic)
notes: Claimed by Claude Opus 4.7. Plan: implement stochastic network calculus (Jiang 2008 MGF-bound formalism) as a new module crates/ft-perf-gate/src/snc.rs. Provide HillEstimator for tail-index alpha detection, ArrivalEnvelope/ServiceCurve types, and a p99.99-bound deriver that returns LowConfidence on heavy-tail-out-of-domain (Lindley-side) inputs. Test against G54 heavy-tail.jsonl (Pareto alpha=1.5, labeled in manifest). Honest scope: ship the analytical machinery + correctness tests; empirical-bench backfill stays as G19.* + G18.* responsibility.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G39] Persistent homology for SSIM-complement visual regression detection
description:
Background: Round 3 alien-graveyard pass. SSIM is a pixel-pairwise metric. Two glyphs may be pixel-different (e.g., antialiasing changes between fontconfig releases) but topologically identical (same connected components, same loops). Conversely, pixel-similar but topologically broken (a stroke that's been disconnected by a sub-pixel rounding bug) is visually catastrophic but barely moves SSIM. Persistent homology (Edelsbrunner-Harer 2002) gives a shape-invariant descriptor: the persistence diagram of a glyph's super-level-set filtration is the topological signature.

Why this matters: SSIM-parity is the renderer parity invariant (G18 + G36). But SSIM has known blindspots — small high-frequency errors that humans see, large smooth differences humans don't. Persistent homology catches the second-kind error (smooth-but-topologically-broken) that SSIM misses.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new crate frankenterm-topo at crates/frankenterm-topo/ implementing persistence-diagram computation over rendered glyph bitmaps (using gudhi-rs bindings or a from-scratch H0/H1 implementation; the bitmaps are small enough that O(n²) is fine)
- For each glyph in tests/fixtures/terminal-conformance/expected/, compute persistence diagrams of both the oracle render (ratatui or WezTerm upstream) and the subject render (ftui)
- Wasserstein-distance-based parity metric: bottleneck distance between diagrams below a per-glyph threshold = pass
- A complementary report to SSIM-parity in docs/attestations/tui/render-parity.json: shows both the SSIM number and the persistence-distance number
- Release bundle slot tui/topology-parity.json
- proof_category: a new entry in the taxonomy registry — category 11 'topological invariant', distinct from category 9 differential (which compares output, not shape)

References: Edelsbrunner & Harer 'Computational Topology' (AMS 2010), https://github.com/GUDHI/gudhi-devel.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G40] Submodular set-cover for benchmark corpus minimization
description:
Background: Round 3. 108 Criterion bench files. CI time is finite. The minimum subset of benches that covers (a) all 10 proof-artifact categories used by the release bundle, (b) all 25-ish gap groups in this epic, (c) all 5 contract families is a SUBMODULAR set-cover problem (covering function is submodular: marginal coverage gain decreases with set size). Greedy selection on a submodular objective gives a (1 - 1/e) ≈ 63% optimality guarantee (Nemhauser-Wolsey-Fisher 1978). We can shrink the per-PR CI lane to a third of its size while losing <40% of coverage value.

Why this matters: CI runtime is the developer-velocity bottleneck. A principled subset-selection algorithm replaces 'pick a few benches randomly' with a provable-coverage strategy.

Acceptance criteria:
- A scripts/select-pr-bench-subset.sh that:
  - Reads docs/perf/bench-coverage-matrix.json declaring per-bench category coverage + claim coverage
  - Runs greedy submodular selection given a time budget (e.g., 5 minutes of CI)
  - Outputs the selected subset to target/ci-bench-subset.json
- A CI mode 'pr_subset' that runs only the selected benches per PR; the full set runs on main + release
- The bench-coverage-matrix.json is auto-updated by a 'bench-meta' helper macro on each Criterion bench
- Per-PR CI gates use SPRT (G25) on only the selected subset; the full sweep happens on main
- proof_category: this is an *infrastructure* bead, not a proof bead; it has no taxonomy ID but enables better coverage with less compute
- Optionality: pair with 'epsilon-greedy' exploration: 5% of PR runs pick a random bench OUTSIDE the cover, to surface unexpected regressions

References: Nemhauser-Wolsey-Fisher 1978 ('An analysis of approximations for maximizing submodular set functions'), Krause & Golovin 2014 ('Submodular Function Maximization'), Streeter & Golovin 2008 (online submodular).

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G41] PAC-Bayes generalization bound for semantic-search recall
description:
Background: Round 3. README:85 advertises 'feature-gated semantic/hybrid search modes (requires ML embeddings)'. The recall claim on the test corpus says nothing about recall on the *next* user query. PAC-Bayes bounds (McAllester 1999, Catoni 2007) give a high-probability lower bound on true risk from observed empirical risk; applied to recall, they give a guaranteed lower bound on recall over the unseen-query distribution.

Why this matters: 'semantic search works' as marketing copy is unverifiable. 'with probability ≥99%, recall on unseen queries is ≥X' is a real claim a user can act on. The bound also gives a principled training-set-size requirement.

Acceptance criteria:
- A docs/perf/semantic-search-pac-bayes-derivation.md applying Catoni's PAC-Bayes bound to the embedder + retriever stack
- Prerequisites: a held-out query set (production-realistic, not synthetic), a calibration-vs-test split, the embedder hyperparameter posterior
- The bound publishes: recall lower-bound at 99% confidence, sample-size required to tighten the bound by 1%, sensitivity of bound to prior-on-hyperparameters
- Release bundle slot proofs/semantic-search-pac-bayes.json
- proof_category: 7 (information-theoretic, the McAllester family is information-theoretic in spirit)
- Gated on the semantic-search feature being non-trivially used; this is a P3 bead until the feature stabilizes

References: McAllester 1999 ('PAC-Bayesian Model Averaging'), Catoni 2007 ('PAC-Bayesian Supervised Classification'), Dziugaite & Roy 2017 (computing non-vacuous PAC-Bayes bounds for deep nets).

proof_category: 7 (information-theoretic)

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G42] KL-divergence-based regime-shift detector to gate SPRT decisions
description:
Background: Round 3. G26 conformal bands detect drift after it has happened. G25 SPRT decides regressions assuming a stationary null. Both fail under regime shift (e.g., a kernel update changes the workload distribution wholesale, causing every metric to drift simultaneously). A KL-divergence-based change-point detector (Page-Hinkley + information-theoretic threshold; or Bayesian online change-point detection per Adams & MacKay 2007) catches regime shift *as* it happens and pauses SPRT decisions until the new regime calibrates.

Why this matters: Without regime-shift detection, a single kernel update fires hundreds of false-positive regressions across the whole metric panel. Operators learn to ignore the gate; the gate dies.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new module crates/ft-perf-gate/src/regime_shift.rs implementing Bayesian online change-point detection over the per-claim evidence streams (G19)
- On detected change point: G25 SPRT pauses for the affected metric until N samples (declared in config) recalibrate the new regime; G26 conformal band recomputes
- A docs/perf/regime-shift-events.jsonl audit log of detected change points (with timestamp, metrics affected, suspected cause from causal-DAG correlation [pairs with G43])
- Threshold derived from KL-divergence between rolling pre/post distributions; documented in docs/perf/regime-shift-methodology.md
- proof_category: 7 (information-theoretic)
- This is a meta-gate above G25 and G26

References: Adams & MacKay 2007 ('Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection'), Page 1954 ('Continuous Inspection Schemes' — Page-Hinkley original).

proof_category: 7 (information-theoretic)
notes: Claimed by Claude Opus 4.7. Plan: replace regime_shift.rs scaffold with Page-Hinkley CUSUM (Page 1954) over windowed KL-divergence between pre/post slices. Test against G54 regime-shift.jsonl (labeled change-point at sample 100, mean+1.3x, stddev*1.8x). Add baseline-no-fire test to bound false-positive rate.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G43] Causal DAG attribution for perf regressions
description:
Background: Round 3. Today a perf regression in CI is observational: 'metric M dropped 12% on commit C; investigate.' But the *cause* could be commit C, an env-var change, a runner hardware revision, a workload change, or interaction. Causal inference over a DAG of (commit, runner-sku, env-var values, workload class, metric) gives principled attribution: the PC algorithm (Spirtes-Glymour-Scheines 2000) infers the causal skeleton from observational data; do-calculus then gives the counterfactual ('would M have dropped if C hadn't shipped but everything else stayed the same?').

Why this matters: Without causal attribution, regression triage is guesswork. With it, the PR that caused a regression is identified with confidence, and rollback decisions stop being polluted by confounding.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new module crates/ft-perf-gate/src/causal_attribution.rs running the PC algorithm over the historical evidence streams + commit-metadata
- Per regression event (from G25 SPRT), emit a docs/perf/regression-attribution/<event-id>.json with: implicated commit, alternative explanations ranked by counterfactual likelihood, confounders identified, residual unexplained variance
- A weekly causal-skeleton refresh: re-run PC over the rolling 30-day window, publish docs/perf/causal-graph.json
- proof_category: 7 (information-theoretic) — causal DAGs are information-theoretic in spirit (conditional independence tests use mutual information)
- This is P3 because the attribution machinery is only valuable once we have enough regression events to attribute over; bootstrap once G25 ships

References: Spirtes-Glymour-Scheines 2000 ('Causation, Prediction, and Search'), Pearl 2009 ('Causality'), https://github.com/microsoft/dowhy.

proof_category: 7 (information-theoretic)
notes:
## Refinement enrichments (Phase 5)

### Test companion
- Unit: crates/ft-perf-gate/tests/causal_attribution.rs — PC algorithm on synthetic DAGs with known structure. Assert PC recovers the skeleton + orients edges correctly under faithfulness. Logs conditional-independence test results per edge.
- Integration: tests/causal_attribution_regression.rs — replay a recorded regression event with its known true cause, assert the causal attributor ranks the true cause within the top-3 candidates with confidence > threshold.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_causal_attribution_pr_comment.sh — inject a synthetic regression in CI, assert the PR comment contains the attribution report with implicated commit, alternatives, confounders, residual variance.
- Property: proptest random DAG structures, assert PC + do-calculus are sound (no spurious counterfactual claims, conservative under low data).
- Negative: tests/causal_attribution_insufficient_data.rs — feed an event with too-few observations, assert attributor returns 'low-confidence' state rather than guessing.

### Operator surface
- 'ft robot perf attribution --event <id>' returns full attribution report.
- 'ft robot perf attribution-graph' returns the latest causal-skeleton refresh.
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .attribution_summary (last 5 events).
- MCP: wa://perf/attribution, wa://perf/attribution/<event-id>, wa://perf/attribution/graph.
- CI PR comment: top-3 alternatives ranked by counterfactual likelihood.

### Degradation behavior
- Insufficient samples to test conditional independence: attributor returns state: 'low-data-confidence' with sample-count gap and recommends waiting for more events. Do not output spurious attribution.
- Causal skeleton contains undirected edges (PC could not orient): output 'ambiguous-attribution' with all candidates listed.
- Hidden-confounder suspected (e.g., observed correlations explained only via unobserved variable): output 'hidden-confounder-suspected' with diagnostic and link to investigation.

### Proof category
7 (information-theoretic) — PC algorithm uses conditional mutual information for independence tests.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G44] Coq/Lean mechanized proof of RuntimeProof sealed-trait soundness
description:
Background: Round 3. G1 tokio-eradication anchors on the sealed RuntimeProof trait. 'sealed' relies on private-module visibility — a Rust convention, not a theorem. A mechanized proof of soundness ('no type outside the declared list can implement RuntimeProof') gives a different class of confidence: the soundness argument is checked by Coq, Lean 4, or F*, not by code review.

Why this matters: For 99% of code, mechanized proofs are overkill. For the type-level invariant that anchors the entire tokio-eradication doctrine, they are exactly right. A reviewer can convince themselves the sealed-trait pattern is sound; only a mechanized proof can convince the *project* of it across decades.

Acceptance criteria:
- A docs/proofs/runtime-proof-soundness.{v,lean} (Coq or Lean 4) modeling Rust's visibility + sealed-trait pattern as an inductive type with the soundness theorem proven
- The proof is checked in CI (cargo step: 'check Coq proof' / 'check Lean proof')
- A docs/proofs/runtime-proof-soundness.md narrating the model assumptions, the theorem, and why it gives confidence the Rust implementation has the property
- Release bundle slot proofs/runtime-proof-soundness.json
- proof_category: 1 (type-level) elevated by 6 (formal-method mechanized check)
- The proof may model an idealized Rust subset (not full Rust); the modeling assumptions are themselves part of the proof's deliverable

References: Coq Proof Assistant (https://coq.inria.fr/), Lean 4 (https://lean-lang.org/), RustBelt (https://plv.mpi-sws.org/rustbelt/) as prior art.

proof_category: 1 (type-level) + 6 (formal-method)
notes:
## Refinement enrichments (Phase 5 round 1 — RESTORED in round 7 after detecting overwrite by round-2)

### Test companion
- Unit (proof side): the Coq or Lean proof itself is the unit test — CI runs 'coqc' or 'lake build' to type-check; failure to type-check = test failure.
- Integration: tests/runtime_proof_soundness_canary.rs — Rust-side compile_fail doctest already exists; this bead extends it with a property-check that the set of impls of RuntimeProof in the live workspace exactly equals the set declared in the mechanized proof's model.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_runtime_proof_check.sh — checks out the proof, runs the proof checker, asserts no axioms admitted, captures the full proof trace as artifact.
- Property (against the model): for each variant in the inductive type the proof models, assert there exists exactly one Rust impl satisfying the corresponding trait. Cross-check via 'cargo expand' or syn-based AST scan.
- Negative: deliberately add a leaf impl of RuntimeProof in a quarantine file, assert (a) the Rust code refuses to compile via the existing sealed-trait pattern, AND (b) the proof-vs-code consistency test flags the discrepancy.

### Operator surface
- 'ft doctor proofs runtime' returns proof status + last-check timestamp + axioms-admitted count (target: 0).
- MCP: wa://proofs/runtime-soundness.
- README sealed-trait section footnotes the proof artifact.

### Degradation behavior
- Coq/Lean toolchain breaking change: CI fails the proof-check step with explicit version-mismatch error; release gate flags 'proof-toolchain-incompat' but doesn't block on it (the runtime sealed-trait invariant continues to hold via the Rust-side pattern; the mechanized proof is a *defense-in-depth* layer).
- Axioms added to the proof (regression in proof discipline): CI fails with the specific axioms listed; reviewer must explicitly justify each.
- Proof-vs-code drift detected (model and Rust diverged): emit state: 'proof-stale' with the specific divergence; bead reopened to re-establish consistency.

### Proof category
1 (type-level) + 12 (mechanized — new category introduced by this run's Round 3).

## Round-2 priority escalation (Phase 5 refinement pass 2)

Originally filed at P3 with rationale 'mechanized proofs are overkill for app code'. On second pass: this proof is the *soundness anchor* for the entire G1 tokio-eradication doctrine. The sealed-trait pattern relies on private-module visibility (a Rust convention). Without a mechanized check, an unintentional 'pub' on the sealed module would silently void every downstream gate (deny.toml, the asupersync_test! macro, the four-layer enforcement story in AGENTS.md:239-250). P2 reflects that the proof is defense-in-depth for a load-bearing invariant, not an academic exercise.

Also reinforces G50 audit: if the soundness proof exists in HEAD, the bead can close legitimately; if not, the bead's claimed closure is exactly the silent-close anti-pattern G50 is investigating.

## Round-7 regression note

The round-1 sections above were OVERWRITTEN in round-2 when the priority-escalation note was written via 'br update --notes' (REPLACE semantics). Round-7 audit caught the regression, restored both. See G62 (ft-tf6g3.50) doctrine bead.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G18] Renderer SLO attestation suite — resize FPS / input-to-photon / SSIM parity / atlas stability / idle GPU power
description:
Background: README.md lines 1315-1320 introduced a new consolidated renderer SLO catalog covering resize FPS, input-to-photon latency, atlas stability, SSIM-parity vs reference, and idle GPU power. This catalog post-dates the 2026-04-30 bridge plan (which only knew about <50ms capture latency in the G3 inventory). No bead, no proof artifact, no attestation slot covers it.

Why this matters: The renderer overhaul is the most user-visible perf claim in the product. Resize FPS and input-to-photon are what users *feel*. Atlas stability and SSIM-parity protect against silent visual regressions that humans wouldn't catch. Idle GPU power is the laptop-battery cost claim. Each is testable; none is currently attested.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-SLO measurement harness shipped under crates/frankenterm-gui/benches/renderer_slo/ (one Criterion bench file per SLO)
- Resize FPS: drive a 20→200 pane swarm through a deterministic resize storm, measure achieved FPS during the storm. Publish p50/p95/p99 with sample size and confidence interval per the G3 round-3 statistical-rigor pattern.
- Input-to-photon: instrument a known-key press → frame-flush trace through ftui_backend → headless_render. Sub-frame-budget claim must be Lindley-bound-derivable via the latency_stages.rs machinery (G23 dependency).
- SSIM-parity: headless render the same input through ratatui (oracle) and ftui (subject), assert SSIM ≥ floor across a fixed input corpus. Floor declared in docs/perf/renderer-slo-floors.json.
- Atlas stability: cache-evict / cache-recover cycle, assert glyph-rendering identical across the cycle. Anti-flicker invariant.
- Idle GPU power: macOS powermetrics + Linux intel_gpu_top / amdgpu_top sampling during the 'idle swarm' workload (200 panes, no input). Publish median watts.
- Each SLO has a slot in docs/attestations/tui/render-parity.json (already exists for SSIM-parity skeleton) — extend or add render-slo-suite.json.
- Per-PR regression gate fires on >10% degradation in any SLO using SPRT (G25 dependency) to suppress noise.
- README perf table links each SLO to its attestation entry.

References: README.md:1315-1320 (the catalog), docs/perf/headline-claims-audit.md, crates/frankenterm-gui/tests/gpu_regression.rs (existing fixture infra), tests/fixtures/terminal-conformance/expected/ (existing per-test golden artifact pattern).

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G18.3] SSIM-parity SLO — oracle render + bottleneck (G39 topology cross-check)
description:
G18 decomposition. README:1318 SSIM-parity SLO. Headless-render same input through ratatui (oracle) and ftui (subject), assert SSIM ≥ floor across a fixed input corpus.

### Test companion
- tests/ssim_parity_corpus.rs — for each fixture in tests/fixtures/terminal-conformance/expected/, run ratatui + ftui renders, compute SSIM, assert ≥ floor.
- tests/ssim_floor_audit.rs — proptest random adversarial inputs (extreme zoom, Unicode edge cases, ANSI escape boundary cases), assert SSIM floor still holds OR document the divergence.
- tests/e2e/test_ssim_parity_release_gate.sh — full corpus run + cross-check against G39 persistent-homology metric.

### Operator surface
- 'ft robot perf slo-status --slo ssim_parity'.
- MCP: wa://perf/renderer-slo/ssim_parity.

### Degradation behavior
- Fontconfig version skew between hosts produces near-identical-but-pixel-different glyphs (high SSIM, may fail floor): cross-check against G39 topology metric (topologically identical → accept).
- Oracle (ratatui) crashes on edge-case input: emit 'oracle-unavailable' for that input, do not silently fail.

References: README:1318, G18, G39 persistent homology, G47, G48 bitmap corpus.

Background: G18.3 is the SSIM-parity renderer oracle slice, cross-checked by topology metrics from G39.

Why this matters: image-quality parity is a conformance claim; low latency is not useful if rendered output diverges from the oracle.

Acceptance criteria: preserve the corpus SSIM test, adversarial floor audit, and e2e release gate with G39 cross-check.

Proof category: 4 (conformance) + 5 (quantitative-attestation)

Background: During the Phase 5 refinement sweep on 2026-05-12, 20 of the 35 freshly-created reality-check beads (ft-tf6g3.2, .5, .6, .7, .9, .12, .13, .14, .16, .17, .18, .19, .22, .24, .25, .26, .30, .31, .33, .34) transitioned from status:open to status:closed within 3 hours of creation. Spot-check on ft-tf6g3.22 (G37 sigstore signing): closed_at=2026-05-12T07:11:57Z, 0 comments, 0 design notes, 0 acceptance-criteria entries written. Spot-check on ft-tf6g3.12 (G27 TLA+ TX-killswitch): closed_at=2026-05-12T14:31:11Z, 0 comments.

This is the 'silent-close anti-pattern' the skill warns about ('Closing beads without verifying the fix works → Require proof before closing'). It is also explicitly the 'silent-close-detected' degradation state the epic ft-tf6g3 declares.

Why this matters: 20 beads claiming closure WITHOUT evidence-of-done means either (a) the deliverables exist somewhere and the closing agent forgot to comment, or (b) the deliverables do not exist and the bead is false-closed. Either way, the release attestation bundle (G16) cannot trust the substrate beneath it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per closed bead in the list above: verify either (i) the deliverable artifact exists on disk at the path the bead's description names, OR (ii) the bead is genuinely premature-closed and should be reopened
- Audit comment added to every closed bead recording the closure-verification outcome (artifact-present | artifact-absent | superseded-by-X)
- Reopen all closed beads with absent deliverables (br update --status open with rationale comment)
- File a follow-on doctrine bead about 'every br update --status closed MUST attach a comment naming the artifact path AND a verification command' — strengthens the discipline going forward
- Cross-link from this bead to each reopened child

This bead's existence is itself the operator surface for the silent-close issue; 'ft reality-check status' (per the epic's enrichment) surfaces it.

References: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan-2026-05-12.md, ft-tf6g3 epic 'degradation behavior' enrichment.

proof_category: process + coordination
notes:
## Round-2 enrichment (Phase 5 refinement pass 2)

### Concrete verification protocol (per silent-closed bead)
For each of the 14 children listed in the description (.2 .6 .9 .12 .13 .14 .17 .18 .19 .22 .25 .26 .31 .33), the audit runs in order:

1. **Description-anchored path check**: extract every file path referenced in the bead's --description body (paths matching docs/**, crates/**, scripts/**, tests/**). For each path: 'git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>'. If a path is named in the bead but absent from HEAD, that path is a 'phantom-deliverable'.
2. **Commit-message correlation**: 'git log --all --oneline --grep <bead-id>' — beads closed legitimately usually have at least one commit referencing the bead ID. Zero matches = strong false-close signal.
3. **Acceptance-criteria probe**: parse the bead's Acceptance Criteria bullets, for each that names a CLI command or artifact, attempt to execute the verification (e.g., 'grep -rE "trait RuntimeProof" crates/' for G44, 'ls docs/specs/<spec>.tla' for G27/G33).
4. **Comment-emit obligation**: every audit outcome is posted as a 'br comments add <bead-id>' entry recording: outcome (artifact-present / artifact-absent / superseded-by-X / requires-reopen), verification-command output excerpt, audit-actor, audit-timestamp.

### Closure protocol for THIS audit bead (G50)
This bead may close ONLY when every cross-linked bead has at least one verification comment. The closure comment on G50 lists per-bead outcome counts and the final reopen list (if any).

### Doctrine sub-bead candidate
If the audit finds ≥5 phantom-deliverables, file a follow-on P1 doctrine bead: 'br update --status closed MUST attach a comment naming the deliverable artifact path AND a verification command. The br CLI itself should enforce this (--require-closure-comment flag in br update).'

### Operator surface
- 'ft reality-check silent-close-audit' returns per-bead audit outcome JSON.
- MCP: wa://reality-check/silent-close-audit.

### Degradation behavior
- If 'git log' grep returns >50 matches for a bead-id (e.g., the bead is referenced in many commits), the correlation signal is weak — fall back to artifact-path check only.
- If the bead's description references no file paths, the audit emits state: 'no-checkable-deliverable' and the bead is reviewed manually rather than auto-flipped.

### Proof category
Substrate / governance (no taxonomy ID — this is a meta-bead enforcing the discipline of all other proof categories).

title: [doctrine] Require close comments with artifact path and verifier command

- Link the rule from docs/process/reality-check-discipline.md and the agent closeout checklist.
- Do not weaken legitimate close_reason usage; the comment requirement is an auditable evidence record, not prose ceremony.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G51] Verify-the-verifier: self-test for ft attestation verify
description:
Background: Round-2 refinement pass 2 critique. G16 ships 'ft attestation verify' as the operator-facing offline verification CLI. The release attestation bundle's whole value proposition is 'an AI agent or human can verify offline that every shipped claim is what we say it is.' But: what if the verifier itself has a bug that always returns 'pass'? A silently-broken verifier is strictly worse than no verifier — it gives false confidence.

Why this matters: This is the bootstrap problem for trust. The verifier must be testable against KNOWN tampered bundles, KNOWN missing slots, KNOWN bad signatures, KNOWN content-hash mismatches, and must produce the correct 'fail' verdict for each. A verifier that passes its own tampered-input fixtures is trustable; one that doesn't has a meta-bug that voids the whole G16 deliverable.

Acceptance criteria:
- A tests/attestation_verify_self_test/ directory containing 12 hand-crafted bundle fixtures, each with a labeled corruption:
  - tampered_perf_slot.json (perf/headline-claims slot's content-hash field mutated)
  - tampered_tui_slot.json (tui/render-parity slot mutated)
  - tampered_security_slot.json (security/redactor-coverage mutated)
  - tampered_doctrine_slot.json (doctrine/agents-md-counts mutated)
  - tampered_proofs_slot.json (proofs/runtime-proof-trait mutated)
  - missing_required_slot.json (a required slot deleted entirely)
  - extra_unknown_slot.json (an unknown slot added)
  - swapped_slot_order.json (slot ordering changed — if ordering matters)
  - signature_wrong_key.json (signed with a non-trusted key)
  - signature_tampered.json (signature bytes corrupted)
  - sigstore_expired_cert.json (Fulcio cert past not-after)
  - sigstore_wrong_identity.json (Fulcio cert from wrong CI identity)
- For each fixture, a corresponding tests/attestation_verify_self_test/expected/<fixture>.json declaring the expected verifier verdict (pass/fail) + the expected error message regex
- The self-test runner: tests/attestation_verify_self_test_runner.rs invokes 'ft attestation verify' on each fixture, asserts verdict matches expected, asserts error message matches regex
- Logging: each fixture run emits target/test-logs/attestation-verify-self-test/<fixture>/<ts>.jsonl with full stderr capture
- CI integration: the self-test runs on every commit touching the verifier OR any attestation-bundle schema; failure blocks merge
- Mutation testing: cargo-mutants on the verifier module; assert ≥90% mutation-kill rate against the 12 fixture set (each mutation should make at least one fixture flip verdict)
- A 'rotate-self-test-corpus' helper: scripts/rotate-attestation-self-test.sh that regenerates the fixtures' positive twins from the current trusted bundle, ensuring the fixtures stay aligned with schema evolution

### Test companion
The bead IS a test plan; the 12 fixtures + runner + mutation harness ARE the artifacts.

### Operator surface
- 'ft attestation verify --self-test' runs the entire fixture set and emits pass/fail counts + first-failure detail.
- 'ft doctor attestation' embeds .verifier_self_test = { last_run_ts, fixtures_total, fixtures_passing, mutation_kill_rate }.
- MCP: wa://attestation/verifier-self-test.

### Degradation behavior
- Sigstore-related fixtures cannot run in offline-only CI: emit state: 'sigstore-unavailable-skip' with per-fixture skip count; do NOT report green if sigstore fixtures were skipped.
- A new fixture-type discovered post-release (e.g., a tampering attack we hadn't enumerated): added to the corpus + the bead reopens for the duration of the harness extension.

### Proof category
4 (conformance) + 10 (cryptographic) + 2 (property/proptest via mutation testing).

Dependencies: blocks ft-tf6g3.1 (G16) — no release bundle ships without the verifier passing its self-test.

proof_category: 4 (conformance) + 10 (cryptographic) + 2 (property)

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G19] Wire 5 unproven headline claims to signed attestation slots
description:
Background: docs/perf/headline-claims.json catalogs the README's measurable claims but five specific ones still have NO link to a signed proof artifact:
1. FTS5 query <10ms (README:1309)
2. Robot Mode response <5ms (README:1310)
3. Memory per pane hot ~200 bytes/line (README:1312)
4. Memory per pane warm ~40 bytes/line at 5:1 zstd (README:1313, also G3 round-2 separate claim)
5. Bloom filter 10-100x speedup (G3 round-2 list)

ft-e87u6.7 covers cross-linking *existing* perf artifacts to README rows; it does NOT cover producing the missing artifacts for these 5 claims. That's this bead.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each of the 5 claims gets a Criterion bench file under crates/frankenterm-core/benches/headline_claims/ (one per claim)
- Each emits a docs/perf/headline-claims-evidence/<claim>.json with p50/p95/p99/p99.9, sample size, confidence interval, hardware fingerprint, source commit
- Each is wrapped in a sequential-test regression gate (G25 dependency)
- Each row in docs/perf/headline-claims.json is updated with an 'evidence' field referencing the per-claim artifact by content hash
- The bundle from G16 includes all 5 evidence files as required slots
- README perf table footnotes link to the evidence files

Hardware baseline: pinned to the GitHub Actions runner SKU documented in docs/perf/swarm-capacity-baseline.md, plus a local M-series Mac baseline. If a claim is target-class-only (e.g., 200-pane memory envelope), explicitly mark it as such with target-class predicate.

Dependencies: G23 (Lindley bounds inform the FTS5 and Robot Mode latency claims), G25 (SPRT gating), G29 (target-class predicate for memory claims).

References: README.md:1309-1313, docs/perf/headline-claims.json, docs/perf/headline-claims-audit.md, docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md G3.

proof_category: 5 (quantitative-attestation)
notes:
## Refinement enrichments (Phase 5 round 1 — RESTORED in round 6 after detecting overwrite by round-3)

### Test companion
- Unit (per claim): crates/frankenterm-core/benches/headline_claims/<claim>.rs — Criterion harness emitting docs/perf/headline-claims-evidence/<claim>.json with p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + sample size + CI + hardware fingerprint + source commit.
- Integration: tests/headline_claim_artifact_link.rs — for each of the 5 claims, assert (a) the README footnote anchor resolves to an existing evidence file, (b) the evidence file's content_hash matches the README footnote's declared hash. Emits per-claim structured trace.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_headline_claim_navigation.sh — uses a headless markdown renderer to follow the README footnote → artifact → signed bundle slot, asserts no broken links.
- Property (proptest): tests/headline_claim_evidence_schema.rs — generates random evidence rows, asserts schema-validation behavior matches expected accept/reject set.
- Logging: every claim emits its bench under target/test-logs/headline-claims/<claim>/<ts>.jsonl; the e2e script aggregates into a single summary.json per run.

### Operator surface
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .headline_claims = [...{ claim, value, slo, evidence_ref, gate_state }].
- 'ft robot perf headline-claims' (read-only).
- 'ft robot --format toon perf headline-claims'.
- MCP: wa://perf/headline-claims, wa://perf/headline-claims/<claim>.
- Per-claim README footnote: '[evidence: <hash> · methodology · last-run <ts>]' with link to signed-bundle slot.

### Degradation behavior
- Claim's evidence file missing or stale (older than configurable window, default 30 days): doctor reports state: 'evidence-stale' and the release bundle records the prior-release content hash with stale_since: <ts>. CI gate fails any release tag that ships >2 stale claims.
- Hardware mismatch (claim measured on different SKU than declared): evidence row carries hardware_drift_warning and the gate routes through SPRT regime-shift (G42) rather than failing outright.
- Per-claim regression detected by SPRT (G25): doctor reports state: 'regression-flagged' with the SPRT decision + change-point analysis from G42.

### Proof category
5 (quantitative attestation), composes with 7 (information-theoretic via SPRT G25 and conformal G26), with target-class predicate from G29 for memory-envelope claims.

## Round-3 decomposition (Phase 5 refinement pass 3)

This bead is now an UMBRELLA over 5 per-claim children:
- ft-tf6g3.4.1 (G19.1) FTS5 query <10ms
- ft-tf6g3.4.2 (G19.2) Robot Mode response <5ms
- ft-tf6g3.4.3 (G19.3) Memory per pane HOT ~200 bytes/line
- ft-tf6g3.4.4 (G19.4) Memory per pane WARM ~40 bytes/line @ 5:1 zstd
- ft-tf6g3.4.5 (G19.5) Bloom filter 10-100x speedup

Each child has its own Criterion bench file, evidence file, test companion, operator surface, degradation behavior, and proof category. The decomposition lets claims close independently and avoids bottlenecking the umbrella on the slowest sibling. The parent closes when all 5 children close.

DoD for this umbrella: all 5 children closed with verified deliverables AND the umbrella's release-bundle slot (G16) has all 5 evidence file content-hashes recorded.

## Round-6 regression note

The round-1 sections above were OVERWRITTEN in round-3 when the decomposition note was written via 'br update --notes'. Round-6 audit caught the regression. Future updates MUST concatenate, never replace.

description:
Background: Round-2 refinement pass 2 critique. Every G16-G49 bead's --notes block declares its own per-test logging path ('target/test-logs/<area>/<test>/<ts>.jsonl'). The pattern is consistent across beads in plan space, but nothing in the substrate ENFORCES the convention. Without a centralized helper, every new test author re-invents the path scheme, the JSONL row shape drifts, and the cross-bead correlation queries in G31 reality-check discipline cannot rely on a uniform format.

Why this matters: The 'great, detailed logging' requirement in the Phase 5 frozen template is only useful if the logs are queryable as a corpus, not just as one-off files. A canonical helper + format makes the logs first-class evidence the release bundle can reference.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new crate ft-test-log at crates/ft-test-log/ providing:

- A docs/testing/log-format-schema.json declaring the canonical JSONL row shape with schemars-generated schema
- A scripts/inspect-test-logs.sh CLI tool for ad-hoc queries (e.g., 'all error rows from the last sprt test run', 'all measurement rows for the lindley pipeline')

- A canonical-format validator runs in CI: any JSONL row under target/test-logs/ that fails the schema fails the test suite
- Migration: every bead's --notes-declared logging path conforms; existing tests get a 'use ft_test_log::TestLogger' import added in a follow-on sweep

### Test companion

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G53] Bundle retraction & corrigendum surface for shipped-but-wrong claims
description:
Background: Round-2 refinement pass 2 critique. G16 ships signed release attestation bundles. Beads describe how bundles get BUILT and CONSUMED. Nothing in the plan describes what happens when a bundle is *later found wrong* — e.g., a published Lindley bound is invalidated by a new heavy-tail discovery (G38), a 'redactor recall ≥99%' claim is invalidated by an adversarial corpus expansion (G24+G34), a Coq proof is invalidated by a tactic deprecation that opened an axiom (G44). A signed-but-wrong claim is worse than no claim — it actively misleads downstream verifiers who trust the signature.

Why this matters: ft is sold to AI agents as a control plane. An AI agent that locally caches an attestation bundle for offline verification must learn 'this bundle was later retracted; the slot X claim is rescinded; here's the corrigendum bundle'. Without a retraction surface, retracted bundles silently linger as authoritative.

Acceptance criteria:
- A docs/attestations/retractions/<original-bundle-hash>/<slot-name>.json shape:
  - { retracted_at, retracted_by_release, retraction_rationale, affected_slot, original_claim_value, corrected_claim_value (if known), retraction_signature }
- Every release bundle includes a 'retractions' field listing prior retractions still in effect (with a configurable forget-window after which old retractions move to docs/attestations/retractions/archive/)
- 'ft attestation verify' learns to consult retractions: if a bundle being verified is on the retraction list, verify returns 'retracted' (NOT 'pass' and NOT 'fail') with the retraction rationale + corrected-claim pointer
- Retractions are themselves signed (sigstore/cosign per G37 doctrine) so a retraction itself cannot be forged
- A scripts/retract-bundle-slot.sh helper guides a maintainer through the retraction workflow: load original bundle → identify slot → write retraction with rationale → sign → publish → ensure the next release bundle picks it up
- A maintainer doc docs/attestations/retraction-policy.md declaring: who is allowed to retract, what constitutes valid retraction rationale, how downstream consumers should propagate the retraction

### Test companion
- tests/attestation_retraction_roundtrip.rs — write a retraction, verify it loads, verify 'ft attestation verify' surfaces 'retracted' state on the affected bundle.
- tests/attestation_retraction_signature.rs — assert retraction signature roundtrip + Fulcio identity validation.
- tests/e2e/test_retraction_workflow.sh — full workflow: ship bundle, discover invalidating evidence, run retract-bundle-slot.sh, verify downstream consumer sees retraction.
- Negative: tests/attestation_unsigned_retraction.rs — assert an unsigned retraction is rejected (cannot poison the retraction stream).
- Logging via the G52 canonical convention.

### Operator surface
- 'ft attestation retract --bundle <hash> --slot <name> --rationale-file <path>' (maintainer CLI).
- 'ft attestation retractions' (read-only) lists active retractions.
- 'ft attestation verify' returns 'retracted' state with retraction details when applicable.
- 'ft doctor attestation' embeds .retractions = [recent].
- MCP: wa://attestation/retractions.

### Degradation behavior
- Retraction signed with a key that has since been rotated: verify still trusts the retraction if the rotated key was the current key at retraction time AND Rekor's transparency log confirms.
- Retraction list grows unbounded: archive policy moves retractions older than configurable window (default 5 years) to a separate signed manifest; verify still consults the archive on a cache miss.
- Two competing retractions for the same slot: latest-by-Rekor-inclusion wins; emit a 'retraction-conflict' diagnostic.

### Proof category
10 (cryptographic) + governance.

Dependencies: blocks G16 (no bundle ships without retraction-surface readiness). Cross-references G37 sigstore.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G54] Evidence-stream fixture corpus for downstream test consumers
description:
Background: Round-2 refinement pass 2 critique. G19's --notes refers to 'a recorded headline-claims-evidence/<claim>.jsonl from G19 fixtures' that G25, G26, G42, G43 consume for integration tests. G47 (.32) declares the canonical schema. But: no bead actually SHIPS the fixture corpus. Every downstream test author would otherwise generate ad-hoc fixtures, breaking cross-test consistency.

Why this matters: The 'great detailed logging' invariant from Phase 5 only pays off if downstream tests can replay against KNOWN-SHAPE evidence. Without a fixture corpus, every test invents its own data and the integration story fragments.

Acceptance criteria:
- A tests/fixtures/evidence-corpus/ directory shipped under version control, containing:
  - per-claim/<claim-id>/baseline-30d.jsonl — 30-day realistic baseline (synthesized from a published bench run + jittered)
  - per-claim/<claim-id>/regression-injected.jsonl — same baseline with a -15% step injected at a labeled timestamp (for SPRT/conformal/causal tests)
  - per-claim/<claim-id>/regime-shift.jsonl — same baseline with a distribution shift at a labeled timestamp (for G42 regime-shift tests)
  - per-claim/<claim-id>/heavy-tail.jsonl — Pareto α=1.5 arrivals for SNC tests
  - per-claim/<claim-id>/sparse.jsonl — sub-min-sample-count stream for degradation behavior tests
  - manifest.json — declares each fixture's content hash, ground-truth label, generation seed, intended test consumers
- A scripts/regenerate-evidence-corpus.sh helper that re-derives the corpus from documented seeds (so the corpus stays reproducible)
- A canonical-format check in CI: every fixture validates against the G47 schema
- A fixture-coverage matrix in docs/perf/fixture-coverage.md showing which fixture flavors exist per claim
- The 5 unproven headline claims from G19 each get their own per-claim/ tree

### Test companion
- crates/ft-perf-gate/tests/fixture_corpus_conformance.rs — assert every fixture validates against the schema and ground-truth label matches the file naming.
- tests/fixture_regeneration_determinism.rs — assert regenerate-evidence-corpus.sh produces bit-identical output across two invocations with the same seed.
- tests/e2e/test_fixture_consumed_by_downstream.sh — run SPRT against regression-injected.jsonl, assert SPRT decides 'reject' with the expected change-point timestamp.

### Operator surface

description:
## CRITICAL — INVESTIGATIVE INTEGRITY BEAD — CLOSURE PROTOCOL ENFORCED

This bead resumes the audit that ft-tf6g3.37 (G50) was filed to do. G50 was silently closed within 1 minute of creation (created 2026-05-12T18:34, closed 18:35:41 with zero comments), confirming the exact pattern G50 was investigating. The closure protocol below MUST be honored or this bead's claimed closure is itself void per the discipline G50 established.

## Background (verbatim from G50, preserved here)

During the Phase 5 refinement sweep on 2026-05-12, 14 of the 35 freshly-created reality-check epic children transitioned from status:open to status:closed within hours of creation, all with zero comments, zero design notes, zero acceptance-criteria entries. They are: ft-tf6g3.2, .6, .9, .12, .13, .14, .17, .18, .19, .22, .25, .26, .31, .33. Spot-check on ft-tf6g3.22 (G37 sigstore signing): closed_at=2026-05-12T07:11:57Z, 0 comments, 0 design notes. Spot-check on ft-tf6g3.12 (G27 TLA+ TX-killswitch): closed_at=2026-05-12T14:31:11Z, 0 comments.

This is the 'silent-close anti-pattern' the /reality-check skill explicitly warns against ('Closing beads without verifying the fix works → Require proof before closing'). Closures without rationale evidence mean the release attestation bundle (ft-tf6g3.1 G16) cannot trust any substrate beneath it.

## CLOSURE PROTOCOL (BINDING — see also G50 ft-tf6g3.37 notes for full version)

This bead MUST NOT close until the following has occurred for each of the 14 affected beads:

1. **Description-anchored path check**: 'git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>' for every artifact path the closed bead's description names. Result posted as a 'br comments add' entry on THIS bead naming the closed bead and the outcome.

2. **Commit-message correlation**: 'git log --all --oneline --grep <bead-id>' for the closed bead. Result posted similarly.

3. **Acceptance-criteria probe**: parse the bead's Acceptance Criteria, execute each verification command (grep, ls, cargo run, etc.), post results.

4. **Verdict**: for each closed bead, declare one of: artifact-present (legitimate close), artifact-absent (false-close, reopen with rationale), superseded-by-X (different bead actually delivers this), no-checkable-deliverable (description doesn't name a verifiable artifact; reviewer judgment required).

5. **Audit comment on each affected bead**: regardless of verdict, post a comment on the affected closed bead itself ('br comments add <closed-bead-id>') recording: audit-actor, audit-timestamp, verdict, verification command output excerpt.

6. **Reopen list**: at the conclusion of the audit, post a closing comment on THIS bead listing the affected-bead IDs that should be reopened. Use 'br update --status open --notes "reopened-by-G55-audit"' for each.

## ENFORCEMENT

Any agent attempting to close THIS bead without those 14×4 = 56 audit comments first SHALL leave the close-rationale comment 'audit-skipped-needs-reverification', which itself reopens the bead immediately by convention. This pattern is reinforced by:
- This bead's status:open requirement until audit comments are visible via 'br comments G55-id'
- A scripts/check-audit-readiness.sh validator that 'ft reality-check status' calls before reporting epic ft-tf6g3 as DoD
- The G16 (ft-tf6g3.1) release-bundle bead BLOCKS on this bead's status:closed (wired by this commit)

## Cross-links

This bead is the successor to ft-tf6g3.37 (G50). G50's verification protocol survives in its --notes field; consult it for the canonical procedure. G50's relate edges to the 14 affected beads should be MIRRORED here (operator action: bulk 'br dep add ft-tf6g3.<NEW> ft-tf6g3.<closed> --type related').

## Operator surface

- 'ft reality-check silent-close-audit' returns per-bead audit outcome JSON.
- 'ft reality-check silent-close-audit --readiness' returns count of pending audit comments vs. required 56.
- MCP: wa://reality-check/silent-close-audit.

## Proof category
Substrate / governance / integrity. No taxonomy ID — this is the meta-bead the entire G32 taxonomy registry rests on.

## Failure mode
If 'git log --grep <bead-id>' returns >50 matches, fall back to artifact-path check only. If no file paths in the closed bead's description, declare 'no-checkable-deliverable' and require human review.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G56] Meta-test for reality-check epic bead structural conformance
description:
Background: Round-3 critique. The reality-check epic invariant is that every child bead carries: (1) Background, (2) Why this matters, (3) Acceptance criteria, (4) References, AND in --notes: (5) Test companion, (6) Operator surface, (7) Degradation behavior, (8) Proof category. Without a meta-test, individual beads silently drift below the invariant — and 14 of the 35 children silently closed with notes_present=false confirms exactly this happened.

Why this matters: A bead invariant that no test enforces is a vibe. A bead invariant that the meta-test asserts on every commit becomes structural. Without this, future reality-check epics will recapitulate the same drift.

Acceptance criteria:
- scripts/check-reality-check-bead-structure.sh — for each bead under the active reality-check epic (parametrized by epic-id and date label), assert:
  - description contains the 4 required H2/H3 sections (Background, Why this matters, Acceptance criteria, References) — fuzzy regex match
  - notes contain the 4 required sections (Test companion, Operator surface, Degradation behavior, Proof category)
  - proof_category resolves to a known ID in docs/proof-taxonomy.json (G32 / ft-tf6g3.17)
  - if status=closed, comments contain at least one with audit-actor / artifact-path / verification-command pattern (the G55 closure protocol)
- CI lane runs the script on every commit touching .beads/issues.jsonl
- Failure mode: per-bead structural-violation report posted to docs/reality-check-bead-structure-violations.md; release gate fails any bundle while violations exist

### Test companion
- tests/reality_check_meta_structure.rs — proptest random bead JSONL rows, assert structure-validator behavior matches expected accept/reject set.
- tests/reality_check_silent_close_canary.rs — synthesize a closed bead with notes=null and 0 comments, assert validator flags it.
- tests/e2e/test_reality_check_bead_structure.sh — run the validator over the live JSONL, capture per-bead pass/fail; emit target/test-logs/reality-check-structure/<ts>/summary.json.

### Operator surface
- 'ft reality-check structure-audit' returns per-bead pass/fail JSON.
- 'ft doctor --json' .reality_check.structure_audit { total, conforming, violations }.
- MCP: wa://reality-check/structure-audit.

### Degradation behavior
- Bead description in foreign language or unusual formatting: validator emits 'parse-warning' rather than failing; reviewer judgment required.
- Validator itself buggy (high false-positive rate): canary test on known-good fixtures catches drift in the validator.

### Proof category
4 (conformance) + governance.

Dependencies: blocks G16 (no release bundle ships while structural violations exist).

proof_category: 4 (conformance) + process

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G57] Implement ft reality-check {status,next,silent-close-audit,structure-audit} CLI verbs
description:
Background: Round-3 critique. Multiple reality-check beads reference 'ft reality-check <verb>' as their operator surface (epic ft-tf6g3, G31, G50, G55, G56). The CLI subcommand tree does not yet exist. Until it does, every operator-surface section in the bead set is aspirational — they are described but cannot be invoked.

Why this matters: An operator surface is not a feature until it's wired through the CLI. Several beads consume the 'ft reality-check status' surface to report DoD readiness; without the CLI, those DoD checks are paper tigers.

Acceptance criteria:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/main.rs (or the relevant binary main.rs) gains an 'ft reality-check' subcommand tree:
  - 'ft reality-check status' — reports epic-readiness for the active reality-check epic
  - 'ft reality-check next' — returns the bv-style next-actionable child bead scoped to the epic
  - 'ft reality-check silent-close-audit [--readiness]' — invokes G55 protocol; --readiness reports audit-comment count vs. required
  - 'ft reality-check structure-audit' — invokes G56 validator
  - 'ft reality-check epic <id> [--json]' — switches scope to a specific epic
- All subcommands honor --json output mode per AGENTS.md agent-ergonomic doctrine
- All subcommands honor --format toon per the broader robot-mode TOON support
- MCP server exposes wa://reality-check/{status, next, silent-close-audit, structure-audit, epic/<id>} resources
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .reality_check.{status, latest_epic, blockers}

### Test companion
- Unit: tests/reality_check_cli.rs — invoke each subcommand with synthetic fixture .beads/, assert exit code + JSON shape.
- Integration: tests/reality_check_status_workflow.rs — full br-CLI driven workflow: create test epic with N children, drive verbs, assert each correctly reports state.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_reality_check_cli.sh — drives all 4 verbs against a synthesized epic, captures output to target/test-logs/reality-check-cli/.
- Property: random epic shapes via proptest, assert subcommand output schema validates against docs/reality-check-cli-schema.json.

### Operator surface
Self — this bead IS the operator surface implementation.

### Degradation behavior
- br CLI unavailable on the host: subcommand emits actionable install hint, exits with state: 'br-unavailable'.
- No active reality-check epic in .beads/: subcommand returns 'no-epic-active' state with the date pattern to look for.
- Cycle detected in dependency graph: subcommand reports 'cycle-detected' and links to br dep cycles.

### Proof category
4 (conformance) — operator-surface CLI contract.

Dependencies: blocks G31 (.16 reality-check discipline doc + cron — discipline depends on the CLI), G55 (audit can't run without 'ft reality-check silent-close-audit'), G56 (structure validator needs CLI invocation), epic ft-tf6g3 (epic-level DoD references the CLI).

proof_category: 4 (conformance)

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G58] Cross-family contract integration matrix (context-horizon × capture-fairness × herd-wave × blocker-radar × resource-cockpit)
description:
Background: Round-4 critique. FrankenTerm's five operator-facing contract families (introduced in the bridge-plan G16-G31 phase) each ship: a contract doc under docs/<family>-contract.md, a child bead family (ft-r920m for context-horizon; ft-n447z for capture-fairness; ft-5bwjf for herd-wave; ft-9ntud for blocker-radar; ft-rz0eb for resource-cockpit), an operator-surface ('ft robot <family>'), a JSON-shape schema, and an evidence-state vocabulary (measured/inferred/simulated/stale/unavailable/mixed). G34 adversarial-fuzz was the only bead testing the 5 families AS A SET and it was silently closed without verified deliverables.

This bead resurrects the cross-family integration story at a stricter granularity: a CONFORMANCE MATRIX asserting that every (family, evidence-state, operator-surface, schema) combination produces correct output AND that cross-family invariants hold (e.g., when resource-cockpit reports 'pressure: red' AND capture-fairness reports 'starvation-risk: yes', herd-wave's stagger-planner must produce a stagger-class downgrade).

Why this matters: The 5 contract families don't live in isolation; they're consumed together by the same operator (an AI agent reading 'ft doctor --json' or browsing MCP resources). A bug where context-horizon says 'budget green' but resource-cockpit says 'pressure red' is a contract violation the per-family tests cannot catch. Without a cross-family matrix, the operator surface is internally inconsistent.

## Acceptance criteria

1. crates/frankenterm-core/tests/contract_families_integration_matrix.rs — a single test file that:
   - Generates a NxNxNxNxN matrix of (context-horizon evidence-state, capture-fairness state, herd-wave state, blocker-radar state, resource-cockpit state) tuples; N=6 per the canonical evidence-state vocabulary
   - For each tuple, synthesizes a deterministic system snapshot (fixture-based, not random — to make failures reproducible)
   - Drives each family's read-only DTO through its synthesizer
   - Asserts: (a) each family produces a valid JSON conforming to its contract schema, (b) cross-family invariants hold (declared in docs/contract-families-cross-invariants.md)
   - Total matrix size after symmetry pruning: ~7,000 tuples; runtime budget ≤5 min on CI

2. docs/contract-families-cross-invariants.md — declared cross-family invariants in TLA+-style notation, e.g.:
   - 'resource-pressure=red ⇒ capture-fairness.starvation-risk MUST flag at least one pane within 60s'
   - 'context-horizon.budget=black ⇒ herd-wave.dry-run-stagger-class=conservative'
   - 'blocker-radar.lane=blocked ⇒ herd-wave.fleet-burst=suppressed'
   - 5-8 invariants total covering the realistic interaction surface
   - Each invariant has a 1-line rationale + the family-bead IDs it cross-references

3. CI integration: the matrix test runs on every commit touching crates/frankenterm-core/src/{context_horizon,capture_fairness*,herd_wave*,blocker_radar*,resource_*}.rs

4. Differential testing: for each tuple, the matrix also captures the 'ft robot --format toon <family>' output and asserts TOON-rendered shape parity with the JSON output. Catches the class of bugs where the TOON renderer accidentally drops or reformats a field.

5. Release-bundle slot: docs/attestations/contracts/cross-family-matrix.json carries the matrix pass-rate (target: 100%), per-invariant pass count, sample workload class identifier, content hash of the invariant doc.

## Test companion

- Unit: tests/contract_families_invariant_parser.rs — parse docs/contract-families-cross-invariants.md, assert every declared invariant has a valid TLA+-style predicate + cross-references valid family-bead IDs.
- Integration: tests/contract_families_integration_matrix.rs (above).
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_cross_family_integration.sh — drive 'ft doctor --json' on a synthesized fixture system snapshot, assert every family's surface co-renders correctly + invariants hold.
- Property: proptest random tuples beyond the fixture set, assert invariants hold under arbitrary states.
- Negative: tests/contract_families_invariant_violations.rs — deliberately synthesize a violation (e.g., resource-pressure=red + capture-fairness=ok), assert the matrix correctly flags the violation rather than masking it.
- Logging via G52 canonical convention to target/test-logs/cross-family/<ts>/.

## Operator surface

- 'ft robot contract-families' returns per-family surface + cross-invariant status.
- 'ft robot --format toon contract-families'.
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .contract_families = { per_family_states, cross_invariant_status, last_matrix_run_ts }.
- MCP: wa://contract-families/matrix, wa://contract-families/invariants.

## Degradation behavior

- One family's synthesizer is unavailable (compile-time feature-gated off): matrix emits state: 'family-unavailable' per affected tuple; cross-invariants involving that family are skipped with explicit list.
- Matrix runtime budget exceeded: emit 'matrix-incomplete' with completed-tuple count + skipped-list; release gate accepts partial coverage only if ≥90% tuples exercised.
- A declared cross-invariant becomes systematically violated by a recent change: emit a 'persistent-invariant-violation' state; the bead reopens for invariant-vs-code-reconciliation.

## Proof category

4 (conformance) + 9 (differential, via JSON-vs-TOON parity check). Composes 5-family substrate.

## Dependencies

Blocks ft-tf6g3.1 (G16 release bundle — no bundle ships without the cross-family matrix passing). Cross-references the family-parent beads ft-r920m, ft-n447z, ft-5bwjf, ft-9ntud, ft-rz0eb (related dep edges to each).

proof_category: 4 (conformance) + 9 (differential)

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G59] G56 structural-validator canary: fixture-based correctness gate
description:
Background: Round-4 critique. G56 (ft-tf6g3.44) declares a meta-validator: 'for each bead under the active reality-check epic, assert it carries Background / Why this matters / Acceptance criteria / References sections plus the 4 --notes sections plus a proof_category resolving to G32 taxonomy'. The validator-script implementation will be a shell/Rust binary parsing JSONL. If the validator is buggy in the always-pass direction, every closed bead passes and we have FALSE confidence in the substrate. This is the same bootstrap-of-trust problem G51 (verify-the-verifier for ft attestation verify) solved.

Why this matters: G56 is supposed to catch silent-close-without-structure cases (which is exactly what 14 of my round-1 beads exhibited). If G56's validator can be tricked or has a regex hole, the integrity guarantee evaporates silently. The validator-canary is what makes G56's invariant trustworthy.

## Acceptance criteria

1. tests/fixtures/bead-validator-canary/ directory containing ~15 hand-crafted bead JSONL fixtures, each with a labeled defect:
   - missing_background.jsonl (description has no Background section)
   - missing_acceptance.jsonl (description has no Acceptance criteria section)
   - missing_test_companion.jsonl (notes has no Test companion section)
   - missing_operator_surface.jsonl (notes has no Operator surface section)
   - missing_degradation.jsonl (notes has no Degradation behavior section)
   - missing_proof_category.jsonl (notes has no proof_category)
   - invalid_proof_category.jsonl (proof_category resolves to non-existent ID 99)
   - closed_without_audit_comment.jsonl (status=closed, comments=[], no audit-actor / verification-command marker)
   - foreign_language_description.jsonl (description in French — should emit parse-warning, not fail)
   - degenerate_short_description.jsonl (description is 5 words — should fail)
   - description_with_unicode_zero_width.jsonl (Unicode tricks to defeat regex — should still pass the validator)
   - duplicate_section_headers.jsonl (two 'Acceptance criteria' headers — should warn)
   - notes_null.jsonl (notes field literally null — should fail)
   - notes_empty_string.jsonl (notes field is empty string — should fail)
   - all_sections_present_valid.jsonl (the positive control — should pass)

2. tests/bead_validator_canary.rs runs the validator against each fixture, asserts verdict matches the labeled expected outcome. Failure to detect any of the 14 negative cases = G56 validator bug.

3. Mutation testing target: cargo-mutants on G56's validator module; assert ≥90% mutation-kill rate against the canary fixture set.

4. The canary is itself a release-bundle slot: docs/attestations/governance/validator-canary.json with pass-count and run-timestamp.

## Test companion
