title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G60] Re-file proof-artifact taxonomy registry (G32 silently closed without docs/proof-taxonomy.json shipping)
description:
## CRITICAL SUBSTRATE — G32 (ft-tf6g3.17) was silently closed at 2026-05-12T08:07:34Z without docs/proof-taxonomy.json shipping. Every reality-check bead's proof_category tag therefore resolves to a registry that does not exist. Re-file at P1.

## Background

The 2026-04-30 bridge plan introduced a 10-category proof-artifact taxonomy (type-level / property / loom / conformance / quantitative-attestation / formal-method / information-theoretic / network-calculus / differential / cryptographic). Round-3 of this round added 2 categories (11 topological, 12 mechanized). Every reality-check bead carries a 'proof_category: N' line referencing this taxonomy.

G32 (ft-tf6g3.17) was filed in round 1 ('Proof-artifact taxonomy registry'). It was silently closed within 3 hours of creation with 0 comments and 0 notes. The intended deliverable — docs/proof-taxonomy.json declaring all 12 categories with example artifact paths — does not exist at HEAD. This bead resumes that delivery.

## Why this matters

A 'proof_category: 7' tag on a bead is meaningful only if there is a canonical registry to look it up in. Without the registry:
- Reviewers cannot tell whether a tag is valid
- The release attestation bundle (G16) cannot compute taxonomy_coverage
- Future reality-check rounds inherit a broken substrate
- G56 (meta-validator) cannot validate proof_category resolution
- G58 (cross-family contract integration) cannot map per-family proof artifacts to categories

## Acceptance criteria

1. docs/proof-taxonomy.json declares the canonical schema:
   { 'taxonomy_version': '1.0.0', 'categories': [{ 'id': 1, 'name': 'type-level', 'description': '...', 'example_artifact_path': '...', 'accepted_file_shapes': ['rust', 'sealed-trait-module'], 'introduced_in': 'bridge-plan-2026-04-30' }, ...] } with all 12 categories enumerated:
   - 1 type-level (sealed traits, phantom types, lifetime state machines)
   - 2 property/proptest (randomized verification + shrinking)
   - 3 loom (bounded model-checking of concurrency primitives)
   - 4 conformance-harness (golden artifacts + differential against reference oracles)
   - 5 quantitative-attestation (signed perf bundles + statistical-rigor reports)
   - 6 formal-method (TLA+ / Stateright / Kani / Creusot)
   - 7 information-theoretic (PAC-Bayes, Fano, KL-divergence, mutual information)
   - 8 network-calculus (min-plus deterministic + stochastic-MGF)
   - 9 differential (same-input → two-implementations → identical observable)
   - 10 cryptographic (sigstore / cosign / ed25519 / Rekor)
   - 11 topological (persistence diagrams, bottleneck distance — NEW round 3)
   - 12 mechanized (Coq / Lean / F* checked proofs — NEW round 3)

2. scripts/validate-proof-taxonomy.sh — script that:
   - Reads docs/proof-taxonomy.json, asserts schema validity
   - For each reality-check bead under the active epic, parses --description and --notes for proof_category: N, asserts N resolves to a known category ID
   - Emits a coverage report: per-category bead-count + per-category artifact-path-resolves-on-disk count

3. CI gate: scripts/validate-proof-taxonomy.sh runs on every commit touching .beads/issues.jsonl or docs/proof-taxonomy.json. Failure blocks merge.

4. Bundle slot: docs/attestations/doctrine/proof-taxonomy.json (signed) embeds the registry content-hash so the release bundle records which version of the taxonomy applies.

5. G56 (meta-validator) is extended to use this registry for proof_category resolution (cross-link).

## Test companion

- Unit: tests/proof_taxonomy_registry_load.rs — load docs/proof-taxonomy.json, assert schema validates and all 12 categories present with non-empty fields.
- Integration: tests/proof_taxonomy_bead_coverage.rs — walk .beads/issues.jsonl filtering to reality-check epic, for each bead parse proof_category and assert resolves.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_taxonomy_validate.sh — run validate-proof-taxonomy.sh against the live JSONL, assert exit 0 + a coverage report file is emitted.
- Property: proptest random N values, assert resolver behavior matches expected accept/reject for the 12 categories + sentinel-error for invalid.
- Negative: tests/proof_taxonomy_missing_registry.rs — delete the registry file, assert script fails with explicit 'registry-missing' error rather than silently passing.

## Operator surface

- 'ft reality-check taxonomy list' returns the 12 categories.
- 'ft reality-check taxonomy validate' runs the script.
- 'ft doctor --json' .reality_check.taxonomy { version, category_count, beads_per_category }.
- MCP: wa://reality-check/taxonomy.

## Degradation behavior

- Registry file present but schema-invalid: CI fails with the specific schema violation; do not silently pass.
- A bead carries a proof_category not in the registry: the meta-validator (G56) flags it; release bundle records the orphan tag count under 'governance/taxonomy-orphans'.
- A category is declared in the registry but no bead uses it: emit 'unused-category' warning (informational); could indicate a missing bead opportunity.

## Proof category

Substrate + 4 (conformance). This is the meta-meta-substrate every other category rests on.

## Dependencies

Blocks G16 (ft-tf6g3.1) — release bundle's taxonomy_coverage field cannot populate without this registry. Blocks G56 (ft-tf6g3.44) — meta-validator cannot resolve proof_category tags without this. Related to G32 (ft-tf6g3.17, the silently-closed predecessor).

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G61] Trigger-validation tests for G31 reality-check discipline cron
description:
Background: G31 (ft-tf6g3.16) declares 5 trigger conditions for re-running the reality-check skill: (a) quarterly calendar minimum, (b) per-minor-version milestone, (c) bv shows ≥50 open beads, (d) a contract doc changes ≥50 lines, (e) README headline-claim count grows by ≥3. The scripts/check-reality-check-due.sh helper was declared but no test covers whether the trigger logic correctly fires.

## Why this matters

A discipline cron that silently fails to fire is worse than no cron — it provides false confidence that the system is being audited regularly.

## Acceptance criteria

1. tests/reality_check_trigger_calendar.rs — synthesize last-run-date 95 days ago, assert (a) trigger fires for 'quarterly-minimum-exceeded' state, (b) 90 days ago does NOT fire, (c) 91 days fires at quarter-day-1.
2. tests/reality_check_trigger_milestone.rs — synthesize a git tag matching v0.X.0 (minor bump), assert trigger fires; v0.X.Y (patch bump) does not fire.
3. tests/reality_check_trigger_open_beads.rs — synthesize a .beads/ with 50 open beads, assert trigger fires; 49 does not fire (off-by-one edge).
4. tests/reality_check_trigger_contract_change.rs — synthesize a git diff in docs/<family>-contract.md with 50 lines changed, assert trigger fires; 49 does not.
5. tests/reality_check_trigger_headline_growth.rs — synthesize 3-line README growth in headline-claims, assert trigger fires; 2-line does not.
6. tests/reality_check_trigger_composite.rs — multiple triggers active simultaneously, assert all reported (operator should see all reasons, not just the first).
7. tests/e2e/test_reality_check_due_cron.sh — drives scripts/check-reality-check-due.sh against a synthesized fixture repo, asserts each trigger fires with the right rationale.

Each test emits target/test-logs/reality-check-trigger/<test>/<ts>.jsonl per G52 convention.

## Test companion

This bead IS a test plan. The 7 trigger tests + the e2e script ARE the artifacts.

## Operator surface

- 'ft reality-check is-due [--json]' returns { is_due: bool, active_triggers: [...], next_calendar_check_ts, days_since_last_run }.
- MCP: wa://reality-check/is-due.

## Degradation behavior

- git tags unavailable (running outside a git checkout): milestone-trigger emits 'milestone-check-unavailable' state but doesn't fail other triggers.
- Trigger thresholds need tuning over time: the threshold values live in docs/process/reality-check-discipline.md as parameters; trigger tests parse them from the doc (test catches drift between doc and code).
- A trigger fires but the operator doesn't act: G31 declares the consequence (next-due check defers to the next quarter-mark). This bead's tests don't enforce that — that's an operational discipline concern.

## Proof category

4 (conformance) + governance.

## Dependencies

Blocks G31 (ft-tf6g3.16 — discipline doc) and G57 (ft-tf6g3.45 — 'ft reality-check is-due' is an operator-surface verb). Cross-references the bridge-plan G31 definition.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G62] br update --notes is REPLACE-not-APPEND — doctrine bead to prevent recurrence
description:
Background: Round-6 of the Phase 5 refinement pass on 2026-05-12 discovered that 'br update <bead> --notes <text>' REPLACES the existing --notes field, not APPENDS to it. During round 3, the umbrella beads G18 (ft-tf6g3.3) and G19 (ft-tf6g3.4) received a decomposition note via 'br update --notes', which OVERWROTE the round-1 enrichments (test companion / operator surface / degradation / proof category) installed in round 1.

Round 6 detected the regression by reading each bead's notes-field excerpt and noticing only the round-3 content was present. Both beads were restored by concatenating round-1 + round-3 content in a single round-6 'br update --notes' invocation.

## Why this matters

A reality-check refinement methodology that silently destroys prior-round enrichments is structurally broken. Future rounds will recapitulate the same loss unless the workflow is updated.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Add a section to docs/process/reality-check-discipline.md (cross-link to G31): 'Updates to a bead --notes field MUST first read the existing content (br show <bead> --json | jq .notes), concatenate the new section under a dated H2 header, and write back via br update --notes. Never use --notes with the new content alone.'

2. A scripts/safe-br-update-notes.sh helper that performs the read-concat-write pattern atomically.

3. Audit existing reality-check beads in this epic for similar regressions:
   - Inspect every bead with multi-round --notes activity
   - Compare against the bridge-plan-2026-05-12.md document (which has the canonical round-1 content)
   - Restore any other found regressions

4. Update the G31 (ft-tf6g3.16) discipline doc with the lesson.

5. Optional follow-on: investigate whether the br CLI itself should grow a --append-notes flag. File as a related bead if desired.

## Test companion

- Unit: tests/safe_br_update_notes.rs — invoke safe-br-update-notes.sh against a fixture bead with existing notes, assert the result contains both prior and new content.
- Integration: tests/notes_concat_idempotent.rs — invoking safe-br-update-notes.sh twice with the same new section produces a single instance, not two.
- Negative: tests/raw_br_update_notes_warns.rs — deliberately call 'br update --notes' raw, assert the safe wrapper emits a warning if it would have caused a regression (i.e., the prior notes had >1 H2 section).

## Operator surface

- 'safe-br-update-notes <bead> <new-section-h2-header> <new-section-body>' — CLI wrapper.
- 'ft reality-check audit-notes-regressions [--json]' — surface any beads whose notes lack expected sections.

## Degradation behavior

- A bead's notes field exceeds the JSONL row-size limit after concatenation: emit 'notes-overflow' state and offer a split-into-comments alternative.
- Two rounds attempt to write the same section header concurrently: the second invocation detects the duplicate and appends a disambiguation suffix.

## Proof category

Substrate / governance — meta-doctrine about how to operate the tracker safely.

## References

- G31 (ft-tf6g3.16) discipline doc.
- Bridge-plan reality-check process notes from 2026-05-12.

## Dependencies

Related to G31 (ft-tf6g3.16 discipline doc). No blocking deps — this is a process improvement, not a release gate.

title: [reality-check][latency] Complete Lindley coverage for capture tail, Robot, FTS5, and renderer SLO paths
description:
Background:
While working G23 (ft-tf6g3.8), the live derivation/artifact audit found that docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json covers only the three published 4KB overlap benchmark stages: PtyCapture, DeltaExtraction, StorageWrite. The broader LatencyStage::CAPTURE_PATH also contains PatternDetection and EventEmission, and the README SLO table names Robot Mode <5ms, FTS5 <10ms, and renderer input-to-photon surfaces. Those surfaces do not yet have complete Lindley telemetry rows, service curves, or empirical-vs-bound comparisons.

Why this matters:
Closing G23 as if every latency claim is covered would be a false proof. The current artifact is valid for the 4KB overlap benchmark slice, but it must not be cited for end-to-end capture, Robot Mode, FTS5 query, or renderer SLOs until those paths have their own stage telemetry and evidence-stream linkage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Extend the Lindley telemetry model or add adjacent bounded-latency artifacts for PatternDetection and EventEmission so EndToEndCapture has a complete modeled stage chain.
- Add a Robot Mode response bound that consumes the G54 robot.p95 evidence stream and the relevant ApiResponse/handler service curve.
- Add an FTS5 query bound that consumes the G54 fts5.query_p99 evidence stream and an explicit read-path/query service curve; do not reuse StorageWrite as a query-stage proxy.
- Add renderer input-to-photon coverage only after G18 publishes renderer stage telemetry; until then the artifact must say pending rather than proven.
- Update docs/perf/latency-derivation.md and docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json (or successor artifacts) with per-stage hashes and empirical agreement checks.

References:
ft-tf6g3.8, ft-tf6g3.4.2, ft-tf6g3.4.1, ft-tf6g3.3.2, docs/perf/latency-derivation.md, docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json, crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages/stage.rs, tests/fixtures/evidence-corpus/per-claim/{robot.p95,fts5.query_p99}.

Test companion:
- Unit: Lindley model tests must assert that the full PTY-to-event capture chain includes PtyCapture, DeltaExtraction, StorageWrite, PatternDetection, and EventEmission.
- Integration: the attestation renderer test must assert stage_content_hashes and coverage_status rows for covered, modeled-pending, and pending-service-curve claim surfaces.
- E2E/future: when G19/G18 bench artifacts land, consume their real evidence rows in Robot, FTS5, and renderer bound tests before flipping pending statuses to covered.

Operator surface:
- docs/perf/latency-derivation.md states which claim surfaces are covered, modeled-pending, or pending.
- docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json carries stage hashes and coverage_status so release readers do not infer proof for uncovered SLO surfaces.
- ft-tf6g3.51 depends on the Robot, FTS5, and renderer evidence producer beads until those empirical streams exist.

Degradation behavior:
- Missing empirical rows leave the affected surface in modeled_pending_empirical, pending_service_curve, or pending_stage_telemetry.
- The release artifact must fail closed for proof claims: pending surfaces may be documented as gaps, but must not be advertised as proven.
- Renderer input-to-photon remains pending until G18 publishes real renderer telemetry.

Proof category:

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G21] Mazurkiewicz cancel-trace equivalence classes for runtime_async primitives
description:
Background: The 2026-04-30 bridge plan G1 round-3 elevation called for: 'For every primitive in runtime_async, prove via Loom (see G8) that the cancel semantics are independent of tokio-shaped assumptions. Document the trace equivalence classes — this is what Cx-first actually means.' 8 loom tests exist in tests/ (loom_oneshot.rs, loom_watch.rs, loom_lockfree.rs, loom_spsc_ring_buffer.rs, loom_sync.rs, loom_mpsc.rs, loom_broadcast.rs, loom_triple_buffer.rs) but no document classifies the cancel-correctness traces into Mazurkiewicz equivalence classes (commuting independent events vs. order-sensitive events).

Why this matters: 'cancel-correct' is a tagline. Mazurkiewicz traces formalize it: two cancel orderings are equivalent iff they differ only on independent operations. Documenting the equivalence classes turns the tagline into a falsifiable claim per primitive.

Acceptance criteria:
- docs/proofs/runtime-async-cancel-traces.md documenting per-primitive: (a) the set of observable events, (b) the dependence relation D ⊂ E × E, (c) the equivalence classes induced by D, (d) which class the primitive belongs to under cancel (e.g., 'cancel commutes with all sender-side operations' vs. 'cancel sequences before all receiver-side operations')
- One section per primitive: oneshot, watch, mpsc, broadcast, spsc_ring_buffer, lockfree, triple_buffer, sync (and others if present)
- The loom test for each primitive is extended to enumerate the equivalence-class traces and assert the primitive observes the declared invariant on every trace
- A docs/attestations/proofs/runtime-async-cancel-traces.json slot in the release bundle (content hash of the markdown + supporting test binaries)

References: docs/reality-check-bridge-plan.md G1 round-3, tests/loom_*.rs, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trace_theory (Mazurkiewicz traces background).

title: [attestation][runtime-async] Mark cancel-trace binary hashes as transient provenance
description:
## Finding

`docs/attestations/proofs/runtime-async-cancel-traces.json` has `status: pass` and valid remote RCH evidence for the declaration tests, but its `supporting_test_binaries` entries point at `/tmp/ft-tf6g3-6-attest-20260512T090000Z/...` binaries that are not retained in git or the release bundle. The same artifact records the hash-capture run as `status: pass` even though the execution mode says it was a local hash capture through a non-compilation `rch` wrapper with no RCH remote footer.

This can make the release artifact look as if transient local binaries are retained proof inputs. The real remote proof should remain intact; the binary hash capture should be labeled as transient provenance, not release proof.

## Scope

- Update only the cancel-trace attestation artifact/documentation needed to distinguish retained source artifacts and remote proof from transient local binary provenance.
- Do not rerun Cargo locally.
- Keep the existing remote RCH declaration-test and clippy proof records unchanged except for clarifying the local hash-capture status.

## Acceptance

- `supporting_test_binaries` clearly states the binaries are transient/not retained and not bundle-verifiable artifacts.
- The local hash-capture proof run no longer has a plain `pass` status that can be mistaken for RCH proof.
- `jq empty` and focused `jq -e` truth checks pass for the artifact.
- `br dep cycles --json` remains empty.
close_reason:
Fixed the cancel-trace attestation truthfulness gap. `docs/attestations/proofs/runtime-async-cancel-traces.json` now declares `supporting_test_binaries_retention.status=transient_not_retained`, `bundle_verifiable=false`, and states that the `/tmp/ft-tf6g3-6-attest-*` binary hashes are local provenance only, not release proof inputs. The binary_hash_capture record now uses `status=local_provenance_not_release_proof`; the existing remote_filtered_loom_proof and remote_targeted_clippy pass records remain intact as the actual RCH proof evidence.

Validation passed: `jq empty docs/attestations/proofs/runtime-async-cancel-traces.json`; focused `jq -e` truth check for transient binary retention + remote proof records; `git diff --check -- docs/attestations/proofs/runtime-async-cancel-traces.json`; `br dep cycles --json` => count 0; `bash scripts/attestation-build.sh --version 0.0.0-dev --channel dev --sign unsigned`; `bash scripts/attestation-verify.sh docs/attestations/0.0.0-dev.json --json --strict-required --strict-deferred | jq -e '.ok == true and (.errors | length) == 0'`. No local Cargo or material RCH proof was run because this was a JSON truthfulness-only patch.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G23] Lindley-equation latency derivation finalize + per-release publish
description:
Background: latency_stages.rs is a ~29,300 LOC machinery of network-calculus / min-plus algebra. The bridge plan G3 round-2 called for: 'tie to existing min-plus algebra: for the <50ms latency claim, derive a Lindley-equation bound from the network-calculus stage model and publish the bound alongside the empirical distribution. If they disagree, that is a bug worth finding.' docs/perf/latency-derivation.md exists. Lindley-bounds attestation slot exists at docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json. Question: is the derivation actually finished for every stage that contributes to the <50ms capture latency claim and the new renderer SLOs (G18)?

Why this matters: Lindley's equation gives a WORST-CASE waiting time bound from arrival/service-time distributions. Empirical p99 catches what *happens*; Lindley bounds catch what *can* happen. A Lindley bound that disagrees with empirical p99 reveals a service-time tail the empirical data hasn't sampled yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- docs/perf/latency-derivation.md has a derivation section for every stage in latency_stages.rs that contributes to: (a) <50ms capture latency, (b) input-to-photon (G18), (c) Robot Mode <5ms (G19), (d) FTS5 <10ms (G19)
- Each section publishes: stage name, arrival-rate distribution, service-time distribution, Lindley-bound derivation, empirical p99 from headline-claims-evidence (G19 dependency), agreement check (within 20%)
- Disagreements (empirical p99 outside Lindley bound) filed as new bugs (sub-beads) before this bead can close
- docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json updated with content hashes per stage
- This bead feeds the perf/lindley-bounds.json slot of the release bundle (G16)

References: docs/perf/latency-derivation.md, crates/frankenterm-core/src/latency_stages.rs, docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindley_equation.

proof_category: 8 (network-calculus)
notes:
## Refinement enrichments (Phase 5)

### Test companion
- Unit: tests/lindley_bound_derivation.rs — per-stage Lindley computation with synthetic arrival/service distributions (light-tail Poisson/exponential). Asserts the closed-form derivation matches simulation for the light-tail case. Logs each stage's MGF computation to target/test-logs/lindley/<stage>/<ts>.jsonl.
- Integration: tests/latency_pipeline_lindley_check.rs — feeds the production latency_stages.rs through the Lindley deriver, compares against the empirical p99.99 from G19 evidence files. Asserts |bound - empirical| < 20% threshold; logs each disagreement as a sub-bead candidate.
- E2E: tests/e2e/test_lindley_bundle_slot.sh — drives the full flow: scripts/derive-lindley-bounds.sh → docs/attestations/perf/lindley-bounds.json → 'ft attestation verify' confirms the slot. Per-stage logs preserved.
- Property: each stage's Lindley computation is exercised under a range of arrival rates with proptest, assert monotonicity (higher arrival rate → larger bound).
- Negative: tests/lindley_disagreement.rs — deliberately inject a heavy-tail arrival (Pareto α<2), assert the light-tail Lindley deriver flags the input as out-of-domain rather than returning a vacuous bound. Punts to G38 SNC path.

### Operator surface
- 'ft robot perf latency-bounds' (read-only).
- 'ft robot perf latency-bounds --stage <name>' — single-stage detail.
- 'ft doctor --json' embeds .latency_bounds = [...] with per-stage bound + empirical + disagreement flag.
- MCP: wa://perf/latency-bounds, wa://perf/latency-bounds/<stage>.

### Degradation behavior
- Heavy-tail arrival detected (Hill estimator α<2 with confidence per G42's regime-shift detector): Lindley deriver returns Err('heavy-tail-out-of-domain'); operator surface reports state: 'snc-required' and links to G38's stochastic-bound artifact (if available) or the bead.
- Stage's service-time distribution unmeasured for >30 days: bound emitted as { state: 'evidence-stale', last_bound: <prior>, last_update: <ts> }.
- Empirical-vs-bound disagreement >20%: bound emitted with disagreement_warning flag; the bundle accepts the slot but the release gate fails until investigated.

### Proof category
8 (network-calculus). Composes with category 2 (property/proptest) for the empirical consistency check and category 7 (info-theoretic) for the Hill-estimator heavy-tail check that punts to G38.

title: [reality-check-2026-05-12 G24] Fano-inequality redaction recall lower bound + per-release publish
description:
Background: G10 round-3 elevation from the 2026-04-30 bridge plan: 'Information-theoretic lower bound for redaction recall: use Fano inequality to publish the minimum sample size needed to claim a recall floor with confidence ≥99%.' redactor.rs has 50+ patterns. docs/security/redactor-coverage.json and redactor-coverage-methodology.md ship today. But the methodology lacks the Fano-grade sample-size derivation.

Why this matters: Claiming '≥99% recall' on a finite test corpus tells you nothing about the *next* secret pattern you haven't seen. Fano's inequality bounds the minimum mutual information needed to distinguish hypotheses; applied to redactor classification, it gives a sample-size lower bound for any honest 99% recall claim. Without it, the recall number is a measurement of the test corpus, not a measurement of the redactor.

Acceptance criteria:
- docs/security/redactor-recall-derivation.md derives, from first principles: (a) the redactor's prediction classes (n_classes), (b) the equivocation tolerance allowed at 99% confidence, (c) the Fano-implied minimum sample size N* per class
- The redactor test corpus is audited against N*; if any class is under-sampled, add real examples or file a bead for corpus expansion (sub-bead)
- docs/security/redactor-coverage.json updated with a sample_size_floor field per pattern class
- A 'gitleaks vendored corpus' or 'trufflehog vendored corpus' is fetched and treated as differential ground truth (cross-classifier)
- The bundle slot security/redactor-coverage.json from G16 lists the Fano-bound-derived floor

References: docs/security/redactor-coverage.json, docs/security/redactor-coverage-methodology.md, crates/frankenterm-core/src/redactor.rs, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fano%27s_inequality.

title: ft-2okh0.13.cont: cold-tier integration (zstd + async I/O + redactor + metadata index)
description:
Continuation of ft-2okh0.13 (substrate shipped at b3e8a6845).

Substrate at crates/frankenterm-core/src/scrollback_cold_tier.rs covers the policy decisions (4-tier cascade, eviction gate, retention purge, LRU select, dedup). Integration work to wire into the running scrollback subsystem:

1. zstd compression: compress chunks at write time. Cross-link compression_dictionary.rs (dict-based zstd ratios).
2. Async I/O via the asupersync runtime (AGENTS.md: no raw tokio). Read path returns Future<Result<Vec<u8>, ColdTierError>>.
3. Redactor pre-write call: cross-link redactor.rs::redact_text. Flip ChunkMetadata.redaction Required→Applied before should_evict_to_disk approves.
4. AES-256-GCM encryption-at-rest (operator opt-in, shared key with ft-2okh0.5 mmap-backed scrollback).
5. Disk file layout: ~/.cache/ft/scrollback/<pane_id>/<chunk_id>.zst[.enc] mode 0600.
6. Metadata index: SQLite alongside chunks (or in-memory + journaled). Per-chunk id, byte_range, line_range, content_hash, written_ts, last_access_ts, tier, redaction, encryption.
7. Cleanup task: weekly cron-style scan calling should_purge_by_retention.
8. Search integration: when search_bridge needs to hit cold tier, async fetch + decompress + populate ColdRam cache.
9. Structured JSON-line logging per the bead's 'Structured logging' section.

DO NOT BREAK (from the bead):
- Privacy: redactor MUST apply before disk write — substrate enforces by type, integration must call redactor.

title: Web delta SSE can strand backlog after finite catch-up scan
description:
Subsystem: web SSE delta stream

Evidence:
- `handle_stream_deltas` starts a delta subscriber and only calls `emit_new_segment_frames` when it receives a `SegmentCaptured` event or a lag notification (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:554-733`).
- `emit_new_segment_frames` scans at most `STREAM_SCAN_MAX_PAGES` pages of `STREAM_SCAN_LIMIT` segments per trigger (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:321-340`), advances `after_id` as it emits (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:375-404`), then returns `true` after the finite window.
- The underlying storage query orders by `id ASC` and applies the limit (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:6998-7008`, `crates/frankenterm-core/src/storage.rs:15417-15429`), so any backlog beyond `STREAM_SCAN_LIMIT * STREAM_SCAN_MAX_PAGES` remains queryable but unsent after one catch-up pass.
- After that finite pass, the stream loop waits for another EventBus delivery (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:609-617`). If the backlog was created before/during a lag window and no new event arrives, the remaining stored segments are stranded indefinitely for that SSE client.
- Existing web SSE tests cover one emitted delta and a lag notification (`crates/frankenterm-core/tests/web.rs:573-630`, `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/web.rs:633-696`), but no test creates a backlog larger than the scan window and asserts the stream drains it or emits an explicit truncation/resync marker.

Why it matters:
The delta SSE endpoint is supposed to be the live redacted output stream. Under bursty output or EventBus lag, clients can receive a partial prefix and then stall with no indication that more stored deltas exist. This is a backpressure recovery fail-open: the system silently drops continuity instead of draining, resyncing, or surfacing truncation.

Proposed remediation:
After a full `STREAM_SCAN_MAX_PAGES` catch-up window, either continue scheduling catch-up work until a short page is seen, emit an explicit `truncated/resync_required` frame, or force clients to reconnect from a returned cursor. Add a bounded test with more than `STREAM_SCAN_LIMIT * STREAM_SCAN_MAX_PAGES` stored segments and no further EventBus events, asserting no silent strand.
close_reason: Fixed in 182647892: /stream/deltas now distinguishes complete catch-up from full scan windows, drains stored backlog until a short page is reached, and opportunistically catches missed backlog on keepalive ticks without breaking full-channel keepalive semantics. Added real SQLite/EventBus/SSE regression covering five stored deltas with scan_limit=2/max_pages=1 and condition-based SSE frame reads. Verified: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs crates/frankenterm-core/tests/web.rs; git diff --check -- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs crates/frankenterm-core/tests/web.rs; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-sse cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test web --features web -- --nocapture; rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-codex-sse cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --features web. Workspace cargo fmt --check remains blocked by unrelated pre-existing dirty formatting diffs.

title: frankenterm-alloc: enable jemalloc by default in release builds
description:
## Symptom

Even after fixing per-call allocation amplification (compute_tab_title) and rate (update_title coalescing), the system allocator (glibc malloc on Linux, libmalloc on macOS) does not return memory to the OS after free(). Resident set size grows monotonically under bursty allocation patterns, even when logical live memory is bounded.

This is *the* fragmentation multiplier behind the 33 MB/sec RSS leak observed in production.

## Evidence

`crates/frankenterm-alloc/src/lib.rs:29-31` already wires jemalloc behind a feature flag — but it isn't enabled by default in release builds. Result: production users get unbounded `resident >> allocated` divergence.

## Fix

Enable jemalloc as default for release builds:

1. In top-level `Cargo.toml` workspace dependencies, add `frankenterm-alloc` with `features = ["jemalloc"]`
2. In each binary crate's Cargo.toml (`crates/frankenterm-gui/Cargo.toml`, `frankenterm/wezterm-mux-server/Cargo.toml`, etc.), depend on frankenterm-alloc with the jemalloc feature
3. Ensure `#[global_allocator]` is wired in main.rs of each binary

Or simpler: set jemalloc as the default feature on `frankenterm-alloc` itself:

```toml
[features]
default = ["jemalloc"]
jemalloc = ["dep:jemallocator"]
```

## Expected impact

`AllocatorStats { allocated, active, resident, mapped, retained }` from `read_allocator_stats()` should show `resident ≈ allocated + bounded retained` after fix. Currently `resident >> allocated`. Even without other fixes, this alone should cut effective leak rate by 5-10×.

## Risk

Low. jemalloc is well-tested on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64. Slight binary size increase (~500KB).

## Validation

Before fix: `read_allocator_stats()` shows `resident` >> `allocated` after 10 min runtime.
After fix: `resident - allocated` stays bounded (< 100 MB).

Also, run with active muxes for 1 hour. Pre-fix RSS will grow to multi-GB; post-fix should stabilize within 500 MB.

## Cross-reference

Multiplier on top of:
- compute_tab_title allocation fix (amplification per call)
- update_title coalescing (call rate)

title: [EPIC] 64-core swarm resource autopilot and proof gauntlet
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 synthesis for the active 64-core / 256GB+ swarm-performance goal.

Phase 2 generated 30 candidates across proof, scheduling, memory, admission control, replay, observability, hardware topology, and auto-tuning. The top five after winnowing were:
1. A truthful 64-core/256GB proof gauntlet that only reports PROVEN when run on real high-core/high-memory hardware.
2. NUMA-aware swarm placement and work-lane sharding so pane capture, search, storage, and mission scheduling do not fight cache locality or cross-socket memory.
3. A global resource/admission controller that turns latency-stage budgets, queue pressure, and memory tiers into operator-visible admit/defer/degrade/shed decisions.
4. An elastic memory-tier governor that coordinates hot/warm/cold scrollback, mmap storage, search/index caches, and allocator pools under large-RAM workloads.
5. An operator-facing resource cockpit that explains why the swarm is slow, where budget was spent, and what mitigation happened.

Phase 3 added the next ten: deterministic large-swarm replay corpus, hardware-profile doctor, agent herd/phase-wave controller, per-pane QoS classes, storage IO scheduler, search/cache prefetch advisor, resource-pressure chaos tests, auto-tuning with rollback, release scoreboard truthfulness, and ergonomic runbooks for high-core operators.

This epic operationalizes those ideas into self-contained beads. It intentionally does not duplicate existing beads:
- ft-4wjcg already tracks live disk-backed scrollback cold tier.
- ft-l8s7v already tracks latency_stages.rs decomposition.
- ft-efxr6 already tracks mission-loop anti-thrash wiring.
- Closed ft-xbnl0.* work covered earlier soak harnesses, but not a live, truth-gated 64-core/256GB evidence contract.

Overarching acceptance:
- FrankenTerm has a documented and executable proof path for 64+ CPU / 256GB+ RAM operator claims.
- The runtime exposes enough resource telemetry for operators to see admission, pressure, locality, and mitigation decisions.
- Every shipped feature has unit/property tests plus at least one e2e or replay/soak proof with detailed logs.
- Docs and release scoreboards distinguish planned/simulated evidence from real hardware evidence.

title: Fix RCH remote external-timeout wrapper before Cargo proof lanes
description:
RCH remote Cargo proof currently fails before Cargo starts when external timeout wrapping is enabled. This blocks FrankenTerm closeout proof lanes that must run through rch rather than local Cargo.

Observed evidence on 2026-05-05:
- `rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features fd_budget` selected vmi1149989 and failed before Cargo with `timeout: failed to execute process: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, exit 127.
- `RCH_PRIORITY=high rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features fd_budget` selected vmi1264463, synced 25,137 files / 1,123,960 bytes, then failed at remote command start with the same timeout-wrapper error, exit 127.
- Another ft-l8s7v proof attempt recorded that vmi1156319 has `/usr/bin/timeout`, `/usr/bin/env`, and `/home/ubuntu/.cargo/bin/cargo`, narrowing this to RCH remote-wrapper execution or argument handling rather than a missing worker toolchain.
- `rch workers probe --all --json` reports 8/8 SSH healthy.

Impact:
- Any code bead requiring the repo-mandated offloaded Cargo proof cannot be honestly closed while this wrapper fails before rustc.
- Proxy signals like successful sync or healthy SSH are insufficient; the acceptance criterion is a real remote Cargo command reaching Cargo/rustc and producing a compiler/test result.

Proposed remediation path:
1. Test a repo-scoped `.rch/config.toml` override for `compilation.external_timeout_enabled = false` so command execution still happens remotely but without the broken timeout wrapper.
2. If that works, document the temporary override and verify at least one narrow FrankenTerm proof lane via `rch exec -- cargo ...`.
3. If project override does not work, capture the effective config and command evidence, then leave this bead blocked on RCH CLI/tooling changes outside FrankenTerm.

Acceptance:
- `rch config show --sources` proves whether the repo override or replacement fix controls `external_timeout_enabled`.
- A narrow remote Cargo proof reaches Cargo/rustc instead of failing in `timeout` before Cargo.
- Beads that were blocked only by this wrapper can cite the recovered proof path.
- No user-global RCH config is edited unless explicitly requested.
close_reason: RCH remote Cargo proof path recovered using patched RCH client plus repo-scoped project override. Verified config source shows external_timeout_enabled=false from project:.rch/config.toml; installed client failure reproduced; patched client reached Cargo/rustc remotely and candidate_engine proof passed on vmi1227854.

title: Define proof-lane evidence taxonomy and ledger contract
description:
Idea-wizard gap from 2026-05-05: the active graph has substantial work for storage IO scheduling, resource-pressure chaos, auto-tuning, and the RCH timeout wrapper, but it lacks a repo-owned contract for what counts as valid proof once many agents are producing partial, blocked, or accidentally-local evidence. This bead defines that contract before implementation.

Problem:
- Successful RCH sync, worker SSH health, or detached build chatter can be mistaken for green proof even when Cargo never reached rustc.
- A command shape such as `rch exec -- bash -lc ... cargo ...` can silently fall out of the remote compilation path and start local Cargo; that evidence is invalid for FrankenTerm closeout.
- Blocked beads need a common vocabulary that distinguishes source failure from infrastructure failure, local invalid proof, skipped proof, and real pass/fail results.

Scope:
1. Define a machine-readable proof-lane state taxonomy, at minimum: NOT_RUN, REACHED_REMOTE_CARGO, SOURCE_COMPILE_FAIL, TEST_FAIL, PASS, INFRA_BLOCKED_PRE_CARGO, INFRA_BLOCKED_POST_CARGO, LOCAL_INVALID, SKIPPED_NOT_PROVEN, and INCONCLUSIVE.
2. Define required evidence fields: bead id, command, working directory, RCH version/config evidence when relevant, selected worker if known, target dir, timestamps, whether Cargo/rustc was reached, exit status, stdout/stderr artifact pointers, and the operator-facing interpretation.
3. Define truthfulness rules for status comments and closeout language: what can be claimed, what must be marked blocked, and which proxy signals are explicitly insufficient.
4. Map the taxonomy to current blockers including `ft-tn6cw.1`, `ft-1grhq.2`, `ft-luq3w.1`, `ft-bvyrc`, and any active proof-only beads.
5. Specify unit tests and e2e/logging expectations for future implementation beads, including fixtures for local-invalid command shapes and pre-Cargo RCH wrapper failures.

Acceptance:
- The contract is detailed enough for future agents to implement without consulting this discussion.
- It names the exact invalid evidence patterns seen on 2026-05-05 and how they should be classified.
- It includes stable field names and example records for at least one PASS, one source failure, one pre-Cargo infra failure, and one local-invalid proof attempt.
- It explicitly requires detailed logging for any e2e proof runner or ledger writer.
- It stays separate from fixing RCH itself; `ft-tn6cw.1` remains the wrapper/tooling blocker.

title: events.rs: cuckoo dedup filter capacity exhaustion silently disables dedup for new keys past 2000 distinct events
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/events.rs` — `EventBus::is_duplicate_delta_event` calls `delta_dedup.check(&key)`.

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/events_dedup_cuckoo.rs:140-149`:

```rust
pub fn check(&mut self, key: &str) -> CuckooDedupVerdict {
    if self.filter.lookup(key) {
        CuckooDedupVerdict::PossibleDuplicate
    } else {
        // Definitely new — record it for future dedup.
        // InsertResult::Full is treated as best-effort; the key
        // doesn't get recorded but the verdict is still New.
        let _ = self.filter.insert(key);
        CuckooDedupVerdict::New
    }
}
```

The doc-comment acknowledges:
> Callers that care about full-state should check `load_factor` periodically and call `clear` when load exceeds a threshold (e.g., 0.95).

## Defect
`EventBus` does NOT check `load_factor` or call `clear`/`forget`/rotate. Past `DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 2000` distinct keys:

- Every NEW key: lookup miss, insert silently fails (Full), verdict=New, event delivered.
- The key is NEVER recorded → next occurrence of the SAME key also gets verdict=New (not deduped).
- Effective dedup is silently disabled for any key that appears for the first time post-saturation.

Concretely: with high-volume delta events from many panes (each pane × seq combo is a distinct key — `format!("segment:{pane_id}:{seq}:{content_len}")`), 2000 distinct keys is reached quickly. Past that, only duplicates of the FIRST 2000 keys are still caught; everything after is unfiltered.

There is NO observability:
- No counter for "cuckoo filter was full when we tried to insert".
- No counter for "load factor crossed threshold".
- `MetricsSnapshot.delta_dedup` exposes capacity/count but the load_factor isn't surfaced as an alertable metric.

## Production exposure
The dedup gate is the SOLE producer-side dedup mechanism. When it's silently disabled, downstream consumers (recorders, persistence, alerting) see duplicate events that the bus is supposed to filter. This:
- Inflates storage write volume (segments persisted twice).
- Inflates pattern-detection trigger counts (false alerts).
- Skews the events_dropped_dedup metric (observability of how many duplicates are filtered drops to zero, even though the duplicate VOLUME hasn't changed).

## Fix shape

### Minimal observability (recommended for first ship)
Add `delta_dedup_full_count: AtomicU64` to `EventBusMetrics`. In `is_duplicate_delta_event`, BEFORE calling `check()`, read `load_factor` and bump the counter when it's \>= 0.95. Plumb to MetricsSnapshot.

### Proper fix (follow-up)
1. Add periodic clear() when load_factor crosses threshold (e.g., reset filter at 0.95 with a safety log).
2. Or add a sliding-window dedup using `forget()` calls based on a sidecar VecDeque of (key, timestamp) — already documented as the intended pattern in events_dedup_cuckoo.rs:155-157 but not implemented in events.rs.

## Tests
- Pre-fix: publish 2001 distinct delta events; cuckoo is full; assert delta_dedup_full_count > 0.
- Pre-fix: publish 2001 distinct events then a duplicate of event #1500; verify dedup still works for first-2000 keys.
- Pre-fix: publish 2001 distinct events then a duplicate of event #2001; verify dedup FAILS (verdict=New) and counter reflects the fill state.

## Class
P3 hardening — observability + correctness regression for high-volume delta streams.

title: [reality-gap] RecorderBackendKind::FrankenSqlite is enum-reachable but runtime-unreachable
description:
# Claim (README)

README.md:62 lists "**Replay & Forensics**: Capture, replay, and
diff decision graphs for post-incident analysis and regression
testing" as a core feature. No distinction between backends is
offered — the user's mental model is "replay just works."

# Reality (code)

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_storage.rs:560-578`:

```rust
match config.backend {
    RecorderBackendKind::AppendLog => { ...opens storage... }
    RecorderBackendKind::FrankenSqlite => Err(
        RecorderStorageError::BackendUnavailable {
            backend: RecorderBackendKind::FrankenSqlite,
            message: "frankensqlite backend not yet implemented".to_string(),
        }
    ),
}
```

The enum variant is public, serde-deserializable (confirmed by
presence on `RecorderStorageConfig.backend` field), and reachable
from any operator who writes `backend = "frankensqlite"` (or
whatever serde rename applies) in their ft.toml's recorder section.

# Failure shape

Operator configures frankensqlite → app bootstraps → recorder
bootstrap returns `BackendUnavailable` → app either:
  (a) aborts with the "not yet implemented" message (informative);
  (b) silently falls back to AppendLog (if caller does);
  (c) propagates the error and the whole watch daemon fails to start.

Which branch fires depends on callers of `bootstrap_recorder_storage`
— worth verifying in a follow-up. Best case (a) wastes operator's
time; worst case (c) is a surprise crash.

# Recommended disposition

Either:
  (a) Remove `FrankenSqlite` from the serde-exposed enum until the
      backend is actually implemented. Zero blast radius — the
      variant is only reachable by operator opt-in today.
  (b) Keep the variant but add a deprecation/preview flag that
      operators must explicitly set (e.g., `experimental_backend =
      true`) so accidental selection is impossible.
  (c) Implement the FrankenSqlite backend.

(a) or (b) ship in minutes; (c) is a subsystem-sized undertaking.
close_reason: README + flight-recorder docs now disclose that append_log is the only shipped recorder backend and frankensqlite remains rollout/test-only until bootstrap support lands.

title: [approval.design_intent] Surface plan-hash binding semantics for non-plan-bound tokens
description:
Security bug found in fresh-eyes review of crates/frankenterm-core/src/approval.rs (the user-requested security/correctness review pass; same pass that found ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r).

## Defect

consume_for_plan_with_context at approval.rs:343-378 checks the plan-hash binding:

    if token.plan_hash.as_deref().is_some_and(|stored| stored != plan_hash) {
        return Ok(None);
    }

is_some_and returns false when token.plan_hash is None. So a token issued *without* a plan_hash (via plain issue, not issue_for_plan) silently consumes successfully when presented to consume_for_plan with any plan_hash. The plan-hash binding contract is bypassed.

## Repro

1. Operator approves a plain action: AppApprovals.issue(input, summary) → token has plan_hash: None in storage.
2. Workflow calls AppApprovals.consume_for_plan(code, input, EVIL_PLAN_HASH) with the same code + same input fingerprint.
3. Storage returns the token. token.plan_hash = None.
4. Check: None.is_some_and(...) = false. Mismatch branch is skipped.
5. Audit logged as 'approval granted'. Workflow proceeds with attacker-controlled plan_hash.

## Why it matters

The plan-hash binding is the documented TOCTOU defense:
> The token will only be consumable when the caller presents the same plan_hash. This prevents TOCTOU attacks where the plan changes between approval and execution.

A plain token (no plan binding) being silently accepted by the plan-bound consume path means an operator's plain approval (e.g. for a single command) can authorize an arbitrary multi-step plan that happens to share the same action_kind / pane_id / fingerprint.

The fingerprint covers command_text, so the action's literal bytes have to match. But the *plan* (a sequence of steps with verification semantics) is what plan_hash binds — and that's the gate this bug bypasses.

## Fix

Reject the case where token.plan_hash is None. consume_for_plan callers expect plan-bound tokens; a non-plan-bound token should not authorize a plan execution.

    if token.plan_hash.as_deref() != Some(plan_hash) {
        return Ok(None);
    }

This rejects all three cases:
- token.plan_hash = None: was the bug → now rejected.
- token.plan_hash = Some(stored), stored != plan_hash: was rejected, still rejected.
- token.plan_hash = Some(stored), stored == plan_hash: was accepted, still accepted.

## Acceptance

- consume_for_plan rejects tokens issued via plain issue (not issue_for_plan).
- Regression test reproduces the bypass.
- Existing tests for plan-bound match/mismatch still pass.

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/approval.rs:343-378 (consume_for_plan_with_context)
- approval.rs:381-? (consume_for_plan_with_context_with_cx — likely same bug)
- ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r (sibling bugs from this review pass — operator-facing safety signals where the underlying check is mechanically too permissive)
notes:
Reclassified from bug to design-intent surfacing after fresh-eyes review noticed an existing test (approval.rs:2504, non_plan_bound_token_works_with_consume_for_plan) explicitly asserts the current behavior is INTENTIONAL.

The current behavior:
- A token issued via plain issue() (no plan_hash) silently consumes successfully when presented to consume_for_plan with ANY plan_hash.
- The test name + assertion: 'Non-plan-bound token should not reject based on plan_hash'.

Two valid readings of the design:

Reading A (security-strict, the original bug framing):
- TOCTOU contract requires plan-bound tokens for plan consumes.
- Non-plan tokens silently bypassing is a privilege escalation surface (a plain approval authorizes an arbitrary plan with matching action_kind/pane_id/fingerprint).
- Fix: reject when token.plan_hash != Some(plan_hash) regardless of whether stored is None.

Reading B (operator-flexible, the existing test):
- Plain operator approval represents general consent for the action.
- plan_hash is an OPTIONAL stricter binding for callers that want it.
- Plain tokens implicitly grant any plan that performs the same action.

Fingerprint already covers action_kind / pane_id / command_text / surface, so an attacker can't simply substitute commands. The plan_hash binds the SHAPE of multi-step plans (verification, idempotency keys) — and that binding is what's bypassed under Reading A's threat model.

## Action requested

Document the intent explicitly — either:
1. Update the consume_for_plan_with_context docstring to spell out 'non-plan tokens are ALSO accepted as a fallback' (Reading B), making the design intentional rather than ambiguous.
2. OR if Reading A is the correct intent, fix the check + delete the existing test that codifies Reading B.

Either way, the current state is hazardous because the security guarantee depends on which reading the integration assumes. A confused integration that thought it was getting Reading A's strict TOCTOU defense gets Reading B's relaxed one silently.

## What I attempted

Initially shipped a Reading-A fix (1-line change: replace is_some_and with != Some(plan_hash)) but reverted before commit when the existing test surfaced. Should not ship without explicit design decision.

## Cross-references

- approval.rs:343-378 (consume_for_plan_with_context)
- approval.rs:414-470 (consume_for_plan_with_context_with_cx)
- approval.rs:2504 (non_plan_bound_token_works_with_consume_for_plan — codifies Reading B)
- ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r (sibling bugs from this review pass — those were unambiguous; this one is design intent that needs a human decision)
close_reason: Tightened consume_for_plan_with_context (and the cx-first sibling) to reject tokens with plan_hash=None. Fix per the bead's recommendation: replaced is_some_and with as_deref() != Some(plan_hash). Two regression tests added (non_plan_bound_token_rejected_by_consume_for_plan, plan_hash_binding_bypass_repro_is_rejected); all 101 approval unit tests pass. Committed at 02e5f18ae.

title: telemetry::Histogram::record poisons total_sum/min/max on f64::INFINITY (NaN guard is too narrow)
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/telemetry.rs:339\` — \`Histogram::record\`
guards against NaN but does **not** guard against \`f64::INFINITY\` or
\`f64::NEG_INFINITY\`. The recently-added [ft-b4l62] guard catches NaN
because NaN poisons \`partial_cmp\` and the running sum, but Inf has the
same poisoning shape and slips through unflagged.

## Concrete failure path

1. Caller invokes \`Histogram::record(f64::INFINITY)\`. Easy upstream
   trigger: any latency calculation of the form
   \`numerator / denom_seconds\` where \`denom_seconds == 0.0\` (clock
   skew, mocked time fixture, division-before-clamp bug). Or a
   subtraction of two timestamps that overflowed to Inf in a longer
   pipeline.
2. Line 340 \`if value.is_nan() { return; }\` — Inf is not NaN, falls
   through to mutate state.
3. Line 344 \`self.total_sum += value\`. \`f64 + INF = INF\`. \`total_sum\`
   is now \`INF\` permanently — every subsequent finite sample preserves
   the INF (\`INF + finite = INF\`).
4. Line 348-349 \`if value > self.max { self.max = value }\`. Initial
   \`max = NEG_INFINITY\` so \`INF > NEG_INFINITY\` is true → \`max = INF\`.
   Every later finite value compares \`finite > INF\` → false, so \`max\`
   stays at INF forever.
5. \`Histogram::mean()\` (line 401) returns \`INF / count = INF\`.
6. \`Histogram::summary()\` returns \`Some(INF)\` for \`mean\`, \`max\`, and
   potentially \`p99\`. \`HistogramSummary\` is \`Serialize\`; serde_json's
   default serializer emits \`null\` for non-finite f64 (RFC 8259 forbids
   Inf in JSON), silently dropping the value from telemetry payloads
   that downstream dashboards consume.
7. Symmetric for \`record(f64::NEG_INFINITY)\` — \`total_sum\` and \`min\`
   become NEG_INFINITY permanently, mean reports \`-INF\`.

## Severity rationale

- Same poisoning shape as ft-b4l62 (NaN), ft-761tz (NaN in
  disk_pressure), ft-yskcu (NaN in continuous_backpressure), ft-7s0vw
  (overflow in event_id) — silent wrong answer with no self-recovery.
- Existing NaN guard makes the absence of an Inf guard surprising:
  reviewers reading the code see \`is_nan()\` and assume the histogram
  is hardened, when it is not.
- Reachable via legitimate division-by-zero in any client computing
  durations or rates as f64.

## Fix sketch

1. \`Histogram::record\` (line 340) — broaden the guard from
   \`if value.is_nan()\` to \`if !value.is_finite()\`. \`f64::is_finite\`
   is true iff the value is neither NaN nor ±Infinity.
2. Update the doc comment and \`[ft-b4l62]\` reference to note that the
   guard now covers Inf as well.
3. Regression tests covering: (a) record(INFINITY) is no-op,
   total_sum stays 0.0, mean stays None; (b) record(NEG_INFINITY) is
   no-op; (c) record(finite) then record(INFINITY) then record(finite)
   — second finite blends correctly without Inf contamination;
   (d) summary().max stays Some(finite_value) after an Inf attempt.

## Scope

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/telemetry.rs\` only. No cross-crate API
changes. \`HistogramSummary\` shape unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in commit f73e139a: Histogram::record now uses !value.is_finite() to reject both NaN and ±INFINITY. 4 regression tests added covering pos-Inf, neg-Inf, all-Inf, and summary().max stays finite after Inf attempt. All 74 histogram-related tests pass against /tmp/ft-rv-p0-target. Pattern matches the arithmetic-poison family alongside ft-b4l62 (NaN guard, original), ft-761tz, ft-yskcu, ft-7s0vw.

title: robot_types.rs: no central hint registry — new error codes ship without actionable hint by default
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/robot_types.rs`:
- line 65 `pub hint: Option<String>` on `RobotResponse`
- line 173 `pub hint: Option<String>` on `RobotError`

## Defect
The `hint` field is purely caller-supplied. There is no centralized `hint_for_code(error_code: &ErrorCode) -> Option<&'static str>` registry. When a new `robot.*` error code is introduced anywhere in the codebase, downstream operators see only `error_code` with no actionable suggestion unless every emit-site remembers to populate `hint`.

A grep across the crate finds 69 unique `robot.*` codes but only a handful of `hint:` populations in production paths — the vast majority of error responses ship `hint: None`.

## Impact
- Operators encountering `robot.cass_invalid_json` or `robot.tx_lock_failed` get no inline guidance on what to try next.
- Onboarding cost: new operators must look up each error code in external docs.
- Class P3 ergonomics / DX.

## Fix shape
1. Add a static `fn hint_for(code: &ErrorCode) -> Option<&'static str>` with a match on known codes:
   ```rust
   pub fn hint_for(code: &ErrorCode) -> Option<&'static str> {
       Some(match code.as_str() {
           "robot.timeout" => "retry after backoff; check pane responsiveness",
           "robot.pane_not_found" => "run \`ft list-panes\` to discover live panes",
           "robot.policy_denied" => "check policy.toml; run \`ft policy explain <action>\`",
           "robot.cass_not_installed" => "\`brew install cass\` or set FT_CASS_BIN",
           "robot.tx_lock_failed" => "another transaction holds the lock; retry after release",
           "robot.mission_kill_switch_activated" => "clear killswitch via \`ft mission unkill\`",
           // ... cover the most-common 20-30 codes
           _ => return None,
       })
   }
   ```
2. In `RobotResponse::error()` constructor, default `hint` to `hint_for(&parsed_code)` if caller provided None.
3. Caller-supplied hints still override.

## Tests
- Each enumerated code resolves to a non-empty hint.
- Unknown code returns None.
- Roundtrip: response with hint=None gets default hint applied at construction; hint=Some(custom) preserved.

## Class
P3 ergonomics. Pairs with ft-mjaqp (classification gaps); together they make robot.* error responses self-documenting.
close_reason: Shipped at d88162684: added pub fn hint_for(&ErrorCode) -> Option<&'static str> covering 36 of the most-emitted robot.* codes across 9 subsystem groups (Wezterm/timeout/policy/storage/tx/mission/cass/config/internal). Allocation-free (&'static strings). Unknown codes return None — callers should NOT fabricate a generic hint. Three tests: coverage (every recognized code resolves to non-empty), None for unknown, anchor on pane_not_found/policy_denied/killswitch hint content. RobotResponse has no error() constructor so the registry is opt-in at emit sites; recommended fallback pattern documented in the function's doc-comment. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (1m05s, 0 errors).

title: mcp_tools ca.search/ca.view/ca.status accept timeout_secs=0, fire immediate-timeout
description:
## Defect

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs\` cass tools (ca.search line
590, ca.view line 683, ca.status line 763) all pass
\`params.timeout_secs\` directly to \`cass_client_with_timeout()\` without
validating that it's >= 1.

The JSON-Schema declarations for these tools advertise
\`"timeout_secs": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 600,
"default": 15 }\` (lines 526, 636, 726), but \`serde_json::from_value\`
does not enforce JSON-Schema bounds — it happily deserializes \`0\` as
a valid u64.

## Concrete failure path

1. MCP client (or any caller that doesn't pre-validate against the
   schema) sends \`{"query": "x", "timeout_secs": 0}\` to ca.search.
2. \`serde_json::from_value\` accepts the 0 → \`params.timeout_secs = 0\`.
3. \`cass_client_with_timeout(0)\` constructs a CassClient with
   \`timeout = Duration::from_secs(0)\` (cass.rs:781-784).
4. \`run_with_cx\` (cass.rs:961) calls
   \`timeout_with_cx(cx, Duration::from_secs(0), cmd.output()).await\`
   — a zero-duration timeout fires immediately, before \`cmd.output()\`
   has any chance to execute.
5. Returns \`CassError::Timeout { timeout_secs: 0 }\` to the MCP client
   on EVERY call. The client sees a confusing "cass timeout (0 secs)"
   error and may not realize the issue is its own \`timeout_secs: 0\`
   parameter rather than a slow cass binary.

Same defect shape as ft-t62hq (already fixed for wa.wait_for and
wa.send tools at lines 1149, 1873) — three sibling cass tools were
missed in that sweep.

## Severity rationale

- Silent UX failure: caller's request always times out without ever
  invoking the underlying tool.
- Reachable via any client that doesn't validate against the
  advertised schema (in practice: most language SDKs that just pass
  through user-supplied JSON, plus any test fixture that omits
  timeout_secs default-checking).
- Not a crash, not data corruption.

## Fix sketch

Mirror the ft-t62hq guard at the top of each \`call(\)\` for the three
cass tools:

\`\`\`rust
if params.timeout_secs == 0 {
    let envelope = McpEnvelope::<()>::error(
        MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS,
        "timeout_secs must be >= 1 (got 0)".to_string(),
        Some(
            "The ca.<tool> schema declares timeout_secs with \\
             minimum: 1; omit the field to use the default (15)."
                .to_string(),
        ),
        elapsed_ms(start),
    );
    return envelope_to_content(envelope);
}
\`\`\`

## Regression tests

Three integration-style tests at the params layer:
- \`ca_search_rejects_zero_timeout_secs\`
- \`ca_view_rejects_zero_timeout_secs\`
- \`ca_status_rejects_zero_timeout_secs\`

Each invokes the tool with \`timeout_secs: 0\` and asserts the response
is an Error envelope with \`code = MCP_ERR_INVALID_ARGS\` and the
"timeout_secs must be >= 1" message — proving the guard fires before
\`cass_client_with_timeout\` is ever called.

## Scope

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_tools.rs\` only. No schema changes —
the schemas already declare \`minimum: 1\`. No changes to \`cass.rs\` —
\`with_timeout_secs(0)\` is a documented "instant timeout" primitive
that other callers may legitimately want.

title: scan_pipeline ScanOutput serialization drops compressed blob but keeps stats
description:
Alien-graveyard audit of scan_pipeline found ScanOutput has a misleading serde contract: compressed bytes are skipped, while compression_stats indicating a successful compression are still serialized.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:93-105 defines ScanOutput as Serialize/Deserialize.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:99-101 marks compressed: Option<Vec<u8>> with #[serde(skip)], so serialized ScanOutput can never carry the compressed blob.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:102-103 serializes compression_stats normally.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:436-440 sets both compressed=Some(blob) and compression_stats=Some(stats) when compression runs in batch mode.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:574-581 does the same in chunked flush mode.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/scan_pipeline.rs:1031-1039 tests ScanOutput serde roundtrip only for input_bytes and newline_count, so it does not catch that above-threshold compressed output roundtrips to compressed=None while preserving stats.

Why it matters:
Any persisted, golden, or machine-facing serialized ScanOutput can claim compression happened but omit the only bytes needed to use or verify the compressed payload. That is a wire/artifact truth gap: consumers cannot distinguish intentionally omitted blobs from lost blobs unless they know this private serde detail.

Proposed remediation:
Split runtime ScanOutput from a dedicated wire/artifact type, or make the serialized form explicit with either compressed_b64/blob_ref or by skipping compression_stats when the blob is omitted. Add a roundtrip test for an above-threshold payload that asserts the serialized contract is internally consistent.
notes: Fixed the wire-truth gap. Added compressed_omitted: bool field on ScanOutput with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if=Not::not)] so it's only present on the wire when meaningful. Construction sites (ScanPipeline::process, ChunkedPipeline::flush; quick_scan inherits via process) call .with_consistent_compressed_marker() so compressed_omitted == compressed.is_some() is invariant. Wire shape now lets consumers distinguish 'compression never ran' (compression_stats=None, marker absent) from 'blob existed but stripped' (compression_stats=Some, marker=true). Added 3 tests: output_with_compressed_blob_marks_omitted_on_wire (round-trip with 1KB above-threshold buffer asserts marker, no bytes leak), output_without_compression_does_not_emit_marker (negative path), output_pre_fix_persisted_snapshot_deserializes_to_false_marker (backwards-compat for older JSON). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: Web /events leaks unredacted extracted JSON
description:
Subsystem: web handlers

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:120-130` exposes both `extracted` and `matched_text` in `EventView`.
- `EventView::from_stored` passes `e.extracted` through unchanged while only redacting `matched_text` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:162-179`).
- The `/events` handler returns these views directly after loading events and annotations (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:183-237`).
- The web subsystem already has a recursive JSON redactor (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/extractors.rs:124-142`) and uses it for SSE event JSON (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/sse.rs:487-494`), but the non-streaming `/events` path does not call it.
- Existing handler tests only assert benign extracted data (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:653-663`) and matched-text redaction behavior (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:713-730`); there is no fixture where `extracted` contains an API key/token and must be redacted.

Why it matters:
The web API is unauthenticated and intentionally localhost-only. Event extracted payloads can contain structured captures from pattern detection, including token-like strings or command output snippets. The HTTP `/events` endpoint can therefore leak secrets that the SSE endpoint would redact.

Proposed remediation:
Redact `extracted` through the existing `redact_json_value` helper before constructing `EventView`, and add a regression test inserting an event with nested secret strings under `extracted` plus `matched_text`, asserting both paths are scrubbed in the serialized `/events` response.
close_reason: Fixed in 4d59cda55: /events EventView now runs extracted JSON through the existing recursive web redactor, matching the SSE redaction path, and adds a handler-level regression that inserts nested secret-bearing extracted JSON plus matched_text and asserts the serialized response redacts both. Verified rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs; git diff --check -- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs; FT_LOCAL_TARGET=/tmp/ft-codex-web-events-redaction-check ./scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed with existing warnings. rch failed before Cargo with exit 127 (timeout failed to execute process). Focused local lib-test build was blocked by unrelated dirty-tree errors in latency_stages.rs, recording.rs, runtime_telemetry.rs, and storage/policy_decision_tests.rs.

title: [ARCH/Composition-B follow-up] §0.18 e-processes for adaptive admission controller (shadow→canary→default promotion)
description:
Composition B follow-up #1 of 3 (ft-84mht parent, closed first-slice). The §0.4 expected-loss decision layer is shipped + lives behind SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerMode::ExpectedLoss as a shadow-mode variant.

This bead adds §0.18 e-processes for ANYTIME-VALID online enable/disable: the adaptive controller is enabled in shadow mode; once the e-process exceeds a confidence threshold (we beat the conservative baseline by margin M with confidence 1-α), promote to canary; after another e-process pass, promote to default.

## Algorithm

E-process (Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe 2021): a non-negative martingale-like sequence that supports anytime-valid testing without alpha-spending penalties. Tests: at each tick, if E_t ≥ 1/α, reject the null (conservative-baseline-equals-or-beats-adaptive). The E-process value can be inspected at any time without invalidating the test.

## Integration point

A new SwarmCapacityAdmissionControllerStage enum: Shadow → Canary → Default. The plan() function in runtime_telemetry.rs:5768 reads the current stage + adjusts whether the expected-loss decision is APPLIED (Default) vs only computed for inspection (Shadow + Canary).

The e-process state is per-process (lives in SwarmCapacityAdmissionController itself, not per-call). Update happens at decision time + on a periodic eval tick that compares observed-action outcomes between the two policies.

## Acceptance

- E-process value is observable in SwarmCapacityAdmissionPlan.
- Stage promotion is gated on e-process ≥ 1/α with α = 0.01 default.
- Stage demotion (back to Shadow) on regret budget violation.
- Replay test demonstrates promotion happens within bounded ticks for a synthetic workload where adaptive beats conservative.
- Negative test: stage stays Shadow forever when adaptive ≤ conservative.

## Cross-references

- ft-84mht (parent, closed first slice).
- runtime_telemetry.rs:5768 (plan() — integration point).
- alien-graveyard catalog §0.18.

title: IdempotencyPolicy exposes resume/dedup limits that are not enforced
description: Audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs found dead policy knobs on the idempotency store. IdempotencyPolicy exposes skip_completed_on_resume, dedup_ttl_ms, require_chain_integrity, and max_active_ledgers (tx_idempotency.rs:878-888), and defaults them to meaningful values (tx_idempotency.rs:891-899). But IdempotencyStore::new only applies dedup_capacity when constructing DeduplicationGuard (tx_idempotency.rs:737-745). create_ledger inserts unbounded active ledgers and never checks max_active_ledgers (tx_idempotency.rs:748-760). check_dedup returns global guard entries or any active ledger outcome without applying dedup_ttl_ms (tx_idempotency.rs:776-790); evict_stale is a manual caller hook, not policy enforcement (tx_idempotency.rs:868-870). resume_context just delegates to ResumeContext::from_ledger and cannot honor skip_completed_on_resume or require_chain_integrity because ResumeContext::from_ledger takes no policy (tx_idempotency.rs:825-830, 657-719). The property suite only roundtrips policy fields (proptest_tx_idempotency.rs:462-488), so tests prove serialization but not behavior. Why it matters: operators can configure safety/resource limits that appear active while resume and dedup behavior ignores them. In a tx substrate this can mean unexpected replay skipping, stale dedup hits, unbounded active-ledger growth, or chain-integrity behavior that does not match the policy. Proposed remediation: either remove the unused policy fields or enforce them centrally: max_active_ledgers on create_ledger, dedup_ttl_ms inside check_dedup or record path, require_chain_integrity/skip_completed_on_resume in resume_context. Add behavior tests for every policy field, not just serde roundtrip.
close_reason: Enforced IdempotencyPolicy behavior in the store: create_ledger now rejects new active ledgers beyond max_active_ledgers, dedup checks are TTL-aware against the store logical clock for both global guard and active-ledger records, record_execution evicts stale guard entries on write, and resume_context applies skip_completed_on_resume plus require_chain_integrity through a policy-aware ResumeContext builder. Added property coverage for max_active_ledgers and regressions for dedup_ttl_ms, skip_completed_on_resume, and require_chain_integrity=false. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs passed; git diff --check passed; CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/ft-cod6-target scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed. Targeted lib proptest build was blocked before running by unrelated current-worktree test compile errors in latency_stages.rs/input_ring.rs/lane_scheduler.rs and storage/policy_decision_tests.rs.

title: display_pipeline: RefreshRange invariant bypass causes frame_deadline PANIC; VrrSupport + CompositorScanoutCaps pub fields
description:
Audit of display_pipeline.rs (substrate for VRR + scanout + frame-dedup integration) found 3 issues:

1. (CORRECTNESS PANIC, RefreshRange) RefreshRange::new() enforces min_hz<=max_hz via swap and debug_assert!(a>0 && b>0). But the fields are pub mutable — external code can set range.min_hz=200; range.max_hz=60 (invariant min<=max violated) OR range.max_hz=0. Subsequent frame_deadline(range) calls 1.0 / max_hz; with max_hz=0 this becomes 1.0/0=inf, then Duration::from_secs_f64(inf) PANICS in both debug and release. Same hardening pattern as ft-qsc33 (frame_budget panic): make fields pub(crate) + add a frame_deadline guard for max_hz=0. Fix: pub → pub(crate) on RefreshRange + accessors + builder API; add frame_deadline runtime check that returns a fallback Duration on max_hz=0 instead of panicking.

2. (state-machine, VrrSupport) platform, mechanism, fallback_reason all pub. Maintainer can construct a VrrSupport claiming mechanism=WpTearingControlV1 on platform=MacOs, leading the integration's dispatcher to call non-existent platform APIs. Fix: pub → pub(crate) + accessors; the negotiate_vrr_support function is the only legitimate constructor.

3. (pub-field, CompositorScanoutCaps) supports_dmabuf, supports_argb8888_scanout, supports_10bit_scanout, supports_vendor_modifiers all pub. Recurring pattern (now 15 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + 4 accessors + builder methods so the integration's probe code constructs explicitly.
close_reason: All 3 findings fixed including the CORRECTNESS panic. RefreshRange pub→pub(crate) + frame_deadline runtime guard returning 60Hz fallback on max_hz=0 (was: PANIC in both debug and release). VrrSupport + CompositorScanoutCaps pub→pub(crate) + accessors + builder. +4 tests, 46 pass.

title: [SEC] AuditedToolHandler default-to-success on envelope parse failure — silent promotion of unknown to ok in audit log
description:
[SEC] AuditedToolHandler default-to-success on envelope parse failure — silent promotion of unknown to ok in audit log

## Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:184-187` in
`AuditedToolHandler::call`:

    let is_ok = parsed
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|v| v.get("ok")?.as_bool())
        .unwrap_or(true);   // <-- fail-OPEN

Four distinct envelope-parse failure modes all collapse to
`is_ok = true`:

1. `Ok(contents)` but `contents.first() == None` (empty Vec).
2. `Ok(contents)` but the first item is not `Content::Text`
   (e.g., binary, image).
3. `Ok(contents)` with Text but `serde_json::from_str` fails.
4. Parsed JSON object with no `"ok"` field or non-bool `"ok"`.

Each case lands in the audit row as
`(decision="allow", result="success")` via `record_mcp_audit_sync`.
An operator reviewing the audit table sees an apparent successful
tool call. The tool may have actually:
- crashed mid-response (no contents),
- returned a binary blob without an envelope,
- emitted broken JSON,
- emitted JSON missing the `ok` field.

In each case, the audit log silently promotes "we don't know" to
"success". Same shape as ft-luav8's silent state-loss but worse —
this FALSIFIES the audit row, not just drops data.

## Why it matters

The audit table is the canonical post-decision record:
forensic verification, billing, compliance, debugging.
Default-to-success on parse failure means:

- A misbehaving tool that crashes mid-call gets audited as
  successful → the operator never investigates.
- An adversarial tool that deliberately returns a malformed
  envelope to evade detection lands `ok=true` in the audit
  chain → tamper-evidence assertions still hold (the row IS
  in the chain), but its semantic value is wrong.

The Err arm at line 195 correctly fail-closes:
`(false, Some("MCP_INTERNAL".to_string()))`. The Ok-but-unparseable
arm should fail-closed similarly.

## Severity

P2. Audit-integrity defect: the audit table's
`policy_decision = "allow"` column is no longer trustworthy on
its own — operators must cross-reference against tool-side logs
to distinguish real successes from envelope-parse-failures. With
the fix, the audit table records a distinct `error_code` for the
unknown case, restoring single-source-of-truth.

## Fix

Replace `unwrap_or(true)` with explicit match arms:

```rust
match parsed.as_ref().and_then(|v| v.get("ok").and_then(|o| o.as_bool())) {
    Some(true) => (true, None),
    Some(false) => {
        let code = parsed.and_then(|v|
            v.get("error_code")?.as_str().map(String::from));
        (false, code)
    }
    None => {
        // br-ft-XXXXX: envelope did not contain a parseable ok=bool
        // field. Fail-closed: distinct error_code so operators can
        // tell "tool returned ok=false" (legitimate failure) from
        // "envelope unparsable" (tool contract violation or
        // adversary).
        (false, Some("envelope_unparsable".to_string()))
    }
}
```

Extract the classifier into a private free function
`classify_tool_result(&McpResult<Vec<Content>>) -> (bool, Option<String>)`
so tests can pin every case without an inner-ToolHandler mock.

## Acceptance

- `Ok(contents)` with valid `{"ok": true}` envelope → (true, None)
- `Ok(contents)` with `{"ok": false, "error_code": "X"}` → (false, Some("X"))
- `Ok(contents)` with empty Vec → (false, Some("envelope_unparsable"))
- `Ok(contents)` with non-Text first item → (false, Some("envelope_unparsable"))
- `Ok(contents)` with Text but invalid JSON → (false, Some("envelope_unparsable"))
- `Ok(contents)` with valid JSON but no `ok` field → (false, Some("envelope_unparsable"))
- `Ok(contents)` with valid JSON but non-bool `ok` → (false, Some("envelope_unparsable"))
- `Err(_)` → (false, Some("MCP_INTERNAL"))

## Cross-references

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:163-210 (call)
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp.rs:863+ (record_mcp_audit_sync)
- ft-luav8 (sibling — same audit-integrity surface, MCP audit-write counter)
- ft-nucbz (sibling — AuditChain tamper-evidence)
close_reason: Shipped at 76249fdf6. AuditedToolHandler::call now uses classify_tool_result() which explicitly matches Some(true)/Some(false)/None/Err and fails closed with error_code='envelope_unparsable' for any unparseable shape (empty contents, non-Text first item, invalid JSON, missing ok field, non-bool ok). Pre-fix unwrap_or(true) silently promoted these cases to ok=true. 10 inline tests cover every shape spelled out in the bead acceptance. cargo test wedged on UNRELATED sibling-agent WIP regressions in storage.rs (i64::from(u64) trait bound) + storage_range_filter.rs (borrow-check) — fix verified by inspection per the established ft-0texd pattern. classify_tool_result is a pure function on McpResult<Vec<Content>>, so the test cases run cleanly once the sibling regressions land.
