title: Recorder timestamp delta can overflow before clamp
description:
Subsystem: recording timestamp accounting

Evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:390-393` computes `(captured_at_ms - start_ms).max(0)` using direct `i64` subtraction before clamping negative deltas to zero.
- `start_ms` is supplied when a recorder starts (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:298-302`) and capture timestamps are supplied by segments/events through `record_output` and `record_event` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:317-348`, `:365-388`).
- The existing tests exercise ordinary small timestamps such as 0, 10, 20, and 50 (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:1492-1531`) and the recording proptests focus on frame/event round-trips, not boundary timestamp arithmetic.

Why it matters:
For extreme or malformed timestamp inputs, `captured_at_ms - start_ms` can overflow in debug builds and wrap in release before the `.max(0)` clamp runs. The result can be a panic or a huge bogus frame timestamp in a recording, both of which undercut replay/forensic ordering.

Proposed remediation:
Replace the subtraction with checked/saturating arithmetic, e.g. `captured_at_ms.saturating_sub(start_ms).max(0)` followed by a checked `u64` conversion. Add property tests over `i64::MIN`, `i64::MAX`, reversed clocks, and normal monotonic captures asserting no panic and nonnegative, bounded deltas.
close_reason: Fixed in e60a6734e: recorder capture timestamps now use saturating_sub before clamp, with regression coverage for reversed clocks and i64 extremes. Verified rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs; git diff --check -- crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs; local ./scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed with existing warnings. rch wrapper failed before Cargo with exit 127 (timeout failed to execute process). Focused local lib-test run was blocked by unrelated latency_stages.rs private-item errors and storage/policy_decision_tests.rs missing upsert_agent_session_sync.

title: FrameWriter finalize timeout makes recorder flush unretryable
description:
Subsystem: recording durability/finalization

Evidence:
- `FrameWriter::finalize_with_timeout` moves the buffered frames and `BufWriter<File>` out of `self` (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:153-162`), spawns a flush worker (`:164-170`), then sets `self.finalized = true` before it knows whether the worker succeeded (`:172-187`).
- On timeout or disconnected worker, the method returns an error (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:175-185`), but the caller no longer has the buffer/writer state needed to retry the flush because both were moved into the background worker and the object is marked finalized.
- `Recorder::stop` marks the recorder stopped before finalization (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:305-307`), so a failed finalize leaves the recorder no longer accepting new frames and without a retry path.
- Tests prove idempotent success (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs:1382-1407`) and drop best-effort flushing (`:1276-1330`), but there is no failure-path test for timeout/disconnected finalize behavior.

Why it matters:
The flight recorder is the forensic trail. A transient slow disk or blocked flush can report failure while also consuming the only in-memory frame buffer and permanently stopping the recorder. Operators see an error, but cannot retry or continue recording without losing or racing the still-running background flush.

Proposed remediation:
Make finalization state reflect durable completion rather than worker dispatch. Keep enough state to retry on timeout, or return a distinct `FinalizePending`/join handle state that lets callers await completion without treating the recorder as durably stopped. Move `Recorder::stop` state transition after successful durable finalize or add an explicit `Stopping/FlushPending` state. Add a deterministic unit test with an injectable writer/finalizer that times out and verifies retry/continued state semantics.
notes:
Shipped at recording.rs (lines 153-330 + 367-381 + ~190 lines of new tests). Fix has three parts:

PART 1 - New pending_finalize field on FrameWriter
A new private Option holds the in-flight worker receiver when a previous finalize_with_timeout call timed out. The original buffer + writer were moved into the worker; storing the receiver lets a subsequent call await it instead of spawning a new worker (which would have nothing to flush). Two new public observability methods: has_pending_finalize and is_finalized.

PART 2 - finalize_with_timeout retry path
On timeout the receiver is stashed in pending_finalize and finalized stays false. Subsequent calls take the receiver and await it via shared await_finalize_receiver helper. On Disconnected (worker panicked or exited without sending) the file handle is unrecoverable so finalized goes true and BrokenPipe surfaces.

PART 3 - Recorder::stop ordering
State transition to Stopped now happens AFTER finalize succeeds. Pre-fix the state was set to Stopped before finalize ran, so a transient slow disk that timed out the finalize would leave the recorder marked stopped (rejecting new frames) while surfacing an error to the caller — and there was no retry path because finalize had already moved out the buffer + writer.

Tests added (4 new tests at the end of mod tests):
- finalize_with_timeout_zero_is_retryable_ft_ye2gs: ZERO-timeout MAY race-win, both Ok and Err+pending branches asserted; retry path completes durably.
- recorder_stop_state_transition_gated_on_finalize_ft_ye2gs: pins the new ordering invariant in Recorder::stop.
- finalize_state_reflects_durable_completion_ft_ye2gs: pins the public API observability contract for has_pending_finalize / is_finalized across the lifecycle.
- finalize_retry_property_sweep_ft_ye2gs: representative-value sweep over (frames_count = 0, 1, 4, 16, 64). Each iteration asserts the post-state invariants (race-win=Ok+finalized OR race-loss=TimedOut+pending; never the cross-product); after retry, terminal state is finalized + no pending.

Verification:
- scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features: 1m20s clean (191 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: clean

Bead acceptance per the original Proposed remediation:
- Make finalization state reflect durable completion rather than worker dispatch: DONE (finalized only true after Ok)
- Keep enough state to retry on timeout: DONE (pending_finalize stashed receiver)
- OR return a distinct FinalizePending state: addressed via has_pending_finalize accessor
- Move Recorder::stop state transition after successful durable finalize: DONE
- Add a deterministic unit test with timeout that verifies retry/continued state semantics: DONE (4 tests including the property sweep)

title: [golden-artifacts] recorder events: schema is validated but encoded byte forms are not pinned with goldens
description:
## The gap

The recorder family (`crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs` plus
`recorder_storage.rs`, `recorder_replay.rs`, `recorder_audit.rs`,
`recorder_export.rs`, etc.) serializes `RecorderEvent` and friends
into persisted bytes — both the active `append_log` backend and the
rollout-only `frankensqlite` backend.

Existing coverage:

- `tests/recorder_event_schema.rs` — validates event JSON against
  `docs/flight-recorder/ft-recorder-event-v1.json`.
- `tests/proptest_recorder.rs` (36 KB) + 8 sibling proptest_recorder_*
  files — property tests on shape, ordering, retention, lexical
  ingest, audit, etc.
- `tests/recorder_correctness_integration.rs` — integration coverage.

Existing **byte goldens** for recorder events: zero. The schema
test pins JSON Schema shape; nothing pins the encoded byte form
that operators' tooling will read off disk during incident replay
months from now.

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

The recorder is the persistence layer for ft's audit + replay +
forensics surface. A schema migration that silently shifts encoded
bytes (e.g., `serde_json` field-order change after a serde version
bump, an `Option<T>` becoming `Option<U>` where `U: Default`, a
new variant tag layout) breaks replay of older sessions. The
README explicitly markets this risk surface ('Replay & Forensics |
Capture, replay, and diff decision graphs for post-incident
analysis').

The PROVENANCE.md at `tests/golden/PROVENANCE.md` already names
this exact concern for `wire_protocol.rs` and `snapshot_engine.rs`
types — but skips the recorder. Per that doc:

> **Varbincode types (in `frankenterm/codec`) are positional.**
> They are covered by `frankenterm/codec/tests/conformance_pdu_wire.rs`;
> this suite does not duplicate that coverage. … Goldens here are
> intentionally JSON because that is the serializer used by the
> in-scope `wire_protocol.rs` and `snapshot_engine.rs`.

Recorder events are JSON-serialized into the append_log backend
(per `recorder_storage.rs`'s comments), making them in-scope for
the same JSON-byte-golden treatment.

## Suggested implementation

1. **Corpus** at `tests/golden/recorder/` mirroring the existing
   `tests/golden/wire_protocol/` and `tests/golden/snapshot/`
   layout:
   - `event_pty_input.json` — RecorderEvent with PtyInput payload
   - `event_pty_output.json` — RecorderEvent with PtyOutput payload
   - `event_pane_lifecycle.json` — pane-create/destroy lifecycle
   - `event_control_marker.json` — RecorderControlMarker (OSC 133)
   - `event_redacted.json` — event with `redaction_level=Redacted`
   - `event_segment_kind_alt_screen.json` — alt-screen segment
   - `event_causality_chain.json` — events with parent/child
     causality
2. **Test driver**
   `tests/golden_recorder_event_bytes.rs`:
   - For each fixture, construct a deterministic `RecorderEvent`
     (canonical IDs, frozen timestamps), serialize via the same
     code path the production recorder uses, diff against golden.
   - Reverse: load golden, deserialize, assert round-trips back
     to identical bytes (catches `skip_serializing_if` traps —
     MEMORY.md flags varbincode-skip-serializing-if-bug).
3. **PROVENANCE.md update** at `tests/golden/PROVENANCE.md` adding
   a `## Recorder` section explaining what's pinned and why
   (incident-replay durability across schema versions).

## Out of scope

- The frankensqlite backend (it's `rollout/test-only` per README;
  add goldens when it ships to operators).
- The `recorder-lexical` Tantivy ingest path (its own proptest
  files cover indexing semantics).
- Replay/diff visualization output (covered by
  `replay_decision_diff_golden.rs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- ≥7 recorder-event byte goldens.
- Adding a field to a `RecorderEvent*` payload struct without a
  schema migration fails the relevant golden(s) with a clear diff.
- Round-trip ↔ byte-equality tests fire on every fixture.
- PROVENANCE.md adds a `## Recorder` section + regenerate command.

## References

- `tests/golden/PROVENANCE.md` (existing infrastructure to extend)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recording.rs` (event types)
- `crates/frankenterm-core/src/recorder_storage.rs` (the on-disk
  byte form)
- `tests/recorder_event_schema.rs` (schema validation — partner,
  not substitute, for byte goldens)
- MEMORY.md `varbincode-skip-serializing-if-bug` warning

Filed by cc_1 golden-artifacts audit, 2026-04-28.

title: triple_buffer: TripleBufferHealth pub counters; publish() docstring missing single-writer concurrency contract
description:
Audit of triple_buffer.rs (Petersen 2005 SWSR triple-buffered terminal state, used by render path) found 2 issues:

1. (pub-field, TripleBufferHealth) All 4 counters pub including force_recycles_total — non-zero is the stuck-reader alert condition (has_force_recycled()). Operators alarm on this counter; silently zeroing it masks recovery events. Same recurring pub-field pattern (now in 9 substrates). Fix: pub → pub(crate) + 4 read accessors.

2. (concurrency-doc, publish) publish() takes &self and TripleBuffer is Send+Sync, allowing multi-writer use. But the Petersen 2005 pattern is single-writer-single-reader: under concurrent writers, Thread A's slot write at slots[w] can be silently overwritten by Thread B's slot write to the SAME index BEFORE Thread A's CAS swaps writer↔presented. The publisher's reported PublishOutcome doesn't match the data the reader subsequently sees. The loom_1_reader_2_writers_no_lost_write test exists but its semantics are opaque. Fix: explicit docstring that publish is safe under multiple writer threads only in the sense that 'one of the publishes wins; no torn data; no lost write counter'; and document that the publisher's PublishOutcome.new_presented_slot may not match what the reader sees if a concurrent publish raced.
close_reason: Both findings fixed. TripleBufferHealth pub→pub(crate) + 4 read accessors with privacy invariant pinned (force_recycles_total only writable via force_recycle()). publish() docstring now documents the SWSR concurrency contract + multi-writer race semantics + Loom-test guarantees.

title: [security][P1] wa.state MCP tool + ft robot state CLI return pane title/cwd UNREDACTED (mismatched invariant with /panes)
description:
## Finding

Audit under ft-h8da2 (docs/security/read-path-redaction-matrix.md) confirms: wa.state MCP tool and ft robot state CLI serve pane `title` and `cwd` **unredacted**, while the sibling web handler on `GET /panes` **does** redact them.

### Evidence

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_types.rs:817-834 — McpPaneState::from_pane_info:

      title: info.title.clone(),
      cwd: info.cwd.clone(),

- crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs:5501-5518 — PaneState::from_pane_info (CLI): same pattern, same unredacted clone.

- crates/frankenterm-core/src/web/handlers.rs:64-70 — PaneView::from_record (web): **CORRECT** reference implementation:

      title: r.title.map(|t| redactor.redact(&t)),
      cwd: r.cwd.map(|c| redactor.redact(&c)),

### Threat

Pane titles are set by whatever process the pane hosts. Agents that bake credentials into the title (e.g. `codex --api-key sk-ant-...` visible in `argv[0]` → terminal title) or workflows that `printf '\\e]0;token=\\\\a'` will leak those values through wa.state and ft robot state.

A peer MCP agent that calls wa.state as part of a normal swarm-wide health check receives the raw title; a network-exposed ft robot state call over a subprocess bridge does the same. Redaction was applied to the web /panes endpoint for this exact reason; the MCP and CLI peers must match.

### Fix

Two equivalent options:

Option A (one-line per call-site, web-matching): in the wa.state and ft robot state handlers, after `McpPaneState::from_pane_info` / `PaneState::from_pane_info`, run the fields through a static `Redactor`:

    let redactor = Redactor::new();
    for s in &mut states {
        if let Some(t) = s.title.as_mut() { *t = redactor.redact(t); }
        if let Some(c) = s.cwd.as_mut()   { *c = redactor.redact(c); }
    }

Option B: change the from_pane_info signatures to accept `&Redactor` and redact inside (symmetrical with web/handlers.rs:64-70).

Option A is smaller-diff and doesn't ripple through test fixtures; preferred.

### Acceptance Criteria

- wa.state envelope serializes title/cwd through Redactor::redact.
- ft robot state envelope serializes title/cwd through Redactor::redact.
- Regression test: seed a pane with title containing `sk-ant-api03-XXXX`, invoke both surfaces, assert the raw token does not appear in the response JSON.
- docs/security/read-path-redaction-matrix.md wa.state + ft robot state rows flip from `✗ LEAK` to `✓`.

### Why P1

Real leak on the default configuration — no operator opt-in required. Blast radius is narrow (titles/cwds, not pane scrollback) but automatic (fleet-wide state poll). Fix is mechanical.

Surfaced by RusticMeadow while landing ft-h8da2's audit matrix, 2026-04-23.

title: policy::RateLimiter::pane_counts leaks entries forever — no eviction on pane destroy or GC path
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:2076` — `RateLimiter.pane_counts: HashMap<(u64, ActionKind), Vec<Instant>>`. Every unique `(pane_id, action)` pair `check()` sees creates an entry. Nothing removes them.

A grep confirms it:

    $ rg 'pane_counts\.(remove|clear|retain)|fn gc|fn cleanup|fn prune_panes' crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs
    (no matches)

## Failure shape

On a long-running ft watcher with high pane churn (the 200+-pane fleet the project is designed for), every closed pane leaves a stale `(pane_id, action)` entry in `pane_counts` — one per ActionKind the pane ever touched. Over weeks those entries accumulate:

- Each entry holds a `Vec<Instant>` of up to `limit_per_pane` entries (default 60, configurable up to u32::MAX).
- After the sliding window expires, `prune_old` empties the Vec on the next `check()` — but only if check() is called with that (pane_id, action) again, which never happens for a destroyed pane.
- The entry itself is never removed, so the HashMap grows monotonically.

For 10k destroyed panes × 5 action kinds × 16B-per-Instant × 60-entries-peak = ~48 MB of leaked state. Not a crash, but a silent drift that scales with fleet uptime.

Global side (`global_counts: HashMap<ActionKind, Vec<Instant>>`) is BOUNDED by the finite ActionKind enum — not affected.

# Fix

Add two method shapes to `impl RateLimiter`:

1. `remove_pane(&mut self, pane_id: u64)` — iterate pane_counts, retain only keys whose first element ≠ pane_id. Called from the runtime's PaneDestroyed handler (same handler that already calls `remove_runtime_pane_state_for_pane` in runtime.rs:3574).

2. `gc(&mut self)` (or `gc_at(&mut self, now: Instant)` for testability) — iterate pane_counts, for each entry call prune_old with now-window as cutoff, drop the whole entry if the resulting Vec is empty. Safe opportunistic cleanup that catches panes closed without an explicit PaneDestroyed signal (crashes, abrupt detaches).

Also add operational telemetry: `pane_entries_evicted: u64` counter so operators can see the leak being managed.

Inline `#[cfg(test)]` in policy.rs:

- `rate_limiter_remove_pane_drops_all_action_entries_for_that_pane`
- `rate_limiter_remove_pane_leaves_other_panes_intact`
- `rate_limiter_gc_drops_expired_empty_entries`
- `rate_limiter_gc_preserves_still-active_entries`

# Severity

MEDIUM — leak is slow, bounded per pane, doesn't panic. But it's cumulative and silent. Fleet operators would only see the symptom as gradual RSS creep over uptime-weeks, attributed to anything-but-rate-limiter. Shipping the eviction path closes the hole before someone has to bisect it from production.

title: PlannerExtractionConfig bad denominators poison feature ranking
description:
Reality-check audit of planner feature extraction found config values can produce NaN/Inf impact and urgency scores, then degrade sorting to input order.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:96-114 exposes PlannerExtractionConfig max_unblock_count, max_critical_depth, max_staleness_hours, and weights as public fields with no validation in the extraction path.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:261-270 divides by max_unblock_count and max_critical_depth as f64, then combines with unchecked f64 weights. Zero denominators, NaN weights, or Inf weights can produce non-finite impact.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:132-138 stores staleness_hours as HashMap<String, f64>, and :291-302 divides those values by max_staleness_hours with no finite/non-negative checks.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:194-199 and :240-244 rank candidates using partial_cmp(...).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal), so non-finite composite scores silently become ties.
- crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_planner_features.rs:103-123 only generates safe positive denominators and 0.0..1.0 weights; :364-417 use fixed finite staleness values, so malformed config/context is untested.

Why it matters: a bad planner config or stale/corrupt staleness metric can poison extracted scores and make ready-bead ranking arbitrary or overly optimistic. The system should fail closed or normalize, not let NaN/Inf erase ranking signal.

Proposed remediation: add PlannerExtractionConfig validation/normalization before extraction. Require denominators to be finite and > 0 (or clamp to sane minima), require finite bounded weights, and sanitize staleness to finite >= 0. Add property tests for zero denominators, NaN/Inf max_staleness_hours, NaN/Inf weights, and NaN/negative staleness values.
close_reason: Fixed in 590a18611: PlannerExtractionConfig now normalizes zero denominators and non-finite/out-of-range extraction weights before feature extraction; staleness inputs are sanitized to finite non-negative values before urgency scoring. Added unit and proptest coverage for zero, NaN, +/-Inf, out-of-range weights, and negative/non-finite staleness producing bounded finite feature vectors. Verified: env FT_LOCAL_NOFORK=1 FT_LOCAL_TARGET=/tmp/ft-cod7-target scripts/cargo-local.sh check -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features passed. Targeted property test compile was blocked by unrelated lib-test errors in latency_stages.rs, recording.rs, runtime_telemetry.rs WIP, and storage/policy_decision_tests.rs.

title: mcp_middleware.rs: AuditedToolHandler::call does not enforce McpContext.cx Budget deadline — hanging inner tool blocks indefinitely with no audit row
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_middleware.rs:163-191`:

```rust
impl<T: ToolHandler> ToolHandler for AuditedToolHandler<T> {
    fn call(&self, ctx: &McpContext, arguments: serde_json::Value) -> McpResult<Vec<Content>> {
        let capacity_timer = ...;
        let start = Instant::now();
        let raw_args = arguments.clone();
        let result = self.inner.call(ctx, arguments);  // ← unbounded
        let (ok, error_code) = classify_tool_result(&result);
        record_mcp_audit_sync(&self.db_path, &self.tool_name, &raw_args, ok, error_code.as_deref(), elapsed_ms(start));
        capacity_timer.finish_result(&result);
        result
    }
}
```

## Defect
`McpContext.cx` (asupersync `Cx`) carries a `Budget` with a deadline. The audit wrapper does NOT enforce that deadline on `inner.call(...)`. If the inner tool is buggy or blocked on an unrelated mutex/IO and never returns:

- The wrapper's `call()` blocks indefinitely.
- `record_mcp_audit_sync` never runs — no audit row for the timeout.
- Capacity timer never finishes.
- Caller's request budget is silently violated.

This wrapper is the **sole audit point** for tool calls; if it doesn't enforce a timeout, the audit-completeness contract (every tool call → an audit row) breaks for the worst class of failure (hangs, the case operators most need to investigate).

## Production exposure
`AuditedToolHandler` wraps every tool registered through `compose_proxy_tools` (mcp_proxy.rs:312) when a db_path is configured. It also wraps native tool registrations in any path that constructs it. So every audited MCP tool call is exposed.

## Fix shape (option A — defer to inner)
Document that inner ToolHandler implementations MUST honor `ctx.cx.budget().deadline()` and bail with an error if exceeded. Add a CI lint that grep-detects long-blocking calls without deadline checks. Lighter touch but doesn't solve buggy inners.

## Fix shape (option B — wrapper enforces)
Promote `fn call` to `async fn call` (requires ToolHandler trait surgery) and wrap with `tokio::time::timeout(deadline, inner.call(...))`. On timeout, emit a Gap-equivalent audit row with `error_code="deadline_exceeded"` and return Err to caller. Bigger change.

## Fix shape (option C — separate watchdog)
Spawn a watchdog thread before `inner.call` that aborts the process or signals the inner if the deadline elapses. Heavyweight but works for sync inners.

Recommended: option A short-term + option B as a follow-up under a separate epic.

## Tests
- Mock ToolHandler that sleeps past the budget deadline.
- Assert wrapper returns Err within deadline + audit row exists with `error_code="deadline_exceeded"`.

## Class
P2 — audit-completeness gap on the worst failure class (hangs).
notes: Shipped option A++ (pre-flight Cx checkpoint). AuditedToolHandler::call now invokes ctx.cx().checkpoint() BEFORE inner.call. On Err (already-cancelled or budget-exhausted Cx), writes audit row with error_code='deadline_exceeded' + returns McpError::internal_error without invoking inner. Caller's budget no longer silently violated for this case + audit row always lands. Mid-call hangs still require option B (ToolHandler trait surgery: fn call → async fn call wrapped with tokio::time::timeout) — DEFERRED to separate epic since it ripples to every ToolHandler impl and is not bounded for one cycle. Regression test audited_tool_handler_bails_pre_flight_on_expired_cx_ft_ymn10 in mcp_middleware.rs::tests uses InnerCallObserver mock + Cx::for_testing_with_budget(Budget::new().with_deadline(Time::ZERO)); asserts wrapper returns Err AND inner.call's flag is NOT set. Lib check at test profile clean (cargo check -p frankenterm-core --lib --profile=test --no-default-features finished in 1m44s with 0 errors). Also fixed downstream proptest_headless_mux_server.rs ServerConfig literal (suspicion_threshold field added by ft-roacq, missed in earlier commit).

title: planner scorer accepts NaN scores as assignable
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs found planner scoring does not fail closed for non-finite inputs.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:19-35 documents PlannerFeatureVector scores as [0.0, 1.0], but the fields are public f64 values that can be deserialized or constructed as NaN/Inf.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:47-58 and :504-531 perform f64 arithmetic plus clamp without any finite validation before producing final_score.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:525 checks confidence < min_confidence_threshold; with NaN this comparison is false, so the candidate is not marked below_threshold.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:545-554 sorts with partial_cmp(...).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal), so unordered NaN scores silently collapse to tie/order input.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:725-728 checks final_score < min_score; with NaN this comparison is false, so solve_assignments can proceed to assignment.
- crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_planner_features.rs:126-162 and :196-213 generate only finite in-range features/config values, so this fail-open path is not covered.

Why it matters: planner inputs are serde-facing f64 structures and bad persisted/configured telemetry can make a candidate with NaN score bypass both scorer and solver thresholds. That undermines admission/ranking guarantees instead of rejecting the corrupted candidate.

Proposed remediation: add finite/range validation at scorer and solver boundaries. Treat NaN/Inf feature values, weights, thresholds, and final_score as fail-closed rejections (or normalize to score 0 before threshold checks). Add property tests explicitly covering f64::NAN, +/-Infinity, and out-of-range floats for score_candidates and solve_assignments.
notes: NaN/Inf fail-closed contract added to planner_features. PlannerFeatureVector::is_finite() and PlannerWeights::all_finite() check finite; score_candidates() forces final_score=0 + below_confidence_threshold=true when features/weights/thresholds are non-finite (also belt-and-braces clamps a non-finite raw final). New RejectionReason::NonFiniteScore variant emitted by solve_assignments() for hand-built ScoredCandidate with NaN/Inf final_score (catches callers that bypass score_candidates). Added 7 unit tests in planner_features.rs::tests covering single-field NaN/Inf permutations, NaN weights, hand-built scorer-report path, format helper. Added 3 proptests in proptest_planner_features.rs (96 cases each) pinning the universal contract: any single non-finite field flips is_finite to false; score_candidates fails closed for any non-finite field; solve_assignments emits NonFiniteScore for any non-finite final_score. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [truth][renderer-slo] Retain SSIM proof ledger outside ignored logs
description:
## Finding

`docs/perf/resize-quality-slo.json` and `docs/attestations/tui/render-parity.json` mark RQ-S13 SSIM parity as `retained_run_validated`, but the proof ledger and RCH meta paths point at `tests/e2e/logs/ssim_parity_release_gate_20260516T024353Z.*`. title: continuous_backpressure EwmaSmoother + sigmoid NaN poison cascade
description:
## Defect

Same NaN-poison pattern as ft-761tz (disk_pressure), in a sibling subsystem:
\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/continuous_backpressure.rs\`.

## Concrete failure path

1. Caller invokes \`ContinuousBackpressure::update(capture_ratio, write_ratio)\` where
   one ratio is \`NaN\`. Easy trigger: an external smoothed source that hit a div-by-zero
   guard upstream and quietly emitted NaN; or any test/consumer using \`observe_ratio\`
   directly.
2. Line 225-226: \`capture_ratio.clamp(0.0, 1.0)\` returns NaN — \`f64::clamp\` propagates
   NaN by design.
3. Line 228: \`self.capture_smoother.update(NaN)\`. \`EwmaSmoother::update\` (line 105)
   has **no NaN guard** — \`alpha.mul_add(NaN, ...)\` → NaN → \`self.value = NaN\`
   permanently. Every subsequent \`update()\` call preserves the NaN.
4. Line 231: \`smoothed_capture.max(smoothed_write)\` — \`f64::max\` does NOT propagate NaN
   under IEEE-754 (returns the non-NaN operand), but if both are NaN you get NaN.
5. Line 232-236: \`severity(NaN, _, _)\` → calls local \`sigmoid\` (line 140) which does
   \`x.clamp(-500.0, 500.0)\` — same NaN-propagation footgun. Returns NaN.
6. Line 232: \`self.current_severity = NaN\` permanently.
7. \`compute_actions\` (line 287-298) multiplies/mul_adds severity into
   \`poll_multiplier\`, \`pane_skip_fraction\`, \`detection_skip_fraction\`,
   \`buffer_limit_fraction\` — every field becomes NaN. ThrottleActions emitted to
   downstream throttle consumers are entirely poisoned.
8. \`BackpressureSnapshot\` (line 320) exposes \`severity\` and \`queue_ratio\` as
   \`f64\`. JSON serialization of NaN is invalid in strict JSON; \`serde_json\` emits
   \`null\` silently, corrupting telemetry payloads downstream.
9. Lucky accident: \`severity_to_tier(NaN)\` returns Black (NaN < x is always false,
   final else branch), so the discrete tier surface fails closed by IEEE-754
   coincidence rather than design. The continuous severity surface fails OPEN.

## Severity rationale

- Same class of silent wrong answer as ft-761tz.
- Continuous surface (severity, queue_ratio, ThrottleActions) fails OPEN — values
  become NaN, poll_multiplier becomes NaN, downstream throttle math becomes useless.
- Discrete \`equivalent_tier\` happens to fail closed by accident, not by design.
- Telemetry consumers (snapshot serialization) silently lose data.

## Fix sketch

1. \`EwmaSmoother::update\` (line 105) — if \`raw.is_nan()\`, return \`self.value\`
   without state change. Same defense as disk_pressure \`EwmaEstimator::update\`.
2. Local \`sigmoid\` (line 140) — short-circuit \`is_nan()\` to \`0.5\` like the
   backpressure_severity sibling does.
3. \`ContinuousBackpressure::update\` (line 224) — defense in depth: if either
   ratio is NaN, return \`current_actions()\` without state change.
4. Regression tests: pin each guard plus end-to-end NaN→Black-tier→clean recovery.

## Scope

\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/continuous_backpressure.rs\` only. No cross-crate API
changes. No changes to \`backpressure.rs\` or \`backpressure_severity.rs\`
(both already hardened).
close_reason: Landed in edab97f4 (fix(continuous_backpressure): NaN fail-closed across EmaSmoother, sigmoid, and update)

title: orphan_reaper misparses wezterm cli flag-value forms before subcommand
description:
parse_ps_line_if_reapable() finds the first non-flag token after `cli` and treats it as the subcommand.
That rejects valid invocations like `wezterm cli --config-file /tmp/x.toml list`, where `/tmp/x.toml` is a flag value, not the subcommand.
Result: legitimate short-lived helper processes can become unreapable if FrankenTerm or operators add value-taking CLI flags before the real subcommand.
Tightest fix: teach the parser to skip known value-taking flags (or parse argv shape more robustly) before matching against REAPABLE_SUBCOMMANDS.
close_reason: Parser now accepts wezterm cli value-taking flags before reapable subcommands; compiled allowlist check fixed.

title: [redraw_predicate_telemetry.audit] Asymmetric counter paths in is_safe — clarify intent
description:
Architectural ambiguity surfaced in the is_safe sweep (the same sweep that found ft-ismxr + ft-05poz).

## Concern

crates/frankenterm-core/src/redraw_predicate_telemetry.rs:241-247:

    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        self.evaluations_total == 0 || self.meets_idle_skip_rq()
    }

The short-circuit returns true when evaluations_total == 0, but the struct has TWO independent counter paths:

1. fold_decision increments evaluations_total + paints_total/skips_total (the predicate path).
2. record_os_paint_consumption + record_force_paint populate BTreeMap counters but do NOT touch evaluations_total.

Concrete state where is_safe returns true but the system has activity:

    let mut h = RedrawDecisionHealth::default();
    record_os_paint_consumption(&mut h, source);
    record_force_paint(&mut h, signal);
    // h.evaluations_total = 0
    // h.os_paint_consumptions has 1 entry
    // h.force_paint_counters has 1 entry
    assert!(h.is_safe());  // returns true via the short-circuit

## Two interpretations

A. Bug: paint signals firing without predicate evaluations is a contract violation; is_safe should reject.

B. Feature: the BTreeMap counters are pure observability surfaces; only the predicate path gates safety.

Without knowing the architectural intent, I refused to ship a unilateral fix. Reading A or B should be made explicit in code + test.

## Action requested

Document the intent. If A: tighten is_safe to also check that the BTreeMaps are empty when evaluations_total == 0. If B: update the docstring to spell out 'pure observability — does not gate is_safe'.

## Context: this is NOT a unique pattern

This is the only ambiguous case from a 19-method is_safe sweep this review pass:

- 5 fixed: ft-ftepl, ft-vgtab, ft-cof0r (policy substring), ft-ismxr (lock), ft-05poz (osc1337).
- 14 verified safe by structure.
- 1 architectural ambiguity (this).

Same shape as ft-trdku in approval.rs (also reclassified from bug to design-intent task).
close_reason: Interpretation A applied at 08c13d06e: is_safe now rejects the state where evaluations_total == 0 but force_paint_counters or os_paint_consumptions are non-empty (paint signals firing without a predicate evaluation = contract violation, must surface as unsafe). 4 regression tests pin the new behavior; existing tests pass. All 29 redraw_predicate_telemetry::tests:: green.

title: policy.rs + mcp_tools.rs silently drop audit decision_context on serde failure (5 sites)
description:
Five sites silently drop the audit row decision_context field on serde_json serialization failure: policy.rs:6458-6462 Allowed, 6485-6489 Denied, 6512-6516 RequiresApproval, 6539-6543 Error; mcp_tools.rs:678-686 serialize_mcp_audit_decision_context (4 callers at 5782/5972/6154/6202). All 5 use serde_json::to_string(ctx).inspect_err(|e| tracing::warn!(...)).ok() — log on Err, return None.

The audit row decision_context column ends up NULL on failure. Operators have a tracing::warn but no counter to surface the rate of silent fidelity loss. The audit chain tamper-evidence relies on decision_context being present for forensic replay; a NULL decision_context defeats that for the affected row.

In practice serde on DecisionContext rarely fails (composed of primitives + Vec<EvidenceEntry>), but the absorption pattern is a code smell and the observability gap is real.

Fix shape: add policy_decision_context_serde_drop_count AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset; bump at all 5 sites alongside the existing tracing::warn. Mirror POLICY_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT and MCP_CLOCK_ANOMALY_COUNT (br-ft-rnpuc).

Cross-references: ft-rnpuc same shape, ft-jyywz audit-chain export drop counter, ft-fp6st policy regex.

title: [reality-gap] ft robot checkpoint/context/work/fleet/profile families return robot.not_implemented
description:
# Claim (README)

README.md:37-38 markets "**Robot Mode API**: JSON/TOON interface
optimized for AI agents to control other AI agents" as a core value
prop — "the closest analogy is Kubernetes for terminal-based AI
agents". This is not a footnote; it's in the opening paragraph.

# Reality (code)

Five of the `ft robot` subcommand families are CLI-parsed but
backend-unimplemented. At `crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs`:

    :22632   RobotCommands::Checkpoint { command } => {
    :22691   RobotCommands::Context    { command } => {
    :22738   RobotCommands::Work       { command } => {
    :22816   RobotCommands::Fleet      { command } => {
    :22876   RobotCommands::Profile    { command } => {

Each arm builds a `RobotNtmCommand`, then calls
`build_ntm_not_implemented_response(&ntm_cmd, elapsed_ms(start))`
(main.rs:10121) which emits a `robot.not_implemented` envelope with:

    "Command `ft robot <family> <action>` is recognized but not yet
     implemented. This command will be available in a future release.
     NTM equivalent: <command>."

So the CLI surface is real, the arg parsing is real, the response
envelope is real — the backend is missing. The "NTM equivalent"
pointer is the current workaround (operator shells out to `ntm`).

# Scope

Subcommands covered by this gap (15+ concrete actions):

- Checkpoint: save, rollback, list
- Context: status, rotate, history
- Work: claim, complete, status, list
- Fleet: status, launch, stop, describe
- Profile: show, list, set

Working `ft robot` surfaces (NOT covered by this gap): state,
trigger, approve — those DO have real backends.

# Gap severity

- README treats Robot Mode as a pillar feature.
- Users following the opening paragraph to `ft robot fleet launch ...`
  get a `robot.not_implemented` envelope at first invocation.
- JSON envelope shape IS honest (structured error code, clear
  message, NTM pointer) — the UX is "recognized but unshipped,"
  not "silently wrong."
- The honest error makes this a DOCS gap more than a correctness
  bug. Priority is for a README disclosure, not an urgent code fix.

# Recommended disposition

Either:
  (a) Add a clear "Currently implemented" subtable under the Robot
      Mode API heading, listing which families ship real backends
      vs. return `robot.not_implemented` (documentation-first,
      1-line-README change, ships today); OR
  (b) Split this into 5 implementation beads (one per family) and
      track them to close. `br` already contains `wa-rsaf` epic and
      the ft-xbnl0 goal-line epic — family-level subbeads would
      hang under one of those.

(a) is the immediate unblocker; (b) is the real closure path.
close_reason: Landed docs fix (disposition (a)) in 0e1432fc. Added 'Implementation status' subsection under Robot Mode API heading listing all 13 families — 8 shipped, 5 pending with use-ntm pointer. Verified each pending family (checkpoint/context/work/fleet/profile) against main.rs:22632-22879 build_ntm_not_implemented_response routing. The 5 pending implementations themselves remain under wa-rsaf.

title: session_restore::load_checkpoint_by_id silently accepts mux_pane_state row count ≠ stored pane_count
description:
# Defect

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/session_restore.rs:473-481` returns `CheckpointData { pane_count, pane_states }` where:

* `pane_count` is the value stored in `session_checkpoints.pane_count` at save time (stored claim).
* `pane_states` is the rows actually loaded from `mux_pane_state WHERE checkpoint_id = ?1` (actual rows).

Nothing in the load path asserts these match. Line 1204-1205 logs both counts but does not fail on disagreement. Post-ft-ybtyg, the state_hash at `session_checkpoints.state_hash` covers `(session_id, pane_id_map, checkpoint_at)` — NOT the contents or row count of `mux_pane_state`. So:

* Adding a bogus `mux_pane_state` row (checkpoint_id matches) → `pane_states.len() > pane_count`, hash recomputes correctly (unchanged inputs), load accepts the extra row silently.
* Removing a legitimate `mux_pane_state` row → `pane_states.len() < pane_count`, same as above.

A subsequent restore step reconstructs panes from `pane_states`, so an extra row creates a pane that was never in the session, and a missing row silently drops a pane.

# Threat model

DB-write is already fatal, so this is hardening against:
1. Naive filesystem-level tampering (e.g., hostile repo ships a crafted `ft.db` for operator to open).
2. Accidental corruption (storage layer bug drops rows or writes orphan rows, and restore produces non-sensical state with no loud failure).
3. Upgrade drift (checkpoint_id collision between pre-/post-migration rows causes stale rows to get bundled into a new checkpoint's load).

# Fix

In `load_checkpoint_by_id`, after loading `pane_states`, assert `pane_states.len() == pane_count` and return `RestoreError::CorruptCheckpoint` with a descriptive message otherwise. Cost: one integer comparison per load.

The fix does NOT close the more comprehensive gap (hash doesn't cover mux_pane_state CONTENT, only count/identity of rows), but it's a high-signal cheap check that catches naive tampering and accidental drift.

# Regression tests

Two symmetric tests:

* `load_checkpoint_rejects_added_pane_state_row`: create a legit checkpoint, then INSERT an extra `mux_pane_state` row with the same checkpoint_id, call `load_checkpoint_by_id`, assert `CorruptCheckpoint`.

* `load_checkpoint_rejects_deleted_pane_state_row`: same, but DELETE one of the rows, assert `CorruptCheckpoint`.

# Severity

MEDIUM — no crash, no data loss on the happy path. Silent wrong-answer on the tampered/corrupt path. Cheap to fix; closes the detection window between state_hash (which covers the pane_id_map) and the separate mux_pane_state table (which the hash does not cover).
close_reason: Withdrawn: the count-mismatch assertion would false-positive in the real write flow where finalize_restore writes session_checkpoints.pane_count BEFORE a separate capture step writes the mux_pane_state rows. load_checkpoint_by_id is a read path that can legitimately see pane_states.len()=0 while pane_count>0 in that window. Re-examine at a higher layer (is the hash scope wrong? is there a two-phase atomicity guarantee?) rather than the naive row-count check I drafted.

description:
Successor to ft-kscfg subset 1. The file format substrate shipped at crates/frankenterm-core/src/scrollback_mmap_format.rs (ScrollbackHeader + RecordHeader + RecordKind + decode/encode + 17 round-trip tests). This bead wires that format into a working mmap-backed write path.

Scope:
1. New module crates/frankenterm-core/src/scrollback_mmap_writer.rs that:
   - Opens / creates ~/.local/share/ft/scrollback/<pane_uuid>.bin (0600)
   - Maintains the .bin.lock flock for owner identity
   - Maps the file (mmap2 crate or memmap2; respects #![forbid(unsafe_code)] via a vetted wrapper)
   - Implements MmapScrollback::append(payload) — runs redactor first, writes a RecordHeader + payload at write_cursor_bytes, increments cursor with wrap-around, opportunistic msync(MS_ASYNC).
   - Flush boundary: every N appends OR every M ms, msync(MS_SYNC) + bump last_msync_at_epoch_ms in the header.
2. Wire MmapScrollback::append into the ingest pipeline at the same site where the in-memory ring is updated (currently crates/frankenterm-core/src/ingest.rs). The in-memory ring stays as the read-side fast path; mmap is the durability sink.
3. Per-pane size cap enforcement (configurable; default 50MB). Honor StorageConfig.scrollback_mmap_cap_mb when set.
4. Integration test: write N records, msync, drop the writer, re-open via the recovery path, assert byte-for-byte equality of pre-msync bytes.

Acceptance:

- Per-pane scrollback file exists at the documented path with mode 0600.
- Redactor applied before write (verified by a known-secret-pattern test).
- Configurable size cap honored.

title: [ARCH/§9.4-sketching] replace flat-buffer Histogram with t-digest for bounded-error tail percentiles
description:
Phase-3 alien-graveyard match: §9.4 Sketching (t-digest / HDR Histogram) for runtime/telemetry domain.

## Symptom

`crate::telemetry::Histogram` (telemetry.rs:299) is a flat sample buffer. Two issues:

1. **O(n) shift on overflow** — fixed inline today via VecDeque substitution (substrate prelude).
2. **No bounded-error tail accuracy** — `quantile()` clones samples + sorts on every call (O(n log n) per p99 read). Sample retention is bounded but quantile estimates depend entirely on which samples survive eviction. For a 1000-sample buffer at 1000 samples/sec, p99 reflects only the most recent ~1 second of traffic; a brief burst that fills the buffer dominates the estimate forever after.

## Algorithm

§9.4 from the alien-graveyard catalog: t-digest (Dunning 2014) or HDR Histogram (Tene).

- **t-digest**: O(log k) update + O(log k) query, k = compression parameter (~100). Bounded-error guarantee: |t_digest.quantile(q) - exact.quantile(q)| / exact.quantile(q) ≤ ε for ε ~ 1/k at the tails (much tighter at p99 than at the median, which matches the use case — we care about p99 + p99.9 for tail-risk decisions).
- **HDR Histogram**: O(1) update + O(buckets) query. Configurable precision (typically 0.1-1% relative error). More memory than t-digest but faster updates.

t-digest is the better match for SwarmCapacityCertificate's tail-risk lens (it's literally optimized for the tail). The `tdigest` crate exists in the Rust ecosystem; pure-Rust, MIT-licensed, no_std-compatible.

## Integration point

`crate::telemetry::Histogram` (telemetry.rs:299) is the only sample-buffer histogram in the runtime stack. Used by SwarmCapacityStageMetrics for service_time / wait_time / retry_latency / queue_depth.

Two integration shapes:

A. **Drop-in replacement**: change `samples: VecDeque<f64>` → `digest: TDigest`. Public surface preserved (record / quantile / p50/p95/p99 / mean / merge_from / summary). Risk: small numerical differences in computed quantiles vs the prior exact-from-buffer answers; some test fixtures may assert exact values.

B. **Sibling type**: new `crate::telemetry::TDigestHistogram` for hot paths; keep `Histogram` for cold paths. Less risk; more API surface to maintain.

Recommend (A) since the public surface stays the same + the prior bounded-buffer was already approximate.

## Proof obligations

1. Bounded-error regression test: assert |t_digest.quantile(0.99) - exact.quantile(0.99)| / exact.quantile(0.99) < 0.01 for a representative input distribution (lognormal — service times are lognormal-shaped per literature).

2. Merge-correctness test: t_digest.merge_from(other) must be associative and commutative, otherwise SwarmCapacityCertificate aggregation across stages would be order-dependent.

3. Memory bound: assert that a t-digest with compression=100 fits in <16KB regardless of insertion count, even after merging 1000 source digests.

## Fallback

Keep the VecDeque-backed Histogram (today's substrate prelude) as the default for `max_samples ≤ 256` where bounded-buffer cost is acceptable + deterministic exact-quantile is a feature. Use t-digest only for hot paths where `max_samples > 1024`.

## EV scoring

Impact 4 (correct tail-percentile estimates unlock SwarmCapacityCertificate's tail-risk decisions) × Confidence 4 (t-digest is well-known + tested) × Reuse 3 (Histogram is used at ~10 sites)  / Effort 3 (substrate replacement + test rewrite) × AdoptionFriction 2 (pure-Rust crate, drop-in API)
= 48 / 6 = 8.0 → Tier S.

## Cross-references

- See cc1's alien-uplift map: ~/.claude/.../project_alien_uplift_runtime_2026_05_03.md (Match 1).
- VecDeque substrate prelude shipped today at $(commit hash filled in this commit).
- ft-eeuaf (open) — telemetry write-side wiring gap; once that lands, this bead's measurement bench has data to chew on.

description:
# Continuation: floating-panes GUI integration

## Context
ft-mpc9b.4.2 retired at substrate scope (commit 4e3305b82):
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/floating_panes.rs ships PanePosition (Tiled / Floating(Rect)), FloatingRect with overlaps/contains, FloatingZStack with monotonic-lane raise/lower/raise_to_top/lower_to_bottom/cycle_among_overlapping, DragResizeState machine (Idle/Dragging/Resizing with begin/update/commit/cancel), 8-handle ResizeHandle enum, snap_target Aero-snap classifier + apply_snap geometry, KeyboardCommand enumerating 19 a11y-required keyboard equivalents, FloatingPaneA11yMessage payload.
- 43 inline tests passing.

## What this bead carries

### Pane abstraction extension
- Add `position: PanePosition` field to the gui's Pane struct
- `frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/pane.rs` updates: tiled panes default to `PanePosition::Tiled` (no behaviour change); new `set_floating(rect)` and `pin_to_tiled()` methods toggle the discriminator
- Per-window `FloatingZStack` lives in `RenderState`; tracks all floating panes for the window

### Layer 2 compositor integration (cross-link ft-mpc9b.4.1)
- Floating panes render in Layer 2 (FloatingPanes) of the LayerStack
- Painter walks `zstack.iter_back_to_front()` and renders each pane at its `FloatingRect` position
- Tiled panes continue to render in Layer 1 (TiledGrid) unchanged

### Mouse hit-testing
- `frankenterm-gui/src/termwindow/render/paint.rs` mouse handler:
  - Walk floating panes top-down; first overlapping pane handles the event
  - Title-bar grab → `DragResizeState::begin_drag`
  - 8 corner/edge hot zones → `DragResizeState::begin_resize` with the appropriate `ResizeHandle`
  - Live preview during drag/resize → render the snapped target if `snap_target` returns `Some(edge)`
  - Mouse-up → `commit()`; Esc during op → `cancel()`
  - Alt-click → `zstack.cycle_among_overlapping(focused, x, y, |id| pane_rect(id))`

### Keyboard handler
- Default keymap (operator-overridable in frankenterm.toml):
  - Cmd+Shift+Arrow → `KeyboardCommand::Move{Direction}` → 1-cell move
  - Cmd+Ctrl+Arrow → `KeyboardCommand::{Grow,Shrink}{Axis}` → 1-cell resize on bottom-right corner
  - Cmd+Ctrl+P → `TogglePin`
  - Cmd+Ctrl+] / [ → `RaiseOne` / `LowerOne`
  - Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+] / [ → `RaiseToTop` / `LowerToBottom`

title: [conformance] MCP spec MUST/SHOULD coverage matrix is missing — clauses tested by ad-hoc tests, not enumerated
description:
## The gap

`docs/mcp-api-spec.md` enumerates explicit MUST/SHOULD/REQUIRED
clauses (3 of them at HEAD: data-shape MUST, side-effects-policy MUST,
resources-readonly MUST) plus implicit shape requirements scattered
across the document. The conformance skill requires:

> Coverage Accounting Matrix (Mandatory) — Before claiming
> conformance, prove it: every MUST/SHOULD clause enumerated, with
> a Pass / Total score per spec section.

There is no such matrix. The 5+ `mcp_conformance*.rs` test files
collectively cover most of the surface, but nobody can answer the
question:

> "Which spec MUST clauses are NOT enforced by a test?"

…without re-reading the spec end to end.

## What exists today

- `tests/mcp_conformance.rs`, `mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs`,
  `mcp_conformance_additional_tools.rs`,
  `mcp_conformance_mission_tx.rs`,
  `mcp_conformance_rules_test.rs` (>100 KB combined).
- `tests/mcp_manifest_golden.rs` + `conformance_mcp_manifest.rs`.
- `metamorphic_robot_envelope_canon.rs`.

These cover *behavior*. They don't index back to the spec. There's
no annotation linking a test to "this enforces clause X of section Y
of mcp-api-spec.md".

## Why this catches real defects (skill criterion)

The skill's coverage-matrix rule exists for exactly this reason: when
a new MUST clause is added to the spec, nothing makes it visible that
no test covers it. Today, when `docs/mcp-api-spec.md` grows a new
section (e.g., "tool calls MUST emit a structured `error_code` from
the documented enum on failure"), there is no mechanism that surfaces
the gap before a release.

This is not the same as the runtime envelope validator (ft-5ikbd) —
that one enforces *one* MUST (`data MUST match the schema`). This bead
covers the meta-question: how do we know we have all the MUSTs?

## Suggested implementation

1. **Enumerate MUSTs** — `docs/mcp-api-spec-coverage.md` tracks
   clauses with stable IDs:
   ```
   | ID         | Section            | Level    | Clause                          | Tested by                          |
   |------------|--------------------|----------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------|
   | MCP-V1-001 | Response Envelope  | MUST     | data matches docs/json-schema/   | tests/conformance_robot_envelope_schema.rs (ft-5ikbd) |
   | MCP-V1-002 | Tool Calls         | MUST     | side-effects route via PolicyEngine | tests/mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs::policy_gate_test |
   | MCP-V1-003 | Resources          | MUST     | read-only, no side effects       | tests/mcp_resources::*::no_side_effects |
   | MCP-V1-004 | Versioning         | MUST     | mcp_version=v1 in every envelope | tests/mcp_conformance.rs::envelope_version |
   | ...        | ...                | ...      | ...                              | ...                                |
   ```

2. **Test annotation convention**:
   ```rust
   /// MCP Spec: enforces MCP-V1-001 (data matches docs/json-schema/).
   #[test]
   fn data_field_conforms_to_robot_state_schema() { ... }
   ```

3. **Coverage report generator** (`tests/conformance_mcp_coverage.rs`):
   - Parses `docs/mcp-api-spec-coverage.md`.
   - Greps test files for the `MCP-Vx-NNN` annotation.
   - Asserts every clause has at least one test annotation.
   - Prints a Markdown table of `(clause, tests, level)` to stdout
     for upload as a CI artifact (per skill: compliance report on
     every PR).

4. **CI gate**: when `docs/mcp-api-spec.md` grows a new MUST/SHOULD
   line, `mcp-api-spec-coverage.md` must be updated in the same PR.

## Out of scope

- Adding tests for clauses that turn out to be unenforced (those
  become individual follow-on beads filed by the matrix).
- Mechanically extracting MUSTs from prose (the matrix is curated;
  prose extraction is a separate research-grade problem).

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/mcp-api-spec-coverage.md` exists with one row per spec MUST/
  SHOULD clause and the test that enforces it.
- `cargo test -p frankenterm-core --test conformance_mcp_coverage`
  fails when a clause has no annotated test.
- The coverage report is uploaded as a CI artifact on every PR (a CI
  workflow change tracks this requirement).

## References

- Skill section "Coverage Accounting Matrix (Mandatory)"
- `docs/mcp-api-spec.md`
- All existing `mcp_conformance*.rs` test files in
  `crates/frankenterm-core/tests/`

Filed by cc_1 conformance audit, 2026-04-28.
close_reason: MCP coverage matrix shipped at 365cb16f1. docs/mcp-api-spec-coverage.md enumerates 6 clauses (5 TESTED, 1 DEFERRED) with stable IDs, status, spec-line refs, and per-clause test references. tests/conformance_mcp_coverage.rs is the 3-test CI gate (matrix-presence, missing-annotation, orphan-annotation checks). Three existing tests annotated: conformance_robot_envelope_schema.rs (MCP-V1-001, MCP-V1-005), mcp_conformance.rs::resource_catalog (MCP-V1-004, MCP-V1-006), mcp_conformance_core_tools.rs::wa_send (MCP-V1-003). One DEFERRED clause (MCP-V1-002) filed as a follow-up since wa.workflow_status is not yet registered as an MCP tool. Regression-injection meta-test confirmed: appending a fake TESTED row with no annotation flips the gate red. Future PRs that add a MUST line to mcp-api-spec.md without updating the matrix + adding an annotation will fail CI on this gate.

title: [ft-cfg-drift-agent-detection] README documents [agent_detection] block but Config silently drops it
description:
## Drift surfaced by ft-2sumi

`tests/conformance_ft_config_schema.rs` (the schema golden landed in
ft-2sumi) flagged this drift while running its
`unreachable_documented_sections_remain_unreachable` XFAIL gate.

## What the README says

`README.md`'s `## Configuration` block (around line 730) documents:

```toml
[agent_detection]
# Agent pane state detection thresholds (milliseconds)
enabled = true
active_output_threshold_ms = 5000
thinking_silence_ms = 5000
stuck_silence_ms = 30000
idle_silence_ms = 60000
```

## What the code does

`crates/frankenterm-core/src/config.rs:42` defines `Config` with 22+
sub-section fields (`general`, `ingest`, `storage`, `gc`, `backup`,
`sync`, `distributed`, `patterns`, `workflows`, `safety`, `vendored`,
`ipc`, `native`, `metrics`, `notifications`, `mcp_client`,
`backpressure`, `cli`, `snapshots`, `search`, `tuning`). **No
`agent_detection` field.**

`AgentDetectionConfig` exists in
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/agent_pane_state.rs:74` and its doc
comment claims it "maps to the `[agent_detection]` section in
`frankenterm.toml`" — but it is never wired to the main `Config`
struct.

When an operator copies the README's canonical block into their
`ft.toml`, default serde drops the entire `[agent_detection]` block
silently and ft falls back to its compiled-in defaults. The operator
sees no error.

## Reproduction

```bash
$ cargo test -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features \
    --test conformance_ft_config_schema -- coverage_inventory_is_visible
...
  [agent_detection  ] XFAIL → tracked in ft-cfg-drift-agent-detection
```

The XFAIL gate `unreachable_documented_sections_remain_unreachable`
in the same test file pins this drift state. Closing this bead
requires moving `agent_detection` from `README_DOCUMENTED_BUT_UNREACHABLE`
to `README_DOCUMENTED_SECTIONS` in that test once the wiring lands.

## Fix options

A. **Wire `AgentDetectionConfig` into `Config` as `pub agent_detection:
   AgentDetectionConfig`** with `#[serde(default)]`. The struct + types
   exist; only the field declaration + a `Default::default()` row are
   needed. Honors the README contract.

B. **Remove the `[agent_detection]` block from the README.** The
   thresholds may be operator-tunable through a different mechanism
   (env vars? a sibling config file?). Document that path instead.

Option A is the right call if `agent_detection` thresholds are
production-tunable — the doc comment in `agent_pane_state.rs:72`
strongly suggests they were intended to be.

## Acceptance

- `Config` struct has an `agent_detection: AgentDetectionConfig` field
  (or the README block is removed).
- `tests/conformance_ft_config_schema.rs::unreachable_documented_sections_remain_unreachable`
  fires its `[XFAIL→PASS]` log and the test array is updated.
- All 9 tests in that suite pass green.

Filed by ft-2sumi (cc_1) reality-check pipeline, 2026-04-28.

title: Mission loop stores raw unbounded external trigger payloads
description:
Reality-check audit finding in crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs.

Evidence:
- MissionTrigger::ExternalSignal carries raw source and payload strings at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:52-53.
- MissionLoopState stores pending_triggers as a Vec at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:414-416.
- trigger() appends every trigger with no queue cap and no payload size/redaction limit at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:516-518.
- should_evaluate only observes len >= max_trigger_batch at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:534-540; it does not bound trigger() itself, so callers can grow memory until tick/evaluate is called.
- tick() clones the most recent pending trigger into the decision at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:557-563, and evaluate stores that trigger inside MissionDecision and last_decision at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:718-727.
- The serde roundtrip test only checks a benign "{}" external payload at crates/frankenterm-core/src/mission_loop.rs:3439-3447.

Why it matters:
External webhook/CI payloads often contain bearer tokens, URLs, or large blobs. The mission loop preserves those strings in pending state and last_decision/reportable state, and a burst of external signals can also allocate unbounded memory before the next tick.

Proposed remediation:
Change ExternalSignal storage to a bounded/redacted summary: source, payload_hash, byte_len, and optionally a small redacted preview. Store pending triggers in a bounded VecDeque or drop/coalesce by source when over limit. Add tests for large payload truncation, secret-like payload redaction, and trigger burst bounds.
notes: Bounded external trigger payload + queue depth. trigger() now applies redact_trigger_payload helper that truncates ExternalSignal::payload to MAX_EXTERNAL_TRIGGER_PAYLOAD_BYTES=2048 (UTF-8 boundary respected; truncation marker carries br-ft-zdpou + original byte length for forensic queries). Queue cap MAX_PENDING_TRIGGERS=256 enforced via drop-oldest pattern (preserves tick()'s most-recent-trigger semantics). Other trigger variants (ManualTrigger, BeadStatusChange, etc.) pass through unchanged. Added 4 tests: trigger_truncates_oversized_external_payload_ft_zdpou (10KB payload -> truncated <2148 bytes with breadcrumb + 'original 10000 bytes' marker), trigger_preserves_under_cap_external_payload_ft_zdpou (sanity: small payloads not modified), trigger_truncation_respects_utf8_boundary_ft_zdpou (1024 4-byte char crab emojis -> valid UTF-8 after truncation), trigger_queue_drops_oldest_when_at_cap_ft_zdpou (burst of MAX+50 triggers leaves exactly MAX with the newest at the tail). Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: ft-2okh0.7: LiveResize wake-override forces 60+ fps on low-refresh displays — use display_max not max(60)
description: adaptive_fps.rs select_decision LiveResize override returns target_fps = snapshot.display_max_fps.max(WAKE_OVERRIDE_FPS) where WAKE_OVERRIDE_FPS=60. On a 30Hz display, this returns max(30,60)=60 — forcing the substrate to recommend 60 fps on a 30Hz display. Integration's renderer would either clamp (wasted work) or attempt (impossible). Likely intent: target_fps = snapshot.display_max_fps directly (use the full display rate during resize for smoothness; on low-refresh displays, that's the actual cap). Tracked under self-review pass.
close_reason: Won't fix — re-reading the existing test 'live_resize_override_floors_at_60_when_display_max_lower' confirms the 60-floor is deliberate design. Trade-off: on a 30Hz display, rendering at 60 fps means input sampling at 60 Hz (smoother mouse tracking during resize) at the cost of 2x GPU work with half-thrown-away frames. Substrate matches design intent. Closing as wont-fix; reverted my change.

title: mcp_framework.rs: build_loader falls back to /dev/null when discovery is unconfigured — non-portable + silent
description:
## Site
`crates/frankenterm-core/src/mcp_framework.rs:166-190` in `build_loader`:

```rust
// If default paths are disabled and no custom paths are provided,
// return a loader pointing to a nonexistent path to ensure it finds nothing,
// rather than panicking. (The caller should ideally guard against this).
return FrameworkConfigLoader::from_path("/dev/null");
```

## Defects

### 1. Non-portable path
`/dev/null` exists on macOS / Linux / BSD but NOT on Windows. The frankenterm crate doesn't currently target Windows, but:
- The `mcp-client` feature is portable; nothing else in mcp_framework requires Unix.
- A future Windows port (or any operator running under WSL with mixed paths) hits this landmine silently.
- The comment in the code itself ("The caller should ideally guard against this") acknowledges the path is a workaround.

### 2. Silent fallback
The branch returns the loader without logging. Operators who:
- Set `mcp_client.include_default_paths = false`
- Forget to populate `mcp_client.discovery_paths`

...get an MCP server with zero discovered remotes and NO indication anything went wrong. The downstream `compose_proxy_tools` early-exit ("no remote MCP servers selected") emits a warn — but it can't distinguish "genuinely no servers configured" from "misconfigured loader fell back to /dev/null".

### 3. No counter
Discovery misconfiguration silently degrades the proxy surface. The existing `MCP_PROXY_MOUNT_FAILURES` (br-ft-8na0z + br-ft-59hlx) covers downstream mount/discovery failures but doesn't catch loader misconfiguration upstream.

## Fix shape

### Minimal (recommended for this ship)
Replace `/dev/null` with a platform-portable guaranteed-nonexistent path:

```rust
let placeholder = std::env::temp_dir()
    .join("__ft_mcp_unconfigured_loader_no_op__");
tracing::warn!(
    target: "ft::mcp_framework",
    event = "mcp_framework_loader_unconfigured",
    placeholder = %placeholder.display(),
    "mcp_client.include_default_paths=false with no discovery_paths; \
     loader will discover zero servers. Set discovery_paths or enable \
     include_default_paths."
);
return FrameworkConfigLoader::from_path(placeholder);
```

### Stronger (follow-up)
Return `Result<FrameworkConfigLoader, ConfigError>` — make misconfiguration a fail-loud error rather than a silent zero-discovery.

## Class
P3 portability + observability. The path is unreachable in practice on supported platforms but the code shape is a future-Windows-port landmine and the silent fallback degrades observability.
close_reason: Shipped at a9aed94b7: replaced /dev/null with std::env::temp_dir().join("__ft_mcp_unconfigured_loader_no_op__") in build_loader. Platform-portable + sentinel suffix for operator inspection. Added tracing::warn at target ft::mcp_framework with event mcp_framework_loader_unconfigured so misconfiguration is observable without log-scraping the downstream compose_proxy_tools call site. New test ft_zfbqo_unconfigured_loader_returns_empty_on_any_platform pins three invariants: empty server list, no path under /dev/, temp_dir+sentinel placeholder in search_paths. cargo check --lib --features mcp-client clean (30.47s, 0 errors). Two related findings filed in the cycle remain open: ft-bd3vr (per-call deadline propagation gap) + ft-dnzum (no explicit lifecycle disconnect).

title: [mock-code-finder][incident] Collect proof_rch_evidence without running new proof
description:
## Finding

title: [Audit] workflows::engine::WorkflowDecision::parse silently drops malformed serialized decisions
description:
PHASE 3 AUDIT — silent serde drop in workflows::engine::WorkflowDecision::parse.

Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/workflows/engine.rs:732

```rust
#[must_use]
pub fn parse(serialized: &str) -> Option<Self> {
    serde_json::from_str(serialized).ok()
}
```

Workflow decisions are persisted then re-parsed for replay/audit. A malformed serialized decision parses to None, and downstream callers can't distinguish "decision did not exist" from "decision existed but was schema-skewed". That's an audit-fidelity defect: the replay machinery loses the decision record without signal.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-ncijf, ft-k6uwb.

Remediation:
1. Add `WORKFLOW_DECISION_PARSE_DROP_COUNT` AtomicU64 (or fold into existing workflows_serde_drop_count from ft-zkthg if scope matches — check first).
2. Replace `.ok()` with explicit match: bump counter + emit structured tracing::warn with `error = %err`, `serialized_len = serialized.len()`.
3. 3-4 unit tests + 1 proptest.

Caution: scope-check ft-zkthg's existing workflows_serde_drop_count before adding a parallel counter.
notes: Replaced .ok() in WorkflowDecision::parse with explicit match. New WORKFLOWS_PARSE_DROP_COUNT counter (separate from ft-zkthg's WORKFLOWS_SERDE_DROP_COUNT which is the serialize/write path) — operators can now distinguish writer-side schema drift (serde counter) from downstream consumer schema drift (parse counter), with different operator responses (fix writer vs upgrade consumer). Pub fn workflows_parse_drop_count() observability surface + cfg(test) reset helper + record_workflows_parse_drop(serialized_len, error) inline that bumps + emits structured tracing::warn at target ft.workflows.audit with serialized_len + error %display + br-ft-zhnaw breadcrumb. Added 3 tests: starts_at_zero_after_reset, bumps_on_malformed_decision (2 calls -> count=2), independent_of_serde_drop_counter (parse-side bump doesn't spill into write-side counter, mirrors ft-k6uwb pattern). Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-k6uwb, ft-0n4nx, ft-crpvd. Lib check clean -p frankenterm-core --no-default-features.

title: [AUDIT/SAFETY] 15 sites use serde_json::to_string/to_value/from_*.unwrap_or_default() — silent failure pattern (ft-jyywz sibling-class)
description:
PHASE 3 PROJECT-WIDE ANALYSIS — sibling-class to ft-jyywz
(audit_chain export drop counter, closed at dc5b42a8c). Same
pattern: \`unwrap_or_default()\` on a \`Result<T, serde_json::Error>\`
silently absorbs serialization failures and substitutes a
default value (empty string, \`Value::Null\`, etc.).

## Sites

\`grep -rEn \"serde_json::(to_string|from_str|to_value|from_value)[a-z_]*\\([^)]*\\)\\.unwrap_or_default\\(\\)\" crates/frankenterm-core/src/\` finds 15 sites at HEAD. Per-site severity:

### HIGH — chain integrity / dedup correctness (1 site, FIXED in same commit)

- **\`tx_idempotency.rs:175\`** — \`StepExecutionRecord::hash()\` used \`unwrap_or_default()\` in the canonical-form construction. Empty-string fallback creates hash collisions across distinct serialization-failure outcomes, corrupting the idempotency-resume chain dedup. **FIXED**: replaced with \`expect(...)\` since \`StepOutcome\` is a typed enum deriving Serialize from primitive fields — the original unwrap was dead code masking a contract the type system already enforces.

### HIGH — replay determinism

- **\`replay_capture.rs:544\`** — \`details = serde_json::to_value(&decision).unwrap_or_default()\`. Failure produces \`Value::Null\` recorded in the replay log; replay determinism breaks because the original \`PolicyDecision\` details are silently lost.

### MEDIUM — webhook / workflow journal

- **\`webhook.rs:140\`** — webhook payload silent loss to remote consumer.
- **\`workflows/handlers.rs:5241, 5394, 5400\`** — workflow handler outcomes (3 sites).
- **\`workflows/handlers.rs:5695\`** — workflow plan.
- **\`workflows/builtin_workflows.rs:882, 887, 939\`** — workflow values (3 sites).
- **\`workflows/engine.rs:330\`** — \`wait_condition\` map.
- **\`workflows/descriptors.rs:687\`** — workflow descriptor val.

### LOW — display / dashboard formatters

- **\`runtime_telemetry.rs:368\`** — telemetry snapshot.
- **\`runtime_diagnostics_ux.rs:417\`** — robot state.
- **\`runtime_health.rs:584\`** — health Display impl.
- **\`vendored_migration_map.rs:693\`** — display format.

These four are operator-facing strings; an empty fallback degrades the message but doesn't corrupt downstream state. Acceptable risk if explicitly documented; a follow-up could replace with \`format!(\"<serialization failed: {e}>\")\` so operators see the failure instead of a blank line.

## Suggested fix shapes

By severity tier:

1. **HIGH** — \`expect(\"...\")\` with diagnostic message naming the type. If the type's Serialize is genuinely infallible (typed enum over primitives), \`expect\` is correct: it surfaces a future-refactor breakage loudly. Done for tx_idempotency.rs:175.
2. **MEDIUM** — observability counter pattern (same as ft-jyywz audit_chain_export_dropped_count): \`AtomicU64 + getter + reset_for_test + bumper + structured tracing::warn\`. Operators see the counter rise when serialization is silently degrading.
3. **LOW** — string fallback that surfaces the error: \`format!(\"<serde failure: {e}>\")\`. Operator dashboards display the failure; downstream parsers can flag it.

## Acceptance

Per site:
- HIGH-tier sites: replaced with \`expect\`. Test verifies hash stability + a synthetic forced-failure asserts the panic message includes the type name (if a synthetic failure can be constructed).
- MEDIUM-tier sites: observability counter added (sibling-class to \`audit_chain_export_dropped_count\`). At least one site (e.g., webhook.rs) documents the operator-facing behavior change.
- LOW-tier sites: error-string fallback OR documented as acceptable.

## Cross-references

- ft-jyywz: closed at dc5b42a8c. Same pattern with observability counter. Template for MEDIUM-tier fixes.
- ft-r24qu / ft-lb5x7 / ft-e3wwx: doc-pin pattern for cases where the runtime stays but docs explain the semantic. Acceptable for LOW-tier.
notes: All 3 tiers shipped: HIGH at tx_idempotency.rs (expect, sibling) + replay_capture.rs (counter, sibling). MEDIUM at 1921ee08c (workflows_serde_drop_count, 9 sites in workflows/*). LOW at b2679d98d (4 display formatters surface error envelope). Plus webhook.rs (sibling expect). 0 production unwrap_or_default sites remain on the original 15-site grep. Lib check clean.

title: [PERF] 9 production Vec::remove(0) callsites doing O(N) FIFO eviction — same pattern fixed at bayesian_ledger 8ea8d676b
description:
PHASE 3 PROJECT-WIDE ANALYSIS — Lens 2 (PERFORMANCE) finding.

Verification: `grep -rn '\.remove(0)' crates/frankenterm-core/src/` (excluding tests + cfg(test)) found 7 production callsites doing FIFO eviction via Vec::remove(0):

1. crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy_dsl.rs:920 — clauses.remove(0) in DSL clause processing.
2. crates/frankenterm-core/src/telemetry.rs:800 — buf.remove(0) in telemetry sample buffer (this one is acknowledged in a comment at line 307 saying VecDeque was the prior fix at a SIBLING site; this site missed the sweep).
3. crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:1080 — self.entries.remove(0) in policy entries cap-eviction.
4. crates/frankenterm-core/src/policy.rs:1295 — self.records.remove(0) in policy records cap-eviction.
5. crates/frankenterm-core/src/explainability_console.rs:693 — self.edges.remove(0) in causal graph edge cap-eviction.
6. crates/frankenterm-core/src/explainability_console.rs:970 — self.traces.remove(0) in trace cap-eviction.
7. crates/frankenterm-core/src/context_budget.rs:643 — registry.remove(0) in context budget eviction.
8. crates/frankenterm-core/src/aegis_diagnostics.rs:524 — self.interventions.remove(0) in interventions cap-eviction.
9. crates/frankenterm-core/src/aegis_diagnostics.rs:549 — self.log_buffer.remove(0) in log buffer cap-eviction.

Same pattern cc1 fixed at bayesian_ledger.rs:361 in commit 8ea8d676b (closed ft-98vk1). Vec::remove(0) is O(N) — shifts all remaining elements left by one. Done on every push past max, the steady-stream amortized cost is O(N²).

Operator impact varies per callsite:
- HIGH: telemetry.rs:800 + aegis_diagnostics.rs:549 (high-frequency hot paths fed by per-event recording).
- MEDIUM: explainability_console + policy.rs (per-decision frequency, can grow under sustained traffic).
- LOW: policy_dsl.rs (DSL processing, bounded by user-supplied clause count).

Recommended remediation: apply the same VecDeque + push_back/pop_front refactor cc1 used at bayesian_ledger.rs. Pattern is mechanical and the boundary (Vec → VecDeque) is local to each struct.

Acceptance:
- Each of the 9 callsites refactored to VecDeque with FIFO regression test pinning eviction order.
- Or: each callsite documented with WHY Vec is correct (some may rely on indexed access; need check).

Why P3:
- No active operator-blocking incident.
- Each call sites is localized; can ship independently.
- Same priority as bayesian_ledger fix (P3) since same class of perf cleanup.
notes:
Closing — re-verification with current HEAD found my initial 21-site count was overcounted due to (a) sibling agents independently shipping VecDeque migrations across most sites in parallel with my cycle, and (b) grep false positives on domain methods named 'remove' (not Vec::remove).

Production sites at HEAD (corrected):
- rate_limit_tracker.rs:186, 265 — SHIPPED in 2714b53ed (cc1, this commit's parent).
- latency_stages.rs:5194, 5678, 10691, 13177, 15417 — 5 sites in the 976KB file. These bundle with ft-l8s7v (latency_stages.rs decomposition); shipping them per-site in the current monolith is high-churn-risk against concurrent agents working in that file.

False positives reverted from the count:
- context_budget.rs:652 — registry.remove(0) is a method call on ContextBudgetRegistry (domain type), inside a #[test] block. Not Vec::remove.
- shadow_mode_evaluator.rs:282 — already uses self.history.pop_front() at HEAD.
- spsc_ring_buffer.rs:733+ (7 sites) — all inside #[test] blocks; test-only consumer-extraction patterns; not production hot paths.

Sibling-shipped (already at HEAD without cc1 ship):
- cost_tracker.rs:306 — uses self.pane_order.pop_front() at HEAD.
- slo_conformance.rs:275 — uses buffer.pop_front() at HEAD.
- semantic_shock_response.rs / frame_budget_signal_coupling.rs / session_workflow_explorer.rs — all migrated.
- policy_dsl.rs / policy.rs / explainability_console.rs / aegis_diagnostics.rs — original bead body called these out; all migrated by sibling activity.

Net: ft-znj5k's production-impact surface is closed except for the 5 latency_stages.rs sites that ride with ft-l8s7v decomposition. The bayesian_ledger pattern (8ea8d676b) propagated through the codebase via parallel-agent activity faster than this single bead could track them.
