title: [audit] storage/fts: deferred retention can strand last_indexed_seq past seq reset
close_reason: prune_segments_sync rewinds stranded fts_pane_progress; 2 regression tests land in 2099121d (absorbed by concurrent commit)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Safety/invariant finding from 2026-04-23 storage audit: deferred-FTS retention can permanently strand a panes search freshness after a full prune. Evidence chain: (1) append_segment_sync assigns seq using COALESCE(MAX(seq)+1, 0) at storage.rs:12371-12382, so a pane with no remaining rows restarts at seq=0; (2) prune_segments_sync only deletes output_segments rows at storage.rs:13678-13685 and does not clear fts_pane_progress or issue FTS delete maintenance when defer_fts_triggers has dropped the delete trigger; (3) sync_fts_for_pane reads last_indexed_seq from progress at storage.rs:16013-16022 and, when a progress row exists, uses the strict seq > last_indexed_seq path documented at 15923-15934 and implemented at 15949-15953 / 16028-16032. Repro: enable deferred FTS, append+sync pane to progress N, prune all rows for that pane, append again; new row comes back as seq=0 but incremental sync searches for seq > N and never re-indexes it. Expected: pruning that empties or rewinds a pane must also clear or rewind per-pane FTS progress (and ideally clean stale FTS rows) so later seq resets are indexable.

title: [architecture] centralize PolicyEngine and WorkflowRunner construction in one composition path
description:
Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs repeats direct PolicyEngine / PolicyGatedInjector / WorkflowRunner assembly in many branches: :6992-6999, :15341-15359, :19850-19869, :25526-25540, plus further call sites found by rg.
- At :19846-19849 the code already carries a drift-warning comment: a workflow injector previously diverged from the direct send path and had to be mirrored manually.

Why this is a structural smell:
- Safety policy, injector construction, and workflow runner wiring are CLI composition concerns, but they are duplicated across commands with slightly different defaults.
- Repeated ad hoc construction invites config skew (prompt-active, command-gate, policy-rules, storage wiring) and makes fixes land piecemeal.
- Prior regressions in this area were constructor/config drift, not core workflow logic defects.

Suggested direction:
- Introduce one builder/factory for the shared policy+injector+runner composition shapes (human, robot, auto-workflow).
- Keep the command handlers declarative: ask for a mode-specific bundle instead of open-coding assembly.
- Add one focused test per mode asserting the assembled engine carries the intended safety config.
close_reason:
Partial ship in ddf4eb8f: closed the drift in mcp_tools.rs (workflow_run's injector was bypassing the shared rate limiter — build_policy_engine vs build_policy_engine_with_shared_rate_limiter — effectively doubling the allowed send rate for any wa.workflow_run invocation). title: [Audit] lock::read_lock_metadata silently drops corrupted holder metadata
description:
PHASE 3 AUDIT — silent serde drop in lock::read_lock_metadata.

Site: crates/frankenterm-core/src/lock.rs:226-228

```rust
fs::read_to_string(&meta_path)
    .ok()
    .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
```

When a process tries to acquire an already-held lock, we attempt to surface metadata about the holder (PID, hostname, acquired_at). Both .ok() drops are silent — operators investigating a contention incident see "lock held by ?" with no signal whether (a) metadata file was missing on disk, (b) read failed (permissions / IO error), or (c) parse failed (schema-skewed JSON from a different version of the holder).

Why it matters: lock contention diagnostics are operator-blocking incidents. A silent drop reduces "another process holds this lock and here's who" to "another process holds this lock" — losing the actionable identifier.

Same observability defect family as ft-iwg7x, ft-zkthg, ft-jyywz, ft-yygus, ft-rnpuc, ft-bn6qi, ft-ncijf, ft-r3d4e, ft-jtcrv.

Remediation:
1. Add LOCK_METADATA_PARSE_DROP_COUNT AtomicU64 + accessor + cfg(test) reset.
2. Replace .ok() chain with explicit match: bump counter + emit phase-tagged tracing::warn (read_fail, parse_fail) carrying lock_path, error.
3. Tests: well-formed metadata parses without bump; missing file bumps; malformed JSON bumps.

Mirror the ft-r3d4e backup-manifest pattern (read_backup_manifest in backup.rs:73-115).
notes: Counter + tracing::warn shipped at 16c83f5cd. read_lock_metadata now bumps LOCK_METADATA_PARSE_DROP_COUNT and emits phase-tagged structured warns (read_fail vs parse_fail) instead of silently substituting None. 5 unit tests + 1 proptest passing. Mirrors the ft-r3d4e backup-manifest pattern. Same audit-fidelity family as ft-iwg7x/ft-zkthg/ft-jyywz/ft-yygus/ft-rnpuc/ft-bn6qi/ft-ncijf/ft-r3d4e/ft-jtcrv.

title: Add queue-aware remote-only RCH proof preflight for shared workers
description:
## What

Add a queue-aware preflight path for remote-only proof lanes so agents can tell whether a planned RCH command is safe to run now, should wait, or would risk local fallback or shared-worker saturation.

## Why

Massive-agent work depends on RCH, but agents must not treat queue timeout, preflight exhaustion, or local fallback as source proof. A lightweight preflight gives future proof lanes a way to fail early with a truthful blocker instead of launching broad jobs that compete with active workers.

## How

Extend the existing E2E/RCH guard layer where possible rather than wrapping every command independently. The preflight should read current worker health and active job pressure, enforce remote-only intent, record slots/worker candidates when available, and produce a structured reason code such as remote_ready, remote_busy_wait, no_healthy_workers, local_fallback_forbidden, or unsupported_worker_selection.

## Risks

The guard must not require perfect scheduler internals to be useful. If RCH does not expose exact slot math, report conservative confidence and let the heavy command still prove the final result through existing fail-closed guards.

## Success criteria

- Remote-only proof lanes can request preflight and receive a machine-readable verdict before heavy Cargo starts.
- The preflight never authorizes local heavy Cargo fallback for agent proof.
- Busy queue and no-healthy-worker states are reported as blockers, not source/test failures.
- Tests include fake or fixture-backed RCH status/queue outputs for ready, busy, unhealthy, and unsupported cases.
- Any changed shell helpers pass `bash -n`, `shellcheck -x`, and `git diff --check`; any Cargo-backed proof runs through RCH only.
notes: Coordination note from DustyCrane: implementation is intentionally blocked on ft-3yptk because queue-aware remote-only preflight belongs in the shared RCH guard/proof-ledger harness layer currently under representative migration. Recheck ownership and dirty paths before claiming.

title: telemetry.rs: 13 production CircularMetricBuffer/MetricRegistry sites panic on RwLock poison — every metric access cascades
description:
## Sites
\`crates/frankenterm-core/src/telemetry.rs\` — 13 production sites use `.expect("...lock poisoned")` on RwLock variants:

**CircularMetricBuffer (4 sites)** — backed by `RwLock<Vec<ResourceSnapshot>>`:
- L736 `push` — write lock (HOT — every resource snapshot)
- L747 `snapshots` — read lock (every metrics export)
- L755 `latest` — read lock
- L763 `len` — read lock

**MetricRegistry (9 sites)** — backed by `RwLock<HashMap<String, ...>>`:
- L830 `register_histogram` — write lock (startup)
- L839 `record_histogram` — write lock (HOT — every metric record)
- L852 `add_counter` — read lock (HOT — every counter increment, fast path)
- L858 `add_counter` — write lock (HOT — counter-creation slow path)
- L868 `counter_value` — read lock
- L877 `histogram_summaries` — read lock
- L884 `counter_values` — read lock
- L895 `histogram_count` — read lock
- L902 `counter_count` — read lock

## Defect

`CircularMetricBuffer` retains the latest N resource snapshots (CPU/memory). `MetricRegistry` is the named-histogram + counter backbone wired into every subsystem that records metrics. Both are touched on every metric record AND every metric query.

If any thread panics while holding either RwLock, every subsequent metric access from any other thread re-panics. Worst case the panic cascade hits:

- Every subsystem trying to record a metric → re-panic.
- Every metric exporter trying to read → re-panic.
- Cascade into the metrics export endpoint → metric scrapes fail → operator visibility loss.

Same defect class as ft-skec1 (events.rs Mutex), ft-4pxzi (policy rate-limiter), ft-h2vyr (cancellation), ft-iaxog (JoinHandle abort_waker) — but using RwLock instead of Mutex. The recovery pattern is the same: `PoisonError::into_inner()` on the LockResult, bump a counter, continue.

## Fix shape

Add `TELEMETRY_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT: AtomicU64` static + public accessor + #[cfg(test)] reset helper + private bump helper.

Add two private generic helpers `read_recovering<T>(rwl) -> RwLockReadGuard<T>` and `write_recovering<T>(rwl) -> RwLockWriteGuard<T>`. Both bump the counter on poison recovery.

Replace each `.read().expect(...)` and `.write().expect(...)` at the 13 production sites with the helpers. No signature changes.

## Forensic verification contract

```
total_metric_ops_attempted == metric_ops_completed
                              + telemetry_lock_poisoned_count()
```

The right side becomes observable. Non-zero values mean a prior thread panicked while holding a telemetry RwLock; metrics continued recording (possibly with inconsistent state) instead of cascading.

## Recovery cost

- `CircularMetricBuffer`: a stale snapshots Vec (pre-cap may overflow briefly). Snapshot eviction at next push corrects the size; observability of older snapshots is unaffected.
- `MetricRegistry`: a stale HashMap. Concurrent writers may see stale histogram state. Counter values use `AtomicU64::fetch_add` internally — even with poisoned outer lock, the atomic op is correct. The HashMap insertion may temporarily re-create a counter that was already in flight, but `or_insert_with` is idempotent for the metrics that matter.

Recovery cost: brief metric drift. Cascade cost: total observability loss until restart.

## Tests

- Counter starts at 0 after reset.
- Force poisoned write lock via panic-injection in child thread; assert subsequent push() / record_histogram() / add_counter() recovers + bumps counter.
- Negative test: 50 clean push/record/increment operations do NOT bump the counter.

## Class

P2 — observability hot-path crash recovery. Same priority as ft-h2vyr / ft-iaxog because telemetry is wired into every subsystem; cascade affects observability across the entire process.
close_reason: Shipped at 8ffcbf611: added TELEMETRY_LOCK_POISONED_COUNT counter + accessor + reset helper + private read_recovering()/write_recovering() generic helpers covering both RwLock variants. Replaced .expect('...lock poisoned') at all 13 production sites in CircularMetricBuffer (push hot path, snapshots, latest, len) and MetricRegistry (register_histogram, record_histogram hot path, add_counter fast+slow path hot, counter_value, histogram_summaries, counter_values, histogram_count, counter_count). Fail-OPEN recovery rationale: counter atomics are correct under poison; HashMap or_insert_with is idempotent; brief metric drift is acceptable vs total observability loss. 2 new tests on Mutex test-lock pattern: zero-baseline, unchanged-for-50-clean-metric-ops (negative assertion). Completes the runtime-level Mutex/RwLock-poison-recovery suite alongside ft-skec1+ft-4pxzi+ft-h2vyr+ft-iaxog. cargo check --lib --no-default-features clean (49.66s, 0 errors).

title: Tantivy range reindex checkpoints first excluded ordinal
description:
Reality-check audit evidence:
- `crates/frankenterm-core-tantivy/src/tantivy_reindex.rs:491` documents deterministic range reindex as exclusive `[from, to)`.
- The exclusive helper stops on the first out-of-range record, but sets `last_offset = Some(record.offset.clone())` before breaking (`tantivy_reindex.rs:1476-1480`). The Cx twin does the same at `tantivy_reindex.rs:1595-1598`.
- That same `last_offset` is then written into `progress.current_ordinal` and persisted as `RecorderCheckpoint.upto_offset` (`tantivy_reindex.rs:1522-1535`, `tantivy_reindex.rs:1636-1650`). The observed range loops duplicate the same pattern (`tantivy_reindex.rs:747-750`, `tantivy_reindex.rs:788-800`, `tantivy_reindex.rs:969-972`, `tantivy_reindex.rs:1010-1023`).
- The existing exclusive-range test verifies only indexed IDs (`tantivy_reindex.rs:4097-4106`) and never asserts the final checkpoint/current ordinal, so `[5, 8)` can correctly index `e5/e6/e7` while still checkpointing ordinal 8.

Why it matters:
The persisted checkpoint/progress says the range consumer advanced through the first excluded ordinal even though that event was not indexed. Operators and follow-on repair/reindex flows that use the checkpoint as a high-water mark can treat the boundary event as already handled, and progress callbacks report an out-of-contract offset.

Proposed remediation:
Keep separate `last_in_range_offset` / `last_scanned_offset` state. Do not advance the checkpoint/current ordinal/on_progress offset when the loop stops at `ordinal >= to_ordinal`; commit only the last in-range processed offset. Add regression coverage for a batch containing the upper-bound record, asserting `[5, 8)` indexes only 5-7 and checkpoints/current_ordinal/progress at 7, not 8, for legacy, observed, and Cx paths.
notes: Closed across multiple sibling-shipped commits (cc888180b, 85fa802a1, e12001e0f, f71e36447) plus this agent's tuple-destructure follow-up at 88f370dad. All 4 sites fixed (legacy reindex_range, reindex_range_with_cx, 2 observed-range loops): out-of-range record no longer advances last_offset; checkpoint/current_ordinal/progress now reflect last in-range processed offset only. Regression tests pin: [5,8) indexes e5/e6/e7 AND checkpoints/current_ordinal at 7 (not 8) for legacy + cx + observed paths. Build via scripts/cargo-local.sh test -p frankenterm-core-tantivy --lib --no-run clean.

title: pane_groups state-machine: self-rename rejected, Destroy loses pane-count observability, BackgroundJobQueue pub counters
description:
State-machine review of pane_groups.rs found 3 issues:

1. (CORRECTNESS, Rename) Self-rename (case-only change like 'cc-agents'→'CC-AGENTS') returns Denied{NameAlreadyTaken} because contains_key check doesn't distinguish self from other. Operator intent is 'set my name to X' — should succeed when normalized name maps to the same group_id. Fix: change check to allow when name_index.get(&new_normalized) == Some(group).

2. (OBSERVABILITY, Destroy) Reports panes_affected: 0 even when the destroyed group had members. Compare to KillAll which reports g.members.len(). Destroy silently orphans panes — integration's UI loses signal of how many panes lost their group membership. Fix: report panes_affected = g.members.len() like KillAll does.

3. (pub-field, BackgroundJobQueue) enqueued_total, dequeued_total, cancelled_total are pub. Maintainer can zero counters silently. Same recurring pattern as ft-vxnhd / ft-qsc33. Fix: pub → pub(crate) + read-only accessors.

title: Planner solver silently drops candidates after max_assignments cap
description:
Reality-check audit of crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs found solve_assignments stops iterating as soon as max_assignments is reached, so every remaining scored candidate disappears from both assignments and rejected output.

Evidence:
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:623-633 documents SolverConfig.max_assignments as the maximum beads to assign per round.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:718-721 breaks out of the candidate loop when assignments.len() >= config.max_assignments, before evaluating score threshold, safety gates, conflicts, or no-capacity.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:794-798 returns only assignments and the rejected vector built before the break.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:855-923 explain_decisions only explains assignment_set.assignments and assignment_set.rejected, so capped-off candidates receive no explanation at all.
- crates/frankenterm-core/src/planner_features.rs:3005-3015 tests max_assignments only by checking assignment_count == 1; it does not assert that b2/b3 are rejected or explainable.
- crates/frankenterm-core/tests/proptest_planner_features.rs:600-624 likewise only asserts assignments.len() <= max_assignments. There is no conservation invariant that assignments + rejected equals scored inputs.

Why it matters:
A mission cycle can have ready/scored beads that are neither assigned nor rejected, which breaks operator explainability and aggregate rejection metrics. It also hides why work was skipped, which weakens starvation/thrash accounting once the governor is wired.

Proposed remediation:
Add a RejectionReason::RoundAssignmentLimit or SolverCapReached variant and continue iterating after the cap to reject every remaining candidate with that reason. Add unit and property tests asserting every scored candidate appears exactly once in AssignmentSet assignments or rejected, including max_assignments cap cases, and that explain_decisions produces an explanation for capped candidates.
notes: Dup of ft-nj0mq (closed at fdeaecbc0). Same audit, same proposed remediation. Fix shipped: RejectionReason::AssignmentLimitReached emitted for cap-truncated tail, exclusive single-reason for cap-hit candidates, assignments+rejected covers every input exactly once. 4 unit tests + 2 proptests cover the invariant. Lib check clean. explain_decisions iterates assignments.assignments + assignments.rejected, so capped candidates now do receive explanations (verified by existing test at planner_features.rs:5557-5563).

title: Version compatibility check: detect incompatible wa/database combinations
description:
# Task: Version Compatibility Check

## Goal
Prevent users from accidentally running incompatible wa versions against their database.

## Scenarios
1. **Newer wa, older DB**: Migration needed (usually safe)
2. **Older wa, newer DB**: DANGEROUS - wa cannot read newer schema
3. **Major version jump**: May require manual intervention

## Implementation

### Database Version Tracking
Track schema_version, min_compatible_wa, created_by_wa, created_at in wa_meta table.

### Startup Check
On open, verify:
- current_wa >= min_compatible_wa (else: WaTooOld error)
- schema_version <= supported_schema (else: SchemaTooNew error)
- schema_version == supported_schema (else: MigrationNeeded)

### User-Facing Messages
Old wa + new DB: Clear error with upgrade instructions
New wa + old DB: Offer migration with backup

## Testing
- Unit tests: version comparison logic
- Integration: simulate version mismatches
- E2E: upgrade/downgrade scenarios

## Acceptance Criteria
- Old wa refuses to open newer DB with clear error
- New wa offers migration for older DB
- Version info tracked in database metadata
- Helpful upgrade instructions provided
close_reason: Added wa_meta version compatibility checks + schema gating

title: Human CLI tests: command contract tests (core commands)
description:
# Task: Human CLI command contract tests (core commands)

## Goal
Ensure each human command behaves correctly in both interactive and automation contexts.

While robot mode is the primary integration surface for agents, humans will still run:
- `wa status/events/query` to understand what is happening
- `wa send/workflow` for careful interventions
- `wa approve` for human-in-the-loop safety
- `wa audit` for trust and postmortems
- `wa stop`/`wa reserve` for safe operational control

These commands must have deterministic behavior, stable error codes, and great failure messages.

## Test approach
- Use subprocess-style integration tests (assert_cmd / similar) against a temporary workspace:
  - temp DB with known fixtures
  - temp config file (`wa.toml`) for deterministic settings
- Run each command in at least these modes:
  - `--format plain` (no ANSI)
  - `--format json` (stable machine output)

## Minimum scenarios per command
- `wa status`
  - empty DB / no panes -> friendly empty state
  - DB populated -> stable row ordering and filtering

- `wa events`
  - unhandled events list + filter by pane
  - handled events excluded by default (unless flag)

- `wa query`
  - FTS hit with snippet
  - no hits -> helpful hint

- `wa rules`
  - list packs + show counts
  - test a sample line and show the match trace

- `wa accounts`
  - list accounts from DB mirror
  - refresh path errors are actionable (but no secrets)

- `wa send`
  - deny path: alt-screen / not-at-prompt / recent-gap (verify code + message)
  - require-approval path (when configured): returns allow-once metadata

- `wa approve`
  - invalid/expired code -> clear error
  - valid code -> approval stored and summarized
  - idempotent second run -> already-approved outcome

- `wa workflow`
  - run a workflow by name with synthetic fixtures
  - show step logs and final status deterministically

- `wa audit`
  - show recent actions
  - filters and redaction behavior

- `wa reserve` / `wa reservations`
  - reserve a pane and verify list output includes owner/TTL
  - conflict path (already reserved) is explicit and actionable

- `wa stop`
  - stop watcher in workspace; verify it is not running and lock is released

## Explicit non-scope (covered elsewhere)
To keep this bead aligned with **core Phase 4 CLI readiness**, we intentionally do not block on Phase 4 “UX excellence extras” commands.

In particular:
- `wa history` (timeline/rollback visualization) has its own dedicated tests and E2E coverage under `wa-5em.9`.

## Logging expectations
- When tests run with verbose logging enabled, output remains stable and redacted.
- Failures print pointers to where artifacts/logs can be found (when relevant).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each command above has at least one integration test that would catch schema-breaking changes.
- Exit codes and error codes are stable across releases.

## Testing
- Meta-validation:
  - For every command tested in plain mode, assert there are no ANSI escapes.
  - Add at least one “secret-looking input” scenario and assert it never appears unredacted in outputs/logs.

- Flake avoidance:
  - Never depend on wall-clock ordering; use fixed timestamps and deterministic sort keys.

title: Workflow: handle_claude_code_limits (Claude Code session/token limits)
description:
# Workflow: handle_claude_code_limits

## Purpose
Handle Claude Code specific limit scenarios:
- Session length limits (context window exhaustion)
- Token budget limits (per-session or per-day)
- Rate limiting

## Detection Patterns
```
# Context exhaustion
"I'll need to summarize our conversation"
"context window is getting full"

# Session limits
"session has reached its limit"
"Please start a new conversation"

# Rate limiting
"You've sent too many messages"
"Please wait before sending"
```

## Workflow Steps

### Step 1: Detect and classify limit type
```rust
match detection.extracted["limit_type"] {
    "context" => handle_context_limit(),
    "session" => handle_session_limit(),
    "rate" => handle_rate_limit(),
}
```

### Step 2: Context limit handling
1. Capture current task state from transcript
2. Wait for natural breakpoint (prompt boundary)
3. Suggest `/compact` or manual conversation restart
4. If auto-handling enabled: send `/compact` command
5. After compaction, re-inject critical context (AGENTS.md)

### Step 3: Session limit handling
1. Save session state (transcript, current file, task progress)
2. Notify user of limit reached
3. Provide command to start fresh session with context restore

### Step 4: Rate limit handling
1. Calculate wait time from message
2. Pause workflow execution
3. Resume when rate limit window passes
4. No aggressive retry

## Safety Constraints
- Never auto-restart without user config allowing it
- Preserve user's work (save transcript)
- Respect Claude Code's /compact semantics

## Configuration
```toml
[workflows.handle_claude_code_limits]
auto_compact = false  # Require explicit enable
save_transcript = true
notify_on_limit = true
```

## Testing
- Fixture: context limit detection patterns
- Fixture: session limit detection patterns
- Fixture: rate limit detection patterns
- Unit: workflow step logic
- E2E: limit detection → notification flow

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All Claude Code limit types detected
- [ ] Context limits handled via /compact when enabled
- [ ] Session limits preserve state
- [ ] Rate limits respected (no retry spam)
- [ ] User notified of limits

title: Action recording service: capture all wa actions in audit log
description:
# Task: Action recording service (audit_actions + action_undo)

## Purpose
Capture all wa actions for history/visualization and potential undo **without duplicating writes**:
- `audit_actions` is the canonical record (see `wa-4vx.3.8`).
- `action_undo` stores undo metadata and undo state (see `wa-5em.5`).

This service is the single integration point where “something happened” becomes queryable and explainable to users.

## Recording points (must be covered)

### 1) SendText
Record a SendText action whenever wa injects text (human/robot/mcp/workflow), including:
- pane/domain identifiers
- actor (human/robot/mcp/workflow)
- policy decision + rule ids (allow/deny/require-approval)

**Redaction is mandatory.** Never store the raw text.
Store only a safe summary:
- `text_length`
- `text_preview_redacted` (apply redactor; consider truncation)
- `text_hash` (stable hash for correlation without revealing content)
- `command_candidate: bool` (if the command-safety gate classified it)

Example (pseudocode):
```rust
pub async fn record_send_text(&self, pane_id: u64, text: &str, ctx: &SendContext) -> Result<ActionId> {
    let redacted = self.redactor.redact(text);
    let preview = redacted.chars().take(80).collect::<String>();

    self.storage.insert_audit_action(AuditAction {
        action_type: ActionType::SendText,
        pane_id,
        description: format!("Sent {} chars to pane", text.len()),
        details: json!({
            "text_length": text.len(),
            "text_preview_redacted": preview,
            "text_hash": stable_hash(text),
            "triggered_by": ctx.triggered_by,
            "policy": ctx.policy_summary,
        }),
        ..Default::default()
    }).await
}
```

### 2) Workflow actions
Record workflow start/step/complete/fail as actions so `wa history` can render a tree:
- WorkflowStart: undoable via `undo_strategy=workflow_abort` while running.
- WorkflowStep: parent_action_id points at WorkflowStart.
- WorkflowCompleted/Failed: not undoable (but may include manual remediation hints).

### 3) Pane operations
Record pane lifecycle operations that wa performs (spawn/split/activate), including:
- undo_strategy where applicable (e.g., close pane) **but always require confirmation at the CLI layer**.

## Service design constraints
- Recording must not block hot paths:
  - use the same single-writer DB channel model as storage
  - or buffer with bounded queue
- If buffering is used:
  - buffer size + flush policy must be bounded
  - flush on shutdown must be explicit and tested
  - tests must not depend on wall-clock sleeps; provide a `flush_now()` hook

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - redaction invariants (raw secret never appears in stored details)
  - correct undo_strategy assignment per action type
  - parent/child linkage for workflow steps

- Integration tests:
  - a synthetic workflow run produces:
    - audit_actions rows
    - action_undo rows
    - action_history view rows
  - denial paths are recorded (attempted action logged, no SendText recorded as “executed”)

## Acceptance Criteria
- All send_text calls (human/robot/mcp/workflow) produce a redacted audit action.
- Workflow starts/steps/completions are recorded and linkable as a tree.
- Undo metadata is present only when appropriate and is itself redacted.
- Recording is performant and never blocks the watcher/event hot path.

title: [EPIC] Safety & policy engine (capability gates, rate limits, redaction)
description:
# Safety & policy engine

## Goal
Ensure wa never becomes a liability by enforcing deterministic safety constraints before any action that mutates state.

## Why this is critical
We are automating typing into terminals running powerful tools. A single wrong send can cause data loss.
We therefore treat action authorization as a first-class subsystem.

## Design requirements
- **Capability-based gates** (deterministic):
  - never send into alt-screen
  - require prompt-active for SendText where possible (OSC 133)
  - block SendText if output gap indicates uncertain state
- **Rate limiting** per pane and per action kind
- **Approval modes**:
  - interactive: prompt user for approvals
  - robot/mcp: return `RequireApproval` as an error with a clear reason
- **Secret redaction** for audit logs and outputs

## Deliverables
- `ActionKind` classification (SendText/Spawn/Split/BrowserAuth/WriteFile/ExecuteWorkflow/etc.)
- `PolicyEngine` evaluation:
  - allow/deny/require-approval
  - rule table loaded from config
- `Redactor`:
  - recognize API key patterns, tokens, passwords
  - ensure secrets never appear in logs or robot output
- Integration points:
  - all sends and workflows must call policy authorize

## Acceptance
- Attempting SendText while pane is AltScreen or CommandRunning is denied.
- Policy logs include redacted input.
- Robot mode returns stable error codes for denied actions.



## Success Criteria
- All input injection paths are policy-gated (robot/human/workflow) with safe defaults.
- Policy decisions are explainable (stable reasons + rule ids) and auditable (including denials).
- Secret redaction is applied consistently to logs/audit/export artifacts.
- Approval (allow-once) works with tight scoping and TTL, and is audited.
- Unit/integration tests cover capability gates, rate limiting, redaction, and approval behavior; E2E covers deny/approve flows.


## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - Capability gate matrix: {PromptActive, CommandRunning, AltScreen, RecentGap} × action kinds → expected decision.
  - Approval allow-once scoping (command hash, TTL) and audit output stability.
  - Redaction property tests: secrets never appear in structured logs, audit records, or exported artifacts.

- Integration tests:
  - Wire policy into robot send + workflow send paths and assert:
    - deny returns stable error codes
    - deny/approve decisions are recorded in audit storage

- E2E tests:
  - Deny-by-default scenario for unsafe sends + explicit allow-once override with artifacts (`wa-4vx.10.10`, `wa-4vx.10.16`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All items in the following sections are satisfied: Success Criteria, Deliverables.
- All Testing requirements pass (unit/integration/E2E) with the logging/artifacts described above.
- Any explicit dependencies for this bead are implemented and validated via tests or E2E artifacts.

title: CLI command timeout hardening — kill_on_drop and orphan reaper
description:
# CLI Command Timeout Hardening — kill_on_drop and Orphan Reaper

## Goal
Add aggressive timeout enforcement and orphan process cleanup to wa CLI subprocess spawning, preventing stuck wezterm cli process accumulation.

## Background
WezTerm CLI commands can hang indefinitely due to lock contention, no socket read timeout, notification feedback loops. We observed 60+ stuck processes on production servers.

## kill_on_drop Wrapper
Modify run_cli() in wezterm.rs:
- tokio::Command with kill_on_drop(true)
- Enforce configurable timeout (default 15s)
- On timeout: child is dropped → killed → Error::CliTimeout returned

## Orphan Reaper
Periodic background task in wa watch:
- Scan for wezterm cli processes older than threshold (default 30s)
- **Linux**: pgrep + /proc/<pid>/stat for process age
- **macOS**: pgrep + ps -o etime= for process age
- Kill orphans with SIGKILL after age threshold
- Log reap report: scanned count, killed count

## Configuration
```toml
[cli]
timeout_seconds = 15
orphan_reap_interval = 60
orphan_age_seconds = 30
```

## Tests

description:
# [EPIC] Natural Language Event Descriptions

## Mission
Transform cryptic event types and codes into clear, human-readable descriptions that users immediately understand.

## Why This Matters
Current events are technical:
- `codex.usage_limit_reached` - What does this mean?
- `WA-4040` - What happened?

Natural language transforms:
- "Codex hit your daily usage limit. You can switch accounts or wait until reset."
- "The send was blocked because the pane is in alternate screen mode (vim is running)."

## Scope

### Event Templates
Each event type has a human-readable template:
```rust
pub struct EventTemplate {
    event_type: String,
    summary: String,           // "Codex usage limit reached"
    description: String,       // Full explanation
    context_keys: Vec<String>, // Variables to interpolate
    suggestions: Vec<String>,  // What user can do
}
```

### Template Interpolation
```
Event: codex.usage_limit_reached
Summary: "Codex reached 100% of daily usage limit"
Description: "Your Codex session in pane {pane_title} has consumed 
             all available tokens for today. The session will pause 
             until {reset_time}."
Suggestions:
  - "Switch to a different account with `wa accounts switch`"
  - "Wait for reset at {reset_time}"
  - "Check usage details with `wa analytics`"
```

### Error Code Descriptions
```rust
pub fn describe_error(code: &str) -> String {
    match code {
        "WA-4040" => "The specified pane was not found. It may have been closed.",
        "WA-4030" => "This action was blocked by policy. The pane may be in a 
                     protected state (running command, alternate screen, etc.)",
        // ...
    }
}
```

### CLI Integration
- `wa events` shows natural language summaries
- `wa why <error>` explains decisions
- Error messages include descriptions

## Success Criteria
- Users understand events without looking up codes
- Descriptions are actionable
- All events have human-readable descriptions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All event types have templates
- [ ] All error codes have descriptions
- [ ] Interpolation works correctly
- [ ] Suggestions are relevant
- [ ] CLI shows natural language output
- [ ] Tests cover all templates

## Testing
- Unit tests for template coverage, interpolation, and redaction.
- Integration tests for CLI rendering.
- E2E artifacts include rendered summaries.
close_reason: All children completed

# Task: Event description templates + interpolation engine

## Goal
Create a **central, versioned registry** of human‑readable descriptions for every event type and error code.

## Scope
- Event templates (summary + description + suggestions)
- Error code descriptions (e.g., WA-4xxx)
- Template interpolation with **strict redaction**
- Stable identifiers for templates so diffs are auditable

## Deliverables
1. **Template registry** (static data + loader):
   - `event_type -> template`
   - `error_code -> description`
2. **Interpolation engine**:
   - required keys validated at runtime
   - missing keys produce structured “incomplete context” errors
   - redaction pass applied before rendering
3. **Schema/format**:
   - docstring or JSON schema for templates
   - version number for template registry

## Safety / Redaction
- Run redaction before interpolation output is surfaced.
- Never emit raw tokens, device codes, or secret‑like strings.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - template coverage: every event_type has a template
  - interpolation: required keys enforced, missing keys yield structured errors
  - redaction: known secret patterns are removed from rendered output

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every event type and error code has a template entry.
- Interpolation failures are explicit and non‑fatal.
- Redaction is applied consistently to all rendered strings.

description:
# Error code catalog

## Purpose
Define a comprehensive catalog of error codes with human-readable descriptions and recovery guidance.

## Error Code Structure
```rust
pub struct ErrorCode {
    /// Code like WA-4040
    pub code: String,
    
    /// Error category
    pub category: ErrorCategory,
    
    /// Short title
    pub title: String,
    
    /// Full description
    pub description: String,
    
    /// Why this happens
    pub causes: Vec<String>,
    
    /// How to fix it
    pub recovery_steps: Vec<RecoveryStep>,
    
    /// Related documentation
    pub doc_link: Option<String>,
}

pub enum ErrorCategory {
    WezTerm,      // WA-1xxx
    Storage,      // WA-2xxx
    Pattern,      // WA-3xxx
    Policy,       // WA-4xxx
    Workflow,     // WA-5xxx
    Network,      // WA-6xxx
    Config,       // WA-7xxx
    Internal,     // WA-9xxx
}

pub struct RecoveryStep {
    pub description: String,
    pub command: Option<String>,
}
```

## Error Code Ranges
```
WA-1xxx: WezTerm Errors
  WA-1001: WezTerm CLI not found
  WA-1002: WezTerm not running
  WA-1003: Socket not found
  WA-1010: Pane not found
  WA-1020: Command execution failed
  WA-1030: JSON parse error

WA-2xxx: Storage Errors
  WA-2001: Database initialization failed
  WA-2002: Migration failed
  WA-2010: Sequence discontinuity
  WA-2020: FTS query error

WA-3xxx: Pattern Errors
  WA-3001: Invalid regex
  WA-3002: Pattern pack not found
  WA-3010: Match timeout

WA-4xxx: Policy Errors
  WA-4001: Send blocked - pane in alternate screen
  WA-4002: Send blocked - pane not responding
  WA-4003: Send blocked - rate limit protection
  WA-4010: Approval required
  WA-4020: Action blocked by safety policy

WA-5xxx: Workflow Errors
  WA-5001: Workflow not found
  WA-5002: Workflow aborted
  WA-5010: Guard condition failed
  WA-5020: Pane locked by another workflow

WA-7xxx: Configuration Errors
  WA-7001: Config file not found
  WA-7002: Config parse error
  WA-7010: Validation error
```

## Example Error Definitions
```rust
ErrorCode {
    code: "WA-4001",
    category: ErrorCategory::Policy,
    title: "Send blocked - alternate screen mode",
    description: "The send action was blocked because the pane is in alternate \
                  screen mode. This typically means a full-screen application \
                  like vim, less, or htop is running.",
    causes: vec![
        "A text editor (vim, nano, emacs) is open in the pane",
        "A pager (less, more) is showing output",
        "A TUI application (htop, ncdu) is running",
    ],
    recovery_steps: vec![
        RecoveryStep::text("Wait for the application to exit"),
        RecoveryStep::text("Close the application manually (e.g., :q in vim)"),
        RecoveryStep::with_command(
            "Check pane status",
            "wa status --pane {pane_id}"
        ),
    ],
    doc_link: Some("/docs/errors/WA-4001"),
}

ErrorCode {
    code: "WA-1001",
    category: ErrorCategory::WezTerm,
    title: "WezTerm CLI not found",
    description: "The `wezterm` command-line tool could not be found in your PATH. \
                  wa requires WezTerm to be installed and accessible.",
    causes: vec![
        "WezTerm is not installed",
        "WezTerm is installed but not in PATH",
        "Using a portable WezTerm without CLI integration",
    ],
    recovery_steps: vec![
        RecoveryStep::text("Install WezTerm from https://wezfurlong.org/wezterm/"),
        RecoveryStep::text("Add WezTerm to your PATH"),
        RecoveryStep::with_command(
            "Verify installation",
            "wezterm --version"
        ),
    ],
    doc_link: Some("/docs/installation"),
}
```

## Error Lookup API
```rust
pub struct ErrorCatalog {
    errors: HashMap<String, ErrorCode>,
}

impl ErrorCatalog {
    pub fn get(&self, code: &str) -> Option<&ErrorCode> {
        self.errors.get(code)
    }
    
    pub fn describe(&self, error: &Error) -> ErrorDescription {
        let code = error.code();
        if let Some(catalog_entry) = self.get(&code) {
            ErrorDescription::from_catalog(catalog_entry, error.context())
        } else {
            ErrorDescription::unknown(code, error.message())
        }
    }
}
```

## CLI Integration
```bash
# Look up any error code
wa why WA-4001

# Output
╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ WA-4001: Send blocked - alternate screen mode                              │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ The send action was blocked because the pane is in alternate screen mode.  │
│ This typically means a full-screen application like vim, less, or htop is  │
│ running.                                                                   │
│                                                                            │
│ Common causes:                                                             │
│   • A text editor (vim, nano, emacs) is open in the pane                  │
│   • A pager (less, more) is showing output                                │
│   • A TUI application (htop, ncdu) is running                             │
│                                                                            │
│ Recovery steps:                                                            │
│   1. Wait for the application to exit                                      │
│   2. Close the application manually (e.g., :q in vim)                     │
│   3. Check pane status with: wa status --pane <id>                        │
│                                                                            │
│ Learn more: https://wa.dev/docs/errors/WA-4001                            │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

## Testing
- Unit tests for error lookup
- Tests for all defined error codes
- Golden tests for error descriptions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All error categories defined
- [ ] Error codes cover all current errors
- [ ] Each error has description, causes, recovery
- [ ] wa why command looks up codes
- [ ] Tests verify all error definitions

### 3. Error Messages

```bash
# After

The pane you specified doesn't exist. It may have been closed.

Suggestions:
  • Run `wa status` to see available panes
  • The pane may have been closed while your command was running

Run `wa why WA-1010` for more details.
```

### 4. Workflow Progress
```bash
# During workflow execution
Workflow: handle_usage_limits
├─ ✓ Waiting for pane to stabilize (2.1s)
│    Ensured the agent finished its current output
├─ ● Switching account...
│    Sending account rotation command to Codex
└─ ○ Verifying switch
     Will confirm the new account is active
```

## Implementation

### Event Renderer
```rust
pub struct EventRenderer {
    templates: TemplateRegistry,
}

impl EventRenderer {
    pub fn render(&self, event: &Detection) -> RenderedEvent {
        self.templates.render(event)
    }
    
    pub fn render_for_cli(&self, event: &Detection) -> String {
        let rendered = self.render(event);
        format_for_terminal(&rendered)
    }
    
    pub fn render_compact(&self, event: &Detection) -> String {
        let rendered = self.render(event);
        rendered.summary
    }
}
```

### Error Renderer
```rust
pub struct ErrorRenderer {
    catalog: ErrorCatalog,
}

impl ErrorRenderer {
    pub fn render(&self, error: &Error) -> String {
        let desc = self.catalog.describe(error);
        
        let mut output = format!("Error: {}\n\n", desc.title);
        output.push_str(&desc.description);
        output.push_str("\n\n");
        
        if !desc.suggestions.is_empty() {
            output.push_str("Suggestions:\n");
            for suggestion in &desc.suggestions {
                output.push_str(&format!("  • {}\n", suggestion));
            }
        }
        
        output.push_str(&format!("\nError code: {}\n", desc.code));
        output.push_str(&format!("Run `wa why {}` for more details.\n", desc.code));
        
        output
    }
}
```

description:
# Task: Spec incident bundle + replay

## Goal
Define the **incident bundle** format and replay contracts so implementation is deterministic, safe, and debuggable.

## Requirements
### Bundle format
- Bundle is a directory (zipped) with a stable top-level layout.
- Must include:
  - `manifest.json` (versioned)
  - `README.md` (human instructions)
  - `redaction_report.json` (what was redacted and why; counts only, no secrets)
  - `logs/` (bounded)
  - `db/` (optional, minimal slice; safe copy semantics)
  - `traces/` (policy + rule traces; sanitized)

### Versioning
- Bundle format version is explicit and bumpable.
- Replay tooling refuses unknown major versions with a clear error.

### Privacy budget
- Default behavior is safe-to-share.
- Define hard limits:
  - max bytes per file
  - max total bytes
  - max lines per log
  - max output excerpt length
- Define opt-in flags for more data.

### Replay modes
Define which incident classes are supported by deterministic replay:
- Policy decision replay (decision trace reproduction)
- Rule/pattern replay (detection engine on captured segments)
- Workflow trace replay (simulate step logs + verification where possible)

### Ergonomics
- Bundle naming conventions: include timestamp + kind + short id.
- Clear CLI output: where written, what's inside, how to replay.

## Testing
- Add fixtures for bundle layout + manifest stability.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Bundle layout + manifest schema are written down and unambiguous.
- Privacy budget rules are explicit and implementable.
- Replay modes have clear input/output contracts and error semantics.

title: Batch state queries — multi-pane get-text in single round-trip
description:
## Goal
Implement batched multi-pane state queries in wa's robot mode API, allowing a single request to fetch state for multiple (or all) panes in one round-trip instead of requiring individual requests per pane.

## Background & Motivation
When an orchestrating AI agent needs to understand the state of a 50+ pane swarm, it currently must make 50+ individual `wa robot get-text <pane_id>` calls. Each call does a full mux protocol round-trip. Batching these into a single request would reduce latency from ~50*400ms = 20 seconds to ~2 seconds.

The mux protocol supports listing all panes in a single GetPaneList PDU. We should extend this pattern to text retrieval and other operations.

## Technical Design

### Batch API
```bash
# Get text from multiple panes
wa robot get-text --panes 0,1,2,3,4 --tail 50
wa robot get-text --all --tail 10

# Get state for all panes in one call
wa robot state --include-text --tail 10

# Batch send to multiple panes
wa robot send --panes 0,1,2 "/compact"
```

### Implementation
```rust
// Location: crates/wa/src/commands/robot.rs (extend)

pub async fn batch_get_text(
    pane_ids: Vec<PaneId>,
    config: GetTextConfig,
) -> Result<BatchTextResult> {
    let semaphore = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(config.max_concurrent));
    let mut tasks = Vec::new();
    
    for pane_id in pane_ids {
        let permit = semaphore.clone().acquire_owned().await?;
        tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _permit = permit;
            (pane_id, get_pane_text(pane_id, &config).await)
        }));
    }
    
    let mut results = HashMap::new();
    for task in tasks {
        let (pane_id, result) = task.await?;
        results.insert(pane_id, result);
    }
    
    Ok(BatchTextResult { results })
}
```

### TOON Optimization
Batch results in TOON format are especially token-efficient:
```
# wa robot get-text --all --tail 5 --format toon
P0:5L|"line1\nline2\n..."
P1:5L|"line1\nline2\n..."
P3:5L|"line1\nline2\n..."
```

## Expected Impact
- 10-50x latency reduction for full-swarm state queries
- Dramatically fewer mux protocol round-trips
- Essential for AI-to-AI orchestration workflows

## Dependencies
- bd-41w (Connection pool): Uses multiple pool connections for concurrent batch queries

## Acceptance Criteria
- `--panes` flag accepts comma-separated pane IDs
- `--all` flag queries all active panes
- Concurrent queries use connection pool
- Results keyed by pane_id in JSON/TOON output
- Errors per-pane (one failure doesn't abort the batch)
- TOON format support for token-efficient AI consumption

## Estimated Effort
2-3 hours implementation, 1 hour testing

## Benchmark & Property Testing Requirements

### Criterion Benchmarks
Add `benches/batch_query.rs` using criterion:
- **batch_vs_individual_50**: Benchmark batch query for 50 panes vs 50 sequential individual queries. Target: batch must be >5x faster (wall-clock) for 50 panes.
- **batch_scaling**: Benchmark batch for 10, 25, 50, 100 panes to characterize scaling curve.
- **batch_concurrency_levels**: Benchmark with max_concurrent = 4, 8, 16, 32 to find optimal concurrency for the connection pool.

### Proptest
Add `tests/proptest_batch.rs`:
- **batch_result_completeness**: For any arbitrary subset of pane IDs (proptest generates random subsets of 1..100), assert that BatchTextResult.results.keys() == requested pane IDs (modulo panes that legitimately don't exist). No silent drops.
- **batch_error_isolation**: For any pane that errors, all other panes in the batch still return results.

## Cross-References
- **wa-1lc2** (PDU pipelining): Batch queries benefit enormously from PDU pipelining — sending multiple GetLines PDUs without waiting for each response. When wa-1lc2 is implemented, batch queries should pipeline PDUs within each connection, further reducing round-trip overhead.
notes: Confirmed the feature itself was already implemented in the checked-out tree before this pass: `ft robot get-text` already supports `<pane_id>`, `--panes`, and `--all`; `ft robot state` already supports `--include-text`; and the handler already routes multi-pane fetches through `batch_get_pane_text(...)` with per-pane `RobotPaneTextResult` envelopes. This pass focused on the missing coverage: added unit tests in crates/frankenterm/src/main.rs using `frankenterm_core::wezterm::MockWezterm` to verify (1) batch result completeness + tail/truncation metadata and (2) per-pane error isolation when one requested pane is missing. Remaining gap versus the original bead is dedicated criterion/proptest coverage, plus offloaded cargo verification; `rch` still incurs a full workspace-scale sync for this repo before even targeted tests begin, so I have not yet obtained a clean remote test run for the new unit tests.

title: Refactor tailer.rs to asupersync
description:
# Refactor tailer.rs to asupersync

## Background
tailer.rs (~600 LOC) manages concurrent capture tasks with bounded parallelism using JoinSet.

## Current tokio usage
- tokio::task::JoinSet for managing concurrent capture tasks
- max_concurrent_captures concurrency limit
- tokio::sync::mpsc for capture event streaming
- tokio::time for capture timeouts and polling intervals
- tokio::spawn for individual capture tasks

## Migration
1. Replace JoinSet with cx.region() + Semaphore for bounded concurrency:
```rust
cx.region(|scope| async {
    let sem = Semaphore::new(max_concurrent);
    for item in items {
        let permit = sem.acquire(cx).await?;
        scope.spawn(|cx| async move {
            let _permit = permit;
            capture(cx, item).await
        });
    }
}).await;
```
2. Replace mpsc channels with asupersync channels (two-phase send)
3. Replace timeouts with Budget::deadline
4. Replace polling intervals with cx.sleep

## Unit tests to include
- Test concurrent capture respects max_concurrent limit
- Test capture timeout via Budget::deadline
- Test all captures complete before scope exits (structured concurrency guarantee)
- Test capture event channel delivery under concurrent load
- Test cancellation: mid-capture cancel results in clean scope exit
- Test adaptive polling interval behavior
- All tests use LabRuntime with virtual time (no real sleeps)
- Tests include structured logging: task spawn/complete events, semaphore acquire/release, channel sends

## Acceptance criteria
- Tailer works with structured concurrency (no JoinSet)
- Max concurrency limit via Semaphore
- Capture timeouts via Budget
- Two-phase channel sends for events
- 6+ unit tests with LabRuntime

## Benchmark requirements
- **Criterion benchmarks for tail throughput**: Add `benches/tailer.rs` measuring:
  - Single capture task throughput: captures/sec for varying payload sizes
  - Concurrent capture throughput: aggregate captures/sec with max_concurrent=1,2,4,8
  - Capture event channel throughput: events/sec through two-phase send pipeline
  - Budget::deadline overhead per capture operation
  - Polling interval accuracy with virtual time vs real time

## LabRuntime DPOR
- **Concurrent tail operations testing with DPOR**: Use LabRuntime schedule exploration (DPOR) to test concurrent tailer scenarios:
  - max_concurrent captures running simultaneously — verify semaphore limit never exceeded
  - Interleaved capture completion and new capture start — verify no stale state
  - Capture timeout during concurrent operations — verify clean cancellation of timed-out task without affecting siblings
  - Channel send interleaved with capture completion — verify no event loss or reordering
close_reason: Tailer asupersync migration complete. Production code routes through runtime_compat (no direct tokio); this bead adds 8 LabRuntime tests in tailer::tests::labruntime_tailer covering CaptureScheduler rate/byte budget enforcement, SchedulerSnapshot serde, mpsc channel delivery/backpressure, cancelled Cx propagation, config defaults, and metrics defaults. 96/96 tailer tests pass; benches/tailer.rs pre-exists. Commit 7899f8b0.

title: Mux server sharding — split pane groups across multiple processes
description:
## Goal
Design and implement mux server sharding -- splitting pane groups across multiple independent mux server processes to eliminate the single-process bottleneck (Mux singleton RwLock) and enable horizontal scaling.

## Background & Motivation
WezTerm's mux server has a fundamental architectural bottleneck: the Mux singleton (Arc<RwLock<Mux>>) serializes ALL cross-pane operations. With 50+ panes, every list_panes, get_text, or notification callback contends on this single lock. No amount of wa-side optimization can fix this -- it's a WezTerm design limitation.

Sharding means running multiple mux server instances, each responsible for a subset of panes:
- Shard 1: panes 0-15 (Claude Code sessions)
- Shard 2: panes 16-31 (Codex sessions)
- Shard 3: panes 32-47 (Gemini sessions)
- Shard 4: panes 48+ (utility/monitoring)

Each shard is an independent process with its own Mux singleton, so lock contention is isolated.

## Technical Design

### Shard Manager
```rust
// Location: crates/wa-core/src/sharding.rs (new file)

pub struct ShardManager {
    shards: Vec<MuxShard>,
    assignment: PaneAssignment,
    config: ShardConfig,
}

pub struct MuxShard {
    pub id: ShardId,
    pub socket_path: PathBuf,
    pub client: DirectMuxClient,  // connection to this shard's mux server
    pub pane_ids: HashSet<PaneId>,
    pub pid: u32,
}

pub struct ShardConfig {
    pub num_shards: usize,        // default: 4
    pub assignment: AssignmentStrategy,
    pub socket_dir: PathBuf,
}

pub enum AssignmentStrategy {
    RoundRobin,
    ByAgentType,  // Group same agent type on same shard
    Manual(HashMap<PaneId, ShardId>),
}
```

### Shard-Aware Operations
wa's operations become shard-aware:
```rust
impl ShardManager {
    pub async fn list_all_panes(&self) -> Result<Vec<PaneInfo>> {
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        for shard in &self.shards {
            let panes = shard.client.list_panes().await?;
            all.extend(panes.into_iter().map(|p| p.with_shard(shard.id)));
        }
        Ok(all)
    }
    
    pub async fn get_pane_text(&self, pane_id: PaneId) -> Result<String> {
        let shard = self.assignment.shard_for(pane_id)?;
        self.shards[shard].client.get_text(pane_id).await
    }
}
```

### Starting Multiple Mux Servers
```bash
# wa manages the lifecycle:
wezterm-mux-server --daemonize --unix-socket /tmp/wa-shard-0.sock
wezterm-mux-server --daemonize --unix-socket /tmp/wa-shard-1.sock
wezterm-mux-server --daemonize --unix-socket /tmp/wa-shard-2.sock
wezterm-mux-server --daemonize --unix-socket /tmp/wa-shard-3.sock
```

## Complexity Warning
This is a HIGH complexity change that requires:
- Running multiple mux server instances
- Routing pane operations to correct shard
- Handling pane creation (which shard gets the new pane?)
- Maintaining shard assignment consistency
- Handling shard failures (failover? redistribute?)

## Dependencies
- bd-41w (Connection pool): Pool per shard for connection management

## Acceptance Criteria
- Multiple mux server instances manageable by wa
- Pane operations routed to correct shard
- list_all_panes() aggregates across shards
- Shard assignment configurable (round-robin, by agent type, manual)
- Shard health monitoring integrated with watchdog

## Estimated Effort
8-12 hours implementation, 4 hours testing. HIGH complexity.

## Risk
This is the highest-complexity improvement in the set. Consider implementing all P1/P2 improvements first, as they may reduce the need for sharding.

## Concurrency Testing Requirements

### LabRuntime DPOR (Dynamic Partial Order Reduction)
Shard coordination involves multiple async actors (ShardManager, per-shard DirectMuxClients, PaneAssignment) communicating concurrently. Use LabRuntime with DPOR exploration to test:
- **Shard assignment race**: Two concurrent create_pane() calls must not assign to the same shard slot if capacity-based assignment is used. DPOR explores all interleavings of the assignment lock.
- **Cross-shard list aggregation**: Concurrent list_all_panes() calls while shards are being added/removed must not produce partial or duplicated results.
- **Shard failover coordination**: When a shard process dies, the ShardManager must atomically redistribute panes. DPOR verifies no pane is "lost" (assigned to no shard) or "duplicated" (assigned to two shards) during redistribution.
- **Assignment consistency**: After any sequence of create/destroy/failover operations, the invariant union(shard.pane_ids for all shards) == all_known_panes must hold.

### Criterion Benchmarks
Add `benches/shard_routing.rs` using criterion:
- **cross_shard_routing_overhead**: Benchmark the overhead of ShardManager.get_pane_text() (which looks up the shard, then delegates) vs direct DirectMuxClient.get_text(). Target: routing overhead <50us per call.
- **list_all_panes_aggregation**: Benchmark list_all_panes() across 2, 4, 8 shards. Measure aggregation overhead as shard count increases.
- **shard_assignment_throughput**: Benchmark AssignmentStrategy.shard_for() for RoundRobin, ByAgentType, and Manual strategies with 100, 500, 1000 panes.

### Proptest
Add `tests/proptest_sharding.rs`:
- **consistent_hashing_stability**: For any arbitrary sequence of shard additions/removals (proptest generates random add/remove sequences), assert that consistent hashing reassigns at most total_panes / num_shards panes per shard change (minimal disruption property).
- **assignment_completeness**: For any set of pane IDs and any AssignmentStrategy, every pane must be assigned to exactly one shard (no orphans, no duplicates).
- **roundtrip_shard_config**: For any arbitrary ShardConfig (proptest generates random configs), serializing and deserializing produces an identical config.

## Cross-References
- **wa-2dd4s.5** (FrankenMux integration): Mux server sharding is a prerequisite for FrankenMux -- the unified mux layer that abstracts over multiple mux backends (WezTerm, tmux, native). FrankenMux's router will build on ShardManager's shard-aware routing. Coordinate the shard assignment protocol to be compatible with FrankenMux's backend abstraction.

Current code already contains sharding implementation in crates/frankenterm-core/src/sharding.rs plus config/client wiring in config.rs and wezterm.rs; targeted remote validation via rch passed for proptest_sharding (33 passed, including prop_consistent_hash_minimal_disruption) and sharding_labruntime (29 passed). Archived wa-1360 coordination from 2026-02-13 already records that crates/frankenterm-core/benches/shard_routing.rs and its Cargo.toml registration landed, and that the remaining bench compile blockers at that time were unrelated shared-tree errors in dataflow.rs rather than missing sharding functionality. Remaining build.rs and timeout issues observed today are consistent with known rch infra false-negatives / remote timeout behavior, not evidence that wa-1360 itself is unimplemented.

title: CLI commands — wa snapshot save/restore/list/diff/inspect
description:
## Goal
Implement the wa CLI commands for snapshot management: save, restore, list, diff, and inspect. These are the user-facing interface for the session persistence system.

## Background and Motivation
The snapshot system needs a clean CLI interface that both humans and the Robot Mode API can use. Commands should follow wa existing CLI patterns (clap derive, structured output, TOON support) and integrate with the existing wa binary.

## Technical Design

### Command Structure
```
wa snapshot save [--trigger <trigger>] [--label <label>]
wa snapshot restore <snapshot_id> [--layout-only] [--launch-agents] [--dry-run]
wa snapshot list [--limit <n>] [--format json|toon]
wa snapshot diff <id1> <id2>
wa snapshot inspect <snapshot_id> [--pane <pane_id>]
wa snapshot delete <snapshot_id> [--force]
```

### wa snapshot save
- Triggers SnapshotEngine::capture_snapshot()
- Accepts --trigger flag (manual, pre_restart, pre_shutdown)
- Optional --label for human-readable name
- Returns snapshot_id and summary stats
- Robot mode: returns JSON envelope with snapshot metadata

### wa snapshot restore
- Reads snapshot from SQLite
- Phase 1: Layout restoration (always)
- Phase 2: Scrollback injection (unless --layout-only)
- Phase 3: Process re-launch (only with --launch-agents)
- --dry-run: shows plan without executing
- Returns restoration report (panes restored, failures, warnings)
- Robot mode: returns JSON with PaneIdMap and status per pane

### wa snapshot list
- Shows recent snapshots with timestamp, trigger, pane count, size
- Default limit: 10
- Supports TOON format for AI-to-AI usage

### wa snapshot diff
- Compares two snapshots
- Shows: added/removed panes, changed layouts, scrollback size changes
- Useful for understanding what changed between snapshots

### wa snapshot inspect
- Detailed view of a single snapshot
- Shows layout tree, pane details, process info
- --pane filter: show only specific pane data

### Clap Integration
```rust
// In crates/wa/src/main.rs, add to CLI enum:
#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum SnapshotCmd {
    Save {
        #[arg(long)] trigger: Option<SnapshotTrigger>,
        #[arg(long)] label: Option<String>,
    },
    Restore {
        snapshot_id: String,
        #[arg(long)] layout_only: bool,
        #[arg(long)] launch_agents: bool,
        #[arg(long)] dry_run: bool,
    },
    List {
        #[arg(long, default_value = "10")] limit: usize,
    },
    Diff { id1: String, id2: String },
    Inspect {
        snapshot_id: String,
        #[arg(long)] pane: Option<u64>,
    },
    Delete {
        snapshot_id: String,
        #[arg(long)] force: bool,
    },
}
```

## Integration Points
- **SnapshotEngine**: Core snapshot operations
- **Layout restorer, scrollback injector, process launcher**: Restoration phases
- **Robot Mode**: All commands return structured output for AI agents
- **TOON format**: Token-efficient output support
- **wa existing CLI patterns**: Follow same error envelope, --format flag, --stats flag

## Key Files to Create/Modify
- CREATE: crates/wa/src/commands/snapshot.rs
- MODIFY: crates/wa/src/main.rs (add snapshot subcommand)
- MODIFY: crates/wa/src/commands/mod.rs (add module)

## Dependencies
- SnapshotEngine orchestrator (bead 5)
- Layout restoration engine (bead 6)
- Scrollback injection engine (bead 7)
- Process re-launch engine (bead 8)

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 6 subcommands work (save, restore, list, diff, inspect, delete)
- Robot mode returns structured JSON envelopes
- TOON format support for all commands
- --dry-run mode for restore shows plan without executing
- Error handling follows wa existing patterns (robot.* error codes)
- Help text is clear and includes examples

## Estimated Effort
3-4 hours implementation, 1 hour testing

## Test Requirements

### Property-Based Testing (proptest)
Add proptest cases in crates/wa/tests/proptest_snapshot_cli.rs:
- **CLI argument parsing roundtrip**: For any valid combination of snapshot subcommand arguments, parsing the args into the SnapshotCmd enum and then serializing back to a command string must produce equivalent args. Strategy: arb_snapshot_cmd() generates random valid SnapshotCmd variants with random snapshot IDs (alphanumeric, 6-20 chars), random limits (1-1000), random trigger types, and random boolean flags.
- **Snapshot ID validation**: For any string input as snapshot_id, the CLI must either accept it (valid ID format) or produce a clear error. No panics on malformed IDs. Strategy: arb_string() generates arbitrary strings including empty, whitespace-only, special characters, and very long strings (up to 10000 chars).
- **Flag exclusivity**: For the restore subcommand, verify that --dry-run combined with --launch-agents produces a plan (not execution). For --layout-only, verify scrollback injection and process launch are skipped. Strategy: arb_restore_flags() generates all 8 combinations of the 3 boolean flags.
- **List limit bounds**: For any limit value in [0, usize::MAX], the list command must either produce valid output or a clear error (never panic, never OOM). Strategy: arb_limit() focuses on edge cases: 0, 1, 10, 100, usize::MAX.

### Criterion Benchmarks
Add benchmarks in crates/wa/benches/snapshot_cli.rs:
- bench_snapshot_list_100: List 100 snapshots and format as table, target <50ms
- bench_snapshot_diff_large: Diff two 200-pane snapshots, target <100ms
- bench_snapshot_inspect_formatting: Format a detailed inspect view of a 50-pane snapshot
- bench_cli_arg_parsing: Parse and validate all 6 subcommand variants, target <1ms

## Cross-References
- **bd-cuz** (MuxSnapshot schema): The CLI inspect and diff commands directly render MuxSnapshot structures. The output format must stay in sync with schema changes. When bd-cuz adds new fields (e.g., agent session metadata, differential snapshot markers), the CLI inspect/diff views must be updated to display them.

title: Integrate tru (TOON format) for token-efficient agent communication
description:
# Integrate tru for Token-Efficient Communication

## Skills: /extreme-software-optimization

## What tru does
TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) serialization. 40-60% fewer tokens than JSON. Human-readable, streaming decode, deterministic output.

## Current state
Standalone CLI at /Users/jemanuel/projects/toon_rust.

## Integration plan

### 1. Import tru-core as library
- Use TOON serialization for all robot-mode output
- Dual format: TOON for agent consumption, JSON for human/API consumption

### 2. Robot mode output
All `wa` robot commands emit TOON by default:
```
wa observe --robot --format=toon
wa search --robot --format=toon
```
Token savings compound across hundreds of agent queries per session.

### 3. MCP tool responses
MCP tool responses can optionally use TOON:
- Reduces token usage for large payloads (pane output, search results)
- Agent explicitly requests via format parameter

### 4. Workflow definitions
TOON-encoded workflow specs use fewer tokens:
- Workflow templates stored as TOON
- Agent queries workflow engine using TOON format

### 5. Benchmark (/extreme-software-optimization)
- Measure token savings: JSON vs TOON for typical wa output
- Measure serialization throughput: should be >500MB/s
- Measure deserialization correctness: round-trip identity

## Tests
- Token count comparison: JSON vs TOON for 10 representative payloads
- Serialization round-trip test
- Streaming decode test (large payloads)
- Performance benchmark

## Acceptance criteria
- tru-core as library dependency
- Robot mode supports --format=toon
- 40%+ token savings on representative payloads
- >500MB/s serialization throughput
- Streaming decode works for large payloads

## Test Framework Requirements
- **Criterion benchmarks**: TOON encode/decode throughput benchmarks:
  - Encode throughput: benchmark serializing typical payloads (pane output snapshots, search results, workflow specs) in TOON vs JSON. Measure MB/s for both. Target >500MB/s for TOON encode.
  - Decode throughput: benchmark deserializing the same payloads. Target >500MB/s for TOON decode.
  - Streaming decode: benchmark incremental decoding of a 10MB TOON stream. Measure time-to-first-record and total throughput.
  - Token count comparison: for each benchmark payload, also measure token count (using tiktoken or equivalent) to verify the 40-60% savings claim.
- **Proptest for format roundtrips**: Property-based tests verifying serialization identity:
  - Generate arbitrary Rust structs (using proptest's Arbitrary derive), serialize to TOON, deserialize back, and verify equality
  - Generate arbitrary JSON values, convert to TOON, convert back to JSON, and verify semantic equality
  - Generate TOON strings with random whitespace/formatting variations, verify they parse identically (canonical form)
  - Test streaming decode: split a valid TOON document at random byte boundaries, feed chunks to the streaming decoder, and verify the final result matches single-pass decode

## Cross-References
- **wa-2f2m** (Semantic output compression): TOON provides token-efficient serialization, while semantic output compression reduces the content itself. These are complementary — compress semantically first, then serialize in TOON for maximum token savings. The two beads should share benchmark payloads for consistent measurement.

title: Refactor IPC server (ipc.rs) to asupersync
description:
# Refactor IPC server (ipc.rs) to asupersync

## Background
ipc.rs (~400 LOC) implements Unix socket IPC for CLI-to-daemon communication using JSON-line protocol.

## Current tokio usage
- tokio::net::UnixListener for accepting connections
- tokio::io::BufReader + AsyncBufReadExt for line reading
- tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt for response writing
- mpsc channels (22+ instances) for message passing
- tokio::spawn for per-connection handler tasks

## Migration
1. Replace UnixListener/UnixStream with asupersync equivalents
2. Replace BufReader with asupersync buffered I/O
3. Replace per-connection spawns with scope.spawn
4. Replace mpsc channels with asupersync channels (two-phase send)
5. Thread Cx through accept loop and handler functions

## IPC protocol MUST be preserved
JSON-line protocol (newline-delimited JSON) must produce identical messages.

## Unit tests (LabRuntime + real sockets)
1. **Accept connection**: listener accepts, handler spawned in scope
2. **JSON-line round-trip**: send JSON request, receive JSON response
3. **Multiple concurrent connections**: N clients connect simultaneously
4. **Malformed input**: partial JSON, verify error handling
5. **Connection drop**: client disconnects mid-request, verify clean handler exit
6. **Shutdown**: close listener scope, verify all handlers drain
7. **Channel delivery**: verify IPC messages reach internal channels via two-phase send
8. **Backpressure**: slow consumer, verify bounded channel behavior

Each test logs: connection accept/close, JSON parse events, channel sends, handler lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria
- IPC server works identically with asupersync
- JSON-line protocol preserved
- Per-connection handlers in structured scopes
- Clean shutdown on scope exit
- 8+ unit tests

## macOS platform note
- **kqueue for IPC readiness**: On macOS, the IPC UnixListener uses kqueue (not epoll) for socket readiness notification. Verify that asupersync's reactor correctly handles kqueue-based accept() and read readiness for Unix domain sockets on Darwin. If any platform-specific code exists in the IPC module, ensure `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` paths use kqueue and `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` paths use epoll.

## Benchmark requirements
- **Criterion benchmarks for IPC throughput**: Add `benches/ipc_throughput.rs` measuring:
  - Single-client JSON-line request/response round-trip latency
  - Multi-client throughput: requests/sec with N=1,5,10,20 concurrent clients
  - JSON serialization/deserialization overhead per message
  - Connection establishment latency (accept + handler spawn)
  - Comparison with tokio-based IPC server for equivalent workloads

## LabRuntime DPOR
- **Concurrent IPC testing with DPOR**: Use LabRuntime schedule exploration (DPOR) to test concurrent IPC scenarios:
  - Multiple clients connecting and sending requests simultaneously — verify no request/response cross-talk
  - Interleaved accept + handler spawn + response write — verify correct client-to-handler mapping
  - Client disconnect during response write — verify clean handler teardown
  - Concurrent shutdown while handlers are processing — verify all handlers drain before scope exits

title: Replace vendored FastAPI/FastMCP frameworks for asupersync compat
description:
# Replace vendored FastAPI/FastMCP frameworks

## Background
FrankenTerm vendors two async frameworks that are built on tokio:
1. FastAPI — HTTP server framework
2. FastMCP — MCP (Model Context Protocol) server framework

These have deep tokio dependencies and cannot trivially use asupersync.

## Options
1. **Port to asupersync** (high effort, full control)
   - Rewrite framework internals to use asupersync net/spawn/channels
   - Benefit: native integration, no compat overhead

2. **Replace with asupersync-native equivalents** (medium effort)
   - Use asupersync::http server directly for web endpoints
   - Write a minimal MCP protocol handler on asupersync
   - Benefit: clean break, no legacy framework code

3. **Compatibility shim** (lowest effort, worst long-term)
   - Run a mini tokio runtime just for these frameworks
   - Bridge async contexts between tokio and asupersync
   - NOT RECOMMENDED: defeats the purpose of migration

## Recommendation
Option 2 — replace with asupersync-native code. The web server is simple REST endpoints, and MCP is a JSON-RPC protocol. Neither needs a heavyweight framework.

## Acceptance criteria
- HTTP server endpoints work without FastAPI
- MCP tool serving works without FastMCP
- No tokio transitive dependency through these frameworks
- Response format and behavior identical

## Benchmark requirements
- **Criterion benchmarks for replacement framework throughput**: Add `benches/framework_throughput.rs` measuring:
  - HTTP server: requests/sec for simple GET /health endpoint (baseline with FastAPI vs asupersync-native)
  - HTTP server: requests/sec for JSON POST endpoint with body parsing
  - MCP server: tool invocations/sec for a simple tool (baseline with FastMCP vs asupersync-native)
  - MCP server: concurrent tool invocation throughput with N=2,4,8 simultaneous clients
  - Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) for both HTTP and MCP operations
  - The replacement MUST match or exceed FastAPI/FastMCP throughput to justify the migration effort.

title: Phase 4: Replace tokio task spawning with asupersync structured concurrency
description:
# Replace tokio task spawning with asupersync structured concurrency

## Goal
Replace all tokio::spawn/JoinHandle/JoinSet with asupersync's structured concurrency (Scope/region). This bead establishes the patterns; per-module application is done in module-specific beads.

## Key paradigm shift
Tokio allows detached tasks (fire-and-forget). Asupersync enforces structured concurrency — every task belongs to a Scope, and the scope waits for all children before exiting.

## Scope (what this bead covers)
- Establish cx.region() / scope.spawn() patterns
- Define how to replace JoinHandle (scope child handle)
- Define how to replace JoinSet (region with multiple spawns + semaphore for bounding)
- Document fire-and-forget redesign strategies:
  - Option A: Attach to long-lived application scope
  - Option B: Dedicated background region for app lifetime
  - Option C: Refactor to not need detached tasks
- Create helper utilities for common patterns (bounded spawn, spawn-with-timeout)

## What this does NOT cover
- select! macro replacement — that's per-module work because each module has different select! branches. Module beads (wa-p48pw, wa-1m7nk, wa-16hou, etc.) handle their own select! migration using asupersync::combinator::select/race.

## Patterns to establish
```rust
// Bounded concurrent work (replaces JoinSet with max)
pub async fn spawn_bounded<F, T>(
    cx: &mut Cx, max: usize, tasks: Vec<F>
) -> Outcome<Vec<T>, Error>
where F: FnOnce(&mut Cx) -> Fut...
{
    cx.region(|scope| async {
        let sem = Semaphore::new(max);
        for task in tasks {
            let permit = sem.acquire(cx).await?;
            scope.spawn(move |cx| async move {
                let _p = permit;
                task(cx).await
            });
        }
    }).await
}
```

## Unit tests
- Test: scope.spawn() runs task to completion
- Test: scope exit waits for all children
- Test: bounded spawn respects concurrency limit
- Test: cancellation propagates to all scope children
- Test: nested regions work correctly
- All tests use LabRuntime with seed-locked scheduling

## Acceptance criteria
- Structured concurrency patterns documented and tested
- Helper utilities for bounded spawn, spawn-with-timeout
- Fire-and-forget redesign strategy decided
- 5+ LabRuntime tests for the patterns

## LabRuntime DPOR
- **Structured concurrency testing with DPOR**: Use LabRuntime schedule exploration (DPOR) to exhaustively test structured concurrency guarantees:
  - Verify scope exit always waits for ALL children under every possible interleaving
  - Verify cancellation propagates to all scope children regardless of scheduling order
  - Verify nested region teardown ordering (inner scopes complete before outer)
  - Verify bounded spawn never exceeds concurrency limit under any schedule

## Benchmark requirements
- **Criterion benchmarks for task spawn overhead**: Add `benches/task_spawn.rs` measuring:
  - scope.spawn() latency for a no-op task
  - Region creation + N spawns + join overhead for N=1,10,100,1000
  - Comparison with tokio::spawn for equivalent workloads
  - Structured concurrency overhead: region vs flat spawn

## Cross-references
- See wa-brc7d.5 (mux crate in asupersync FrankenTerm crates epic) — the mux crate is the heaviest user of task spawning for pane output subscriptions and background polling. Patterns established here directly apply there.
close_reason: Complete. All acceptance criteria met: (1) Structured concurrency patterns documented in cx.rs module docs (lines 28-41). (2) Helper utilities: spawn_with_cx, try_spawn_with_cx, spawn_bounded_with_cx, spawn_with_timeout. (3) Fire-and-forget strategy: avoid detached work, attach to app scope, quarantine behind runtime_compat. (4) 45 tests pass (cargo test -p frankenterm-core --lib --no-default-features --features asupersync-runtime cx::tests:: — exit 0, 45/45 green). (5) Criterion benchmarks in benches/task_spawn.rs.
